sections.heading: What the market charges around Al Ain, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Look first at the gap between two of the published bands, because it answers a question Al Ain families ask constantly. Qualified subject tutors working online publish AED 150 to 300 an hour. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Dubai table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. The difference between those two bands is the travel premium, and in a city 130 kilometres inland it buys exactly one thing: physical presence. It does not buy a better match on Standard Level Applications and Interpretation, because the pool of people who can drive to an Al Ain address is small and the pool who have taught this course is not the same pool.

The rest of the published market, for completeness. Budget online tuition and university-student tutors advertise AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. IB and IGCSE subject specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase published at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-level provision reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions - and the gap between those two monthly figures is the travel premium again, expressed by the month.

All of those figures are published by the providers named and were read in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list, and we quote after a free trial lesson has produced a diagnosis. Where this page is useful is in letting you interrogate any quote you receive: ask what is included beyond the hour, whether marked work comes back in writing, whether the tutor has taught this specific course rather than Diploma mathematics in general, and whether travel is inside the number.

Our own delivery is stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, because in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Ain sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, calculator keystrokes visible on screen and marked scripts returned in writing. For a city this far inland, that is not a workaround - it is the only reliable way to put a specialist on this course in front of a student every week for thirty weeks.

process.title: Tell us the school and the next three dates
process.description: The campus, the exploration deadline, the internal examination fortnight and whether any sibling board examinations overlap. In Al Ain those dates vary by campus and they decide which weeks the hours should land in far more than the topic list does.

process.title: Send two marked papers
process.description: The last two mathematics scripts with the school's marks still on them. We read them for the three recurring faults - finance by reasoning, bare chi-squared conclusions, unjustified model choices - rather than for the grade at the top.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the actual tutor
process.description: Sixty minutes with the person who would teach the course, not a consultant. It is spent on diagnostic questions and on the school's own calendar, and you receive a written summary of both afterwards.

process.title: A plan written against the school's calendar
process.description: The weekly slot is fixed for the term around the mandatory-subject afternoons, the school's heaviest assessment fortnight and Ramadan timings. Where a conflict is unavoidable, the plan says which item moves.

process.title: Review against the baseline, not against impressions
process.description: Every few weeks we compare marked work with the diagnostic baseline and say whether the targeted fault has gone. If it has not after two reviews, we change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Al Ain, and is it the same one Dubai parents talk about?
faqs.answer: No. Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools fall under ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. KHDA, which features in most UAE education coverage, is responsible for private education in Dubai and has no authority here. The practical consequence is that KHDA notices about fees or mandatory subjects are not statements about your child's school, and the guidance that applies in Al Ain comes from ADEK and from the federal Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: How many papers does Applications and Interpretation SL have, and how long are they?
faqs.answer: Two. Paper 1 and Paper 2 each run one hour thirty minutes for eighty marks, and each carries forty per cent of the final grade. A graphic display calculator is required in both; unlike Analysis and Approaches, this course has no non-calculator paper. The remaining twenty per cent is the mathematical exploration, a piece of coursework marked out of twenty across five criteria. The course runs to 150 teaching hours at Standard Level against 240 at Higher Level. Confirm durations and weightings against your cohort's subject guide before planning revision around them.

faqs.question: What topics does this course cover that Analysis and Approaches does not?
faqs.answer: Financial mathematics is the clearest example - compound interest, amortisation, annuities and percentage error appear here and not in the other Standard Level course. Voronoi diagrams sit in the geometry topic and solve nearest-facility problems. The statistics content goes further into correlation, regression and the chi-squared test for independence, and the calculus is applied, using the trapezoidal rule rather than formal integration techniques. The overall emphasis is on modelling data and justifying a choice of model, which is a different skill from algebraic manipulation.

faqs.question: When do we need to confirm examination entries, and who sets that deadline?
faqs.answer: Far earlier than most families expect, and the board sets it through the centre. A UAE candidate sits Cambridge in June or in November - the February and March series is offered in India only - and for either one the entry deadline falls months before the first paper, in the spring for June and in the autumn term for November, with the exact day confirmed on the statement of entry the school issues. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and there the published window is firm: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the IB Diploma, ask your school's coordinator - no IB date on this page would be verified, so we do not publish one.

faqs.question: My daughter's school is a Cambridge centre. Does the exam timetable zone matter?
faqs.answer: It does, and Cambridge says so explicitly. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. In practice that means revision schedules should be built from the timetable your centre is actually working to, obtained from the school's examinations officer, rather than from a timetable found online. We ask for it before building any pre-examination plan.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons really affect a maths plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, because they occupy fixed hours. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations, and those subjects are assessed by the school rather than by the IB. The homework attached to them lands on the same evenings a tutoring session wants. So we put the mandatory-subject afternoons and the school's heaviest assessment fortnight into the calendar before fixing a slot, which is the difference between a plan kept in February and one abandoned.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on financial maths questions when he understands the idea?
faqs.answer: Because the questions are built for a calculator routine and he is reasoning his way through them. Amortisation, annuity and compound-growth questions have an application on the graphic display calculator designed for exactly this, and a student working from first principles typically arrives nearly right, which earns nothing. This is one of the fastest fixes in the course: an hour on the finance routines, then a set of past questions to make it automatic. It then returns marks in every subsequent paper, and in Business Management too if he takes it.

faqs.question: What does a chi-squared answer have to say to get full marks?
faqs.answer: More than the verdict. The marks are awarded for stating the hypotheses, carrying out the test correctly, comparing against the critical value at the stated significance level, and then writing a conclusion in the context of the data - whether there is evidence of association between the two named variables. Students routinely compute everything correctly and then write a bare sentence saying the variables are independent, dropping the contextual marks. It is one of the cheapest sets of marks in the Standard Level course and one of the most commonly lost.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education require for equivalency on a British curriculum?
faqs.answer: Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the IB we publish no points figure, because none was read on the Ministry's own site for this project. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority; IB Gram performs no part of this process.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring in order to get their certificate recognised in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone suggesting otherwise is inventing urgency. Equivalency is a documentary process run by the Ministry of Education about grades already achieved, with published requirements by curriculum track. Tutoring may help a student reach a grade threshold before results exist, but it plays no part in the recognition process itself, and no provider can perform, expedite or guarantee it. The right channel is the Ministry's own service, and the right people to ask about a specific file are the Ministry and your child's school registrar.

faqs.question: Can my son's own school teacher tutor him privately in Abu Dhabi emirate?
faqs.answer: It has been reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That reporting should be verified against ADEK's current policy document before being treated as exact wording. Either way, arranging paid tutoring with your child's own classroom teacher is the arrangement most likely to create a problem for the teacher.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Al Ain need a government permit, and what does it cost them?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those working without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor quoted higher than an online one in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Travel. Published market bands put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home visits with travel included at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. The difference is the journey, and in a city 130 kilometres inland it is a real cost. What it does not buy is a better match on this specific course, because the set of tutors who can reach an Al Ain address is much smaller than the set who have taught Applications and Interpretation.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram provide in-home maths tutoring anywhere in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we hold no office, centre or branch anywhere in the Emirates. Al Ain sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, the calculator keystrokes visible on screen, and marked scripts returned in writing. Given how far the city sits from the capital, that is also the only arrangement that reliably puts the same specialist in front of a student every week across a whole academic year.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and the long Al Ain summer?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. During Ramadan most Al Ain families switch to post-iftar slots and we shorten sessions while keeping the weekly rhythm, because a four-week gap mid-topic costs more than it saves. Over the summer, families travelling out of the city usually keep a reduced schedule across time zones, which works because nothing about a video session requires either person to be in Al Ain. We ask for the revised schedule in advance so the plan's week blocks move as a set instead of collapsing.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutoring provider before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which specific course have you taught, Applications and Interpretation or Analysis and Approaches, and at which level. Does marked written work come back every week. Who holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit for the person teaching. Is travel inside the quoted rate or added. And what regulator or board approval are you claiming - because no education regulator in the UAE licenses or approves tutoring providers, so an approval claim should be evidenced from the regulator's own register or withdrawn.

al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Programme Physics at Higher Level to students in Al Ain and across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Each one is matched to a named theme, a named paper and a named deadline before the trial lesson is booked, so the first hour is spent on your child's actual gap.

intro.heading: Where your child is now, and what the weeks between here and the May session look like
paragraphs: An IB DP Physics HL tutor in Al Ain is answering a timeline question, not a subject question. A parent rarely searches this phrase because they want a general overview of Higher Level Physics. They search it because a predicted grade has landed lower than the university offer needs, because the scientific investigation draft came back with a weak Evaluation mark, or because Theme D arrived and the student stopped understanding lessons they used to follow. The useful first question is not what Physics HL covers. It is how many teaching weeks are left, and what has to happen inside them.

The Diploma is a two-year course with a Higher Level subject allocation of 240 guided teaching hours, and almost every recoverable problem in Physics HL is a sequencing problem. Kinematics and forces in Theme A are taught early, assessed lightly in DP1, then relied on constantly in Theme C and Theme D a year later. A student who never fully fixed vector resolution in October of DP1 will meet the same gap again in the autumn of DP2 wearing a different costume: as circular motion, as the component of a gravitational field along a slope, as a flux calculation. Finding the original gap is what makes a term of tutoring different from a term of re-teaching.

Al Ain adds a specific constraint. The city is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The inland school set is smaller than the capital's, and Higher Level sciences are where that shows. A cohort of eight Physics HL students in one Al Ain school is normal. One teacher may carry both the SL and HL sets in the same room, which is workable for Theme A and much harder for the HL-only material in A.4, A.5, B.4, D.4 and E.2.

What a tutor can honestly offer against that is time and specialisation, not proximity. Lessons here are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The trade is deliberate. A family in Al Ain gets a Physics HL specialist who has taught the current guide and marked work against the current investigation criteria, instead of whichever tutor is willing to drive 130 kilometres from Abu Dhabi island on a Tuesday evening.

The rest of this page is laid out as a countdown. It starts with what the course actually contains and what the HL-only additions are, moves through the assessment weightings and the places marks are lost, sets out the investigation criteria and their mark allocations, and then works backwards from the May session through every internal deadline a DP student in Al Ain meets on the way. The AED rate bands, the permit position and the ADEK context sit at the end, because they are decisions a parent makes once and the teaching plan is the thing that changes week to week.
bullets: Higher Level Physics is assessed by two papers and one internal investigation, weighted 36%, 44% and 20%
The HL-only material is concentrated in rigid body mechanics, relativity, thermodynamics, induction and quantum physics
A 3,000-word limit applies to the scientific investigation report, marked out of 24 across four criteria
Al Ain private schools sit under ADEK, not KHDA, so inspection reports and policies come from a different authority

al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Four routes bring an Al Ain student to this page, and each one starts the countdown at a different point. The notes below say what the gap usually is at each stage and how long it typically takes to close in weekly one-to-one sessions.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics, Higher Level
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · DP1 and DP2 · 240 guided hours
programmes.description: The full Higher Level course: the five themes plus the HL-only extensions, two written papers and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 carries the long structured and extended-response questions. The data booklet is supplied in the examination, which changes what is worth memorising and what is worth practising.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the HL set is often small enough to share a room with the SL set. That means the HL-only topics are frequently taught in compressed blocks late in DP2, and a student who misses two weeks of D.4 induction through illness or travel has no second pass through it at school. Weekly one-to-one sessions exist mainly to hold that material open.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics, Standard Level
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · DP1 and DP2 · 150 guided hours
programmes.description: The same five themes without the Higher Level extensions, shorter papers and the same investigation worth 20%. Standard Level students who are considering a move up to Higher Level need the decision made early, because the HL additions are not evenly spread across the two years and catching up on A.4 and A.5 in DP2 is a different task from meeting them in sequence.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students sometimes start Physics at Standard Level because the HL set did not run, then need Higher Level for an engineering application to a UK or UAE university. Where a school can accommodate the switch, the realistic window is the first term of DP1. We will say plainly when a switch is no longer sensible rather than sell sessions against it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed on four criteria and rewards investigation design and communication. Diploma Physics rewards algebraic fluency, unit discipline and the ability to read a graph gradient as a physical quantity. The gap between the two is the single most common reason a strong MYP student finds DP1 Physics harder than expected in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain families moving from an MYP programme into a Diploma set in the same school still cross this gap, and so do students arriving from a British Year 11 or a CBSE Class 10. The pre-DP summer is the cheapest time to close it: six to eight sessions on rearranging formulae, logarithms, trigonometry in context and uncertainty notation.

programmes.name: Physics Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge link
programmes.description: A Physics Extended Essay needs a question narrow enough to answer with data a student can actually gather. Supervision here means process coaching: reading the research question for feasibility, checking that the method generates enough data points, questioning the uncertainty treatment, and reviewing the student's own drafts against the published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: A tutor working with an Al Ain student on a Physics Extended Essay never produces text for it. The school supervisor signs the authenticity declaration, and the IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice. What a tutor adds is feasibility pressure early, when a research question is still changeable, and honest criticism of the student's own analysis later.

al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the Physics Higher Level course as a tutoring plan rather than a syllabus listing. Each entry names what the theme assesses and where Al Ain students most often lose marks on it, so a trial lesson can start somewhere specific.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with A.4 and A.5 Higher Level only
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work, energy and power at both levels, then rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity for Higher Level. Marks go missing on vector resolution, on momentum problems where the system boundary is chosen carelessly, and on relativity questions where the student picks the wrong frame before doing any algebra.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with B.4 Higher Level only
subjects.description: Thermal energy transfers, the greenhouse effect, gas laws and current and circuits, plus thermodynamics for Higher Level. The usual losses are specific heat capacity questions answered without tracking which body gains and which loses, circuit questions where internal resistance is ignored, and entropy answers that describe disorder instead of using the definition.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, the wave model, wave phenomena, standing waves and resonance, and the Doppler effect. Higher Level pushes further into single-slit and multiple-slit interference and quantitative Doppler treatment. Students who never secured phase relationships in simple harmonic motion lose marks across the whole theme rather than in one place.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with D.4 Higher Level only
subjects.description: Gravitational fields, electric and magnetic fields, motion in electromagnetic fields, and electromagnetic induction for Higher Level. This is where Al Ain HL students most often report that lessons stopped making sense, because the theme assumes fluent vector work and comfort with inverse-square relationships from Theme A a year earlier.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with E.2 Higher Level only
subjects.description: Atomic structure, radioactive decay, fission, fusion and stars at both levels, with quantum physics added at Higher Level. Taught late in DP2, so it is the theme most often compressed. Mass-energy calculations lose marks on unit conversion more often than on physics, and stellar questions lose them on reading a Hertzsprung-Russell diagram.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20% of the final mark
subjects.description: One report of up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. Evaluation is the criterion where UAE students most often leave marks behind, because it asks for method-specific weaknesses and realistic improvements rather than general statements about human error and more repeats.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data analysis
subjects.description: The data-based section of Paper 1 asks students to process unfamiliar experimental data: plot, linearise, read a gradient, assign uncertainty, and comment on whether the data support a relationship. It is the most trainable part of the whole course and the part most often left untrained until the final weeks.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response
subjects.description: Long structured questions that cross themes inside a single scenario, where command terms decide the mark. Explain, describe, outline, determine, deduce and justify each ask for a different shape of answer, and a correct physics answer written to the wrong command term still loses the mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics AA alongside Physics HL
subjects.description: Physics HL leans on calculus, logarithms and trigonometric manipulation that Mathematics AA covers directly. Students taking Mathematics AI alongside Physics HL are not disadvantaged by the IB, but they usually need the algebraic fluency built deliberately rather than picked up in the maths lesson.

subjects.name: Physics Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation with its own criteria and its own supervision rules. The common failure is a research question that cannot be answered with the data available in a school laboratory, discovered too late to change. Feasibility pressure in the first fortnight is worth more than any amount of editing later.

sections.heading: What an IB DP Physics HL tutor in Al Ain is actually being asked to fix
paragraphs: Three problems account for most searches for an IB DP Physics HL tutor in Al Ain. The first is a predicted grade that sits below a university offer, usually discovered in DP1 reports or at the start of DP2. The second is the scientific investigation, where a student has collected data that does not support the relationship they expected and has six weeks to turn it into a report marked out of 24. The third is a specific theme, almost always Theme D fields or the Higher Level thermodynamics in B.4, where the student can follow worked examples in class and cannot start a question alone.

Each of those needs a different plan, and the distinction matters because the cheapest mistake a family makes is booking open-ended weekly sessions for a problem that has a finish point. A predicted-grade problem is a sequencing problem and takes a term. An investigation problem is a four-to-six-hour block timed to specific deadlines. A single-theme problem is three to five sessions and then stops. Selling a term of tuition for a three-session problem is how tutoring gets its reputation in this city.

The diagnostic that separates them is simple and happens in the trial lesson. The student attempts two past-paper questions on the topic they say is the problem, talking through what they are doing. If they cannot start, the gap is prerequisite and sits earlier in the course. If they start correctly and lose marks at the end, the gap is command-term and exam-technique work. If they produce correct physics and the wrong quantity, the gap is unit and notation discipline, which is the fastest of the three to fix and the most commonly misdiagnosed as a content problem.
bullets: Cannot start the question: the gap is earlier in the course, not in this theme
Starts correctly, loses the final marks: command terms and answer structure
Correct method, wrong quantity: units, prefixes and significant figures
Correct everything, too slow: timing practice rather than more teaching

sections.heading: The Higher Level course, theme by theme, and what the HL-only material adds
paragraphs: The current IB Physics guide organises content into five themes rather than the older topic-and-option structure, and the Higher Level course is the Standard Level content plus a set of named extensions. Knowing exactly where those extensions sit matters for planning, because they are not spread evenly across the two years. A student who joins Higher Level late, or who misses a block of DP2 through travel, loses a disproportionate share of the HL-only material rather than a slice of everything.

The table below maps the five themes to their Higher Level additions. The right-hand column is the planning answer: how much extra tutoring time that extension usually needs for a student who is secure on the Standard Level content underneath it. Those figures are our own teaching estimate for one-to-one sessions, not a published IB figure, and a student weak on the prerequisites needs more.

One pattern is worth naming before the table. Theme A is the prerequisite for Theme C and Theme D, and Theme B's circuits material is the prerequisite for the induction work in D.4. This is why a Physics HL student in Al Ain who struggled quietly in the first term of DP1 tends to hit a visible wall in the autumn of DP2. The wall is not Theme D. It is Theme A, met again at a level that no longer tolerates approximation.

The guide also sets out a tools and inquiry strand that runs through every theme rather than sitting in one of them: experimental technique, use of technology, and the mathematics a physicist is expected to apply without prompting. Schools teach it inside practical work, which means it is rarely revised as a topic and rarely tested as one until Paper 1B arrives. For an Al Ain student in a small Higher Level set, that strand is often the quietest gap on the page, because nobody has ever marked it separately.

sections.heading: How Higher Level Physics is assessed, and where the marks go
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics is assessed by two written papers and one internal investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries 44% and holds the structured and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%. A parent reading a report that says Physics is going fine is reading an opinion about Paper 2 performance; the other 56% of the grade is often not being tested at school at all until late.

That weighting has a direct consequence for how tutoring hours are spent. Paper 1B data analysis is a trainable skill with a small syllabus: plot, linearise, read a gradient as a physical quantity, propagate uncertainty, and judge whether the data support the claimed relationship. A student can move several marks on it in four or five focused sessions. The same hours spent on general content revision move far less, because content knowledge is usually not the binding constraint by the spring of DP2.

The investigation is the other asymmetry. It is 20% of the grade, it is marked out of 24 by the school and moderated by the IB, and it is the only component where the student controls the conditions completely. A mark of 18 rather than 12 on the investigation is worth more to a final grade than most students' realistic gain on Paper 2 in the same number of weeks. Families who understand this book the investigation clinic in DP1 and the exam block in DP2, in that order.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion, with its mark allocations
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is one report of up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across four criteria: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, each carrying 6 marks. No competitor page on this search names a single criterion or a single mark allocation, and parents are routinely asked to support a component they have never seen described. The breakdown below is what the student is actually being marked against.

Research design is where most recoverable marks sit, and it is decided before any data exists. A research question that names the independent variable, the dependent variable and the range, with a method that controls the obvious confounders and generates enough data points to plot, is most of the criterion. A question like whether temperature affects resistance is not answerable at this level; the same investigation framed around resistance against temperature over a stated range with a stated number of readings is.

Evaluation is where UAE students most often lose marks, and the reason is consistent. The criterion asks for weaknesses specific to this method and improvements that would actually address them. Writing that human error affected the results, or that more repeats would help, describes any experiment ever conducted and earns little. Writing that the thermometer's resolution limited the temperature readings to the nearest half degree, which accounts for the scatter at the low end, and that a thermocouple with data logging would reduce it, is the same length and earns the mark.

paragraphs: Diploma students in Al Ain sit the May session, as do almost all UAE schools. The table below is deliberately expressed in windows relative to that session rather than in calendar dates. IB examination and results dates are set by the IB and published through ibo.org and the school's Diploma coordinator, and dates found on tutoring sites are frequently out of date, so the authoritative source for your child's cohort is the coordinator's own calendar.

What the table does give is the shape of the two years, which does not change. Subject choices and Higher Level decisions are made before DP1 begins. The investigation is proposed, run and written across DP1 term 3 and DP2 term 1. Internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and the investigation cluster in the autumn of DP2, which is also when Theme D and Theme E are being taught. That overlap is the single busiest point in the course and it is predictable eighteen months in advance.

Reading the table backwards is the useful direction for a parent who has just arrived at this page in the spring of DP2. If the investigation is already submitted and the papers are the remaining problem, the realistic plan is a six-to-ten week intensive block built from the student's own scripts. If the investigation is still open, that comes first regardless of how the papers look, because it is 20% of the grade under the student's own control and the papers are not.

sections.heading: What Physics tutoring costs in Al Ain and across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Published rates for IB tutoring in the UAE are scarce, and the pages that do publish them usually quote in dollars. The bands below are market rates gathered from providers' own published pricing and from Bestimate's 2026 tutoring cost survey for Dubai. They are what the market charges, not an IB Gram price list. Our own pricing is quoted after the free trial lesson, against the subject, the level and the number of weeks left, because a four-session investigation block and a two-year weekly booking are not the same product.

Two things are specific to Al Ain. In-home rates in the city carry the same travel loading as the capital without the same supply of Higher Level science specialists, so a family paying the top of the in-home band is frequently paying a travel premium for a tutor who teaches Standard Level content confidently and Higher Level content from a textbook. Online rates do not carry the travel loading, which is most of the gap between the two columns below.

The other Al Ain factor is scarcity rather than price. A Physics HL specialist who has taught the current guide, marked investigations against the current criteria and worked through a full Paper 2 series is not a common find within driving distance of Al Jimi. The honest comparison is not cheaper against more expensive. It is a subject specialist at an online rate against a generalist at an in-home rate, and for Higher Level Physics in the final year that difference shows up in the marks.

sections.heading: Online sessions against a tutor driving to a villa in Zakher
paragraphs: The phrase most Al Ain parents start with is home tuition, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring in Al Ain is a real market. It is priced at roughly AED 180-500 an hour depending on level and tutor, according to the market sources above, and a substantial part of that is travel. A tutor crossing Al Ain between Zakher and Al Jimi in the late afternoon is giving up a working hour to do it, and that hour is in the rate whether it is itemised or not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Lessons for Al Ain families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The comparison below is the honest case for that choice rather than a dismissal of the alternative. For Higher Level Physics specifically, the deciding factor is the size of the available tutor pool: online, the pool is every Physics HL specialist who can teach at a Gulf Standard Time evening slot, which is a different order of magnitude from those within a 20-minute drive of a particular Al Ain district.

There are genuine advantages on the other side and it is dishonest to pretend otherwise. A younger student who needs supervision as much as teaching is often better served face to face. A student who will not engage with a screen will not learn from one. For a DP2 Physics HL student working through past papers on a shared document with a tutor annotating the same script in real time, the screen is not a compromise; it is a better tool than two people and one piece of paper.

sections.heading: ADEK, the private tutor permit, and how to check your child's tutor is legal
paragraphs: Al Ain sits in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. This is a different authority from Dubai's KHDA, and it matters in practice: inspection reports, policy circulars and staff conduct rules for an Al Ain campus come from ADEK, and a tutoring page that explains Dubai's KHDA framework to an Al Ain parent is explaining the wrong regulator.

Private tutoring itself is regulated federally through MoHRE. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting a figure is guessing.

One Abu Dhabi rule deserves particular attention from Al Ain parents. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported to bar the same thing. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but treat an offer of your child's own classroom teacher for paid private lessons as a question worth asking rather than a convenience. IB Gram holds no ADEK, MoHRE or IB accreditation and claims none; what we can do is tell you what to ask.

sections.heading: If the Physics grade decides a medicine or engineering application
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics is a prerequisite rather than a preference for a large share of engineering courses, and it is a common third subject in science applications. That changes what a tutoring plan is for. A student who needs a 6 to hold an offer is in a different position from one who needs a 4 to pass the Diploma, and the sections of the course worth hours are different. A borderline 5-to-6 student usually gains most from Paper 1B and command-term work; a borderline 3-to-4 student gains most from securing Theme A and Theme B properly.

For students staying in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency process is a separate matter from the university's own entry requirements, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it. For British-track students, the published requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB specifically, no points threshold for equivalency should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one. The published British-track and American-track figures above come from a named news source reporting the Ministry's clarification; the IB figure was not stated there and must be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. Al Ain families applying to United Arab Emirates University, Al Ain University or a capital institution should also read the programme's own entry requirements, which can be stricter than the equivalency floor.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a Physics tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: The Physics course has two components where the boundary matters: the scientific investigation and, for students who choose it, the Physics Extended Essay. Both must be the student's own work, and the school's supervisor signs an authenticity declaration. A tutor who crosses that line exposes the student to an academic misconduct finding, which is a far larger risk than a disappointing mark. Some providers in this market sell completed coursework outright, and that is an IB malpractice trigger, not a service.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. Teach the technique on different data. Ask whether a research question is answerable with the equipment available. Point out that an uncertainty has been propagated inconsistently and teach the rule, so the student can find the rest themselves. Read a student's own draft and say which criterion a paragraph is failing and why. Set practice questions and mark them. All of that is teaching, and all of it is allowed.

What a tutor may not do is produce any part of the submitted work. No text, no graphs built for the student, no rewritten paragraphs returned for pasting, no suggested conclusion the student has not reached from their own data. The practical test we use with students is whether they could explain and defend every sentence to their supervisor without help. If not, it is not their work, and they should not submit it. This boundary is stated to the student in the first session, not discovered at the deadline.

A request that says Physics HL, Theme D, investigation draft due in five weeks gets matched to a different tutor from one that says Physics HL, DP1, predicted grade slipped.

process.title: Matching against the gap we can see
process.description: We match on the named theme and component rather than on general subject coverage, and we say so if the right specialist is not free at the slot you need. A Gulf Standard Time evening slot for Higher Level Physics is the most contested slot in the week, and an honest wait beats a poor match.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, with no card details taken beforehand. The tutor uses it to watch the student attempt two past-paper questions aloud, which is what separates a prerequisite gap from a command-term problem. You get a written summary of what the tutor found whether or not you continue.

process.description: After the trial you receive a plan naming the topics, the number of sessions and what will be different at the end. Block bookings for a single theme or for the investigation have an explicit end date. Open-ended weekly sessions are offered only where the problem genuinely runs across the course.

process.title: Weekly notes and an honest review point
process.description: Notes go to parent and student after each session. At the review point we say whether the plan is working, and if the answer is that the student needs a different tutor or that school support is now enough, we say that instead of extending the booking.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a theme, not to a postcode
whyPoints.description: The constraint on Higher Level Physics tutoring in Al Ain is specialist supply, not distance. Online delivery means the match is made against the HL-only topic your child is stuck on rather than against who can drive to Al Muwaiji by five o'clock on a Tuesday.

whyPoints.title: The investigation treated as 20% of the grade
whyPoints.description: Most support in this market concentrates on the papers because that is what school reports describe. The scientific investigation is a fifth of the grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria, and it is the component where the student controls the conditions. We plan it early rather than rescue it late.

Our own pricing is quoted after the trial against the level and the number of weeks, and the comparison with in-home tutoring is set out with the travel cost shown rather than buried.

whyPoints.description: The investigation and the Extended Essay must be the student's own work. Our tutors teach, question, mark and give criterion-referenced feedback, and they produce no part of a submission. The boundary is explained to the student in the first session.

whyPoints.description: A single-theme repair block runs three to five sessions and then stops. An investigation clinic is four to six hours. Saying so in advance is how a family can tell the difference between support and a subscription.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Physics HL tutoring does an Al Ain student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of three problems you have. A single Higher Level topic that went past too fast, such as induction or thermodynamics, is typically three to five sessions. The scientific investigation is a four-to-six-hour block spread across planning, analysis and drafting. A predicted grade that has slipped across the whole course is a term of weekly sessions, because the repair work sits earlier in the syllabus than the symptom. We say which of the three it is after the trial lesson, and block bookings for the first two carry an agreed finish point rather than rolling on.

faqs.question: Which parts of IB Physics are Higher Level only?
faqs.answer: Under the current guide the Higher Level additions sit in named sub-topics rather than being spread evenly: rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity in Theme A, thermodynamics in Theme B, electromagnetic induction in Theme D, and quantum physics in Theme E, along with extended treatment of interference and the Doppler effect in Theme C. Theme C and Theme D depend heavily on the vector and energy work from Theme A, so a student who joins Higher Level late loses more than a proportional share. Confirm the exact sub-topic list against your school's own scheme of work.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1B worth training separately from the rest of the course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the clearest return on tutoring hours in the final months. Paper 1B asks students to handle unfamiliar experimental data: plot it, linearise it, read a gradient as a physical quantity, propagate uncertainty, and judge whether the data support a relationship. The skill set is small and repeatable, which is why four or five focused sessions move marks. General content revision in the same hours usually moves fewer, because by the spring of DP2 content knowledge is rarely the binding constraint on a Higher Level script.

faqs.question: Why does my child suddenly find Theme D fields impossible?
faqs.answer: Almost always because Theme A was never fully secured. Fields work assumes fluent vector resolution, comfort with inverse-square relationships and the ability to track energy through a system, all taught in the first term of DP1 and all easy to get through with approximations. Theme D does not tolerate approximation. The visible wall is in fields; the actual gap is a year earlier. A diagnostic session that asks the student to attempt a Theme A question aloud usually finds it inside twenty minutes, and fixing it there is faster than re-teaching Theme D repeatedly.

faqs.question: What does the scientific investigation get marked out of?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks, across four criteria carrying six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. The report is capped at 3,000 words, it is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and it carries 20% of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level. Research design is decided before any data exists, which makes it the criterion where early help is worth most. Evaluation is the one UAE students most often lose marks on, because it needs weaknesses specific to this method rather than general statements about human error.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can question whether the research question is answerable with school equipment, teach uncertainty propagation on separate practice data, mark the student's own draft against each criterion, and say which paragraph is failing and why. A tutor cannot supply text, build graphs that go into the report, rewrite paragraphs, or suggest a conclusion the student has not reached from their own data. The test we use with students is whether they could defend every sentence to their school supervisor unaided. If not, it should not be submitted.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Physics tutor to our home in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Ain families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The reason is supply rather than cost: a Higher Level Physics specialist who has taught the current guide and marked investigations against the current criteria is hard to find within driving distance of any single Al Ain district, and online delivery removes distance from the matching problem entirely.

faqs.question: What do in-home Physics tutors in Al Ain charge compared with online?
faqs.answer: Market sources put in-home one-to-one tutoring in the UAE at roughly AED 180-500 an hour depending on level and tutor, with Bestimate's 2026 survey quoting AED 180-350 for general in-home work and specialist IB rates at AED 200-450 and above. Online bands sit lower for comparable qualifications, largely because no travel hour is being paid for. Those are market figures from the providers named, not an IB Gram price list; our own rate is quoted after the free trial against the level and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Is Al Ain under KHDA or a different school regulator?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the Ministry of Education. The distinction matters because inspection reports, policy circulars and staff conduct rules for an Al Ain campus come from ADEK. Any page that explains Dubai's KHDA framework to an Al Ain parent is describing the wrong regulator.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor in Al Ain need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism. Ask any tutor to show the permit.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school Physics teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi emirate this is reported to be prohibited. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported to carry the same restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical position for an Al Ain parent is that an offer of your child's classroom teacher for paid lessons is a question to raise with the school, not a convenience to accept quietly.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the papers. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change a paper grade and not enough to re-teach two years. The plan in that window is built from the student's own marked scripts rather than from a revision sequence: triage the themes into secure, shaky and abandoned, drill Paper 1B data analysis as a separate skill, and work command terms on Paper 2 questions that cross themes. We will tell you honestly if the realistic gain is half a grade rather than two, because buying twenty sessions on a false expectation is worse for the student than buying eight on a true one.

faqs.question: Will the weekly Physics slot still work through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Al Ain families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window moves later in the evening, so the weekly slot usually shifts rather than pausing. Keeping the same tutor across the move matters more than keeping the same hour, because a tutor who has seen a student's scripts for a term does not need to re-diagnose anything. Slots also move for school examination weeks, family travel and the days either side of the eid holidays without losing your place with that tutor.

faqs.question: Does Physics HL affect the Ministry of Education equivalency process?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is run by the Ministry of Education and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it. For British-track students the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page, this one included. Confirm the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning around it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Physics HL specialist is free at the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a general science tutor. The Gulf Standard Time early-evening window is the most contested part of the week for Higher Level sciences, and a Physics HL match sometimes means waiting a week or taking a slightly earlier slot. Where the wait is not workable, the honest options are a different weekday, a weekend session, or starting with the component that is least tutor-specific, such as Paper 1B data technique, while the specialist slot opens up. We will tell you which applies.

al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the deadline that is closest
al-ain/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.closingBody: If you are reading this in DP1, the thing that pays for itself is the investigation: get the research question pressure-tested before any data is collected, and the Research design marks follow. If you are reading it in the spring of DP2, bring your child's last two marked Physics scripts to the trial lesson instead of a list of topics. Tell us the school, the level, the theme that is not working and the next internal deadline, and we will match an IB DP Physics HL tutor against that rather than against a general subject request. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is free with no card details taken.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Programme Psychology at Standard and Higher Level: the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, the option topics, research methodology and the internally assessed experimental study. Al Ain students are matched on level and option choice first, then on a workable evening slot.

intro.heading: Psychology taught against the rules your school actually works under
paragraphs: Almost every page about IB Psychology tuition in the UAE is written as though the UAE were one place with one regulator. It is not. Al Ain sits inside the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which means your child's school is licensed and accredited by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and not by Dubai's KHDA. That distinction changes which inspection report you should be reading, which authority sets the rules on teachers tutoring privately, and which published guidance applies to the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons sitting in your child's timetable next to Psychology.

It also changes the local supply picture. Al Ain is 130 kilometres inland from the capital and its private-school set is small, so Psychology is often a single class covering both Standard and Higher Level, with option topics chosen by the teacher rather than by the student. A Higher Level student needs two option topics, research methodology for the third paper and the Higher Level extensions inside each core approach. In a combined class, some of that gets fewer hours than it needs — not through neglect, but through arithmetic.

Psychology is also the Diploma subject most often chosen by students who expect it to be easier than it is. It reads approachably, it has no mathematics at Standard Level beyond descriptive statistics, and the content is genuinely interesting. Then the first assessed essay comes back with a 3, because the student wrote everything they knew about a study instead of answering the command term in the question. That failure is specific, diagnosable and entirely fixable, and it is what most of the sessions on this page are spent on.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Al Ain that is the format that works rather than a compromise: it puts a Psychology specialist who has marked these essays in front of your child without anyone driving to the capital, and it keeps a weekly slot alive through a term instead of collapsing the first time the school run runs late.

What follows is the version of this subject anchored to this emirate rather than to a generic UAE. Who regulates your school and what their published report actually means for a tuition decision. Which Al Ain campuses run the subject, at which levels, and how a combined Standard and Higher Level class changes what gets taught thoroughly. The assessed components and the command terms that decide the grade more often than content does. The experimental study from design approval to submission, counted backwards from the school's own internal deadline. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons that sit alongside the Diploma and quietly eat the evenings a revision plan assumed were free. The Ministry of Education equivalency route for a student heading to a UAE university, with the figures we can source and a plain statement of the one figure we will not publish. And the market rate in AED, with the date it was read and the source named, because a price without a method behind it helps nobody choose.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology exists only at Diploma level in the IB, but the route into it starts earlier and the exit route runs through equivalency and university admission. These are the stages that matter for an Al Ain family, with what each one means in this emirate specifically.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no MYP Psychology, so the feeders are Individuals and Societies and the MYP sciences. What transfers is the ability to use evidence to support a claim and the habit of writing to a criterion rather than to a word count. What does not transfer is essay discipline under a command term, because MYP marking is far more forgiving of a student who writes everything they know.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the MYP and DP cohorts are often substantially the same group of students moving up through one small campus, so a year group that was never pushed on evidence-based writing in Individuals and Societies arrives in DP1 Psychology with the same habit intact. Ask the school which MYP subject your child's Psychology teacher also teaches; the answer frequently explains the house style of the marking.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: DP1 covers the three approaches to behaviour — biological, cognitive and sociocultural — plus research methodology and ethical considerations. The experimental study is usually designed and run late in DP1 or across the summer. A student who finishes DP1 able to recite studies but unable to evaluate them has done the easier half of the year.
programmes.countryNote: The Al Ain academic year runs roughly September to late June with a long July and August break. For Psychology that break is the natural window for the experimental study, because running a replication needs participants and time that term weeks do not give. Families travelling for most of the summer should have the design approved before they leave rather than after they return.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, second year
programmes.description: DP2 adds the option topics, the Higher Level extensions and, for Higher Level students, the research methodology paper built on an unseen abridged study. The experimental study report is finished and submitted, mocks are sat, and the final term is essay technique against the published criteria rather than new content.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain students sit the May session. Internal coursework deadlines are set by the school's Diploma coordinator and sit months before the papers because teachers need time to mark, moderate and upload. Get those dates in writing from the coordinator rather than from the student, and treat them as the real deadlines in any plan.

programmes.name: Higher Level Psychology
programmes.description: Higher Level adds a second option topic, the Higher Level extension content inside each core approach, and a paper on research methodology that presents an unseen abridged study and asks about its design, ethics and conclusions. That paper rewards a student who has read real studies critically all year, and punishes one who has only memorised the prescribed ones.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is one of very few Higher Level Psychology students in an Al Ain cohort, ask the coordinator how many weekly hours the second option topic and the research methodology paper receive. Combined-level classes in small schools tend to teach the shared core thoroughly and compress the Higher Level additions, and that compression is exactly where one-to-one time pays.

al-ain/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is the subject on this page. These are the Diploma subjects our tutors cover for Al Ain students, described by what the assessment actually rewards rather than by what the syllabus contains.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, one or two option topics, research methodology and the experimental study. Marks are lost on command terms ignored, on studies described rather than used as evidence, and on evaluation that lists strengths and weaknesses without connecting them to the claim being argued.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual partner for a Psychology student heading towards medicine or neuroscience. The overlap with the biological approach is real — localisation, neurotransmission, hormones — but Biology's assessment demands far more precision in terminology and far more care with data analysis.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Shares Psychology's essay structure and its need for real-world application, and the behavioural economics content overlaps directly with cognitive biases. Students who evaluate well in one subject usually transfer the skill, which makes a shared tutor efficient where the timetable allows.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Motivation theory, organisational culture and leadership overlap with the sociocultural approach. The assessment rewards application to a named organisation rather than theory recall, which trains the same discipline the Psychology essays need.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Another group 3 subject Al Ain schools commonly pair with Psychology. The written papers reward precise use of case studies and data, and students who can structure a Psychology essay generally structure a Geography one well once the command terms are mapped across.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The subject that most often limits a Psychology student's total, because Paper 1 is an unseen text under time pressure and the Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen months ahead. Both reward planning rather than flair.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content is directly useful to the experimental study: sampling, measures of central tendency, dispersion and the logic of inferential testing. Students doing Psychology and this course together tend to write stronger analysis sections.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside any international curriculum in UAE private schools under federal rules. These are separate from the Diploma and marked by the school, but they occupy timetable space and homework time that a Psychology revision plan has to work around.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Psychology is a popular Extended Essay subject and a natural source of Theory of Knowledge examples, because the subject's own debates about evidence and method are knowledge questions already. Support is teaching, feedback and process coaching on the student's own work only.

sections.heading: ADEK, not KHDA: what your regulator actually changes
paragraphs: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so your child's private school is regulated by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's KHDA has no authority here. This matters practically rather than academically: the inspection report you should be reading is ADEK's, the fee approval route is ADEK's, and the professional-conduct rules that apply to your child's own Psychology teacher are Abu Dhabi's.

That last point is worth knowing before you ask the school for private help. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff indicates that teachers are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact current wording, and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it. The practical consequence is simple: the obvious solution of paying your child's own teacher is the one route that is likely closed.

The regulator map across the UAE is five bodies, not one, and no competitor page in this market sets it out. Dubai has KHDA, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi, and therefore Al Ain, has ADEK. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has the Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum approval sits with the regulator and not only inspection.

None of this is bureaucratic trivia for a parent choosing tuition. It tells you whose published report to read when judging a school, whose rules constrain who may legally teach your child privately, and which authority to contact when something goes wrong. All of it comes from the federal portal at u.ae, which is the source to check rather than any tutoring company's summary of it.

sections.heading: Which Al Ain schools run Psychology, and how it is usually staffed
paragraphs: Psychology is a group 3 option, and in a city with a small private-school set that makes it a departmental decision rather than a guaranteed offering. Some Al Ain campuses run it at both levels. Some run a single combined class. Some do not offer it at all and steer students into Geography or Business Management. Before you look for a tutor, establish from the Diploma coordinator which levels are actually running for your child's cohort, which option topics the department has chosen, and how many weekly contact hours the Higher Level additions receive.

The combined-level class is the pattern worth understanding, because it produces a predictable gap. The three core approaches are shared between Standard and Higher Level, so a combined class teaches them to everybody and teaches them well. What gets compressed is the Higher Level-only material: the second option topic, the extension content inside each approach, and the research methodology paper. In a class of fifteen with four Higher Level students, that compression is a timetabling fact rather than a failure of teaching.

The option topics are the second thing to pin down. A Standard Level student studies one option; a Higher Level student studies two. Which options your child's school has chosen determines what revision material is relevant, and a tutor working from the wrong option wastes the term. Abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and human relationships each carry their own studies, their own debates and their own typical essay questions, and they are not interchangeable.

Finally, ask how the experimental study is organised. Some departments assign a narrow menu of replicable studies to keep the process manageable; others let students propose their own and then spend weeks rescuing undeliverable designs. Knowing which model your school uses tells you whether the support you need is design help in DP1 or analysis and write-up help later.

sections.heading: The assessed components and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Diploma Psychology is assessed through written papers plus one internally assessed experimental study. Standard Level students sit papers on the core and on one option, alongside the experimental study. Higher Level students sit the core paper, a paper covering two options and an additional paper on research methodology, alongside the same experimental study. Exact durations and component weightings are published in the subject guide your child's cohort follows, so confirm them with the Diploma coordinator before a revision plan is built on them.

The core paper is the one most students underestimate. It mixes short answers requiring tight, controlled responses with an extended response demanding a sustained argument. Short answers fail when a student writes an essay; extended responses fail when a student writes a list. Both failures come from the same root, which is not reading the command term and not planning the shape of the answer before writing.

The options paper rewards depth over breadth. A student who knows four studies well in a single option outperforms one who knows twelve superficially, because the marks sit in how the evidence is used rather than in how much is cited. The Higher Level research methodology paper is different in kind: it presents an unseen abridged study and asks about its design, ethics and conclusions, which rewards a student who has spent the year reading studies critically rather than memorising them.

The experimental study is the only component entirely within the student's control. It is a report on a replication of a simple published experiment, assessed against published criteria, and the commonest failures are a design too ambitious to deliver, ethical considerations treated as a paragraph of boilerplate, and an evaluation that lists limitations without explaining what each one does to the conclusion.

sections.heading: The command terms that decide a Psychology grade
paragraphs: More Psychology marks are lost to command terms than to missing content. The question tells the student exactly what kind of answer is wanted, and a student who writes a good answer to a different question gets credit for almost none of it. Outline wants a brief account. Describe wants a detailed account without judgement. Explain wants reasons and causes. Discuss wants a balanced review of the arguments. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by evidence on both sides. Contrast wants differences made explicit rather than two separate descriptions placed side by side.

The diagnostic is quick and you can run it at home. Take your child's last marked essay and ask them, without looking, what the command term in the question was. A student who cannot say is a student whose essays will keep scoring in the middle regardless of how much they revise, because the revision adds content to an answer whose shape was wrong. This is the single highest-return thing tuition fixes in this subject, and it usually takes weeks rather than terms.

Evaluation is where it bites hardest. Students are taught to produce strengths and weaknesses, so they produce a list: the sample was small, the setting was artificial, the study was ethically questionable. None of that scores well on its own. What scores is connecting the limitation to the claim: if the sample was twenty undergraduates in one country, say what that does to the generalisation the student has just made. The difference between those two answers is often two grades.

The second recurring failure is the study used as decoration. A named study dropped into a paragraph without being tied to the argument reads as recall. The habit worth building is one sentence of claim, one of evidence from a named study, one of what that evidence does to the claim. Practising that three-sentence unit on unfamiliar questions is more useful than rereading notes, and it is what timed practice in the final term should mostly consist of.

sections.heading: The experimental study, from design to submission
paragraphs: The experimental study is a report on a replication of a simple published experiment, and almost every problem with it is created at the design stage. A student who picks a study requiring specialist equipment, a large sample or a sensitive population has chosen a project that cannot be delivered inside an Al Ain school term, and the weeks spent discovering that are weeks taken from the write-up. The useful discipline is to test the design against four questions before any data is collected: can the participants be recruited, can the procedure be standardised, can the data be analysed with the statistics the student knows, and is it ethically defensible.

Ethics is not a paragraph to be added at the end. Informed consent, the right to withdraw, debriefing, protection from harm and the handling of data about minors all have to be thought through before the study runs, and in a school setting the participants are frequently other students. A report where the ethical considerations clearly came after the data is visible to a marker in a sentence, and it loses marks it never needed to lose.

A tutor's role here has a hard boundary and we state it at the first session. A tutor may explain the published criteria, challenge whether a design is deliverable, teach the statistics, question whether an evaluation actually connects to the conclusion, and read a draft and say where evidence is missing. A tutor may not design the study, analyse the data on the student's behalf or rewrite the report. The experimental study is assessed as the student's own research, and anything else puts the diploma at risk under IB academic-honesty rules rather than merely being against our policy.

Count the plan backwards from the school's internal deadline rather than forwards from today. Subtract a fortnight that belongs to the student for final checking, then the write-up, the analysis, the data collection and the design approval. For most Al Ain cohorts the design needs approving inside DP1, which is why the long summer matters: it is the only block of time in two years when a student can run a replication without a timetable in the way.
