al-ain/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Which option suits a family depends partly on which programme the student is in, because the three IB programmes make different demands on continuity and on subject specialism. A Primary Years child and a Diploma Higher Level candidate are not shopping in the same market even when the parent types the same phrase into Google.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: At primary level the subject specialism required is modest and the supervision requirement is high, which is the one case where a visiting adult has a genuine advantage: a seven-year-old needs someone physically turning pages. What primary children actually need is reading fluency, number facts held in memory and the habit of recording a method, none of which requires a Diploma specialist. A university student at the lower market band, properly permitted, is often the sensible match here.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain this is the one segment where the local pool is adequate, because the requirement is general rather than specialist and the city has a large student population around the United Arab Emirates University. Families in Asharej in particular find visiting primary tutors easily. The comparison on this page matters much less at this level, and we say so rather than arguing for video where it adds nothing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years marks four criteria per subject from one to eight, and the help a student needs is usually in one criterion rather than across a subject. That is specialist work in a narrow band: knowing what criterion C rewards in a science investigation is not general teaching knowledge. The pool of people who know a given subject's criteria properly is smaller than the pool who know the subject, which starts to favour choosing on expertise rather than on proximity.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools run Middle Years and a British Year 10 and 11 stream in the same building, so a visiting tutor who covers one may be assumed to cover the other. They are different assessment systems with different mark schemes. Asking directly which of the two a candidate has taught, and for how many cohorts, separates the two groups quickly and is a question worth putting to any of the four options.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the comparison tilts hardest. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, externally marked papers in May and internally assessed work spread across two years: this is the point at which a generalist stops being useful and a subject specialist at the right level becomes the whole value of the hour. Continuity over two years matters as much as specialism, because a tutor who has held the record since the first year knows what was repaired and what is next.
programmes.countryNote: The number of adults resident in Al Ain who can teach Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry or Economics at Diploma depth is small, and those few are sought by every family in the city at the same hour of the same weekday. That is the structural reason a visiting arrangement at this level is hard to secure and harder to keep. Removing the travel radius changes the pool from a city to a timezone.

programmes.name: The Diploma core
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service sit outside the six subjects and together carry up to three bonus points, with failing conditions that can cost the whole Diploma. Core support is episodic rather than weekly: a block of sessions around a research question, then another around a draft. That shape suits booked blocks far better than a standing weekly visit, whichever option a family chooses.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's smaller supervisor pool means an Extended Essay in a specialised field may be supervised by a teacher outside it, which is where independent subject review earns its place. The boundary must be explicit under any option: review, challenge and criterion explanation are legitimate, and supplying any part of a text that will be assessed is not. We put that in writing before a core block starts.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subject list below is ordered by how hard each one is to staff with someone resident in Al Ain, because that is the variable the four-way comparison actually turns on. Where the local pool is adequate the options are genuinely close. Where it is thin, proximity stops being a feature and becomes the thing limiting your choice.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The hardest Diploma subject to staff locally in Al Ain, and the one families most often settle for a generalist in. Higher Level carries additional content and an extra paper, and the data-analysis questions need practice with uncertainty and gradients. A tutor who teaches Middle Years science well is not automatically able to teach Higher Level fields and circuits.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics drive the requests; stoichiometry and multi-step calculation reading is where marks are most reliably recovered. The internal assessment needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen early. Local availability at Higher Level is thin, and a chemistry teacher comfortable at IGCSE depth is a different proposition from one comfortable at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the course, and Higher Level rewards moving between algebraic and graphical arguments at speed. Marks are lost in unjustified steps rather than wrong answers. This is the subject where parents most often compare a nearby maths tutor against a distant specialist, and where the two are least interchangeable at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and assumed calculator fluency define this route. Students who crossed from a Middle Years course are often procedurally sound but unused to interpreting output in context. Higher Level adds statistical inference that cannot be absorbed late. Confirm which of the two maths routes a candidate has actually taught; many have taught only one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with recall structure rather than understanding as the usual limiting factor. Extended responses need command-term discipline, since explain, outline and evaluate reward different things. Local availability is better than for physics and chemistry, so for biology the four options sit closer together than this page's general argument suggests.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment commentaries decide most grades. Marks go on diagrams that do not match the article and on evaluation that lists both sides without judging. Higher Level adds quantitative content. Economics specialists are scarce in Al Ain specifically, which is why this subject appears so often in requests that begin as a search for a visiting tutor.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Upper-band answers apply a named framework to a given organisation rather than describing it. The Higher Level research project needs its scope agreed early and real data available. Business is more widely taught than economics, so the local pool is deeper, though at Higher Level the research project still rewards someone who has supervised one before.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed orals and a paper on unseen non-literary texts make this a skills course with a reading list attached. The individual oral rewards preparation because the student chooses the extract and the global issue. Availability in Al Ain is reasonable, but experience with the current assessment model rather than an older one is the question to ask.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Al Ain asks for Arabic more often than most UAE cities, and the route matters: Arabic A is language and literature for first-language speakers, Arabic B an acquisition course with a different structure. Matching the wrong route wastes a term. Local first-language teaching capacity is good; capacity for the Diploma assessment model specifically is narrower.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The programming solution dominates the internal assessment and documents badly when nobody has supervised one before. Paper questions on data structures and system fundamentals need taught content rather than coding practice. Among the thinnest subjects locally, and one where a nearby enthusiast and an experienced Diploma teacher are not close substitutes.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be recalled precisely and deployed as evidence rather than retold, and the internal assessment is a replication with strict reporting conventions. Requested steadily in Al Ain and almost never available locally at Diploma level, which makes it a clear case where the radius is the constraint rather than the budget.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Because three of the four options involve somebody driving, the district a family lives in changes the comparison directly. The notes below describe each area in terms of what a visiting arrangement would actually require there, which is the detail a general tutoring page tends to skip.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central, dense and close to several long-established campuses, so a visiting tutor can plausibly fit two households in one evening. This is the district where in-home arrangements work best in Al Ain, and where the price gap between options is therefore the smallest.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Villa district by the oasis and the main hospital, with many medical and university households on shift patterns. A visiting tutor needs a time that survives a changing rota, which is exactly the kind of arrangement that breaks after a month of rescheduling.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: Beside the United Arab Emirates University campus, so the local pool of available adults is unusually large at primary and lower-secondary level. For Diploma Higher Level that pool is no deeper here than anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Established area where British and Indian curriculum timetables often run in one household. Two siblings on different boards usually need two specialists, and expecting one visiting tutor to cover both is the most common way these arrangements disappoint.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Large villa neighbourhood with a strong Emirati household share, where Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education sit alongside Diploma subjects. Scheduling has to avoid the school's own Arabic support sessions, which tightens the window a visiting tutor could use.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: West of the centre, with a longer return from the city-edge campuses. A visiting tutor arriving at five-thirty has to leave by six-thirty to reach a second household, which caps the session at a length that often does not suit Higher Level work.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: Southern edge towards Jebel Hafeet, with the city's longest school commute for children at central campuses. A visiting tutor here is effectively giving up their whole evening for one session, and the rate quoted reflects that honestly.

regions.name: Hili and Al Foah
regions.note: Northern districts out towards the border crossing. The daily drive is the longest in Al Ain, and a second journey in the evening is what most families here are specifically trying to avoid when they start comparing options.

regions.name: Al Khabisi and Al Maqam
regions.note: Inner districts with short runs to the central schools and a mix of apartments and villas. Two subjects in one evening is a common request, which works under any option provided the two tutors share one note rather than each starting from scratch.

schoolClusters.city: Central Al Ain campuses
schoolClusters.note: Schools in and around Al Jimi, Al Mutaredh and Al Towayya. Students we support from these campuses are the ones most likely to have had a visiting arrangement first, usually ended by a scheduling clash rather than by the teaching.

schoolClusters.note: Campuses towards Asharej, Zakher and the Abu Dhabi road, where the evening drive is long in both directions. Requests from this cluster skew towards Diploma Higher Level sciences, which is also where the resident specialist pool is thinnest.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.modesIntro: IB Gram offers three session shapes to Al Ain families, all of them delivered live over video. They are listed here so that the comparison on this page is against something specific rather than against a vague notion of online tutoring, which is how most provider comparisons are written.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one in one subject
modes.description: A standing slot in the same subject with the same tutor, set against the hour your child is genuinely home and able to work. The tutor holds a running record of what the school has covered and what deadlines are ahead, so sessions start from the current week. This is the direct equivalent of the visiting-tutor arrangement most families begin by looking for, minus the travel component in the price.

modes.title: Paired siblings, back to back
modes.description: Two children in one household booked consecutively on the same evening, each with their own tutor and their own hour, sharing one quiet room. This is how the per-household cost is reduced without putting two students of different ages in the same lesson, which is what a centre group class effectively does and which rarely suits either of them.

sections.heading: What an Al Ain parent actually means by a home tutor
paragraphs: Three different requests hide behind the same phrase. The first is literal: an adult in the house, sitting next to the student. The second is locational: tuition that happens at home rather than requiring a trip to a centre. The third is practical: one-to-one attention at a time the family chooses, with no second car journey after a long school day. Only the first requires anybody to drive anywhere, and it is the least common of the three once parents are asked directly.

That distinction decides the whole comparison. If the requirement is the second or third meaning, live video satisfies it and the hourly figure drops by the travel component, while the pool of possible tutors expands from people living in Al Ain to people available at that hour anywhere. If the requirement is genuinely the first, then the comparison on this page should push you towards a local visiting arrangement, and we would rather say that than sell you something else.

IB Gram provides the online version to UAE families. We do not sell home visits in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India, where the operating model is different. So the honest framing of this page is not that one option is better, but that for a Diploma student in Al Ain needing a Higher Level specialist, the local supply is small enough that proximity and specialism are usually in direct conflict, and most families, once they see the trade clearly, choose the specialist.
bullets: Literal meaning: an adult physically present, which only a local visit provides
Locational meaning: tuition at home rather than at a centre, which video satisfies
Practical meaning: one-to-one at our chosen time with no second journey
Ask yourself which of the three you actually need before comparing prices

sections.heading: Option one: the visiting tutor who lives nearby
paragraphs: The visiting tutor is the default mental model and it has real advantages. A person in the room can see a student's working as it happens, can take a phone away, and can read the body language that tells an experienced teacher when someone has stopped following. For younger children and for students who genuinely will not engage without physical supervision, that is worth paying for and worth the logistics.

The costs are equally real and tend to be understated at the point of agreement. Published in-home rates in this market run from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Travel time sits inside that figure. In a city where districts are twenty to thirty minutes apart in evening traffic, a tutor giving a sixty-minute lesson in Zakher has committed two hours of their evening, and the rate reflects that whether or not it is itemised.

The structural limit is the pool. Only someone living in or near Al Ain can take the booking, and they must be free at the hour your child is home. For Diploma Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science or Psychology, the number of Al Ain residents who meet both conditions is very small, and the usual outcome is not a long wait but a quiet substitution: the family accepts a capable generalist instead, and nobody describes the compromise out loud.

sections.heading: Option two: the tuition centre and its group class
paragraphs: Centres occupy a different part of the market and they are frequently the cheapest option per hour, because the cost is divided across a group. For some students that works well: a motivated child who needs structure, pace and the company of others revising the same paper can do better in a group of four than one-to-one, and the social accountability is genuinely useful during an exam term.

What a group cannot do is run at one student's speed. If the gap is two absent syllabus topics in Higher Level Chemistry, a class covering the scheme of work will not stop for them, and the student spends the hour watching content they already have. Group size is the variable that decides this, and it is worth asking for the actual number rather than the advertised maximum, along with how the group is split by level, since Standard and Higher Level students in one room get a compromise aimed at neither.

A centre is also a different legal animal from an individual tutor. An operation with premises and staff is a business, and in Dubai that means a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and an annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. Al Ain centres answer to ADEK as the Emirate of Abu Dhabi's regulator for private education, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The point for a parent is simply that a centre should be able to answer a direct question about its own permissions, and an individual arriving at a villa should be able to answer the equivalent question about theirs.

sections.heading: Option three: a teacher from your child's own school
paragraphs: This is the option families raise most often and the one most quickly closed. The appeal is obvious: the teacher knows the scheme of work, sets the assessments and knows the student. The difficulty is that the same facts create a conflict of interest, and Abu Dhabi has addressed it directly.

Reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff states that teachers are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document itself, so a family relying on it should verify the current wording with the school or with ADEK directly. The direction of the rule, though, is not in doubt.

What this means practically is that a parent should not ask, and a school should not facilitate, paid tutoring by a child's own subject teacher in Abu Dhabi emirate, which includes Al Ain. A teacher from a different school is a different matter and may be entirely proper, provided they hold the permit. We never market access to a student's own teacher, and a provider who offers that in this emirate is offering something a parent should question rather than buy. The second reason to avoid it is less often discussed: a teacher paid privately by one family in a class they also mark is in an impossible position when that class is assessed, and the student carries the consequences of any suspicion raised later.
bullets: Reported ADEK ethics rules bar paid tutoring of a teacher's own enrolled students
The MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction

sections.heading: Option four: live one-to-one over video, and what it changes
paragraphs: The fourth option keeps the one-to-one attention and the at-home convenience and removes the travel. What that buys is not primarily money, although the hourly band is lower. It buys the pool. A student in Al Maqam can work with a Higher Level Physics specialist without anyone calculating whether a round trip from the city centre at six in the evening is worth the fee, which means the match is made on subject and level rather than on geography.

It also buys the honest hour. A visiting tutor who must reach a second household has a hard stop; a video session can sit at six-thirty or seven, which in Zakher, Hili and Al Muwaiji is when a student is actually home and able to concentrate. Sessions move rather than cancel during Ramadan, usually to after Iftar, and they survive a family's travel because only the clock changes. Those three things together are why online arrangements in this city last longer than visiting ones, in our experience of the ones that replace them.

What it does not do should be stated plainly too. A tutor on a screen cannot confiscate a phone, cannot make a reluctant nine-year-old sit still, and cannot run a chemistry practical. For practical work the honest position is that an online tutor teaches the technique, the data analysis and the alternative-to-practical question types, while the practical itself happens at school. Where a family needs physical presence, option one is the right answer and we will say so.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This is the question almost no comparison asks, and it applies equally to all four options. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the published eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service for issuing a new private tutor work permit, which lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so no amount appears on this page.

For a parent the practical step is one sentence in a first message: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? A permitted tutor answers without hesitation. The question is free to ask, it costs a permitted tutor nothing to answer, and asking it of every option, including a platform, is a reasonable standard rather than an accusation. IB Gram holds no permit or accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not claim one.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic in a city this spread out
paragraphs: Al Ain is not a dense city, and that single fact drives most of the price difference between the options. From Zakher in the south to Hili and Al Foah in the north is a substantial drive, and the central schools pull children from every direction at the same time of day. A tutor crossing the city for one sixty-minute lesson spends most of an evening on it, and prices accordingly.

Run the numbers for a two-subject household. Two visiting lessons a week in different subjects means two tutors making two round trips, and the realistic slots will be whatever suits their routes rather than whatever suits your evening. The same two subjects over video can be booked back to back from six o'clock, with two specialists who never meet, in one quiet room. The practical saving is not just the fee; it is that both sessions actually happen in the same week, every week, which is what produces a result.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. Because a visiting arrangement is expensive per hour, families buy fewer hours and buy them later, usually once a mock result has already arrived. Because the online band is lower, the same budget buys a weekly slot through the first Diploma year, which is the stage where an hour does the most good. The format therefore changes not only the price of an hour but the stage at which a family can afford to start, and starting earlier is the single largest cost saving available in this market.

sections.heading: A six-question test that separates the four options
paragraphs: Rather than ranking the options, work through six questions about your own household. First: does your child need physical supervision to work at all? If yes, option one, and the rest of this page is interesting rather than useful. Second: is the subject a Higher Level science, mathematics at Higher Level, economics, computer science or psychology? If yes, the resident pool in Al Ain is thin and proximity will cost you specialism.

Third: what time is your child genuinely home, able to eat and then concentrate? If the honest answer is after six, a visiting arrangement in an outer district is hard to sustain. Fourth: how long do you expect to need this, one term or two years? Continuity favours whichever option you can keep, and a cheaper arrangement that collapses in February is not cheaper. Fifth: can every candidate, under any option, answer the permit question?

Sixth, and most often skipped: what is the coursework boundary, written down? Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, and a tutor's role is to teach, question and explain criteria. Any provider or individual who offers more than that on assessed work is offering the student a malpractice risk, and that risk sits with the student rather than with the tutor. Ask the question in writing and keep the answer, whichever of the four options you choose. Taken together the six answers usually point at one option rather than two, and they point there for reasons a parent can explain to a sceptical spouse, which is more than can be said for choosing on a recommendation at the school gate.

process.title: Decide which of the three meanings you need
process.description: Tell us whether you need a person physically present, tuition that happens at home, or one-to-one at a time you choose. The first points to a local visiting arrangement and we will say so. The second and third are what we deliver, and knowing which it is saves a conversation that otherwise takes a week.

process.title: Name the subject and the level precisely
process.description: Higher Level or Standard, which maths route, which board for a sibling on a different system. Precision here decides whether the match is a specialist or a generalist, and in Al Ain that distinction matters more than in Abu Dhabi or Dubai because the resident pool is smaller.

process.title: Ask us the permit question
process.description: Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and ask the same of every other option you are considering. It is free to obtain, valid for two years, and a permitted tutor will answer at once. Treat hesitation from anyone, including us, as information.

process.title: Trial the match against the alternative
process.description: One lesson at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. Run it in the same week you trial a local option if you can, because comparing two real sessions tells you more than comparing two descriptions. Then choose on evidence rather than on format.

process.title: Set the slot and write the boundaries down
process.description: Fix the weekly time against your child's real arrival home, and agree in writing what the tutor may do with coursework. Those two documents, a time and a boundary, are what make an arrangement last past February. They take ten minutes and they prevent the two failures we see most.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is written down, not implied
whyPoints.description: Most provider pages compare themselves against an unnamed alternative. This one names four models, gives the published rate bands with their sources, and states where another option fits a family better. For a primary-age child needing physical supervision, that option is not us.

whyPoints.title: No radius on the match
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science and Psychology are the subjects Al Ain is thinnest in. Matching over video removes the travel constraint entirely, so the choice is made on subject and level rather than on who happens to live within a twenty-minute drive.

whyPoints.title: Slots set to this city's evenings
whyPoints.description: A six or six-thirty start in Zakher, Hili or Al Muwaiji is normal for us and impossible for a tutor with a second household to reach. Sessions move to after Iftar during Ramadan rather than pausing, and they follow a family through travel because only the clock changes.

whyPoints.title: The permit question asked in both directions
whyPoints.description: We ask tutors for the MoHRE private tuition work permit and we tell parents to ask us, and every other provider, the same thing. We also state what we do not hold: no accreditation or approval from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries in writing
whyPoints.description: Before any block on an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, the boundary is agreed in writing. Review, challenge and criterion explanation are in scope. Supplying text that will be assessed is not, under any deadline. The malpractice risk sits with the student, which is why this is non-negotiable.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what video cannot do
whyPoints.description: A tutor on a screen cannot take a phone away, cannot settle a reluctant young child, and cannot run a practical. We teach practical technique, data analysis and the alternative-to-practical question types; the practical itself happens at school. Where presence is the requirement, a local arrangement is the better answer.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we provide only in India, where the operating model is different. What we offer Al Ain families is live one-to-one tuition over video, which satisfies the two meanings most parents actually have in mind: tuition at home rather than at a centre, and one-to-one at a time you choose with no second journey. If what you need is genuinely an adult physically present in the room, a local visiting arrangement is the right answer, and this page sets out what that market charges so you can judge it fairly.

faqs.question: What does a visiting IB tutor in Al Ain charge once travel is included?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in this market run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. Bestimate's 2026 rate table gives AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500. Travel sits inside that figure rather than beside it, which matters in Al Ain because the districts are far apart: a tutor giving one hour in Zakher has committed most of an evening. Ask whether the quoted rate assumes a particular district, because a figure set for a central Al Jimi household often rises for the outer areas. These are other providers' published bands, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: How big is the pool of IB Higher Level tutors living in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Smaller than most families expect, and that is the single most important fact in this comparison. Al Ain has far fewer IB World Schools than Abu Dhabi island, so the number of adults resident here who teach Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science or Psychology at Diploma depth is genuinely small. Those same few people are sought by every family in the city at roughly the same hour of the same weekday. The usual outcome is not a long wait but a quiet substitution to a capable generalist, which nobody describes out loud at the time and which shows up in the second year.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class a reasonable substitute for one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is often the cheapest option per hour. A motivated student who needs pace, structure and the company of others working the same paper can do better in a small group than alone, and the accountability helps through an exam term. What a group cannot do is stop for one student's two missing topics. Ask for the actual group size rather than the advertised maximum, and ask how groups are split by level, because Standard and Higher Level students in one room receive a compromise aimed at neither. For narrow content repair, one-to-one is the format that works.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored privately by a teacher from their own school?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi emirate, which includes Al Ain, you should not pursue this. Reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff states that teachers are barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction. That reporting should be checked against the current policy document, but the direction of the rule is clear. A teacher from a different school is a separate matter and may be entirely proper, provided they hold the permit. We never market access to a child's own teacher.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi emirate need a permit, and who issues it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories published by the authorities include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application route is the Ministry's own private tutor licensing service, which states a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor arriving at my door is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask one direct question in your first message: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Because the permit is free and takes two working days to issue, a working tutor has no good reason not to hold one, and a permitted tutor will answer immediately. Ask the same question of a centre about its own business permissions, and of any platform, including this one. The question costs nothing, and hesitation in response to it is useful information. Do not accept a general claim of being licensed as a substitute for the document itself.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an agency, a marketplace and a freelance tutor?
faqs.answer: An agency selects the tutor for you, holds the relationship and usually handles replacement, at a higher price. A marketplace lists many tutors and leaves selection, vetting and continuity to you, at a lower price and with more variance. A freelance tutor found by word of mouth is the cheapest per hour and carries the whole risk in one person: if they relocate, the arrangement ends that week. The relevant question is not which model is best but who carries the risk of a wrong match, and whether anything happens when the match is wrong.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not send tutors to homes in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Because the model would make the service worse for the families we serve here. Sending someone to a villa means the tutor must live within reach of that villa and be free at that hour, which in Al Ain reduces the pool for scarce Higher Level subjects to a handful of people. Online matching removes that constraint and lets a student in Al Maqam work with a Higher Level Physics specialist on a weekday evening. In-home tuition is a service we run in India, where the density and the operating model are different, and we do not claim it in the UAE.

faqs.question: Does an online lesson lose the things a home visit gives you?
faqs.answer: It loses three things honestly. A tutor on a screen cannot take a phone away, cannot settle a reluctant younger child, and cannot run a practical experiment. For practical work the position is that the tutor teaches technique, data handling and the alternative-to-practical question types, while the practical itself happens at school. What is not lost is seeing a student's working: a shared screen, a document camera or a photographed page shows a method as clearly as sitting beside someone. For a motivated secondary student the difference is small; for a distractible eight-year-old it is not.

faqs.question: What happens to a home-tutor arrangement when the tutor moves away?
faqs.answer: It ends, usually with little notice, and that is a real cost of a single-person arrangement in a city with a mobile expatriate population. The replacement search starts from nothing, the new tutor repeats a diagnosis the family has already paid for, and a term's continuity is lost at whatever point in the year it happens. Continuity is worth money in a two-year Diploma: a tutor who has held the record since the first year knows what was repaired and what deadline is next. Ask any provider, under any option, what actually happens if the person stops being available.

faqs.question: Which of the four options is cheapest over a full Diploma year?
faqs.answer: On published bands, a centre group class is cheapest per hour, live one-to-one over video sits next at the AED 150 to 300 qualified-tutor band, and a visiting tutor is most expensive at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Over a year, though, the bigger variable is when a family starts. A lower hourly rate that allows a weekly slot from the first Diploma term usually costs less in total than a higher rate bought late, because the late purchase buys specialist hours under deadline pressure. The expensive decision is rarely the tier; it is the delay.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share a session to bring the cost down?
faqs.answer: Not in the same hour, in our view, unless they are in the same subject at the same level and roughly the same position, which is rare. What works is consecutive slots on one evening: each child gets their own tutor and their own hour, and one quiet room covers both. That halves the household's logistical load without giving either child a lesson aimed at the other. In villa districts where study space is contested, the shared-room arrangement is often the real constraint, and sequencing solves it better than combining.

faqs.question: How do we trial each option before committing to one?
faqs.answer: Run them in the same fortnight if you can. Ask a local visiting tutor for a first session, ask a centre for a trial class, and take a trial lesson with us, which is at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. Then compare what each produced rather than what each promised: did the tutor identify something specific, did they name the syllabus topics at issue, and did they say what the next six weeks would contain? Two real sessions tell you more than ten descriptions. Nobody should expect a family to choose a format blind.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor need to be told my child's school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Any tutor does, under any option, and surprisingly often nobody passes them on. Internal assessment dates, mock windows and Extended Essay checkpoints are set by the school's own departments, and a tutor working without them plans against a generic calendar rather than your child's. Write every internal deadline on one page at the start of the year and give a copy to whoever teaches your child privately. A tutor who does not ask for that list within the first two sessions is working from a template, which is worth noticing early rather than in February.

faqs.question: What should be written down before any tutoring arrangement starts?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they take ten minutes. The weekly time, set against when your child is genuinely home rather than when school ends. What happens if a session is missed by either side. And the coursework boundary: that internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are the student's own work, that the tutor teaches, questions and explains criteria, and that no text which will be assessed comes from the tutor. That last point protects the student, because an academic-honesty breach is a malpractice matter for the candidate rather than for the person who caused it.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Choose the option, then choose the tutor
al-ain/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: The useful order is the one most families reverse. Decide first whether you need physical presence, tuition at home, or one-to-one at your chosen hour, because that answer eliminates two of the four options immediately. Then ask every remaining candidate the permit question and get the coursework boundary in writing. If the answer leads you to a local visiting tutor, this page has given you the market bands to judge the quote against. If it leads to live one-to-one over video, take the trial lesson, which runs at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken first, and judge the match on what the session actually produced.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jimi.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are matched by subject and level first. For an Al Jimi family that usually means a Diploma Programme specialist in one named subject, working to your child's own school deadlines rather than a generic revision plan.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Al Jimi who actually knows the IB syllabus?
paragraphs: That is the real question behind the search, so start there. Al Jimi sits in the northern half of Al Ain, built around the Al Jimi Oasis and the mall that gives the district its name, and it is one of the older established residential quarters of the city. It is a comfortable place to live and a difficult place to find a Diploma Programme specialist. Al Ain's private-school sector is a fraction of the size of Dubai's, the Diploma Programme is a minority curriculum within it, and the people qualified to teach Higher Level Chemistry or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at that level number in the low dozens across the whole city.

The honest answer is that proximity and subject expertise rarely arrive in the same person here. A parent in Al Jimi who insists on a tutor living nearby is choosing from whoever happens to be within a twenty-minute drive. That pool contains excellent primary teachers, capable IGCSE scientists and a handful of DP specialists who are already fully booked by families at the school they teach at. It will not reliably contain somebody who has marked Paper 3 scripts, knows what the Chemistry Internal Assessment criteria are called, or can tell you why your child lost four marks on a question they thought they answered.

The second thing worth saying plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service. For Al Jimi, tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, which is the whole reason the subject match is possible at all. A family here gets the Physics Higher Level specialist, not the nearest available teacher, and the forty minutes that would have gone on a drive across Al Ain goes into the lesson instead.

Parents are right to be sceptical of that argument when an agency makes it, because every agency makes it. So this page is built to be checked rather than believed. It names what the market charges and where those figures come from. It names the regulator that licenses your child's school and the permit a private tutor is required to hold. It sets out the specific questions that separate somebody who knows the Diploma Programme from somebody who has read about it, so you can run that test yourself on a free trial lesson before any money changes hands.

The last section deals with the part nobody likes discussing: what happens when no specialist is free for a niche subject in the week you need one. There is an honest answer to that, and it is not that we will find somebody immediately. Reading it is probably the fastest way to decide whether this is a serious operation or a lead form with a paragraph of copy on top.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jimi.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run in the UAE and they ask completely different things of a tutor. A Primary Years child needs a teacher who can work inside an inquiry unit; a Diploma student needs somebody who knows a command term from a marking point.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and moderated externally. Final grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. The Diploma is where almost every tutoring request in Al Jimi originates.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain families sitting the Diploma face a thinner local specialist pool than Abu Dhabi island, and the gap shows most in Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Students here sit the May session alongside the rest of the northern-hemisphere cohort. Because the city is 130km inland, a tutor commuting from the capital is not a realistic weekly arrangement, which is why video delivery matters more here than it does on the coast.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of interdisciplinary study assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1 to 7 grade after a published conversion. There are no external papers unless a school enters students for eAssessment. The criteria language is where most of the marks sit, and most students have never had it explained to them line by line.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years to Diploma step is the single most common reason an Al Jimi parent books tuition. Criterion-based marking rewards process and communication; Diploma papers reward precision under time pressure. A student who scored sevens in Middle Years Science can land a four in Chemistry Higher Level in the first DP1 term without anything being wrong with them. Al Ain schools running both programmes see this every October.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised into units, with no external examinations and a culminating Exhibition in the final year. Reporting is against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than marks. Tutoring at this stage is about securing number fluency, reading stamina and written structure so the Middle Years workload does not arrive as a shock.
programmes.countryNote: Primary Years requests from Al Jimi are usually about English writing or mental maths rather than a subject crisis. The useful work is short and frequent: two half-hour sessions a week beat one long one for a nine-year-old, and both fit after the Al Ain school day without touching evening family time. Arabic and Islamic Education run alongside the programme as mandatory subjects in every UAE private school.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment and core components
programmes.description: Every Diploma subject carries internally marked coursework, from the Mathematics exploration to the science investigation, the History essay and the Language A written task. Together with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, these components decide a large share of the final grade and are completed over months rather than hours.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the rules matter most. A tutor working with an Al Jimi student may teach the underlying skill, explain what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not supply text, invent data or hand over a finished piece. Submitting work that is not your own is a malpractice finding under IB academic-honesty rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jimi.subjectsIntro: Requests from Al Jimi cluster tightly. The list below is ordered roughly by how often a Diploma family in this part of Al Ain asks for each one, with a note on where the marks actually go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-heavy route, demanded by engineering and most economics courses. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and deeper calculus. Marks disappear in the unstructured Paper 2 questions where no method is prompted, and in the exploration, where students pick a topic too large to handle in twelve to twenty pages.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led work. It is not the easy option: Higher Level includes matrices, graph theory and hypothesis testing. The usual failure is treating the graphic display calculator as the answer rather than the tool, then losing method marks for writing down a result with no working behind it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry most of the difficulty, and Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth. Students lose marks by describing when the command term says explain, and by rounding away significant figures in calculations. The investigation needs a question narrow enough to generate real uncertainty analysis.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The hardest subject to staff locally in Al Ain at Higher Level. Fields, circular motion and quantum topics are where grades are decided. The recurring error is algebraic rather than conceptual: students understand the physics and then lose the marks rearranging the equation under exam pressure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem, not difficulty. The syllabus rewards precise terminology and the ability to apply a known process to an unfamiliar context. Extended-response answers fail when a student writes everything they know instead of answering the question asked, and data-based questions need practice reading unfamiliar graphs quickly.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral and the Paper 1 guided analysis are the pressure points. Strong readers underperform because they summarise rather than analyse, and because they have never been taught how to structure ten minutes of spoken argument around a global issue with two extracts in front of them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks. A labelled, correctly shifted diagram with an explanation tied to it scores where a paragraph of prose does not. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that trip students who have treated the subject as essay-only. The commentary portfolio needs genuinely current articles and a clear theoretical anchor.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in every UAE private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and language-of-instruction rules set by the regulator. Al Jimi families frequently need support here precisely because it sits outside the IB timetable and gets squeezed.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study command terms and tool application decide the grade. Students who can define a concept still lose marks for failing to apply it to the stimulus organisation. Higher Level adds the depth expected in the extended response, and the internal work needs primary or secondary research chosen deliberately.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Rarely staffed locally at Higher Level. Abstract data structures, recursion and the Higher Level case study carry the difficulty, and the solution development requires a client, a genuine problem and documented testing. Students who can code often lose marks on the written paper's design and evaluation questions.

sections.heading: The honest state of IB tutor supply in Al Ain
paragraphs: Al Ain is a city of around half a million people whose private-school sector is small, inland and stable. The brief that governs these pages puts it plainly: the private-school set here is much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so Higher Level Diploma sciences and the less common languages are the usual gaps. That is not a marketing position, it is arithmetic. A curriculum taken by a minority of students in a mid-sized city produces a small number of teachers qualified to teach it, and most of them are already employed full time by the schools that teach it.

There is a second constraint that parents often discover late. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours is required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct carries the same restriction. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it. The practical effect is real either way: the obvious local candidate, your child's own subject teacher, is the one person who should not take the work.

What remains, for a family in Al Jimi who will only consider somebody local, is a short list that gets shorter as the subject gets more specialised. Mathematics at Standard Level is findable. Chemistry at Higher Level is harder. Computer Science Higher Level or Japanese ab initio will not be on the list at all. sections.heading: Why a twenty-minute drive stopped predicting a better lesson
paragraphs: For a generation, a home tutor was the premium product and everybody understood why. The tutor arrived, sat at the table, saw the exercise book and could not be interrupted by a dropped connection. The cost of that was invisible because it was paid in somebody else's time. In Al Jimi, a tutor travelling from the far side of Al Ain spends forty to fifty minutes a session on the road, and that time is in the price whether it is itemised or not.

The trade a family makes is therefore not convenience against quality. It is a smaller pool of tutors who can reach your door against a larger pool who can reach your screen. For a Year 4 numeracy problem the local pool is deep enough that the trade barely matters. For Higher Level Physics in a city this size, the local pool is the problem, and solving the travel question by hiring somebody nearby means accepting a generalist for a specialist's job.

What a video session loses is worth naming rather than glossing over. A tutor cannot see the exercise book unless the student shows it, cannot read body language as reliably, and depends on a stable connection and a quiet room. Those are real costs and they are manageable: a shared screen, a document camera or a phone photograph of the working, a fixed desk rather than a sofa, and a parent who checks in for the first two minutes of the first few sessions. The comparison below prices both sides rather than arguing for one.

sections.heading: How to test whether a tutor actually knows the Diploma
paragraphs: The question in the search bar deserves a usable answer, and here it is: you can establish whether somebody knows the Diploma Programme in about twenty minutes, without being a subject specialist yourself. The trick is to ask about assessment structure rather than content. Anybody can discuss organic chemistry. Only somebody who has taught the course can tell you what each paper is worth, what the command terms demand, and how the Internal Assessment is marked.

Start with weightings. Ask what proportion of the Higher Level grade comes from the Internal Assessment and what each paper contributes. A specialist answers without hesitation and will usually volunteer where their students historically lose marks. Then ask about command terms: the difference between state, describe, explain and evaluate is not a semantic nicety in IB marking, it is the difference between one mark and four. A tutor who waves that away has not read a mark scheme recently.

Finish with the Internal Assessment criteria. Ask them to name the criteria for your child's subject and say what each rewards. This is the single most diagnostic question available to a parent, because the criteria have letters and names, the mark allocations are published in the subject guide, and somebody who has supervised real coursework knows them the way a driver knows the gears. Run all three questions in a free trial lesson and let the answers decide. A tutor who finds the questions reasonable is the tutor you want.

sections.heading: ADEK, the tutoring permit, and what an Al Jimi parent can verify
paragraphs: Al Jimi is in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator for every private school your child could attend is the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, which covers Al Ain as fully as the capital. That single fact is useful to a parent because it tells you where to look for an inspection report and a school listing, and because none of the competitor pages researched for this project names ADEK at all.

Private tutoring in the UAE is separately regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anybody offering private tuition without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with suspicion.

What this gives you is a clean question to ask. Does the person teaching my child hold a private tuition work permit, and under which category? The permit is free and the MoHRE application route takes two working days through the ministry's smart app and e-services system, so there is no good reason for a professional tutor not to hold one. IB Gram holds no regulatory approval from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise. A platform that claims accreditation it does not hold has told you something important about itself.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor cannot cross
paragraphs: One competitor found during research sells completed Internal Assessments. That is worth naming because it tells you what some of the market is willing to do, and because the consequence lands on the student. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting work that is not your own is malpractice, and a malpractice finding can cost a candidate the Diploma. No tutoring arrangement is worth that risk, and a parent in Al Jimi has every right to ask exactly where a provider draws the line.

Here is where this one draws it. A tutor teaches the underlying skill. A tutor explains what each assessment criterion rewards and in what language the examiner expects to see it. A tutor reads a draft the student has written and says what is missing, unclear or unsupported. A tutor helps a student choose a research question narrow enough to be answerable and a method that generates usable data. All of that is teaching, and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor does not do: supply sentences for the student to paste, restructure a piece until the student's own thinking is gone, invent or adjust experimental data, or hand over anything the student then submits as their own. The distinction is not subtle in practice. If the student cannot explain every line of the work to their own teacher without help, it should not be in the document. Say that to your child once, early, and it saves a difficult conversation in DP2.
bullets: Teaching the skill is permitted; producing the work is not
Feedback on the student's own draft is normal supervision practice
Data must come from the student's own investigation
If the student cannot explain a line, it should not be submitted

sections.heading: Fitting sessions around the Al Jimi school day
paragraphs: Scheduling is where good intentions go to die. Al Ain schools finish in the early to mid afternoon, the drive home from the central cluster to Al Jimi is short by UAE standards, and most students are through the door between three and four. That sounds like an open afternoon, but it is not. There is a meal, there is decompression, there is homework set by six subject teachers, and for many families there is Arabic or Islamic Education revision that sits outside the IB timetable entirely.

The slot that works for Diploma students in this district is usually late afternoon, between five and seven, with homework afterwards or before depending on the child. Younger students do better earlier and shorter. Across the week, two sixty-minute sessions in different subjects beat one two-hour block in a single subject almost every time, because concentration in a Diploma student is a depleting resource and the second hour of any session is worth less than the first.

Two Al Ain-specific factors are worth planning for. Ramadan shifts the whole rhythm of the day, and many families prefer post-Iftar sessions during the month; that is a normal arrangement rather than an exception. And school assessment calendars move, particularly around inspection visits and internal mock windows. A session that is pinned to a fixed hour regardless of what the school is doing that week is a session that gets cancelled. Agree at the start that the slot flexes around the school's calendar, not the other way round.

sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market has a page that implies instant availability. Almost none of them says what happens when a request lands for Higher Level Computer Science on a Thursday in the week before mocks. The honest answer is that sometimes the right person is not free, and the way a provider behaves at that moment tells you more than any testimonial.

The behaviour worth looking for is disclosure before booking rather than substitution after it. If the subject specialist is not available for three weeks, you should be told that it is three weeks, before any payment, and offered the choice between waiting for the right tutor and starting with somebody adjacent who can cover the fundamentals in the meantime. The failure mode to watch for is a provider who takes the booking and then quietly assigns a generalist, which is how a family ends up paying specialist rates for homework supervision.

The same applies to tutor location. Some specialists working with UAE families are based outside the country, and that should be stated plainly rather than hidden behind a local-sounding phone number. Two of the competitor pages reviewed for this project route UAE parents to Indian numbers without explaining why. There is nothing wrong with a tutor in Mumbai teaching a Diploma student in Al Jimi over video if the teaching is good and the timing suits Gulf Standard Time. There is a great deal wrong with not mentioning it.

faqs.question: Is there an IB specialist actually based in Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for Standard Level subjects, and rarely at Higher Level. Al Ain's private-school sector is small and the Diploma is a minority curriculum within it, so the number of people qualified to teach Higher Level Chemistry or Physics across the whole city is low. Most are employed full time by the schools that teach the programme, and in Abu Dhabi emirate a teacher is barred from tutoring students enrolled at their own school. The practical answer for Al Jimi is that the specialist exists but usually not within driving distance, which is why lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an address in Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Tuition for Al Jimi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. This is stated plainly because the alternative, implying a visit and then explaining the real arrangement after a booking, wastes everybody's time. The practical upside is that your child is matched to the right subject specialist rather than the nearest available teacher, and the forty to fifty minutes a cross-city Al Ain drive would have consumed goes into teaching instead.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor really knows the Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions and listen to how quickly they answer. First, what each paper is worth at your child's level as a percentage of the final grade. Second, the difference in marking terms between describe, explain and evaluate. Third, the names of the Internal Assessment criteria for that subject and what each one rewards. Somebody who has taught the course answers all three without pausing and usually volunteers where their students lose marks. Somebody who has only read about it deflects to general reassurance. Run the test in a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: What do in-home tutors charge in the Al Ain and wider UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with a Dubai cost survey quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, and specialist IB or IGCSE tutors at 200 to 450 and above. The overlap tells the story: the in-home premium largely pays for travel rather than better teaching. These are other providers' published rates as reviewed in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees private schools in Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, usually called ADEK. Al Ain sits inside the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here exactly as it does in the capital. That matters practically because ADEK is where you look for the official school listing and inspection information rather than relying on a third-party summary. It is worth knowing that none of the competitor tutoring pages reviewed for this project mentions ADEK at all, which is a reasonable signal about how locally informed they are.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Al Ain students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anybody providing private tuition without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no official fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with caution. Because the permit is free and processed in about two working days, a professional tutor has no reason not to hold one.

faqs.question: Can an Al Jimi tutor support my child's Internal Assessment without breaching IB academic-honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain what each criterion rewards and in what language, help narrow a research question to something answerable, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot supply text, invent or adjust data, or hand over work the student then submits. Submitting work that is not your own is malpractice under IB academic-honesty rules and the consequence falls on the candidate. A useful household test: if your child cannot explain every line to their own teacher, it should not be in the document.

faqs.question: My child has moved from the Middle Years Programme into DP1 and is struggling. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is one of the most common reasons an Al Jimi parent books tuition, and it is usually a change in assessment style rather than a drop in ability. Middle Years marking uses four criteria per subject out of eight each, rewarding process, inquiry and communication. Diploma papers reward precision under timed conditions with specific command terms. A student who scored consistent sevens in Middle Years Science can land a four in Chemistry Higher Level in the first term purely from that shift. Targeted work on exam technique and command-term discipline usually closes the gap faster than more content revision.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to staff locally in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics first, then Higher Level Chemistry, Computer Science at Higher Level, and the less common languages taken ab initio. The pattern is consistent: the more specialised the subject and the higher the level, the smaller the pool of people in a city this size who have actually taught it. Standard Level mathematics and the sciences are findable locally. For the scarce subjects the realistic choice is live video delivery or no specialist at all, and that position is stated before you book rather than discovered afterwards.

faqs.question: With so few DP specialists in Al Ain, can one tutor cover two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually a bad idea at Higher Level. Mathematics and Physics overlap enough that one strong tutor can sometimes handle both, and Economics with Business Management is another plausible pairing. Beyond those, a tutor stretched across two Higher Level sciences is a generalist in both. The Internal Assessment requirements alone differ enough to make genuine dual expertise rare. If the household budget is the constraint, it is more effective to run one subject properly for a term than two subjects thinly for the same money.

faqs.question: What time of day do sessions usually work for Al Jimi families?
faqs.answer: Late afternoon, generally between five and seven. Al Ain schools finish in the early to mid afternoon and the drive back into Al Jimi from the central school cluster is short, so most students are home between three and four. The hour after that goes on a meal and decompression, and homework from six subject teachers is still waiting. Younger students do better earlier and in shorter blocks. During Ramadan many families move to post-Iftar timing, which is a routine arrangement rather than an exception that needs negotiating.

faqs.question: What happens if no Al Ain tutor is free for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You are told the wait before anything is booked, with a date rather than a vague reassurance, and offered a choice between waiting for the specialist and starting with somebody who can cover the fundamentals meanwhile. What does not happen is a quiet substitution, where a booking is accepted and a generalist assigned at specialist rates. For Higher Level Physics or Computer Science in Al Ain, a wait of one to two weeks is a realistic answer rather than an unusual one, and it is better heard early than discovered in week three.

faqs.question: Are some of the tutors teaching Al Jimi students based outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, some are, and it is stated rather than hidden. Where a subject specialist for a scarce Diploma subject is based in India, you are told that before booking, and sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so the arrangement works around the Al Ain school day. Two of the competitor pages reviewed for this project route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers without explaining the delivery model at all. There is nothing wrong with a specialist teaching your child from another country over video; there is something wrong with concealing it.

faqs.question: How does the free trial lesson work for a family in Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: One lesson, no payment, with your child present and the subject and level agreed in advance so the right tutor takes it. Treat it as an assessment of the tutor rather than a demonstration for your child. Ask about paper weightings, command terms and the Internal Assessment criteria, and watch whether the tutor works from your child's own school materials or an off-the-shelf worksheet. If the trial does not convince you, nothing follows from it. Any condition attached to a free lesson should be stated before you book it, by any provider.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply to Diploma students here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools across the UAE teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and the language of instruction set by regulation. For a Diploma student in Al Jimi this means real timetable load sitting outside the six IB subjects, and it is frequently the first thing squeezed when coursework deadlines arrive. Planning tuition without accounting for it is how a family ends up with a session nobody can attend in November.

intro.heading: What this costs a month, before anything else
paragraphs: A family in Al Khabisi deciding about IB tuition is almost never deciding about one hour. They are deciding about a line item that will sit in the household budget for two to twenty-four months, and the honest unit for that decision is the monthly figure, not the hourly rate. One sixty-minute session a week at the middle of the UAE market band costs roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month, which is the range Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring rate table gives for a mid-tier tutor on a weekly hour. Two sessions a week in an exam year, with a specialist, moves that to AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Those are the numbers worth arguing about.

The hourly rates behind them are wide because the market contains very different things under one word. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour. Tutopiya starts from AED 33 to AED 52. Unitors publishes AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650. All of those are real published prices from October 2026, and the spread is not a pricing error; it is five different products. A university student revising with your child is not the same purchase as a Diploma Chemistry specialist who has marked the Higher Level paper, and neither is a mistake if you know which one you bought.

Al Khabisi sits inside Al Ain, which is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and therefore regulated by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Al Ain's private-school set is a great deal smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and that scarcity has a direct price effect: when only a handful of local teachers can cover Diploma Physics Higher Level or Spanish B, the in-home rate for those subjects drifts to the top of the band and the waiting list gets longer. This is the single most important local fact about tutoring cost in Al Khabisi, and no competitor page mentions it.

An in-home visit carries a travel premium. The UAE in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor. The premium is not fraud. It pays for a car, fuel, forty minutes of unbilled driving and the fact that one tutor can serve perhaps four households an evening instead of eight. What it does not buy is a wider choice of teacher, and in a city 130 kilometres inland that is the thing a Diploma student needs most.

IB Gram's position is deliberately narrow. We deliver one-to-one IB tuition to Al Khabisi over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, matched by subject and level rather than by postcode. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. If an adult physically in the room is what you want, hire locally and ask the questions set out further down this page. If what you want is the right Higher Level teacher at a predictable monthly cost, the online route is the one that works from Al Khabisi.
