programmes.countryNote: This is where Al Khabisi money is best spent and most often wasted. Diploma Higher Level sciences and the less common languages are the thinnest part of Al Ain's local teaching pool, so families pay the top of the in-home band for whoever is available rather than for the right subject specialist. Online matching removes the premium and the compromise at the same time: you are choosing from a national pool of Diploma teachers, not from the drivable radius around Al Khabisi.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight, with an ePortfolio and the Personal Project in the final year. There are no external papers for most students, so parents see criterion levels rather than percentages and often cannot tell whether a 5 is comfortable or fragile. A tutor's first job in the Middle Years is translation: which criterion is losing marks, and what a level 7 answer looks like in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years tuition is the cheapest effective intervention available to an Al Khabisi family, and the one most often skipped. A single term of fortnightly support in Years 9 and 10, at the AED 150-300 online band, costs less than a single exam-year month and removes the gap that later needs a Diploma rescue. ADEK-regulated schools in Al Ain run the Middle Years alongside the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements, which adds workload the budget should account for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with the Exhibition in the final year. Assessment is formative and descriptive, so there is rarely a mark to chase. The useful tuition at this stage is narrow and mechanical: number fluency, reading stamina, written structure. Anything broader is usually a parent paying for reassurance rather than for learning, which is a legitimate purchase but should be a conscious one.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Khabisi primary families the honest cost advice is to buy less. Two half-hour online sessions a week on one specific skill, at the lower end of the band, does more than a weekly ninety-minute general session at the in-home rate. Al Ain's Primary Years cohort is small enough that local availability is unpredictable, which is exactly the case where a short online block beats waiting for a tutor who can drive to the villa.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge supervision
programmes.ageRange: Diploma year one into year two
programmes.description: The coursework strand sits outside the subject timetable and needs a different kind of hour. The work is marked against named criteria, the student's school supervisor has limited contact time, and the single biggest cause of lost marks is a methodology chosen in week one that cannot carry the analysis required in week ten. Support here is reading, questioning and feedback on the student's own draft.
programmes.countryNote: This is the line where the market behaves worst. One operation found in the research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at AED 3,750. Buying that is an academic-honesty breach that can cost a student the whole Diploma, and it is money spent on the single worst outcome available. IB Gram tutors read drafts, ask questions and give written feedback on work the student has produced. They do not write, redraft to completion or supply any part of an assessed piece.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject is not uniform, because the scarce subjects cost more everywhere and the scarcity is sharper in Al Ain than on the coast. These are the subjects Al Khabisi families request, with what the hour actually has to do in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the Paper 3 extended-response problems at Higher Level. Marks go on method lines a student skipped because the answer looked obvious, and on calculus notation under time pressure. The Higher Level course is the most requested single purchase from Al Khabisi and the one where a non-specialist hour is most clearly wasted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and mandatory graphical calculator technique. Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches because the common failures are procedural rather than conceptual, but the route choice matters: several engineering and economics degrees expect Analysis and Approaches, and switching late is expensive in every sense.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the data-based paper. Higher Level adds depth rather than new habits, which is why a student can be fine in class and lose a grade on Paper 2 extended response. Chemistry Higher Level is one of the two subjects where Al Ain's local supply is thinnest and the in-home premium bites hardest.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields, with the Higher Level extension topics arriving late in year two. Most lost marks are not physics at all: they are unit handling, significant figures and uncertainty treatment in the data questions. A specialist fixes that in a handful of hours, which makes it unusually good value per session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline is the whole subject at exam level. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'discuss' carry different mark allocations, and students who revise content without revising command terms plateau. Biology is well supplied online, so the rate should sit in the middle of the band, not the top.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world evidence and the three commentaries that form the Internal Assessment. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that reward exam technique over reading. A frequent Al Khabisi request, and one where two or three well-aimed hours on diagram labelling returns more than a term of general support.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, the comparative essay and the Individual Oral. The Oral is the component families underestimate: it is assessed on a global issue the student must choose and defend, and preparation is coaching, not content delivery. Works well online because the whole component is talk.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools applied to a real organisation, plus a research project at Higher Level. Students lose marks by describing a company rather than applying a framework to it. Cheap to support well, because the correction is structural and transfers across every question in the paper.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Productive skills under timed conditions and the individual oral assessment. These are the 'less common languages' in Al Ain's school set, which means local in-home availability is genuinely limited and the published rates for them run high. Online is not a compromise here; it is usually the only route to a subject-trained teacher.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay on a prescribed title and the exhibition. Both are marked on the quality of argument about knowledge rather than on subject content, so a student who writes well elsewhere can still score poorly. A small number of hours spent on how a knowledge claim is structured changes the grade; more hours rarely add anything.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.regionsIntro: Al Khabisi is one neighbourhood in a city where everything is a short drive from everything else, which is precisely why the in-home model looks workable in Al Ain and still fails on subject choice. These are the areas families ask about alongside it.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Dense, long-established and close to the souk and hospital. Household schedules here are shaped by shift work as much as by school hours, so evening and late-evening online slots are the ones that get used.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Central and residential, with several of the city's older private schools within a few minutes. Families here are often choosing between two schools rather than two tutors, and the tutoring question follows the school decision.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Villa housing with a high proportion of professional families and a strong Diploma cohort. Requests from Al Towayya skew to Higher Level sciences, which is also where the local rate premium is steepest.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: North of the centre, near the archaeological park and the Oman road. The commute to schools on the city's south side is long enough that a 4pm session is unrealistic for many Hili students on weekdays.

regions.name: Al Maqam
regions.note: Southern and spread out, with newer villa compounds. Distances here are the clearest argument against in-home tuition in Al Ain: a tutor covering Al Maqam and Al Khabisi in one evening loses most of an hour to driving.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: On the city's southern edge towards the Omani border, where the drivable tutor pool thins out sharply. Online delivery removes the distance question entirely for Zakher families.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza
regions.note: Established residential district close to central amenities. A common second address for families who moved within the city, and one where tutoring continuity matters more than proximity.

regions.name: Al Yahar
regions.note: Outlying and agricultural in character, some distance from the main school cluster. In-home rates quoted to Al Yahar families routinely sit at the top of the UAE band purely because of travel.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Close to the centre and to several of the city's larger private schools. Short school runs here free up the late-afternoon slot that students elsewhere in Al Ain cannot use.

schoolClusters.city: Central Al Ain, around Al Khabisi and Al Mutaredh
schoolClusters.note: The central schools take most of Al Khabisi's cohort, and their timetables are what determine whether a 4pm or a 6pm session is realistic. Families should check ADEK's own published listing for the current licensed curriculum and inspection outcome of any school below before relying on either.

schoolClusters.city: Outer Al Ain, towards Zakher, Al Maqam and Al Yahar
schoolClusters.note: The outer schools serve the southern and western neighbourhoods and involve genuine travel. For a student here the difference between an online session and an in-home one is not convenience but whether the session happens at all on a school night.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.modesIntro: Three ways of buying the same hour, with genuinely different monthly consequences. The choice should follow the budget horizon rather than the subject.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-length
modes.description: One sixty-minute live session a week across a term, on a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. This is the baseline against which every other option should be priced, and at mid-market rates it is the AED 600-1,200 monthly line. It works because the tutor sees the same student through a whole unit rather than arriving at a crisis.

modes.title: Twice-weekly exam-year block
modes.description: Two sessions a week through the final two terms of the Diploma, one on content and one on timed paper practice. This is the AED 1,000-2,000+ monthly band and the highest-value version of it splits the week deliberately rather than doubling the same lesson. Families who buy two identical sessions pay twice for one effect.

modes.description: Four to six sessions on one named weakness: calculus notation, uncertainty treatment, economics diagrams, a Theory of Knowledge argument structure. The cheapest intervention that reliably moves a grade, and the one families discover last. It needs a diagnosis first, which is what the free trial lesson is for.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Khabisi costs a month
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Khabisi, hired locally for in-home visits, costs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is included; the same teaching delivered online sits at AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor. Translated into months, that is the table below. These are market bands drawn from published competitor rates and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring rate table, not an IB Gram price list.

Reading the monthly column rather than the hourly one changes decisions. Families who would never agree to AED 1,800 a month frequently agree to AED 450 an hour twice a week without doing the arithmetic, and families who flinch at AED 300 an hour will happily pay AED 65 for four hours that achieve nothing. The monthly figure is also the number a school year is actually budgeted in, which is why it belongs at the top of the page.

One caution on the rightmost column. 'What it covers' is written from what the hour can realistically do, not from what a provider promises. No amount of weekly tuition substitutes for a student doing the practice between sessions, and any plan priced on the assumption that it will is mispriced.

One figure deliberately absent from the table is an IB Gram price. We match on subject and level and quote per plan after the trial lesson, and publishing a rate card next to competitors' bands would invite exactly the comparison this page is trying to replace. What the table is for is to let an Al Khabisi family walk into any conversation, local or online, knowing what the market charges before anyone names a number.

sections.heading: The hourly bands behind those figures, and who publishes them
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no Al Ain family transacts in. The bands below are what the market actually publishes in AED, each attributed to the provider that published it in October 2026. They are competitors' figures, quoted for comparison, not claims about their quality.

The useful thing about the spread is that it is not a quality ladder with a single scale. The AED 45 to AED 65 tier and the AED 650 tier are not the same service at different margins. The first is supervised practice; the last is a named specialist with examining experience whose scarcity sets the price. In between sits the band that covers most real decisions, AED 150 to AED 300, where a subject-trained teacher is affordable on a weekly hour.

For an Al Khabisi family the practical rule is to pay the middle band for the subject that is actually at risk, and nothing at all for the subjects that are not. Four subjects supported weakly costs more and achieves less than one subject supported properly, and that is the most common overspend in this market.

One more use for the spread. If a quote arrives above AED 500 an hour, the question to ask is what makes this individual scarce, and the answer should be a name, a subject and a level rather than an adjective. If a quote arrives below AED 100, the question is what the hour contains. Both answers are often fine; neither should be assumed.

sections.heading: Where Al Khabisi families lose money on tutoring
paragraphs: The first loss is paying the travel premium for a compromise. In Al Ain, with a private-school set much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, the tutor who can reach Al Khabisi on a Tuesday evening is frequently not a teacher of the subject in question. Families then pay AED 300 to AED 500 an hour for general academic supervision because it arrives at the door, while the Higher Level Chemistry teacher who would have fixed the actual problem was available online at AED 220.

The second loss is buying hours instead of buying a diagnosis. A student losing marks on Physics data questions does not need thirty hours of Physics; they need three hours on uncertainty and significant figures and then nothing. Without a diagnosis, the default purchase is open-ended weekly support that renews every month because nobody has defined what finished looks like. This is the single largest preventable cost in the market and it is entirely within a parent's control.

The third loss is paying for coursework that cannot be bought. Completed Internal Assessments are sold to UAE students at around AED 3,750. A student who submits one risks the entire Diploma under the IB's academic-honesty rules, which makes it the worst possible return on any tutoring spend. Legitimate coursework support is a tutor reading a draft, asking what the data actually shows and marking against the criteria, and it costs ordinary hourly rates.

A fourth and quieter loss is churn. Changing tutor three times in a year means paying three times for the first four sessions, which are always the slowest, and a student who has explained their own weakness to three different adults stops bothering. Diagnose first, match once, and review on a schedule rather than on a bad week.
bullets: Paying an in-home premium for a tutor who does not teach the subject at risk
Open-ended monthly support with no defined endpoint or exit condition

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor driving to Al Khabisi
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search term implies, so here it is on the merits rather than as a sales line. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that is a real limitation worth stating plainly rather than burying. What the table sets out is what each model costs an Al Khabisi family and what each one gives up.

The decisive row is tutor pool. An in-home arrangement in Al Khabisi selects from teachers who can drive there and back on a school night. Online selects from every Diploma teacher available in the slot. For Mathematics or Biology that difference is modest. For Chemistry Higher Level, Physics Higher Level or Spanish B, which the Al Ain school set covers thinly, it is the entire question.

The second decisive row is reliability. A 5pm in-home session in Al Ain depends on a car, a route and an evening with no incident in it. Sessions that slip become sessions that stop, and a plan that runs forty weeks instead of thirty-two is worth more than a slightly better room. Online sessions from Al Khabisi slip for illness and travel, not for traffic.

What the table does not claim is that online suits every child. Some students work far better with an adult physically beside them, and for those the in-home premium is money well spent. The point is that it should be a decision about the child, taken knowingly, rather than the default because a local number answered the phone first.

sections.heading: Costing the whole Diploma, not the next month
paragraphs: A Diploma is two years, and tutoring spend across those two years is lumpy rather than level. Families who budget a flat monthly figure from Year 12 September either overspend in the quiet terms or run out of appetite in the term that matters. The table maps where the hours genuinely belong.

The pattern is worth stating in words. Early Year 12 needs very little: the course is new and the school is teaching it for the first time, so a tutor is mostly duplicating. The first real need is the Internal Assessment methodology decision, which is a small number of hours with a very large consequence. The heaviest block is the two terms before the exam session, and the last four weeks need less than families expect because by then the student should be practising, not learning.

Totalled at mid-market online rates, a sensibly staged two-year plan in one subject lands well below a flat AED 1,200 a month sustained for twenty-four months, and does more. That is the argument for staging rather than for spending.

Two caveats on the hour counts. They assume one subject, and a student needing two subjects supported does not need double the hours in each; the study-habit work overlaps. They also assume the school is teaching the course competently, which in Al Ain's established private schools is usually the case. Where it is not, the plan is different and should be discussed openly rather than priced from a table.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is legally permitted before you pay
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two cost implications follow. First, because the permit is free, no tutor can justify a higher rate by reference to it; anyone who does is describing something else. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you, and a tutor quoting one is guessing.

There is a further restriction specific to Abu Dhabi and therefore to Al Khabisi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars the same thing. A tutor who offers to teach your child privately while teaching them at school is offering something they are not permitted to provide, and the arrangement is the parent's exposure as well as theirs.

One further check costs nothing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is a specific thing issued to institutes with premises, and no online tutor or matching platform should be described as holding it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, and the IB's academic-honesty framework treats a breach as grounds for withholding the Diploma. That makes the boundary a practical matter rather than a philosophical one, and it is worth knowing exactly where it sits before you pay anyone for coursework support.

Inside the boundary: explaining what a criterion rewards, asking why a method was chosen, pointing at an analysis that does not follow from the data, identifying missing evaluation, teaching citation properly, and marking a student's own draft against the published criteria. All of that is teaching, all of it improves the mark, and all of it is bought at ordinary hourly rates.

Outside the boundary: writing any sentence that goes into the submission, rewriting a paragraph rather than commenting on it, supplying a research question or dataset as finished work, and editing to completion. IB Gram tutors do not cross that line, and an operation that offers to is selling the student a risk disproportionate to anything a grade is worth.

The reason to say all this on a cost page is that the boundary has a price attached. Legitimate coursework support is bought at ordinary hourly rates and typically takes four to six hours across the Internal Assessment cycle, most of it early. The alternative on sale in this market costs several thousand dirhams and risks the qualification the whole two years was for, which makes it the worst value available anywhere on this page.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, and why late money costs more
paragraphs: UAE Diploma students sit the May session, which is the one Al Ain schools work towards. IB session and results dates are not restated here: the IB's own site is the only place to confirm them, and a date on a tutoring page that is wrong by a week is worse than no date. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator for the internal deadlines, which matter more to planning than the external ones anyway.

For any Al Khabisi student also taking Cambridge or Pearson qualifications, the UAE pattern is worth knowing precisely because one widely repeated claim is wrong. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the school's zone version is the one to work from.

The cost consequence is simple arithmetic. Eight weeks before a paper, an hour buys paper technique on content the student already knows. Three weeks before, the same hour buys triage. Families who start in the final month pay the same rate for a fraction of the effect, and often buy more hours to compensate. Starting a term earlier is the cheapest decision available in this market.

A practical planning note for Al Khabisi families. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines at the start of Year 12, write them on the calendar, and work the tutoring plan backwards from those rather than from the exam window. The internal deadlines are the ones that actually constrain when work has to be done, and they are the ones nobody tells a parent about until they are close.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and these sit on top of a Diploma student's six subjects. Families budgeting for tutoring often leave them out of the plan entirely and then find they are the subjects consuming weekday evenings.

The rules are specific. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines, which set the pattern the sector follows, require separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and state that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; for non-Arabs the school's licensed-curriculum language applies.

There is also a content constraint that matters for anyone buying support in these subjects: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support here therefore means working through the school's own material and the school's own expectations, not importing a parallel course. For Al Khabisi families the practical point is to decide early whether these subjects are part of the tutoring budget, because adding them in March is expensive and late.

For an Al Khabisi family the budgeting consequence is concrete. If Arabic as an additional language is going to need support, it needs it from Year 7 onwards in short regular doses, not as an emergency in the Diploma years when there is no room left in the week. Treat it as a standing small line in the plan rather than a surprise.

sections.heading: What happens when nobody covers the subject
paragraphs: Availability transparency is the gap nobody in this market fills, so here is the honest version. Al Ain's small private-school set means the local pool for Diploma Higher Level sciences and the less common languages is thin, and that is true for us as well as for every in-home agency in the city. There are weeks when a specific subject at a specific level in a specific evening slot is not available.

When that happens we say so rather than substituting. A Chemistry Higher Level request is not filled with a general science tutor, and a Spanish B request is not filled with a Spanish speaker who has not taught the course. The alternative we offer is a different slot, a start date a fortnight out, or a clear statement that we cannot cover it, at which point a family should look elsewhere with the permit questions above in hand.

This matters financially because the hidden cost of a bad match is paid twice: once in the fee and once in the term lost before anyone admits it was not working. Al Khabisi families have the right to ask, before the first session, which subject and which level the tutor has actually taught, how recently, and for how many cohorts. Any provider unwilling to answer that is answering it.

The same transparency applies in reverse. If a subject is well supplied, say Biology or Business Management, there is no reason to accept a long wait or a premium rate, and a family should push back on both. Scarcity is real in some subjects in Al Ain and absent in others, and knowing which is which is worth money.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the problem
process.description: Not 'maths help' but 'Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, losing marks on Paper 3 extended response'. The more precise the request, the faster the match and the fewer hours the plan needs. Al Khabisi families usually arrive with a mock paper, which is the ideal starting document.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: A full session, no card required, with the tutor who would actually teach the course. Its purpose is diagnosis: at the end you should have a named weakness and an estimate of how many hours it takes to close. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than the student.

process.title: Agree a plan with an endpoint
process.description: Sessions per week, the slot in Gulf Standard Time, and what finished looks like. A plan with a defined end is cheaper than one that renews by default, and it forces both sides to be specific about what the hours are for. The plan is written down and can be changed.

process.title: Lessons, notes and marked work
process.description: Live one-to-one video on the agreed slot, with a short written note after each session saying what was covered and what to practise. Work done between sessions is marked, so the next hour starts from evidence rather than from a conversation about how last week felt.

process.title: Review against the original problem
process.description: Every six to eight sessions, check the plan against the weakness it was bought to fix. If it is closed, stop or move to the next one. If it is not, change the approach or the tutor. Open-ended continuation without this review is how a tutoring budget quietly doubles.

whyPoints.title: Prices in AED, attributed, with a date
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page is a market band from a named source published in October 2026, not an unsourced claim and not our own price list. Three of the six pages currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Subject and level, not postcode
whyPoints.description: A match is made on which Diploma subject at which level the tutor has taught, and how recently. Geography is not a selection criterion because it cannot improve a Paper 2 mark, and in Al Ain it actively narrows the field.

whyPoints.title: A stated delivery model
whyPoints.description: One-to-one live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. We say that at the top of the page rather than after the deposit, because a family expecting a tutor arriving in person in Al Khabisi should know before they book.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support with a boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors read drafts, mark against published criteria and ask the questions a supervisor has no time for. They do not write, redraft to completion or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and we would rather lose the booking than blur that.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If the subject, level and slot are not covered, we say so and give a date or decline. The thin Al Ain pool for Higher Level sciences and less common languages is a real constraint, and concealing it would cost a family a term.

whyPoints.title: No invented numbers
whyPoints.description: No self-reported satisfaction percentages, no star rating we generated, no claim of approval or accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge. We hold none of those, and pages that imply otherwise are the ones to be careful of.

faqs.question: How much should an IB home tutor in Al Khabisi cost per month?
faqs.answer: Budget on the monthly figure rather than the hourly rate. One weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month, using Bestimate's 2026 rate table for the UAE market. The same hour delivered in home, with travel priced in, runs AED 720 to AED 2,000. An exam-year plan of two sessions a week with a specialist lands at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. A short targeted block of four to six sessions is a one-off AED 600 to AED 1,800. These are market bands from published sources, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home rate in Al Ain higher than the online rate?
faqs.answer: Because it includes a car. A tutor driving to Al Khabisi loses thirty to fifty unbilled minutes per visit and can serve roughly half as many households in an evening, so the hour is priced to cover that. The UAE in-home band is AED 180 to AED 500 against AED 150 to AED 300 online. The premium is legitimate, but it buys presence rather than a better-matched teacher, and in Al Ain's smaller private-school set the drivable pool often does not include a specialist in the subject you need.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Al Khabisi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Khabisi families are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We state this before any booking because the search term says 'home tutor' and a family should not discover the delivery model after paying. If a tutor physically present in the room is a requirement rather than a preference, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE permit, the subject taught and the level before the first session.

faqs.question: Which single subject is worth paying a specialist rate for?
faqs.answer: The one where marks are being lost on a specific component, not the one with the lowest overall grade. A student at 4 in Chemistry Higher Level who is losing most of those marks on the data-based paper needs a Chemistry specialist for a handful of hours. A student at 5 across four subjects usually needs study-habit work, which is a cheaper purchase. Spending the specialist rate on everything is the most common overspend in this market, and spending it on nothing is the second.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor at AED 60 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a defined job. Published budget bands start at AED 33 to AED 52 and AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, and that money buys supervised practice: someone keeping a student at the desk, checking homework is done, answering straightforward questions. For a Middle Years student who works well but not consistently, that is often exactly the problem. It does not buy Higher Level subject expertise, and using it for a Diploma paper-technique problem means paying four times for an effect you will not get.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move one IB grade?
faqs.answer: Nobody can honestly quote a number, because it depends on what is missing. What can be said is where the hours cluster. A procedural weakness such as uncertainty handling in Physics or diagram labelling in Economics typically takes three to six hours and then stops needing attention. A conceptual gap carried from the Middle Years takes a term. A whole subject behind takes two. Any provider quoting a guaranteed grade gain for a fixed hour count is selling something they cannot deliver, and we do not publish such a figure.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Al Ain need a permit, and does it cost extra?
faqs.answer: They need one, and it costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion. Because it is free, no tutor can price the permit into their rate. Working without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at an Al Ain school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Not for payment. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the permit. Any arrangement that places your child with their own classroom teacher privately puts both parties at risk, and a provider offering it as a selling point is offering something it should not. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document.

faqs.question: What exactly can an IB Gram tutor do on my child's Chemistry IA in Al Khabisi?
faqs.answer: They can explain what each published criterion rewards, question whether the chosen method can support the analysis the criteria ask for, point out where a conclusion does not follow from the data, flag missing evaluation of uncertainty, and mark your child's own draft against the criteria. They cannot write a sentence that goes into the submission, rewrite a paragraph rather than comment on it, or hand over a research question or dataset as finished work. Completed assessments are sold in this market at around AED 3,750, and submitting one puts the entire Diploma at risk under the IB's academic-honesty rules.

faqs.question: Are tutoring rates higher closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens more than headline rates move, and the effect on a family's bill is the same. From the second term of Year 13 the specialists with good slots are booked, so what is left is either a worse match or a worse time. Families who start then also tend to buy more hours to compensate for the shorter runway, which is where the real increase shows up. Beginning a term earlier at the same hourly rate is the cheapest available decision, because an hour eight weeks out does more than an hour three weeks out.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Al Ain students actually sit?
faqs.answer: IB Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session. For Cambridge International qualifications, UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, a detail several tutoring sites get wrong for Gulf families. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so always work from the school's zone version and the live official timetable.

faqs.question: How do I avoid paying for a tutor who does not know the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions before the first session and insist on specifics. Which subject and which level have you taught, how recently, and for how many cohorts? Which components do your students most often lose marks on, and what do you do about it? What will you ask my child to do between sessions? A tutor who answers those with syllabus-level detail is a specialist. A tutor who answers with reassurance is a generalist, which may be fine at the budget band and is not worth AED 300 an hour.

faqs.question: Is a group class better value than one-to-one for an Al Khabisi family?
faqs.answer: On price per hour, obviously. On price per outcome, only when every student in the group has the same gap. A group of four working through a whole syllabus suits a cohort revising broadly, and it is poor value for a student who is secure everywhere except Paper 3 extended response, because most of the hour addresses someone else's problem. Our delivery is one-to-one for that reason. If a group is what the budget allows, pick one organised by topic rather than by subject, and ask what the group's actual starting point is.

faqs.question: What should we have in hand by the end of the trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they are yours whether or not you continue. First, the name of the specific weakness and the component where it shows up, such as calculus notation in Paper 1 or uncertainty treatment in the data questions. Second, an honest estimate of how many hours closing it takes. Third, the practice the tutor expects between sessions. The trial is a full session with the tutor who would teach the course, no card is required, and if the match is wrong we change the tutor rather than asking your child to adapt.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies need to be in the tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: Decide early rather than in March. Every UAE private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, so these sit on top of a Diploma student's six subjects. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines, which set the sector pattern, require separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so support must work through the school's own material.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.closingHeading: Start with one subject, one weakness and a number you can budget
al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB home tutor in Al Khabisi against online one-to-one, the deciding figures are on this page: AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online against AED 180 to AED 500 in home, and roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month for a weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor. The cheapest effective route from Al Khabisi is usually a short, diagnosed block in the one subject that is actually losing marks, bought early rather than in the final month. Book a free trial lesson, bring a recent mock paper, and leave with a named weakness and an hour estimate. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.tutorsIntro: Tutors below are matched to a subject, a level and a time of day. A Diploma student arriving home at twenty past five needs a tutor who holds a six o'clock slot every week, and that constraint is part of the match rather than an afterthought.

intro.heading: The real question in Al Maqam is what time, not who
paragraphs: Al Maqam sits on the southern side of Al Ain, spread out across newer villa compounds, and the distances inside it are larger than the city's central districts. Students from here attend schools across the city, and once an after-school commitment and the drive home are counted, a Diploma day frequently ends after five. That single fact decides most of what a tutoring plan can contain, and almost nothing published about tutoring in this market acknowledges it.

Work it through. A Higher Level student with six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment has a finite number of evenings. If the first usable hour begins at six and the student is genuinely done by half past nine, there are perhaps two weekday sessions available in a week before something else gives way. Families who book three and expect four are not planning, they are hoping.

This is why the common matching question is the wrong way round. Asking who can come to Al Maqam on a Tuesday produces a short list of people whose own driving schedule happens to fit, and their subject is whatever it is. Asking who teaches Chemistry Higher Level and holds a six o'clock Tuesday slot every week produces a list of specialists, because the slot is negotiable in a way that a car journey is not.

Al Maqam is part of Al Ain, which sits in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's listing is the right place to confirm which programmes a school is licensed to deliver and how it has been inspected, and it matters here because Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's.

The scarcity that follows from that smaller school set lands hardest on exactly the subjects a Diploma student is most likely to need: Higher Level sciences and the less common languages. Combine thin local supply with a southern address and a narrow evening window and the in-home arithmetic stops working. The tutor who can reach Al Maqam at seven on a Wednesday is rarely also the person who has taught Physics Higher Level for six cohorts.

IB Gram's answer is one-to-one live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, matched on subject and level. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For an Al Maqam family the practical gain is specific rather than philosophical: the session starts when the student sits down, it does not depend on a route across the city, and it moves when the week does.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.programmesIntro: Each stage of the IB continuum makes different demands on the week, and the school-day constraint bites in a different place in each. These are the parts of the programme an Al Maqam family is most often inside.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The workload is the defining feature rather than the difficulty of any single part, and the externally marked papers and internally assessed components run on separate clocks. A tutoring plan that ignores the student's total weekly load will be abandoned by February whatever its subject merits.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Maqam Diploma family the binding constraint is the number of usable evenings, so each session has to be aimed precisely from marked work rather than spent on general review. Two well-aimed hours a week beat four vague ones, and they are also the only two that will actually happen. Al Ain's smaller private-school set makes Higher Level science specialists scarce locally, which is a second reason to fix the subject match first and negotiate the time second.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with an ePortfolio and the Personal Project in the final year. Parents see criterion levels rather than percentages and often cannot judge whether a 5 is comfortable or fragile. The translation work is the tutoring: which criterion is losing marks, and what a level 7 response looks like in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years is when an Al Maqam family still has room in the week, and that makes it the cheapest stage at which to fix anything. A fortnightly session in Years 9 and 10 fits comfortably around a southern Al Ain school run, which a twice-weekly Diploma plan does not. Families who use that window rarely need a rescue in Year 13, when there are no spare evenings left to put one in.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with the Exhibition in the final year and no external assessment. Useful support at this stage is narrow and mechanical rather than broad: number fluency, reading stamina, written structure. Short sessions work better than long ones, and two half-hours a week outperform one ninety-minute block for most primary-age children.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in Al Maqam have the easiest scheduling of anyone on this page and should use it. Early-afternoon sessions are genuinely available before the senior school run begins, and those slots disappear permanently once a child moves to a school on the far side of the city. The summer before Year 7 is the single best-placed block in a primary child's schedule.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.ageRange: Diploma year one into year two
programmes.description: The coursework strand runs on school-set internal deadlines and needs concentrated attention rather than weekly attention. Each piece is marked against published criteria and the decisive moment is early: a methodology or research question that cannot support the required analysis caps the mark before any writing happens. Support is reading, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts.
programmes.countryNote: Because coursework hours are concentrated rather than spread, they fit an Al Maqam week far better than families expect. Four to six sessions clustered around the school's internal deadlines, mostly on methodology, can sit on weekend mornings and leave the weekday evenings for subject teaching. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline list in September and place those blocks deliberately.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.subjectsIntro: Where the hour goes differs by subject, and for an Al Maqam family with two usable evenings the choice of which subject gets one of them is the whole decision. These are the subjects we are asked for, with what the session has to do.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the Higher Level Paper 3 extended-response problems. Marks go on method lines skipped under time pressure and on calculus notation. The most requested single subject from this area and the one where a general tutor is most visibly not enough.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and mandatory graphical calculator technique. Failures tend to be procedural rather than conceptual, which makes it a good candidate for a short block rather than a standing weekly slot in a crowded week.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, organic mechanisms and the data-based paper. Organic content lands late in the course, so a student can look secure in October and meet the hardest material with no runway. Among the scarcest Higher Level subjects in the Al Ain pool.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields, with Higher Level extension topics late in year two. A large share of lost marks are unit handling, significant figures and uncertainty treatment, which a specialist fixes in a handful of sessions. Good value for a family with few available evenings.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content heavy and command-term sensitive. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'discuss' carry different mark allocations, and students who revise content without revising command terms stall. Well supplied online, so the slot can usually be chosen to suit the commute.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world evidence and three commentaries forming the Internal Assessment on school-set dates. Higher Level adds quantitative questions rewarding technique over reading. Responds quickly to a few sessions on diagram labelling and evaluation structure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, the comparative essay and the Individual Oral, which the school schedules earlier than most parents expect. The Oral is coached rather than taught, and it works particularly well in a video session because the component is entirely talk.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks applied to a real organisation plus a Higher Level research project with its own timeline. Students describe companies where the mark scheme wants application, and the correction is structural so it transfers across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Timed productive skills and a scheduled individual oral. These are the less commonly taught languages in Al Ain's school set, so in-home availability from a southern address is close to non-existent and online is usually the only route to a subject-trained teacher.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay with a firm internal deadline and an exhibition earlier in the course. Both reward argument structure rather than content, so a small number of concentrated hours changes the grade and further hours add very little.

sections.heading: When the school day actually ends for an Al Maqam student
paragraphs: The useful number is not the final bell, it is the moment a student is home, fed and able to hold an argument about calculus. For many Al Maqam families that is somewhere between half past five and half past six on a weekday, and nothing in a tutoring plan should be scheduled before it. The table below works through the stages, which is a calculation no competitor page in this market performs.

Two of the stages are invisible in a timetable and dominate the result. After-school commitments, including the Creativity, Activity, Service element that every Diploma student carries, routinely add an hour. And the journey from the central or northern clusters to a southern compound is not a fixed figure; it stretches at the end of the working day in a way that a morning run does not.

The practical consequence is that an Al Maqam family planning around a four o'clock session is planning around a slot that does not exist, and a family planning around seven is planning around a slot that exists but produces poor work. The honest window is narrow, and it is better to use one hour well inside it than to pretend there are three.

This is also why weekend mornings matter more here than they do in the central districts. A Saturday morning session from Al Maqam is the same hour a central family can get on a Tuesday afternoon: fresh, unhurried and long enough for a full timed paper. Treating the weekend as the main slot rather than the overflow is the single most useful scheduling change available to this area.

sections.heading: Building a Diploma week that actually survives
paragraphs: Here is the week most Al Maqam Diploma families should be running, written as a shape rather than a prescription. The organising principle is that hard new work goes where the student is fresh and review goes where they are tired, which in this area means the weekend carries the load and the weekday evening does the follow-up.

The second principle is that practice tasks have to be sized for the evening they will be done in. A tutor who sets a full past paper for a Tuesday night in Al Maqam has set something that will not be done, and the session that follows will be spent discussing why. A single question section, marked, is worth more than a paper attempted at eleven o'clock.

The third is that one of the week's slots should be left empty on purpose. Mock weeks, school trips, illness and travel all happen, and a week with no slack loses sessions permanently rather than moving them. A plan built at ninety per cent capacity delivers more sessions across a year than one built at a hundred.

Note the final column. The point of writing a week down is to be able to see what it cannot hold, which is usually a second subject. Families who want two subjects supported should look at the holiday block option rather than trying to find a third evening that is not there.

Write the week down on paper and show it to the student. Diploma students are better judges of their own capacity than their parents are, and they will tell you which evening is already gone. A plan the student helped build is a plan that survives March, which matters more than any refinement of its contents.

sections.heading: Which schools Al Maqam feeds, and what their Diploma students need
paragraphs: Al Maqam students split between the southern school cluster and the central one, and the split matters because it determines the journey. For families at a southern school the run is manageable and a six o'clock start is comfortable. For those travelling to the central cluster it is not, and that group should plan around a weekend-led week from the outset.

Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and that shows up in subject offerings as much as in numbers. Higher Level science groups are smaller, which means less in-school support when a student struggles, and the less commonly taught languages may not be offered at all or may run with a single teacher. Those are the gaps that bring families to this page.

Before relying on anything about a school, read ADEK's own listing. It records what each school is licensed to deliver and the outcome of its inspections, and it is the authority rather than a school's own prospectus. If you are choosing a school as well as a tutor, start the comparison there; if you are already enrolled, it is still the right place to check what the Diploma offering actually includes.

One thing not to do is treat a school's published results as a guide to whether your child needs support. A strong cohort average tells you nothing about an individual student's Paper 2 technique, and a weaker one tells you nothing either. The useful document is your child's own marked work, which is why we ask for it before matching anyone.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a visiting tutor in southern Al Ain
paragraphs: The search phrase says home tutor, so here is the comparison made properly, built around the thing this page is about: whether the session happens at the hour it was meant to. Cost is in the table, but it is not the decisive row for a family in Al Maqam.

The decisive row is the tutor's own journey. A visiting tutor arrives after finishing a previous household and crossing the city, which on a southern round trip costs them something like forty unbilled minutes. That is why the UAE in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor: the driving is real and someone pays for it. It also means the arrangement is pinned to a route, so the slot is theirs rather than yours.

The second decisive row is what happens to a plan over thirty weeks. An arrangement that loses a session a month to a long drive, a late finish or a route change delivers around thirty sessions in a school year where a reliable one delivers forty. Ten sessions is an entire technique block, which is worth more than any improvement in the room.

The third is match. With Higher Level sciences and the less common languages thin across the whole city, a visiting arrangement from Al Maqam usually means accepting the available person rather than the right one. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, so on the in-home axis we are not an option at all, and the table says so.

sections.heading: Ramadan, shortened days and the slot that appears
paragraphs: Ramadan changes the Al Maqam timetable in a way that is, unusually, an improvement. Shortened school days mean students get home earlier, and for a family whose problem is the length of the commute that creates afternoon capacity which does not otherwise exist during term. The month falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so check it against the plan rather than assuming.

The right adjustment is to move sessions, not to pause them. Post-iftar slots suit many households, and an earlier afternoon slot suits others; what fails is treating the month as ordinary and then losing four sessions in a row to fatigue and last-minute cancellation. Agree the Ramadan shape with the tutor a fortnight ahead, not on the first day.

The same logic applies to every other break in the UAE academic year. Mid-year holidays and the long summer remove the commute entirely and make morning sessions available, which is the one thing an Al Maqam family cannot buy during term. A concentrated block in those windows is the cheapest way for this area to accumulate hours.

One warning about breaks. Internal coursework deadlines sometimes fall close to a holiday, which means a student loses either the break or the marks. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline list in September, mark the school breaks on the same calendar and look for collisions. A collision spotted in September is a scheduling note; the same collision found in February is a ruined week.

sections.heading: ADEK, and who is allowed to teach your child privately
paragraphs: Al Maqam is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, which is itself worth noticing when judging how locally informed a tutoring site is.

The rule with the most direct effect on an Al Maqam family is about their child's own teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the same thing. A tutor who pitches on the basis of teaching at your child's school is offering an arrangement to decline.

Separately, private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified. For completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge International, and a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing entirely.

sections.heading: Coursework support that fits an Al Maqam week
paragraphs: Coursework is the part of the Diploma that suits this area's constraints best, because the hours are concentrated rather than weekly and can sit on a weekend morning. The Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay are marked against published criteria, and the decisive work happens early, before any writing.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial and worth paying for. They can explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a chosen method can support the analysis the criteria demand, point out where a conclusion does not follow from the data, identify missing evaluation, teach citation properly and mark the student's own draft against the criteria. Most of that belongs in the first weeks of the cycle.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of the submission, rewrite rather than comment, or supply a research question or dataset as finished work. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750; submitting one risks the whole Diploma under the IB's academic-honesty rules, which makes it the worst available use of any tutoring budget.

The scheduling advice follows from the honesty position. Front-load the hours onto methodology in the first fortnight of the cycle, where four sessions outperform twenty at the end, and the late-night panic conversation never arrives. For an Al Maqam family that also means the coursework block uses weekend mornings and leaves weekday evenings intact for subject teaching.

sections.heading: What we can and cannot cover from this area
paragraphs: Availability transparency is absent from every competitor page reviewed for this project, so here is ours, stated as a constraint rather than a feature. Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English are well supplied and can usually be matched inside a week in any slot. Chemistry Higher Level and Physics Higher Level are tighter. Spanish B and French B are thin, and often declined.

The second constraint is the slot itself. The six to eight o'clock weekday band is the narrowest part of the week and it is narrow for every family in Al Ain, so it fills first. An Al Maqam family willing to use a weekend morning or an earlier Friday slot gets a materially wider choice of tutor, and in the scarce subjects that choice is the difference between a specialist and a wait.

When we cannot cover a request we give a date or decline. We do not fill a Chemistry Higher Level request with a general science tutor or a language request with a fluent speaker who has not taught the course. That substitution survives about a month and then costs a term, and it is the most common concealed failure in this market.

Ask the same of anyone you are considering. Can you cover this subject, at this level, in this slot, starting when, and what happens if the first tutor is not right. Specific answers make a provider comparable. In a city with a school set this size, an unqualified yes to every question is not an answer.

process.title: Tell us when the student is actually free
process.description: Not the school's finish time but the hour at which they are home, fed and able to concentrate, and which days carry an after-school commitment. For an Al Maqam family that usually produces one weekday evening and a weekend morning, and knowing it up front means we only propose tutors who hold those slots every week.

process.title: Send a marked paper with the subject
process.description: A marked paper shows which questions were attempted and which were blank, and those point to different problems with different durations. With one usable evening a week, choosing the right subject matters more here than almost anywhere, and that choice should come from evidence rather than from a report grade.

process.title: Free trial in the real slot
process.description: A full session, no card required, held at the time the actual lessons would run. That matters: a trial at four on a Saturday tells you nothing about whether your child can work at half past six on a Wednesday. The output is a named weakness, an hour estimate and a week shape you can keep.

process.title: Build the week with slack in it
process.description: One protected slot, one working slot and one left deliberately clear so clashes move sessions rather than deleting them. Practice tasks are sized for a tired evening after a long run, which is why they are single question sections rather than full papers.

process.title: Use the holidays for the volume
process.description: Concentrated morning blocks in school breaks are the only way an Al Maqam family can buy a meaningful number of hours, and the summer between Diploma years is the largest. We plan those deliberately rather than treating term time as the only place tutoring happens.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling treated as part of the match
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed only if they hold your child's realistic slot every week, because a specialist available at a time your child cannot use is not available. For a southern Al Ain address that filter removes most of the field before anything else is discussed.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that move instead of disappearing
whyPoints.description: Mock weeks, travel, illness and Ramadan timings all require movement, and an online slot moves in a message. Over a school year that is the difference between about forty sessions delivered and about thirty, which is a whole technique block.

whyPoints.title: Weekend mornings treated as the main slot
whyPoints.description: For Al Maqam the weekend morning is the equivalent of a central family's weekday afternoon: fresh, unhurried and long enough for a full timed paper. We plan around it rather than offering it as overflow.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that service exists only in India. On the in-home axis we are the wrong choice and we say so at the top of the page rather than after a deposit has been taken.

whyPoints.title: Subject scarcity named, not concealed
whyPoints.description: Higher Level sciences and the less common languages are thin across Al Ain because the private-school set is small. We say which requests need booking in the autumn, and we give a date or decline rather than substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals or invented figures
whyPoints.description: No accreditation or partnership claimed from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, no self-generated ratings, no guaranteed grades, and no statistic without a named source and a date.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start in Al Maqam on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Around six for most Diploma students, and later for those travelling from the central cluster. Work it through rather than guessing: the school day ends, an after-school or CAS commitment can add an hour, the journey to a southern compound stretches at the end of the working day, and then there is eating and settling. Anything scheduled before that window produces a session nobody gets value from. The honest conclusion is one good weekday hour rather than two mediocre ones, with a weekend morning carrying the heavier work.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week can a Diploma student in Al Maqam actually sustain?
faqs.answer: Two, in most cases, and one of those is better placed at the weekend. A Higher Level student with six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and a CAS commitment has limited evening capacity, and a southern commute removes the earliest usable hour. Plans built for three weekday sessions tend to deliver two and then collapse in February. Building for two, with a third evening left deliberately clear to absorb clashes, delivers more sessions across the year than building for three.

faqs.question: Why does a weekend morning work better than a weekday evening here?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only fresh, unhurried block an Al Maqam family has during term. A Saturday morning session is the equivalent of the Tuesday afternoon a family next to the school can use: long enough for a full timed paper, early enough that the student is not already tired, and unaffected by the journey that defines their weekdays. The sensible shape is the weekend morning for hard new work and timed papers, and a weekday evening afterwards for marking and correction.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa in Al Maqam?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Maqam students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We state that before any booking because the phrase families search is 'home tutor' and nobody should find out the format afterwards. If an adult physically present is a requirement, hire locally, ask about the MoHRE permit category and book the latest slot the tutor has rather than the earliest.

faqs.question: Which subject should get our one weekday slot?
faqs.answer: The one where a marked paper shows a specific, diagnosable loss, not the one with the lowest overall grade. A student at 4 in Chemistry Higher Level losing most of those marks on the data-based paper has a narrow problem a specialist can address in a few sessions. A student at 5 across four subjects usually has a study-habit problem, which is a different and cheaper purchase. Send the marked paper first; with only one usable evening a week, choosing the wrong subject costs a term and not just an hour.

faqs.question: How does a visiting tutor's own journey affect our session time?
faqs.answer: It pushes it later and makes it fragile. A tutor reaching a southern Al Ain compound arrives after finishing a previous household and crossing the city, losing something like forty unbilled minutes on the round trip. That is part of why the UAE in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 online. It also means the slot belongs to the route rather than to your evening, so a change at the other end of the city becomes your problem.

faqs.question: Can we use the school holidays to catch up instead of term time?
faqs.answer: It is the best option available to this area and the most underused. During a break the commute disappears, which makes morning sessions possible for the first time, and morning work is categorically better than evening work for content repair. A block of six to twelve sessions across a holiday buys more real learning than the same hours spread thinly through a term. The summer between Diploma years is the largest such window, with no competing coursework deadlines, and families who use it rarely need a spring rescue.

faqs.question: How should we handle sessions during Ramadan in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Move them rather than pausing them, and agree the shape a fortnight ahead. Shortened school days often create afternoon capacity that a long Al Maqam commute normally consumes, so for some families the month is actually easier to schedule than an ordinary term. Post-iftar slots work well for others. Ramadan falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so check it against the plan before the term begins. What fails is treating the month as ordinary and then losing four consecutive sessions to fatigue and cancellation.

faqs.question: Why do you ask for a marked paper before matching a tutor?
faqs.answer: Because a report grade says where a student is and a marked paper says why. We sort losses into four kinds: blank questions, method errors, timing failures and mark-scheme phrasing. Blanks mean content, which takes a term. Method errors and phrasing mean technique, which takes hours. Those have different durations, different costs and in some cases different tutors, and the distinction cannot be made from a grade. With one usable weekday evening, starting from evidence is worth more here than anywhere.

faqs.question: Can a tutor at my child's own Al Ain school teach them privately?
faqs.answer: Not for payment. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the same thing. Teachers who tutor outside school hours must hold that permit. If a tutor's pitch rests on teaching at your child's school, that is a reason to decline rather than a credential, and the current wording should be checked against ADEK's own published policy document.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL harder to find a tutor for in southern Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Harder to find anywhere in Al Ain, and the southern address compounds it. The city's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the number of teachers who have taken Higher Level Physics cohorts through to examination is modest. Add a long drive and a narrow six-to-eight evening band and in-home options thin out almost entirely. Book Higher Level sciences in the autumn term of Year 13 at the latest, and if you can use a weekend morning the choice of specialist widens considerably.

faqs.question: What practice should a tutor set for a weeknight after a long commute?
faqs.answer: One question section, marked and brought to the next session. Not a full past paper. A tutor who sets a two-hour paper for a Tuesday evening in Al Maqam has set something that will not be done, and the following session gets spent discussing why rather than on the subject. The working loop matters more than the volume: a single section attempted properly, marked honestly and corrected in the next hour moves a grade. Full papers belong on the weekend morning, where there is time and a fresh head.

faqs.question: How do coursework hours fit a week with no spare evenings?
faqs.answer: Better than subject teaching does, because coursework hours are concentrated rather than weekly. Four to six sessions clustered around the school's internal deadlines, mostly on methodology before any writing starts, can sit entirely on weekend mornings and leave weekday evenings for subject work. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline list in September and place the blocks deliberately. Front-loading matters: four sessions in the first fortnight of a cycle outperform twenty at the end, and they remove the late-night panic entirely.

faqs.question: What happens if the slot we need is already taken?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give a date rather than filling it with someone unsuitable. The six to eight o'clock weekday band is the narrowest part of the week across the whole of Al Ain, so it books out first, and in scarce subjects such as Higher Level Chemistry or a second language the wait can run to a fortnight or more. Families able to use a weekend morning or an earlier Friday slot see a materially wider choice of tutor immediately. What we will not do is substitute across specifications to keep a booking alive.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.closingHeading: Send us the hour your child is actually free
al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.closingBody: Hiring an IB home tutor in Al Maqam works when the plan is built from the real timetable rather than an idealised one. Tell us what time your child gets home, which days carry an after-school commitment, and which subject a marked paper says is losing the marks. We will propose a tutor who holds that slot every week, usually a weekend morning for the heavy work and one weekday evening for marking, and leave a third evening clear so clashes move sessions instead of deleting them. The free trial runs at the real time, with no card required. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
