intro.heading: The problem in Al Mutaredh is sequence, not scheduling
paragraphs: Al Mutaredh is central, minutes from several of Al Ain's larger private schools, and families here have something most of the city does not: a usable weekday afternoon. A student can be home by four and working by half past, which means two or three real sessions a week are genuinely possible rather than theoretically possible. That is a considerable advantage and it quietly creates its own problem.

The problem is that available time gets used late. When the week has room in it, there is no pressure to decide anything in Year 12, and the plan that forms by default is to start tutoring when something goes wrong. Something usually goes wrong in the spring of Year 13, by which point the cheapest and most effective windows have gone and the family is buying recovery rather than progress.

So this page is organised as a sequence rather than as a run-in. It maps the Diploma across its full twenty-four months, names the three core deadlines that sit outside the subject timetable and catch almost every family, and says which subjects book out in which month. The aim is that a Year 12 family in Al Mutaredh spends less overall and gets more, by putting hours where they do work.

One honest limitation. This page publishes no IB session or results dates. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a tutoring page carrying a date that is wrong by a week is worse than one carrying none. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; for specifics, ask the school's Diploma coordinator or read the IB's assessment pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates, which are sourced, appear further down.

Al Mutaredh is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's listing is where to confirm what a school is licensed to deliver and how it has been inspected, and it is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project.

IB Gram teaches Al Mutaredh students one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a family with good weekday availability the practical benefit is choice rather than logistics: the shortlist is every available teacher of the subject at that level, rather than those who can reach the neighbourhood.

The planning here works whoever you hire. The twenty-four month map, the three core deadlines and the booking order for scarce subjects all apply to a tutor an Al Mutaredh family finds locally, and the review discipline costs nothing to adopt. What we sell is the teaching; the sequence is simply what the course requires.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mutaredh.programmesIntro: Each part of the continuum has a different natural sequence, and knowing where the decisive points sit is most of the value a parent can add. These are the stages an Al Mutaredh family will be inside.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The externally marked papers arrive in one window and the internally assessed components arrive on school-set dates spread across two years. Treating those as one timeline is the single most common planning error, and it is the one that produces a difficult spring.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Mutaredh family's advantage is that the week has room in it, which makes a long, light plan genuinely possible: one session a week from the autumn of Year 12, rather than four a week from February of Year 13. That shape costs less in total and achieves more, because content work in Year 12 sits where there is time to consolidate it. Al Ain's smaller private-school set also makes Higher Level science specialists scarce, so an early booking secures a better match.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria out of eight, with an ePortfolio and the Personal Project in the final year. The sequence here is driven by school reporting cycles and by the Personal Project, which is a process assessment: the marks come from documented planning and reflection as much as from the final product.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Mutaredh family the Middle Years is the period in which to fix anything structural, because the weekday afternoon exists and the Diploma workload does not yet. Years 9 and 10 are the cheapest place in the whole school career to close a maths or writing gap, and families who use them rarely find themselves buying Diploma recovery three years later.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with the Exhibition in the final year and no external assessment. The sequence question here is simply when a specific skill gap becomes a barrier, which is usually at the transition into the Middle Years. Reading stamina, written structure and number fluency are the three worth watching for.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in Al Mutaredh have the easiest scheduling in the city, with genuine mid-afternoon availability. The honest advice is still to buy narrowly: two short sessions a week on one named skill rather than a general weekly hour. The summer before Year 7 is the best-placed block, before the senior timetable arrives and the week becomes a negotiation.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS
programmes.description: The three core requirements run on school-set internal dates and together they account for most of the deadline pressure a Diploma student feels. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, and Creativity, Activity, Service requires documented engagement over time rather than a submission at the end.
programmes.countryNote: These are the deadlines Al Mutaredh families most often meet by surprise, because none of them is set by the IB calendar a parent might find online; the school sets them. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal date list at the start of Year 12, put all three on one calendar alongside school breaks, and look for the collisions. A collision found in September is a note; the same one found in February ruins a fortnight.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mutaredh.subjectsIntro: Each subject has a stage at which support does most good, determined by when its hardest content arrives and when its internally assessed component falls. These are the subjects Al Mutaredh families request.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level content continues to the end of the course, so content support stays useful later here than elsewhere. The best-value window is the autumn of Year 12 for algebraic foundations and the second term of Year 13 for Paper 3 practice, with little need in between if the first went well.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The route decision against Analysis and Approaches has to be made in Year 11, because switching later costs a term the course does not have. After that, statistics and calculator technique are best drilled early and maintained rather than revisited in a panic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and the harder energetics arrive late, so a student can look secure in October of Year 13 and struggle in February. The booking window that matters is the autumn of Year 13, which is also when Al Ain's scarce Higher Level chemistry teachers are still available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level extension topics land late, while the data-handling skills that carry easy marks can be fixed at almost any point. That split makes Physics unusually forgiving on sequence, and a short block on uncertainty works even close to the session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content heavy, so consolidation belongs in Year 12 and the summer between years. Command-term work pays in any month and is the obvious thing to buy if a family is starting late, because it transfers across every question in the paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries forming the Internal Assessment, spread across Year 12 and into Year 13 on school-set dates, each needing a current article. These are the dates that catch families out, because each commentary is a small project rather than a piece of homework.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is scheduled by the school, often earlier than parents expect, and it is coached rather than taught. Ask for its date in the autumn term; preparation needs three or four sessions and cannot be improvised the week before.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A Higher Level research project with its own timeline, plus framework application for the papers. The project needs an organisation and a question agreed early; late starts here are more salvageable than in the sciences but still cost marks.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Scheduled individual oral assessment plus timed productive skills. These are the least commonly taught languages in Al Ain's school set, which means booking has to happen earlier than for any other subject, not later.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word prescribed-title essay with a firm internal deadline, and an exhibition earlier in the course. Both reward argument structure rather than content, so three or four concentrated hours change the grade and further hours add almost nothing.

sections.heading: The Diploma as a twenty-four month sequence
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes the Diploma as a two-year map, which is strange, because that is the form in which a family actually makes decisions. The table below runs from the start of Year 12 to the session, with what each stage needs and what it costs to skip. It contains no IB dates, for the reason given at the top of this page.

Read the second column as the point of the exercise. The early stages need small amounts of the right thing: foundation repair, habit setting, a defensible research question. The late stages need large amounts of a different thing: timed practice, mark-scheme discipline, triage. Families who buy late are buying from the right-hand side of the table only, and the left-hand side cannot be bought retrospectively.

The stage families most often skip entirely is the summer between Year 12 and Year 13. It is the largest block of uncommitted time in the whole course, with no coursework deadlines and no timetable, and it is precisely where a content gap named in the Year 12 reports can be closed properly. In Al Mutaredh, where the week already has room, this is the cheapest eight weeks available.

The stage families most often overbuy is the final fortnight. The instinct is to add hours as the papers approach; the evidence from marked work usually says fewer new inputs, more self-marking and earlier nights. A provider proposing extra sessions in the last week without pointing at a script is responding to anxiety rather than to the student.

sections.heading: The three core deadlines nobody warns you about
paragraphs: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service sit outside the subject timetable, are set by the school rather than by any public calendar, and between them account for most of the deadline pressure a Diploma student feels. Almost every family we speak to has met at least one of them by surprise.

The Extended Essay is the biggest single piece of independent work in the Diploma, capped at 4,000 words, with a supervisor who has limited contact time. Its decisive moment is the research question: too broad and it cannot be answered in the space, too narrow and there is nothing to analyse. That decision happens in Year 12 and determines the ceiling of the mark.

The Theory of Knowledge essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title, and the commonest failure is simply not answering the title as set. It rewards argument structure rather than content, which means a student who writes well in their subjects can still score poorly, and three or four focused hours are usually the entire sensible intervention.

Creativity, Activity, Service is the one that quietly fails. It requires documented engagement over time, so it cannot be completed late, and a student who leaves the record empty until Year 13 has a problem no tutor can solve. Ask the Diploma coordinator for all three internal date lists at the start of Year 12 and put them on one calendar with the school breaks marked.

sections.heading: Having time is not the same as using it
paragraphs: This is the specific trap for a central Al Ain family, and it is worth naming plainly because it is invisible while it is happening. When the week has room, nothing forces a decision. Sessions can always start next term, the Extended Essay can always be thought about after the holidays, and the student is coping, which is the most expensive word in the Diploma.

Coping in Year 12 looks identical to thriving. A student can be two marks from a 6 in three subjects, carrying a Middle Years algebra gap that nobody has noticed, and still be reported as doing fine. The gap appears when Higher Level content arrives in Year 13 and the foundation is asked to carry something heavier, which is a predictable failure on a predictable schedule.

The practical answer is to create artificial decision points, because the calendar will not supply them. Three reviews a year, each triggered by a date rather than by a problem, at the start of Year 12, the end of Year 12 and after mocks. At each one, look at marked work rather than reports and ask whether anything needs buying. Often the answer is no, which is itself worth knowing.

The second answer is to use the weekday advantage for the right thing. An Al Mutaredh family's extra sessions should go into Year 12 content and coursework methodology, not into a heavier Year 13. Front-loading is what the available time is actually good for, and it is the opposite of what a family with spare evenings tends to do.

sections.heading: The rhythm of a UAE school year, and where tutoring fits
paragraphs: A Diploma plan has to survive the actual academic year rather than an idealised one, and the UAE year has features that generic advice ignores. Terms, mid-year breaks, Ramadan and a long summer each change what tutoring can achieve in a given month, and the table lays out the useful shape.

Ramadan deserves its own note because it moves. It falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so in some years it sits inside the heaviest revision block and in others it does not. Shortened school days can free afternoon capacity, and post-iftar slots suit many households. What fails is treating the month as ordinary and then losing four consecutive sessions to fatigue and cancellation; agree the shape a fortnight ahead.

The summer is the other distinctive feature and the more consequential one. It is long, it is uncommitted, and for a Year 12 student it is the only period in the Diploma with no competing deadlines. Content repair done there consolidates in a way that the same hours spread through a term cannot, because consecutive days allow a topic to be built rather than revisited.

The third feature is that internal deadlines do not always respect breaks. A submission falling immediately after a holiday means a student loses either the break or the marks. That is a collision worth finding in September, when it is a scheduling note, rather than in February, when it is a ruined fortnight.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson dates, for students sitting both
paragraphs: Some Al Mutaredh students carry Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside or before the Diploma, and those calendars are sourced and can be published. One widely repeated claim about Cambridge is wrong for this country, and acting on it would mean a missed entry.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates keep their years because they are backward-looking and that is what makes them checkable.

For anything forward-looking the rule is to name a series by its month and check the live official timetable, since Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. That is also why this page names the IB's May session without a date: the discipline is the same, and a tutoring site is not a source of record for either board or for the IB.

sections.heading: When each subject books out
paragraphs: Sequence applies to availability as well as to learning, and this is the part of the calendar nobody publishes. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the city's pool of Diploma teachers is modest and the scarce subjects fill in a predictable order each year. Knowing that order is worth money to a family with the luxury of planning ahead.

The pattern is consistent. Higher Level sciences go first, from the autumn of Year 13, because demand peaks exactly when the hardest content arrives. The less commonly taught languages go earlier still and sometimes are never available, because the teaching population for them is tiny. Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English remain matchable through the year.

For an Al Mutaredh family the practical instruction is simple: book the scarce subjects in the autumn and treat the plentiful ones as plentiful. That means refusing both a premium rate and a long wait for Mathematics or Biology, and accepting a named start date rather than a substitution for Chemistry Higher Level.

When we cannot cover a request we give a date or decline. We do not fill a Higher Level science request with a general science tutor, or a language request with a fluent speaker who has not taught the course. That substitution survives about a month and then costs a term, and it is the most common concealed failure in this market.

One nuance about coursework supervision. Those blocks cluster around school deadlines, which means every family at the same school wants the same fortnight. Taking the block a week earlier than the crowd, rather than a week later, is usually possible and always better, because methodology work is more useful before the deadline looms than after.

sections.heading: ADEK, permits and verification
paragraphs: Al Mutaredh is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's own listing is the authority on what a school is licensed to deliver and how it has been inspected, and it should be read in preference to a school's own account.

Private tutoring runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion.

One restriction bears directly on a central Al Ain family, where the school is close enough that staff and families overlap socially. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars the same. A tutor whose pitch rests on teaching at your child's school is offering an arrangement to decline.

Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any quoted amount is unverified. For the record: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge International, and we do not describe any tutor as an examiner without current evidenced status.

sections.heading: Coursework support, placed where it works
paragraphs: Coursework is the clearest case for sequencing, because the same number of hours produces entirely different results depending on when they are spent. Four sessions in the first fortnight of an Internal Assessment cycle, aimed at the method and the question, outperform twenty sessions at the end aimed at the writing.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial: explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a chosen method can support the analysis the criteria demand, point out where a conclusion does not follow from the data, identify missing evaluation, teach citation properly, and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. Most of that belongs early.

What a tutor must not do is write any part of the submission, rewrite rather than comment, or supply a research question or dataset as finished work. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750. That is the purchase a family makes under deadline pressure, and front-loading the hours is what removes the pressure.

We also will not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. The correct route is to cite the official page and link to it. A provider advertising a library of board material has already told you how it treats the rules, and by extension how it will treat your child's submission.

The practical test to apply, before paying anyone for coursework support, is a scenario question. Ask what they would do if your child brought a draft the night before submission. An answer about reading it and marking it against criteria is the right one. An answer that involves fixing it tells you what else is for sale.

faqs.question: When should an Al Mutaredh family start IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: The autumn of Year 12, lightly, if anything was carried over from the Middle Years. One session a week then costs less in total than four a week from February of Year 13 and achieves more, because content work in Year 12 sits where there is time to consolidate it. The specific trap for a central Al Ain family is that the week has room in it, so nothing forces a decision, and the default plan becomes to start when something goes wrong. Something usually goes wrong at the most expensive possible moment.

faqs.question: Which Diploma deadlines are set by the school rather than the IB?
faqs.answer: The ones that matter most to planning. The Extended Essay milestones, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition deadlines, the Creativity, Activity, Service record requirements and every subject Internal Assessment date are all set internally by the school, not by any public IB calendar. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the full list at the start of Year 12 and put it on one calendar with the school breaks marked. A collision found in September is a note; the same collision found in February ruins a fortnight.

faqs.question: What is the single most wasted window in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 12 and Year 13. It is the largest block of uncommitted time in the whole course, with no coursework deadlines, no timetable and no commute, which makes it the only period where consecutive days allow a topic to be rebuilt rather than revisited. Eight to twelve sessions there, aimed at the two topics named in the Year 12 reports, remove the gap that otherwise appears in the spring of Year 13 when there is no room left to fix it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a house in Al Mutaredh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Mutaredh students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We say so before any booking because the phrase families search is 'home tutor' and the format should not be a surprise. For a central family with good weekday availability, the practical gain from online delivery is choice of specialist rather than convenience, since the shortlist is national rather than drivable.

faqs.question: Why does the Extended Essay research question matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it sets the ceiling of the mark before any writing happens. The essay is capped at 4,000 words, so a question that is too broad cannot be answered in the space and a question that is too narrow leaves nothing to analyse. Students then write competently towards a mark the question will not allow. That decision is made in Year 12 with a supervisor who has limited contact time, which is exactly why four early sessions on the question and method are worth more than twenty late ones on the prose.

faqs.question: How do we avoid buying tutoring we do not need?
faqs.answer: Set three review dates rather than waiting for a problem: the start of Year 12, the end of Year 12 and the fortnight after mocks. At each one look at marked work rather than reports, and ask whether anything needs buying. Frequently the answer is no, and knowing that is worth as much as a term of sessions. Reports tell you where a student is; marked papers tell you why, and only the second supports a decision about whether to spend.

faqs.question: What does 'coping' in Year 12 usually hide?
faqs.answer: A foundation gap that has not yet been asked to carry anything heavy. A student can sit two marks below a 6 in three subjects, with an unnoticed algebra or writing weakness from the Middle Years, and be reported as doing fine. The gap surfaces when Higher Level content arrives in Year 13 and the foundation is loaded properly, which is a predictable failure on a predictable schedule. That is why the first review belongs at the start of Year 12 and should look at scripts rather than grades.

faqs.question: When do Higher Level science tutors run out in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: From the autumn of Year 13, because demand peaks exactly when the hardest content arrives. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the city's pool of experienced Higher Level chemistry and physics teachers is modest. The less commonly taught languages go earlier still and are sometimes never available. Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English stay matchable through the year, so the sensible rule is to book the scarce subjects early and treat the plentiful ones as plentiful.

faqs.question: How should a Diploma plan handle Ramadan in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Move sessions rather than pausing them, and agree the shape a fortnight ahead. Ramadan falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so in some years it sits inside the heaviest revision block and in others it does not; check it against the plan before the term starts. Shortened school days can free afternoon capacity and post-iftar slots suit many households. What fails is treating the month as ordinary and then quietly losing four consecutive sessions to fatigue and last-minute cancellation.

faqs.question: Is the Theory of Knowledge essay worth paying for?
faqs.answer: For three or four hours, yes, and rarely for more. The essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title and the commonest failure is not answering the title as set. It rewards argument structure rather than subject content, which means a student who writes well in their subjects can still score poorly, and the fix is a short, specific intervention on how a knowledge claim is built and challenged. A provider proposing a term of Theory of Knowledge sessions is padding; the component does not contain that much teachable material.

faqs.question: Can you tell us the exact May session dates for Al Ain Diploma candidates?
faqs.answer: Because none has been confirmed from the IB itself in this project, and a tutoring page carrying a date that is wrong by a week is worse than one carrying none. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and that much is safe to say. For anything specific, read the IB's own assessment pages or ask the school's Diploma coordinator, who can also give you the internal deadlines that matter more to planning anyway. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are sourced and attributed, which is the difference.

faqs.question: Do Al Ain students sit the Cambridge February/March series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October at Lower Secondary. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so always work from the school's zone version and the live official timetable.

faqs.question: Should we use the extra weekday time for more sessions in Year 13?
faqs.answer: Use it in Year 12 instead. The weekday advantage an Al Mutaredh family has is best spent on front-loading: foundation repair in the autumn of Year 12, coursework methodology in the spring, consolidation in the summer. Spending it on a heavier Year 13 means buying recovery at the most expensive point in the course, when the cheap windows have gone and the scarce specialists are already committed. Front-loading is precisely what available time is good for, and it is the opposite of what spare evenings tend to produce.

faqs.question: What happens at the post-mock session, and why book it early?
faqs.answer: Every lost mark gets sorted into one of four kinds: blank questions, method errors, timing failures and mark-scheme phrasing. Blanks mean content was never learnt and need a block. Method and phrasing mean technique and need hours. Timing failures need practice under the clock. That sorting is the only point in the year when the whole plan can be redirected on evidence, which is why it is the highest-return session available. Book it before the mocks happen, because afterwards everyone wants the same fortnight.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mutaredh.closingHeading: Use the time you have, early
al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mutaredh.closingBody: Al Mutaredh families have the best weekday availability in Al Ain, which makes the sequence of a Diploma plan more important than its intensity. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, CAS and Internal Assessment dates in September; set three review points instead of waiting for a problem; put content repair in the summer between years; and book Higher Level sciences or a second language in the autumn, because Al Ain's pool is small and fills in a predictable order. Send us the stage, the subject and a recent marked paper, and the free trial will come back with a two-year shape rather than a standing appointment. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muwaiji.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches a named Diploma subject at a named level, with the current assessment criteria in front of them. That is what separates coaching a component from discussing a subject, and it is the difference a marked piece of coursework makes visible within one session.

intro.heading: Start with the criteria, not with the subject
paragraphs: Al Muwaiji sits in the western part of Al Ain, close to Al Jimi and the old fort, in a city where the Diploma cohort is small enough that families often know every student in it. That has an upside — teachers are reachable, cohorts are tight — and a specific downside, which is that the number of adults locally who know the assessment criteria for a given Higher Level subject is very small indeed.

This page is built around those criteria, because they are where the marks are. Most Diploma tutoring conversations begin with a subject and a feeling: Chemistry is hard, the essay is going badly, maths used to be fine. The conversation that changes a grade begins somewhere else, with the published assessment instrument. How many marks does criterion C carry? What does the command term in this question stem actually require? Is the word limit a guideline or a limit? Those questions have exact answers, and students who know them write differently.

The International Baccalaureate is unusually transparent about this. Every internally assessed component has published criteria, each with a letter and a mark allocation, and every examination question uses a command term with a defined meaning. None of it is secret. What happens in practice is that students are told the criteria exist, are shown them once in a lesson, and then write as if they had never seen them. A tutor's most valuable half hour is often spent making a student mark their own draft against the criteria themselves.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For Diploma work that format matters more than it might seem. Coursework coaching is a document-centred activity: both people need the same draft, the same criteria and the same annotations on screen. That is easier on a shared screen than across a table, and it leaves a record the student can return to.

What follows is a page of specifics. How the 45 points are built and where the core fits. The internal assessment criteria for the subjects Al Ain families most often ask about, by letter and mark. The command terms, with what each one earns. The word and page limits as a single reference table, which almost no competing page publishes. Where Diploma students in this emirate actually lose marks. And a clear statement of what a tutor may and may not do with work the student must submit as their own.

One note on dates. We publish no IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and a wrong date is something a parent acts on. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; for the exact calendar, ask your school's Diploma coordinator.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muwaiji.programmesIntro: The Diploma is a two-year structure with a core bolted through the middle, and what a tutor works on changes sharply between its stages. These are the four that generate enquiries from Al Ain.

programmes.name: The year before the Diploma
programmes.description: Subject choice, and the groundwork that makes the first year survivable. Algebraic fluency, extended writing at Diploma length, and the ability to read a source critically. A short block here is the cheapest useful intervention in the whole programme, and almost nobody buys it because nothing is urgent yet.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the Diploma cohort is small and option blocks are correspondingly tight. A student should check which Higher Level subjects actually run in a given year before building a university plan on one, because a subject offered on paper is not always offered in practice when numbers are low.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: Content at pace in six subjects, plus the start of the core. The high-value work here is getting the coursework foundations right: a research question that can carry an Extended Essay, an investigation with enough depth for the top criterion band, and a Theory of Knowledge exhibition that engages with a real knowledge question.
programmes.countryNote: The spring of DP1 is the cheapest moment in the Diploma to buy help, because the content is still being taught and nothing has become a deadline. Families in this city who use that window rarely generate the emergency enquiries that fill the following spring.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 2
programmes.description: Internal deadlines, syllabus completion and university applications in the same months. The work is sequencing and triage as much as teaching: clear the coursework, protect the subjects nearest a grade boundary, and leave something alone deliberately rather than spreading too thin across six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain schools set their own internal deadlines for coursework components, and they generally fall earlier than students expect. Ask for the published internal calendar in the autumn of DP2 rather than discovering it in January.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Up to three points sit in the combination of these two components, and a failing condition in either can cost the diploma outright. Both are coachable in the legitimate sense: the thinking is taught, the criteria are explained, the reasoning is questioned, and the student writes every word themselves.
programmes.countryNote: The core is the part of the Diploma most often neglected by families budgeting for tutoring, and the part where a small, early intervention has the largest effect. Testing whether a research question can sustain four thousand words takes one session and saves a term.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muwaiji.subjectsIntro: The list below names the assessed components rather than the topics, because the components are what carry the marks. Al Ain requests concentrate in the sciences, mathematics and English, with the core close behind.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level, three at Higher, plus the Exploration at twenty per cent. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. The Exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with use of mathematics carrying six of them, and topic depth decides that ceiling before writing starts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator permitted throughout, with heavier statistics and modelling. Marks are lost by producing a number and not interpreting it in context, which is exactly what the mark scheme asks for. Calculator fluency is a syllabus requirement rather than a convenience.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Papers plus the scientific investigation, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks. Students lose evaluation marks by listing limitations without explaining their effect on the conclusion.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same investigation structure as the other sciences, with uncertainty and error analysis the recurring loss point. Paper questions reward algebraic manipulation of unfamiliar relationships, which is a mathematics problem more often than a physics one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heaviest content load of the three sciences and the one where command terms matter most. A question asking students to analyse and receiving a description earns nothing, however accurate the description is.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Externally assessed papers plus the individual oral, with the Higher Level essay as an additional component. Marks go on how a text works rather than what it says, and the oral is the least rehearsed component in most students' Diploma.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A portfolio of three commentaries, each written to a word limit and based on a different section of the syllabus and a different source. Diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation carry the marks; definition-heavy writing plateaus quickly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Written papers plus an internally assessed project, with the Higher Level version requiring primary research. Students lose marks by describing a business rather than applying a tool to a specific decision it faces.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A historical investigation marked out of 25, with a source evaluation section that students consistently under-weight. Essay structure under time pressure is the transferable skill, and it is trainable in a small number of sessions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay carry their own word limits; the Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria, with critical thinking carrying twelve of them. Together these two components are worth up to three points of the Diploma total.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Muwaiji actually works on
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Muwaiji, as families here use the phrase, is a Diploma subject specialist working one-to-one with one student. IB Gram provides that over live video to Al Ain households and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. For Diploma work the online format is a good fit rather than a compromise, because so much of the work is document-centred: a draft, a set of criteria and a page of annotations that both people can see and the student can return to.

What the tutor works on is narrower than the subject. In a two-year programme with six subjects and a three-part core, nobody has the hours to be generally better at everything, and the students who do well are the ones whose effort is pointed at specific assessed components. So the opening question is never how the subject is going. It is which component is costing marks, what the criteria for it say, and what the student's own last marked piece of work shows.

That is a different service from reteaching the syllabus, and it is faster. A Higher Level science student who writes evaluations that list limitations without explaining their effect on the conclusion is losing marks in a known criterion, and fixing it takes two sessions of writing and annotating rather than a term of content revision. A student who answers an analysis question with a description is losing marks on command terms, which is trainable in a single focused session with real question stems.

In a small Diploma cohort there is one further advantage worth naming. Because the local market is thin, Al Ain students are often taught by generalists who are good teachers but have not marked that component. Choosing by component rather than by proximity removes the single biggest cause of wasted terms in this city.
bullets: Work is aimed at an assessed component, not at a subject in general
The criteria and the last marked piece of work come first
Document-centred coaching suits a shared screen well
Component matching matters more than proximity in a small cohort

sections.heading: How the 45 points are actually built
paragraphs: Families frequently plan tutoring without a clear picture of where the points come from, which leads to effort being spent on the wrong things. The structure is simple enough to hold in your head and worth doing so before deciding what to fund.

Six subjects are each graded from 1 to 7, which accounts for forty-two points. The remaining three come from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, awarded on a matrix of the two grades together. There are also conditions attached to the award of the diploma itself, including a minimum total and requirements about failing conditions in individual components, which your school's coordinator will explain in terms of your child's specific subject set.

The practical consequence is that the core is worth more attention than most families give it. Three points is the difference between offers at many universities, and the core is also where a failing condition can cost a diploma outright rather than merely reducing a total. A student who has quietly deferred the Extended Essay is carrying a larger risk than one who is a grade behind in a subject.

The second consequence concerns triage in the second year. Where resources are limited — and in a two-year programme time is always the binding resource — the rational order is to protect the components where a small amount of work produces a whole point. That is usually a subject sitting just below a boundary, or a core component in danger of a low grade, rather than the subject the student finds hardest.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria by letter, with mark allocations
paragraphs: This is the material competing pages leave out, and it is the single most useful thing a Diploma family can have in front of them. Every internally assessed component has published criteria, each labelled with a letter and carrying a stated number of marks. A student who knows that one criterion carries six marks and another carries three writes differently, and better.

Two patterns appear across subjects. First, the criteria that reward reflection, evaluation and engagement are consistently the ones students treat as decoration — an introduction saying the topic is interesting, a conclusion saying it was. Those criteria want evidence inside the work: a method rejected and the reason given, a result that surprised the student and what they did about it. Second, the criteria that reward communication are lost to small things: unlabelled axes, undefined variables, inconsistent notation, missing citations.

The third pattern is the most expensive. Several criteria have a ceiling set by a decision made before any writing: whether the topic or research question carries enough depth for the level. An Exploration on a trivial piece of mathematics caps the use-of-mathematics criterion no matter how well it is written, and an Extended Essay question that cannot sustain four thousand words of argument caps critical thinking. Those are one-session conversations that should happen weeks before a draft exists.

The table below covers the components Al Ain families ask about most often. Confirm current criteria and mark allocations against the subject guide your child's school holds, since the board revises specifications on a cycle and we do not reproduce the guides themselves.

sections.heading: Command terms, and what each one earns
paragraphs: Command terms are the most mechanical source of lost marks in the whole Diploma, and the easiest to fix. The board defines them, the subject guides list them, and examiners mark against them. A student who treats describe, explain, analyse and evaluate as synonyms for write about this will lose marks in every subject, every paper, consistently.

The hierarchy is worth learning explicitly rather than absorbing by osmosis. State and outline want brevity: a fact, a step, no justification. Describe wants detail without reasons. Explain wants the mechanism — because, therefore, which causes. Analyse wants the parts broken out and their relationships examined. Evaluate and discuss want judgement supported by both sides, and to what extent wants a position taken and defended with a limit acknowledged.

The expensive mistakes run in both directions. Writing a paragraph where state wanted a sentence wastes time that the paper does not give back. Writing a description where evaluate was asked earns nothing at all, however accurate it is. In a timed paper the second error is usually worth several marks per paper, and across six subjects that is a significant fraction of a points total.

The way to train this is not to read the list. It is to take fifteen real question stems from the student's own subject, cover the content, and have the student state what the command term requires and roughly how many marks it implies. Twenty minutes of that, repeated twice, changes how a student reads a paper for the rest of the Diploma.
bullets: State and outline want brevity, not justification
Explain wants a mechanism; describe does not
Analyse wants parts and relationships, not a summary
Evaluate, discuss and to what extent require a defended judgement

sections.heading: Word and page limits, in one place
paragraphs: Limits are enforced, and students treat them as advisory until something goes wrong. The practical effect of exceeding one varies by component, but it is never favourable: examiners may stop reading at the limit, which means the conclusion a student spent a week on is simply not marked.

The commonly cited figures are worth having in one list rather than hunting for them across six subject guides. The Extended Essay has an upper limit of four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay runs to sixteen hundred, and the exhibition commentary to nine hundred and fifty. Economics commentaries run to eight hundred words each. The Higher Level essay in English A has its own range, and mathematics Explorations have a recommended page length rather than a strict word count.

Writing to a limit is a skill in itself, and it is one of the most transferable things a tutor can teach. The method is not cutting at the end; it is planning to a budget at the start, allocating words per section against the criteria so that the twelve-mark criterion gets the space and the four-mark one does not. Students who plan that way rarely need to cut anything.

Confirm every figure against the current subject guide your school holds, because the board revises specifications on a cycle. We do not reproduce or supply board guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; they belong to the International Baccalaureate and are available through your school and the board's own site.

sections.heading: Where Diploma students in this emirate lose marks
paragraphs: Patterns repeat across marked work from students in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and almost none of them are about intelligence or effort. They are about the gap between what a student produced and what the criteria asked for, which is exactly the gap a tutor can close quickly.

The largest in the sciences is evaluation. Students identify limitations accurately and then stop, without explaining how each one would have affected the result or the confidence in the conclusion. The criterion wants the second half and routinely does not get it. In mathematics the largest is unclaimed method credit: a student who can do the question writes three lines where the scheme rewards six, makes one slip, and loses everything on a question they understood.

In the humanities and languages the pattern is command terms and structure. An analysis question answered with a description, an evaluation left implicit because the student assumed the examiner would infer it, and extended responses with no visible argument shape. All three are training problems rather than knowledge problems, and all three respond to annotated practice within a few sessions.

In the core the pattern is timing rather than quality. Students defer the Extended Essay and the TOK components because they have no weekly homework pressure attached, then meet both in the same term as their subject coursework. The students who are comfortable in the second year are not the strongest ones; they are the ones who cleared the core early.
bullets: Sciences: limitations named but their effect not explained
Mathematics: method lines not written, so credit is unclaimed
Humanities: analysis answered with description, evaluation left implicit

sections.heading: Past-paper work that counts, and what we will not supply
paragraphs: Diploma past-paper practice goes wrong in a specific way. A student works through questions untimed with notes open, checks answers against a solution, and finishes feeling reassured. That activity rehearses none of the conditions that produce the mark, and in a programme with six subjects it also consumes time that the student does not have.

Practice that counts has four features. It is timed. It is attempted without notes. It is marked against criteria rather than against an answer, so the student sees where the band boundaries sat. And it is followed by rewriting two or three lost-mark responses in full, which is where the learning actually happens and which almost everyone omits. One paper a fortnight treated that way beats one a week skimmed.

At Higher Level the component most often neglected is Paper 3 where a subject has one, because it feels unpractisable in isolation. It is practisable, but only as a whole paper, and with explicit coaching on what to do when an early part has not resolved cleanly. Students who have never rehearsed carrying an unresolved result forward lose the back half of a paper to a single early error.

On materials, our position is firm. We do not reproduce, supply or host International Baccalaureate syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those belong to the board and reach students through their school and the board's own channels. A provider advertising a download library of them is advertising a copyright problem, and for unreleased material a malpractice exposure.
bullets: Timed, closed-book, marked against criteria, then rewritten
One properly processed paper a fortnight beats a weekly skim
Paper 3 must be rehearsed whole, including recovery from an error
We cite and link board material; we never reproduce or supply it

sections.heading: The line on every assessed component
paragraphs: The Diploma asks students to submit a great deal of work, and this region's tutoring market contains providers who will produce it for them. One has advertised completed Internal Assessments for sale outright. That is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, who risks their diploma rather than their money.

The defensible boundary is specific and we state it before any coursework support begins. A tutor may teach the skill the component assesses. A tutor may explain the published criteria and what their command words mean. A tutor may test whether a topic or research question can carry the work. A tutor may question the student about their own reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write any part of the work, does not rewrite the student's sentences into better prose, and does not supply content for submission.

That boundary is not merely a rule to be observed grudgingly; it is where the value is. The intervention that most reliably improves a coursework grade is early and legitimate: checking that a research question is answerable, that an investigation has enough depth for the top band, that the data a student plans to collect will actually support a conclusion. All of that happens before writing, which is precisely when families do not think to ask for help.

It follows that a tutor who is vague about this is a risk rather than a bargain. Ask directly what they will refuse to do. The answer tells you more about a Diploma tutor than any qualification on their profile.
bullets: The student writes every word of every submitted component
A tutor teaches criteria, tests viability and questions reasoning
Feedback is given as questions on the student's own draft
Ask any Diploma tutor what they will refuse to do

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: Tell us which assessed component is costing marks — an investigation, a commentary, Paper 3, the Extended Essay — and send the last marked piece of work for it. That turns a general worry into something a specialist can act on in the first session.

process.title: Free trial on your child's own work
process.description: The trial runs on the actual draft or paper, with the published criteria open. You should see the student mark their own work against the criteria at least once during it, because that is the habit the whole arrangement is trying to build.

process.title: A scoped plan with the boundary stated
process.description: The plan names the sessions, the criteria being targeted and the finish date. Where coursework is involved it also states in writing what the tutor will not do with the draft, before any work begins rather than when a deadline is close.

process.title: Weekly sessions with annotated feedback
process.description: Fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time over live video, with the draft or paper on a shared screen. Feedback arrives as annotations and questions rather than as rewritten text, and the student keeps the record to work from between sessions.

process.title: Review against criteria, not impressions
process.description: At the midpoint the student's work is re-marked against the same criteria and compared band by band. The review recommends continuing, changing or stopping, and stopping is a real option rather than a formality.

whyPoints.title: Criteria taught by letter and mark
whyPoints.description: A student who knows that one criterion carries twelve marks and another four writes differently. Publishing and teaching those allocations is standard practice here and absent from almost every page competing for this search.

whyPoints.title: Component matching, not subject matching
whyPoints.description: A tutor who has marked the component is worth more than one who knows the subject broadly. In a small Diploma cohort that distinction is the main reason terms get wasted, and it is the one thing proximity cannot fix.

whyPoints.title: Viability checked before writing
whyPoints.description: The highest-value coursework help is testing whether a topic or research question can reach the top band at all. It takes one session, it happens weeks before a draft exists, and almost nobody asks for it.

whyPoints.title: A boundary stated in writing
whyPoints.description: What a tutor will refuse to do with a draft is set out before the work starts. This market contains providers selling completed Internal Assessments; the risk in that transaction sits entirely with the student.

whyPoints.description: Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundaries belong to the International Baccalaureate. We cite and link them and point families to their school's coordinator rather than hosting copies.

whyPoints.description: We publish no IB examination or results dates, because the board's site cannot be checked automatically and a wrong date is something a parent acts on. UAE candidates sit the May session; your coordinator holds the calendar.

faqs.question: How is a Diploma total of 45 points assembled, component by component?
faqs.answer: Six subjects are graded from 1 to 7, giving up to forty-two points, and the remaining three come from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, awarded on a matrix of those two grades together. Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points but is a completion requirement. There are also conditions attached to the award of the diploma itself, including a minimum total and rules about low grades in individual components, which your school's coordinator will explain for your child's specific subject set.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment criteria carry the most marks?
faqs.answer: It varies by component, which is why knowing the allocation matters. The mathematics Exploration is marked out of 20, with use of mathematics carrying six and presentation and communication four each. The current science investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34, with critical thinking carrying twelve of them. Confirm the current figures against the subject guide your school holds, since the board revises specifications on a cycle.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe, explain and analyse in an IB question?
faqs.answer: They are defined command terms with different expectations. Describe wants detail without reasons. Explain wants a mechanism: because, therefore, which causes. Analyse wants the parts broken out and the relationships between them examined. Writing a description where analyse was asked earns nothing however accurate it is, and writing a paragraph where state wanted a sentence wastes time the paper does not return. Twenty minutes practising with real question stems from your child's own subject changes how they read every paper afterwards.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay word limit really matter?
faqs.answer: Yes. The commonly cited upper limit is four thousand words and examiners may simply stop reading at it, which means a conclusion the student spent a week on is not marked at all. The way to avoid trouble is not cutting at the end but budgeting words by criterion at the start, so that the twelve-mark critical thinking criterion gets the space and the four-mark presentation criterion does not. Students who plan that way rarely need to cut anything substantial.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to a home in Al Muwaiji?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Al Ain Diploma families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For coursework coaching that is genuinely well suited to the format, because the work is document-centred: the draft, the criteria and the annotations sit on a shared screen, and the student keeps the record to work from between sessions.

faqs.question: Exactly which parts of an Internal Assessment may a tutor touch?
faqs.answer: Teach the skill it assesses, explain the published criteria and their command words, test whether the topic carries enough depth for the top band, question the student about their own reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor does not do is write any part of it, rewrite sentences, or supply content for submission. We state that before the work begins. This market includes providers selling completed Internal Assessments, and the risk in that transaction falls on your child.

faqs.question: My child is strong in a science but loses marks on the investigation. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always the evaluation criterion. Students identify limitations accurately and then stop, without explaining how each would have affected the result or the confidence in the conclusion. The criterion wants that second half and routinely does not get it. The fix is two sessions of writing and annotating evaluation paragraphs against the published descriptors, not more content revision. Research design is the other common loss, usually because the controlled variables were decided after the data was collected rather than before.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student in Al Ain start the Extended Essay properly?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do, because the research question decides the ceiling. The single most valuable session is the one that tests whether a proposed question can sustain four thousand words of argument and whether the sources actually exist — and that conversation is worth having in the first year, long before a draft. Students who defer the core until the second year meet it in the same term as their subject coursework, which is why the comfortable students in DP2 are usually the ones who cleared it early rather than the strongest ones.

faqs.question: Does paying for Theory of Knowledge coaching change a Diploma total?
faqs.answer: It can be, because up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay and a low grade can create a failing condition for the diploma. The component is coachable in the legitimate sense: the criteria are explained, the knowledge claims are questioned, and the student writes every word. Two or three sessions on structure and on narrowing an over-broad essay title tend to produce more movement than the same spend in a subject the student already passes comfortably.

faqs.question: How should a DP2 student decide which subjects to fund help in?
faqs.answer: By proximity to a boundary, not by difficulty. The rational order is to protect components where a small amount of work converts into a whole point: a subject sitting just below a grade boundary, or a core component at risk of a low grade. Spreading a handful of sessions across three struggling subjects in the spring of the second year reliably produces no visible change anywhere. A tutor who accepts all three without discussing priority is taking an order rather than planning.

faqs.question: Can a single tutor take on two of my Al Muwaiji child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, where the subjects share a skill — the mathematics inside physics or economics, or argument structure across two humanities. Where the request is for two separate content specialisms, two tutors is usually the honest answer and we will say so. The exception worth noting is the core: a tutor coaching Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is working on thinking and structure rather than subject content, so that can sit alongside a subject tutor without duplication.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give the IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the International Baccalaureate directly. The board's site blocks automated checking, secondary sources circulate dates that disagree, and a wrong examination date is the one error on a page like this that a parent will actually act on. faqs.question: Are Higher Level specialists available for a small Al Ain cohort?
faqs.answer: Through a screen, usually yes; locally, often no. That asymmetry is the practical argument for online delivery in a city this size. The exception is genuinely scarce combinations — a particular Higher Level option at a particular hour — where we tell you at the first conversation rather than placing a generalist. You then choose between a different time with the right specialist, a wait with a date attached, or a tutor whose location is disclosed before the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can we get past papers and mark schemes from IB Gram?

Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate and reach students through their school and the board's own channels. We cite and link them rather than reproducing or hosting copies, because copying is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. In a small cohort that matters twice over: once because a Higher Level specialist is rarely available locally, and once because the Standard and Higher courses in the same subject are not the same course taught at two speeds.

intro.heading: The comparisons worth making before you hire anybody
paragraphs: Al Towayya sits in the eastern part of Al Ain, near the hospital district and a short run from Asharej and the university area. Families here tend to arrive at a tutoring conversation with a decision still open rather than a disaster in progress, which is a better place to start from and deserves a page built for it. The questions are comparative: is the Diploma the right route at all, should a subject be taken at Higher or Standard Level, will the school actually run the combination on paper, and what will the Ministry of Education want at the end.

Those comparisons matter more in a city with small sixth-form cohorts than they do in Dubai. An option block that works in a school with ninety Diploma students may not exist in a school with eighteen, and a subject listed in a prospectus can quietly fail to run. A family who checks before committing has a genuine choice; a family who discovers it in September of the first Diploma year has a problem that no tutor can fully solve.

The answer to the comparison usually turns out to be the same whichever way it resolves: the student needs somebody who teaches their exact subject at their exact level. That is where a small city creates a supply problem rather than a quality problem. The number of adults in Al Ain who have marked Higher Level Chemistry coursework against the current criteria is small; the number who teach it somewhere in the region is not.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a Diploma student in eastern Al Ain the practical effect is that the subject and level decide the tutor, and that a Higher Level option the school runs with four students can still be supported properly.

This page runs five comparisons in order. Diploma against A Level against a national-curriculum route, which is a decision made at fifteen and lived with until eighteen. Higher against Standard Level, where most families underestimate what actually differs. The option block question in a small cohort. The core against extra subject work, when time is limited. And the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements by curriculum, which almost no competing page mentions at all.

One omission to flag up front. We publish no IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and a wrong date is something a parent acts on. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; for the calendar, ask your school's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates where they appear are sourced and attributed.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-towayya.programmesIntro: Each route below is a real alternative for an Al Ain student, with what it demands and who it suits. The comparison is best made at the point of subject choice rather than retrospectively.

programmes.name: The IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Breadth is compulsory: a language, a second language, a humanity, a science, mathematics and usually an arts or elective subject. Suits a student who is broadly capable and organised, and punishes a student who is strong in two subjects and disengaged in four.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain has a smaller Diploma population than the coastal cities, so cohorts are tight and option blocks are constrained. The upside is close contact with teachers; the downside is that a Higher Level subject may run with a handful of students, or not run at all in a given year.

programmes.name: A Levels after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, with no compulsory breadth and no core. Suits a student who already knows their direction and wants to go deep, or one who would struggle to carry six subjects plus coursework. Assessment is almost entirely examination-based, which rewards students who perform on the day.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools offer a British sixth form rather than the Diploma, which makes this a live local alternative rather than a theoretical one. For Ministry equivalency on the British track, one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade is required alongside five IGCSE or GCSE passes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the years before
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment with no external board grade, which lets a student build strong profiles while carrying fluency gaps. The two that matter for the Diploma are algebraic manipulation and sustained writing, and both are cheap to fix in MYP 4 and 5 and expensive to fix in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP student moving into a Diploma cohort at a different Al Ain school arrives with coverage gaps nobody has mapped, because the two schools taught to different internal schemes. A single mapping session before term starts is worth more than a month of catching up afterwards.

programmes.name: The Ministry of Education equivalency file
programmes.description: The paperwork behind a UAE university application, and a reason to care about specific subjects rather than an overall average. The requirements differ by curriculum and the authority publishes them; a family should read the current version rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one.
programmes.countryNote: On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. At least one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. No IB points threshold in this project has been verified, so none is published here.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-towayya.subjectsIntro: In a small cohort the subject list is shaped by what the school can staff. The entries below note where Higher Level availability is typically the constraint, because that is the comparison families actually face.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most quantitative degrees expect at Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Higher Level adds a third paper worth twenty per cent. Frequently the Higher Level option that a small Al Ain cohort does run, because demand for it is reliable.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology, with a calculator permitted throughout. Often the only maths route available at Standard Level in a tight block, and an entirely respectable qualification — but not a universal substitute for Analysis at Higher Level in admissions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Consistently among the hardest Higher Level subjects to staff anywhere, including in this city. The scientific investigation is marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and evaluation is where marks are lost most reliably.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty and error analysis are the recurring loss points, and many paper questions are mathematics problems in physical clothing. A student strong in Analysis and Approaches usually finds Higher Level Physics more tractable than the reverse.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The heaviest content load of the sciences, with command terms deciding a large share of the marks. Commonly offered at both levels even in small cohorts because uptake is high, which makes it the safer science choice in a constrained block.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Papers plus the individual oral, with an additional essay at Higher Level. The oral is the least rehearsed component in most students' Diploma and one of the cheapest places to gain marks with focused coaching.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Both assess application and evaluation rather than definitions, and both carry internally assessed components with their own word limits. Usually available at Standard Level in a small cohort, less reliably at Higher.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: The historical investigation is marked out of 25 with a source evaluation section students under-weight. Essay structure under time pressure is the transferable skill and the fastest thing to improve.

subjects.name: Arabic and second-language options
subjects.levels: Language acquisition and language A routes
subjects.description: Arabic is required alongside the international curriculum under the federal position, and separately available as a Diploma language. Which route a student should take depends on home language and prior schooling, and schools stream Arab and non-Arab students separately.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three points sit in the combination of these two, and a low grade can create a failing condition for the diploma. The highest-value coaching is early: testing whether a research question can carry four thousand words of argument.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Towayya is usually asked to settle
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Towayya, in the ordinary sense of the phrase, is a Diploma subject specialist working one-to-one with one student. IB Gram provides that over live video to Al Ain families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. What distinguishes enquiries from this part of the city is that a good share of them are not about a failing subject at all. They are about a decision.

Those decisions have a short window and a long shadow. A subject set chosen in Year 11 is lived with until the end of DP2 and determines which degrees are reachable. A Higher Level allocation made because a block forced it can close a faculty door that no grade reopens. And in a city with small cohorts, the set a family plans is not always the set the school can staff, which is a conversation to have in the spring before the Diploma rather than the autumn after it starts.

A tutor is not the only person to ask, and should not pretend to be. The school's Diploma coordinator and university adviser hold information nobody outside the school has: which blocks run, which subjects were viable last year, what offers past students actually received. What an independent specialist adds is a view of what each course demands week by week, which is the part a prospectus cannot convey and a parent cannot easily judge.

So the comparisons below are written to be taken to the school rather than used instead of it. Each one ends in a question a coordinator can answer, and the answers together make a two-year commitment an informed one.
