sections.heading: Diploma, A Level or a national-curriculum route
paragraphs: The three post-16 routes available to an Al Ain student are genuinely different products, and the right one depends on the student rather than on prestige. Families who choose on reputation alone tend to regret it in the second year, when the workload profile of the chosen route meets the actual student.

The Diploma demands breadth and organisation. Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus three core components with their own deadlines. It suits a student who is broadly capable and who can run several pieces of long-form work in parallel. It is unkind to a student who is excellent in two subjects and disengaged in four, because the disengaged four still have to be passed.

A Level sixth forms demand depth and examination performance. Three or four subjects, no compulsory breadth, no core, and assessment concentrated into terminal papers. That suits a student with a clear direction, and it suits a student who would be crushed by six subjects. It is less forgiving of a weak examination day, because there is less coursework to cushion it.

The third consideration is what each route must show for Ministry of Education equivalency, which is covered later on this page. Families planning a UAE university route should read the authority's current requirements before choosing, because the British-track rules are specific about subject counts and excluded subjects, and tutoring cannot substitute for a qualification that was never taken.

A fourth factor is reversibility. A student who starts the Diploma and cannot carry it has a difficult transfer ahead, because the two routes are not interchangeable partway through a year. A student who starts A Levels and wants breadth has a similar problem in reverse. That makes the decision worth an hour of proper comparison rather than an afternoon of impressions, and it is why the advisory session on this page exists as a product in its own right.

sections.heading: The option block problem in a small cohort
paragraphs: This is the comparison that catches Al Ain families most often, and it has nothing to do with teaching quality. A school with a small Diploma cohort cannot run every subject in every block, so subjects are grouped and a student choosing one forfeits another. With eighteen students in a year group, a block containing both Higher Level Physics and Higher Level Economics means nobody takes both.

The consequence is that a planned subject set can be impossible before the student has sat a single lesson. And because blocks are built around the previous year's choices, they change annually. A subject that ran last year with five students may not run this year with two, and a prospectus printed in the autumn is not a commitment.

The questions to ask are specific. Which subjects ran at Higher Level last year, as against being listed? What is the minimum number of students required for a subject to run? When are the blocks finalised, and is there any flexibility after that? And if a required subject does not run, what alternatives exist — a timetable adjustment, an online provider, or a private candidate route?

A tutor cannot change a block, and this page will not pretend otherwise. What support can do is make an available combination work for the student's intended destination, including covering material the school cannot timetable. Where a university prerequisite is genuinely unavailable locally, that is a conversation to have with the coordinator and the university adviser early, not a problem to discover in the second year.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what actually changes
paragraphs: Families routinely treat this as a decision about difficulty, and it is better understood as a decision about what the subject becomes. Higher Level is not the Standard course with harder questions; it has more content, more teaching hours, and in several subjects an additional paper with a different task type.

The practical differences compound. More content means less slack when a topic is missed. An additional paper means an additional skill to rehearse, and in mathematics and the sciences that paper rewards sustained problem-solving rather than recall. The internal assessment is often similar in structure across levels but marked against expectations calibrated to the level, which catches students who assume a Standard-standard investigation will do.

The other half of the decision is external. Many quantitative degrees specify a subject at Higher Level, and no grade in the Standard course substitutes for it. That makes the Higher Level allocation a university decision taken two years before any application, which is an uncomfortable thing to decide at sixteen and the reason the consultation session on this page exists.

The honest advice is to work backwards from two or three target degrees, confirm their published prerequisites, and then ask whether the student can carry that combination alongside the core. A higher grade in the right level beats a lower grade in the more impressive one, and a student drowning in three Higher Level sciences plus the Extended Essay is not demonstrating anything useful to anybody.

sections.heading: Core work against extra subject work, when time is short
paragraphs: In a two-year programme the binding resource is time, and families eventually have to choose between funding a weak subject and funding the core. The arithmetic favours the core more often than instinct suggests, and it is worth setting out why.

Up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. A low grade in either can also create a failing condition that blocks the award of the diploma rather than merely reducing a total. Against that, lifting a subject from a 4 to a 5 is one point, and it usually requires sustained weekly work across a term. Two or three sessions spent narrowing an over-broad Extended Essay question, or structuring a TOK essay around two defensible knowledge claims, can be worth as much and cost far less.

The second argument is timing. Core components have no weekly homework pressure attached, so students defer them, and the deferral is invisible until it collides with subject coursework in the same term. Students who are comfortable in the second year are rarely the strongest; they are the ones who cleared the core early. Funding the core is partly buying that sequencing.

None of which means a failing subject should be ignored. Where a student is at risk of a grade that creates its own failing condition, that is the priority. The point is that the default — put the money where the lowest grade is — is not automatically right, and the question deserves ten minutes with the actual points arithmetic rather than an instinct.

sections.heading: A local generalist against a component specialist
paragraphs: In a city the size of Al Ain this is the comparison families actually resolve with their wallets, and it deserves to be made explicitly. A local generalist is reachable, recommended by somebody you know, and usually cheaper. A component specialist has marked the thing your child is being assessed on.

For some needs the generalist is the better buy. A disorganised student who needs company and structure, a Standard Level subject where the content is the whole problem, a younger sibling needing fluency work. Paying specialist rates for any of those is paying for capability that will not be used.

For others the generalist cannot do the job at all, however good a teacher they are. A Higher Level investigation losing marks on the evaluation criterion needs somebody who knows how that criterion is banded. A Paper 3 collapse needs somebody who has taught the recovery skill. An Extended Essay question that cannot carry four thousand words needs somebody who has seen fifty of them. None of that is about intelligence; it is about having marked the component.

The way to tell which you are being offered takes five minutes. Ask which criteria the component has, how many marks each carries, and where students most often lose them. A specialist answers in specifics. A generalist answers in generalities, honestly and helpfully, and that answer is your comparison made for you.

Worth adding that the two are not mutually exclusive across a Diploma. A sensible household might use a local generalist for a Standard Level subject where content is the whole issue, and a component specialist for one Higher Level coursework piece in the same term. Splitting the spend that way is usually cheaper than paying one rate for everything, and it is the arrangement we recommend more often than a single tutor across several subjects.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, route by route
paragraphs: Almost no page competing for this search mentions equivalency at all, and it is the part of the comparison with the hardest edges. For a family intending a UAE university route, the qualification profile at the end of school has to satisfy the Ministry, and the requirements are specific about subject counts and exclusions.

On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong, and inheriting that error would cost a family a subject's worth of work.

On the American track, the published requirements include English proficiency demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics demonstrated by at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. For the IB, no points threshold has been verified from the Ministry's own publications in this project, so none is published here; a family should read the current requirement directly rather than trust any figure found on a tutoring site.

Two further cautions. Equivalency is a process the authority performs, not something a tutoring provider does or guarantees, and nobody should imply that tutoring is required for it. And the requirements change; the only safe version is the one currently published by the Ministry or the relevant attestation authority.

whyPoints.title: No claims that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No regulator or board approval, no partner schools, no ratings, no statistics without number and method, no grade guarantees, and no production of assessed work. Each of those appears in this search result and each shifts risk to the student.

faqs.question: Should my child in Al Towayya take the IB Diploma or A Levels?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student rather than on prestige. The Diploma demands breadth and organisation: six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, plus three core components with their own deadlines. A Level sixth forms demand depth and examination performance in three or four subjects with no core. A student excellent in two subjects and disengaged in four will struggle with the Diploma, since the disengaged four still have to be passed. A student with a clear direction often does better going deep.

faqs.question: Why might a Higher Level subject not run at my child's Al Ain school?
faqs.answer: Cohort size. With a small Diploma year group a school cannot staff every subject in every block, so subjects are grouped and choosing one forfeits another. A subject that ran last year with five students may not run this year with two, and a prospectus printed in the autumn is not a commitment. Ask which Higher Level subjects actually ran last year, what the minimum cohort is, when blocks are finalised, and what the fallback is if a prerequisite subject closes.

faqs.question: What really changes between Standard and Higher Level in the same subject?
faqs.answer: More than difficulty. Higher Level carries additional content and substantially more recommended teaching hours, and in several subjects an extra paper with a different task type — an extended-problem paper that rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. Internal assessment is often similar in structure but marked against expectations calibrated to the level. And many quantitative degrees specify a subject at Higher Level, which no grade at Standard Level substitutes for, making this an admissions decision taken two years early.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to a home in Al Towayya?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Al Ain Diploma families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. In a city with small sixth-form cohorts that is a supply advantage rather than a compromise: a Higher Level option running locally with four students can still be supported by somebody who teaches that course and level regularly.

faqs.question: If money is tight, should we fund a weak subject or the Diploma core?
faqs.answer: Run the points arithmetic rather than the instinct. Up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and a low grade in either can create a failing condition that blocks the diploma rather than merely reducing a total. Lifting a subject from a 4 to a 5 is one point and usually needs a term of weekly work. Two or three sessions narrowing an over-broad Extended Essay question can be worth as much for far less, unless a subject grade itself threatens a failing condition.

faqs.question: How do I tell a Diploma specialist from a good general tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions about the component your child is being assessed on. Which criteria does it have? How many marks does each carry? Where do students most often lose them? A specialist answers in specifics — criterion letters, mark allocations, a named recurring error. A generalist answers in generalities, usually honestly and helpfully. Both are legitimate products at different prices. The comparison is only a problem when a family pays specialist rates for generalist work, or expects criteria-level help from somebody who has never marked the component.

faqs.question: What will the Ministry of Education want from a British-track student?
faqs.answer: The published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One currently ranking competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong. Confirm the current wording with the Ministry or the attestation authority; equivalency is a process they perform, not something a tutoring provider does or guarantees.

faqs.question: Has anyone verified an IB points threshold for the UAE equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Not one we have been able to verify from the Ministry's own publications, so we publish none. The British-track numbers are sourced and quoted on this page; the IB figure is not, and an unsourced threshold on a tutoring page is the kind of number a family would plan around and should not. Ask the Ministry or the attestation authority directly, and ask your school's Diploma coordinator what past students from your cohort have actually been required to show.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if the school cannot timetable a subject my child needs?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and with limits worth stating. Teaching the content of an untimetabled subject is possible, but entry for the examination is a separate matter that sits with the school or with a centre accepting private candidates, and not every centre does. Raise it with the coordinator and the examinations officer early, because the answer determines whether self-study is a route or a dead end. A tutor cannot enter a candidate and should never imply otherwise.

faqs.question: How early should an Al Ain family make the subject-choice decision?
faqs.answer: In the spring before the Diploma starts, not the autumn after. That is when blocks are being built, when a family still has influence, and when a change of school across the city is practical rather than disruptive. The useful inputs are the published prerequisites for two or three target degrees, the school's account of what ran last year, and an honest assessment of whether the student can carry three Higher Level subjects alongside the core.

faqs.question: Does an MYP student need bridging work before DP1 in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Often, and more so when the student changes school at the same time. MYP assessment is criterion-referenced with no external board grade, which lets a student build a strong profile while carrying fluency gaps — typically in algebraic manipulation and in sustained writing. Four to six sessions over the summer on those two things, plus one mapping session against the receiving school's expectations, removes most of the autumn shock. Almost nobody buys it, which is why the first term generates so many enquiries.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees Diploma schools in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Al Ain sits within the emirate of Abu Dhabi, so private schools here are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation and publishes inspection outcomes. The framework is the same as in Abu Dhabi city, so reports are comparable between them. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval from ADEK or from any other authority, and a page implying otherwise is making the most dangerous claim available in this market.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma tutor working with an Al Ain student need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any page quoting an amount is inventing it.

faqs.question: What should the advisory session produce that we can actually use?
faqs.answer: A written summary of the proposed subject set against the published prerequisites of two or three target degrees, the points at which the set carries risk, and a short list of questions for the Diploma coordinator about blocks, minimum cohorts and fallbacks. It should not produce a recommendation that bypasses the school, because the school holds information nobody outside it has. The test of a useful hour is whether you can take it to a meeting and get better answers than you would have asked for.

We will check the set against published prerequisites, flag where a Higher Level allocation closes a door, and give you a written summary to take to the Diploma coordinator. Where teaching is the right answer we will match a specialist in that subject at that level and arrange a free trial lesson. Teaching runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time for families across Al Towayya, Asharej and the rest of Al Ain.

intro.heading: Is there a real IB specialist within reach of Al Yahar?
paragraphs: The honest answer splits by subject. For Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English there are competent Diploma teachers reachable from Al Yahar, in home or online. For Chemistry at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, Spanish B or French B, the drivable pool from an outlying agricultural district on the edge of Al Ain is close to empty, and searching harder will not populate it. That is a structural fact about the city, not a sales line.

Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, which is the root of it. Fewer schools means fewer Diploma teachers, and the subjects a smaller school set offers thinly are exactly the ones where a student most needs a specialist. Al Yahar sits well away from the main school cluster, so a visiting tutor's journey is long and unpaid, which shrinks the willing pool further.

The deeper problem is that 'knows the IB' is not a checkable claim as usually stated. Almost anyone who has taught a British or American curriculum will say they can support a Diploma student, and for a Standard Level subject taught well that may be true. At Higher Level, and for anything involving the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge, it very often is not, and parents have no obvious way to tell.

So this page supplies a test rather than a promise. An Internal Assessment is marked against criteria identified by letter, with published mark allocations, and the letters differ by subject group. A teacher who has taken Diploma cohorts through assessment can name them without looking. A teacher who has not will talk about the Internal Assessment in general terms, pleasantly and vaguely. One question settles it in about fifteen seconds, and you can ask it of anyone.

Al Yahar is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project. Its own listing is where to confirm whether a school is licensed to deliver the Diploma at all, which is a reasonable first check when a family is new to the area.

IB Gram's position is deliberately plain. We teach Al Yahar students one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, matched by subject and level. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Where we cannot cover a subject at the level required, we say so before any booking and give a date or decline, because a concealed gap costs a family a term and a stated one costs them nothing.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-yahar.programmesIntro: Specialist knowledge means different things at different points in the continuum, and the gap between a generalist and a Diploma specialist widens sharply as a student moves up. These are the stages Al Yahar families ask about.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. This is where subject expertise becomes non-negotiable: each subject has its own paper structure, its own weightings and its own Internal Assessment criteria, and a tutor who does not know those is guessing about where the marks are. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra content; the assessment emphasis differs.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Yahar family the Diploma is where the local pool runs out first. Higher Level sciences and the less commonly taught languages are thin across the whole of Al Ain because the private-school set is small, and an outlying address compounds it. The practical answer is to stop treating distance as a selection criterion: fix the subject and level first and negotiate the slot afterwards, which is the only order that produces a specialist.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with an ePortfolio and the Personal Project in the final year. Here the specialist knowledge that matters is about criteria rather than content: parents see levels rather than percentages, and a tutor's first job is to say which criterion is losing marks and what a level 7 response looks like in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years support is more widely available in Al Ain than Diploma support, because the content sits within reach of any strong subject teacher. That makes it the stage where an Al Yahar family can realistically hire locally if they prefer. It is also the cheapest stage at which to fix a gap, and a fortnightly session in Years 9 and 10 prevents the Diploma rescue that this area struggles to staff.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with the Exhibition in the final year and no external assessment. The useful support is narrow and mechanical: number fluency, reading stamina, written structure. Programme-specific expertise matters least here, which is worth saying plainly rather than selling expertise that adds nothing.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in Al Yahar have the widest choice of anyone on this page, because the teaching required is not Diploma-specific. The honest advice is to buy less and buy narrowly: two short sessions a week on one named skill, rather than a general weekly hour. The summer before Year 7 is the best-placed block, since once a child commutes to a senior school the week has far less room in it.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.ageRange: Diploma year one into year two
programmes.description: This is the single clearest test of whether a tutor knows the Diploma. Each piece is marked against named criteria with published mark allocations and a word or page limit, and the decisive error is a methodology or research question chosen before anyone checked it could support the required analysis. Support means reading, questioning and feedback on the student's own work.
programmes.countryNote: The coursework strand is also where the market behaves worst. One operation found in the research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750. That is an academic-honesty breach that can cost the whole Diploma, and it appears in the same search results as legitimate tutoring. An Al Yahar family should be able to tell the two apart, and the criteria table on this page is how.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-al-yahar.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names what a genuine Diploma specialist in it would be able to discuss on a first call. If a tutor cannot, that tells you which band of the market you are in.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A specialist can explain how Higher Level Paper 3 differs in demand from Papers 1 and 2, and can name the Internal Assessment criteria including the weight carried by personal engagement and mathematical communication. Well supplied, so there is no reason to accept vagueness in this subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A specialist knows which university routes expect Analysis and Approaches instead, and can say what the graphical calculator is required for rather than merely allowed. Route choice has to be settled in Year 11, and a tutor who cannot discuss it is not advising, only teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A specialist can name the four Internal Assessment criteria for a Group 4 science and their mark allocations, and can say where Higher Level adds assessment demand rather than only content. Among the scarcest Higher Level subjects in Al Ain's pool and the first to book out.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A specialist talks immediately about uncertainty propagation and significant figures, because that is where easy marks are lost across the whole paper set. Also thin locally at Higher Level, so expect a wait rather than instant availability from an outlying address.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A specialist can distinguish what 'outline', 'explain' and 'discuss' require and name the marks each typically carries. Content knowledge is common; command-term discipline is the specialist part, and it is what changes a 5 into a 7.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A specialist can name the Internal Assessment criteria for the commentaries, including the one that rewards use of a key concept, and knows the word limit per commentary. Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are the two things worth buying hours for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A specialist can describe what the Individual Oral is assessed on, including the requirement to anchor it in a global issue, and knows the Higher Level essay's place in the scheme. The Oral is coached rather than taught and suits video delivery particularly well.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A specialist knows the difference between the Standard Level and Higher Level internally assessed work and can say what a research project needs to be viable. Students describe organisations where the criteria reward application, and that correction transfers across the paper.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: A specialist can explain how the productive and receptive components are weighted and what the individual oral assessment actually requires. These are the least commonly taught languages in Al Ain's school set, so availability is the binding constraint rather than price.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A specialist knows the essay's 1,600-word maximum, the prescribed-title requirement and how the exhibition differs in what it rewards. A small number of hours on how a knowledge claim is structured changes the grade, and a tutor who offers more than that is padding.

sections.heading: The criteria a real IB tutor can name
paragraphs: Here is the test. An Internal Assessment is marked against criteria identified by letter with published mark allocations, and those letters differ by subject group. A teacher who has taken Diploma cohorts through assessment can name them for their own subject without looking anything up. A teacher who has not will describe the Internal Assessment in general terms. Ask the question on the first call, before any money moves.

The table below sets out the criteria for the subject groups Al Yahar families most often ask about. It is deliberately specific because none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project names a single Internal Assessment criterion anywhere, which means a parent currently has no way to check the one claim that matters most.

Two things follow from reading it. First, the criteria tell you where tutoring hours should go: for a Group 4 science, evaluation and conclusion are routinely the weakest-scoring criteria and they are also the most teachable, which makes them the obvious target. Second, they show why generic 'IB help' is not useful: a tutor who does not know that personal engagement carries marks in a Mathematics Internal Assessment cannot advise on one.

A caution on how to use this. The criteria are the IB's and are published in the subject guides; this page names them and their allocations rather than reproducing the guides, because reproducing board documents is a copyright problem. Ask your child's subject teacher or Diploma coordinator for the current guide, and verify any detail against it rather than against a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, as a reference a parent can hold
paragraphs: The second test is simpler and almost as effective. Every assessed written component in the Diploma has a limit, and those limits are hard: work beyond them is penalised or not read. A tutor who does not know the limit for the piece they are supposedly supervising has not supervised one recently.

The limits also carry planning information that families find useful in their own right. A 4,000-word Extended Essay is a different project from a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay, and an 800-word Economics commentary is a different discipline again: with that few words, every sentence has to earn a criterion mark. Students who write long and then cut tend to lose the structural marks rather than the surplus prose.

None of the pages reviewed for this project publishes these limits as a reference table, which is a small gap with an outsized practical value. Pin it up. A student who knows the limit before starting plans differently, and a parent who knows it can ask a useful question about a draft without needing to understand the subject.

As with the criteria, these are the IB's requirements and should be verified against the current subject guide or with the school's Diploma coordinator, because the IB revises specifications on its own cycle. This page names the limits; it does not reproduce board documents, and no tutoring provider should be offering those as downloads.

One practical use for the limits beyond hiring. Ask your child how many words they have left for the evaluation or reflection section before they start writing it. If the answer is a few hundred, the piece has already been planned badly, and that is a conversation worth having three weeks early rather than three days late.

sections.heading: Subject by subject, what we can cover from Al Yahar
paragraphs: Availability transparency is absent from every competitor page reviewed for this project, so here is ours stated as a constraint rather than a feature. In-home coverage is zero in every row, because IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE. What the table gives is our online coverage, the typical time to match and what happens when we cannot.

The pattern reflects Al Ain's school set rather than anything about Al Yahar. Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English are taught by every Diploma school, so the teaching population is large and matching is quick. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are tighter. Spanish B and French B are thin, and often declined outright.

When a request cannot be filled we offer one of three things: a different slot, a named start date a fortnight or so out when a tutor finishes another commitment, or a straight decline. We do not substitute across subjects or levels. A general science tutor filling a Chemistry Higher Level request looks like a solution for about a month and then costs a term, and that substitution is the most common concealed failure in this market.

Ask the same questions of any provider, including a local in-home tutor. Can you cover this subject at this level, in this slot, starting when; what happens if the first tutor is not right; and can the tutor name the Internal Assessment criteria for the subject. Three specific answers make a provider comparable. An unqualified yes to everything, from a city with a school set this size, is not an answer.

sections.heading: Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra pages
paragraphs: A tutor who treats Higher Level as Standard Level plus content will teach well and leave marks on the table, because the two differ in assessment emphasis as well as in syllabus. This is the second most useful question to put to a prospective tutor after the criteria question, and the answer is diagnostic.

At Higher Level the additional paper or extended components reward sustained reasoning across a longer problem rather than recall of more material. A student who is secure on Standard Level content can still be unprepared for the demand of an extended-response question that requires three linked steps, and that is a technique gap rather than a knowledge gap.

The practical consequence for an Al Yahar family is about where hours go. A Higher Level student with a content gap and a technique gap should spend the early hours on content and the later ones on extended-response practice, in that order, because technique work needs something to be applied to. Reversing the order is the common error and it wastes most of the technique sessions.

The level question also affects who is worth hiring. For Standard Level subjects, a strong general subject teacher with some Diploma familiarity will often do well, and for an outlying area that widens the local options considerably. For Higher Level, particularly in the sciences, it does not, and this is where the city's thin supply starts to matter.

There is one more consequence worth naming. A student who drops from Higher to Standard Level mid-course does not simply shed content; they change the paper they are practising for, and practice done on the wrong component is close to worthless. Any level change should be followed immediately by a change in what the tutoring hours are aimed at.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: The criteria table above is also the clearest way to explain the boundary, because the criteria describe what the student must demonstrate. A tutor who supplies any of it has not helped; they have substituted themselves for the candidate, and the IB's academic-honesty framework treats that as grounds for withholding the Diploma.

Inside the boundary, and genuinely valuable: explaining what a criterion rewards, questioning whether a method can support the analysis the criteria demand, pointing out where a conclusion does not follow from the data, identifying missing evaluation, teaching citation properly, and marking the student's own draft against the published criteria. That is teaching, it raises marks, and it is bought at ordinary hourly rates.

Outside the boundary: writing any sentence that goes into the submission, rewriting a paragraph rather than commenting on it, supplying a research question or dataset as finished work, or editing to completion. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750, which is both the worst value and the largest risk available in this market.

There is a related line about materials. We will not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. The correct route is to cite the official page and link to it, and a provider advertising a library of board material is telling you something about its approach to everything else.

One final point about how to raise this with a tutor. Ask the question as a scenario rather than as an accusation: what would you do if my child brought you a draft the night before the deadline. The answer separates providers instantly and without any awkwardness, and it is the single most informative question on this page.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Subject expertise is one check and legal standing is the other, and the second is quicker. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no listed fee.

Because Al Yahar is in Abu Dhabi emirate, one further restriction applies. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. A tutor whose pitch rests on teaching at your child's school is offering an arrangement to decline.

Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule, so any amount quoted is unverified. And for the avoidance of doubt: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge International, and no individual should be described as an IB examiner without current, evidenced status.

sections.heading: Why Al Ain's supply is thin, and what that means for you
paragraphs: It is worth understanding the cause rather than treating it as bad luck. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and a Diploma teaching population is a function of how many schools deliver the programme. Fewer Diploma schools means fewer Higher Level science groups, which means fewer teachers who have taken a cohort through to examination in those subjects.

The same logic explains the languages. A school offering Spanish B may run it with a single teacher, and a city with few such schools therefore has very few people who have taught the course to assessment. That is not a quality judgement about anyone; it is a headcount, and no amount of local searching changes a headcount.

For an Al Yahar family the consequence is practical. Book the scarce subjects early, in the autumn term of Year 13 at the latest, and expect a wait rather than instant availability. Treat the plentiful subjects as genuinely plentiful, which means refusing both a premium rate and a long wait for Mathematics or Biology.

And be willing to widen the slot rather than the search area. Widening the search area in Al Ain adds almost nobody. Offering a weekend morning or an earlier Friday slot adds a materially larger number of specialists, because availability is distributed by time rather than by geography once nobody has to drive.

The encouraging half of the picture is that supply in the plentiful subjects is genuinely plentiful. Mathematics in both routes, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English are taught in every Diploma school in the emirate, so an Al Yahar family should expect a match inside a week and should refuse both a premium rate and a long wait in those subjects.

sections.heading: What a first conversation should actually cover
paragraphs: Collect the three answers before any payment, in whatever order suits the conversation. Which subject and level have you taught, how recently, and for how many cohorts. Can you name the Internal Assessment criteria for that subject and their mark allocations. What will you set between sessions, and will you mark it.

The answers sort providers reliably. A Diploma specialist gives paper numbers, criterion letters and a recurring error pattern they have seen in their own students' scripts. A capable generalist gives warm, plausible answers about experience and confidence, which is a fair product at the lower end of the market and is not worth specialist money. Neither is dishonest; they are different purchases.

Add a fourth question if the student is in Year 13: what is the review point, and what happens if this is not working. An answer involving a session count and a willingness to change tutor is a provider with a plan. An answer involving more hours is a provider with a subscription, and for a family in an area with limited alternatives that distinction matters more than usual.

Finally, bring a marked paper to the first conversation. It converts a vague worry into a diagnosis, and it lets a genuine specialist show their expertise in two minutes rather than claim it in ten. Any tutor who does not want to look at marked work before quoting a plan is quoting a plan they have not thought about.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor near Al Yahar really knows the IB?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the Internal Assessment criteria for your child's subject and the marks each carries. A Group 4 science Internal Assessment is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each for twenty-four in total. A Mathematics Internal Assessment runs across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Someone who has taken Diploma cohorts through assessment answers without looking. Someone who has not will talk pleasantly and generally about the Internal Assessment, which tells you which band of the market you are in.

faqs.question: Are there IB Diploma specialists willing to visit Al Yahar?
faqs.answer: Very few, and the reason is arithmetic rather than attitude. Al Yahar is an outlying district well away from the main school cluster, so a visiting tutor loses a long unpaid journey each way and can serve fewer households in an evening. Al Ain's private-school set is also considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, which makes Higher Level science and less common language teachers scarce across the whole city. The subset who are both specialists and willing to make that drive weekly for a full term is close to empty.

faqs.question: What is the Extended Essay word limit, and why does it matter when hiring?
faqs.answer: Four thousand words maximum, and the Theory of Knowledge essay is sixteen hundred. It matters because a tutor who does not know the limit for the piece they are supposedly supervising has not supervised one recently. The limits also carry real planning information: a 4,000-word essay needs a research question narrow enough to answer in that space, and students who write long and then cut tend to lose structural marks rather than surplus prose. Verify current limits with the school's Diploma coordinator or the subject guide.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to Al Yahar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Yahar students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We say so before any booking because the phrase families search is 'home tutor' and the format should never be a surprise. If physical presence is a requirement, hire locally, ask the criteria question above and ask which MoHRE permit category the tutor holds before the first session.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects can you not cover from Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Spanish B and French B are thin and we often decline them outright, with a referral suggestion. Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level are limited rather than unavailable, typically needing one to two weeks to match and best booked in the autumn term of Year 13. Mathematics in both routes, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English are well supplied and usually matched within a week. We publish this because a stated gap costs a family nothing and a concealed one costs them a term, and no competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: At Higher Level, what changes besides the amount of syllabus content?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who thinks so will teach well and leave marks on the table. Higher Level adds syllabus content, but it also changes the assessment demand: the additional or extended components reward sustained reasoning across linked steps rather than recall of more material. A student secure on Standard Level content can still be unprepared for a three-step extended-response question, which is a technique gap rather than a knowledge gap. Content hours first, technique hours second; reversing the order wastes most of the technique sessions.

faqs.question: Where do most students lose Internal Assessment marks in the sciences?
faqs.answer: On evaluation and conclusion, which are also the two most teachable criteria. A Group 4 science Internal Assessment is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Students put their effort into method and data and then run out of space and energy for evaluating limitations and sources of uncertainty, which is where a disproportionate share of the available marks sit. A tutor who starts by asking how much room the student has left for evaluation is a tutor who has marked these before.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do on my child's Economics commentaries?
faqs.answer: Explain what each criterion rewards, including the one for use of a key concept; check that diagrams are accurate and correctly labelled; question whether the analysis actually follows from the article; identify missing evaluation; and mark your child's own draft against the criteria. Each commentary is limited to eight hundred words, which means every paragraph has to earn a mark, so structural feedback is worth a great deal. What a tutor cannot do is write any part of it, rewrite rather than comment, or supply the article and analysis as finished work.

faqs.question: Do I need a Diploma specialist for Primary Years support?
faqs.answer: No, and paying for one is a waste. Primary Years has no external assessment, and the useful support is narrow and mechanical: number fluency, reading stamina, written structure. Any strong primary teacher can deliver that, which means an Al Yahar family has the widest choice at this stage rather than the narrowest. The honest advice is to buy less and buy narrowly, with two short sessions a week on one named skill rather than a general weekly hour, and to use the summer before Year 7 as the main block.

faqs.question: Should we hire locally for Standard Level subjects?
faqs.answer: It is a reasonable option and worth considering seriously. For Standard Level subjects a strong general subject teacher with Diploma familiarity will often do well, and for an outlying area that widens the local field considerably. Apply the same two tests: can they name the Internal Assessment criteria, and will they set and mark work between sessions. Where the honest answer changes is Higher Level, particularly in the sciences, because that is exactly where Al Ain's teaching population is thin and a general teacher's knowledge stops being sufficient.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book a Chemistry HL tutor in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: The autumn term of Year 13 at the latest. Two factors compound. The hardest Higher Level chemistry content arrives late in the course, so a student can look secure in October and meet organic mechanisms and the harder energetics in February with no runway. And experienced Higher Level chemistry teachers are scarce across the whole city because the private-school set is small, so by spring the ones holding good slots are committed. Expect one to two weeks to match even in the autumn, and consider a weekend morning to widen the field.

faqs.question: Why does a weekend slot give us more choice of specialist than a different search area?
faqs.answer: Because once nobody has to drive, availability is distributed by time rather than by geography. Widening the search radius inside Al Ain adds almost nobody, since the city's teaching population is modest and the scarce subjects are scarce everywhere in it. Offering a weekend morning or an earlier Friday slot adds a materially larger number of specialists, because the six to eight weekday evening band is what every family in the emirate wants and it fills first. The slot is the lever; the map is not.

faqs.question: Can you name an IB tutor as an examiner?
faqs.answer: Not unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and we do not use the word to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Several pages in this market lean on examiner language without the evidence, and it is fair to ask directly who the examining body is, for which component, and in which recent series. What does matter and is checkable is whether a tutor has taught the subject at that level, for how many cohorts, and whether they can name the assessment criteria.

faqs.question: What should we bring to a first conversation with any tutor?
faqs.answer: A recent marked paper, the subject and the level, and the three questions from this page. The marked paper converts a vague worry into a diagnosis and lets a genuine specialist demonstrate expertise in two minutes rather than claim it in ten. Any tutor who does not want to look at marked work before quoting a plan is quoting a plan they have not thought about. If the student is in Year 13, add a fourth question about the review point and what happens if the plan is not working.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-falaj-hazza.tutorsIntro: The tutors shown teach IB Diploma courses at Higher and Standard Level. Each is matched to a specific course - Physics HL, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL, English A Language and Literature - because the syllabus and the assessment outlines differ by level, not only in volume.

intro.heading: The doubt behind the search, taken seriously
paragraphs: Falaj Hazza sits in the denser western half of Al Ain, with a shorter run to the central school cluster than the outlying districts have. That makes in-home tutoring a little more practical here than in Zakher or Hili. It does not solve the problem a Diploma parent actually has, which is subject depth. A graduate who read chemistry at university has not necessarily taught IB Chemistry HL, and the difference between those two things is the Internal Assessment, the data-based questions on Paper 3 and a mark scheme that rewards a particular kind of precision.

The Diploma is also unusual in how badly a near-miss match performs. A student taking six courses across two years, with an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and a Core to manage, does not need general academic help. They need somebody who knows that the Mathematics exploration is marked against five criteria with a fixed mark allocation, that command terms in sciences map to specific assessment objectives, and that the thing a student is panicking about in October of DP2 is usually a deadline rather than a topic.

Al Ain makes that match harder than Abu Dhabi island does. The Garden City's private-school set is considerably smaller, which means fewer Diploma teachers live here, and the ones who do are mostly employed. Higher Level sciences, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL, and the less widely taught language A courses are where families run out of local options first. This is a supply fact, not a complaint, and it is the reason the online route exists.

IB Gram teaches Falaj Hazza students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are something we run only in India; we do not provide them in the UAE at all. What that buys a family here is a choice made on teaching rather than on geography - a Physics HL specialist rather than the best available science graduate inside a fifteen-minute radius. The comparison later on this page sets out the cost and logistics side of that trade with the market's own published figures attached.

What follows is written to be used rather than skimmed. It sets out how Higher and Standard Level actually differ in assessment weight, how the Analysis and Approaches versus Applications and Interpretation decision interacts with UAE and overseas university expectations, what the Internal Assessment criteria reward letter by letter, what ADEK does and what its inspection vocabulary means, and exactly where a tutor's help on an IA stops being help. It also says what we do when we cannot staff a course, because in a city this size that is a real possibility. And it ends with the dull, practical setup questions - room, device, slot - that decide whether an online hour teaches anything, which most providers leave a family to work out alone after the money has been taken.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-falaj-hazza.programmesIntro: IB Gram works across the IB continuum, and Falaj Hazza families arrive at different points on it. These are the programmes we touch and what each one means for a student in Al Ain specifically.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examination. Progress is reported against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than subject grades, which is why parents moving from a British or Indian system often find the reports hard to read.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the practical issue is continuity: a PYP student may have to move to an MYP or British setting for secondary because the local continuum schools are few. Numeracy fluency and formal written structure are the two things worth building deliberately before that transition.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each on a one-to-eight scale, with a Personal Project in the final year. Criterion-referenced marking is the novelty: a student can know the content and still score poorly by not addressing the criterion the task is set against.
programmes.countryNote: MYP to DP is the transition Al Ain families most often ask about, and the gap is usually algebraic fluency and timed-exam stamina rather than subject knowledge. MYP has no external papers in most subjects, so DP1 is often a student's first experience of a three-hour examination.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. Each subject carries internally assessed work alongside external papers, and the internal component is often the difference between two grades.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools normally enter candidates for the May session. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page, because the IB's own site cannot be verified automatically and a wrong date is worse than no date; confirm every deadline with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fewer UAE schools offer it, and those that do tend to pair it with business, hospitality or engineering pathways.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain families considering CP should check the current ADEK school listing for which local schools are authorised for it, since authorisation changes and a programme offered one year may not be the next. Equivalency implications differ from the full Diploma and should be checked with the Ministry directly.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-falaj-hazza.subjectsIntro: The Diploma courses Al Ain families ask for most often, written at the level of what each one actually assesses. If your child's course is not listed, say so - the absence usually means the pool is thin rather than nonexistent.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carried into calculus, proof and, at HL, a substantial complex numbers and vectors load. Marks go on unwritten working and on the HL-only topics met late. The exploration is assessed against five criteria with fixed allocations.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led approaches. Easier to underestimate than AA: the HL statistics content is demanding, and candidates who chose AI to avoid calculus still meet differentiation and integration in applied contexts.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 3 rewards data analysis and experimental reasoning rather than recall, and it is where HL candidates most often underperform. Uncertainty handling in the Internal Assessment separates a mid-band investigation from a top-band one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the weight. The common failure is quantitative presentation - rounding too early, dropping units, omitting state symbols - rather than conceptual misunderstanding of the chemistry itself.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with strict command-term marking. Describe, explain, outline and evaluate earn different marks for the same knowledge, and students who answer sincerely rather than to the command term plateau well below their ability.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary forms, with the Individual Oral and the HL Essay as internal components. The Individual Oral fails most often on the global issue being too broad to evidence in ten minutes.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across five prescribed themes. Writing tasks are marked partly on choosing and sustaining the correct text type, so a strong essay submitted as a blog post loses the conceptual understanding marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the structured-question marks: axes labelled, the correct curve shifted, the new equilibrium identified. HL adds quantitative questions and a policy paper that rewards evaluation rather than description.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure, and an Internal Assessment built on real organisational evidence. Students lose marks by describing a tool rather than using it to reach a supported recommendation about the business in front of them.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Taken by many Al Ain students alongside the Arabic provision their school is required to deliver. Register is the recurring issue at A level: formal Standard Arabic is expected in extended writing rather than the dialect used at home.

sections.heading: Who within reach of Falaj Hazza has actually taught the Diploma?
paragraphs: Begin with the number of people this could be. Al Ain has a private-school sector a fraction of the size of Abu Dhabi island's, and only a minority of those schools are authorised for the Diploma. The teachers who have stood in front of a DP class here are therefore few, mostly employed full time, and - under Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff - barred from taking paid private work with students enrolled at their own school. The pool that is both qualified and available is smaller than it looks from a search results page.

That is not an argument that nobody competent is available. It is an argument for asking a precise question. The useful one is not 'do you tutor IB?' but 'which course and level have you taught, and what did your students' Internal Assessments score against which criteria?' A tutor who has taught Physics HL will talk about Paper 3, uncertainties and the investigation's personal engagement criterion without prompting. A tutor who has not will talk about physics.

Where the local market tends to fall down is the Core and the internal components. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and subject-specific internal assessments are the parts of the Diploma that have no analogue in other systems, and they are the parts that most reliably move a final points total. A tutor who is strong on content and vague on criteria will leave marks on the table in exactly the places a parent cannot see.

IB Gram's position is straightforward. We match on course and level, from a platform-wide pool rather than a Falaj Hazza radius, and we teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - that is an India-only service - so the question of who happens to live nearby stops being relevant. If we cannot staff a course properly, we say so at the consultation, which is the section further down this page.

sections.heading: Higher and Standard Level are different courses, not different quantities
paragraphs: Parents often read HL as 'more of the same, faster'. The assessment outlines say otherwise. Higher Level courses carry additional topics that have no Standard Level equivalent, a longer and differently weighted paper set, and in the sciences an extra paper or extended section that tests reasoning rather than recall. A student moved from HL to SL in DP1 is not dropping a quarter of the work; they are changing course.

The practical consequence for tutoring hours is large. An SL student who is behind usually needs content consolidation and timing practice. An HL student who is behind in the same subject frequently needs the HL-only topics taught from scratch while simultaneously keeping pace with the shared material, which is why HL support tends to run as a longer commitment rather than a short block. Families who budget for an HL subject as though it were an SL subject run out of weeks in February.

The table sets out how the comparison works in practice across the dimensions that actually change. The last column is the one to read if you are deciding whether to commit to weekly support or a shorter block, because it translates assessment structure into teaching time rather than leaving you to infer it.

One caution on level changes. Dropping from HL to SL has knock-on effects on university eligibility in several systems and on the Diploma's own requirement to carry three subjects at Higher Level. The decision belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator, who knows the registration deadlines; a tutor's job is to tell you honestly what the current paper marks suggest is achievable, so the conversation with the school is evidence-based.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the single most consequential subject decision a Diploma student in Al Ain makes, and it is routinely made for the wrong reason - that one course is easier. The courses are different in character rather than in difficulty. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic, proof-oriented and calculus-heavy. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led, statistics-heavy and technology-dependent. A student who chose AI to avoid calculus still meets differentiation and integration in applied form, and the HL statistics content surprises people.

The decision that matters is downstream. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most economics degrees in the United Kingdom, and many in North America, expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. UAE universities publish their own entry requirements per programme and do change them, so the only reliable method is to read the current requirement on the university's own admissions page for the specific degree and year of entry, then work backwards. A tutor can tell you what each course contains; the university tells you what it wants.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. Because AA and AI are examined differently, moving between them after DP1 has begun is not a simple transfer of marks. A student switching from AA HL to AI SL mid-course has to pick up modelling and statistical content they have not met, usually while revising for mock examinations. Where a switch is being considered, the useful input is a marked paper from each course, not an opinion.

For tutoring purposes the two courses need different specialists. An AA HL tutor spends time on proof technique, algebraic manipulation and the vectors and complex numbers topics. An AI tutor spends it on model selection, interpreting statistical output and the technology steps the paper expects to see. We match to one or the other rather than to 'IB maths', because a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: Almost no page competing for this search names a single assessment criterion, which is strange given that internal assessment is where Diploma marks are most reliably won and lost. The criteria are published in each subject guide, they are lettered, and each carries a fixed maximum. A student who writes a thoughtful investigation without addressing a criterion directly will score in the middle band for that criterion no matter how good the thinking is.

Take the sciences investigation. It is marked against criteria covering the research design, the data analysis, the conclusion and the evaluation, and the mark is awarded for evidence of the thing rather than for its presence. An evaluation that lists limitations scores lower than one that explains how each limitation affected the specific result and proposes a realistic improvement. Uncertainty handling is where strong students lose the most: propagating uncertainty through a calculation and then reflecting on what it means for the conclusion is a learnable technique, and it is rarely taught twice.

The mathematics exploration works the same way. Presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics each carry their own allocation. Students routinely produce competent mathematics and then lose a third of the available marks on communication and reflection, because nobody told them those were separately assessed. In English A, the Individual Oral fails most often on scope: a global issue too broad to evidence through two extracts inside the time limit.

A tutor's legitimate work here is to teach the criteria, question the student's own draft against them, and point at what is under-evidenced. That is coaching. Writing, rewriting or restructuring the text is not, and the next section sets out that boundary explicitly, because it is the part of this market where the most damage is done to students.

sections.heading: What ADEK does, and what the regulator map looks like
paragraphs: Al Ain families are sometimes surprised that KHDA has nothing to do with their school. Private-school regulation in the UAE is organised by emirate, and Al Ain sits in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here. ADEK is named by almost none of the tutoring pages competing for these searches, which tells you something about how locally researched those pages are.

What the regulator does matters practically. It licenses the school, accredits it, inspects it and publishes the outcome, and in some emirates it also approves fee levels and curricula. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities, for example, approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum approval, not only inspection, sits with the emirate body. Reading a school's inspection outcome on the regulator's own site, rather than on the school's prospectus, is the single most useful twenty minutes a new family in Al Ain can spend.

The inspection vocabulary is worth decoding before you read a report. Bands run from the top rating down to the weakest, and the overall band is an aggregation that can hide a weak secondary phase inside a strong primary one, or strong attainment in English alongside weak attainment in mathematics. For a Diploma family the phase-level and subject-level detail is the part that predicts your child's experience; the headline band mostly predicts the fee conversation.

None of this makes IB Gram a regulated school, and we should be explicit about that. We are an independent tutoring platform. We hold no approval, accreditation or licence from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and any tutoring provider claiming otherwise should be asked to produce the permit number. A training institute operating from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit; that is a specific thing issued to specific organisations, and it is not something an online matching platform holds.

sections.heading: The line between coaching an Internal Assessment and writing one
paragraphs: This boundary decides whether a qualification is safe. IB academic-honesty rules make the submitted work the student's own, and a finding of malpractice can cost a candidate the Diploma rather than a mark. One site competing in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments. A family should understand exactly what a legitimate tutor will and will not do before they ask for help under deadline pressure, because that is when the line gets crossed.

A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain each criterion in plain language, help narrow a research question until it is answerable, suggest what category of evidence would strengthen a claim, teach a referencing convention, read the student's own draft and say which criterion is under-served, and run practice on a comparable task that is not the assessed one. All of this is teaching and all of it is defensible if a coordinator asks.

A tutor may not write any part of the submission, dictate sentences for transcription, rewrite a paragraph in their own prose, supply a structure for the student to fill in, edit a draft until the final text is substantially theirs, or hand over another student's work. The test a coordinator applies is whether the submitted work represents this candidate's own thinking and expression. Help that makes the text better while making it less the student's fails that test even when every sentence is technically original.

In practice at IB Gram the document stays with the student. Tutors question, annotate and point; they do not type into the file. If a tutor is asked to cross the line, the answer is no, and the request is recorded rather than quietly accommodated. We would rather lose a booking in Falaj Hazza than put a candidate's Diploma at risk, and we would rather set that out here than let a parent assume.

sections.heading: When no Higher Level specialist is free for an Al Ain family
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider has coverage limits. Almost none publish them. For a Diploma family in a city the size of Al Ain that silence is costly, because the subjects most likely to be unstaffed are precisely the ones a student cannot afford to drift in: Higher Level sciences, AA at Higher Level in the autumn rush, and the less widely taught language A courses.

Our rule is that we disclose before you pay. At the consultation we tell you whether a specialist for that exact course and level is free this week, free in two weeks, or not available. If the only honest option is a tutor teaching on Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, we say that rather than letting a parent infer a local arrangement. If the only option would be a generalist, we say we cannot staff it properly and decline, which costs us the booking and is still the right answer.

There is a related disclosure about delivery that belongs here. Some providers in this market route UAE parents through a non-UAE telephone number and present the arrangement as local. We would rather state the position in plain words: IB Gram's UAE tuition is online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run in India and nowhere else. A family that wants somebody physically in the room in Falaj Hazza should hire locally, and should still ask for the permit and the course-level experience.

The practical middle path, where a specialist is two weeks out, is usually worth taking rather than filling the gap with somebody else. Two weeks of a student working from their own notes with a clear task list, followed by the right tutor, beats four weeks with the wrong one. We will say which of those two situations you are in, and we will say it before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Setting up a session that actually works from Falaj Hazza
paragraphs: Online tuition fails for mundane reasons far more often than pedagogical ones. The three recurring causes are a shared room, a device that cannot show working, and a slot chosen before anybody measured the school run. All three are fixable in an afternoon, and getting them right before the first paid lesson is worth more than changing tutors later.

On the room: a Diploma lesson involves reading a marked script together, so the student needs a surface for paper, a position where the camera shows that paper if required, and an hour without a younger sibling in the frame. On the device: a laptop or tablet with a working microphone and, ideally, a stylus or a cheap graphics tablet for mathematics and physics, because a student who can write on the shared screen participates and a student who can only talk watches. On the connection: a wired or near-router position beats a strong signal two rooms away.

On timing, be realistic about the Al Ain afternoon. School pick-up plus the drive back to Falaj Hazza means a four o'clock start is usually fiction; half past four or five is the truth, and for a student who eats first, six. Fix the slot where it will actually survive a normal week rather than an ideal one, because a slot that is missed twice a month stops being a slot. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing without a renegotiation or a fee.

One habit makes more difference than any of the hardware. Have the student send the tutor the thing they are stuck on before the lesson - a photograph of the marked question, the paragraph of the exploration that will not come out, the past-paper script with the mark total on it. A tutor who reads that twenty minutes before the hour starts teaching at minute one instead of minute fifteen. Over a term that is several hours of teaching recovered for nothing.
