faqs.question: Are there IB Diploma tutors living near Falaj Hazza?
faqs.answer: Some, and fewer than a search results page suggests. Al Ain's private-school sector is much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's and only a minority of schools here are authorised for the Diploma, so the number of people who have actually taught a DP class in this city is small. Most of them are employed full time, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. IB Gram sidesteps the arithmetic by teaching online over live video, matching on course and level rather than postcode.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to prove they know the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Ask which course and level they have taught, and what their students' internal assessments scored against which criteria. Somebody who has taught Physics HL will mention Paper 3, uncertainty propagation and the personal engagement criterion without being prompted. Somebody who has not will talk about physics in general. A second useful question is what they will refuse to do with an Internal Assessment; a straight answer names writing, restructuring and editing to completion as out of bounds.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to a Falaj Hazza home?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and we do not provide them anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for Falaj Hazza students are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared annotation of marked scripts and drafts. We state it directly because the phrase parents search is home tutor and the assumption would otherwise stand. The trade is that your child is taught by a specialist in their exact course rather than by the nearest available science or maths graduate.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level just more work than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: No, it is a different course. Higher Level carries topics with no Standard Level equivalent, more guided hours, and in the sciences an additional paper or extended section that tests reasoning rather than recall. That changes tutoring arithmetic: an HL student who is behind often needs HL-only content taught from scratch while keeping pace with shared material, so support runs as a year-long commitment rather than a revision block. Families who budget for HL as if it were SL tend to run out of weeks before the mock examinations.

faqs.question: Should my child in Al Ain take Mathematics AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Decide it from the intended degree, not from which course looks shorter. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic, proof-oriented and calculus-led, and is what engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics degrees expect, often at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-led and is accepted for business, social sciences and design routes. Neither is the easy one; they fail differently. Read the current entry requirement on the specific university programme page for the year of entry, then work backwards to the level.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach my child's Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, explain each lettered criterion and its mark allocation, help narrow a research question, teach referencing, and read the student's own draft to say which criterion is under-evidenced. A tutor may not write, dictate, restructure or edit the work to completion, or supply another candidate's work. At IB Gram the file stays with the student and tutors annotate rather than author. A request to cross that line is refused and recorded.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects the school my child attends in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so private schools here are licensed, accredited and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK. KHDA covers Dubai and the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, so a family arriving from either emirate meets familiar vocabulary under a different authority. Read the inspection outcome on the regulator's own site rather than the school prospectus, and look at the phase and subject detail rather than the headline band, which can hide a weak secondary phase inside a strong overall rating.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by the IB or by ADEK?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring provider should tell you otherwise without producing a permit number. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform holding no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes operating from premises in Dubai; it is not something an online matching platform holds. Claims of regulator approval are the most common misrepresentation in this market.

faqs.question: When do Al Ain Diploma candidates sit their examinations?
faqs.answer: UAE schools normally enter candidates for the May session. We deliberately do not publish a specific IB examination or results date here: the IB's own site cannot be verified automatically, and a wrong date that a family plans around is worse than no date at all. Confirm every window and internal deadline with your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the registration relationship. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the position is different, because both publish official timetables that can be cited and linked.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma tutor working privately in Al Ain need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no amounts are published, so treat a specific figure quoted at you with suspicion. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Can my child get help with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, as coaching rather than authorship. For Theory of Knowledge the useful work is narrowing a prescribed title into an argument the student can actually sustain, then testing their own claims and counterclaims for evidence. For the Extended Essay it is narrowing the research question until it is answerable in the word limit, teaching the referencing convention, and reviewing the student's own draft against the criteria. The writing is theirs throughout, and a tutor who offers to draft either should be declined.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a struggling HL student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the gap is content or technique, and a diagnostic answers that in one session. An HL student missing HL-only content in DP1 frequently needs two hours a week for a term to close the gap while the class moves on. An HL student whose content is sound but whose paper marks are not usually needs one weekly hour plus timed paper practice. We would rather tell you one hour is enough than sell two, and the half-term review exists to reduce the commitment when the subject no longer needs it.

faqs.question: Will sessions still run during Ramadan and the Al Ain school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes. During Ramadan slots move to post-Iftar timing at no extra cost and without renegotiating the arrangement, because a lesson placed in a fasting afternoon is wasted for both sides. Across the holidays families usually either pause and keep the slot, or use the break for a concentrated block on an Internal Assessment or a weak paper. Because delivery is online, a student travelling out of Al Ain keeps the same tutor and the same hour, adjusted for the time difference rather than cancelled.

faqs.question: What if my child's Diploma course is not on your subject list?
faqs.answer: Tell us anyway. The absence of a course from the list usually means the specialist pool is thin rather than empty, and the answer is one of three: a slot this week, a slot in a fortnight, or an honest no. Where the only available specialist teaches from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time, we disclose that rather than implying a local arrangement. Where the only option would be a generalist on an HL course, we decline, because a wrong match costs a Diploma student more than a wait does.

intro.heading: Start from the date, not from the subject
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring decision a Hili family makes is really a decision about when. A Diploma student in the first term of Year 12 who starts weekly tuition is buying foundation repair and study habits, and that purchase pays over eighteen months. A student starting in the second term of Year 13 is buying paper technique and question selection, and that purchase pays in weeks. The hourly rate is identical. The product is not, and a tutor who treats October and March the same way is not planning anything.

Hili sits north of central Al Ain, towards the archaeological park and the Oman road, and the distance to the southern school cluster is long enough to matter to this calendar. For many Hili students the school day plus the journey home rules out a four o'clock start on weekdays, which pushes sessions later into the evening and reduces how many a week are realistic. That is a scheduling fact with a planning consequence: a Hili family has fewer usable slots than a central Al Ain family, so each one has to be aimed better.

Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's published inspection record is the thing to read before trusting a school's own account of its Diploma results, and it is also the right place to check which programmes a school is actually licensed to deliver. None of the competitor pages reviewed for this project mentions ADEK at all.

One honest limitation up front. This page publishes no IB exam or results dates. The IB's own site blocks automated access, which means no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date that is wrong by a week on a tutoring page is worse than no date. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; for anything more precise, ask the school's Diploma coordinator or read the IB's own assessment pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates, which are sourced, appear further down.

IB Gram's delivery is one-to-one live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a Hili family with a long school run and a narrow evening window, the online format is not a compromise on the calendar question, it is the thing that makes the calendar workable: a session can begin the minute a student sits down, and it can move when a mock week or a travel week moves.

Nothing on this page requires you to hire us. The eight-week table, the backwards calendar and the board dates all work on a tutor you find yourself in Al Ain, and a Hili family who uses them to hire well locally has still got the value out of reading it.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-hili.programmesIntro: Each part of the IB continuum has its own calendar pressure, and the point at which tuition is worth buying differs sharply between them. These are the three a Hili family is likely to be inside, plus the coursework strand that sits across them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject combines internally assessed work with externally marked papers, and the two run on different clocks. The internal work has school-set deadlines across Year 12 and early Year 13; the papers all land in one window. Planning that treats them as one timeline is the usual cause of a bad spring.
programmes.countryNote: For Hili students the binding constraint is the week, not the year. A long commute and a full Diploma workload leave perhaps two usable evening slots, so the calendar has to decide what those slots are for at each stage. Al Ain's private-school set is smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, which also means Higher Level science and less common language teaching is thin locally; booking those early in Year 12 rather than in the spring of Year 13 is the difference between a specialist and whoever is left.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with the Personal Project in the final year. There is no external paper for most students, so the calendar is driven entirely by school reporting cycles and the Personal Project deadline. That makes the Middle Years the easiest stage to plan tuition for and the stage at which families most often leave it too long.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project deadline is the one date a Hili family should put in the calendar two terms early. It is a process assessment, so the marks come from documented planning and reflection rather than from a strong final product, and support that arrives in the last fortnight cannot create the record the criteria want. Two short sessions in the autumn term are worth more than ten in the spring.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with the Exhibition in the final year and no external assessment. The useful calendar question in the Primary Years is not when exams are but when a specific skill gap becomes a barrier, which is usually at the transition into the Middle Years. Reading stamina, written structure and number fluency are the three worth watching.
programmes.countryNote: For Hili primary families the best-timed intervention is the summer before Year 7 rather than during it. A short block then, before the Middle Years workload begins and while the week still has space in it, prevents the problem that otherwise surfaces in Year 9 reports. Once a Hili student is commuting to a senior school with a long day, there is far less room in the week to fix anything.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.ageRange: Diploma year one into year two
programmes.description: The coursework strand runs on school-set internal deadlines that most parents never see written down. Each piece is marked against published criteria, and the single most expensive mistake is a methodology or research question chosen in week one that cannot support the analysis the criteria demand in week ten. Support here is reading, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's internal deadline list at the start of Year 12 and build the tutoring plan from that, not from the exam window. Those dates are the ones that actually compress a Hili student's spring, because they arrive while subject teaching is still running at full pace. Four to six well-timed hours across the Internal Assessment cycle, most of them early, is the whole legitimate requirement.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-hili.subjectsIntro: Timing differs by subject, because the components arrive in different months and the failure modes are not alike. These are the Diploma subjects Hili families ask for, with the window in which the hour does most good.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level content runs to the end of the course, so content support stays useful later here than in most subjects. Paper 3 extended response rewards practice that cannot be crammed, which makes the second term of Year 13 the heaviest and most productive block.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling, with mandatory graphical calculator technique that is best drilled early and then maintained. The route choice against Analysis and Approaches has to be settled in Year 11, because switching in Year 12 costs a term that the calendar does not have spare.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms land late in the course, so a student can look secure until February and then meet the hardest material with no runway. Booking Chemistry Higher Level support in the autumn of Year 13 rather than the spring is the single best-timed decision in this subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension topics arrive late and the data-question skills that carry easy marks can be fixed at almost any point. That split makes Physics unusually forgiving on timing: a short block on uncertainty and significant figures works even close to the session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content heavy and command-term sensitive. The useful calendar insight is that command-term work pays in any month, while content consolidation needs to happen before the final ten weeks. Students who leave both until April get neither.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries forming the Internal Assessment, spread across Year 12 and into Year 13 on school-set dates, plus diagram and evaluation technique for the papers. The commentary dates are the ones that catch families out, because each needs a current article and a real deadline.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is scheduled by the school, often earlier than parents expect, and it is coached rather than taught. Preparation has a hard date attached, which makes it the component most worth asking the school about in the autumn term.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project at Higher Level with its own internal timeline, plus applied framework technique for the papers. The project needs an organisation and a question agreed early; late starts in Business Management are the most salvageable of the coursework pieces but still cost marks.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Productive skills under timed conditions plus a scheduled individual oral. These are the less commonly taught languages in Al Ain's school set, so local availability is thin and booking has to happen earlier than for other subjects, not later.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title with a firm internal deadline and an exhibition earlier in the course. Both are argued rather than remembered, so a small number of hours on how a knowledge claim is structured changes the grade and more hours add very little.

regions.note: Close to Hili and considerably closer to the central schools, so the four o'clock slot survives for many students here. The practical effect is one extra usable session a week over a term.

regions.name: Al Khabisi

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve
paragraphs: If a Hili family is reading this with a session eight weeks away, the plan is narrow and the table sets it out week by week. The governing principle is that content learning stops being efficient somewhere around the ten-week mark and technique work keeps paying until the last few days. Spending week two of eight on new content and week seven on mark schemes is the correct order; doing it the other way round is the common one.

The second principle is that the student does more of the work than the tutor. Two sessions a week with nothing in between is two hours of attention; two sessions with a timed paper completed and marked between them is a working loop. Hili students with long commutes have limited evening capacity, so what goes between the sessions has to be chosen rather than assigned by volume.

The third is that the last fortnight should get quieter, not busier. Families instinctively add hours as the date approaches, and the evidence from marked work usually says the opposite is needed: fewer new inputs, more self-marking, earlier nights. A tutor who proposes extra sessions in the final week without evidence from a paper is responding to anxiety rather than to the student.

Read the table as a default to be adjusted, not a prescription. A student who has never sat a full timed paper needs to start the paper column in week one regardless of where their content sits, because the discovery that they cannot finish in time changes everything else in the plan.

sections.heading: The Diploma year, counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a Diploma calendar counted backwards, which is odd, because that is the form a parent can act on. The table below works in that direction: the milestone, who sets it, and what should already be true by then. It deliberately contains no IB exam or results dates, for the reason set out at the top of this page.

The most useful row is the first one. Internal deadlines are set by the school, not the IB, and they are the dates that actually compress a Diploma student's year. They arrive while subject teaching is still running, which means a student can be simultaneously behind on content and due to submit a piece of assessed coursework. Families who have the internal deadline list in September plan around that; families who do not meet it as a surprise in January.

The second most useful row is the mock window. Mocks are the only full-length diagnostic most Diploma students get before the real thing, and their value is almost entirely in the analysis afterwards rather than the grade. A Hili family should treat the fortnight after mocks as the most important tutoring purchase of the year, because that is the only point at which the plan can be redirected on evidence.

What the table cannot do is tell you how long anything takes for your child. A content gap in Chemistry organic mechanisms is a term; a command-term problem in Biology is three hours. Use the structure for sequencing and get the durations from a marked paper rather than from a page.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson dates a Hili family can rely on
paragraphs: Where IB dates cannot be published here, Cambridge and Pearson dates can, because they are sourced from the boards themselves. Many Hili students take IGCSEs before the Diploma or alongside other qualifications, and one widely repeated claim about the Cambridge calendar is simply wrong for this country.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE family given a February/March entry deadline has been handed another country's calendar, and acting on it means missing an entry. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates are quoted with their years precisely because the year is what makes them checkable.

The forward-looking rule follows from how boards work: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. So a page like this one names a series by its month and links the live official timetable rather than restating a future date that may move. Ask the exams officer at your child's school for the zone version and the confirmed entry deadline.

sections.heading: Ramadan, term dates and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar has features that a generic revision plan ignores, and a Hili family planning a spring run-in has to account for them. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a different household rhythm, and it falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so in some years it lands squarely in the heaviest revision block and in others it does not.

The practical adjustment is to move sessions rather than to reduce them. Post-iftar slots work well for many families and a shortened school day can actually free afternoon capacity that does not otherwise exist, which for a Hili student with a long commute is a rare gain. What does not work is pretending the month is ordinary and then losing four sessions to fatigue and cancellation.

The second feature is the long summer and the mid-year break. For a Year 12 student the summer between Diploma years is the single largest block of uncommitted time in the whole course, and it is the cheapest place to put content repair. Families who spend it resting completely and then start tutoring in September have given away the easiest eight weeks available to them.

The third is that school term dates in the UAE do not always align with when boards set deadlines, so a submission can fall close to a break. Ask for the internal deadline list early, mark the breaks on the same calendar, and look for the collisions. Finding one in September costs nothing; finding one in February costs a weekend and a grade.

sections.heading: The Hili school run and the slot it leaves
paragraphs: Hili lies north of the city centre near the archaeological park and the Oman road, and many of its students attend schools in the central and southern clusters. The journey home after a Diploma school day with an after-school commitment is long enough that a four o'clock weekday session is not realistic for a significant share of them, and a five o'clock one is tight.

That has a direct consequence for in-home tutoring in particular. A tutor driving to Hili arrives after their own journey across the city, having finished a previous household, which pushes a weekday visit later still and makes the arrangement fragile. The UAE in-home market band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included is partly a reflection of exactly this: the driving is real and someone pays for it.

Online delivery changes the arithmetic rather than the rate. A session can begin the moment a student is home, it does not depend on a route, and it can be moved to a Saturday morning in a mock week without anyone losing a journey. For a Hili student with perhaps two usable evening slots a week, those three properties are worth more than the room the lesson happens in.

IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that is worth repeating here rather than implying. If an adult physically present is what your child needs, that is a legitimate requirement and the right move is to hire locally, book the latest slot the tutor has and ask what happens when the drive runs long.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit in Hili
paragraphs: Because the search term says home tutor, here is the comparison on the merits, written around the thing this page is about: whether the plan survives the calendar. Cost appears in the table but it is not the deciding row for a Hili family, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.

The deciding row is sessions delivered. A plan that loses one weekday session a month to traffic, a late finish or a clash delivers roughly thirty sessions across a school year instead of forty, and ten sessions is a whole technique block. Reliability compounds in a way that a slightly better learning environment does not.

The second deciding row is movement. Mock weeks, Ramadan timings, travel and family events all require sessions to move, and an in-home arrangement moves badly because it is pinned to a driving route serving several households. An online slot moves in a message. Over an eighteen-month Diploma that flexibility is worth several weeks of teaching.

The third is match. Al Ain's smaller private-school set means Higher Level sciences and the less common languages are thin locally, so an in-home arrangement in Hili often means the right availability with the wrong specialism. Online matching inverts that: the specialism is fixed first and the slot is negotiated second, which is the correct order when a calendar is tight.

One row deserves a caveat. Some students genuinely work better with an adult in the room, and for them the in-home premium is money well spent even at the cost of a few lost sessions. The table is an argument about calendars, not a claim that online suits every child, and a Hili family should decide that part on their own child rather than on a table.

sections.heading: Coursework on a deadline, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: Deadline pressure is exactly when the academic-honesty boundary gets tested, so it belongs on a calendar page rather than in a footnote. The Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, and the IB treats a breach as grounds for withholding the Diploma. A family three days from an internal deadline is in the worst position to make a good decision about that.

What a tutor can legitimately do, even late, is substantial. They can explain what a criterion rewards, ask whether the method can support the required analysis, point out where a conclusion does not follow from the data, identify missing evaluation, teach citation properly and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. All of that is teaching and all of it raises marks.

What a tutor cannot do is write any part of the submission, rewrite rather than comment, or supply a research question or dataset as finished work. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750. That is the thing a panicking family is most likely to buy and the single worst purchase available, because it risks the whole qualification the two years were for.

The calendar answer is to make the late decision unnecessary. Put the internal deadlines in the calendar in September, book the coursework hours early and front-load them onto methodology. Four hours in week two are worth twenty in week eleven, and they remove the week-eleven conversation entirely.

sections.heading: ADEK, the inspection record and what to read before you choose
paragraphs: Hili is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. This matters to a tutoring decision in two concrete ways, and neither is mentioned by any competitor page reviewed for this project.

The first is verification. ADEK publishes what each school is licensed to deliver and the outcome of its inspections, which is the right source for whether a school is actually offering the Diploma and how it has been judged. A school's own website is marketing. If a Hili family is choosing between schools as well as tutors, the regulator's listing is where the comparison should start.

The second is the limit on who may tutor. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the same thing. Teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold that permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

It is worth being explicit about what IB Gram is not. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge International, and we will not imply one. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; that is a specific thing with initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal, and nobody operating online should be described as holding it.

Teachers may not take paid private students from their own school
The MoHRE permit is free, lasts two years and is applied for in about two working days
No published fine schedule exists for unpermitted tutoring, so quoted amounts are unverified

sections.heading: What happens when the subject is not covered in time
paragraphs: Availability on a deadline is where transparency matters most, and no competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all. Ours is straightforward: Al Ain's private-school set is small, Higher Level sciences and less common languages are thin in the local pool, and in the spring of Year 13 the specialists with good evening slots are already committed.

So the honest version of the calendar advice is to book the scarce subjects early and the plentiful ones whenever. Chemistry Higher Level, Physics Higher Level, Spanish B and French B should be arranged in the autumn term of Year 13 at the latest. Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English can usually be matched inside a week at any point.

When we cannot cover a request, we give a date or decline rather than substituting. A general science tutor is not a Chemistry Higher Level teacher and a fluent speaker is not a language teacher, and the substitution looks like a solution for about a month. On a tight calendar a month is the whole margin.

This is a fair question to put to any provider, local or online. Can you cover this subject, at this level, in this slot, starting this week, and if not, when. A date is a useful answer. Yes to everything, in a city this size and this close to a session, is not.

There is a second kind of coverage limit worth naming: our own capacity in a given evening slot. Hili's usable window is narrow and it is narrow for everyone in the city, so the six to eight o'clock weekday band fills first. Families who can use a Saturday morning or an earlier Friday slot get a wider choice of tutor, and in the scarce subjects that choice is the whole decision.

process.title: Send the date before the subject
process.description: Tell us when the session is, where the student is in the course and what the school's next internal deadline is. The plan for a Hili family eight weeks out is different in kind from the plan for one eighteen months out, and starting from the date rather than the subject means the first session is already aimed correctly.

process.title: Bring the mock paper, not the report card
process.description: A report grade says where a student is; a marked paper says why. We sort the losses into blanks, method errors, timing failures and mark-scheme phrasing, because each has a different fix and a different duration. Blanks mean content and a term; phrasing means three hours.

process.title: Free trial, which produces a dated plan
process.description: A full session with the tutor who would teach the course, no card required. The output is a plan with dates on it: what the next eight or eighty weeks contain, what is set between sessions, and when we check whether it worked. If the tutor is not right, we change the tutor.

process.title: Run the loop against the calendar
process.description: Teach, set, mark, review, with sessions scheduled around the school's own mock window and internal deadlines rather than across them. Sessions move for Ramadan timings, travel and clashes instead of being lost, which is where the extra ten sessions a year come from.

process.title: Taper, do not escalate
process.description: In the final fortnight the plan should get quieter: no new content, the student marking their own practice, the tutor arbitrating. If anyone proposes extra sessions in the last week, ask which paper the evidence came from. Anxiety is not a diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: Plans built from internal deadlines
whyPoints.description: We ask for the school's own coursework deadline list and build backwards from it, because those dates compress a Diploma student's year far more than the exam window does and almost no parent is shown them in writing.

whyPoints.title: No invented exam dates
whyPoints.description: This page publishes no IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site is the only source and none has been confirmed in this project. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear with their sources, and future series are named by month only.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives a Hili commute
whyPoints.description: Sessions start when the student is home, not when a car arrives, and they move in a message when a mock week or Ramadan timing requires it. Over a year that is the difference between forty sessions delivered and thirty.

whyPoints.title: Scarce subjects flagged early
whyPoints.description: Higher Level sciences and the less common languages are thin in Al Ain's pool, so we say when a request needs booking in the autumn rather than the spring, and we give a date or decline instead of substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that is front-loaded
whyPoints.description: Most of the legitimate hours on an Internal Assessment belong before any writing starts, on methodology and research question. Tutors read drafts, question and mark against criteria; they do not write, redraft to completion or supply any part of a submission.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits, including ours
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no regulator approvals claimed, no guaranteed grades, and no statistic without a source and a date. The things a tutoring page refuses to claim are usually more informative than the things it does.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the exams in Hili. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the plan is technique rather than content. Eight weeks is enough to fix command-term use, mark-scheme phrasing, calculation drills, question selection and timing, and those routinely carry a grade. It is not enough to rebuild a topic nobody ever learnt. So the purchase at this point is a block on named components, working from a marked paper, with a timed paper completed and marked between each session. The last fortnight should be quieter, not busier, with the student marking their own work and no new material entering the plan.

faqs.question: Which IB session do students at Al Ain schools sit?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and Al Ain schools work towards it. This page deliberately publishes no IB session or results dates, because the IB's own website is the only reliable source and none has been confirmed here. Get the specifics from the IB's assessment pages or from your school's Diploma coordinator, and treat any tutoring site quoting precise IB dates with caution. What the coordinator can also give you, and what matters more for planning, is the school's internal deadline list for coursework.

faqs.question: Why do the school's internal deadlines matter more than the exam date?
faqs.answer: Because they arrive while teaching is still running at full pace, and they are set by the school rather than published anywhere a parent would look. A Diploma student can be simultaneously behind on content and due to submit assessed coursework, which is the situation that produces a bad spring. Ask the coordinator for the list at the start of Year 12, put it on a calendar alongside school breaks, and look for the collisions. Finding a clash in September costs nothing to fix; finding it in February costs a weekend and some marks.

faqs.question: Does a long school run from Hili really change the tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: It changes how many sessions a week are possible, which changes what the plan can contain. Many Hili students attend schools in the central or southern clusters, and after an after-school commitment and the journey home a four o'clock weekday session is unrealistic. That typically leaves two usable evening slots rather than three or four. With fewer slots, each one has to be aimed more precisely from a marked paper, and weekend sessions carry more of an exam-year block than they would for a family living beside the school.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Hili?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Hili students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We say so before any booking because the search phrase is 'home tutor' and the format should not be a surprise. For a family with a long commute the online route also removes the two things that break weekday plans: the tutor's own drive across the city, and a slot pinned to a route rather than to your evening.

faqs.question: When should we book a Chemistry HL tutor for a Hili student?
faqs.answer: The autumn term of Year 13 at the latest, and earlier if you can. Two reasons. Organic mechanisms and the harder Higher Level content arrive late in the course, so a student who looks secure in October can meet the hardest material in February with no runway. And Al Ain's private-school set is small, which makes Higher Level science teaching genuinely scarce locally; by the spring the specialists with good evening slots are committed. Mathematics, Biology and Economics can usually be matched within a week at any point in the year.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect a revision plan in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Move the sessions rather than cancelling them. Shortened school days can free afternoon capacity that a long Hili commute normally consumes, and post-iftar slots work well for many households. Ramadan falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so in some years it sits inside the heaviest revision block and in others it does not; check it against the plan before the term starts rather than during it. What fails is treating the month as ordinary and then quietly losing four sessions to fatigue and last-minute cancellation.

faqs.question: Do UAE students ever sit the Cambridge February/March series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for Lower Secondary. If a tutoring site quotes a UAE family a February/March entry deadline, it has published another country's calendar and acting on it would mean missing an entry. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

faqs.question: What is the single best-timed tutoring purchase in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The fortnight after mocks. Mocks are the only full-length diagnostic most students get, and their value is in the analysis rather than the grade. In that fortnight a tutor can sort the losses into blank questions, method errors, timing failures and mark-scheme phrasing, and each of those has a different fix and a different duration. That is the only point in the year when a whole plan can be redirected on evidence. A close second is the summer between Diploma years, which is the largest uncommitted block in the course.

faqs.question: How many hours should a Hili family budget in the final term?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families expect, aimed more narrowly. A ten-week block of two sessions a week is twenty hours, and that is ample if a timed paper is completed and marked between each one. What does not work is adding hours in the last fortnight. If a tutor proposes extra sessions in the final week, ask which paper the evidence came from. Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor run AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, so a twenty-hour block is a known figure you can plan rather than an open commitment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay three weeks before it is due?
faqs.answer: Within limits, and the limits are the point. A tutor can read the student's own draft, mark it against the published criteria, ask whether the argument is supported, point out missing evaluation and teach citation properly. A tutor cannot write a sentence that goes into the submission, rewrite rather than comment, or supply material the student presents as their own. Three weeks out, the most valuable thing is usually structural feedback on what already exists. The deeper answer is to book those hours in the first term instead, where four of them outperform twenty later.

faqs.question: What does Pearson's documented timetable tell us about resit timing?
faqs.answer: That a November entry means a January result, which matters if a university or school deadline sits in between. The documented pattern: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so check the live official timetable before planning around any future series, and name the series by its month.

faqs.question: Should a Year 12 student in Hili use the summer for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest content-repair window in the whole course, and most families give it away. The summer between Diploma years is the largest block of uncommitted time a student has, with no competing coursework deadlines and no commute. Eight sessions across it, aimed at the two topics named in the Year 12 reports, remove the gap that otherwise surfaces in the spring of Year 13 when there is no room for it. The alternative is paying the same rate for the same work in February while three other things compete for the same evening.

faqs.question: How do we agree an endpoint so the Hili tutoring bill does not just run on?
faqs.answer: Agree the stopping condition before you start, in writing. It should be a named weakness on a named component, with a session count attached, and a review at the end of it. If the weakness has closed, stop or move to the next one. If it has not, change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours. Plans without a review point renew by default, which is how a tutoring budget doubles without anyone deciding. An honest provider should be willing to tell a Hili family that there is nothing left worth buying.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-hili.closingHeading: Tell us the date, and we will tell you what the hours can do
al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-hili.closingBody: An IB home tutor in Hili is a timing decision before it is anything else. Eighteen months out, the right purchase is a weekly hour on content and habits. Ten weeks out, it is a technique block on named components with a timed paper between sessions. Two weeks out, it is the student marking their own work while someone arbitrates. Send us the session, the school's next internal deadline and a recent marked paper, and the free trial lesson will come back with a plan that has dates on it. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and they move when your calendar does.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-zakher.tutorsIntro: Tutors here are matched on three things rather than two: the subject, the level and whether they hold the same weekend morning slot every week. For a Zakher family the third is not a convenience, it is the condition that makes the other two usable.

intro.heading: Build the week from the bus timetable
paragraphs: Zakher lies on the southern fringe of Al Ain, out towards the Omani border, and families here face the longest routine journey of any neighbourhood in the city. Most of the private schools that serve them sit in the central or southern clusters, which means a school bus leaving early and returning late. For a Diploma student the practical effect is that a weekday evening starts later and ends no later than anyone else's, so there is less of it.

That is the frame for everything below. A Higher Level student carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment has limited weeknight capacity anywhere. In Zakher the bus removes the first usable hour entirely, and most families who try to run two midweek sessions find that the second quietly stops happening somewhere around November.

So the sensible plan for this area is weekend-led rather than evening-led, and that is an unusual recommendation in a market that sells weekly evening slots almost exclusively. A Saturday morning session from Zakher is the direct equivalent of a Tuesday afternoon session for a family living beside the school: the student is rested, the time is unhurried and a full timed paper fits inside it.

The second Zakher-specific fact is about supply. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, which makes Higher Level sciences and the less common languages thin across the whole city. Add the longest drive in Al Ain and the number of specialist tutors willing to make that journey on a weeknight approaches zero. This is not a complaint about local tutors; it is simple arithmetic about unpaid driving time.

Zakher is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's own listing is where to confirm what a school is licensed to deliver and how it has been inspected, and it is worth reading before taking a school's own account of its Diploma provision at face value.

IB Gram teaches Zakher students one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For the furthest-out families in Al Ain that is not a sales position so much as the only version of the service that survives contact with the bus timetable: the session starts when the student is home, and it moves when the week moves.

Everything below is written to be useful even if you hire someone locally. The weekday table, the component-by-component week and the holiday argument all apply to any tutor a Zakher family finds, and the questions at the end work on anyone. The format we sell is online; the planning advice is not for sale.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-zakher.programmesIntro: The transport constraint falls differently on each part of the IB continuum. These are the stages a Zakher family is most likely to be managing, with the scheduling consequence spelled out.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The programme's defining feature is total load rather than the difficulty of any part, and the externally marked papers and internally assessed components run on different clocks. A plan that exceeds the week's real capacity gets abandoned rather than adjusted.
programmes.countryNote: For a Zakher Diploma family the weekend is the plan and the weeknight is the follow-up. That ordering is the opposite of what most tutoring is sold as, and it is what the bus timetable dictates. It also changes which subject is worth supporting: with one weeknight available, the subject has to be chosen from marked work rather than from a report grade, because there is no room to be wrong twice.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria out of eight, with an ePortfolio and the Personal Project in the final year. Because there is no external paper for most students, the calendar is driven by school reporting cycles and by the Personal Project deadline rather than by an exam window. That makes the stage flexible, which suits a difficult timetable.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is where a Zakher family should spend their Middle Years tutoring money, and they should spend it early. It is assessed on documented planning and reflection as much as on the product, so support arriving in the final fortnight cannot create the record the criteria want. Two short weekend sessions in the autumn term outperform a scramble in the spring, and they fit the transport reality.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with the Exhibition in the final year and no external assessment. Useful support here is narrow: number fluency, reading stamina and written structure. Short sessions beat long ones, and consistency matters more than volume, which again favours a format that does not depend on anyone travelling.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age children in Zakher often have a shorter school day than their older siblings, which creates genuine mid-afternoon availability. That window closes permanently once the child moves to a senior school on the far side of the city, so it is worth using while it exists. The summer before Year 7 is the best-placed block a Zakher primary family has.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.ageRange: Diploma year one into year two
programmes.description: The coursework strand runs on school-set internal deadlines and rewards concentrated attention rather than weekly attention. Each piece is marked against published criteria, and the decisive moment is the methodology or research question, chosen before any writing. Support means reading, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts.
programmes.countryNote: Coursework suits this area better than subject teaching does, because the hours are concentrated and can sit entirely on weekend mornings. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's internal deadline list in September, place four to six sessions around it with most of them early, and the weeknight stays free for ordinary study. Front-loading is what removes the late-night panic that this timetable makes especially likely.

al-ain/ib-home-tutor-in-zakher.subjectsIntro: With one weeknight and one weekend morning available, the choice of subject is the whole decision. These are the Diploma subjects Zakher families ask for and what a session has to do in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and Higher Level Paper 3 extended response. Needs sustained practice rather than explanation, which makes it a weekend subject: a full timed paper on a Saturday morning does more than two tired weeknight hours ever will.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and graphical calculator technique. The failures are procedural, so this is one of the few subjects that genuinely responds to a short weeknight session, because drills survive tiredness better than reasoning does.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, organic mechanisms and the data-based paper, with the hardest material arriving late in the course. Among the scarcest Higher Level subjects in Al Ain's pool, which for a Zakher family means booking in the autumn of Year 13 rather than the spring.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields and late Higher Level extension topics. A large share of lost marks are uncertainty treatment and significant figures, which can be drilled in short sessions and therefore fit a weeknight unusually well.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content heavy and command-term sensitive. Command-term work is short and transfers across the whole paper, so it is good use of a limited slot; content consolidation belongs in the weekend block or a holiday.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation structure and three commentaries on school-set dates. The commentaries need a current article and a real deadline, so they belong on a weekend morning where a student can read and plan in one sitting.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, the comparative essay and the Individual Oral, scheduled by the school earlier than most parents expect. The Oral is coached and is entirely talk, which makes it well suited to a video session after a long day.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks applied to a real organisation, plus a Higher Level research project with its own timeline. Students describe where the mark scheme asks for application, and that correction is structural, so it transfers once taught.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Timed productive skills and a scheduled individual oral. The less commonly taught languages in Al Ain's school set, so in-home availability in Zakher is effectively nil and online is the only route to a subject-trained teacher.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay with a firm internal deadline, plus the exhibition earlier on. Rewards argument structure rather than content, so a few concentrated hours change the grade and additional hours add almost nothing.

sections.heading: What a Zakher weekday actually leaves
paragraphs: The number that matters is not the school finish time but the point at which a student is home, fed and able to hold a technical argument. For a Zakher family, with the longest bus run in Al Ain, that point arrives late, and anything scheduled before it produces a session nobody gets value from. The table works through the day as it is rather than as a timetable describes it.

Two stages dominate and neither appears in a school calendar. The return bus run is long and it does not shorten at the end of the working day; if anything it stretches. And the Creativity, Activity, Service element that every Diploma student carries, plus any sport or club, routinely adds an hour on some days and none on others, which is why the first thing to establish is which weekdays are actually clear.

The honest reading of the table is that there is one usable weeknight hour and it is not a strong one. That is not a reason to skip tutoring; it is a reason to put the right thing in it. Marking, correction, drills and oral practice all survive tiredness. New Higher Level content and full timed papers do not, and attempting them at half past eight teaches a student that they cannot do the subject.

Which is why weekend mornings matter more here than in any other part of Al Ain. A Saturday morning session is the same quality of hour that a family next to the school gets on a Tuesday afternoon, and treating it as the main slot rather than the overflow is the single highest-value scheduling decision available to this neighbourhood.

sections.heading: A weekend-led Diploma week, component by component
paragraphs: Here is the week written the way it should be for this area, which is the inverse of how tutoring is normally sold. The organising rule is that each component of the Diploma has a natural home in the week, determined by whether it needs a fresh head or merely a functioning one.

Timed papers, coursework methodology and anything requiring sustained reasoning go on the weekend morning. Marking, correction, calculation drills, command-term work and oral rehearsal go on the weeknight, because all of those survive a long day. Independent practice tasks are sized for a bus and an evening rather than for a free afternoon, which usually means a single question section rather than a paper.

The second rule is to leave a slot deliberately empty. Mock weeks, school trips, illness, travel and the occasional bus that does not arrive all happen, and a plan running at full capacity loses those sessions permanently. A plan built at about ninety per cent of capacity delivers more sessions across a year, which is counter-intuitive until you have watched a tight plan collapse in February.

The final column is the useful one. Writing the week down makes visible what it cannot hold, which from Zakher is almost always a second subject during term. Families who want two subjects supported should put the second into a holiday block rather than hunting for a third weeknight that is not there.

One refinement worth making with an older student. Ask them which of the two slots they would defend if they could keep only one. Diploma students judge their own capacity better than their parents do, and a week they helped design survives March, which matters more than any improvement to its contents.

sections.heading: Why the specialist match matters more the further out you live
paragraphs: There is a counter-intuitive consequence of living at the edge of a city with a small school set. The further out a family is, the smaller the pool of tutors willing to travel to them, and therefore the greater the gap between the tutor who is available and the tutor who teaches the subject. In central Al Mutaredh that gap is modest. In Zakher it is the whole problem.

The arithmetic behind it is unsentimental. A visiting tutor loses unpaid time on the journey, and the further the journey the more households they cannot serve that evening. That shows up in the UAE in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For Zakher the premium is at its highest and the choice at its narrowest.

Layer on the city's supply picture and the result is stark. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the number of people who have taught Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics or Spanish B to examination standard is small for the whole city. The subset of those who would drive to Zakher on a Wednesday evening, every week, for a term, is smaller still.

Matching online inverts the order of the decision. The specialism is fixed first and the slot negotiated second, which is the correct sequence when a student's grade depends on one particular teacher knowing one particular paper. Geography stops being a selection criterion, which for this neighbourhood is the entire practical argument.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a visiting tutor in Zakher
paragraphs: The search phrase says home tutor, so the comparison deserves to be made properly rather than dodged. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and on that axis we are simply not an option; the table says so in its last row rather than reframing it.

The decisive column here is not cost. It is what happens to a plan over thirty weeks when every session depends on the longest drive in the city. An arrangement that loses one session a month to a late bus, a long drive or a route change delivers around thirty sessions in a school year where a reliable one delivers forty, and ten sessions is an entire technique block.

The second is rescheduling. When a session cannot happen, an online slot moves in a message and a visiting slot moves only if the tutor's whole evening route can be rearranged. Over a Diploma that difference compounds into weeks of teaching, and it is the reason the headline rate is the wrong thing to compare.

The third is the weekend morning. Visiting tutors rarely offer weekend mornings to outlying areas, and when they do the rate reflects it. For Zakher that is the slot the entire plan should be built on, which makes its routine availability worth more than anything else in the comparison.

The caveat belongs here too. Some students genuinely work better with an adult physically in the room, and for them the in-home premium and the lost sessions may still be the right trade. The table argues about reliability and choice, not about every child, and a Zakher family should settle that part on their own child rather than on a comparison.

sections.heading: Using the holidays, because the bus stops
paragraphs: School breaks change the position for a Zakher family more than for anyone else in Al Ain, because the thing that constrains them disappears entirely. With no bus run, mornings become available every day, and morning work is categorically better than evening work for anything requiring consolidation rather than drill.

The right use of a break is content repair rather than exam technique. Technique work needs the context of the term, with marked school papers and a live mock to react to, whereas content gaps need consecutive days and a rested student. A block of six to twelve sessions across a break does more real learning than the same hours spread through a term at half past eight at night.

The largest such window is the summer between the two Diploma years, and most families give it away. There are no competing coursework deadlines, no commute and no school timetable, and the two topics named in the Year 12 reports can be closed properly. Families who use it rarely need a rescue in the spring of Year 13, when the week has no room for one.

Ramadan deserves its own note, because its effect here is unusually positive. Shortened school days mean an earlier return, which for a family whose problem is the length of the journey creates afternoon capacity that does not otherwise exist in term time. Agree the Ramadan shape a fortnight ahead, use either an afternoon or a post-iftar slot, and move sessions rather than cancelling them.

sections.heading: ADEK, permits and what a Zakher parent can verify
paragraphs: Zakher is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. None of the competitor pages reviewed for this project names ADEK at all, which is a reasonable signal about how locally grounded a tutoring site is.

The rule with the most direct bearing on a Zakher family concerns their own school's staff. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the same. Where a tutor's pitch rests on teaching at your child's school, that is a reason to decline rather than a credential.

On permits generally: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students, and the route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted is unverified. For the record, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge International. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different and specific thing.

sections.heading: Coursework, deadlines and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: A difficult timetable raises the risk of a late-night coursework decision, which is why the academic-honesty boundary belongs on this page rather than in small print. The Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, and the IB treats a breach as grounds for withholding the Diploma.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial and worth buying. They can explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a method can support the analysis the criteria demand, point out where a conclusion does not follow from the data, identify missing evaluation, teach citation properly and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. Most of that work belongs early in the cycle.

What a tutor must not do is write any part of the submission, rewrite rather than comment, or supply a research question or dataset as finished work. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750. For a family already short of time that is the most tempting and the most damaging purchase in the market.

The scheduling answer is to make the late decision impossible. Put the internal deadlines in the calendar in September, book the coursework block onto weekend mornings in the first fortnight of each cycle, and front-load it onto methodology. Four sessions then outperform twenty at the end, and the panic conversation never arrives.

One related boundary, since it comes up under deadline pressure. We will not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. The correct route is to cite the official page and link to it, and a provider offering a library of board material is telling you something about its approach to everything else.

sections.heading: What we can cover from here, and what we cannot
paragraphs: Availability transparency is missing from every competitor page reviewed for this project, so here is ours stated as a limit. Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English are well supplied and can usually be matched within a week in most slots. Chemistry Higher Level and Physics Higher Level are tighter and should be booked in the autumn of Year 13. Spanish B and French B are thin, and often declined.

The second limit is the slot. The weekend morning band and the six to eight weekday band are the two parts of the week every Al Ain family wants, so they fill first. A Zakher family that can also use an earlier Friday slot or a later weekend morning sees a wider choice of tutor immediately, and in the scarce subjects that choice is the difference between a specialist and a fortnight's wait.

When we cannot cover a request we give a date or decline it. We do not substitute a general science tutor for a Chemistry Higher Level request, or a fluent speaker for a language teaching request. That substitution looks like a solution for about a month and then costs a term, and on a timetable this tight a term is the whole margin.

Put the same questions to anyone you are considering, including a local in-home tutor. Can you cover this subject at this level, in this slot, starting when, and what happens if the first tutor is wrong. Specific answers make a provider comparable. In a city with a school set this size, an unqualified yes to everything is not an answer.
