faqs.question: Is private tutoring cheaper in Al Ain than in Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Partly. Group classes, centre packages and informal local arrangements are usually cheaper here, because they are priced against a smaller local economy. Specialist one-to-one rates are not, because they are set by a Gulf-wide online market and because local supply of a given specification is thinner. Published qualified online rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour wherever you live. What is genuinely different in Al Ain is waiting time for a local in-home specialist, which can cost weeks rather than dirhams.

faqs.question: What would an in-home tutor charge to come to Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for in-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350 and some home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500. Those are other providers' rates. IB Gram makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If you do choose a visiting tutor locally, ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, which costs nothing to obtain.

faqs.question: What is the least we can spend and still find out what is wrong?
faqs.answer: Three sessions. One reading a marked paper and naming the recurring error types, two fixing the largest one, finishing with your child attempting the same question type unaided. At published qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour that is a few hundred dirhams, and you keep the written diagnosis whatever you decide next. Most families are quoted a term instead, which is worth noticing: ask for the smallest option and see whether it is offered.

faqs.question: Is a group class at an Al Ain centre good value for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: For a specific purpose, yes. A class retells a subject with structure at the lowest cost per hour of any supervised option, which suits a student who has fallen behind across the whole specification. What it cannot do is find your child's individual mark losses, because nobody in the room is marking your child's script against the published scheme. If the problem is two marks a question going missing on units and method, a class will not touch it however many you attend.

faqs.question: Why does a specialist in my child's subject cost more here than a local tutor?
faqs.answer: Scarcity rather than distance. A tutor who works to Cambridge 0625 Paper 6 or Edexcel 4CH1 at mark-scheme level is uncommon anywhere in the Gulf and uncommon locally, and the rate reflects how few people can do it. A local generalist is cheaper because the skill is more widely held. The decision should follow the marked script: a content gap can be closed by a good generalist, while a mark-scheme loss needs somebody with the scheme in front of them.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a house in Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service for us. Teaching for Al Ain families is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through paper questions. In a city with a thin local supply of specification specialists, that is a supply fix rather than a convenience: your child is taught by somebody who knows their exact code and tier.

faqs.question: When in the two IGCSE years is money best spent?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families spend it. The common pattern is nothing in Year 10 and a great deal between the mock and study leave in Year 11, which is the most expensive possible ordering because availability is tightest and what tutoring can achieve is narrowest then. Moving part of the same budget into Year 10, while content is still being taught and the tier decision is still open, buys considerably more. The largest single line in a sensible plan sits a year before the papers.

faqs.question: How much does it cost us if nobody confirmed the syllabus code?
faqs.answer: A term, usually. A Cambridge candidate drilling Pearson-style questions, or a 0580 candidate working through 0607 papers, practises diligently and builds the wrong instincts, and nobody notices until the real paper looks unfamiliar. The fix is free: email the examinations officer and ask in writing for the code and tier on each entry. It is the single highest-value ten minutes available to a parent and it costs nothing at all.

faqs.question: Is a monthly tutoring package in Al Ain better value than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Only buy a package where marked work has already been read and the length is justified by it, and only where you can stop. Monthly packages advertised in this market have included AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The question to ask about any of them is what happens at the midpoint if the evidence says stop. If the answer is nothing, the discount is being paid for with your ability to change course.

faqs.question: What free help should an Al Ain family use before paying anyone?
faqs.answer: Four things. The marked script rather than the grade sheet. The subject teacher's answer to which three topics they would prioritise, a question they are rarely asked and answer well. Any departmental revision clinic the school runs, which is often under-attended through sheer lack of awareness. And the code, tier and study-leave date in writing from the examinations officer. Then the boards' own published specifications and official timetables, which we link rather than copy.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Al Ain help with IGCSE coursework in subjects that have it?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor teaches the skill the component assesses, explains the published criteria and their command words, questions the student about their own reasoning, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write the work, does not rewrite sentences and does not supply material for submission. We state that before any coursework support begins, because crossing the line creates a malpractice problem for the student rather than for the tutor.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working in Al Ain need a permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason for an independent tutor not to hold one. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Al Jimi?
faqs.answer: Al Ain sits within the emirate of Abu Dhabi, so private schools here are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation and publishes inspection outcomes. Elsewhere in the country the map differs: Dubai has KHDA, Sharjah has SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. No tutoring provider, including us, holds approval from any of them.

faqs.question: After six weeks, what should show that the money was well spent?
faqs.answer: A second timed paper, marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic, showing movement in the specific areas the diagnosis named. Not a higher overall mark alone, which can move for reasons unrelated to the teaching. You should also hear your child name their own weakest topic without prompting, which is a reliable sign that the work has become theirs. If neither has happened, the plan or the match is wrong and should change rather than continue.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below is listed against a named syllabus and tier rather than a subject label, because Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry are not the same course and a tutor who has only taught one will say so.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Al Khabisi who knows this syllabus?
paragraphs: The honest answer has two halves. In a subject such as Mathematics or Biology, yes: Al Ain has enough British-curriculum teaching capacity that a competent IGCSE tutor is findable, in home or online. In Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Pearson Further Pure Maths, Computer Science 0478 or a second modern language, probably not within driving distance of Al Khabisi, and no amount of searching will change that. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and the teaching pool mirrors it.

That matters more in IGCSE than families expect, because the word 'IGCSE' hides two different qualifications. Cambridge International runs IGCSE with syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry. Pearson runs International GCSE with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry. The content overlaps heavily. The paper structures, the tiering, the practical arrangements and the assessment objectives do not. A tutor who has taught 0625 for six years and has never seen 4PH1 will be good value and still occasionally wrong about what is on the paper.

So the first thing to establish is not availability but identity. Which board does your child's school enter them with, which syllabus code, and which tier. The school office will tell you, and the code is usually printed on the statement of entry. Walking into a tutoring conversation with 'Cambridge 0580, Extended tier, Paper 2 and Paper 4' is a different conversation from walking in with 'she needs help with maths', and it filters out most of the mismatch risk before any money changes hands.

Al Khabisi sits in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, which is itself a signal about how locally informed those pages are. The emirate regulator matters to a tutoring decision because it sets what the school must deliver and publishes the inspection record you can read before trusting a school's own account of its results.

IB Gram's answer to the availability question is deliberately unromantic. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. We match an Al Khabisi student to a teacher of their specific syllabus and tier, teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and tell you before you book if the combination you need is not covered. That last part is the whole point. A stated gap costs a family nothing; a concealed one costs them a term.

Everything below is written to be useful even if you hire someone else. The codes, the four questions, the tier table and the permit checks all work on any tutor in Al Ain. We would rather an Al Khabisi family hired well locally than badly from us.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.programmesIntro: Three qualification routes run through Al Ain's British-curriculum schools, and the tutoring question is different in each. Knowing which one your child is on is the precondition for everything else on this page.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subjects are identified by four-digit codes and most sciences and maths are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5 depending on the subject's grading scale. Sciences carry a practical component, either a laboratory test paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one a school uses changes how a student should revise. Cambridge also runs Checkpoint tests in Lower Secondary in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the dominant British-curriculum route in Al Ain's private schools, and the administrative detail that catches UAE families is zoning. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. Work from the school's zone version, not a timetable found by searching.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1 and so on. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; the sciences are untiered single-route specifications with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical exam. Some subjects are available as modular units, which changes when a student can bank a result and when a resit is possible.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Progression to AS and A Level
programmes.description: The IGCSE tier and grade a student finishes with determines which AS subjects are realistically open. Extended tier Mathematics at grade 7 or above is the normal expectation for AS Mathematics; Core tier closes it. Students who discover this in Year 12 have lost the option, which is why tier choice in Year 10 is a decision with a two-year shadow.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Khabisi families this connects to the Ministry of Education equivalency rules, which matter for UAE university entry. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Al Khabisi families most often ask about, each with the syllabus codes to quote and the component where marks actually go missing. Codes are the fastest way to check a tutor knows what they are talking about.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended tier adds functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and harder algebraic manipulation. Marks are lost on method lines omitted in multi-step questions and on calculator discipline. A tutor should be able to say which paper numbers your child sits and what each is worth without looking it up.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Calculus, series and a far heavier algebraic load than 0580, taken by stronger cohorts as preparation for A Level. This is the clearest example of local scarcity around Al Khabisi: few tutors in the drivable radius have taught it, and a 0580 specialist is not a substitute. Online matching is the realistic route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, waves and the practical component are where the two boards diverge most. Cambridge students sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Revision that ignores which applies wastes a third of the preparation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry, then organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. Most lost marks are arithmetic and unit handling rather than chemistry, and the fix is drill on a narrow set of calculation types. A good tutor will ask for a marked paper before the first session rather than after it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade. 'State', 'describe' and 'explain' carry different mark allocations and students who revise content without revising command terms plateau around grade 6. Well supplied online, so there is no reason to accept a long wait or a premium.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award covering all three sciences in compressed form, with different content coverage from the separate sciences. Families frequently assume a separate-science tutor can cover it; the content map differs, and an hour spent on topics not on the specification is an hour lost.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Directed writing, reading response and, for second-language candidates, a different specification entirely. The commonest misdiagnosis in Al Ain is placing a first-language candidate with a second-language tutor or the reverse; the mark schemes reward different things.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, definitions and applied data response. Students lose marks by describing rather than analysing, and the correction is structural, so it transfers across every question in the paper. Usually four to six hours of work, not a term.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and, for ICT, a practical component on specific software tasks. Another genuinely scarce subject in the Al Ain tutoring pool, and one where an enthusiastic programmer who has not taught the specification will teach the wrong things well.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source skills, case-study recall and extended-answer structure. The marks sit in how an answer is organised rather than in how much is remembered, which is why these respond quickly to a small number of focused sessions on essay and source technique.

sections.heading: The honest answer about local syllabus expertise
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Khabisi who genuinely knows your child's specification exists for the common subjects and frequently does not for the uncommon ones. That is not a sales position; it is what a city of Al Ain's size and school count produces. The private-school set here is much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and the pool of teachers who have taught a given syllabus to a given tier for several cohorts scales with it.

The failure mode this creates is specific and avoidable. A family searches, finds two or three local tutors, and hires the one who can come on a Tuesday. That tutor is competent, pleasant and teaches the subject in general. Three months later the student is no better on Paper 4 extended response because nobody ever looked at Paper 4 extended response. Nothing dishonest happened. The match was made on availability, and availability is not a teaching qualification.

The alternative is to make the match on the specification and let the schedule follow. That is what online delivery does: it replaces a question about who can drive to Al Khabisi with a question about who has taught 0580 Extended, and those produce different shortlists. For Mathematics or Biology the shortlists overlap. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 or a second language they barely intersect at all.

What follows is the practical version of that argument. The syllabus codes to establish first, four questions that test whether a tutor knows them, an honest coverage table showing where our own pool is thin, and the regulatory checks worth making before any money moves. None of it requires you to use IB Gram, and the questions work just as well on a tutor you find yourself.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: the codes that decide the answer
paragraphs: Two boards dominate British-curriculum entries in Al Ain, and conflating them is the commonest technical error in this market. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel examine overlapping content through different paper structures, different tiering and different practical arrangements. A tutor fluent in one can be confidently wrong about the other, and the student is the one who discovers it.

The table below gives the codes for the subjects Al Khabisi families ask about most, with the difference that actually changes how a student prepares. Quote the code at the start of a tutoring conversation and the response tells you a great deal. A specialist will immediately reference paper numbers and weightings. A generalist will say the subject is the subject.

One structural difference deserves emphasis because it affects revision directly. Cambridge sciences carry a separate practical component, either a laboratory test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and schools choose which route to enter. Pearson's international sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers instead. A student revising for a practical paper they are not sitting, or ignoring practical technique because they assume it is not examined, loses marks that were never about the science.

The second is tiering. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended with a grade ceiling on Core; Pearson Mathematics A splits into Foundation and Higher. The sciences behave differently again. Before buying tuition, confirm which tier your child is entered for, because a tutor teaching Extended content to a Core candidate is wasting the hour and a tutor teaching Core content to an Extended candidate is capping the grade.

sections.heading: Four questions that separate a specialist from a generalist
paragraphs: These take about five minutes and you can ask them of anyone, local or online, before paying. The point is not to catch a tutor out but to find out quickly whether the hour you are buying is syllabus teaching or general academic support, both of which are legitimate and are priced differently in this market.

A specialist answers with structure: paper numbers, weightings, components, the two or three topics where their students historically lose marks and what they do about it. A generalist answers with reassurance: they know the subject well, they have helped many students, your child will gain confidence. There is nothing wrong with the second answer at the lower end of the market, where published rates start around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, but it should not be bought at specialist prices.

Ask about between-session work as well. A tutor who sets nothing between sessions is selling you an hour of attention, and IGCSE grades do not move on an hour a week of attention. A tutor who sets a specific past-paper question, marks it and brings it to the next session is selling you a working loop, which is the thing that changes outcomes.

Finally, ask what happens if it is not working. The useful answer involves a review point and a willingness to change tutor. The unhelpful answer involves more hours. Families who do not agree a review point at the start tend to discover six months later that nobody ever defined what success looked like, which is how a tutoring budget doubles without a decision being taken.

sections.heading: Where our own Al Ain coverage is thin
paragraphs: Availability transparency is absent from every competitor page reviewed for this project, so here is ours. The table states, by subject and tier, how well we can cover an Al Khabisi request, how long a match typically takes, and what we do when we cannot cover it. In-home coverage is zero in every row, because IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE.

The pattern follows Al Ain's school set. Mathematics, the separate sciences, English and the humanities are well supplied, because every British-curriculum school teaches them and the teaching population is large. Additional Mathematics, Computer Science, ICT practical work and second modern languages are thin, because few schools offer them and fewer teachers have taught them to examination standard.

When a combination is not covered we say so and offer one of three things: a different slot, a start date a fortnight out when a tutor finishes another commitment, or a straight decline. We do not substitute a general science tutor for a Chemistry request or a fluent speaker for a language teaching request. A substitution looks like a solution for about four weeks and then costs a term.

This is worth asking of any provider, including local in-home agencies. The question is simply: can you cover this exact syllabus and tier, and if not, when. A provider that answers with a date is being useful. A provider that answers yes to everything is either very large or not listening, and in a city the size of Al Ain the second is more likely.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision with a two-year shadow
paragraphs: Tier choice is made in Year 10 and felt in Year 12. Cambridge Core tier carries a grade ceiling, so a student entered for Core cannot reach the grades that AS Mathematics and the separate sciences expect at the next stage. That is a reasonable choice for a student who would otherwise be out of their depth, and a costly one made by default because a mock went badly in October.

The specific error around Al Khabisi, where the Extended cohort is strong, runs the other way as often as not. Students are kept on Extended when the mark evidence says the content is not secure, on the reasonable logic that Extended keeps options open. It does, right up until the paper, where an insecure Extended candidate can land below what a secure Core candidate would have achieved. Both errors are tier decisions taken on hope rather than on marked work.

The practical approach is to decide on evidence and to decide late but not too late. Collect three marked papers across a term, look at which questions were attempted rather than which were correct, and have the conversation with the school in the spring of Year 10 rather than the autumn of Year 11. Tuition in this window is unusually valuable because it can genuinely change the tier a child is capable of sitting.

The table sets out what each tier means for the next step. Note the final column: the number of tutoring hours implied is not the same, because moving a student from secure Core to secure Extended is a content project, while moving a secure Extended student from grade 6 to grade 8 is a technique project and much shorter.

sections.heading: Is this tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and a parent can check it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no listed fee. Because the permit is free and quick, a tutor who does not hold one has no practical excuse, and a tutor who cites it as a reason for a higher rate is describing something else.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you and any specific amount circulating online should be treated as unverified. The useful question for a parent is not the penalty but the permit: which category, issued when.

One restriction applies specifically to Al Khabisi because of the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording on ADEK's own policy document, but treat any offer of your child's own classroom teacher as privately paid tuition to be declined.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and what a tutor must not touch
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the Diploma, but the boundary still matters, and it matters in a specific place: practical and investigative work, and any component completed under school supervision. Work submitted as the student's own must be the student's own, and a tutor's job stops at teaching, questioning and marking.

Inside the boundary: teaching a technique, explaining why a mark scheme rewards one phrasing over another, marking a student's own practice work, drilling calculation types, and rehearsing an oral or presentation component. For practical papers, that includes teaching apparatus conventions, uncertainty treatment and how to read a results table, all of which are examinable skills that can be taught in the abstract.

Outside the boundary: producing data, writing up an investigation, supplying answers for work that will be submitted, or preparing material that a student presents as their own. Reproducing board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is also something we will not do; the right move is to cite the official page and link to it, because reproducing them is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, worse.

Say this out loud when hiring anyone. A tutor who offers to help with submitted work in any form beyond feedback is offering the student a risk, and a provider that advertises it is telling you what else it is willing to do. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed assessments to UAE students outright; the existence of that market is the reason the boundary is stated here rather than assumed.

sections.heading: The series UAE candidates sit, counted backwards
paragraphs: One factual correction first, because it is widely repeated and acting on it would make a family miss an entry. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any page offering a UAE family a February/March entry deadline is describing another country's calendar.

Counted backwards, the June series shapes the whole of Year 11. School entry decisions and tier confirmations happen in the autumn term, months before the papers. Mocks fall in the winter. The last useful window for closing a content gap ends roughly ten weeks out, after which an hour buys technique rather than knowledge. The final fortnight should be the student marking their own practice against mark schemes.

The November series is the resit and second-chance route for Cambridge candidates, and for Pearson it is a full series in its own right. The documented Pearson pattern gives a sense of the lag between paper and result: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Two administrative points worth more than any revision tip. First, Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so always work from the school's own zone version. Second, Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so link the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.

Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: MoE equivalency for IGCSE students
paragraphs: Families in Al Khabisi planning on a UAE university place need to know what the Ministry of Education equivalency route asks of a British-curriculum student, and one ranking competitor publishes the wrong number, which is a useful demonstration of why sourcing matters.

On the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five.

No Diploma points threshold is published here, and this page does not invent one. Where an IB figure is needed, it must be read on the Ministry's own site or the emirate attestation authority's page rather than taken from a tutoring site. The same caution applies to anything about attestation processing: describe it, cite the authority, and send parents to the official channel.

Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and nobody should be told that tutoring is required for it. What tuition can legitimately do is help a student secure the grades the rule asks for, which for most Al Khabisi families means making sure five subjects are comfortably clear of the threshold rather than one or two being spectacular.

process.title: Find the syllabus code first
process.description: Before contacting anyone, get the board, the four-digit or alphanumeric code and the tier from the school office or the statement of entry. Cambridge 0620 Extended and Pearson 4CH1 are different requests. Arriving with the code turns a vague conversation into a specific one and removes most of the mismatch risk at no cost.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and a marked paper
process.description: A recent marked paper is worth more than a description of the problem, because it shows which questions were attempted and which were left blank. Blanks point to content; method errors point to technique. We match from that evidence rather than from a subject label, which is why the first session starts further along.

process.title: Free diagnostic trial with the proposed tutor
process.description: A full session, no card required, with the person who would teach the course. Use the four questions from this page on them. By the end you should have a named component, a named weakness and an estimate of hours. If the tutor was describing a course like your child's rather than your child's, say so and we match again.

process.title: Agree a plan with a review point
process.description: Sessions per week, the fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, what gets set between sessions, and the session number at which we check whether the original weakness has closed. The review point is the part families skip and the part that keeps the cost finite.

process.title: Work the loop, then stop
process.description: Teach, set, mark, review. When the weakness is closed, end the block or move to the next named one. Continuing by default is how tutoring becomes a subscription, and an honest provider should be willing to tell you when there is nothing left worth buying.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE syllabus my child in Al Khabisi is actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office for the board and the syllabus code, or look at the statement of entry, where the code is printed. You are looking for something like Cambridge 0580 Mathematics Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher. Also ask which paper numbers your child is entered for and, in the sciences, whether they sit a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Those three facts determine what any tutor should be teaching and are the fastest way to tell whether a tutor is describing your child's course or a similar one.

faqs.question: Is there really nobody in Al Ain who teaches Additional Mathematics 0606?
faqs.answer: There are some, and not many. Additional Mathematics is offered by relatively few schools, so the pool of teachers who have taken a cohort through it is small, and in a city with a much smaller private-school set than Abu Dhabi island that pool shrinks further. The practical consequence is a longer wait and a higher local rate. A 0580 Extended specialist is not a substitute, because 0606 introduces calculus and series that sit outside the 0580 specification entirely. Online matching is usually the realistic route from Al Khabisi.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our house in Al Khabisi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Khabisi students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We state this before booking because the phrase people search is 'home tutor' and nobody should discover the format after paying. If having an adult physically in the room is a requirement, hire locally and use the permit and syllabus questions on this page to check the person you find.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE the same qualification?
faqs.answer: They are different qualifications with overlapping content. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580, 0625 and 0620 and tiers many subjects into Core and Extended. Pearson uses codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1, tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher, and assesses science practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical component. Universities treat both as international GCSEs. For tutoring purposes the difference is decisive, because paper structures, mark-scheme wording and practical arrangements all differ.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to prove they know the specification?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which syllabus code and tier have you taught, and for how many cohorts. Which paper do your students lose most marks on, and what causes it. What will you set between sessions, and will you mark it. What is the review point, and what happens if it is not working. A specialist answers with paper numbers, weightings and a recurring error pattern. A generalist answers with reassurance about experience and confidence, which is a fair product at budget rates and not worth a specialist price.

faqs.question: My child is on Core tier. Can tutoring move them to Extended?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding evidence is in the mock papers rather than the mock grades. Look at which Extended questions were attempted, not which were correct. A student attempting most questions and making method errors has a technique problem and can usually move tier with a term of work. A student leaving half the paper blank has a content problem, which takes longer and may not be the right choice at all. Have the conversation with the school in the spring of Year 10, because Core carries a grade ceiling that closes AS routes later.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutors in Al Ain need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's own Al Ain school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Not for payment. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Teachers who tutor outside school hours must hold the permit. If a tutor pitches themselves on the basis that they teach at your child's school, that is a reason to decline rather than a selling point. Check the current wording on ADEK's own published policy.

faqs.question: If 0625 Physics has a practical paper, how does an online tutor prepare my child for it?
faqs.answer: Practical marks in IGCSE come from examinable skills rather than from a tutor watching an experiment. Apparatus conventions, drawing and reading a results table, uncertainty and significant figures, choosing a suitable scale for a graph, and the standard phrasing a mark scheme rewards can all be taught and drilled remotely using past practical papers. Which paper your child sits matters: Cambridge offers a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, while Pearson examines practical skills within the written papers. Confirm with the school before any revision plan is built.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, and a page that offers a UAE family a February/March deadline is quoting another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so always work from your school's zone version and the live official timetable.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry of Education equivalency rule ask Al Khabisi students for?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and separately submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the family through the official channel; no tutoring provider performs, guarantees or speeds it up.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Al Ain families request tuition for most often?
faqs.answer: In our Al Ain requests the order is Mathematics, then Physics, then Chemistry, then English for second-language candidates. Mathematics dominates because the Extended tier's algebra and trigonometry load is where a weak Year 9 foundation shows. Physics appears because electricity and the practical component are taught late and revised badly. Chemistry appears because moles arithmetic defeats students who are otherwise fine. English for second-language candidates appears when a child has been placed on the wrong specification, which is worth checking before buying any tuition at all.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring in the spring of Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is late for content and fine for technique, and the distinction decides what to buy. Ten weeks out, an hour can still fix command-term use, mark-scheme phrasing, calculation drills, timing and question selection, and those commonly carry a grade. It cannot rebuild a topic that was never learnt. So the right purchase that late is a paper-technique block on named components, working from marked papers, rather than a general course. Starting a term earlier is cheaper for the same effect, but late help aimed narrowly is not wasted money.

faqs.question: Should we use one tutor for both Maths 0580 and Chemistry 0620, or two?
faqs.answer: Occasionally and not usually. A Physics and Mathematics combination is plausible because the specifications share technique. Chemistry and English is not, and a tutor who offers both is almost certainly a generalist. Two subjects also need two diagnoses, and an hour split between them gives neither enough time to move. Where a family needs two subjects, two specialists with one hour each works better than one person with two, and the cost is identical. The exception is study-habit work, which transfers and is worth buying once.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor you match is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: We change the tutor, not the plan, and we do it on your judgement rather than after a negotiation. The trial session exists so that this is discovered before money is committed. If it emerges later, say so at the review point. What we will not do is fill a gap with a substitute from a different specification to keep a booking alive, because that is the failure that costs a family a term. If we cannot cover your syllabus and tier, we give you a date or decline.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.closingHeading: Start with the syllabus code, then ask the four questions
al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khabisi.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Khabisi, the sequence that saves the most money and time is: get the board, code and tier from the school; find a tutor who can discuss that specification in paper numbers; ask what gets set and marked between sessions; and agree a review point. intro.heading: Start with the cheapest thing that works
paragraphs: The usual way to shop for tutoring is to decide a budget and then find out what it buys. That gets the order wrong. The better sequence is to establish the smallest intervention that would actually fix the problem, price that, and only move up when the cheap option demonstrably cannot do the job. For a large share of IGCSE problems the smallest intervention is four to six sessions on one component, which at mid-market rates is a one-off figure rather than a monthly commitment.

Here are the published bands this market works in, each attributed and read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 an hour. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65. Unitors publishes AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. That is a twentyfold spread, and it is not a quality ladder with a single rung size.

Monthly, the same picture looks different and more useful. Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour sessions. Those are the numbers a household budget is actually built from.

Al Maqam is on the southern side of Al Ain, spread across newer compounds, and distance has a direct cost effect. A visiting tutor loses something like forty unbilled minutes on a southern round trip, and the in-home band exists partly to pay for that. Online delivery at AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor removes the travel component from the price without removing the teacher.

Al Maqam sits in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Al Ain's private-school set is much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and that scarcity has a price consequence: in the subjects few schools offer, local rates sit at the top of their band and waits get longer. That is the most important local cost fact on this page.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. We quote per plan after a free trial session, and every AED figure on this page is a market band from a named source rather than an offer. The point of publishing them is that a family should know what the market charges before anyone names a number.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.programmesIntro: Price varies by route as well as by subject, because the amount of assessed material and the number of papers differ. These are the three routes a cost-conscious Al Maqam family will be choosing between.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes with many subjects tiered into Core and Extended, and a grade ceiling on Core. Sciences carry a practical component, either a laboratory test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses which. Cambridge runs the qualification in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests at Lower Secondary in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: The cost-relevant detail is that Extended tier covers more content, which means more hours if a student is behind. Moving a student from insecure Extended to secure Extended is a term's project, while polishing a secure Extended student's technique is a short block. Confirming the tier before buying anything is therefore the single cheapest decision available, and it is free: the school office will tell you.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and 4EA1. Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher; the international sciences are untiered and assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than separately. Modular availability in some subjects changes when a result can be banked and when a resit is possible, which has a cost implication of its own.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry historically means a January result, which matters if a deadline falls in between and a family is deciding whether a resit is worth paying for.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: The tier and grade a student leaves IGCSE with determines which AS subjects remain open. Core tier generally closes AS Mathematics and the separate sciences, and discovering that in Year 12 means paying for a recovery that a Year 10 conversation would have prevented. This is the most expensive avoidable error in the whole British-curriculum route.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university entry the Ministry of Education equivalency rule on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five. The cost consequence is that five comfortable passes are worth more than two outstanding ones and three marginal ones.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.subjectsIntro: The cost of support is not uniform across subjects, because scarcity sets the rate and the failure modes differ in how long they take to fix. Each entry below says what the hour has to do.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Well supplied, so the rate should sit mid-band rather than high. Most lost marks are omitted method lines in multi-step questions, which is a technique problem and therefore a short block rather than a term. The most commonly over-bought subject in this market.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Calculus and series outside the 0580 specification. Offered by few Al Ain schools, so the pool is small and local rates sit at the top of the band with longer waits. This is the clearest case where paying more is justified and a cheaper substitute is not a substitute.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, waves and the practical component. Uncertainty treatment and significant figures are cheap to fix and carry easy marks, which makes a three to five session block unusually good value compared with a standing weekly slot.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic defeats students who understand the chemistry perfectly well. Because the failure is narrow, so is the fix, and a family should resist being sold a whole-syllabus course when a calculation drill is what is needed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade and transfers across the paper once learned. Well supplied online, so there is no reason to accept a premium rate or a long wait. Among the cheapest subjects to improve per hour spent.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: A different content map from the separate sciences, so hours spent with a separate-science tutor can go on material that is not examined. Confirming the code before booking prevents an expensive and entirely invisible waste.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 first language, 0510/0511 second language; Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: First and second language are separate specifications. Placing a candidate with a tutor for the wrong one is the costliest misdiagnosis in this subject, because the mark schemes reward different things and the student improves at the wrong skill.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and applied data response. The usual failure, describing rather than analysing, is structural and transfers, so four to six hours does most of the available work. Poor value as an open-ended weekly commitment.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and ICT practical tasks. Scarce in Al Ain, so expect a top-of-band rate and a wait. A capable programmer who has not taught the specification is cheaper and will teach the wrong material competently.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source skills and extended-answer structure. The marks are in organisation rather than content volume, which makes these among the most improvable subjects per dirham spent, and almost always a block rather than a course.

sections.heading: The cheapest intervention that actually works
paragraphs: Start here rather than at the top. The table below lists interventions from least to most expensive, with what each genuinely fixes and the point at which it stops being enough. Most IGCSE problems presented to us are narrower than the family thinks, and a narrower problem needs a cheaper solution.

The first row is free and is skipped by almost everyone. Confirming the board, syllabus code and tier with the school office, and getting hold of a marked paper, costs nothing and frequently changes the diagnosis entirely. Families who buy a term of general support for a problem that turns out to be a wrong-specification placement have spent several thousand dirhams on the wrong question.

The second row is nearly free: using the school. Subject teachers hold clinics, departments run revision sessions and schools will usually explain a mark scheme if asked directly. None of that replaces one-to-one teaching for a real gap, but it closes a surprising number of the small ones, and it is the first thing worth exhausting.

The paid rows start where those stop. The ordering principle is that cost should follow scarcity and difficulty: a technique problem in a well-supplied subject is the cheapest thing in this market, and a content rebuild in a subject few teachers cover is the dearest. If a quote does not reflect that logic, ask why.

One caution about the cheapest rows. Free is not the same as sufficient, and a family who exhausts the school's own support and still has a student stuck on extended-response technique has learned something useful rather than wasted a term. The ladder is meant to be climbed, not admired from the bottom.

sections.heading: What a properly supported IGCSE year costs
paragraphs: Families budget tutoring as a flat monthly figure and it is not one. The need is lumpy: light in early Year 10, heavier when tier decisions are made, heaviest in the ten weeks before a series, and lighter again in the final fortnight. The table stages it, which is the form a two-year plan can actually be priced in.

The most valuable row is the tier decision window in the spring of Year 10. A small number of hours there, aimed at whether a student can be made secure on Extended content, changes the qualification they leave with and therefore what the next stage will cost. Hours spent later cannot buy back a tier.

The row most families get wrong is the final fortnight. The instinct is to add sessions as the papers approach, and the evidence from marked work usually says the opposite: fewer new inputs, more self-marking, earlier nights. A provider proposing extra hours in the last week without pointing at a paper is responding to anxiety, and anxiety is expensive.

Totalled, a staged plan in one subject across both IGCSE years lands well below a flat AED 1,000 a month sustained for twenty-four months, and does more work. That is an argument for sequencing rather than for spending, and it is the single most useful thing on this page.

A second planning note. These hour counts assume one subject. A student needing two supported does not need double the hours in each, because the study-habit and timing work overlaps, but they do need two diagnoses and two tutors. From Al Maqam, with limited weekday capacity, the second subject usually belongs in a holiday block rather than in a third weeknight.

sections.heading: The hourly bands, cheapest first, and the question to ask each
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no Al Ain family transacts in. The table below gives the published AED bands in ascending order, with the question worth asking at each level. The bands are competitors' figures quoted for comparison, not claims about their quality.

Reading upward rather than downward changes behaviour. A family that starts at AED 650 and negotiates downward ends up paying a lot for reassurance. A family that starts at AED 50 and moves up only when the cheaper option visibly fails ends up paying for the specific thing that was missing, which is usually one band up rather than four.

The questions in the final column are the actual value of the table. At the budget end the right question is what the hour contains, because supervised practice and syllabus teaching are different products sold under one word. At the top end the right question is what makes this individual scarce, and the answer should be a subject, a level and a track record rather than an adjective.

One band deserves particular scepticism, and it is the in-home one. AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included is a legitimate price for a car and forty unbilled minutes. From a southern Al Ain address it is also the band where a family is most likely to be paying a premium for a tutor who does not teach the subject at issue, which is the worst combination available.

sections.heading: The three extras nobody quotes
paragraphs: A quoted hourly rate is not the price of tutoring, and the gap between them is where family budgets quietly fail. Three extras recur, none of them dishonest in itself, and all of them worth asking about before the first session rather than discovering in month three.

The first is cancellation. A tutor who bills for sessions cancelled inside twenty-four hours is being reasonable about their own income, and a family with an unpredictable week should know the figure. Over a term, two or three billed cancellations is the price of a whole short block, and it is entirely avoidable with a stated policy and a slot that can move.

The second is tax treatment. Ask simply whether the quoted figure includes value added tax, and get the answer in writing. This page does not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that would need a Federal Tax Authority citation, and a tutoring site is the wrong place to learn it. What a family can reasonably insist on is clarity about the number they are being asked to pay.

The third is materials and marking. Some providers charge for resources or for marking work between sessions, and some include both. Neither model is wrong, but they are not comparable on the hourly rate alone. Ask whether work set between sessions is marked, and whether that marking is inside the hour or billed on top; for an IGCSE plan that detail changes the real cost by a meaningful fraction.

sections.heading: Group or one-to-one: the economics for an IGCSE student
paragraphs: Group tuition is obviously cheaper per hour and not obviously cheaper per grade, and the distinction depends on one thing: whether every student in the group has the same gap. That is a question with a factual answer, and a family can ask it before joining.

Where a group works is broad revision. Four students covering a full syllabus at similar standard get most of the benefit of the hour each, and the cost per student falls sharply. Where it fails is a specific weakness: a student who is secure everywhere except extended-response questions spends most of each hour watching someone else's problem being solved.

There is a second, quieter cost to groups that nobody prices. A student who is behind will not ask the question they need to ask in front of three peers, and a student who is ahead will stop paying attention. Both are real losses, and both are invisible in a rate comparison.

IB Gram provides one-to-one only, which is a commercial position as well as a pedagogical one and should be read as such. If the budget points to a group, the sensible approach is to find one organised by topic rather than by subject, ask what the group's actual starting point is, and keep a short one-to-one block in reserve for the component the group will not reach.

A reasonable hybrid exists and is rarely offered. Use a group for broad syllabus revision at the lower rate, and keep three or four one-to-one sessions in reserve for the component the group will never reach. That costs less than a full one-to-one plan and more than a group, which is usually the correct answer for a family genuinely constrained on budget.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of UAE school fees
paragraphs: Tutoring spend makes more sense placed beside school fees than examined alone, and there is published context worth using. In Dubai, the private school sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7.

On fees, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

Those figures are Dubai's and are cited as such; Al Maqam sits under ADEK rather than KHDA and nothing above should be read as applying to Al Ain's fees. What the context does give an Al Ain family is a sense of scale. Against a school fee measured in tens of thousands of dirhams a year, a staged tutoring plan of AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month for part of a year is a modest marginal cost, and an unstaged one running for twenty-four months is not.

The honest conclusion is that tutoring is worth buying deliberately and worth stopping deliberately. The families who spend least per grade are the ones who defined the problem, bought the narrowest thing that would fix it and ended the arrangement when it was fixed. Nobody in this market has a commercial interest in telling you that, which is why it belongs on the page.

sections.heading: A free permit, and why nobody should charge you for it
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit and the permit is free, which matters on a cost page because it is sometimes presented as a justification for a higher rate. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

The breadth of the eligible list is the part that surprises families in Al Maqam, where a good tutor is as likely to be a neighbour as an agency name. MoHRE admits teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students — so the UAE University undergraduate taking Core maths on a Saturday morning and the full-time school teacher doing evening work sit under one scheme. The service to ask about by name is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, the website or the e-services system. Its page lists no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time, which is short enough that a tutor who has been teaching in this district for a term has had no reason not to hold one.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere, so no amount should be quoted to you, and a figure circulating online as a penalty should be treated as unverified. The question worth asking is about the permit rather than the penalty: which category, issued when.

One further distinction, because it is sometimes used loosely in pricing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, involving initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific thing, and no online tutor or matching platform, including IB Gram, should be described as holding it.

sections.heading: What money cannot buy, at any price
paragraphs: The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750. That number belongs on a cost page because it is the single worst purchase available in this market: it buys a risk to the qualification the whole two years were for, and it is marketed in the same search results as legitimate tutoring.

The boundary is checkable. Legitimate support means teaching a technique, explaining why a mark scheme rewards one phrasing over another, marking the student's own practice work, drilling calculation types and rehearsing oral components. For IGCSE practical papers it includes apparatus conventions, uncertainty treatment and reading results tables, all examinable skills that can be taught without a laboratory.

What falls outside is producing data, writing up an investigation, supplying answers for submitted work, or preparing material a student presents as their own. We also will not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; the right move is to cite the official page and link to it.

One test, asked before any money moves, settles which kind of provider you are speaking to. Ask what they will do if a student brings coursework the night before it is due. An answer about reading the draft and marking it against criteria is correct. An answer that involves fixing it tells you what else that provider is willing to sell, and at that point the rate is irrelevant.

sections.heading: Where Al Maqam families waste money
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the preventable spend we see from this area, and all four are within a parent's control. The first is paying the in-home travel premium for a compromise: a southern address, a thin local pool and a narrow evening window combine so that the tutor who can come is often not a teacher of the subject at issue, and the family pays the top of the band for general supervision.

The second is buying hours instead of a diagnosis. A student losing marks on Chemistry calculations needs a few hours on moles arithmetic, not a syllabus course. Without a diagnosis the default purchase is open-ended weekly support that renews every month because nobody defined what finished looks like, and that is the largest single waste available in this market.

The third is spreading thinly. Four subjects at one hour each costs more and achieves less than one subject at four hours, because each subject gets too little to change anything. A family with a real budget constraint should support one subject properly and use the school's own clinics for the rest.

The fourth is churn. Changing tutor three times in a year means paying three times for the first few sessions, which are always the slowest, and a student who has explained their own weakness to three different adults stops bothering. Diagnose once, match once, review on a schedule rather than on a bad week.

process.title: Do the free step first
process.description: Get the board, syllabus code and tier from the school office and obtain a recent marked paper. This costs nothing, takes one phone call and frequently changes the diagnosis, which means it occasionally removes the need to buy anything at all. Families who skip it buy a term of support for the wrong problem.

process.title: Ask for the narrowest plan that would work
process.description: Send the marked paper and ask what the smallest intervention is. A good answer names a component, a session count and a stopping condition. An answer that starts with a monthly package has not looked at the evidence, and a family is entitled to push back on it before paying anything.

process.title: Free trial, which produces a priced plan
process.description: A full session with the tutor who would teach the course, no card required. The output should be a named weakness, an hour estimate and therefore a cost you can compare against the bands on this page. You keep the diagnosis whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Settle the extras in writing
process.description: Cancellation window, whether late cancellations are billed, whether the figure includes value added tax, and whether marking of between-session work is inside the hour or charged on top. These three details move the real cost of an IGCSE plan by a meaningful fraction and nobody volunteers them.

process.title: Review and stop
process.description: Check the plan against the weakness it was bought to fix at the agreed session count. Closed means stop or move to the next named component. Not closed means change the approach or the tutor, not add hours. Plans without a review point renew by default, which is how a budget doubles without a decision.

whyPoints.title: Cheapest option named first
whyPoints.description: This page opens with the free steps and the short block rather than the premium plan, because for most IGCSE problems presented to us the narrow intervention is the correct one and the market has no commercial reason to say so.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here come from named providers and from Bestimate's 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. Three of the six pages currently ranking for these queries publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars.
