whyPoints.description: We quote per plan after a free trial because the right figure depends on the subject's scarcity and the plan's length. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a different market from Mathematics 0580, and a single published rate would be either misleading or too high.

whyPoints.title: The extras raised before you ask
whyPoints.description: Cancellation policy, tax inclusion and whether marking is inside the hour change the real cost materially. We put them in the process rather than in the small print, because they are where family budgets actually break.

whyPoints.title: Online, stated up front
whyPoints.description: One-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. On the in-home axis we are not an option, and from a southern Al Ain address that is also the band where a premium buys the least.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: No accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson, no self-generated ratings, no guaranteed grades and no figure without a source and a date.

faqs.question: What is the smallest amount an Al Maqam family can usefully spend on IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Confirming the board, syllabus code and tier with the school and getting a marked paper, which is free and sometimes changes the diagnosis completely. After that, the cheapest paid option that reliably works is a block of four to six sessions on one named component with a qualified subject tutor, which at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour is a one-off figure of roughly AED 600 to AED 1,800. It cannot rebuild a topic nobody taught, but for a technique failure it does most of the available work.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor in Al Maqam cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published bands in this market, read in October 2026: AED 33 to AED 52 and AED 45 to AED 65 at the budget end, AED 150 for IGCSE from one specialist agency, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for subject specialists, and AED 650 for one premium named tutor. Rates are set by provider type rather than by Al Ain district, so searching a different neighbourhood will not lower them. What does differ locally is supply in the scarce subjects.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium worth paying from a southern Al Ain address?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and for a specific reason. The premium of roughly AED 30 to AED 200 an hour over the online band pays for a car and about forty unbilled minutes on a southern round trip. That is a fair price for travel. The problem is what it buys alongside: a tutor who can reach Al Maqam on a weekday evening is often not a teacher of the subject at issue, because Al Ain's smaller private-school set makes specialists scarce citywide. Paying more for a worse match is the pattern to avoid.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE year actually cost if we plan it properly?
faqs.answer: Less than a flat monthly figure sustained for two years, and staged rather than level. The need is light in early Year 10, concentrated in the spring tier decision, heavier in Year 11's first term and after mocks, heaviest in the final ten weeks and lighter again in the last fortnight. Staged that way at mid-market rates, one subject across both years comes in well below AED 1,000 a month maintained for twenty-four months, and achieves more because the hours sit where they do work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge extra for a tutor to visit our home in Al Maqam?
faqs.answer: We do not offer it at any price. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Maqam students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We say so before any booking because the phrase families search is 'home tutor' and the format should not be a surprise. If physical presence is a requirement, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE permit category, the syllabus taught and the cancellation policy.

faqs.question: Are the AED 50 an hour tutors a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not for the right job. Published budget bands start around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour and buy supervised practice: someone keeping a student at the desk, checking homework is done and answering straightforward questions. For a Year 10 student who understands the material but does not work consistently, that is precisely the problem. It is a false economy when used for syllabus-level teaching, because the hour will be pleasant and the Paper 4 technique will not change. Match the band to the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What extras should we ask about before booking an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Three, and none of them is usually volunteered. The cancellation window and whether late cancellations are billed, because two or three billed cancellations across a term costs as much as a short block. Whether the quoted figure includes value added tax, in writing. And whether marking of work set between sessions is inside the hour or charged on top, because for an IGCSE plan that detail moves the real cost by a meaningful fraction. Get all three answered before the first session, not during the third month.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE class better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: On price per hour, clearly. On price per grade, only when every student in the group has the same gap. A group of four revising a whole syllabus at similar standard works well. The same group is poor value for a student secure everywhere except extended-response questions, because most of the hour addresses someone else. There is also an unpriced cost: a student who is behind will not admit confusion in front of peers. If a group is what the budget allows, choose one organised by topic rather than by subject.

faqs.question: Why does Additional Mathematics 0606 cost more in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Because few schools here offer it, so few local teachers have taken a cohort through it. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's and the teaching population scales with it, which pushes scarce-subject rates to the top of their band and lengthens the wait. A Mathematics 0580 specialist is cheaper and is not a substitute, since 0606 introduces calculus and series outside the 0580 specification entirely. This is one of the few cases where paying more is the correct decision rather than an avoidable one.

faqs.question: Do we have to pay anything for a tutor's UAE permit?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be suspicious of anyone who suggests otherwise. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Working without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published anywhere.

faqs.question: How does tutoring spend compare with UAE school fees?
faqs.answer: It is a small marginal cost if staged and a significant one if open-ended. For scale, Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no fee increase for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Those figures are Dubai's, and Al Maqam sits under ADEK rather than KHDA. Against an annual fee, a staged plan of AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month for part of a year is modest; the same figure maintained for two years is not.

faqs.question: Should we buy more sessions in the final fortnight before the papers?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and this is where anxiety becomes expensive. By then the evidence from marked work usually points the other way: no new content, the student marking their own practice against mark schemes, earlier nights. The final fortnight should be quieter than the eight weeks before it. If a provider proposes extra sessions in the last week, ask which paper the evidence came from. Two or three sessions in that window, used to arbitrate the student's own marking, is the sensible ceiling.

faqs.question: We can only afford one subject. Which one?
faqs.answer: The one where a marked paper shows a specific, diagnosable loss, and ideally one of the five needed for equivalency rather than a sixth or seventh entry. On the British track, the Ministry of Education asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. So five comfortable passes are worth more than two outstanding ones and three marginal ones. Within that, pick the subject where a narrow technique failure is costing the most marks, not the one with the lowest grade.

faqs.question: How do we stop the monthly cost from running on indefinitely?
faqs.answer: Write the stopping condition down before the first paid session. It should name a component, a weakness and a session count, with a review at the end of it. If the weakness has closed, stop or move to the next named one. If it has not, change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours. Plans without a review point renew by default, which is how a tutoring budget doubles with nobody deciding to spend more. A provider who will not agree one is telling you something useful.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.closingHeading: Buy the narrowest thing that would fix it
al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-maqam.closingBody: The cheapest route to a better IGCSE grade in Al Maqam starts with two free steps: confirm the board, syllabus code and tier with the school, and get hold of a marked paper. Most of what families buy after that is wider than the problem. A block of four to six sessions on one named component, at the published AED 150 to AED 300 band, is a one-off figure rather than a monthly commitment and does most of the available work on a technique failure. Send us the marked paper and we will tell you what the smallest useful plan looks like, with the cost attached. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The dates that decide the grade are not the exam dates
paragraphs: Families plan IGCSE around the papers and then discover that the decisions were taken earlier. Entries are confirmed months before anyone sits anything. The Core or Extended tier is settled in Year 10 and determines the grade ceiling. The resit question has to be answered before results arrive, not after. None of those dates is published where a parent would look, and all of them matter more to an outcome than the week of the exam itself.

Al Mutaredh sits beside Al Ain's central school cluster, so families here have short school runs and genuinely usable weekday afternoons. That removes the scheduling excuse and leaves only the planning problem, which is why this page is a calendar rather than a timetable. With two or three real sessions a week available, the question is not whether tuition fits but when in the two-year cycle it should happen.

One factual correction belongs at the top because acting on it would make a family miss an entry. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any page quoting a UAE family a February/March deadline has published another country's calendar.

The schools serving Al Mutaredh use both of the main boards, and the two keep different calendars with different structures. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended and runs separate practical components; Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher and examines practical skills inside the written papers. Confirming which board and which code applies is the first and cheapest step in any plan.

Al Mutaredh is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's own listing is where to confirm a school's licensed curriculum, and it is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project.

IB Gram teaches Al Mutaredh students one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a central family the practical benefit of online delivery is not logistics but choice: the shortlist is every available teacher of that specification, rather than those who can reach the neighbourhood on a weekday.

Everything that follows is usable whoever you hire. The counting-back table, the tier evidence table and the resit weighing table all apply to a tutor an Al Mutaredh family finds locally, and the four facts to collect from the exams officer cost nothing but one email. The teaching is what we sell; the calendar is simply what the qualification imposes.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mutaredh.programmesIntro: Two boards and one progression route, each with its own calendar logic. The differences below change when a plan has to act rather than merely what it contains.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes, with many subjects tiered into Core and Extended and a grade ceiling applying to Core. Sciences carry a separate practical component, either a laboratory test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, chosen by the school. The qualification runs in a June series and a November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. Get your school's zone from the exams officer in writing in the first term of Year 11 and keep the reply, then work from that version of the timetable only.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and 4EA1. Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher; the international sciences are untiered and examine practical skills inside the written papers. Modular availability in some subjects changes when a result can be banked and therefore when a resit becomes a sensible option rather than a gamble.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so plan from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: The tier and grade a student finishes with decides which AS subjects stay open, and Core tier generally closes AS Mathematics and the separate sciences. Because the tier is chosen in Year 10 and its consequence appears in Year 12, this is the longest-dated decision in the British curriculum and the one most often made by default.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university entry the Ministry of Education equivalency rule on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five. That shapes resit decisions: securing a fifth comfortable pass can matter more than improving an existing good one.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mutaredh.subjectsIntro: Each subject has a point in the two years at which support does most good, set by when its hardest content arrives and how its practical or coursework element falls. These are the subjects Al Mutaredh families request.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision subject. Support in the autumn and spring of Year 10 can change which tier a student is entered for, which is worth more than anything bought in Year 11. After entry, the work is method-line discipline and timed practice.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger cohorts and taught by few Al Ain schools, so it needs an early booking as well as early teaching. Calculus and series require sustained attention, which makes this a subject to start in Year 10 rather than rescue in Year 11.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves land late in the course, while the data-handling skills that carry easy marks can be taught at any point. Confirm early which practical route applies, because revising for the wrong structure wastes a third of the preparation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic should be fixed in Year 10, because every later topic sits on it. Organic chemistry and qualitative analysis arrive in Year 11, which is when a student who skipped the arithmetic discovers the problem.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content heavy, so consolidation belongs across Year 10 and the summer. Command-term work pays in any month and transfers across the paper, which makes it the obvious purchase for a family starting late.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: The route decision between separate and combined sciences is a Year 9 conversation with Year 12 consequences. Once set, confirm the code before booking anyone, because the content map differs from the separate sciences.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 first language, 0510/0511 second language; Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: Check the specification before anything else, because first and second language reward different things. Directed-writing and reading-response technique improve steadily rather than suddenly, so early regular work beats a late block.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Definitions and diagram accuracy can be built in Year 10; applied data response needs Year 11 context. The usual failure of describing rather than analysing is structural and transfers, so it is worth correcting as soon as it appears.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables improve with regular practice over time rather than with intensity. Both subjects are scarce in Al Ain, so an early booking matters as much as an early start to the teaching.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source skills and essay structure can be taught at almost any point and improve quickly, which makes these the best subjects to add late if a family has left planning until Year 11. Case-study recall needs the term's own material.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines sit months before the papers
paragraphs: This is the part of the calendar nobody publishes and the part that occasionally costs a family a whole series. Entries are made by the centre, confirmed well ahead of the papers, and once the window closes the tier and the subject set are fixed for that series. A plan that assumes decisions can be made in the spring of Year 11 has already missed several of them.

The table works backwards from a series to the decisions that precede it. The column worth reading twice is who sets the date, because almost none of it is the board acting directly on the family: the school's exams officer holds the entry window, the subject teachers hold the tier recommendation, and the board publishes the timetable. A parent who knows which door to knock on gets answers quickly.

The Cambridge zoning point belongs here too, because it is an administrative detail with an absolute consequence. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask for the zone in writing and keep the reply.

The practical instruction for an Al Mutaredh family is to collect four things in the first term of Year 11: the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier for each tiered subject, the centre's entry deadline, and the Cambridge zone. That takes one email and removes the entire class of calendar failures described on this page.

sections.heading: The tier decision has a date, and it is earlier than you think
paragraphs: Cambridge Core tier carries a grade ceiling, which means a student entered for Core cannot reach the grades that AS Mathematics and the separate sciences expect. Pearson Mathematics A behaves similarly across Foundation and Higher. The decision is made in Year 10 and its consequence surfaces in Year 12, which makes it the longest-dated and least discussed choice in the British curriculum.

The useful evidence is not the mock grade but the mock script. Look at which questions were attempted rather than which were correct. A student attempting most Extended questions and making method errors has a technique problem and can usually be made secure with a term of work. A student leaving half the paper blank has a content problem, which takes longer and may make Core the right choice rather than the disappointing one.

The timing that works is to collect three marked papers across the autumn and spring of Year 10 and have the conversation with the school before the spring ends. Tuition in this window is unusually valuable because it can change the tier a student is capable of sitting, which no amount of Year 11 support can do. After entry, the tier is a fact.

Both errors are common and they run in opposite directions. Students are moved to Core on a single bad October mock, and students are kept on Extended on the reasonable logic that it preserves options, right up until a paper they cannot access. Neither is a decision about the child; both are decisions made on insufficient evidence at an inconvenient moment.

sections.heading: The resit decision, made before results arrive
paragraphs: Resits feel like an after-the-fact decision and are not. Entry windows for the next series close well ahead of the papers, and for a November entry that means acting close to when summer results land. A family that waits to think about it has often lost the November option and is looking at the following June instead.

The question to answer first is what the resit is for. Improving a good grade to a better one rarely changes anything, because the Ministry of Education equivalency route on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Securing a fifth comfortable pass can matter a great deal; polishing a sixth usually does not.

The second question is whether the evidence supports improvement. A student who lost marks on timing and phrasing can realistically gain a grade with a focused block, because the fix is short and the content is already there. A student who left a third of the paper blank is being asked to learn in one term what they did not learn in two, and the honest answer is sometimes no.

The documented Pearson pattern gives a sense of the lag involved. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November entry historically produces a January result, which matters if a sixth-form or university deadline sits between.

sections.heading: Mocks, Checkpoint and the diagnostic calendar
paragraphs: A two-year plan needs diagnostic points, and the school supplies more of them than families use. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which for a Year 9 student is a genuine external read on where they stand before any IGCSE decision is taken. Most parents see the result and file it.

The mock window in the winter of Year 11 is the big one, and its value is in the scripts rather than the grades. The fortnight afterwards is the highest-return tutoring purchase in the two years, because it is the only point at which the whole plan can be redirected on evidence. Sort every lost mark into blanks, method errors, timing failures and mark-scheme phrasing; each has a different fix and a different duration.

What families do instead is react to the number. A grade of 5 produces relief or panic, neither of which contains information, and the same 5 can come from a student who left a third of the paper blank or one who attempted everything and lost marks on phrasing. Those two need entirely different plans and entirely different amounts of money spent on them.

Book the post-mock session before the mocks happen, and book it long. A ninety-minute session with the scripts on the table is worth more than four shorter sessions afterwards spent guessing, and because every family at the school wants that same fortnight, the slot has to be reserved rather than requested.

sections.heading: Ramadan, breaks and the UAE academic year
paragraphs: A revision calendar built on a generic school year will be wrong in the UAE, and the differences are worth planning for rather than absorbing. Ramadan falls at a different point in the academic year each time, so in some years it sits inside the heaviest revision block for a Year 11 student and in others it does not touch it.

The adjustment is to move sessions rather than to pause them. Shortened school days can free afternoon capacity, and for a central Al Mutaredh family with a short school run that means a genuinely usable earlier slot. Post-iftar sessions suit other households. What fails is treating the month as ordinary and then losing four consecutive sessions to fatigue and cancellation; agree the shape a fortnight ahead.

The mid-year break and the summer are the two places where content repair belongs. Consecutive days allow a topic to be rebuilt rather than revisited, which is a different and better thing than the same hours spread through a term. For a Year 10 student the summer before Year 11 is the most valuable block available, because it precedes the year in which the tier is already fixed.

The third point is collisions. Entry windows and internal deadlines do not always respect school breaks, so a deadline falling immediately after a holiday means a student loses either the break or the marks. Put the entry window, the internal deadlines and the school breaks on one calendar in September and look for overlaps while fixing them is still free.

sections.heading: Starting late in Year 11, and what still works
paragraphs: Plenty of families reach this page in the spring of Year 11, and the honest answer is that late help aimed narrowly is not wasted money, while late help aimed broadly mostly is. Ten weeks out, an hour can fix command-term use, mark-scheme phrasing, calculation drills, question selection and timing, and those routinely carry a grade. It cannot rebuild a topic that was never taught.

So the right late purchase is a technique block on named components, working from a marked paper, rather than a general course through the syllabus. The diagnostic matters more when time is short, not less: with eight sessions available, spending two of them discovering the problem is sensible and spending all eight on the wrong thing is the alternative.

Some subjects respond to late help better than others. Geography, History, Economics and Business improve quickly because the marks sit in structure rather than in content volume. Physics data-handling, chemistry calculations and command-term discipline in Biology are all short, high-yield fixes. Additional Mathematics and organic chemistry are not; those need time nobody has in April.

The one thing to avoid late is adding hours in the final fortnight. The instinct is natural and the evidence from marked work usually points the other way: no new content, the student marking their own practice against mark schemes, earlier nights. If a provider proposes extra sessions in the last week, ask which script the evidence came from.

One more thing worth doing late, and it is free. Read the mark scheme for one past paper with your child, question by question, and ask them to say what each mark is actually for. Most students have never done this, and it reliably changes how they answer within a single sitting.

sections.heading: ADEK, permits and verification
paragraphs: Al Mutaredh is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's own listing is the authority on what a school is licensed to deliver and how it has been inspected, which is also the right first check for a family new to the city.

Private tutoring runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service with a stated two-working-day completion.

One restriction matters particularly in a central district where school staff and families live close together. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat such an offer as a reason to decline rather than a credential.

Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule, so any quoted figure is unverified. For completeness, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson, and a tuition centre with premises in Dubai would need a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit.

sections.heading: Practical papers, submitted work and the boundary
paragraphs: Deadline pressure is when the academic-honesty boundary gets tested, which is why it belongs on a calendar page. IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the Diploma, but the practical component and any school-supervised work still have a line, and work submitted as the student's own must be the student's own.

Inside the line, and worth buying: teaching a technique, explaining why a mark scheme rewards one phrasing over another, marking the student's own practice work, drilling calculation types and rehearsing oral components. For practicals that includes apparatus conventions, uncertainty treatment, reading results tables and choosing a sensible graph scale, all examinable skills that need no laboratory.

Outside the line: producing data, writing up an investigation, supplying answers for submitted work or preparing material a student presents as their own. We also will not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; the correct route is to cite the official page and link to it.

The question that settles which kind of provider you are speaking to is a scenario rather than an accusation. Ask what they would do if a student brought submitted work the night before it was due. An answer about reading and marking it against criteria is right. An answer that involves fixing it tells you what else is for sale, and the research behind this page found completed assessments offered to UAE students at around AED 3,750.

A related point about materials, because it arrives under time pressure. A provider advertising a downloadable library of past papers and mark schemes has already answered a question about how it treats board copyright, and by extension how carefully it will treat your child's submitted work.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entry deadlines fall for a school in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, and the centre rather than the family holds the window. The practical approach is to ask the exams officer in the first term of Year 11 for the entry deadline, the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier for each tiered subject, and the school's Cambridge administrative zone. Once the window closes, the tier and the subject set are fixed for that series. A plan that assumes these decisions can still be made in the spring of Year 11 has already missed several of them.

faqs.question: Why does the Core or Extended decision need making in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Because Core carries a grade ceiling that closes AS Mathematics and the separate sciences later, and because entry fixes it. The decision should rest on three marked papers collected across Year 10, looking at which Extended questions were attempted rather than which were correct. A student attempting most questions with method errors has a technique problem fixable in a term. A student leaving half the paper blank has a content problem, and Core may genuinely be the right choice rather than the disappointing one.

faqs.question: Do UAE students sit the Cambridge February/March series?
faqs.answer: No. The February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. If a tutoring page quotes a UAE family a February/March entry deadline, it has published another country's calendar and acting on it would mean missing an entry. Always confirm against the board's own live timetable and your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to Al Mutaredh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Mutaredh students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We state this before any booking because the phrase families search is 'home tutor' and the format should not be a surprise. For a central family with short school runs, the benefit of online delivery is choice of specialist rather than convenience, since the shortlist becomes national rather than drivable.

faqs.question: At what point does the November resit option close for an Al Ain candidate?
faqs.answer: Before summer results arrive, because the entry window for the next series closes well ahead of the papers. Ask the exams officer for the date in advance. Then answer what the resit is actually for: securing a fifth comfortable pass matters for Ministry of Education equivalency, which asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, while improving a sixth good grade usually changes nothing. The evidence in the script decides whether improvement is realistic.

faqs.question: How long after a November entry do Pearson results arrive?
faqs.answer: Historically, January. The documented pattern is that the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That lag matters if a sixth-form or university deadline falls between the paper and the result. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so confirm against the live official timetable before planning.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone and why should I ask for it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. So a timetable found by searching online may not be your child's. Ask the exams officer for the zone in writing in the first term of Year 11, keep the reply, and work only from that version.

faqs.question: We are in the spring of Year 11. What is still worth buying?
faqs.answer: A technique block on named components, built from a marked paper, rather than a general course. Ten weeks out, an hour can still fix command-term use, mark-scheme phrasing, calculation drills, question selection and timing, and those routinely carry a grade. It cannot rebuild a topic nobody taught. Keep the diagnostic even though time is short: with eight sessions available, spending two to find the real problem is sensible, and the alternative is spending all eight on the wrong thing.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects improve fastest with late help?
faqs.answer: Geography, History, Economics and Business, because the marks sit in answer structure and source technique rather than in content volume, and structure can be taught quickly. Physics data-handling, chemistry calculation drills and command-term discipline in Biology are also short, high-yield fixes. The subjects that do not respond well to late help are Additional Mathematics 0606, organic chemistry and second languages, all of which need time that is not available in the spring of Year 11.

faqs.question: How do we use the Lower Secondary Checkpoint results?
faqs.answer: As an external read before any IGCSE decision is taken. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and for a Year 9 student the result is a genuine independent measure of where they stand rather than a school's internal judgement. Most parents see it and file it. Used properly, it is the earliest reliable signal about whether the Extended tier is realistic, and it gives a full year of runway to act on the answer.

faqs.question: How should an Al Ain family plan around Ramadan in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Check where it falls against the plan before the term starts, because it moves each year and in some years it sits inside the heaviest revision block. Then move sessions rather than pausing them. Shortened school days can free a genuinely usable afternoon slot, which for a central Al Mutaredh family with a short run is a real gain, and post-iftar sessions suit other households. Agree the month's shape a fortnight ahead. What fails is treating it as ordinary and losing four consecutive sessions to fatigue.

faqs.question: What exactly happens in the post-mock session?
faqs.answer: Every lost mark gets sorted into one of four kinds: blank questions, method errors, timing failures and mark-scheme phrasing. Blanks mean content was never learnt and need a longer block or a holiday. Method errors and phrasing mean technique and need a handful of hours. Timing failures need split-paper practice with a clock. That sorting is the only point in the two years where the whole plan can be redirected on evidence, which is why it should be booked long and booked before the mocks happen.

faqs.question: Is a school report enough to decide whether to hire a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the commonest planning error on both boards. A report grade tells you where a student stands; a marked script tells you why, and only the second supports a decision. Two students with the same grade of 5 can need entirely different plans, different tutors and different amounts of money, depending on whether marks were lost to blank questions or to phrasing. Ask the school for marked papers rather than a summary, and send those with any tutoring enquiry.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's Al Ain school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Not for payment. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the same thing. Teachers who tutor outside school hours must hold the permit, which is free and valid two years. In a central district where staff and families live close together this comes up often; treat it as a reason to decline rather than a credential, and check ADEK's own policy wording.

intro.heading: Four comparisons, and which one decides anything
paragraphs: Al Muwaiji lies in the west of Al Ain, near the old fort and a short drive from Al Jimi, Al Khabisi and Hili. It is a city of short journeys, settled neighbourhoods and a compact school market, and families here compare carefully before they buy anything. The problem is that most of the comparisons on offer are between things that turn out to be identical.

Four get made. District against district: is there somebody better in Al Jimi than in Al Muwaiji? School against school: would my child be better entered at the school down the road? Board against board: does it matter that one school enters Cambridge and another Pearson Edexcel? And format against format: local arrangement, tuition centre, or something online. Only two of those four comparisons change an outcome, and the two that matter are not the two families spend most time on.

District against district changes nothing at all. Al Ain journeys are short, the tutor pool for any given specification is thin everywhere in the city, and the thing a student needs is somebody who knows their paper. A tutor two streets away who has never marked the specification is worse than a specialist on a screen, and in a city this size the specialist is almost never two streets away.

School against school is a real comparison, but not on the axes parents usually use. It is not about reputation; it is about which board each school enters, which tier it tends to enter students for, and which subjects it actually runs in a given year. Those three facts are obtainable by asking, and they affect a child's grade ceiling far more than any difference in atmosphere.

Board against board matters once your child is already entered, because practice material from the wrong board builds the wrong instincts. And format against format matters on exactly one axis: whether the format can look at your child's own marked script. That is the comparison this page is built around, because it is the one that converts spending into marks.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because a family comparing options deserves to know what is and is not on offer before they read another two thousand words.

One more reason to take the comparison seriously rather than drifting into the nearest option. Al Ain is a city where recommendations travel fast and far: a tutor who helped one family in one subject gets passed around a dozen households within a term, regardless of whether the subject, board or tier matches. That word-of-mouth network is genuinely valuable and it is also the main reason students here end up with a tutor who is good at something other than the thing they need. The checks later on this page exist to make a recommendation testable rather than to replace it.

programmes.description: Content is delivered and the internal examination at the end of the year usually fixes the tier recommendation. al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-muwaiji.subjectsIntro: Each entry notes what differs between the two main boards for that subject, because that is the comparison a family can actually act on once the entry is made.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended with a non-calculator paper at each tier under the current syllabus; Pearson tiers into Foundation and Higher and permits a calculator in both papers. Same mathematics, different examination habits, and the wrong board's past papers drill the wrong ones.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates may sit a practical-skills paper requiring a written method precise enough for a stranger to repeat; Pearson assesses practical understanding differently. That single difference changes what a tutor should spend sessions on more than any content difference does.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic pathways decide the upper grades on both. The recurring loss is identical across boards: a correct calculation written without units or significant figures, costing marks the chemistry had already earned.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heaviest content load, and the subject where command terms matter most on either board. An explain question answered with a description earns nothing, and that is a training problem rather than a revision problem.

subjects.name: English Language

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Muwaiji means in a compact city
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Muwaiji, as the phrase is used locally, means one-to-one teaching for one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram provides that over live video to Al Ain families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we run only in India. In a city where a cross-town drive takes twenty minutes, the convenience argument for visiting is weaker than it is on the coast, and the supply argument for going online is stronger.

Here is why supply dominates in Al Ain. The city's IGCSE cohort is modest and spread across a handful of schools, so the number of adults locally who have marked Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4PH1 against the published scheme is small. A family restricting its search to people within driving distance is choosing from that small number, at the one hour everybody wants, which is how a reasonable instinct produces an unreasonable shortlist.

The comparison that solves it is simple to state and slightly uncomfortable to accept: a specialist who has marked the paper, on a screen, beats a competent generalist in the next street. Not because presence has no value — for a younger child it clearly does — but because IGCSE grades are decided inside written papers, and finding where the marks went requires somebody who knows what the examiner rewards.

This page therefore spends its time on the comparisons that change something. How to compare two Al Ain schools properly. What genuinely differs between this city and Abu Dhabi. Five checks that sort a specialist from a generalist in five minutes. And what the two main boards do differently once your child is already entered for one of them.

sections.heading: Al Muwaiji against Al Jimi: four variables, one that counts
paragraphs: Families genuinely ask this, usually when a neighbour in the next district recommends somebody. It is worth answering with the variables laid out rather than dismissing, because the answer turns out to be instructive about the whole market.

Four things could in principle differ between two Al Ain districts: journey time to school, which schools are realistically accessible, the availability of a local specialist, and the hour at which a session can start. The first two differ slightly and in ways that mostly cancel out. The third does not differ at all, because the local pool for any given specification is thin across the entire city rather than concentrated anywhere. The fourth differs by about fifteen minutes.

So the honest answer is that the district comparison resolves to a quarter of an hour of session timing, and that whichever district a family lives in, the same conclusion follows: choose by specification, not by location. A recommendation from a neighbour is worth having, but it should be tested with the five checks later on this page rather than accepted because the person is nearby.

The table below runs the comparison across the districts an Al Muwaiji family actually weighs. The final column is the point: the availability answer is identical everywhere, which is what makes the whole exercise moot.

It is also worth noticing what the comparison does to a family's decision-making. Time spent weighing two districts is time not spent on the school and specification questions that genuinely move a grade, and the district question is the more comfortable one to think about because it has a simple answer. sections.heading: How to compare two Al Ain schools properly
paragraphs: This is the comparison worth real effort, and families usually run it on the wrong criteria. Atmosphere, facilities and word of mouth dominate the conversation; board, tier policy and subject viability decide the grade. All three of the latter are obtainable by asking, and schools answer them readily when asked specifically.

Ask each school which board it enters for each subject, and get the syllabus codes. Ask how the tier decision is made, what evidence it rests on, and whether it is revisited after the autumn term of Year 11. Ask which subjects were actually taught last year as against listed, because small cohorts close options. Ask what internal assessment calendar the school runs and when study leave starts. And ask what happens if a student wants a subject the school does not enter, since a private candidate route is sometimes possible and sometimes not.

Those five questions produce a comparison a family can act on. They also produce something more valuable: a sense of how the school handles a specific, slightly awkward enquiry from a parent, which predicts how it will handle the next two years rather better than a tour does.

The table below is the version to take to a meeting. Note that none of it requires judging teaching quality, which parents cannot reliably assess from outside and which inspection reports cover at department level anyway.

There is a sixth question worth adding if your child is in Year 10 or 11 already: what happens to a student who transfers in mid-course. Schools vary in how much mapping they do against the receiving specification, and a transfer between boards partway through a two-year course creates coverage gaps that nobody owns unless somebody asks. The answer to that question tells you whether the school is used to handling transfers or merely willing to accept them.

sections.heading: Al Ain against Abu Dhabi city: what genuinely differs
paragraphs: Families moving within the emirate, or weighing a longer commute, ask this constantly. Three things differ and two do not, and knowing which is which saves a lot of wasted deliberation.

What differs: the size of the school market, and therefore the number of Higher Level and specialist options available locally. The length of journeys, which in Al Ain are short enough to make early sessions genuinely possible. And the local price of group and informal tutoring, which is lower here because it is priced against a smaller local economy.

What does not differ: the regulator, since Al Ain sits within the emirate of Abu Dhabi and private schools in both are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge; and the specialist one-to-one market, which is priced Gulf-wide once lessons move online. A qualified online subject tutor publishes in this market from around AED 150 to 300 an hour whether the student is in Al Muwaiji or on Abu Dhabi island.

There is a fourth item that cuts both ways. Al Ain's compactness means a family can change school across the city without a punishing commute, which makes the school comparison more actionable here than almost anywhere else in the country. On the coast, a better school forty minutes away is often not a real option. Here it usually is.

A fifth factor deserves mention because families raise it: the perception that a smaller city means weaker teaching. Inspection reports do not support a blanket version of that, and in any case the relevant unit is the department rather than the school. The subject-level commentary inside an ADEK report is the place to look, and it is directly comparable between Al Ain and the city because the framework is the same.

sections.heading: Five checks that sort a tutor in five minutes
paragraphs: Qualifications are a weak signal. A mathematics degree says nothing about whether somebody has marked Cambridge 0580 Extended against the published scheme. What does signal competence is specificity, and specificity can be tested by any parent in a short conversation without knowing the subject.

Ask which syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, and see whether they ask you for it or guess. Ask how many papers the subject has and what each is worth. Ask which series a UAE candidate sits, and listen for June and November rather than a vague answer; Cambridge offers its February and March sitting to India only, so a tutor who quotes those dates at an Al Ain family is working from the wrong country's calendar. Ask where students most often lose marks in that subject, and look for a specific, repeatable answer rather than a general one. And ask what they will refuse to do with coursework.

The answers sort people quickly and fairly. A specialist answers the first four without hesitation and the fifth with a clear boundary. A generalist talks about building confidence, covering the basics and making the subject enjoyable. Neither is dishonest; they are different products, and a family comparing them should know which they are buying before the money moves.

One more check, for an independent tutor rather than a platform: ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no reasonable excuse not to, and a conspicuously low rate sometimes means the question has never been asked.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: Once a child is entered, the board comparison stops being a choice and becomes a practice question. The two specifications assess overlapping content in different ways, and using the wrong board's material is the most common silent waste of a revision term. It feels productive throughout, and the error only becomes visible when the real paper looks unfamiliar.

The differences worth knowing are structural rather than topical. Cambridge and Pearson tier differently and label grades differently. Under the current Cambridge mathematics syllabus a non-calculator paper sits at each tier, while Pearson's International GCSE mathematics permits a calculator throughout, which changes what a student needs to drill. In the sciences, the way practical understanding is assessed differs, and for Cambridge candidates sitting a practical-skills paper the marked skill is writing a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat.

Computer Science deserves a specific warning. Pseudocode conventions are specification-dependent, so cross-board practice here is actively misleading rather than merely inefficient. A student who learns one board's conventions and sits the other's paper loses marks for presentation that they never knew were at stake.

The practical rule is short. Get the code in writing, use only that board's published past material, and if a tutor supplies practice from elsewhere, ask why. In a city where tutors often teach students from several schools at once, cross-board contamination is a real and under-noticed risk.

There is one more difference families should know about, which concerns resits. Both boards run a November series available to UAE candidates, but the practicalities of entering for one — whether the school enters November at all, and what it charges — vary by centre rather than by board. That is a question for the examinations officer, and it is worth asking in the autumn rather than in August, because it changes whether a June entry can sensibly be treated as a baseline.

sections.heading: What no comparison can change
paragraphs: Some things are fixed whichever district, school, board or format a family chooses, and they are worth stating because several pages competing for this search imply otherwise.

The regulator is fixed. Al Ain sits within the emirate of Abu Dhabi and private schools here are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation and publishes inspection outcomes. Elsewhere the map differs: KHDA in Dubai, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval from any of them, and a page claiming otherwise is making the most dangerous claim available in this market.

The permit position is fixed. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

And the line on coursework is fixed. A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria, questions the reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write, complete or rewrite the work. No comparison of providers changes that boundary, and a provider offering to cross it is not a cheaper option, it is a risk transferred onto the student.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in Al Jimi any better than one in Al Muwaiji?
faqs.answer: No, and the comparison resolves to about fifteen minutes of session timing. Al Ain journeys are short, the two districts share much of the same school catchment, and the local supply of specialists in any given specification is thin across the whole city rather than concentrated anywhere in it. What changes an outcome is whether the tutor has marked your child's paper against the published scheme. Test a neighbour's recommendation on that basis rather than on proximity.

faqs.question: How should we compare two Al Ain schools for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: On mechanics, not atmosphere. Ask each school which board and syllabus code it enters per subject, how the tier decision is made and whether it is revisited in Year 11, which subjects actually ran last year as against being listed, when the internal assessment calendar and study leave fall, and what happens if you want a subject the school does not enter. Those five answers change a grade ceiling. A tour does not, and small cohorts in this city close options that prospectuses still advertise.

faqs.question: Does it matter that one Al Ain school enters Cambridge and another Pearson?
faqs.answer: It matters once your child is entered, because the practice material has to match. The boards tier differently, label grades differently, and differ on calculator rules; under the current Cambridge mathematics syllabus a non-calculator paper sits at each tier while Pearson permits a calculator in both papers. In Computer Science the pseudocode conventions differ, making cross-board practice actively misleading. Before choosing a school the difference is minor; after entry it decides which past papers are worth your child's evenings.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a house in Al Muwaiji?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Al Ain families is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through paper questions. In this city the supply argument matters more than the convenience one: the number of people locally who have marked a given specification is small, and online delivery replaces that small pool with everyone who teaches it.

faqs.question: What five questions should I ask a tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and will you ask me or guess? How many papers does the subject have and what is each worth? Which series does a UAE candidate sit? Where do students most often lose marks in this subject, specifically? And what will you refuse to do with coursework? A specialist answers the first four without hesitation and the fifth with a clear boundary. A generalist talks about confidence and the basics, which is a different product at a different price.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Al Ain a fair alternative to one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For one purpose, yes. A class retells a specification with structure at the lowest cost per hour available, which suits a student who has fallen behind across a whole subject. What it cannot do is examine your child's own marked script, so it cannot find an error pattern. If the marked paper shows two marks a question going missing on units and method, no number of classes will touch it. Compare the formats on diagnosis rather than on price per hour.

faqs.question: Are specialist tutoring rates lower in Al Ain than on the coast?
faqs.answer: No. Group classes and informal local arrangements are generally cheaper here because they are priced against a smaller local economy, but specialist one-to-one rates are set by a Gulf-wide online market. Published qualified online rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialist IB and IGCSE rates from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, wherever the student lives. What does differ locally is waiting time for a visiting specialist, which can cost weeks rather than dirhams.

faqs.question: Which regulator inspects schools in Al Muwaiji?
faqs.answer: Al Ain sits within the emirate of Abu Dhabi, so private schools here are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation and publishes inspection outcomes. The framework is the same one applied in Abu Dhabi city, so inspection reports are directly comparable between the two. Elsewhere in the country it differs: KHDA in Dubai, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

faqs.question: Can we compare our way out of a tier that caps my child's grade?
faqs.answer: Only before entries are submitted, and only with marked evidence. The tier decision belongs to the school and is made to a board deadline months ahead of the papers. Two timed sections and a diagnostic session produce the evidence a school needs in order to reconsider, and schools in this emirate are generally reasonable where it exists. After the deadline the question is closed, and the honest plan is to use the available ceiling fully, with the November series considered where it helps.

faqs.question: Is it worth moving school across Al Ain for a better IGCSE offer?
faqs.answer: More often than on the coast, because the city is compact enough that a cross-town move does not impose a punishing commute. The comparison is worth making on the five mechanical questions — board, tier policy, subjects actually running, assessment calendar, private-candidate flexibility — rather than on reputation. Year 9 is the stage at which the move is genuinely executable; by Year 11 the board and tier are fixed and a move usually costs more continuity than it gains.

faqs.question: How do we avoid a tutor using the wrong board's past papers?
faqs.answer: Get the syllabus code in writing from the examinations officer and give it to the tutor at the first contact, then check the header on any material that comes back. In a city where tutors often teach students from several schools in the same week, cross-board contamination is a real and invisible risk: the practice feels productive throughout and the error only surfaces when the real paper looks unfamiliar. A specialist will ask you for the code before you offer it.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Al Ain students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because it costs nothing there is no good reason not to hold one, and tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately here?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. In a city the size of Al Ain the arrangement is easy to fall into and is poor practice besides: the person marking the work should not also be paid to prepare it. An independent specialist gives you a separate read on where the marks are going.

faqs.question: After four weeks, how do we compare the result against doing nothing?
faqs.answer: With two marked papers rather than two impressions. The first session should produce a timed paper with the error types written down; the fourth or fifth should produce a second one on the same specification, marked the same way and compared by topic. Movement should be visible in the specific areas named, not just in the total. You should also hear your child describe their own weakest topic unprompted. If neither has happened, the comparison favours stopping and changing something.

intro.heading: Two years of closing doors
paragraphs: Al Towayya sits in the eastern part of Al Ain, near the hospital district and within a short run of Asharej and the central areas. Families here usually begin thinking about IGCSE support when something arrives in writing: a report, a set placement, a mock result. By then several decisions that mattered have already been taken, and the useful service a page like this can perform is to lay out which doors close when.

There are more of them than parents realise. A subject can be dropped or added only while the timetable allows. A tier can be argued only before the school submits entries, which happens months ahead of the papers. The entry itself fixes the board, the code and the tier. After results there is a short window to request a review of marking, and a separate window to enter the November series. Each of those has an owner — the school, the examinations officer, the board — and none of them is negotiable once passed.

The reason this matters for tutoring is that what a tutor can usefully do changes completely depending on which doors are still open. Before entries, a tutor can produce marked evidence for a tier conversation, which may be worth more than a whole term of teaching. After entries, the evidence is irrelevant and the work becomes maximising the ceiling that now exists. Buying the same block of sessions at those two moments buys two quite different things.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. In Al Ain, where journeys are short, the practical gain is less about convenience than about supply: the number of people locally who have marked a given specification is small, and a screen removes that constraint entirely.

This page is organised around the clock. The doors, in the order they close. The June series counted backwards in school weeks rather than calendar dates. The results window, including the review of marking and the November route. What the Al Ain school year does to the usable weeks, including the Ramadan period. And the private candidate route for a subject a school does not enter, which is the one option most families never hear about.

Two deliberate omissions. We publish no International Baccalaureate dates anywhere on this site, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking. And for Cambridge and Pearson we name the series by month rather than by month and year, because a timetable date restated on a page goes stale without anybody touching it. Where a past date is cited it is kept, because the date is what makes it checkable.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-towayya.programmesIntro: Each stage below is defined by which doors are still open rather than by the student's ability, because that is what determines what support can achieve.

programmes.name: Year 9: every door open
programmes.description: Subject choice, set placement and school are all still adjustable, and nothing has a board deadline attached. The cheapest support in the whole pipeline sits here: algebraic fluency, writing stamina and the habit of showing full working. Fortnightly across two terms is normally sufficient, and the gains carry through both IGCSE years.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain, Year 9 is also the stage at which a move between schools is genuinely practical, because the city is compact enough that a cross-town change does not impose a punishing commute. programmes.name: Year 10: the tier door narrows
programmes.description: Content is delivered, mostly once, and the internal examination at the end of the year usually becomes the tier recommendation. Support here buys two things: closed coverage gaps and marked evidence for the tier conversation. The second is time-limited and is the part families most often miss.

The remaining work is narrow and diagnosable: method marks, command terms, units, timing and question order, plus the two or three topics the student has quietly avoided for two years.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the sciences, which makes it the subject where a late start helps least. Command-term discipline is the exception and is trainable in two sessions at any point in the year.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Planning and criteria awareness move marks fast, so this subject tolerates a later start than most. Where a non-examination component exists, its internal deadline is set by the school and closes earlier than families expect.

subjects.name: Computer Science

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Towayya can still affect
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Towayya, as the phrase is used here, is a subject specialist working one-to-one with one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram provides that over live video to Al Ain families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. The teaching and the marking are the same; what is absent is the journey, which in this city is short but which still takes the first ten minutes out of a session.

What a tutor can affect depends entirely on the date. That sounds obvious and it is routinely ignored, including by providers quoting the same eight-week block to a Year 10 family in October and a Year 11 family in April. In October the block can teach content, rebuild a topic and generate evidence for a tier change. In April it can recover marks the student can already earn and nothing more. Both are worth buying. They are not the same purchase.

The most valuable thing a family in this district can do before buying anything is to obtain three dates in writing from the school: when entries are submitted, when the mock window falls, and when study leave begins. Those three numbers convert a vague sense of urgency into an actual count of usable weeks, and almost every complaint about a block not working traces back to it being bought for weeks that did not really exist.

The fourth date, which nobody asks for, is the November entry deadline. Knowing it in the autumn turns a resit from a consolation into a planned option, and for a student on a capped tier that single piece of information can be worth more than a term of sessions.

sections.heading: The doors, in the order they close
paragraphs: Set out as a sequence, the IGCSE years look different from how they feel. The examination date is the last thing to arrive and the least adjustable, while the decisions that actually shape a grade all close earlier and quietly. No competing page in this market publishes this sequence, which is strange, because it is the part parents can act on.

The first door is the subject list. Dropping a subject, moving from separate sciences to a combined award, or adding an extension course all depend on timetable capacity and all become impractical once teaching is underway. The second is the tier, which the school decides on evidence and submits to a board deadline. The third is the entry itself, which fixes board, code and tier together.

After the papers two further doors open briefly and then shut. A review of marking is requested through the centre within a short window after results, not directly by a family, and the decision to request one should be made with the subject teacher rather than alone. And the November series has its own entry deadline, which arrives while a family is still absorbing a summer result.

The table below is a planning skeleton rather than a list of dates, deliberately. Dates are revised, schools differ, and a page that restates them is wrong within a year. Fill in your own school's version and keep it on one page.

One more thing worth noting about the sequence. Because each door is owned by somebody different — the timetable, the department, the examinations officer, the board — there is no single person who will warn a family that one is about to close. A coordinator will answer the question accurately when asked, and will rarely raise it unprompted, simply because they are managing a cohort rather than your child alone. Keeping the list on one page and checking it each term is therefore a parent's job and nobody else's.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards in school weeks
paragraphs: Calendar weeks mislead. A family looking at the months between October and June sees plenty of time, and a family counting school weeks and subtracting holidays, mock weeks and the Ramadan period sees something much tighter. The second number is the one a plan should be built on.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two an Al Ain candidate works to. Cambridge offers a February and March sitting to India only, so a page quoting those dates to a UAE family has the wrong country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that using the correct version is essential because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Counted in terms rather than months, the structure is roughly this. The autumn term carries content teaching and the entry decision. The winter period carries mocks and the confirmation of predicted grades. The spring term finishes content and turns to technique. Then study leave removes teaching entirely, and the papers follow. A family that writes its own version of that on one page, with the school's actual dates in it, will plan better than one working from a general sense of urgency.

sections.heading: The results window, and the two decisions inside it
paragraphs: Results arrive and most families treat the moment as an ending. It contains two time-limited decisions, and both are easy to miss while the household is absorbing a number.

The first is whether to request a review of marking. This is requested through the centre rather than by a family directly, within a short published window, and it carries a fee and a risk: a review can confirm a mark or move it, and in some arrangements a mark can go down as well as up. The decision should be made with the subject teacher, who has seen the script and the cohort pattern, rather than on the strength of a disappointing number alone.

The second is the November series. Both main boards run one and UAE candidates can use it. The entry deadline arrives soon after results, which is precisely when a family is least ready to make a considered decision, so the sensible move is to work out the position before results rather than after. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November window has run from late October into November — the November 2026 final timetable finished on 19 November 2026 — with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

A tutor's role in this window is limited and should be stated honestly. We cannot request a review, cannot enter a candidate and cannot influence a grade after the fact. What we can do is help a family read a script if the centre supplies it, and scope a short autumn block for a resit that is actually worth taking.
