process.title: Map the week before the subject
process.description: The first conversation covers school finish times, both pick-ups, sport and Arabic classes, and the hour at which your child stops being teachable. Two or three usable slots normally emerge. Choosing from those rather than from a tutor's availability is what makes the arrangement last past November.

process.title: Confirm the syllabus code
process.description: Ask the exams officer for the code on each entry - 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1 - and the Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in. Matching happens against the code, because board-matched past-paper practice is most of what the final two terms consist of.

process.title: Diagnostic on a marked script
process.description: The first paid session is spent on a recent marked paper rather than on teaching, producing a categorised list of where marks were lost. That list becomes the baseline against which every later paper is measured, so progress is visible rather than asserted.

process.title: Free trial in the chosen slot
process.description: The trial runs in the slot you have chosen, not a convenient one, so you find out whether the hour really works. It is free and needs no card. If the tutor is not the right fit, say so and we propose somebody else without an argument.

process.title: Hold the hour, review at half term
process.description: The slot stays fixed through the year and moves on request rather than being cancelled, including to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. At half term we ask whether the subject still needs the hour, and we are willing to answer no.

whyPoints.title: Built around the real afternoon
whyPoints.description: Slots are set after pick-up, the drive into Falaj Hazza and twenty minutes of food, rather than against a published finish time. A slot that reflects the actual afternoon is attended; one that reflects the timetable is abandoned by November.

whyPoints.title: The hour moves without a negotiation
whyPoints.description: Because nobody is driving, a session can shift on a short-day week or when a sibling's schedule changes, and it survives a trip to Abu Dhabi. That flexibility is the practical advantage of online delivery over an in-home arrangement in this district.

whyPoints.title: Costs shown by the month
whyPoints.description: Published market figures are given as monthly totals with the number of sessions stated and the publisher named, because that is the unit a household budgets in. Market rates are presented as the market's, not as our price list.

whyPoints.title: Progress coded, not described
whyPoints.description: Mark losses are categorised and tracked across papers, so you can see which category is shrinking. A short written note follows every session. A provider who cannot show you a trend is asking you to take the hour on faith.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own coursework and refuse to write it. The document stays with the student. In a market where completed assessments are advertised, that boundary is worth stating in public.

whyPoints.title: Online, and we say so up front
whyPoints.description: UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are an India-only service. A family that wants somebody in the room should hire locally, and we would rather say that at the top of the page.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start in Falaj Hazza?
faqs.answer: Half past four, and five o'clock is more common. Al Ain school finish times spread over about an hour, pick-up queues absorb fifteen to twenty-five minutes, and the drive back into Falaj Hazza from the central school belt adds ten to twenty more. A student then needs food and a short break before they can concentrate. A four o'clock booking looks tidy on paper and gets missed twice a month, which is usually why a family concludes tutoring is not working for them.

faqs.question: Can the lesson time change on a week when school finishes early?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the practical case for online delivery in Al Ain. Because no tutor is driving to the district, a session can move by half an hour or shift to a different evening without renegotiating travel. An in-home arrangement is far less elastic: the tutor's own route decides what is possible, which is why families often end up with the one evening their local tutor had free rather than the evening that suits the household.

faqs.question: How much should a Falaj Hazza family budget each month for IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, according to Bestimate's 2026 figures. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published numbers rather than an IB Gram price list, and duration matters more than rate.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home package nearly double an online one?
faqs.answer: Travel. The advertised in-home monthly packages in this market sit at roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, against about AED 799 for eight online sessions, and a meaningful share of that difference is the tutor's journey into the district rather than teaching time. Bestimate's hourly figures show the same pattern: in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 against qualified online tutors at AED 150 to 300. What a family buys with the premium is presence in the room.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have tutors who will come to Falaj Hazza?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. Lessons for Falaj Hazza students are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared marking of past papers. The search phrase is home tutor because that is what parents type, and we would rather answer the question honestly than let the assumption stand. If presence in the room is what you need, hire locally and ask for the permit and the syllabus code.

faqs.question: Are two shorter sessions better than one long one for a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. A student who has been in school since half past seven rarely sustains ninety productive minutes at six in the evening, and the last twenty minutes of a long session tend to be expensive silence. Two forty-five minute slots keep attention higher, fit either side of a sport evening, and mean a single missed evening costs half as much progress. The trade-off is two defended slots in the week instead of one, which some Al Ain households cannot manage.

faqs.question: What happens to a Falaj Hazza lesson slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They move to post-Iftar timing, at no extra cost and without renegotiating the arrangement. School days shorten and late afternoon becomes the least useful teaching hour of the day, while mid-evening sessions are often the sharpest of the year because the house is calm and nothing else is scheduled. This is straightforward for online delivery and much harder for an in-home tutor, whose own evening and travel have to shift too.

faqs.question: Is it worth booking sessions during the Al Ain school holidays?
faqs.answer: For paper technique, yes; for new content, less so. A student who does nothing for two weeks loses recall, while one who sits two timed papers and reviews them properly comes back ahead of the class. The useful holiday work is the error log, timed practice and the one topic that has been avoided since October. Three focused sessions across a break typically achieve more than six squeezed into a busy term fortnight.

faqs.question: How will I know the weekly hour is actually working?
faqs.answer: By a trend rather than a feeling. The first paid session produces a categorised list of where marks were lost on a real marked script - unwritten method, command-term error, rounding and units, topic gap - and every later timed paper is coded against the same categories. After three or four papers you can see which categories are shrinking. Each session also leaves a three-line written note. If a category has not moved in six weeks, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the equivalency total for an Al Ain student?
faqs.answer: No, not among the five subjects required on the British track. The sourced Ministry requirement is passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level pass at E or two Advanced Subsidiary passes. So a student needs five other qualifying subjects. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs or can promise, so verify your own child's position through the official channel.

faqs.question: How much timetable time do the mandatory UAE subjects take?
faqs.answer: Enough to affect how much tutoring a week can absorb. Private schools must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum. Dubai's published requirements, a useful reference for structure, calculate instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in several of those subjects. The practical effect for a Falaj Hazza family is that one well-attended extra hour beats three poorly attended ones.

faqs.question: Where does help with IGCSE coursework stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, explain the criteria, read the student's own draft and say which criterion is under-served, teach referencing, and set timed practice on a comparable task that is not the assessed one. A tutor may not write, dictate, restructure or edit the work to completion, or supply another student's work. At IB Gram the document stays with the student and tutors annotate rather than type. A request to cross that line is declined and recorded.

faqs.question: Should we plan a November entry before results day?
faqs.answer: Yes, and almost nobody does. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit June and November, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a genuine resit route exists. A student who knows in April that November is the fallback revises differently in May from one who is told in August that they have six weeks to rescue a grade. Pearson November results reach students the following January - November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026 - so check whether that timing fits any application deadline you have.

faqs.question: Which district of Al Ain is best for finding a tutor?
faqs.answer: For in-home arrangements, the central districts: Al Jimi and Al Khabisi have the shortest journeys and the largest local pool, though their evening slots fill earliest. For the thing that actually moves a grade - somebody who has taught your child's exact syllabus code - the district makes no difference at all, because the constraint is the size of Al Ain's teaching population rather than the length of a drive. Online delivery makes a Falaj Hazza family's choice identical to a central family's.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-falaj-hazza.closingHeading: Pick the hour first, then the tutor
al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-falaj-hazza.closingBody: Spend ten minutes with a calendar before you book anything. Write down school finish times, both pick-ups, sport, Arabic classes and the hour your child stops being teachable, and choose the slot that still exists in a bad week. Then get the syllabus code from the exams officer. With those two things in hand you can judge any tutor in Al Ain in a single conversation. When you are ready, book a free trial in the slot you actually want, and we will run it there rather than at a time that suits us.

intro.heading: Hili, or the next neighbourhood over: what actually changes
paragraphs: A parent in Hili comparing tutoring options against Al Jimi or Al Mutaredh is really asking two questions at once. Does a different address give me access to different tutors, and does it give me a different price. In Al Ain the answers are, in order, barely and no. The city is compact enough that the drivable tutor pool from one central neighbourhood looks much like the pool from the next, and the published market rates do not vary by district at all.

What does change between Hili and the areas around it is the evening. Hili sits north of the centre near the archaeological park and the Oman road, and many of its students attend schools in the central and southern clusters, which makes the journey home long enough to rule out a four o'clock weekday session for a good number of them. A family in Al Mutaredh, next to the central school cluster, keeps that slot. Over a term that is one extra session a week, which is a real difference and the only geographic one worth planning around.

The thing that genuinely varies between two students in the same street is the specification. 'IGCSE' covers two different qualifications: Cambridge International, with four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, with codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. The content overlaps; the paper structures, the tiering and the practical arrangements do not. Two neighbours at different schools can need genuinely different tutors, and no amount of local searching reveals that.

Hili is in Al Ain, part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is worth knowing because the regulator differs across the country in ways that affect what a school must deliver, and because ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project. A comparison table of the five UAE regulators appears further down.

IB Gram's position is the same in every neighbourhood, which is the honest version of this page's argument. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Hili students are matched on syllabus code and tier and taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That makes the neighbourhood question almost irrelevant and the specification question decisive, which is the right way round.

The rest of this page is built as comparisons rather than claims: four neighbourhoods side by side, six provider models with their published rates, the separate and co-ordinated science routes, the tutor permit categories, the two board calendars and the five UAE regulators. All of it works on a tutor a Hili family finds without us, which is the point of publishing it.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-hili.programmesIntro: Three qualification routes run through Al Ain's British-curriculum schools and they are easiest to understand side by side. The differences below are the ones that change which tutor a Hili student needs.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes, with many subjects tiered into Core and Extended and a grade ceiling applying to Core. Sciences carry a separate practical component, either a laboratory test paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and schools choose which route to enter. Cambridge runs the qualification in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests at Lower Secondary in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: The administrative detail that catches Al Ain families is zoning. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. Ask the exams officer which zone your school sits in and work from that version only.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and 4EA1. Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher; the international sciences are untiered and assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical exam. Some subjects are offered modularly, which changes when a result can be banked and when a resit is available.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so plan from the live official timetable.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: The IGCSE tier and grade determine which AS subjects stay open. Extended tier Mathematics at a strong grade is the normal expectation for AS Mathematics, and Core tier generally closes it along with the separate sciences. The decision is taken in Year 10 and discovered in Year 12, which is why it deserves a conversation long before anyone thinks of it as urgent.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university entry the Ministry of Education equivalency rule on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. No tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency; the family applies through the official channel.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-hili.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, the comparison that matters is between the two boards rather than between two neighbourhoods. Each entry names the codes and the component where marks actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Tier names and grade ceilings differ between the boards, and so do the paper numbers. Marks are lost on omitted method lines in multi-step questions. Ask any tutor which paper numbers your child sits; an answer without hesitation is the fastest competence check available.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Calculus and series sitting outside the 0580 specification entirely, so a 0580 specialist is not a substitute. Taught by few Al Ain schools, which makes it the clearest case where the local pool is thin in every neighbourhood equally, Hili and Al Mutaredh alike.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The practical arrangement is the real difference. Cambridge students sit a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson examines practical skills within the written papers. Revising for the wrong structure costs marks that have nothing to do with physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and qualitative analysis, examined differently by each board. Most lost marks are unit handling and calculation rather than chemistry, which makes the fix narrow and quick once a marked paper has shown which calculation types are failing.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade, and the two boards allocate marks differently for the same wording. Well supplied online, so a Hili family has no reason to accept either a long wait or a premium rate in this subject.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award with a different content map from the separate sciences. Families often assume a separate-science tutor covers it; the specification differs, and hours spent on content that is not examined are hours lost whichever area you live in.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 first language, 0510/0511 second language; Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: First and second language are separate specifications rewarding different things. The commonest misdiagnosis in Al Ain is a first-language candidate placed with a second-language tutor or the reverse; check the code before buying anything.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, definition precision and applied data response. Students describe where the mark scheme asks them to analyse, and the correction is structural so it transfers across the paper. Usually a short block rather than a term.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables, plus a practical component for ICT on specified software tasks. Genuinely scarce in Al Ain, and a subject where a capable programmer who has not taught the specification will teach the wrong material competently.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source skills, case-study recall and extended-answer structure. The marks sit in organisation rather than volume of content, which is why these respond quickly to a handful of focused sessions on source and essay technique.

sections.heading: Hili against the next neighbourhood over, row by row
paragraphs: Here is the comparison in full. The columns are the things a family can actually feel: how long the school run is, when a weekday session can realistically start, how deep the drivable tutor pool is, and what the market charges. Three of those four are identical across the city, which is the finding of the table rather than a disappointment in it.

The only column that moves is the earliest usable slot, and it moves because of distance to the school cluster rather than anything about the neighbourhood itself. A Hili student finishing at a southern school and arriving home at twenty past four cannot start at four. A student in Al Mutaredh walking home in ten minutes can. Over a thirty-week term that is around thirty sessions against twenty.

The drivable pool column deserves a word, because families assume it varies and it does not, much. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the whole city's teaching population is modest and the scarce subjects are scarce everywhere in it. Moving from Hili to Al Jimi does not find you an Additional Mathematics 0606 teacher who was not there before.

Which leads to the point of the exercise. If three of four columns are identical and the fourth is a commute, then the decision a family is actually making is not where they live but what they match on. Matching on who can drive to Hili narrows the field for no gain; matching on who has taught the specification widens it for no extra cost.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same in every one of them
paragraphs: Two structural facts make the neighbourhood question less important than it looks. The first is that published tutoring rates in the UAE are set by provider type, not by district. The bands quoted across this market, from AED 33 to AED 65 at the budget end up to AED 500 or more for a named premium tutor, are the same bands whether a family is in Hili, Al Jimi or Zakher. Nobody discounts for a short drive.

The second is that subject scarcity is a citywide property. Al Ain has a much smaller private-school set than Abu Dhabi island, so the number of people who have taught Cambridge 0606 or 0478 to examination standard is small for the whole city. A family in a more central neighbourhood has a marginally shorter list of willing drivers, not a different list of qualified teachers.

What follows is that the useful lever is not location but specification. Establish the board, the code and the tier, then look for someone who has taught exactly that. Done that way, a Hili family and an Al Mutaredh family arrive at the same shortlist, and the only remaining difference is what time the session starts.

The honest caveat is that location does matter for one thing: whether an in-home arrangement is practical at all. In Zakher or Al Maqam it frequently is not, in Al Mutaredh it usually is, and Hili sits between. That is a real difference, and it is a difference about logistics rather than about teaching quality or price.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, with rates attributed
paragraphs: Comparing brands is not useful and, where it involves claims about a competitor's quality, not fair. Comparing models is useful, because the model determines what you get for the money and almost every page in this market compares itself only to an unnamed alternative. The table below compares provider types, with rate bands attributed to whoever published them in October 2026.

Three findings from the research behind this page are worth stating alongside it. Three of the six best-ranking pages for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all. The two that do quote US dollars rather than dirhams. And one publishes a schema price range that contradicts the figure visible on its own page. A family comparing options is therefore working with less published information than it should be.

The rows that matter most to a Hili family are replacement policy and permit verification, neither of which appears on competitor pages. Replacement policy is what happens when a match does not work: whether you get a new tutor, a refund or a conversation about persevering. Permit status is whether the person teaching your child is legally allowed to, which is checkable and free to confirm.

Read the AED column as a market band, not as an IB Gram price. We quote per plan after a free trial lesson and we do not publish a rate card, partly because the figure depends on the subject's scarcity and the plan's length, and partly because a rate card next to competitor bands invites the comparison this table is trying to replace.

sections.heading: Separate sciences or co-ordinated: comparing the two routes
paragraphs: This is the comparison that actually changes a tutoring decision in Year 10, and it is one no competitor page in this cluster addresses. A student takes either the three separate sciences, each with its own syllabus code, or a combined or co-ordinated award covering all three in compressed form. The content maps differ, and so does what the next stage expects.

The practical risk is a mismatch of tutor to route. A Physics 0625 specialist asked to support a co-ordinated science candidate will teach excellent physics, some of which is not on that student's specification, and will not necessarily know what the co-ordinated papers ask. Families book on the subject name and discover the gap in the spring.

The progression consequence matters more in Al Ain than families expect. Where a school's sixth form expects separate sciences for AS entry, a co-ordinated award can close a route, and the smaller school set here means fewer alternative places to go. That is a conversation to have with the school in Year 9, not Year 11.

Compare the two on the table's final column in particular. The hours required are not proportional to the content, because the co-ordinated route's difficulty is breadth under time pressure rather than depth, and the technique that fixes it is different.

One last comparison inside the comparison. A student moving from co-ordinated to separate sciences mid-course is taking on content nobody has taught them, and that is a two-term project rather than a block. A student staying put and working on pace and breadth is usually a short block. Decide which problem you have before buying hours against either.

sections.heading: Which tutors may legally teach, compared by category
paragraphs: Only one competitor page in the entire research set touches tutor licensing, in a single subheading, and it ranks partly on that alone. The position is checkable and worth comparing properly, because the categories differ and a parent can verify which applies.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The route is MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two comparisons matter for a Hili family. A teacher at your child's own school is in a category of their own: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal entirely, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the steps and annual renewal.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere, so no amount should be quoted to you and any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. For the avoidance of doubt, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson.

sections.heading: Comparing the two exam calendars a Hili student may face
paragraphs: Boards do not share a calendar, and a student taking subjects with both of them is managing two timetables. The comparison is worth setting out plainly, not least because one widely repeated claim about Cambridge is wrong for this country and acting on it would mean a missed entry.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the school's zone version is the only one to use.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The documented pattern is useful for planning a resit: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry therefore means a January result.

The forward rule is to name a series by its month and check the live official timetable, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. No future date on this page carries a year for that reason, and any page that gives you one should be checked against the board before you plan around it.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the five UAE authorities
paragraphs: Comparison is the right form for this, and the whole map is absent from the pages currently ranking: ADEK is named by none of the researched competitors and SPEA by one. A Hili family may well have relatives or a previous address in another emirate, and the rules are not the same.

Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain and therefore Hili, is governed by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai is governed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same in its own.

The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. One difference is worth noting because it surprises people: Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not just inspection sits with the emirate regulator there.

Across all of them, the federal baseline is the same: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the mandatory UAE subjects every private school teaches alongside its international curriculum.

For a Hili family the practical use of this table is portability. Families move between emirates for work more often than they change schools, and a plan built on the assumption that KHDA rules apply in Al Ain, or ADEK rules in Sharjah, will be wrong in detail. The subject teaching transfers; the regulatory context does not.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, compared with what is on sale
paragraphs: This comparison is uncomfortable and necessary. The research behind this page found an operation selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE students at around AED 3,750, and that product is marketed alongside legitimate tutoring in the same search results. A family comparing options should be able to tell the two apart quickly.

Legitimate support, on either side of the IGCSE and Diploma boundary, means teaching a technique, explaining why a mark scheme rewards one phrasing over another, marking the student's own practice work, drilling calculation types and rehearsing oral components. For practical papers it includes apparatus conventions, uncertainty treatment and reading results tables, all of which are examinable skills teachable in the abstract.

What falls outside is producing data, writing up an investigation, supplying answers for submitted work, or preparing material a student presents as their own. We also will not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; the correct move is to cite the official page and link to it.

The comparison test is simple enough to apply in one question. Ask a prospective provider what they will do if a student brings coursework the night before it is due. An answer about reading the draft and marking it against criteria is the right answer. An answer that involves fixing it is a description of a risk the student carries alone.

There is a second line worth comparing, around examiner claims. Tutors should not be described as IB or Cambridge examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Several pages in this market lean on the word without the evidence, and it is a fair thing to ask about directly.

sections.heading: Comparing availability honestly, including ours
paragraphs: No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit, which makes availability the easiest thing in this market to compare dishonestly. Our position in Hili is the same as in every Al Ain neighbourhood, because the pool is citywide: strong in Mathematics, the separate sciences, English and the humanities; limited in Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and ICT; thin in second modern languages.

When a request cannot be covered we offer a different slot, a named start date a fortnight or so out, or a straight decline. What we do not do is substitute across specifications, because a general science tutor filling a Chemistry 0620 request looks like a solution for a month and then costs a term. That substitution is the single most common hidden failure in this market.

In-home coverage from IB Gram is zero in every row and every neighbourhood, because home visits are a service we run only in India. Comparing us with a local in-home tutor on that axis is a comparison we lose, and the honest version of the table says so rather than reframing it.

Put the same questions to anyone you are comparing. Can you cover this code and tier, in this slot, starting when. What happens if the first tutor is wrong. Which permit category does the tutor hold. A provider that answers all three with specifics is comparable; one that answers yes to everything in a city this size is not answering.

process.title: Get the board, code and tier
process.description: From the school office or the statement of entry. Cambridge 0620 Extended and Pearson 4CH1 are different requests, and two Hili neighbours at different schools may need different tutors. This single step removes most of the mismatch risk in this market and it costs nothing but a phone call.

process.title: Send a marked paper with the request
process.description: A marked paper shows which questions were attempted and which were left blank, and the two point to different problems with different durations. Blanks mean content, which takes a term. Method errors and phrasing mean technique, which takes hours. We match from that rather than from a subject label.

process.title: Free trial with the proposed tutor
process.description: A full session, no card required, with the person who would teach the course. Ask them which paper their students lose most marks on and why. A specialist names a paper and a pattern; a generalist says it varies. You keep the written diagnosis whether or not you continue.

process.title: Pick the slot the commute allows
process.description: For a Hili family that usually means after five-thirty on weekdays, with a weekend morning carrying part of an exam-year block. Sessions are fixed in Gulf Standard Time and move in a message when a mock week, travel or Ramadan timing requires it rather than being lost.

process.title: Review at the agreed session count
process.description: Check the plan against the weakness it was bought to fix. Closed means stop or move on; not closed means change the approach or the tutor. Comparing providers on this question alone is informative, because the ones without a review point are the ones whose plans renew by default.

whyPoints.title: Comparisons by model, not by brand
whyPoints.description: We compare provider types with rates attributed to whoever published them, and we do not make claims about a competitor's quality or legality. Every AED figure on this page carries a source and the month it was read.

whyPoints.title: The same answer in every neighbourhood
whyPoints.description: Rates do not vary by Al Ain district and the scarce subjects are scarce citywide, so we match on syllabus code and tier rather than on a drivable radius. A Hili family and an Al Mutaredh family get the same shortlist and a different start time.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before booking
whyPoints.description: One-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. On the in-home axis we are the wrong choice, and we would rather say that at the top of the page than after a deposit.

whyPoints.title: Permit questions we invite
whyPoints.description: Ask which MoHRE permit category a tutor holds and when it was issued. The permit is free and valid two years, so there is no excuse for not holding one, and no basis for charging more because of it.

whyPoints.title: The regulator map, in full
whyPoints.description: ADEK for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, KHDA for Dubai, SPEA for Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge for Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. We hold no approval from any of them and claim none.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on submitted work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and marking the student's own practice, with no writing, no redrafting to completion and no supplied material. We also will not reproduce board papers or mark schemes as downloads, because citing and linking them is the correct route.

faqs.question: Would we get a better tutor by searching Al Jimi instead of Hili?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural. Al Ain is compact and its private-school set is much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the city has one modest teaching population rather than a different one per district. Published market rates do not vary by neighbourhood either. What changes between Hili and Al Jimi is the school run, which shifts the earliest realistic weekday session by around an hour. That is a genuine difference worth planning around, and it is the only one. Match on the syllabus code instead and both families get the same shortlist.

faqs.question: What actually differs between two IGCSE students living on the same Hili street?
faqs.answer: Usually the exam board. One may sit Cambridge 0625 Physics with a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper, and the other Pearson 4PH1, which examines practical skills inside the written papers. Same subject, same year group, different specification, different revision plan. Tier differs too: Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended with a grade ceiling on Core, while Pearson Mathematics A splits into Foundation and Higher. Get the board, code and tier from the school before you compare tutors, because those three facts decide the match.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor in Hili worth the extra AED per hour?
faqs.answer: It depends on one thing: whether your child works better with an adult in the room. The UAE in-home band is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the premium pays for a car and unbilled driving time rather than a better-matched teacher. For a child who needs physical presence, that is money well spent. For a child who does not, it buys a smaller choice of specialist and a session that starts later in the evening.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer in-home IGCSE lessons anywhere in Hili?
faqs.answer: No, and not anywhere else in the UAE either. In-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Hili students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The URL says home tutor because that is the phrase families search, and the honest answer belongs at the top of the page rather than after a payment. If physical presence is a requirement, hire locally and use the permit, syllabus and replacement-policy questions on this page to judge the person you find.

faqs.question: How do the provider models compare on what happens if the tutor is wrong?
faqs.answer: This is the column nobody publishes and the one worth asking about. A large online platform will usually offer another tutor from a deep pool. A specialist agency should have a stated policy. An independent in-home tutor has no replacement at all, so a bad match means starting the search over. A marketplace leaves you to rebook yourself. Our position is that we change the tutor on your judgement rather than after a negotiation, which is also why the free trial exists: the question is better settled before money moves.

faqs.question: Should my child take the separate sciences or the co-ordinated award?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the school in Year 9, because it affects both qualification count and progression. Separate sciences means Cambridge 0625, 0620 and 0610 as three qualifications with full specifications. Co-ordinated 0654 is a double award and combined 0653 a single, covering all three sciences in compressed form with a different content map. Where a sixth form expects separate sciences for AS entry, the co-ordinated route can close it, and Al Ain's smaller school set means fewer alternatives. For tutoring, confirm the code so nobody teaches off-specification material.

faqs.question: Are tutoring rates in Al Ain lower than in Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Not in any published figure we could find. The bands quoted across this market are set by provider type rather than by city: AED 33 to AED 65 at the budget end, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel, and AED 500 or more for a named premium tutor. What differs in Al Ain is supply rather than price. With a smaller private-school set, the scarce subjects attract longer waits and sit at the top of their band rather than the bottom.

faqs.question: Which permit should I ask a Hili tutor about?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service, with a stated two-working-day completion. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask which category and when it was issued. Because the permit is free and quick, there is no excuse for not holding one and no basis for charging more because of it.

faqs.question: Can a teacher at my child's Al Ain school tutor them privately for payment?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the permit. If a tutor's pitch rests on teaching at your child's school, treat that as a reason to decline rather than a credential. The current wording should be checked against ADEK's own published policy document rather than taken from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school if we move from Al Ain to Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate. Al Ain sits under ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, as part of Abu Dhabi. Dubai is KHDA, Ras Al Khaimah is the Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. One practical difference: Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate regulator there.

faqs.question: Why does this page refuse to name the best tutoring company in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Because claims about a competitor's pricing, quality or legality are not ours to make, and because the research behind this page found that published comparisons in this market are unreliable. One ranking page contradicts its own prices; another publishes a schema price range that differs from its visible figure; a third asserts its own star rating. What is fair to compare is models: budget platform, specialist agency, independent in-home tutor, marketplace, premium individual, tuition centre. That comparison is in the table above, with every rate attributed to whoever published it.

faqs.question: Is a group class a reasonable alternative for a Hili family on a budget?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the whole group shares the same gap. A group of four revising a full syllabus broadly works and costs less per hour. The same group is poor value for a student who is secure everywhere except Paper 4 extended response, because most of each hour addresses someone else's weakness. If a group is what the budget allows, choose one organised by topic rather than by subject, and ask what the group's actual starting point is. We provide one-to-one only, for that reason.

faqs.question: How long does a match take for a Hili request?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, the separate sciences, English or the humanities, usually two to six days. For co-ordinated science or a confirmed second-language English specification, closer to a week. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 or ICT, one to three weeks and sometimes a decline. For second modern languages, two to four weeks and most often a decline with a referral suggestion. Those timings are citywide rather than specific to Hili, and the narrow six-to-eight evening band fills first, so a Saturday morning slot widens the choice considerably.

faqs.question: What is the one question that separates a good provider from a weak one?
faqs.answer: Ask what they will do if a student brings coursework the night before it is due. The right answer is that a tutor reads the draft, marks it against the published criteria and asks whether the argument is supported. The wrong answer involves fixing it, and it tells you what else that provider is willing to do. The research behind this page found completed assessments on sale to UAE students at around AED 3,750, so this is not a hypothetical distinction. One question, asked before any money moves, settles it.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-hili.closingHeading: The neighbourhood is not the variable; the specification is
al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-hili.closingBody: Comparing an IGCSE home tutor in Hili with one in Al Jimi, Al Mutaredh or Zakher produces the same shortlist and a different start time. Rates do not move by district, and the subjects that are scarce are scarce across the whole city because Al Ain's private-school set is small. What does change the answer is the board, the code and the tier your child is entered for, and that comes from the school office in one phone call. Get those three facts, then compare provider models using the table above. Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a free trial session and a marked paper as the starting point.

intro.heading: Answering the question Zakher parents actually type
paragraphs: Zakher sits on the southern edge of Al Ain, out past the ring road towards the Jebel Hafeet approach, and that geography is the whole reason this search exists. A family here is not short of tutors in the abstract. The country has plenty. What a Zakher family is short of is a tutor who both teaches the precise IGCSE syllabus their child is entered for and can reach their living room before the evening is gone. Those two conditions rarely hold at once in a residential district this far from the city centre, and most parents work that out after two or three disappointing trial lessons.

So the honest answer is this. If you want somebody physically in the room in Zakher, your realistic pool is whoever happens to live in or near southern Al Ain, holds a valid MoHRE private tuition work permit, is free at the hour your child is awake and willing to work, and has taught your child's exact specification. That is four filters applied to a small local population, and the fourth filter is the one that usually fails. A graduate who studied physics is not automatically someone who has taught Cambridge 0625 Paper 4 and knows that the alternative-to-practical paper rewards a particular kind of written precision.

IB Gram takes the geography out of the problem. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, so the pool a Zakher family chooses from is the full set of IGCSE subject specialists on the platform rather than the handful who live nearby. Home visits are an India-only service for us; we do not run them anywhere in the UAE. That is a limit worth stating plainly rather than burying, because the comparison is the argument: a specialist on screen for sixty minutes beats a generalist in the room for ninety.

The rest of this page is written for a parent who wants to make that decision properly. It sets out what the Al Ain and wider UAE market charges for in-home and online IGCSE tuition, with the figures attributed to whoever published them. It explains how to find out which board your child's school actually enters students with, since Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different papers and different tiering rules. It covers who is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE and how you can check. It names the marks Al Ain students most often lose, by subject. And it says what we do when no specialist is available for a niche subject, because that happens and concealing it would be worse than disclosing it.

One framing point before the detail. Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, not by KHDA. If you have moved from Dubai you will find the inspection vocabulary familiar and the authority different. The Garden City's private-school set is also much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, which is exactly why Higher-tier sciences, Additional Mathematics and the less common languages are the subjects Zakher families most often struggle to staff locally.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-zakher.programmesIntro: Zakher students arrive at IGCSE from several directions: a Cambridge Lower Secondary feeder programme, a British Year 9, or a transfer from another system entirely. These are the programmes our IGCSE-level tutoring actually touches, and what each one means for a family in southern Al Ain.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed internally and optionally through Cambridge Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Checkpoint sittings run in March, May and October, and the reports give a diagnostic band rather than a grade. This is where the algebra fluency and the written-explanation habits that IGCSE science demands are either built or missed.
programmes.countryNote: For a Zakher family this stage matters more than it looks. Al Ain's smaller private-school set means subject setting decisions in Year 9 can be hard to reverse, and a child placed in a lower maths set in Year 9 may find Extended tier closed off by Year 10. A term of targeted work before those sets are fixed is cheaper than two years of catch-up afterwards.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, each subject examined separately, with most sciences and mathematics split into Core and Extended tiers. Core maths (0580) caps at grade C; Extended reaches A*. Sciences are examined through a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, which most UAE centres use.
programmes.countryNote: Zakher students sit these papers in the June and November series. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that version only.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other international GCSE route, with subject codes such as 4MA1 for mathematics and 4PH1 for physics. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; several subjects are available in a modular structure where units can be sat across sessions rather than all at the end. Papers are structured differently from Cambridge even where the topic lists overlap.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from that series reach students in January, as November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead, so always work from the live official PDF rather than a date copied onto a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programmes.description: The two years after IGCSE for most Al Ain British-curriculum students. AS sits as a standalone qualification or as the first half of the full A Level. Subject content steps up sharply from IGCSE Extended, particularly in mathematics, where the pure content assumed on day one is roughly the top third of the Extended syllabus used fluently rather than recognised.
programmes.countryNote: This matters to a Zakher parent choosing tiers now. UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, alongside five IGCSE or GCSE passes. A Core-tier IGCSE in a subject your child intends to continue at A Level closes a door quietly.

al-ain/igcse-home-tutor-in-zakher.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Ain families ask for most, written with the syllabus code attached. If your child's code differs from the one shown, say so at the consultation; the paper structure, not the subject name, decides what the lessons do.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended runs two papers, a non-calculator and a calculator paper, and reaches A*. Marks go on method lines that are never written down, on bearings and transformations, and on the vectors and functions topics that sit only in the Extended content. Core candidates lose marks mostly on multi-step percentage and ratio problems.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics. Calculus, trigonometric identities and the factor theorem arrive early and the question style assumes algebraic fluency rather than teaching it. In Al Ain this is one of the hardest subjects to staff locally, and a frequent reason families look beyond the city.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Three components: multiple choice, theory, and either Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative-to-practical. Paper 6 rewards a specific written discipline - naming the variable controlled, describing how it was kept constant, reading a scale to the right precision. Electricity and the kinematics graphs are where Extended candidates bleed marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, ionic equations and the organic chemistry section carry disproportionate weight. The common failure is not the chemistry but the arithmetic presentation: unrounded intermediate values, missing units, and state symbols omitted from equations where the mark scheme requires them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy, and the mark schemes are strict about command terms. 'Describe' and 'explain' earn different marks for the same knowledge, and transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance are the three topics where Extended students most often write a sound answer that scores half.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, which is what many Al Ain students actually sit rather than three separate papers. The compression is uneven: physics content is cut hardest, so students who choose it then meet A Level physics with real gaps in the waves and electricity material.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510/0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, directed writing and either a written or spoken endorsement depending on the code. The directed-writing task is scored on register and audience as much as accuracy, and students who write a strong essay in the wrong form lose the task marks entirely.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Two papers covering reading passages and directed writing, plus composition. The summary question has a strict mark allocation split between content points and writing quality, and candidates routinely sacrifice the writing marks by listing points instead of composing prose.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the whole game in the structured questions: axes labelled, curves shifted the correct way, the new equilibrium marked. Students who can explain a concept in words but cannot draw it correctly plateau around a grade C regardless of how much reading they do.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven. The marks that separate grades are application marks, awarded only for answers that refer to the specific business in the insert rather than to business theory in general. A generic answer that would pass a classroom test scores poorly here.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory paper plus an algorithms and programming paper. Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the binary and hexadecimal conversions are predictable mark earners, and are also the three things self-taught candidates most often get formally wrong while being conceptually right.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Sat by many Al Ain students alongside the mandatory Arabic provision their school delivers. Comprehension and summary writing dominate the marks, and the register expected in the extended writing task is formal Standard Arabic rather than the dialect used at home.

sections.heading: What "IGCSE home tutor in Zakher" really asks
paragraphs: Searched literally, the phrase means: find me a person who will come to my house in Zakher and teach IGCSE. Taken as the question behind it, the phrase means something narrower and more useful: find me somebody competent for this syllabus who can actually fit into my week. The second question has a much better answer than the first, and in southern Al Ain the gap between the two is wide.

Consider the arithmetic of the first version. A tutor travelling to Zakher from the central school cluster is adding perhaps forty minutes of driving to a sixty-minute lesson, and that cost is priced in. The Bestimate rate table for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages advertised in the market sit around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. None of that is our price list; it is what the market publishes, and it tells you that roughly a quarter to a third of an in-home fee is buying transport rather than teaching.

Now consider the supply side. The filter that fails in Zakher is not willingness to travel. It is subject match. A parent whose child sits Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics, or Pearson 4PH1 physics, or First Language English at the top of the grade range, needs somebody who has taught that specification and marked against that mark scheme. In a city the size of Al Ain, with a private-school set much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, that person may simply not live within thirty minutes of your villa. Many families discover this by paying for two months of pleasant, well-meaning, slightly off-target lessons.

IB Gram's answer is to separate the teaching from the travel. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the constraint on who teaches your child is their subject and their availability at 5pm Al Ain time, not their postcode. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India - and stating that clearly is better than letting a parent assume otherwise and find out on booking day.

sections.heading: Can anyone near Zakher actually teach your child's syllabus?
paragraphs: This is the section most tutoring sites leave out, because the honest answer is sometimes no. Coverage is uneven by subject, and it is uneven in a predictable way: the subjects with the largest cohorts are the easiest to staff, and the ones a small inland city produces a handful of candidates for each year are the hardest. Publishing the shape of that gap is more useful to a Zakher parent than pretending it does not exist.

The table below sets out, by subject group, what a family in Al Ain should expect in terms of local in-home availability, what we can do online, and what happens if the specialist is not free. The fallback column is the part worth reading. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a niche IGCSE subject, we will say so at the consultation and offer either a tutor based elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time or a wait for a slot to open. We will not substitute a generalist and describe them as a specialist.

There is a second availability question underneath the first, which is whether the person teaching your child is legally permitted to do so. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: individuals need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. People tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

One ADEK point specific to Al Ain. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's school. If somebody offers you your child's own classroom teacher, privately, for a fee, that is the arrangement those rules exist to prevent. Treat the detail as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1: find out which before you book
paragraphs: A surprising number of Al Ain parents do not know which board their child is entered with, and a tutor who guesses wrong wastes a term. The two qualifications share topic lists in places and diverge sharply in paper structure, tiering and what the mark schemes reward. Booking a tutor without the code is like buying textbooks without the subject.

Finding out takes one message. Ask your school's exams officer for the subject code on the entry, not the subject name. You are looking for a string like 0580, 0625 or 0455 for Cambridge, or 4MA1, 4PH1 or 4EB1 for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Schools in Al Ain commonly enter students with one board for sciences and another for English or mathematics, so the answer may not be uniform across your child's subjects.

The structural differences matter in practice. Cambridge tiers most sciences and mathematics as Core and Extended, with a grade ceiling on Core. Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher, and offers several subjects in a modular structure where units can be sat across sessions. Cambridge science candidates in the UAE usually meet the alternative-to-practical paper rather than a hands-on practical test, which changes revision completely: it is a written exam about experimental method, and it is learnable in a way a practical is not.

Session timing differs too, and it is the thing to get right. Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong zone's timetable. Get the zone from the exams officer and bookmark the official timetable page rather than a third-party summary.

sections.heading: Where Al Ain students lose IGCSE marks, subject by subject
paragraphs: Most students who finish on a grade below their ability are not short of knowledge. They are losing marks in patterned, diagnosable ways, and the patterns repeat across cohorts. A tutor who knows the mark scheme can usually find three or four of them in a single marked paper, which is why the first paid lesson in our model is usually a diagnostic rather than teaching.

In mathematics the dominant loss is unwritten method. Extended candidates who can reach a correct answer mentally forfeit the method marks that carry most of a multi-step question, and then lose everything when the arithmetic slips. The second loss is topic-specific: vectors, transformations and the functions material sit only in the Extended content, so a student who has drifted through the shared topics meets them cold. Bearings reliably cost marks because the convention - three figures, clockwise from north - is examined rather than described.

In the sciences the losses split into language and precision. Biology mark schemes distinguish command terms strictly, so a student who describes when asked to explain writes a true answer that scores half. Chemistry punishes presentation: intermediate values rounded too early, units dropped, state symbols missing from an equation where the scheme requires them. Physics loses marks on graph work and on the alternative-to-practical paper, where the credit sits in naming the controlled variable and saying how it was held constant rather than in knowing the physics.

In the written and applied subjects the issue is form. First Language English candidates list summary points instead of composing prose and sacrifice the writing marks. English as a Second Language candidates write a good essay in the wrong register for the directed task. Economics candidates explain in words what the paper wants drawn, with labelled axes and a correctly shifted curve. Business Studies candidates answer in theory when the application marks require them to name the business in the insert. None of these are intelligence problems; all of them are fixable inside a term.

sections.heading: Questions worth asking any tutor before you pay
paragraphs: A Zakher parent considering a local in-home tutor and an online specialist side by side needs a way to compare them that is not price. The following questions do that work, and a competent tutor will answer all of them without hesitation. We would expect to answer them too.

Start with the specification. Which syllabus code have you taught, and in which series? A tutor who has taught 0625 will say so and will tell you whether their students sat Paper 5 or Paper 6. A tutor who answers 'IGCSE physics' has told you nothing. Follow with: can you mark a past paper against the official mark scheme and show me where the marks went? That single request separates teaching from supervision, and it is the service a family is actually buying.

Then the legal and practical questions. Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and when does it expire? The permit is free and valid for two years, so there is no cost reason for anybody to be without one. Are you currently employed at the school my child attends? If yes, the arrangement runs into ADEK's professional-ethics rules and the permit's code of conduct, and you should walk away. What happens if the match is wrong after three lessons, and who do I speak to?

Finally the honesty questions, which are the ones that predict how the next six months will go. What will you not do? A straight answer names coursework: a tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work, and does not write it. What grade are you promising? The correct answer is none; nobody can promise a grade, and anybody who does is selling something other than teaching. And where does your rate come from - is it per hour or per lesson, does it include marking time between sessions, and what are the rescheduling terms?

sections.heading: Online lessons set against an in-home visit in Zakher
paragraphs: This comparison is usually presented as a question of preference. For a family in southern Al Ain it is closer to a question of arithmetic, because the variables that differ are measurable: cost per teaching hour, travel time absorbed by the household, the size of the pool you are choosing from, and how easily a session survives a disrupted week.

On cost, the market is clear enough. Published UAE rates put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with budget online options from AED 33 to 65 at platforms such as Tutopiya and EdFlik, and specialist IB and IGCSE rates at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in. For the same money, a Zakher family either buys a local generalist in the room or a subject specialist on screen. That is the real trade, and it is why the comparison does the selling rather than the adjectives.

On logistics, online removes three failure modes that bite hardest in a spread-out district. Nobody is late because of the Zakher run. A session can move to a different hour on a day when school ends early without a travel renegotiation. And a student who is away in Abu Dhabi or travelling in the holidays keeps their slot rather than losing a month. Against that, online asks for something in return: a quiet room, a stable connection, a device with a working microphone, and a parent who checks in on the first few sessions.

The one genuine advantage of in-person tuition is physical presence with a young or easily distracted child, and it is worth naming rather than arguing away. For IGCSE-age students the balance tips the other way in our experience, because the work itself is paper-based and screen-shared annotation of a marked script is closer to what an examiner does than a conversation across a kitchen table. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so for us this is a disclosure rather than an upsell.
