sections.heading: Why the entry closes months before the paper
paragraphs: Almost every family is surprised by this, and the surprise is expensive when it concerns a retake or an additional subject. Entries close long before the examination itself, and the school or centre has its own internal deadline ahead of the board's. Because IGCSE boards publish their dates, this can be shown with real figures rather than described in general terms.

Start with what each board actually offers a UAE candidate, because in a mixed-board household the answer differs per subject. Cambridge examines IGCSE, O Level and International A Level here in a June series and a November series, and the entry for either closes months before the first paper: in the spring for the June papers, in the autumn term for a November sitting, with the binding date on the statement of entry the centre issues rather than on any page like this one. Pearson runs International GCSE series in May and June and in November, published its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and sent June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. The practical consequence is the same on either board: the decision about tier and subject is made before the entry closes, so it is made before revision has had time to tell you anything.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a tutoring plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised. For an Al Ain family the procedural steps are short: ask the school who holds entry responsibility, ask for the school's internal entry deadline, ask which series and which tier your child is entered for, and get all three in writing. Then build the revision plan backwards from the examination window rather than from the end of term.

sections.heading: What the Ministry of Education counts
paragraphs: Equivalency is the reason IGCSE grades matter beyond school, and it is a subject almost nobody competing for these searches covers. For the British track, the published requirement is that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade three, and submits proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Two details inside that rule matter to Al Ain families specifically. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises households where those are strong grades and which means the five has to be made up from other qualifications. And the figure is five: one page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the sourced requirement. Publishing the correct number is more useful than publishing a confident one.

For completeness, the American-track requirement published alongside it asks for English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics evidenced by at least 450 in the SAT mathematics test. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on the Ministry's own pages, so none is published here. Equivalency is a process families complete through the Ministry's own channel. It is not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or is required for, and no part of it depends on tutoring.

sections.heading: Practical science when the tuition happens over video
paragraphs: This is the honest limitation and it deserves a section rather than a footnote. A tutor working over live video cannot run an experiment with your child. What a tutor can do is everything around the experiment, and in IGCSE science that is where most of the marks sit.

The practical component in the Cambridge sciences exists in more than one form depending on what the school enters, and the first job is finding out which one applies to your child's code. Where a written alternative to the practical is sat, the question types are entirely teachable remotely: identifying variables and controls, reading a method for flaws, completing results tables with correct significant figures, plotting and interpreting graphs, calculating gradients, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data rather than to the expected result. Those are skills, and they respond to practice.

Where a laboratory practical test is sat, the experiment happens at school and the tutor's job is apparatus knowledge, method discipline and the write-up conventions the mark scheme rewards. Either way, the practical skills component is the part of IGCSE science most often neglected in revision, because it is the hardest part to revise from a textbook. That makes it one of the better uses of tutoring time rather than a reason to avoid tutoring, provided nobody pretends the experiment itself can be done through a screen. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards reading a method and a results table rather than holding a pipette, which is exactly the skill a shared screen trains well.

sections.heading: After IGCSE in Al Ain: the Year 11 decision
paragraphs: IGCSE results arrive as a set, and the set opens or closes doors. In Al Ain the post-sixteen options are a British sixth form taking International A Levels, an IB World School taking the Diploma, or a move to a campus outside the city for either. The city's IB school count is lower than Abu Dhabi island's, which means the Diploma route can involve a shorter list of campuses and fewer Higher Level options running at each.

The subject-mapping question is where tutoring decisions in Year 10 and 11 start to matter. IGCSE Extended mathematics maps reasonably onto Diploma Standard Level mathematics or onto an A Level with support; the step to Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is substantially larger and is the commonest place a confident IGCSE student struggles in the first Diploma term. Separate sciences map more comfortably onto A Level and Higher Level sciences than combined science does, which is worth knowing before the Year 10 option forms are submitted.

The practical sequence for a family is short. Ask the intended sixth form or Diploma school, in Year 10, what grades and which subjects it requires. Check whether the route your child is entered on, Core or Extended, can deliver those grades. Then decide what the following eighteen months need to contain. Doing this in Year 10 keeps every option open; doing it after results arrive narrows the choice to whatever is still available in late August.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in this market
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages audited for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below are what other providers publish in dirhams, with the provider type attached. They are market context rather than our price list, and IB Gram's own figure is set at consultation after the trial lesson.

The spread is wide and the reason is mostly format rather than quality. Budget online rates begin around AED 45 to 65 with one provider and AED 33 to 52 with another, typically for university-student tutors. A qualified subject tutor working online is published from AED 150 for IGCSE by one agency. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 350 in one 2026 Dubai rate table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors, with travel inside the figure. Specialist rates are quoted at AED 270 by one UK-based agency and AED 200 to 450 and above elsewhere, and one premium provider publishes AED 650.

Monthly packages are also published in this market: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. For a weekly one-hour arrangement, one rate-comparison source estimates AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Read all of this against the two-year shape of IGCSE: Year 10 content work at the ordinary band costs less in total than Year 11 crisis work at the specialist band, and buys more.

process.title: Email the school the three questions
process.description: Which board, which tier or route, and which syllabus code, subject by subject. One email, usually answered in a day, and it changes what any tutor should be teaching. Families who skip this step routinely pay for several sessions aimed at the wrong specification before anyone notices.

process.title: Send us the code and a marked paper
process.description: The syllabus code tells a tutor which specification to read; a recent marked paper shows where the marks actually went. Those two documents together are worth more than a long description of the problem, and they let the first session start with a diagnosis rather than an introduction.

process.title: Confirm the series and the entry deadline
process.description: Ask the school which series your child is entered for and what the school's own internal entry deadline is. For a retake or an additional subject this is the binding constraint, because entries close more than two months before the paper and the plan has to be built backwards from that.

process.title: Trial the match before paying
process.description: One lesson at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. It runs as a working session: the tutor identifies something specific against the syllabus, teaches a piece of it, and sets out what the next six weeks would contain. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor rather than asking the student to adapt.

process.title: Set the slot against the real arrival time
process.description: Not the school finish, the hour your child is genuinely home and able to concentrate, which from Zakher, Hili or Al Foah is after six. Hold the first choice for a fortnight before moving it. A slot that survives into the spring term is worth more than one that looked neat in September.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier established first
whyPoints.description: Nothing is planned until we know which board sets the papers, which route the student is entered on and which syllabus code applies. A tutor fluent in Cambridge conventions teaching a Pearson candidate produces answers that read well and score less, and that error is entirely avoidable in one email.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the boards themselves
whyPoints.description: Every date on this page comes from Cambridge International's or Pearson's own published material and is attributed to it. No date is restated as fact where a board publishes it only provisionally, and the live official timetable is where a family should confirm anything that matters.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency explained, not performed
whyPoints.description: The Ministry's published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade three, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus the post-sixteen layer. We explain it and point to the official channel. IB Gram does not perform, guarantee or expedite equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about practical science
whyPoints.description: A tutor over video cannot run an experiment. We teach the alternative-to-practical question types, graph and significant-figure work, variable identification and write-up conventions, which is where most of the recoverable marks are, and we say plainly that the experiment itself happens at school.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Three of six audited competitor pages publish no price at all. Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider type that published it, in dirhams rather than dollars, and presented as market context. Our own figure is set at consultation, after the trial lesson.

whyPoints.title: No status we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, OxfordAQA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. We explain what those bodies do and never imply that any of them endorses us.

faqs.question: Is my child sitting Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, subject by subject, because the answer can differ between subjects in the same timetable and frequently does. Al Ain schools use Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel and in some cases OxfordAQA, and nothing obliges a school to use one board for everything. The difference matters because the papers are structured differently, the tiering arrangements differ and the published mark schemes reward different things in extended answers. A tutor teaching the wrong board's conventions produces answers that read well and score below their potential, which is the most avoidable loss in the whole qualification.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Core covers a reduced subset of the syllabus, is examined on different components and caps the highest grade available. Extended covers the full specification and keeps the whole grade range open. They are not easier and harder versions of one paper set, which is the common misunderstanding. A capable student placed on Core can be held below the grade their sixth form or Diploma school requires, and a struggling student placed on Extended often performs worse than they would have on Core. Ask the school which route your child is entered on and what would need to change for that to move.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: The decision belongs to the school and depends on how much of the Extended content remains untaught, which is why the question is far easier to answer in Year 10. Earlier in the course a move is usually possible with a term of concentrated work. By the spring of Year 11 the hours rarely exist, because Extended requires additional taught content rather than simply more practice on the same material. The useful parental question is not whether a move is allowed but how many taught hours the gap represents, and a tutor can give an honest estimate of that after a diagnostic session.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry of Education need to see for equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade three, together with proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the sourced requirement. Verify the current position on the Ministry's own pages before acting, because the process belongs to the Ministry rather than to any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education included in the five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published rule states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. That surprises Al Ain households where those are among the strongest grades, and it has a practical consequence: the five qualifying subjects have to be made up from other qualifications entirely. It is worth checking the full subject set against this rule in Year 10 rather than after results, because the fix at that stage is simply an option-form adjustment rather than an additional entry in a later series.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entries close relative to the exam itself?
faqs.answer: Much earlier than most families expect, and the school's own internal deadline sits ahead of the board's. In the UAE the sittings are June and November, and the entry for either closes months before the first paper - in the spring for June, in the autumn term for November - with the binding date printed on the statement of entry the centre issues. Pearson publishes its own series dates and issues provisional timetables ahead of each one; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. For a retake or an additional subject this is the binding constraint on the whole plan, so ask the school for its internal entry deadline in writing.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series do Al Ain schools normally enter?
faqs.answer: Most enter the main summer series, with November used for retakes and for individual subjects. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series for candidates in the UAE, and its Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are a different thing entirely, sit in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May and June and in November. Which series applies to your child is a question for the school rather than something to infer, because entry decisions are made per subject and per candidate.

faqs.question: What does the syllabus code on my child's paper mean?
faqs.answer: It identifies the exact specification, which is what determines the component structure, the content and the practical arrangements. Cambridge mathematics is 0580, physics 0625, chemistry 0620, biology 0610, English as a first language 0500, economics 0455, business studies 0450, computer science 0478 and additional mathematics 0606. Pearson uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The code matters because specifications are revised, and a tutor working from an older version teaches content that has moved or gone. Ask the school for it and read the board's current syllabus against it.

faqs.question: If lessons are online, how does my child's IGCSE science practical get assessed?
faqs.answer: By the school, through whichever practical component the syllabus code specifies, which may be a laboratory test or a written alternative. A tutor working over video cannot run the experiment and we do not suggest otherwise. What a tutor can teach is everything around it, and that is where the marks mostly sit: identifying variables and controls, spotting flaws in a method, completing results tables to the right significant figures, plotting and interpreting graphs, calculating gradients, and writing conclusions that refer to the data. These are the most neglected marks in IGCSE science revision.

faqs.question: Where do IGCSE maths candidates lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: In three predictable places. First, method marks not shown, because a correct answer with no working scores less than the question offers. Second, speed of algebraic manipulation, which costs time rather than marks directly and then costs marks at the end of the paper. Third, misreading the demand of multi-part questions, particularly where a later part depends on an earlier result. None of those is a content gap, which is why a student who seems to know the material can still underperform, and all three respond quickly to timed practice marked against the board's own published mark scheme.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, by a wide margin, because most of the syllabus is taught then and an hour spent keeping content level is worth several spent recovering it. Year 10 work also sits at the ordinary market band rather than the specialist exam-year band, so the same budget buys more weeks. Year 11 tutoring is technique, timed papers and targeted repair, and it works well when the content is broadly in place. Where half a specification is missing in the spring of Year 11, the honest conversation is about triage rather than about buying more hours.

faqs.question: What IGCSE tutoring rates do providers in Al Ain publish?
faqs.answer: The published spread is wide. Budget online rates begin around AED 33 to 65 with platforms using university-student tutors. A qualified subject tutor working online is published from AED 150 for IGCSE by one agency, with the band running to roughly AED 300. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 350 in one 2026 Dubai rate table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors, travel included. Specialists are quoted from AED 200 to 450 and above, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. These are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Can my child take different IGCSE subjects with different boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many Al Ain students already do without the family realising it. Schools choose a board per subject, so Cambridge sciences alongside Pearson mathematics is an ordinary arrangement. The implication for tutoring is that the board question has to be asked subject by subject rather than once. The implication for revision is that past papers, mark schemes and command-term conventions have to be drawn from the right board for each subject, and mixing them is one of the quieter ways a well-prepared student loses marks.

faqs.question: What happens after IGCSE for an Al Ain student choosing between DP and A-Levels?
faqs.answer: A Levels narrow to three or four subjects with greater depth; the Diploma keeps six with a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. The practical constraint in Al Ain is supply: the city has considerably fewer IB World Schools than Abu Dhabi island, so the Diploma route may mean a shorter list of campuses and fewer Higher Level options at each. Ask the intended sixth form or Diploma school in Year 10 what grades and subjects it requires, then check whether the route your child is entered on can deliver them.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child have tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: One or two, almost always. A student taking nine or ten subjects has limited independent study time, and three or four tutored subjects consume the hours in which the rest of the work has to happen. The better pattern is to fix the weakest subject properly, then move the hour to the next one, rather than running four shallow arrangements in parallel. The exception is the final term, where two subjects at two sessions a week is manageable if both are technique work rather than content repair.

faqs.question: Can a resit improve an IGCSE grade, and when would it be sat?
faqs.answer: Resits are possible and are usually taken in a later series, which for Cambridge means the November series and for Pearson its own November series. The constraint is the entry deadline rather than the preparation: entries close well before the paper, and a school or centre has its own internal deadline ahead of the board's. Decide early, confirm who is making the entry, and get the series and tier in writing. The entry itself is always made by the school or an approved examination centre rather than by a tutoring provider.

al-ain/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Send one email before you book anything
al-ain/igcse-tutor.closingBody: The highest-value thing you can do this week is not hiring a tutor. It is sending one email to the school asking, subject by subject, which board sets the papers, which route or tier your child is entered on, and which syllabus code applies. Those three answers determine what any tutor should be teaching, and they are usually returned within a day. Bring them to the trial lesson, which runs at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken first, along with one recently marked paper. With the code and the paper in hand, the first session can start with a diagnosis against your child's actual specification instead of a conversation about it.

intro.heading: A map pin is the wrong filter for an IGCSE problem
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Ain is a search sorted by distance. That is a sensible filter for a plumber and a poor one for a Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended candidate, because the thing that decides whether the hours work is whether the tutor has taught that specification through a series, and geography has no relationship to that at all. The result a parent gets is a list of whoever is closest and most visible, which in a city the size of Al Ain is a short and semi-random list.

Do the arithmetic and the problem becomes obvious. Al Ain's private-school set is considerably smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, and far smaller than Dubai's, where 387,441 students attended 227 private schools across 17 curricula in 2024-25. Fewer schools means fewer cohorts, and a subject with four or five candidates a year per school produces a very small number of teachers in the whole city who have taught it. For Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 or Computer Science 0478, the honest count of local specialists is low enough that distance-first searching will often return nobody suitable and several people willing.

Proximity does buy real things, and this page is not going to pretend otherwise. A person in the room can watch a younger student's attention wander and act on it. Handwriting, calculator habits and the physical business of laying out a maths answer are easier to correct beside someone. A household that wants visible supervision gets it. Those are genuine, and for some Al Ain families they outweigh everything else. The question worth asking is not whether proximity has value, but what you are paying for it in specification match.

The cost shows up in three places. It shows up in the AED rate, since published UAE in-home one-to-one figures run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. It shows up in scheduling, because a tutor driving from central Al Ain to Al Yahar or Al Maqam has to leave before they know if the previous lesson overran. And it shows up in the shortlist, which narrows from everyone qualified to everyone nearby and available.

IB Gram's position is stated rather than implied: there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE and no office, centre or branch in the country, because in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Ain families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is not a claim that screens beat rooms. It is a claim that in a city this size, choosing by syllabus code beats choosing by driving distance, and that a family in Zakher should be able to work with whoever has actually taught 0606 rather than whoever is twelve minutes away.

al-ain/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Which option is right depends partly on what stage the student is at, because the value of proximity falls as the subject gets more specialised. These are the four stages and what each one changes about the search.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The stage where proximity is worth the most, because the work is general, the student is young, and supervision matters more than specification depth. Any competent maths or English teacher can close a Year 8 gap. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and are diagnostic rather than certificated, which makes this a low-pressure stage to intervene in.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain this is also the stage to find out what the school will actually offer at IGCSE. Narrower option blocks than on Abu Dhabi island mean a subject your child wants may run as a very small group or not at all, and Year 9 is when that is still fixable without changing school.

programmes.name: Year 10, the first IGCSE year
programmes.description: Specification experience starts to matter more than proximity. A tutor needs to know whether the entry is Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Foundation or Higher, because the papers differ and so does the working the mark scheme rewards. A generalist can still help, but the gap between a generalist and a specialist opens here.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain families often discover mid-Year 10 that their child is being taught Core and Extended content in the same room, with differentiation left to worksheets. That is the most common reason a local search starts, and it is a specification problem rather than a proximity problem.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examined year
programmes.description: Proximity is now worth least and specification match worth most. The work is paper technique against a known mark scheme: command terms, timing, and the two or three question types the student reliably drops. A tutor who has not marked against the board's own scheme cannot see which word was missing from an answer that scored two of three.
programmes.countryNote: Availability in Al Ain tightens sharply in the ten weeks before a series, and so does the market. A distance-first search in April returns whoever still has slots, which is the weakest possible selection criterion at the point when selection matters most.

programmes.name: AS, A Level and the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: At this level the local pool thins to almost nothing for most subjects. A Higher Level Diploma science or an A Level further maths tutor is a specialist job, and the number of people in Al Ain who have taught the current specification is small. Distance-based searching at this stage reliably produces a mismatch.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain offers fewer Diploma Programme places than Abu Dhabi island, so students wanting a particular Higher Level combination sometimes commute or change school. Planning that from Year 10, with the IGCSE grades it needs, is far cheaper than discovering it in Year 11.

al-ain/igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: The honest answer to a local search varies enormously by subject. These are the IGCSE subjects Al Ain families search for, and what the local supply position actually looks like in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: The one subject where a local search usually works, because the pool is the largest in the city. Even here, ask which route and tier the tutor has taught: 0580 requires a non-calculator paper and 4MA1 does not tier the same way.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606), Further Pure (Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: The thinnest local pool of any IGCSE subject in Al Ain. Cohorts of a handful per school mean very few teachers in the city have taken it through a series. A distance-first search here reliably returns a willing generalist rather than a specialist.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Reasonable local supply at Core level, thinner at Extended. Ask specifically about Paper 6 Alternative to Practical, which is 20% of a Cambridge Extended grade and which many general science tutors have never taught as a component.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Similar local picture to Physics. The subject contains three separate problems, moles calculations, qualitative analysis and organic patterns, and a tutor strong on one is not automatically strong on the others. Ask which they teach most often.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The best-supplied science locally, and the one where general teaching helps least. Most lost marks are command-term failures rather than knowledge gaps, which needs someone who reads mark schemes rather than someone who knows biology.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Widely taught in Al Ain because triple science blocks are small, and widely misunderstood by tutors who prepare candidates with single-science papers. Ask directly whether they have taught 0654 rather than 0625, 0620 or 0610.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Good local supply and a subject where proximity genuinely helps younger students. The exercises are predictable and unforgiving about following instructions, so marked timed practice matters more than the teaching venue.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reasonable local supply, variable quality. The test is whether the tutor talks about the mark scheme split between structure and expression, or about reading more widely. Only one of those answers earns marks in June.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478, 0417)
subjects.description: Thin locally, and the two subjects are routinely confused with each other. Computer Science needs pseudocode and trace tables; ICT needs timed software technique. Ask which code, then ask what they have taught, in that order.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Moderate local supply. The useful skill is case-study technique and reaching the evaluation mark at the end of a long question, which is where most candidates stop. General business knowledge does not substitute for it.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as an Additional Language (Cambridge 0508, 0544)
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Local supply exists but is often matched by subject name rather than by route. These are separate specifications with separate demands, and a first-language tutor teaching a foreign-language candidate is the common mismatch.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460, 0470)
subjects.description: Thin locally at IGCSE level. Both are source-handling and structured-recall subjects where the loss is structural: students answer the question they revised rather than the one printed. Essay planning under time is the intervention.

al-ain/igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: In a city as spread out as Al Ain, near me means something different in each district. These are the areas families search from and what the local answer realistically looks like.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: The densest part of the city and the one place where a distance-first search returns a reasonable list, because several long-established campuses sit close by. Even so, the list is of nearby tutors, not of tutors who teach your syllabus code.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh and Al Khabisi
regions.note: Central-west districts with mixed curriculum catchments. Households here often have two children at different schools on different boards, which is precisely the situation a single nearby tutor cannot usually cover.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza and Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Established villa districts west of the centre. The drive from the central school belt is short enough that local arrangements work, and long enough that a travel premium appears in the rate without being itemised.

regions.name: Hili and Al Qattara
regions.note: Northern districts with longer bus routes, so children arrive home late and local tutors arrive later. A near-me search here tends to return a shorter list than the same search in Al Jimi, for no reason other than density.

regions.name: Al Towayya and Asharej
regions.note: Close to the university quarter, so the nearby pool includes a high proportion of university students. That is a legitimate budget-tier option for Year 9 and Year 10 support and a weak one for an Extended exam-year subject.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: A spread-out southern district where local supply thins quickly for specialist subjects. Families here are the most likely to find that the nearest suitable tutor is not near at all, which is where the online shortlist does its work.

regions.name: Al Maqam and Al Yahar
regions.note: The outlying districts. A tutor's round trip from the centre can exceed the lesson, so a local search returns either a very small list or a rate that quietly prices the journey. A no-journey slot from 4.30pm is the practical alternative.

regions.name: Al Foah and Al Sarooj
regions.note: Northern and central districts with fewer private-school catchments nearby. A near-me search returns few results, and the useful response is to widen the filter from distance to specification rather than to accept the nearest option.

schoolClusters.note: These schools run IGCSE into AS and A Level or into the Diploma Programme. This is the structural reason a near-me search works for maths and fails for Additional Mathematics.

sections.heading: What a near-me search returns in Al Ain, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: A distance-sorted search answers a question about geography. It returns businesses and individuals who have claimed a location, filled in a profile and in many cases paid for visibility, ranked roughly by how close that claimed location is to your pin. None of those inputs is correlated with whether the person has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1. The list is real, but it is a list of availability and marketing, not a list of specification experience.

What it leaves out is everything that decides the outcome. It does not tell you which board the tutor has taught, which tier or route, or whether they have ever marked against the published mark scheme for your child's paper. It does not tell you whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It does not distinguish between a university student in Asharej who is excellent with a Year 9 and a subject specialist who can see which single word was missing from an answer that scored two marks out of three.

There is also a quieter omission. A near-me list cannot tell you that the subject you need has almost no local pool, because an empty result looks the same as a result the algorithm chose not to show. A parent in Zakher searching for Additional Mathematics help sees three nearby tutors who teach maths and reasonably concludes the problem is solved. The three may never have opened an 0606 paper. The list has no way to say so and no incentive to.

The fix is to change the filter, not to search harder. Replace distance with the syllabus code, then ask about availability in your one realistic slot, then ask about the permit, then ask about the rate. That order matters: a cheap, nearby, available tutor who has not taught the specification is not a bargain, it is a term of hours aimed at the wrong paper structure. A specialist on live video who is twenty minutes from nowhere in particular is the same lesson without the drive.

sections.heading: The tutor-pool arithmetic nobody writes down
paragraphs: This is the section that makes the rest of the page concrete. Work from cohort size. A subject taught to a handful of candidates per year group at a handful of schools produces, over a decade, a small number of teachers in the city who have taken it through a full series. Some have left the country, some no longer tutor, and some are barred from tutoring the students who most need them because ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

Subtract those and the pool for a thin-cohort subject in Al Ain is genuinely small. That is not a criticism of the city; it is arithmetic that applies to any smaller market, and it is the reason the brief for this city notes that Higher Level Diploma sciences and the less common languages are the usual gaps. The same arithmetic runs the other way for mathematics and for the sciences at Core level, where every school has large cohorts and the local pool is comfortable.

The practical consequence is that the right answer to a local search differs by subject rather than by family. For 0580 maths, a local arrangement is perfectly reasonable and you should choose on specification fluency rather than on distance. For 0606, 0478 or a less common language, the realistic choice is between a generalist nearby and a specialist on screen, and the generalist costs more in the end because the hours produce less.

The table sets this out subject by subject. The availability column describes the realistic local position in Al Ain rather than a promise about any particular week, and the final column is what we actually do when the local answer is no: disclose it, give a match time, and say where the tutor would be teaching from. No competitor page found in research discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to overseas numbers without mentioning it.

sections.heading: The four options an Al Ain family is actually choosing between
paragraphs: A near-me search presents one option: a person nearby. In reality there are four, and three of them rarely appear in a distance-sorted list at all. The first is the school's own support, which is free and underused. Many Al Ain schools run subject clinics, catch-up sessions or a lunchtime maths room, and the teacher running them knows the scheme of work better than any outsider will. The reason to start here is not cost, it is information: a conversation with the subject teacher tells you what the school thinks the problem is.

The second is a tuition centre, which trades attention for price. Group classes are priced well below one-to-one and work when a whole cohort needs the same coverage in the same order, which suits breadth revision. They work poorly for a diagnosed individual weakness, because the pace cannot stop on your child's specific error. Note also that a centre with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the relevant education authority, which is a different instrument from an individual tutor's permit, and is worth asking about.

The third is an independent local tutor, which is what the search was looking for. Done well this is excellent, particularly for younger students and for mainstream subjects. The things to establish are the ones the listing does not show: the syllabus code they have taught, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, who replaces them if they leave the country mid-term, and what happens to your money if a session is missed. Independent arrangements usually have no replacement mechanism, which matters more in a smaller city.

The fourth is an online specialist, which is what this platform provides. The trade is explicit: you give up a person in the room and you gain a shortlist drawn from everyone who has taught the code. sections.heading: Why the tutor who transformed your neighbour's son may do nothing for your daughter
paragraphs: Recommendations travel faster than any search result in Al Ain, and they are usually the reason a family picks a particular tutor. They are worth listening to and worth interrogating, because a recommendation carries almost no information about transferability. What the neighbour is reporting is the outcome of one specific match: that tutor, that subject, that board, that loss pattern, that child's temperament, in that term.

Change any one of those and the result changes. A tutor who moved a student from a 5 to a 7 in Cambridge Biology 0610 was almost certainly fixing a command-term problem, because that is the dominant loss pattern in that subject and it responds quickly. Point the same tutor at a student with genuine content gaps across 0620 Chemistry and the work is completely different, slower and less suited to their strength. The recommendation was accurate and the inference from it is wrong.

Board is the next trap. Cambridge Extended sciences use a multiple-choice paper worth 30%, an extended theory paper worth 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical worth 20%, while Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them. A tutor fluent in one may be fluent in both, but the neighbour's recommendation does not tell you which, and in Al Ain plenty of households sit different boards.

So convert the recommendation into questions rather than treating it as a verdict. Which subject and which code did they teach your child? What was actually going wrong, in the tutor's own words? What changed, and how did you know? Was it a short block or a year? A neighbour who can answer those has given you something genuinely useful. A neighbour who says the tutor was wonderful has given you a starting point for a trial lesson, which is where the question gets settled anyway.

sections.heading: What proximity genuinely buys, stated fairly
paragraphs: It would be easy to write this page as a case against local tutoring and dishonest to do so. Proximity buys several real things, and for some families they are decisive. The first is presence with a younger or easily distracted student. A person in the room notices the moment attention goes and can act on it without the student being able to hide behind a muted microphone. For Years 7 to 9, that is often the whole value of the arrangement.

The second is the physical craft of written subjects. Handwriting, calculator fluency, the layout of a long maths answer, how to annotate a source, how to manage a paper's physical pages under time pressure: these are easier to correct sitting beside someone. A good online tutor works around this with a shared whiteboard, a stylus and photographed work annotated live, and most of the gap closes. It does not close entirely, and saying so is more useful than pretending.

The third is household visibility. Some parents want to see the session happening, and that is a legitimate preference rather than a lack of trust. Online delivery answers it differently, with annotated work saved and sent after each session and a short written note of what was covered and set, which is a more durable record than overhearing an hour. Different, not worse, and a family entitled to prefer the room should prefer the room.

What proximity does not buy is specification experience, mark-scheme fluency, availability in the one slot your family can hold, or a replacement when the tutor leaves. In Al Ain, with a smaller pool and a wide geography, those four are usually what is actually limiting. The decision is therefore not online against local in the abstract. It is this subject, this year, this child: a Year 8 in Al Jimi who needs supervision, or a Year 11 in Al Yahar who needs someone who has taught 0606.

sections.heading: How far near me actually stretches across Al Ain
paragraphs: Al Ain is a low-density city, and the districts families live in sit minutes apart on a map and considerably further apart in a tutor's evening. The practical radius for an in-person arrangement is not a distance, it is a round trip that a tutor will repeat weekly for a term after already teaching all day. Once the round trip exceeds the lesson, the arrangement becomes fragile: sessions drift later, cancellations rise, and the rate rises to compensate.

The second constraint is the school run. Bus routes in a spread-out city are long, so a child in Hili or Al Yahar can arrive home close to an hour after a child who left the same campus for Al Jimi. That compresses the window in which an in-person session can start, and it compresses it exactly where the drive is longest. The two constraints multiply rather than add.

The third is the sequencing problem no parent sees. A local tutor with three evening sessions has to leave for the second before knowing whether the first will overrun. In central districts that absorbs; from Al Jimi to Al Maqam it does not. This is why in-person arrangements in outlying Al Ain districts tend to settle into later and later slots across a term, and why the family that agreed 5pm in September is sitting down at 6.15pm by February.

The table gives a planning view. The online-start column is the earliest slot a family can hold every week for a term with no journey in the way, which is the only start time worth agreeing to. Treat the in-person column as a judgement about reliability rather than about possibility: almost anything is possible once.

sections.heading: Checking a local tutor in one message
paragraphs: If you do hire locally, the checks are quick and almost nobody makes them. Start with the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a published two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Two quick tests follow. A tutor who says the permit is expensive has not applied, because it is free. A tutor who says it takes months has not applied either, because the published completion time is two working days. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published by the ministry, so any specific amount quoted to you is unsourced, and none appears on this page.

Then the Al Ain-specific check. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. The MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current ADEK policy document, so verify the wording with ADEK, but do not pursue the arrangement in any case.

Finally the commercial questions, which are the ones that cause the most grief later. Is the rate per hour or per session, because a 90-minute session quoted as an hourly figure is a large difference hiding in plain sight. What happens to a missed session, and who absorbs a cancellation. Does the quoted figure include any tax the provider is obliged to charge, which is a question for the provider rather than for a web page, since UAE tax treatment should be confirmed against the Federal Tax Authority. And if a trial is described as free, what the length, eligibility and conditions actually are.

sections.heading: Five questions that beat a map pin
paragraphs: Replace the distance filter with five questions and the search gets shorter and better. First: which syllabus code have you taught, and for how many series? A specialist names 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher without hesitating and says how recently. A generalist says they teach maths. Both answers are honest; only one of them is a match for an exam-year candidate.

Second: what are the components on this specification and what is each worth? For a Cambridge Extended science that is a multiple-choice paper at 30%, a theory paper at 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20%. For Pearson 4PH1 it is two written papers with practicals assessed inside them. A tutor who has to look this up has not taught the paper, which is a fact worth knowing before you book, not after.

Third: given this marked paper, where is my child losing marks and which is cheapest to fix? This is the question that separates tutors most sharply, and it needs the artefact in hand. A specialist separates a knowledge gap from a command-term failure, a timing problem or accuracy under pressure, and says which to attack first. Fourth: what is your availability in the one slot we can actually hold, every week, for a term? An excellent tutor with the wrong slot is not available.

Fifth, and the one that tells you most: what would make you tell me my child does not need tutoring in this subject? A tutor with an answer is thinking about your child. A tutor without one is thinking about the booking. Ask all five in a free trial lesson rather than over messages, and ask the fifth last, when the answer costs them something.

process.description: Fix a review point four to six weeks out and decide now what evidence it will use: marked whole papers compared side by side, not impressions. Build in the option to reduce or stop, so continuing is a decision someone makes rather than the default that happens.

faqs.question: Why does searching for a tutor near me in Al Ain return so few useful results?
faqs.answer: Because the search sorts by claimed location and visibility, and because Al Ain's private-school set is smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so the local teaching pool in any specialised subject is genuinely small. A subject taught to a handful of candidates per year group at a handful of schools produces very few teachers in the city who have taken it through a series. For mathematics and Core sciences the local pool is comfortable. For Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 or a less common language, a distance-first search tends to return willing generalists rather than specialists.

faqs.question: Should I try my child's school before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families skip it. Many Al Ain schools run subject clinics, catch-up sessions or a lunchtime help room, and the teacher running them knows the scheme of work better than any outsider will. The reason to start there is information as much as cost: a conversation with the subject teacher tells you what the school thinks is going wrong, which is a useful second opinion against your own. What you should not do is ask your child's own teacher to tutor them privately, which ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit for students enrolled at that teacher's school.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives nearby cheaper than an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Usually the reverse. Published UAE in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and budget-tier online rates have been published from around AED 45 to AED 150. Proximity adds travel to the hour whether or not it is itemised, and in outlying Al Ain districts it adds more. Those are market observations read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who published them, not IB Gram prices; our rate is agreed after a free trial and a match.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child needs a specialist or just supervision?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked paper. A student whose answers are broadly right but who did not finish, or who loses marks to dropped units and sign errors, often needs structure and a checking routine more than expertise, and a budget-tier tutor or even a well-run homework routine can deliver that. A student whose answers score two marks out of four despite being knowledgeable has a command-term problem, which needs someone who reads mark schemes. Blank responses clustered on particular topics mean content gaps and ordered coverage. Those are three different purchases at three different prices.

faqs.question: What should I ask a local Al Ain tutor before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Five things. Which syllabus code have you taught, and how recently. What are the components on it and what is each worth. Given this marked paper, where is my child losing marks and which loss is cheapest to fix. Are you free in the one slot we can hold every week for a whole term. And what would make you tell me we should stop. Add the permit question: ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge, valid for two years and has a published two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: My neighbour's tutor was excellent for her son, so why might that not work for us?
faqs.answer: Because a recommendation reports one match rather than a general capability. The tutor who moved a student from a 5 to a 7 in Cambridge Biology 0610 was most likely fixing a command-term problem, which responds quickly. Point them at genuine content gaps in Chemistry 0620 and the work is slower and less suited to their strength. Board matters too, since Cambridge Extended sciences carry Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20% while Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Convert the recommendation into questions about code, problem and evidence, then settle it in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre in Al Ain count as a tutor near me?
faqs.answer: It is a different product rather than a nearer version of the same one. Group classes are priced well below one-to-one and work when a whole cohort needs the same coverage in the same order, which suits breadth revision before a series. They work poorly for a diagnosed individual weakness, because the pace cannot stop on your child's particular error. One practical check: a centre operating with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the relevant education authority, which is a different instrument from an individual tutor's permit, so ask which they hold.

faqs.question: What happens if a local tutor leaves Al Ain halfway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: With an independent arrangement, you restart the search in the worst possible month, and in a city with a thin pool in your subject that can take weeks. This is the risk nobody discusses at the start and the one that does the most damage, because the replacement has to rebuild the diagnosis from scratch. It is worth asking any independent tutor directly what their plan is if their circumstances change. Where a platform made the match, a different specialist in the same specification can be proposed without the family starting again.

faqs.question: Is a university student in Asharej a reasonable tutor for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For the right job, yes. University students are eligible to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and published budget-tier rates of roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour make them an efficient choice for Year 9 and Year 10 structure, homework accountability and basic topic revision. They are a weak choice for exam-year work on an Extended or Higher tier paper, where the value comes from mark-scheme fluency and knowing which single word was missing from an answer. Match the tier of tutor to the tier of problem rather than to the budget alone.

faqs.question: How late can a weekly session start in an outlying Al Ain district?
faqs.answer: Later than most families plan for, which is why so many arrangements drift. School buses in a spread-out city run long routes, so a child in Al Yahar or Hili can arrive home close to an hour after a child who left the same campus for Al Jimi. Add thirty minutes for food and the realistic start is 5.30pm or 6pm. With no journey involved, a 4.30pm slot becomes practical in those same districts, and the slot that matters is the one the family can hold every week for a term, not the earliest one they can manage once.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor correct handwriting, layout and calculator technique?
faqs.answer: Mostly, and this is the fairest thing to say about the format's limits. A shared whiteboard with a stylus lets a tutor watch working appear stroke by stroke, which is better diagnosis than reading a finished answer, and handwritten school work photographed before the session can be annotated live. Calculator sequences can be demonstrated on screen. What does not transfer completely is the physical management of a paper under time pressure, which is best rehearsed by sitting whole past papers at home under exam conditions and sending them in to be marked.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates tutoring in Al Ain, and does it vet tutors for me?
faqs.answer: No authority vets individual tutors on a parent's behalf. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain, and MoHRE issues the private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Neither sets what a tutor may charge you, and neither publishes a directory of approved individuals. The checks are yours to make: ask for the permit, ask about the syllabus code, and settle the commercial terms in writing. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of these bodies and claims none.

faqs.question: Is it worth running trial lessons with several IGCSE tutors at once?
faqs.answer: One, if the first trial produces a real diagnosis; two if it does not. The point of a trial is not to compare personalities, it is to find out whether someone can read a marked paper and tell you where the marks are going. A tutor who does that convincingly is worth starting with, and the arrangement can be reviewed on evidence four to six weeks later. Trialling four tutors costs a fortnight of a Year 11 term, which is a real cost in the spring, and comparison on charm rather than diagnosis tends to pick the most confident rather than the most useful.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have a tutor based in Al Ain who can come to us?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE and has no office, centre or branch in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Ain families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason we work this way in a city like Al Ain is supply: the shortlist is drawn from every tutor who has taught your child's syllabus code rather than from those who can reach Zakher or Al Maqam by six, and no session depends on a journey that traffic can ruin.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful thing to send when asking about a tutor?
faqs.answer: One recently marked school paper, with the marks and comments still on it, plus the syllabus code and the series your child is entered for. That combination lets a specialist say something specific in the first conversation rather than describing their approach. It also tells you quickly whether you are talking to someone who teaches the paper: a specialist reads the paper and names the loss pattern, while a generalist reads it and describes the subject. Everything else, rate, slot, frequency, follows more easily once that is settled.

al-ain/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Change the filter, then take the trial
al-ain/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If a search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Al Ain has returned a short and unconvincing list, the problem is usually the filter rather than the city. Send the syllabus code, the series and one recently marked paper, and name the single slot your household can hold every week for a term. We will come back with a specialist who has taught that code, a diagnosis of where the marks are going, and an honest view of how many sessions it needs, including the option that it needs none. The trial lesson is free, lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the annotated work from each session is saved and sent to you.

al-ain/zakher.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the stages that come up together in Zakher households: Diploma mathematics and sciences for the eldest, IGCSE sciences and mathematics in the middle, and focused primary number and reading work where a younger sibling has a specific gap rather than a general need.

intro.heading: Three or four children, one evening, one dining table
paragraphs: Zakher spreads across the southern edge of Al Ain, past the oasis belt and out towards the farms and the road to the mountain. Plots here are large, houses are generous and the streets are quiet, which is why families with several children choose it. The trade is distance: the school buses run long routes to collect a full load from a low-density district, and children here are among the last dropped off in the city despite the modest figure on a map.

The defining feature of enquiries from Zakher is not the journey, though. It is the number of children. A household with four school-age children spread across primary, the middle years, an IGCSE examination year and the Diploma has four different academic problems, four different sets of deadlines and one evening in which to deal with all of them. Advice written for a single-child household is close to useless here, because the binding constraint is not money or motivation. It is hours and table space.

What makes this harder is that the four stages have genuinely different needs, and the loudest need is rarely the most urgent. The Diploma student with an internal assessment due makes the most noise. The Year 11 student in an examination year has the most at stake in the shortest timeframe. The middle-years child is at the stage where a small intervention has the longest-lasting effect. The primary child needs twenty minutes of arithmetic, not an hour of tuition, and usually gets either nothing or far too much.

There is also a budget question that families in this district ask more directly than most, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a brochure. Four children cannot each have two weekly sessions, and attempting it produces eight appointments a week, a household that resents the calendar and four partial relationships that improve nothing measurably. The better arrangement is uneven on purpose: one child taught properly, one child's specific gap closed in a block, and two children left alone with a clear reason.

This page therefore works through the household rather than the subject. It sets out who lives here and what the stage spread does to an evening, what each stage needs and what it does not, how to stack the week so the slots survive to March, when sharing a tutor between siblings works and when it fails, and what the whole arrangement costs with the market figures attributed. It then covers the long bus run and the decisions that protect the younger children's options.

Everything described is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE and nobody will be sent to a Zakher address; home visiting is an India-only service. In a household with several children the online format has one unglamorous practical advantage: two sessions can run in the same house at the same time, in different rooms, which is impossible with a visiting tutor and is often the only way the week fits together.

The loudest need is rarely the most urgent one
An uneven plan beats an equal one in a multi-child household

al-ain/zakher.programmesIntro: A Zakher household frequently spans the whole continuum at once, which is why this section describes each stage by how much adult attention it genuinely requires rather than by its educational philosophy.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units assessed by teacher judgement with no external papers, reported against learning outcomes and approaches to learning. A parent can read two reports and still not know whether their child can subtract reliably or read fluently for ten minutes, which is the genuine weakness of the format from a household's point of view.
programmes.countryNote: In a busy Zakher household the primary child is the one most likely to be either ignored or over-tutored. What they need is short and specific: number fluency, reading stamina and handwriting speed. Twenty focused minutes several times a week beats an hour on a Sunday, and almost none of it needs a tutor if somebody at home has the time.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade. Criteria assess skills rather than topics, so a low score points at a process. The Personal Project closes the programme and is the first long independent deadline most students manage themselves.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where a small intervention has the longest effect and the smallest audience. A middle-years child in a household containing an examination candidate and a Diploma student gets whatever attention is left, which is usually none. One term of work on written structure here saves two years of remediation later.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by terminal papers, tiered in several subjects, with the entry tier setting the grade ceiling before a paper is sat. Cambridge syllabuses carry codes such as 0580 and 0620; Pearson uses forms like 4MA1 and 4CH1. Both award marks against command terms and visible method.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 11 child in a Zakher household has the shortest runway and the clearest stakes, which usually makes them the right recipient of the one properly resourced weekly slot. The tier decision is worth checking early, because it is made by the school and caps the available grade regardless of how the year goes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at two levels with internal assessments throughout, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Internal assessment typically carries twenty to thirty per cent of a subject grade. The programme assumes a substantial independent working week, which is the resource a crowded household has least of.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in a house with three younger siblings has a space problem before they have an academic problem. On a large Zakher plot there is usually a room that can be theirs for two hours, and establishing that is worth more than a tutoring hour. Where it is not possible, the local library or a university sibling's desk sometimes is.

al-ain/zakher.subjectsIntro: Requests from this district arrive in clusters rather than singly, because a household asks about two or three children at once. The entries below are the subjects that recur, with the specific thing that needs fixing at each stage.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus and proof with a Higher Level paper that assumes fluent manipulation. Method marks go missing when a student works mentally and writes only answers. The exploration needs a topic that can genuinely be modelled, chosen early rather than in the final term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and heavy calculator work. Interpretation sentences cost the most marks: a correct test followed by a conclusion that ignores the context. Three sessions on interpretation typically move more marks than ten on new content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level load. Calculations are lost to presentation as much as to method, and internal assessments fail on investigations with no real independent variable. Both are fixable without laboratory access.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and the practical skills component take most recoverable marks. Explanation questions need a causal chain in order, and a list of correct facts in the wrong sequence scores poorly however accurate it is.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume subject, where rereading is most common and least effective. Retrieval practice against past questions marked to the scheme is what moves the grade, and statistical treatment is reliably the weakest area on arrival.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The tier decides the ceiling, so establish which paper the school has entered your child for. Multi-step questions escalate inside a single question, and students who stop at the first unfamiliar part leave the accessible marks behind.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and qualitative analysis carry the paper. A student who can define a term but cannot lay out a calculation loses marks steadily across both papers, and structured working is the faster repair.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical component are the usual sites of loss. The alternative-to-practical paper is trainable on paper: reading apparatus, identifying variables and processing an untidy result table are all coachable skills.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Command terms decide this paper more than any other science at the level. Describe, explain, suggest and compare each want a different shape of answer, and confusing them costs whole grades across a full paper.

subjects.name: English First Language and Literature
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and analysis at a register most students have not been asked for. The gap is paragraph architecture rather than vocabulary, and six to eight weeks of marked writing usually moves it noticeably.

subjects.name: MYP mathematics and science criteria work
subjects.description: The highest-leverage stage and the quietest one. Learning to read a criterion descriptor and compare it against your own answer at thirteen pays off every year afterwards, and it needs a rubric and an hour rather than a course.

subjects.name: Primary number fluency and reading stamina
subjects.description: Short, specific and frequently over-bought. Twenty minutes of arithmetic several times a week, or ten minutes of sustained reading aloud, does more than an hour-long tuition session, and much of it can be done by a parent or an older sibling.

al-ain/zakher.modesIntro: Three patterns fit a multi-child household, and they are chosen by which child the hours should go to rather than by subject. All three are one-to-one over live video, which is what allows two of them to run in the same house at once.

modes.title: One child resourced properly, the others left alone
modes.description: The arrangement that works and the one families resist because it feels unfair. One child, usually the one with the shortest runway and the clearest stakes, gets a weekly specialist hour for the year. The others get a stated reason for why they are not being tutored, which is a more useful thing to receive than a diluted half hour.

modes.title: A short block for a named gap
modes.description: Four to six sessions aimed at one specific weakness in one child, with a defined end. A middle-years child who cannot structure a written answer, or a Year 10 student whose algebra is not secure enough for Extended tier, is a block rather than a standing arrangement. Blocks end, which is what keeps a household budget intact.
bullets: A named gap, a session count and a finish date agreed at the start

modes.title: Parallel sessions in different rooms
modes.description: Two children, two tutors, two rooms, the same hour. On a large Zakher plot this is usually achievable and it halves the number of evenings the household gives up. It is only possible because the lessons are online, which is a practical argument for the format rather than a philosophical one.

sections.heading: Who lives in Zakher, and what the stage spread does to an evening
paragraphs: Large plots and quiet streets attract large families, and enquiries from this district reflect that. Where a Dubai apartment household typically asks about one child, a Zakher household asks about two, three or four, and often across the full range of stages. That changes the nature of the question entirely. The academic problems are ordinary; the problem of fitting four academic problems into one evening with one table and two capable adults is not.

The first thing worth doing is writing the household out as a grid: each child, their stage, their nearest deadline and the thing they currently most need. Done honestly, the grid usually produces a surprise. The child making the most noise is often the one whose need is least time-sensitive, and the quiet middle child turns out to be at the stage where intervention has the longest shelf life. Families rarely see this until it is written down.

The second is to accept that the plan will be uneven. Four children cannot each have two sessions a week: that is eight appointments, most of a budget, and a household that comes to dislike the whole arrangement by December. An uneven plan concentrates resource where it changes an outcome and tells the other children why, which children handle better than adults expect when the reason is specific rather than financial.

The table below sets out the household shapes that recur in this district with the characteristic evening problem each one produces. Recognising your own row is useful because the fix differs: a household with two examination candidates has a scheduling problem, while a household with one Diploma student and three young children has a space and attention problem, and those need different solutions.

sections.heading: What each stage needs now, and what it does not
paragraphs: Spending decisions become much easier once each stage is described by what genuinely moves an outcome at that age. The common error in a multi-child household is to treat all four children as needing the same product at different levels of difficulty, which produces four weekly hours and no visible change. In practice two of the four stages are better served by something other than a weekly tutoring hour.

At primary level the needs are short and specific: arithmetic fluency, reading stamina and handwriting speed. Twenty minutes several times a week does more than a sixty-minute session once, and much of it can be delivered by a parent or an older sibling with a clear instruction. Buying an hour a week for a Year 4 child with no identified gap is the single commonest waste in a household budget, and it also uses the slot a Year 11 sibling needs.

The middle years are the highest-leverage stage and the easiest to neglect. A child who learns to read a criterion descriptor and compare it against their own answer at thirteen carries that skill through IGCSE, the Diploma and beyond. One term of work on written structure here costs less than remediating the same weakness in Year 11, when the runway is short and the stakes are immediate. This is the stage a crowded household should protect deliberately.

The examination years are where depth matters. A Year 11 or Year 13 student needs a specialist in a named subject, weekly, with work marked against the published scheme. That is the expensive product and it is worth what it costs, which is why the arithmetic in a multi-child household usually resolves to one child getting this and the others getting blocks or nothing. The table attaches rough weekly hours to each stage so the total can be checked against the household's actual capacity.
