best-ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes, and UAE schools licence them in different combinations. Knowing which one a child is in decides what tuition can usefully do, because the assessment model changes completely between them. Each note below says what the UAE school system adds on top of the IB's own requirements.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and reporting is based on teacher judgement against the programme's learning outcomes rather than on marks. Support at this stage is about literacy, number fluency and the habits that make a Middle Years transition survivable: reading stamina, written structure, and comfort with being asked to explain a method rather than produce an answer.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, a PYP child already carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies on the timetable, streamed separately for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Families often discover the Arabic stream only when the first report arrives. Getting the stream right early is cheaper than correcting it in Year 7.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is assessed against criteria lettered A to D in each subject, scored out of 8 per criterion, with grade boundaries applied to the total. Those letters are the grammar of the whole programme, and most lost marks come from writing an answer that never addresses the criterion being tested. Optional eAssessment in Year 11 gives an externally moderated result for schools that choose it.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 then switch to IGCSE, which means a child can meet two assessment systems in three years. A Middle Years student heading for the Diploma in a UAE school needs the criterion habit intact; a child heading for IGCSE needs the opposite reflex, because mark schemes reward different things.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is scored out of 7, with up to three further points from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, to a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the pass threshold, subject to the IB's conditions on failing grades and core components.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE Diploma student carries the compulsory Ministry subjects on top of six IB courses, so the week is tighter than the IB's own guided-hours figures suggest. Registration for the session is made by the school, not the family, and the Diploma then needs a Ministry of Education equivalency file before it can be used for a UAE university application.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, plus a core of personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project. It suits a student who wants Diploma-level subject rigour in two or three areas without the full six-subject load, and it is assessed through a mix of IB examinations and the career-related provider's own assessment.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is licensed by only a small number of UAE schools, so a family that wants it is usually choosing a school as much as a programme. Tuition for a CP student is normally concentrated on the Diploma courses inside it, because those carry the externally examined marks that universities read.

best-ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses UAE families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses. The description matters more than the subject name: a tutor who knows Mathematics in general is not the same as one who knows where the Applications and Interpretation papers differ from Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with a no-calculator paper at both levels. Higher Level adds depth across the same five topic areas and a third paper of extended problem-solving. Marks are lost in the move between a correct method and a justified conclusion, and in the exploration where modelling is left unexamined.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference. Students who chose this route to avoid proof are often surprised by how much interpretation of output the papers ask for in words rather than symbols.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and nuclear physics, with Higher Level extending the same chapters rather than adding separate ones. The scientific investigation and the data-based questions reward uncertainty handling, which is the single most commonly undertaught part of the course in a crowded UAE timetable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across organic, physical and inorganic topics, with multi-step calculation under time pressure. Higher Level work on organic mechanisms and energetics separates grades. The internal investigation asks for a research design that can actually be run, and weak designs cap the mark long before the data is analysed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, interaction and interdependence, across molecular to ecosystem scales. The volume of content tempts memorisation, but the papers reward applying a named mechanism to an unfamiliar context. Command terms do most of the damage here: outline, explain and justify ask for three different answers of three different lengths.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through extended response and a portfolio of three commentaries on published articles. Higher Level adds quantitative demands and a policy paper. Diagram accuracy is worth more than most students expect, and an unlabelled axis costs marks no amount of prose recovers.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with case-study examinations and a written commentary. Tools are examined as analysis, not recall, so a student who can define a framework but cannot apply it to the case loses the top band. Financial calculation is the fastest place to recover marks before a session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, assessed through guided analysis, a comparative essay, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a separate essay on a studied work. Students who read well but write loosely sit in the middle bands; structure and a controlled line of inquiry move them up.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across the IB's prescribed themes. For UAE families this course usually runs beside the school's own compulsory Arabic lessons, which follow Ministry content rather than the IB's. Keeping the two separate in a child's head is a real part of the work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking and a solution developed for a real client. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study set annually. The solution component fails most often on documentation and testing evidence rather than on code, which is where a review session earns its fee.

best-ib-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Which authority sits above your child's school, emirate by emirate
best-ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Tuition plans in the UAE are shaped by the emirate more than by the neighbourhood, because the emirate decides who licenses, inspects and in some cases approves the assessment your child sits. Here is the practical position in each, with what it changes for a family buying private lessons.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees private education quality here and publishes the mandatory-subject requirements that apply whatever curriculum a school holds. With 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, two children on the same street can sit entirely different papers.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An IB Diploma tutor in Abu Dhabi should never be your child's own class teacher taking cash.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under the same Abu Dhabi authority as the capital, but with a smaller IB cohort and fewer Higher Level sets per school. That is precisely the situation where a drive-time search returns a tutor for the subject you did not need and nobody for the one you did.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. An IB Higher Level tutor in Sharjah therefore works to a syllabus that has been cleared locally as well as by the board.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education here is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families routinely drive to Dubai or Sharjah for subject help; over live video that drive stops being part of the cost of a Tuesday evening.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Ajman's private schools fall to the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Many Ajman Diploma students commute into Sharjah or Dubai for school, so a session rarely starts before 6pm on a weekday.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The IB cohort is small enough that a single Higher Level option can run with a handful of students, which makes a specialist outside the emirate the realistic option rather than the fallback.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education, on the opposite coast from the Dubai school cluster. Nobody is driving a Physics Higher Level specialist over the mountains twice a week at a sensible price, which is the clearest case in the country for teaching live over video.

sections.heading: Best IB home tutor in the UAE: what is fixed, and what is actually yours to choose
paragraphs: Treat the search as a shortlist problem and you will compare the wrong things. Most of what determines whether a child's Diploma goes well was decided by an institution: the emirate regulator that licensed the school, the board that administers the papers, the Ministry rule that puts three extra subjects on the timetable, and the option blocks that decided which Higher Levels were even available. None of those move because a better tutor was hired.

What does move is the quality of the match inside those constraints. A family choosing between two tutors is really choosing between two levels of syllabus knowledge, two levels of honesty about availability, and two formats with very different time costs. Those are worth comparing carefully. Whether a tutor lives in Jumeirah or in Mumbai is worth almost nothing once the lesson is delivered live over video.

sections.heading: Four authorities sit above a single IB lesson in the UAE
paragraphs: A Diploma lesson in Dubai looks like a private arrangement between two people. It is not. Five separate bodies have a say in what is taught, when it is examined and who may be paid to teach it, and each of them publishes its position. A provider that cannot name them is telling you something about how closely it has read the market it sells into.

The federal position is the baseline everything else sits on: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single sentence explains why an IB school in Ajman and a British school in Dubai both run the same three compulsory subjects, and why no international curriculum licence exempts a child from them.

Above the individual lesson sits the private tuition question. Paid private teaching in the UAE runs through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here. A parent may simply ask to see the permit before the first paid lesson.

sections.heading: A school sector adding places faster than it adds Higher Level teachers
paragraphs: The reason a Higher Level specialist is hard to book in a city this size is arithmetic rather than bad luck. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37% of the roll, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. The Diploma is a minority programme inside a very large market.

The sector is also growing. Six new private schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven more, four following the UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Three additional IB schools is good news for choice and awkward news for staffing, because experienced Higher Level teachers in the harder sciences and mathematics are the scarcest item in the system and new schools recruit from the same pool everybody else does.

Cost context has moved in the opposite direction. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A family's tutoring budget is not being compressed by a fee rise this year, which makes the planning question how to spend it well rather than whether to spend at all. The sensible move in a tightening staff market is to book the scarce subject early and treat the easier ones as the flexible part of the plan, rather than the other way round.

sections.heading: The subjects on the timetable that a private tutor may not redesign
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are not optional extras in a Dubai private school. They are mandatory regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma student that means three courses running beside six IB subjects and the core.

What surprises families is how prescriptive the rules are. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students runs primarily in Arabic; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further rules constrain what any outside tutor can honestly offer. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who arrives with a worksheet pack of their own for these courses is not adding value; they are working outside the rule the school has to follow. Instructional time, meanwhile, is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with lesson length allowed to vary provided the weekly total is met and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson.

paragraphs: Parents type home tutor because that is what the market has sold for twenty years in this region, and the phrase still describes the thing being bought: private, one-to-one teaching organised around the family's week rather than the school's. What has changed is that the delivery no longer requires somebody in the car. IB Gram delivers this as live one-to-one online tuition to families in all seven emirates, and home visits are a service offered in India only.

Said plainly: no IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE, in any emirate, at any price. That is a product decision and it has reasons a parent can check. A visiting tutor is selected from whoever teaches the subject within a tolerable drive; an online specialist is selected from everybody who has taught that syllabus at that level. For Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, those two pools are not close in size.

The time arithmetic is the other half of it. A visiting tutor usually needs a two-hour minimum because the travel has to be worth the trip, which forces a weekday session that starts late and ends later. A 60 or 90-minute video session fits between the school bus and dinner, survives a traffic day, and can move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan without anybody renegotiating a driving route. sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for each arrangement
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. Below are the AED bands actually published by providers selling into this market, read in October 2026, with the source named in every row. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

Read the bands as descriptions of what is inside the hour rather than as quality tiers. The low band usually buys supervised homework from someone with a good recent grade in the subject. The middle band usually buys a teacher who knows the paper structure and the mark scheme's language. The upper bands buy scarcity: a Higher Level specialist in a thin subject, or short-notice work in an exam term. Travel is the single biggest reason an in-home rate sits above an online one for the same teacher.

Monthly packages are where the arithmetic gets slippery. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and rate trackers put weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Divide any package by its teaching hours before comparing it with an hourly rate, and ask what happens to unused sessions. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and a free trial lesson rather than publishing a tariff, because the hours a child needs depend on the subject, the level and how far out you are starting.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and the hours each one actually needs
paragraphs: The level decision does more to a tutoring budget than the choice of tutor does, and it is usually made in a rush during an option-block meeting. The IB publishes guided teaching hours of 150 for a Standard Level course and 240 for a Higher Level one. That ninety-hour gap is roughly a term and a half of classroom time, which is why a student who switches up late cannot be caught up by six weeks of private lessons, however good they are.

Points behave differently from how families expect. Every subject is scored out of 7 whether it is taken at Higher or Standard Level, with up to three further points available from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Moving a struggling Higher Level down to Standard does not cost points directly. What it changes is which university courses will accept the profile afterwards, which is a question for the named university's own entry page rather than for a tutor.

Where tutoring earns its place is after the level is locked. Higher Level work is topic-specific: the extra material in a Higher Level science is depth inside the same chapters rather than separate units, so general revision does very little and targeted teaching does a lot. Standard Level students more often need exam technique, command-term discipline and timing, because the content load is manageable and the marks are lost in how answers are written rather than in what the student knows.

sections.heading: What each piece of internally assessed work is allowed to be
paragraphs: Internally assessed components are where a tutoring relationship either proves itself or becomes a liability for the student. The limits are published in the subject guides and they are limits, not targets: an Extended Essay stops at 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 on a prescribed title. Markers stop reading at the limit, so a student who writes past it has thrown away the best part of their argument.

Those limits move between syllabus versions, and a page that publishes them as permanent facts will eventually be wrong. Treat the table below as a working reference and confirm each figure against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, who holds the version the school is actually teaching. The marks matter as much as the word counts. The Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The sciences investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students lose most of their marks in the criteria that reward thinking about the work rather than doing it.

The boundary is simple to state and the thing most essay-selling competitors ignore. A tutor may discuss a research question, teach the criterion a student keeps missing, read one draft and give written feedback the student then acts on, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply paragraphs, process the data or edit a draft to a finished state. Your child's coordinator has to declare what outside help was used, and that declaration must be accurate. IB Gram works only on the teaching side of that line, and the most useful thing a provider can do for a worried parent is say so in writing before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Who owns each deadline in the exam year
paragraphs: Almost every date that matters in an exam year belongs to somebody other than the parent, and the most expensive mistakes are administrative rather than academic. The pattern is easiest to see on a Cambridge series a UAE candidate can actually sit. There are two of them, June and November, and in both the administrative work finishes long before the academic work does: the entry closes months ahead of the papers, the forecast grade is collected before them, and the results and certificates arrive on the board's schedule afterwards. Nobody in the family owns any of those dates. What a parent owns is the decision that feeds each one, and the window for making it is always earlier than the date itself suggests.

Read that sequence backwards and the planning becomes obvious. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper, which means tier and subject decisions have to be settled in the autumn term, while the mocks that justify a forecast grade have to be sat and marked before late February. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in, in writing.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, always work from the live official PDF rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. IGCSE exam entry deadlines in the UAE are set by the board and submitted by the school as examination centre, never by the family. For the IB's own session dates we publish nothing: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so ask your child's coordinator and work from what the school confirms in writing.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation: what the Ministry counts, and the number nobody should invent
paragraphs: A Diploma or a set of IGCSEs is not automatically usable for a UAE university application. The Ministry of Education runs an equivalency route that converts a foreign secondary certificate into something UAE institutions recognise, and the requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that rule are routinely got wrong by pages ranking for these queries. The first is the subject count: the reported requirement is five accredited subjects, and at least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents it is six. The second is what counts towards the five: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For MoE equivalency for IB students there is a deliberate blank on this page. The reporting we have read does not state an IB points threshold, and no figure should be published without reading it on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's own attestation channel. Nor is equivalency something a tutoring company performs or influences. It is a process a family completes with the Ministry, using documents the school issues. What tuition can legitimately do is prepare a child for the standardised tests the American track asks for, and make sure the certificate arriving in June is one worth attesting.

sections.heading: When nobody is free: what honest unavailability looks like
paragraphs: No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. The useful thing a provider can tell a parent is where it runs out, because a wasted trial lesson in an exam term costs more than the lesson. Our position on availability is published rather than implied, and it is the same whether you are in Dubai Marina or Dibba.

Supply is shaped by the same thing that shapes everything else here: cohort size. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most requested single slot in the country, and the 5pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics thin out quickly in the northern emirates, where a school may run the option for a handful of students. Arts subjects at Higher Level are barely covered by any UAE provider, ourselves included, and saying so early is more useful than a hopeful maybe.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, we match a Diploma teacher from our India-based teaching team, delivered over the same live video format, and we say that at the point of matching rather than after the first invoice. The syllabus, the board and the criteria do not change with the teacher's time zone; the session time sometimes does. Extended Essay supervision in the UAE remains with the school's own supervisor in every case, and what we provide around it is process coaching, not supervision.

process.title: Tell us the school and the emirate first
process.description: Not just the subject. Which school, which emirate, which programme and which level decides the regulator, the board, the compulsory subjects and the option blocks a tutor has to work inside. Two Diploma students in different emirates can need different plans for the same subject at the same level.

process.title: A short consultation, with the dates on the table
process.description: We ask what the last three pieces of assessed work scored, which session the school has registered the child for, and what the coordinator has said about coursework deadlines. That conversation decides whether this is a two-year build or a single-term push, and roughly how many hours it needs.

process.title: Matched to a named specialist, with availability stated
process.description: You are told who the teacher is, what they have taught at that level, and whether they are based in the UAE or elsewhere. If nobody suitable is free for the time you need, we say so at this point rather than offering a near-enough match and hoping.

process.title: A free trial lesson before any payment
process.description: One lesson, with the specialist you would continue with, on a topic you choose from recent schoolwork. No payment is taken before it and no card is held. You get a written summary afterwards saying what the teacher found, which is the honest basis for deciding whether to carry on.

process.title: A weekly slot, a written record, and a review date
process.description: Lessons run live over video in Gulf Standard Time, with a short written note after each one. We set a review date about six sessions in to look at what has actually changed in the marks. Sessions move for Ramadan timings, mocks and the examination weeks themselves.

whyPoints.title: The regulator is named, not implied
whyPoints.description: This page names KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education, and says what each one governs. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or recognition from any of them, and claims none. Explaining a regulator is useful; borrowing its authority is not.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The rate table quotes what other providers and a published rate tracker put in print, read in October 2026, with the source in the row. We publish no invented statistics, no satisfaction percentages and no self-assigned star ratings, because a figure without a source is worth nothing to a parent comparing options.

whyPoints.title: Coursework is taught, never produced
whyPoints.description: There are operations in this market selling completed internal assessments. We teach the criterion, question the research question and read one draft with written feedback. The student writes the work. That is an IB rule, and it is also the difference between help that survives a coordinator's declaration and help that ends a Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated before you pay, not after
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online. No IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE; home visits are a service offered in India. If the specialist for your subject sits outside the UAE, you are told at the point of matching, with no overseas phone number standing in for an explanation.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the body that sets them
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own published key dates and timetables. The IB's session dates are absent on purpose, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is how a family misses a deadline that belongs to the school.

faqs.question: Why is this page about a home tutor when the lessons happen over live video?
faqs.answer: Because home tutor is the phrase UAE parents actually search, and it describes the service accurately: private, one-to-one teaching organised around your family's week. The delivery is the part that has changed. IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video to families in all seven emirates, and home visits are a service offered in India only. No IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE. The trade is deliberate: you give up somebody in the room and you get the specialist who has actually taught your child's syllabus at that level, instead of whoever teaches that subject within a tolerable drive.

faqs.question: Which parts of my child's IB course are fixed before I hire anybody?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. The curriculum the school is licensed to teach, the authority that inspects it, the compulsory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, the exam board, the timetable zone, the option blocks that decided which Higher Levels were available, and the session the school registers for are all settled by institutions. What is left to you is genuinely significant: which specialist teaches your child, at what level, for how many hours a week, in what session length, and when the work starts relative to the entry deadline. Spend your attention there, because that is where it changes an outcome.

faqs.question: Which authority licensed my child's school, and what does it reach into?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. So the body above your school can reach into fees and assessment methods, not just inspection, and its school listing is where you verify any school a provider names.

faqs.question: Does the federal Ministry of Education decide anything inside an IB school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why an IB school and a British school in the same street both run the same three compulsory subjects, and why no international curriculum licence exempts a child from them. For the mandatory subjects the Ministry also controls content: using different or additional material without prior permission is strictly prohibited, which is a real limit on what any outside tutor can offer in those lessons.

faqs.question: Dubai opens seven more private schools in 2026-27. Does that help us find a Higher Level teacher?
faqs.answer: Not immediately, and possibly the opposite in the short term. The seven new schools include three running the International Baccalaureate, and they create 16,846 new places. Those schools recruit experienced Higher Level teachers from the same pool every existing school draws on, and the pool grows more slowly than the seat count. Six schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6% over the same period. More choice of school is good news. For a family trying to book a Higher Level Chemistry specialist in an exam term, it mostly means booking earlier and accepting that the right teacher may not live nearby.

faqs.question: Why is a tutor not free to invent their own Islamic Education or Social Studies material?
faqs.answer: Because the content for the mandatory UAE subjects is controlled. KHDA's guidance states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. So a tutor arriving with a worksheet pack of their own is not adding value in these lessons; they are working outside the rule the school itself has to follow. Legitimate support means working from the school's own material, in the language the school assesses the child in, on revision method and exam technique.

faqs.question: Our school builds its timetable from 40-minute units. How long should a tuition session be?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. That tells you something useful about attention: a child used to 40-minute blocks does not suddenly concentrate for 120. For Diploma subject teaching we normally use 60 or 90 minutes, which gives room for a timed question plus feedback without losing the second half. A visiting tutor's two-hour minimum usually exists because the travel has to be worth the trip, not because two hours teaches better.

faqs.question: Which criteria is the IB Mathematics exploration marked against, letter by letter?
faqs.answer: The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation. Most students arrive with the mathematics in reasonable shape and lose marks on reflection and personal engagement, because those reward writing about the decisions made rather than the calculation itself. Confirm the exact allocations against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, since criteria wording and marks change between syllabus versions. A tutor may teach the mathematics and show how reflection is credited; selecting the topic or writing the commentary is not available at any price.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay really have to stop at 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: Yes, 4,000 words is a maximum rather than a target, and it is enforced by markers simply stopping at the limit. A student who writes 4,600 words has thrown away whatever argument sat in the last 600, which is usually the conclusion they worked hardest on. Confirm the current figure with the coordinator, because component requirements move between guide versions. A tutor's legitimate role is to question whether the research question is answerable in that length, teach referencing properly, and read one draft with written feedback the student then acts on. The supervisor remains the school's supervisor throughout.

faqs.question: How many taught hours separate a Higher Level subject from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: The IB publishes guided teaching hours of 150 for a Standard Level course and 240 for a Higher Level one. The ninety-hour difference is roughly a term and a half of classroom time, which is the single most useful number in any conversation about switching levels. It explains why moving up late in the first Diploma year rarely works, and why six weeks of private lessons cannot substitute for it. Moving down is a different matter and often sensible, because every subject is scored out of 7 regardless of level. The real cost of moving down is which university courses will accept the profile afterwards.

faqs.question: My daughter wants to move a Higher Level down to Standard Level. Who has to agree?
faqs.answer: The school does, through the Diploma coordinator, and the window is narrower than most families assume because the change has to be reflected in the registration the school submits to the IB. Ask in writing, ask early, and ask what the deadline for the change actually is rather than when the coordinator would prefer to discuss it. Before you ask, check the entry requirements of the courses your daughter is likely to apply to, since medicine, engineering and economics-type degrees commonly expect specific subjects at Higher Level. A tutor can tell you whether the current grade is recoverable; only the university can tell you whether the profile still works.

faqs.question: Can a UAE family enter a child for IGCSE as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Entries are made by a registered examination centre, not by a family directly, so the practical question is which centre in the UAE will accept a private candidate for the subjects you want and in which series. Some schools and independent centres do; many do not, and availability varies by subject because practical and speaking components need facilities and assessors. Ask the centre about final entry deadlines, the administrative zone its timetable follows, and which components it can host before you plan any teaching. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, so for a June series this is a conversation to have in the autumn term, not one to open in the spring.

faqs.question: Who owns each deadline in the exam year, the school, the board or us?
faqs.answer: Almost none of them belong to the family. On a Cambridge June series, final entries close in the spring and are submitted by the school as examination centre; forecast grades come from the subject teacher on the centre's internal cut-off; the examination period runs across May and June and is set by Cambridge, by administrative zone; results reach the centre on Cambridge Direct in the summer and certificates follow some weeks later. The November series repeats the same shape with its own earlier deadline. The family owns only the preparation and the decisions that feed those dates: level choices before entries close, and mocks sat early enough for a forecast grade to rest on evidence.

faqs.question: Is the equivalency file something a tutoring provider should be handling for us?
faqs.answer: No. Ministry of Education equivalency is a process a family completes with the Ministry and the emirate's attestation channel, using documents the school issues. Any provider offering to perform or secure it is overstating its role. What the reporting does establish for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. For the IB there is no points figure we can cite, so verify it on moe.gov.ae rather than trusting any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects run short of teachers across the UAE, and what then?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are the usual pressure points, badly so in the northern emirates where a school might run the option for a handful of students. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is not scarce so much as congested, with everybody wanting the same 5pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window. Higher Level arts subjects are barely covered by providers in this market, ourselves included. Where no UAE-based specialist is free we match a Diploma teacher from our India-based team over the same live video format, and we say so at matching. Where we cannot cover a subject properly, we decline on the first call.

faqs.question: If our tutor teaches from outside the UAE, whose rules apply?
faqs.answer: The IB's academic-honesty rules and your school's own policies apply regardless of where the teacher sits, and those are the rules that can actually affect your child's Diploma. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, governs individuals providing paid private tuition in the UAE; it is granted free of charge for two years and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any UAE-resident tutor to show theirs. The service page on mohre.gov.ae is the official route and lists no fee.

faqs.question: How long is the Theory of Knowledge essay, and what else does the course require?
faqs.answer: The Theory of Knowledge essay is written on a prescribed title set by the IB and runs to a maximum of 1,600 words, alongside an exhibition component in which a student explains how objects connect to a prompt. It is externally marked. Theory of Knowledge is also one half of the combination that can add up to three points to a Diploma total, with the Extended Essay, so it is worth more attention than its timetable allocation suggests. A tutor can teach the knowledge framework and question the strength of an argument. Choosing the line of argument, or drafting the essay, is not legitimate help.

faqs.question: Does my child's UAE school even offer the November IB session?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and it is worth establishing before anybody plans around a retake. UAE schools overwhelmingly sit the May session, which fits the local academic year, and whether a November option exists for your child depends on what the school registers for rather than on what the IB offers globally. Ask the coordinator in writing which session the registration names and what the school's position is on a November retake. We publish no IB session or results dates on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so any date here would be unverified, and a wrong date is how a family misses something that belongs to the school.

best-ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the school, the emirate and the session
best-ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up the best IB home tutor in the UAE, the three facts that shape every sensible answer are which school your child attends, which emirate regulates it, and which session the school has registered for. Send those with the subject and level and we can tell you in one conversation whether a specialist is free for the time you need, whether the plan is a two-year build or a single-term push, and roughly how many hours it takes. The first lesson is free and happens before any payment. Lessons are live, one-to-one and online, and if we cannot cover your child's subject properly we will say so on that first call.

intro.heading: The best IB IGCSE tutor is the one who knows which series your child is entered for
paragraphs: There is no single best IB IGCSE tutor in the UAE, and any page that claims to have one is selling you a ranking it invented. What exists is a smaller, answerable question: which tutor is right for a Year 11 student sitting Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended in the June series, or for a Diploma student whose Chemistry Internal Assessment draft is due in nine days. Those two students need different people. The way you tell a good match from an expensive one is to ask calendar questions rather than quality questions.

Ask a prospective tutor which series your child is entered for. A tutor who knows the answer will come back with the board, the series, the syllabus or specification code, and the date your school has set for internal deadlines. A tutor who answers with a sentence about passion and personalised attention has told you nothing you can check. The whole of this page is organised around that test, because it is the one test that separates the people who teach UAE exam students from the people who advertise to UAE parents.

The calendar is not a detail. A UAE candidate sits Cambridge IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series or a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in May/June or November. Those windows are fixed years ahead, and every board publishes its final entry deadline months before the first paper, because zone timetables have to be built and question papers printed and shipped to centres. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its results reach students in January rather than December — the November 2025 series released to students on 22 January 2026. Each of those dates has a consequence for when tutoring has to start, and none of them moves because a family started late.

Delivery matters here too, and we would rather be blunt about it than let you discover it after a deposit. IB Gram arranges one-to-one tuition delivered online, over live video, screen-sharing a shared whiteboard and the student's own past-paper script. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are something we offer only in India. That is a real constraint and we think it is also the better arrangement for exam work, because the pool you choose from stops being whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive of your community and becomes whoever has actually taught the paper your child is sitting.

What follows is the information a UAE parent normally has to assemble from eight different websites: the series calendar counted backwards, the Cambridge zone rule that decides which timetable applies to your centre, the Cambridge and Pearson codes for the same subject side by side, the AED rates the market charges with the source of each figure, the permit position under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the academic-honesty line a tutor must not cross on an Internal Assessment, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether five IGCSE subjects are enough. Read the sections that apply to your child and skip the rest.

best-ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four programmes account for almost every enquiry that reaches us from the UAE. They share a word in the search box and almost nothing in their assessment architecture, so the notes below say what each one actually demands of a tutor working to a UAE school year.

programmes.name: Cambridge Upper Secondary (IGCSE)
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined by terminal papers, with each subject carrying its own four-digit syllabus code: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English as a First Language. Most subjects offer a Core and an Extended tier, and the tier a student is entered for caps the grade available. Entry decisions are made by the school months before the papers, which is why tier conversations belong in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the dominant upper-secondary route in UAE British-curriculum schools, and a UK curriculum accounts for roughly 37 per cent of private-school enrolment in Dubai. The practical UAE wrinkle is the administrative zone: every centre is allocated to one of six zones and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version of the timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in and keep that timetable, not a generic one found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same qualification level as Cambridge IGCSE under a different specification architecture, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language A. Some Pearson International GCSE subjects are available in a modular pattern, meaning units can be sat in different series and the best result carried forward. That changes revision planning completely: a modular student has a real decision to make about which units to bank in November and which to leave for June.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and revises them, so a UAE family should work from the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. Two fixed points from the last cycle are useful as planning anchors: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. January results are the moment a retake decision becomes real.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each criterion marked out of eight and reported as a level rather than a percentage. There is no terminal paper in most MYP schools, so the grade a student carries into Diploma selection is built from internal tasks and the Personal Project. Students who are strong at content but weak at criterion language lose marks they could keep, because the mark descriptors reward specific behaviours and reward them in specific words.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of UAE MYP students move into the Diploma at the same school, which means the MYP-to-DP transition happens without a change of building and often without a change of expectation. The subjects where that transition hurts most in our UAE enquiries are Mathematics and the sciences, where MYP criterion-based tasks do not look much like a DP Paper 1. Dubai added three new International Baccalaureate schools to its 2026-27 intake, so this cohort is growing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard Level courses, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment with its own criteria and word limit, and those internal deadlines are set by your school, not by the IB. The Diploma is a two-year accumulation, so the tutoring question is almost never only about the final papers; it is about which internal component is due next and whether the student understands what the criteria actually reward.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and that session governs the whole Diploma year, from internal draft deadlines through mocks to upload dates. We do not publish IB exam or results dates on this page: the IB's own assessment pages are the authority, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds the internal calendar that matters more day to day. International Baccalaureate students make up roughly 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, a small share of a very large sector.

best-ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects UAE families ask for most often, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where marks tend to leak away. The IGCSE grid follows underneath, because a page about an IB IGCSE tutor needs both.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. HL adds proof, complex numbers and a far heavier calculus load, and Paper 3 at HL is an extended investigative problem that rewards students who can keep going when the first method stalls. Marks are lost in presentation of reasoning more often than in the final answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-rich questions, with heavier reliance on the graphic display calculator than Analysis and Approaches. Students lose marks by giving an unrounded answer, by failing to define variables in context, or by treating a modelling question as a pure algebra question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the Chemistry help we are asked for in the UAE. The Internal Assessment is where a strong student most often underperforms, because a question that is not genuinely investigable caps the marks available before a single measurement is taken.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields are the backbone; the HL extension in fields and quantum work is where SL habits stop transferring. Data analysis questions reward students who state uncertainties properly, and penalise those who quote a calculator readout to six figures from a ruler measured to the millimetre.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content makes Biology look like a memorisation subject and it is not marked as one. Command terms do the work: distinguish, outline, explain and evaluate each expect a different shape of answer, and students who write the same paragraph for all four lose marks they already knew the content for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a surprising share of the grade, and the HL paper adds quantitative work that catches students who learned the theory verbally. The Internal Assessment is three commentaries on published articles, which means article choice is itself a marked decision.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis plus the Individual Oral and the HL Essay. Students who read widely still lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and by treating the global issue in the Individual Oral as a topic rather than as an argument the two extracts can actually support.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole skill. Tools applied generically earn little; tools applied to the stimulus material earn most of the marks. The Internal Assessment demands primary or secondary research handled properly, and weak sourcing is the most common ceiling on the final mark.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, data structures and the HL extension into resource management and abstract data types. The Internal Assessment is a solution developed for a real client, and students who skip the success-criteria stage find the evaluation criterion impossible to write convincingly later.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and Internal Assessments
subjects.description: The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words and the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 on a prescribed title. Support here is supervision and feedback on the student's own drafting, never drafting on their behalf, and the distinction is explained in full further down this page.

best-ib-igcse-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: At IGCSE the syllabus or specification code matters more than the subject name, because Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subject through different papers. Bring the code from your child's school report and the first session can start on content rather than on diagnosis.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and probability carry the Extended tier. The tier a student is entered for caps the grade available, so the tier conversation is a Year 10 decision. Pearson 4MA1 and Cambridge 0580 differ in paper structure and in how heavily each leans on a calculator.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or for A-Level Mathematics. It front-loads calculus and functions, and it is the single most useful bridge we see between IGCSE and the Diploma for students who struggle with the jump in algebraic fluency.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity is the topic that generates most of our UAE Physics enquiries, usually because series and parallel circuits were taught before the student was fluent with rearranging formulae. Practical skills are examined on a written paper in both specifications, so technique is learned through past-paper scripts rather than through a lab bench.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the gate: students who are shaky there lose marks across titration, electrolysis and energetics questions that look unrelated. Organic chemistry rewards naming discipline, and qualitative analysis rewards knowing the expected observation rather than guessing at a colour.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Genetics, transport in plants and human physiology dominate the mark scheme. The common failure is writing everything known about a topic instead of answering the command term, and the fix is timed answer-shaping against a published mark scheme rather than more reading.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 · Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and reading response are the two components where UAE students most often plateau at a grade 6. Progress comes from learning what the reading questions reward — selection and inference, not retelling — and from writing to the specified audience and form rather than writing well in general.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 and 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study papers reward applied answers and punish textbook recital. Students lose marks in the longer evaluation questions because they list advantages and disadvantages without ever reaching a judgement, which is the part of the question carrying the top band.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 · Pearson 4CP0)
igcseSubjects.description: Binary and hexadecimal conversion, logic gates, and the algorithm-writing questions that reward a disciplined pseudocode style. Students who code confidently in Python still lose marks by writing Python where the mark scheme expects structured pseudocode or a trace table.

sections.heading: What parents are really asking when they search for the best IB IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: The honest answer to this search is that best is not a property of a tutor. It is a relationship between one tutor and one student at one point in a two-year course. A tutor who is excellent with a Diploma Year 2 student rebuilding Chemistry Higher Level from scratch may be the wrong choice for a Year 10 student who needs Cambridge 0580 algebra made solid before the tier decision is made. So the useful version of the question is: what can I check, before I pay anything, that tells me this particular tutor fits this particular child?

Four things are checkable, and all four are factual rather than a matter of taste. First, board and code: can the tutor name the syllabus or specification your child is entered for, and talk about its papers specifically? Second, series awareness: does the tutor know which series your child sits and what falls between now and then? Third, the permit position: can the tutor confirm they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023? Fourth, the honesty line: does the tutor state clearly what they will not do with an Internal Assessment?

Everything else parents are usually told to assess is either unverifiable or a proxy. A claimed years-of-experience figure is unverifiable. A star rating published by the agency selling the tutor is a self-assertion, and several of the agencies competing for this search publish two contradictory ratings on the same page. An examiner claim is only meaningful if current status can be evidenced, and it should never be used to imply access to marking or to grade boundaries. We would rather give you four questions you can put to a tutor in the trial lesson than a badge you cannot audit.

The trial lesson is the real test, and it should be in the specific subject and at the specific level you are worried about. Ask the tutor to work through one past-paper question your child got wrong. In fifteen minutes you will learn whether the tutor diagnoses the error or simply re-explains the topic. That distinction is the whole difference between a tutor who moves a grade and a tutor who fills an hour.
bullets: Ask for the board, the series and the syllabus code in the first message, not the first invoice
Ask the tutor what falls between today and the first paper — a good answer has dates in it

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring page in this market is written forwards: here is what we offer, contact us. Exam years do not work forwards. They work backwards from a fixed first paper, through a sequence of deadlines that were set by the board and by your school long before you started looking for help. The table below is that sequence, with the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 series used as the worked example, because it is a window a UAE candidate genuinely sits and its published timetable shows exactly how far ahead of the papers the real decisions sit.

Read the gaps rather than the dates. The Pearson November 2026 papers run from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that fixed which subjects and which tier each candidate sits was submitted by the centre long before the autumn term got going — the exact deadline sits on the school's own exams calendar and on the statement of entry, never on a tutoring page. Results then reach students in January rather than in December, which is what makes the gap between a November grade and the next entry window so narrow: the November 2025 series released to students on 22 January 2026. A family that starts looking for a tutor in the week the timetable goes up on the noticeboard has already passed the two decisions that most affect the grade: which subjects were entered, and at which tier.

The consequence for tutoring is a specific one. Work that changes content knowledge needs months; work that changes exam technique needs weeks. If you are more than a term out, the sessions should be about closing content gaps in the order the syllabus builds them. If you are inside ten weeks, the sessions should be almost entirely timed past-paper work against published mark schemes, because that is where marks move fastest at short notice. A tutor who runs the same lesson shape in both situations is not planning to the calendar.

Two UAE-specific items belong on any backwards plan. Ramadan falls in the second half of the academic year at present and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which shifts family routines and makes post-Iftar session times genuinely useful for several weeks. And UAE school terms do not align neatly with the series: the gap between the end of a term and the start of a paper is often the most productive revision window available, and it is also the window families most often spend travelling.

sections.heading: Which series, which zone, which results day
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and in November. The IB session UAE schools sit is May. Those are the fixed facts. What is not fixed, and what catches UAE families, is which timetable applies to your centre.

Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. It also states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is not a formality. A paper can sit on a different day or at a different time in a different zone, and a family revising to a timetable found through a search engine can prepare the wrong subject for the wrong morning. Ask the school office for your zone and work only from that document.

Pearson handles the same problem differently: it publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then revises them, including for International GCSE series well in advance. The right behaviour is identical in both cases — work from the live official timetable on the board's own site, and treat any date printed on a tutoring website, including ours, as a prompt to go and check rather than as a source. The table below separates what we can source from what you must confirm yourself.

Results days deserve the same care, because they are decision points rather than endings. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge publishes its own release day on Direct for each of the June and November series, with certificates following some weeks later. Between a disappointing grade and the next available series there is usually a review-of-results window and an entry deadline, and both are short. Knowing them in advance is the difference between a planned resit and a lost year.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, a different paper
paragraphs: Parents often discover mid-year that their child's school teaches Pearson Edexcel International GCSE rather than Cambridge IGCSE, or that the sciences follow one board and Mathematics another. Both are legitimate international qualifications at the same level, and UAE universities and the Ministry of Education equivalency route treat them in the same family. They are not interchangeable in a tutoring room, because the papers are built differently and the practice material is not transferable without judgement.

The first difference is the code. Cambridge uses four digits — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English as a First Language, 0478 Computer Science. Pearson uses an alphanumeric specification code — 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A, 4CP0 Computer Science. Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the entire area-page cluster we researched for this market, which gives you a sense of how little attention this gets from the pages competing for your search.

The second difference is structure. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, and the tier entered caps the grade available. Pearson tiers Mathematics into Foundation and Higher and offers a modular route in some subjects, meaning units can be sat across different series with the better result carried forward. A modular student therefore has a strategic question a linear student does not: which units to bank in November, and which to hold for June. Any tutor planning revision without knowing which route applies is planning in the dark.

The third difference is practical assessment. Neither board examines IGCSE science practical skills through a graded lab visit for most candidates; the skills are examined on a written paper. That is why online tuition works for IGCSE sciences: the examinable skill is reading an experimental description, handling the data, identifying the variable that was not controlled and explaining the improvement. All of that is done on a script, which can be shared on screen and annotated line by line in a live video session.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks go missing, and the week to fix each one
paragraphs: A grade is lost in identifiable places, and almost never evenly across a paper. When we look at a marked past paper from a UAE student sitting somewhere in the 5 to 6 band, the lost marks cluster in a handful of recurring behaviours rather than across the syllabus. Naming those behaviours is more useful than naming topics, because a student who fixes a behaviour recovers marks across every topic where it appeared.

The most common one is answering the topic instead of the command term. A question that says explain is asking for a causal chain; a question that says describe is asking for observable facts; a question that says evaluate is asking for a judgement with support. Students who write everything they know about a topic score the marks available for the first sentence and nothing for the rest. This is fixable in three or four focused sessions and it moves marks in every written paper the student sits.

The second is arithmetic and notation under pressure. Units dropped, significant figures invented, an unrounded calculator readout copied into a final answer, a rearrangement done in the head and done wrong. These are not understanding failures and they should not be treated as revision topics; they are habits, and they respond to short, repeated, timed drilling rather than to re-teaching. The third is time allocation: students who spend twelve minutes on a four-mark question have already decided not to attempt the last page.

The table below maps the recurring losses we see at IGCSE to the practice that actually addresses each, and to roughly when in the run-up it should start. The ordering matters: content repair belongs early, technique repair belongs in the middle, and the final fortnight belongs to full papers under exam timing with nothing new introduced.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and what a price does not tell you
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below are market rates in AED gathered from competitor pages and from a published Dubai tutoring rate table, each attributed to whoever published it. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. For our own arrangement, start with the free trial lesson and a consultation, and you will be quoted for the specific subject, level and session length your child needs.

What the bands tell you is that price in this market tracks two things: scarcity of the specialism and the cost of travel. An online session with a university-student tutor sits at the bottom. A qualified subject tutor online sits in the middle. An in-home visit carries the travel inside the hourly figure, which is why the same tutor costs more on a home visit than in an online session. A named or examiner-track specialist sits at the top, and the premium there is scarcity rather than a different hour of teaching.

What price does not tell you is anything about fit. A high rate does not confirm the tutor has taught your child's specification, and a low rate does not mean the hour is wasted. The questions that correlate with a useful session are the ones earlier on this page: the board and code, the series, the permit, the honesty line. Ask those before you ask the rate, because an AED 450 hour with someone who has never taught Pearson 4CH1 is worse value than an AED 200 hour with someone who has taught it for years.

Two context items help a UAE family judge whether the number is reasonable. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. And monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Set any quote against those anchors rather than against a feeling.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against the in-home tutor a neighbour recommends
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real and well-established service in the UAE, and it is worth describing properly rather than dismissing. A tutor arrives, sits with the student at the kitchen table, and works for an hour or two. Parents like the visibility, younger children often settle better with someone physically present, and there is no technology to fail. The market charges for it accordingly: a published Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, and that figure carries the travel inside it.

The costs are structural rather than incidental. The tutor pool shrinks to people who can reach your community at the hour you want, which in practice means evening slots fought over by every family in the neighbourhood. Travel time is paid for whether it is itemised or not. Rescheduling is harder, because a missed slot is a wasted journey. And the match is made on geography first and specialism second, which is exactly backwards for a student who needs Chemistry Higher Level or Pearson 4PM1 rather than general help.

IB Gram's arrangement is one-to-one tuition delivered online, over live video. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and we would rather say so on the page than after a deposit; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What the online format buys a UAE family is selection: the tutor is chosen because they have taught your child's specification and series, not because they live nearby. Screen-sharing a marked past-paper script and annotating it line by line is also, for exam technique, a better working surface than a shared notebook.

The table sets the two formats against each other on the things that actually differ. Neither column is the right answer for every family. For a Year 6 student who needs a reading habit built, physical presence may well win. For an exam-year student sitting a specific paper in a specific series, specialist match and mark-scheme fluency win, and those are the columns where the online format is strongest.
