programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations, which means there is nothing for a tutor to revise towards. Support at this stage is about the mechanics underneath the inquiry: number fluency, reading stamina, writing at length in English, and the habit of recording what was tried before it is forgotten. The exhibition at the end of the programme is the first piece of sustained independent work most children produce.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run beside the PYP from the start, with Arab and non-Arab pupils taught in separate classes under KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines. Parents arriving mid-year often find their child placed into an Arabic stream before anyone has explained which stream it is, and that placement follows the child upward.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, and reports an achievement level rather than a percentage. Parents who expect a mark out of a hundred often cannot tell whether a 5 is comfortable or a warning. The Personal Project in the final year carries a report of 1,500 to 3,500 words and is the first assessment where the process journal matters as much as the outcome.
programmes.countryNote: MYP schools in the Emirates feed into two very different destinations. Some pupils continue into the Diploma at the same school; others move to an IGCSE school for Years 10 and 11, because a UK-curriculum place is easier to find here than an IB one. That decision is usually made in Year 8 or 9, and it changes which subjects need attention first.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The core adds up to three bonus points. Most of the teaching load, and nearly all of the panic, sits in the Higher Level subjects and the coursework deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE Diploma student is carrying the Ministry's mandatory subjects at the same time as the internal assessments, and the two sets of deadlines are set by different people. The school's coordinator fixes internal dates months before the IB's own upload windows. Families who only discover this in the second year lose the cheapest weeks of the whole programme.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language development component. It is offered by a small number of schools in the Emirates and suits a student who wants Diploma-standard subjects without the full six-subject load. The reflective project is assessed against its own criteria and carries a word limit.
programmes.countryNote: Because few UAE schools run the Career-related Programme, a CP student's subject combination is often unique in their year group, and the school may have one teacher covering a course for two or three pupils. Outside support here is less about remediation and more about the student not being the only person in the building reading the subject guide.

best-ib-tuition.subjectsIntro: Subject descriptions below name the criterion letters and the limits that decide the marks, because that is the level at which a tutoring hour either helps or does not. Each subject is taught at Higher and Standard Level unless the subject guide says otherwise.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries 6 of the 20, and at Higher Level it asks for sophistication, not volume. Students lose marks for unexplained notation and for a topic too large to finish inside twelve to twenty pages.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same five criteria, same 20 marks, a different mathematical register. Applications rewards modelling with real data and a technology-supported argument, which makes the choice of dataset the single biggest decision in the exploration. The route also matters for admissions: some engineering and economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, so the choice should be checked against named course pages before Year 12.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each, and carries 20% of the subject grade at both levels. Reports fail on evaluation rather than on chemistry: a sound method with no serious discussion of limitations caps the mark. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where paper marks go missing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same four criteria and the same 24 marks as the other sciences, with a 3,000-word limit on the report. Physics students tend to design a competent experiment and then under-analyse it, losing data analysis marks on uncertainty propagation and graph choices. Higher Level adds depth in fields, induction and quantum physics, where the mathematics becomes the limiting factor rather than the concept.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The investigation uses the same research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation criteria out of 24. Biology candidates most often lose research design marks for an unquantified variable list and conclusion marks for claiming more than the data supports. Statistical treatment, rather than extra experimental repeats, is usually the cheapest improvement available in the final fortnight.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The portfolio is three commentaries, each capped at 800 words, each built on a news article the student selects. The limit is the whole difficulty: a diagram, an explanation and an evaluation inside 800 words leaves no room for background. Higher Level adds a policy paper that rewards quantitative handling, and the terminology criterion punishes loose use of elasticity and welfare language.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The research project runs to 1,800 words and is assessed against criteria that reward a genuine research question and the selection of tools, not the number of tools used. Students who apply six frameworks superficially score below those who apply two properly. Supporting documents have their own rules, and exceeding them is the most common avoidable loss in the component.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Higher Level adds an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words on a studied work, and both levels sit the Individual Oral on a global issue with an extract from a literary and a non-literary text. Marks are lost on the global issue being stated rather than argued, and on the extract being described instead of analysed within the fifteen minutes.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is 2,200 words and marked out of 25, with the investigation section carrying 15 of those marks and the source evaluation 6. Students routinely spend their word count on narrative and arrive at the reflection with nothing left. The reflection is only 4 marks but it is the section most often written in the last hour.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution is a developed product with documentation, assessed on planning, design, development, functionality and evaluation. The marks sit in the documented reasoning, not in the code volume, and the client or adviser requirement is a real constraint rather than a formality. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management, which are the usual paper weak points.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic appears twice in a UAE student's week: as an IB language subject and as the Ministry's mandatory subject for school. The two are assessed by different people against different expectations. For the IB course, the productive skills carry the risk, because written Arabic at Higher Level demands register control that conversational fluency does not supply.

best-ib-tuition.regionsTitle: Where your child's school file sits, emirate by emirate
best-ib-tuition.regionsIntro: Which authority holds your child's school file changes what you can read about the school, who approves its fees and curriculum, and where an inspection judgement comes from. It does not change who may tutor your child, which is a federal matter.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes both school inspection reports and the mandatory-subject guidelines. It also issues the Educational Services Permit that a tuition business with premises needs. The largest IB cohort in the country sits here, and so does the largest pool of UK-curriculum teachers competing for the same tutoring hours.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at the teacher's own school. If a teacher offers evening lessons to your child and teaches them by day, that is the rule to read before accepting.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits inside Abu Dhabi emirate, so its private schools answer to the same Abu Dhabi authority rather than to KHDA, and the same staff ethics rules apply. The IB school count here is small, which means a Higher Level cohort of three or four pupils is normal and a subject specialist within driving distance is not.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families send children to schools in Dubai, which means the school is under KHDA while the home is under Sharjah, and evening session timing is set by the commute rather than by either authority.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level authority, so inspection material is thinner on the ground than a Dubai parent would expect. IB provision is limited, and families routinely combine a local school place with outside teaching for Higher Level subjects the school cannot staff.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain also falls under the federal Ministry of Education for private-school supervision. It is among the emirates that returned no mentions at all across the competitor pages researched for this market, which tells you something about where tutoring providers put their attention and nothing about the students living there.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai school belt is the practical constraint: a visiting specialist is a two-hour round trip, which is why online teaching changes the available subject list here more than anywhere else.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education. The east-coast location makes a visiting Higher Level specialist close to impossible to arrange on a weekly basis, and families here are usually choosing between a generalist who can attend and a specialist who can teach over video. The second option is the one that matches a syllabus.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the country's deepest IB provision, and three more International Baccalaureate schools are among the seven private schools opening for 2026-27. Students we support are enrolled across the schools below. Their internal coursework deadlines differ from each other by several weeks, which is why a tuition plan has to start from the school's calendar rather than from a generic one.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi's IB schools are fewer and further apart than Dubai's, and the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than KHDA holds their files. Students we support attend the schools below. Small Higher Level cohorts are the defining feature here: a Physics Higher Level class of four changes how much individual explanation a student actually receives in a week.
schools: The American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: North of Dubai the IB map thins quickly, and supervision shifts between the Sharjah authority, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education. Students we support attend the schools below alongside Dubai-based schools reached by a daily commute, which is the single biggest constraint on when a weekday session can realistically begin.

best-ib-tuition.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the UAE school system only; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and families should verify any school's current programmes with the school and its regulator.
best-ib-tuition.modesIntro: Three ways of buying teaching, separated by what they are pointed at rather than by price. All three run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and all three can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan.

modes.title: Weekly subject teaching
modes.description: One or two sessions a week against the school's own scheme of work, so the hour lands on the topic being taught rather than on whatever the tutor prefers. This is the arrangement that moves a Standard Level grade over a term and keeps a Higher Level subject from accumulating gaps that only surface in a mock paper.

modes.title: Criterion clinics for coursework
modes.description: Short, focused sessions on a draft the student has already produced, read against the published criterion letters for that component. The tutor identifies which criterion is costing marks and what the student must do about it. The student makes every change themselves, and the school's academic-honesty declaration remains accurate.

modes.title: Exam-term intensives
modes.description: A block of sessions counted backwards from the first paper, built around past-paper technique and the specific question types the student has been avoiding. Papers are worked under timed conditions and then marked against the published mark scheme the school holds, so the student sees where a four-mark answer became a two-mark answer.

sections.heading: What a search for the best IB tuition in the UAE is really asking
paragraphs: The search is asking a comparison question that no public record in the Emirates can answer. There is no official rating of tutors, no register of tuition quality, and no body that compares one provider with another. KHDA, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education all regulate schools. MoHRE issues a permit to individuals who give private lessons. None of those five authorities, and not the IB itself, produces anything resembling a ranking of tuition providers.

That leaves a parent with two options. One is to believe whichever site says it the loudest, which is why three of the six competitor pages measured for this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. The other is to replace the ranking question with a fit question, and the fit question is answerable, because the documents that define fit are all published. The subject guide states the criteria and the marks. The school states its internal deadlines. The board states the entry deadline. MoHRE states who may lawfully tutor.

The rest of this page works through those documents in order, because that is the order in which they bite. A tuition hour that does not know which criterion is losing marks is an hour of general encouragement. An hour that arrives after the coordinator's internal deadline cannot change the mark at all. And an arrangement that nobody in the household has checked for lawfulness is a problem waiting for a different kind of attention. Fit is specific, checkable and far more useful than a superlative.

sections.heading: What each authority publishes, and the question it cannot answer
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and each publishes something a parent can use. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge does the same there, both of them approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The pattern worth noticing is what each one stops short of. A school rating tells you how the school was judged across a long list of indicators. It does not tell you whether your child's Higher Level Chemistry teacher is explaining energetics well, because inspection reports are written about schools, not about individual teachers and certainly not about outside tutors. A MoHRE permit tells you that an individual is permitted to give private lessons. It is a permission, not a grade, and nothing about it speaks to teaching quality.

This matters because the most dangerous phrase available to a tuition website in this country is a claim of regulator approval. A permit issued to a training institute with premises is a specific object with a specific scope. An individual's tuition permit is a different object. Neither is an endorsement of anybody's teaching, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of these bodies. What the table below does is match each authority to the question it can answer and name the question it cannot, so the gap is visible rather than filled with marketing.

sections.heading: Dubai is adding IB places faster than it is adding IB teachers
paragraphs: The supply side of this market explains more about tutoring prices than any claim about quality does. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula. UK curricula took 37% of that roll, Indian curricula 26%, US curricula 14%, and the International Baccalaureate 7%. The IB is the smallest of the four large blocks, which means the number of teachers in this city who have actually taught a Diploma Higher Level course is a fraction of the number who have taught GCSE or A-Level.

The direction of travel makes it tighter. Seven new private schools open in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, four on UK curricula and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Three new IB schools will be recruiting experienced Diploma teachers from the same pool that families are trying to hire from in the evenings. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two consequences follow for a family choosing tuition. The first is that scarcity, not quality, sets the price of a Higher Level specialist, and a provider quoting the same rate for Standard Level Business Management and Higher Level Physics is not pricing the market honestly. The second is that the booking window matters more than the rate. A family looking for Higher Level Chemistry in September has options; the same family looking in February is choosing from whoever is left. With the school fee line frozen for a year, the tuition line is where a household budget actually moves.

sections.heading: The criteria your child is marked against, letter by letter
paragraphs: Here is the test that separates a subject specialist from a confident generalist, and it takes one question. Ask what the criteria are for the component your child is working on, by letter, and how many marks each one carries. A teacher who has taken a cohort through that component answers without pausing. Not one of the competitor pages researched for this market names a single criterion letter. That is a remarkable gap, because the criterion list is the document the mark is produced from.

The numbers are concrete. A Diploma mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with use of mathematics worth 6 of them. The sciences investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each and carries 20% of the subject grade at both Standard and Higher Level. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34, and critical thinking alone carries 12 of those marks. A History investigation is out of 25, with 15 in the investigation section. These allocations tell you where an hour of help is worth buying.

They also tell you where it is wasted. A student polishing presentation on an exploration is working on a 4-mark criterion while use of mathematics, worth 6, goes unaddressed. A candidate adding a third body paragraph to an Extended Essay is adding knowledge and understanding, worth 6, when the 12 marks live in critical thinking. Verify the exact criteria against the subject guide for the cohort your child sits, because the guides are revised and the Diploma coordinator holds the version that counts. The pattern below is stable enough to plan around.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, component by component
paragraphs: Every written component in the Diploma carries a published limit, and a limit is a planning instrument rather than a formality. A 4,000-word Extended Essay and a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay need different drafting behaviour entirely: the first fails on scope, the second fails on anything that is not argument. An 800-word Economics commentary leaves room for one diagram, one explanation and one evaluation. No competitor page researched for this market publishes these limits as a reference set, which is odd, because they are the first thing a student needs when planning.

The practical use is backwards planning. Count the limit, divide it by the sections the criteria require, and the student can see immediately whether the plan on the table is possible. A History investigation of 2,200 words with 15 marks in the investigation section cannot afford 900 words of context. A sciences report capped at 3,000 words with six marks each for conclusion and evaluation cannot afford a method section that reads like a recipe. These are arithmetic problems before they are writing problems.

Treat the figures below as the stable pattern and the subject guide as the authority. Limits are revised between cohorts, and the guide your child's year group sits is the one that governs. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the current version rather than trusting a number from a website, including this one. A tutor who checks the limit with you at the start of a coursework block is doing the single most useful thing available in that first session.

sections.heading: What an internal assessment mark is worth once the paper marks land
paragraphs: Parents often ask what a coursework mark converts to, and the honest answer is that it converts to a contribution, not to a grade. In a Diploma science, the investigation carries 20% of the subject grade at both levels. The remaining 80% comes from the papers. Those components are weighted, added into a scaled total, and the total is then placed against grade boundaries that the IB sets for that session and publishes to schools. The boundaries move between sessions, because they are set against the demand of the papers actually sat.

Three things follow. A strong investigation cannot carry weak papers, because it is one-fifth of the subject. A weak investigation is expensive in a different way: it caps the ceiling before the student enters the examination hall, and it cannot be improved after the school's internal deadline. And a mark that looks comfortable in isolation may sit just below a boundary once scaled, which is why the useful question is never what the investigation scored but how many scaled marks separate the student from the next grade.

Nobody outside the examination system can tell you where a boundary will fall, and any tutor who offers a number is guessing. What a good tutor can do is work from the published weightings: identify which component is leaking the most marks per hour of study, and spend the hours there. For a Higher Level student sitting three papers plus an investigation, that is a calculation, and it usually points somewhere less comfortable than the topic the student most enjoys revising.

sections.heading: Two permissions, two different objects, and why the difference matters
paragraphs: Private tuition in the Emirates is a permitted activity with paperwork, not an informal arrangement. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can be quoted.

A tuition business with premises and staff is a different legal animal. In Dubai that requires an Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. The two documents are frequently conflated in marketing copy, and the conflation always runs in the same direction, with a business permission presented as a quality endorsement of individual teaching. It is not one. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no claim to one.

There is one more rule worth knowing before accepting an offer. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to pupils enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but it means the most convenient offer a parent receives, from the teacher who already knows the child, may be the one to decline.

sections.heading: The part of the timetable where the Ministry writes the content
paragraphs: A UAE Diploma student is not studying six IB subjects. They are studying six IB subjects plus the subjects the country requires. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. At federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. These hours are already booked in your child's week.

The organisation of them is prescribed in detail. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

The rule that changes what tuition can do here is the content rule: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. So outside support in this part of the timetable is not a parallel syllabus. It is help with the language, the reading and the examination technique, worked on the material the school has been given, and a tutor who offers their own Arabic curriculum has misunderstood the rule.

sections.heading: Equivalency is where a confident website gets the number wrong
paragraphs: A UAE certificate equivalency file is the step that turns a school-leaving qualification into something a UAE university or employer will accept, and it is where the accuracy of a tutoring website becomes measurable. For the British track, a student must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects.

That number is the test. One competitor ranking for this market publishes that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The reported requirement is five, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count. A parent who planned a timetable around six when five was required has paid for an entry fee and a term of teaching they did not need. For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB Diploma itself, this page publishes no points threshold, because none was read on a Ministry source during the research for these pages. Several sites state one with confidence. Treat any unsourced figure as a drafting decision rather than a fact, and check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation channel directly. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tuition provider performs, guarantees or can accelerate, and no tuition is required by any regulation in order to complete it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty is where best and cheapest point in opposite directions
paragraphs: One site researched for this market sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is the clearest illustration available of why a ranking question is the wrong question. On a pure value-per-mark basis a purchased assessment looks efficient. Under IB rules it is malpractice, the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller, and the risk is to the whole Diploma rather than to one component. A page that competes on price against that offer has already accepted its terms.

The line itself is not vague. Assessed work must be produced by the student. A tutor teaches the subject, explains what a criterion is asking for, questions an argument, points out that a conclusion is not supported by the data, and insists on the word limit. A tutor does not supply text, rewrite paragraphs into their own prose, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The student's coordinator signs a declaration about the authenticity of the work, and that declaration has to remain true after every session.

Two further rules sit beside it. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson; they are referenced and linked, not reproduced or handed out as downloads. And examiner status should not be asserted for anyone whose current status cannot be evidenced, nor used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. A provider that is clear about all three of these is easier to judge than one that offers the most, which is the practical version of choosing well.

sections.heading: Does paying more buy a better hour?
paragraphs: Published rates in this market run from AED 33 an hour to AED 650 an hour for what is described, in all cases, as tutoring. The spread is not a quality scale. It is five different products sold under one word, and the useful exercise is to name what each band is actually buying and how it tends to fail. Every figure below was read in October 2026 on the provider's own published rate pages or on a public rate tracker, and every figure is a market rate rather than an IB Gram price.

At the bottom of the range sits generalist teaching, often by a university student: useful for building confidence and working through exercises, unreliable for coursework, because marking a draft against criterion letters requires having taught the component. In the middle sits a qualified subject tutor, which is where most Standard Level teaching belongs. Above that sits a genuine programme specialist, and that band exists because of the supply arithmetic rather than because of brand. At the top sits scarcity and reputation, sometimes attached to a named individual.

Two patterns are worth knowing before any negotiation. A visiting tutor's hourly rate includes travel time, which is why two-hour minimums are normal in that band; the household is buying the journey as well as the lesson. And a provider quoting one rate for every subject and level is not pricing scarcity, which means either the Higher Level work is underserved or the Standard Level work is overpriced. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page; the first lesson carries no charge, no card details are taken, and pricing is discussed for the specific subject and level once the match is identified.

paragraphs: IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address. Tuition for families here is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered in India only. That is the position on every country page on this site, and it is stated here rather than buried, because a family searching for tuition near them deserves to know the format before the first conversation rather than after it.

The argument for it is the supply arithmetic from earlier on this page. If 7% of Dubai's private school roll sits in the IB, and Higher Level cohorts in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah run to a handful of pupils, then a geographically filtered search returns a generalist far more often than a specialist. A family in Khor Fakkan choosing a tutor who can physically attend is choosing from a list of perhaps two. The same family choosing over video is choosing from everyone who has taught that paper.

There are real losses in the trade, and they are worth stating. A tutor in the room reads body language better and can see a worked page without anyone sharing a screen. A young child needs an adult nearby for the first few sessions. Against that sits criterion work on coursework, which suits a shared screen and a marked-up draft better than a kitchen table, plus continuity: a family moving from Dubai to Abu Dhabi keeps the same tutor, even though the school's regulator changes. sections.heading: Starting, and what honest unavailability sounds like
paragraphs: The first conversation is short and it is mostly questions. Which school, which programme, which subjects and levels, which exam session, and what the last two reports and the most recent mock said. For a coursework block, which component, which criteria, and what the coordinator's internal deadline is. That last date decides whether the work can still change, and it is the question most providers do not ask because it can rule out the sale.

Then a trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach the sessions, not a consultant. The trial carries no charge, no card details are taken, and no obligation follows. Sit in on the first ten minutes if you want to. The things worth watching are whether the tutor asks the student to do the work during the hour or performs the explanation at them, and whether the syllabus topic and the criterion are named out loud at some point.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is free. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry and the smaller language and arts subjects are the combinations where a specialist can genuinely be unavailable in the week you ask. When that happens the useful response is a date, an alternative level of support with its limits named, or a referral elsewhere, rather than a general tutor presented as a specialist. Disclosed unavailability is a better signal about a provider than a calendar that is never full and never empty. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit of any kind, and several route UAE parents to an overseas number without saying where the teaching happens.

process.title: Say which school and which authority holds its file
process.description: Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah under its own authority, Ras Al Khaimah under the Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry. The school sets the internal deadlines a plan has to respect.

process.title: Name the component and the criteria
process.description: A subject and a level are not enough to plan an hour. The component matters, and so do the criterion letters: an exploration out of 20, an investigation out of 24, an Extended Essay out of 34. Naming the component is what turns a general request for help into a specific one the tutor can prepare for.

process.title: Count backwards from the real deadline
process.description: The deadline that binds is usually the coordinator's internal one, not the board's. Cambridge's published key dates for one series show final entries due in November for an exam period starting in February, so entries close months before the paper. Put every date on one sheet and plan the weeks against it.

process.title: Take the trial lesson and watch the first ten minutes
process.description: The trial is taught by the tutor who would teach the sessions. No charge applies, no card details are taken, and nothing obliges you to continue. Watch whether the student is made to do the work, and whether the syllabus topic and criterion get named. Both are visible inside ten minutes.

process.title: Review against the criteria, not against a feeling
process.description: After a block of sessions, the question is whether the marks moved on the criterion that was targeted. A mathematics exploration that gained on use of mathematics worth 6 marks has improved in a way a report comment cannot capture. Review on that basis, and change tutor without embarrassment if it has not happened.

whyPoints.title: Criteria named, letter by letter
whyPoints.description: Feedback is given against the published criterion letters and their mark allocations for the component in question, so a parent can see which criterion an hour was spent on. Not one competitor page researched for this market names a single criterion letter, which makes this the easiest quality difference to verify.

The coordinator's authenticity declaration stays accurate, which matters more to a Diploma candidate than any amount of convenience.

What those bodies do is explained so a parent can check the claims other pages make.

faqs.question: Is there any official ranking of IB tuition providers in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA oversees private education in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge licenses private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority and the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge regulate their emirates, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. All five regulate schools. None of them rates tutors or tuition companies, and neither does the IB. Any site presenting itself as the market leader is stating an opinion that no public register could confirm. The checkable alternatives are a tutor's subject teaching history, the criteria they can name, and a trial lesson you watch.

faqs.question: What should I read about my child's school before spending anything on tuition?
faqs.answer: Start with the inspection or evaluation material published by the authority that holds the school's file, then the school's own coursework calendar from the Diploma coordinator. The second document is the one that changes decisions. An internal deadline for an internal assessment sits months before the IB's own upload window, and once it passes, no amount of teaching can change that mark. Read them together: the school report tells you how teaching was judged across the school, and the calendar tells you how many weeks are left in the components your child is actually being marked on this term.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Extended Essay worth, and which criterion carries most of them?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. Critical thinking carries 12 of the 34, which is more than a third, and it is the criterion a descriptive essay cannot score on no matter how well researched it is. Presentation is worth 4, so formatting work is a poor use of a late hour. Confirm the current allocations with your child's supervisor, because the guides are revised between cohorts. The essay must be drafted by the student; a supervisor or tutor discusses reasoning and sources.

faqs.question: Is the Theory of Knowledge essay really capped at 1,600 words?
faqs.answer: The published limit for the essay on a prescribed title is 1,600 words, and the exhibition commentary is 950 words across three objects. Those are short, and the shortness is the difficulty. There is no room for defining terms at length or for an introduction that restates the title. Two knowledge arguments developed properly, each tied to a real example, will score above four arguments gestured at. Check the current limit in the subject guide your child's cohort sits, which the coordinator holds. A tutor's useful job here is teaching how a knowledge claim is built and tested.

faqs.question: What happens if my child's internal assessment runs over the word limit?
faqs.answer: Treat an over-length piece as a problem that will cost marks rather than one that might. Limits are published per component in the subject guide: 4,000 words for the Extended Essay, 3,000 for a sciences investigation, 2,200 for a History investigation, 800 for each Economics commentary. Examiners are not required to reward material beyond a stated limit, and the practical effect is that the sections written last, which are usually evaluation and reflection, are the ones that fall outside it. The fix is arithmetic at the planning stage: allocate the word count across the criteria before the first draft, not after it.

faqs.question: Can a high internal assessment mark carry weak examination papers?
faqs.answer: Not far. In a Diploma science, the investigation is 20% of the subject grade at both Standard and Higher Level, so four-fifths of the grade comes from the papers. Component marks are weighted, added to a scaled total, and the total is placed against grade boundaries that the IB sets for that session. A strong investigation protects the ceiling and removes one source of anxiety, but it cannot compensate for a paper that is losing marks across several topics. The planning question is which component is losing the most marks per hour of study available.

faqs.question: Where are grade boundaries published, and can we see them before the exams?
faqs.answer: Boundaries are set for each session against the papers actually sat and are released to schools, not to the public in advance. Nobody outside the examination system can tell you in advance where a boundary will fall, and a tutor who offers a figure is guessing. Official boundary tables, past papers and mark schemes belong to the awarding bodies; they are referenced and linked rather than redistributed. What a teacher can legitimately do is work from the published component weightings to show how many scaled marks a given improvement is worth in that subject.

faqs.question: Dubai is opening three more IB schools next year. Does that make tutors easier to find?
faqs.answer: It makes them harder to find in the short run. Seven new private schools open in Dubai for 2026-27, four on UK curricula and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places, and six new schools opened during 2025-26 while enrolment rose 6%. New IB schools recruit experienced Diploma teachers from the same pool families hire from in the evenings. The practical consequence is that the booking window matters more than the hourly rate for a Higher Level subject: September gives you options, February gives you whoever has not been taken.

faqs.question: Does the fact that Dubai schools teach seventeen curricula change how we choose?
faqs.answer: It changes which question you ask first. With seventeen curricula in one city, and the IB at 7% of the private-school roll against 37% on UK curricula, most tutors available here trained on GCSE and A-Level. Someone describing themselves as a maths tutor may never have taught a Diploma exploration or seen the criteria it is marked against. So ask about the syllabus and the component rather than the subject: which papers have you taught to, and what are the criterion letters for this coursework piece. The answer separates the two groups immediately.

faqs.question: Should I prefer a provider with premises in Dubai over one that teaches online?
faqs.answer: Premises answer a different question from teaching quality. A tuition business with premises and staff in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the steps and annual renewal. That document says nothing about whether any individual tutor has taught your child's Higher Level subject. An individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead. Ask about both where they apply, then judge the teaching separately, on the criteria the tutor can name and what you see in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: How do I check that a school a tutoring website lists actually exists?
faqs.answer: Check it against the regulator that would hold its file: the Dubai authority for Dubai schools, the Abu Dhabi authority for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah authority, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, or the federal Ministry for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Spelling matters, because a school listed under a slightly wrong name is a signal in itself. During research for these pages one competitor listed a school that appears not to exist, and several present twenty or more schools as clients with no relationship of any kind. School names are context, not evidence.

faqs.question: Which single document tells me most about whether tuition will help?
faqs.answer: The subject guide for the component your child is currently being assessed on, read alongside the most recent marked piece of work. The guide names the criteria and the marks each one carries; the marked work shows which criterion is actually losing them. Together they turn a vague sense that a subject is going badly into a target: 6 marks in use of mathematics, or 6 in evaluation, or 12 in critical thinking. The Diploma coordinator holds the correct version of the guide for your child's cohort, which is the version that counts.

faqs.question: My child's subject guide changed between year groups. Does that affect tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth checking at the first session rather than discovering later. The IB revises subject guides, and criteria, mark allocations and word limits can move between cohorts. The sciences investigation, for example, is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation under the current guide, which is not how earlier cohorts were marked. A tutor working from an older guide will give confident feedback against criteria that no longer apply. Ask which guide version they are using and compare it against the one your child's coordinator holds.

faqs.question: If the Ministry sets the Arabic content, what is left for tuition to do?
faqs.answer: Language, reading fluency and examination technique, worked on the material the school has been given. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited, and schools must ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. Outside support therefore cannot run a parallel syllabus or supply its own curriculum. What it can do is build vocabulary and script confidence, practise answering in the register the paper expects, and help a non-Arab student keep pace in a class streamed by first language.

faqs.question: Is the most expensive hour on the market the right hour for a Standard Level student?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Published rates in this market run from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, and the top band is priced by scarcity and reputation rather than by suitability. A Standard Level subject taught to the school's scheme of work is well served by a qualified subject tutor, where published rates sit between AED 150 and AED 300. The premium band earns its price on Higher Level teaching and on coursework where criterion knowledge is decisive. Paying specialist rates for Standard Level homework support is the most common way a UAE tuition budget is wasted.

faqs.question: If this is the better option, why does nobody drive to our address?
faqs.answer: Because a geographically filtered search returns a generalist far more often than a specialist. With the International Baccalaureate at 7% of Dubai's private-school roll, and Higher Level cohorts in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah running to a handful of pupils, the pool of people who can physically attend and have taught the paper is often empty. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we run in India only. The trade is a room for a subject match, and it is stated here rather than discovered later.

faqs.question: What should the first lesson actually produce if we are still deciding?
faqs.answer: Three things you can look at afterwards. A named target: the syllabus topic or the criterion letter the sessions will work on. A realistic view of the time available, counted from the coordinator's internal deadline rather than from the exam date. And evidence that the student did the work during the hour instead of watching an explanation. The trial carries no charge, no card details are taken and nothing obliges you to continue, so the only thing at risk is an hour. If none of those three appears, that is the answer.

best-ib-tuition.closingHeading: Judge it on the documents, not on the adjectives
best-ib-tuition.closingBody: Nobody in the Emirates publishes a ranking of IB tuition, so the useful version of this search is narrower and far more answerable. Which criteria is the work marked against, by letter and by mark. Which deadline actually binds, the coordinator's or the board's. Who is permitted to teach privately here, and under which permit. What a rate includes, with a source and a date beside it. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the first lesson at no charge and no card details taken. Bring the school name, the subjects and levels, the exam session and the next coursework deadline, and the first conversation can be specific from the start.

intro.heading: Why there is no league table of IB tutors, and what to use instead
paragraphs: Search for the best IB tutor in the UAE and you get pages that assert it rather than pages that evidence it. The International Baccalaureate does not rate tutors. Neither does the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, or the federal Ministry of Education that supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. No register exists that ranks one tutor above another, and no regulator publishes a quality mark a tutoring business can carry. Every superlative in this market is self-issued.

That leaves a parent with two options. One is to trust the loudest claim. The other is to work out which statements about a tutor can be independently confirmed, and treat the rest as marketing. A surprising amount turns out to be confirmable. The private tuition work permit is a real document with a real issuing authority and a stated validity. The authority that holds your child's school file is a matter of public record, as are the subjects that school is licensed to teach and the mandatory UAE subjects it must run alongside them. The exam board's entry deadlines and results dates are published. The Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for a British-track school leaver are published in specific grades and subject counts.

What cannot be confirmed is just as useful to know. A star rating assembled by the business showing it proves nothing a parent can audit. Examiner status for a named individual has no public register in this region. A grade guarantee is a commercial promise dressed as an academic one, and the only version worth anything is one with refund terms printed beside it. Treat each of these as a question to ask rather than an answer to accept.

This page is built around that separation. It sets out the permit categories under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and who falls into each, the authority map across the seven emirates and what each body actually approves, the Arabic and Islamic Education requirements that sit inside your child's timetable whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, the equivalency rules a Diploma or IGCSE leaver meets at the end, and the hourly bands the UAE market publishes in AED with the source of each figure named. Then it says plainly how IB Gram delivers lessons, and lets a comparison table carry the argument rather than an adjective.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, not a school and not a licensed training institute with premises in the Emirates. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on UAE evening slots. Home visits are a service offered only in India; no one from IB Gram travels to an address in the Emirates. The reason that works in your child's favour is scarcity: a Higher Level Chemistry specialist who can teach the current syllabus is a rarer thing than a competent graduate who happens to live twenty minutes away, and video removes the twenty minutes from the equation.

best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes, and UAE schools license them in different combinations. Which one your child sits changes what tutoring can usefully do, because the assessment model changes completely between them. A Middle Years student needs criterion-referenced work habits; a Diploma student in the second year needs paper strategy and internal assessment process support against a fixed calendar.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units, no external examinations, and reporting against learner-profile attributes rather than paper marks. Tutoring at this stage is about literacy and number fluency, not technique. The honest answer for most PYP families is that an hour a week of reading and arithmetic practice does more than a subject specialist, and that a tutor who claims to prepare a nine-year-old for the Diploma is selling something that does not exist.
programmes.countryNote: A PYP school in Dubai still has to deliver Arabic, Islamic Education for Muslim students and Social Studies within its weekly timetable, counted by the authority in forty-minute lesson units. That is often the first place a non-Arab family discovers their child has a subject nobody at home can help with, and it arrives years before any IB assessment does.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against criteria A to D, each scored out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Students lose marks for not answering the criterion in front of them rather than for not knowing the content. A tutor working well here teaches the student to read the criterion strand, then write to it, which is a transferable skill the Diploma rewards two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 or 10 and then move students to IGCSE, so a family can find their child switching assessment model mid-school. Ask the school which years sit which, because the gap between criterion-marked MYP work and an IGCSE paper with mark-scheme bullet points is the single most common reason a strong Year 9 student slides in Year 10.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three or four Higher Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Points run to 45, with the core contributing up to three. Internal assessment sits inside every subject and is marked by the teacher against published criteria, then moderated externally. This is where most UAE tutoring demand sits, and where a subject-and-level match matters more than anything else on a tutor profile.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE Diploma student finishes with a certificate issued outside the country and then needs it recognised inside it. The Ministry of Education runs equivalency for that, and the figures it applies to the IB route are not something this page will publish without a ministry source. Start the paperwork conversation with the school's university-guidance office in the first year, not in July.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, language development and service learning. Fewer UAE schools license it, so finding a tutor who has taught the CP core is harder than finding one for Diploma subjects. The Diploma courses inside a CP, though, are assessed identically, so a Diploma-experienced subject tutor transfers directly.
programmes.countryNote: Because the CP is less common here, a family choosing it should check what the Ministry of Education and the universities on their shortlist say about it before Year 12 rather than after. The equivalency route for a CP certificate is not the same conversation as the one for a full Diploma, and the answer comes from the ministry channel, not from a tutoring site.

best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: A tutor profile that lists twenty subjects is telling you about an agency's roster, not about who will teach your child. The useful version is narrower: which subject, which level, which syllabus version, and what the tutor can say about where marks go. Each entry below includes the question that separates someone who has taught the course from someone who has read about it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus depth and the Paper 3 extended-response problem at Higher Level. Ask a prospective tutor how they would structure a Paper 3 investigation under time pressure. Someone who has taught the course answers with a method; someone who has not talks about mathematics in general. The exploration is the other half of the mark and needs a topic that can actually be developed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-dependent work, with the graphical display calculator doing real labour in the exam. Ask which calculator model the tutor teaches on and how they handle a question where the answer depends on the regression the student chooses. Route choice between AA and AI should be settled against the degree shortlist before Year 12, not afterwards.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields carry the conceptual load; the extended-response questions carry the marks. Ask the tutor to explain how they teach uncertainty propagation in a write-up, because that is where competent students quietly lose internal assessment marks. A tutor who only talks about content coverage has not marked a scientific investigation against the criteria.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium at Higher Level, with data-based questions rewarding precision over recall. Ask how the tutor would narrow a student's investigation idea into something with a measurable variable and a defensible method. The students who struggle most are usually those whose investigation question was never answerable in the first place.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content plus command-term discipline: explain, outline, suggest and evaluate each want different things. Ask the tutor to show how they drill command terms rather than topics. Higher Level adds depth in plant and animal physiology that students often meet for the first time three months before the paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world context and the internal assessment commentaries built on published news articles. Ask how the tutor sources suitable articles and how they stop a student writing a summary instead of an analysis. Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject expecting an essay course.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under exam conditions and a research project at Higher Level that lives or dies on the quality of its question. Ask the tutor what makes a research question too broad. A good answer references the data the student can realistically obtain, not the interest of the topic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of unseen text, the comparative essay and the individual oral built around a global issue. Ask how the tutor prepares the oral, since many students arrive with a global issue that cannot be evidenced in both their chosen texts. This is the subject where UAE families most often assume fluency equals a high grade.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, pseudocode in the IB's own dialect, and a solution the student develops with a real client. Ask whether the tutor teaches the IB pseudocode conventions specifically, because a student who writes perfectly good Python in a paper answer still loses marks. Higher Level adds abstract data structures that reward early practice.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core carries up to three points and is the part of the Diploma most often left until it is too late. Support here means supervision-adjacent coaching: narrowing a question, testing an argument, planning a schedule. Ask the tutor where they stop. Anyone willing to supply text for a student's own submission is a risk to the Diploma, not a help to it.

best-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Which authority sits behind your child's school
best-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: The UAE does not have one school regulator. It has five, split by emirate, and they publish different things on different scales. A tutor does not need to be an expert in any of them, but they do need to know which one your child's school answers to, because that determines what evidence about the school exists and what the school is permitted to do with its curriculum.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. It publishes school inspection outcomes and sets the mandatory-subject requirements every licensed curriculum must accommodate.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and has issued professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff that touch directly on who may tutor whom for a fee.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Part of the Abu Dhabi emirate, so the same department holds the file. Families here sometimes assume a separate local authority exists; it does not, which means an Al Ain school's published evidence sits in the same place as an Abu Dhabi island school's.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate here.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and holds the same fee-and-curriculum approval powers as Sharjah's authority. Fewer IB schools operate here, which changes the subject-availability conversation more than the regulatory one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here rather than an emirate-level body. Parents looking for an inspection report should expect a different publication pattern from the Dubai or Abu Dhabi one.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Many secondary students commute to Sharjah or Dubai schools, which means the authority holding the school file is often not the authority of the emirate the family lives in.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, on the east coast, with the smallest IB cohort of the seven emirates. Subject combinations at Higher Level are the practical constraint here, not regulation.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 students across 227 schools offering seventeen different curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for seven per cent of enrolment. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Raha IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi's IB cohort is smaller than Dubai's and more spread out, so a single school often runs one teaching group per Higher Level subject. That is the structural reason a parent here looks outside the school for subject depth rather than for extra hours.

best-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of working, all delivered one-to-one over live video on UAE evening slots. The choice is about how much of the Diploma you are trying to support and how close the next deadline is, not about the technology. Every option starts with one free trial lesson, booked without card details, so the match is tested before anything is paid for.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one subject support
modes.description: One or two sessions a week in a single subject at a fixed level, running with the school's own sequence rather than ahead of it. This is the setup that suits a student who understands the course but is losing marks on technique, and it is the only mode where progress can be read reliably, because the variable being changed is small enough to see.

modes.description: Scheduled sessions around the school's internal deadlines for an investigation, a commentary, an exploration or the Extended Essay. The work is the student's throughout. What a tutor adds is a narrower question, a testable method, a schedule that survives contact with mock week, and feedback on drafts the student has written themselves.

modes.description: A fixed number of hours in the weeks before a paper, built around diagnosis rather than coverage. The first session is spent finding which marks are recoverable in the time available; the rest go to those. A block of this kind is honest work when it starts eight weeks out and increasingly cosmetic when it starts at two.

sections.heading: What a parent can verify about a tutor, and what nobody can
paragraphs: The word best, on a tutoring page, is an assertion with nothing behind it. There is no UAE register of tutors, no board-issued quality mark for tutoring businesses, and no inspection regime that reaches past school gates into private lessons. Anyone searching for the best IB tutor in the UAE is therefore choosing between unverified claims unless they change the question from who is best to what can be shown.

Four things can be shown. First, the permit: a private tutor's work permit is a document with an issuing authority, a stated validity and an application route, and asking to see it is a normal request. Second, the teaching record: which syllabus, which level, which board, over how many years, with a straight answer about the last time they taught it. Third, the honesty position: what the tutor will and will not touch on assessed work, stated before money changes hands. Fourth, the delivery method, which should be described the same way in a sales conversation as it is on the website.

Four things cannot be shown, and a page that leans on them is telling you something. A self-published star rating cannot be audited by a parent, and ratings that differ between the visible page and its markup are a known pattern in this market. Examiner status for a named individual has no public register here. A promised grade has no mechanism behind it at all. A regulator's name used adjacent to words like approved or accredited is the most dangerous construction in this industry, because the permits those bodies issue are specific objects granted for specific activities, and an individual tutor's permit is not one of them.

sections.heading: Six questions that shorten a shortlist, and the answers that end it
paragraphs: A first conversation with a tutoring provider usually runs on their script. Taking it back is a matter of six questions, asked in order, each of which has an answer that disqualifies. The first is which subject and level the named tutor has taught, and when. A roster answer — our tutors cover all IB subjects — is a disqualifying answer, because the person on the call has not matched anybody yet.

The second question is about the permit: which category under the private tuition rules does this tutor fall into, and can the document be shown. The third is about employment: does the tutor teach at a UAE school, and if so, is your child enrolled there. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the tutor permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. A provider who treats that question as awkward rather than routine has not read the rules they operate under.

The fourth question is where the tutor stops on assessed work. The answer you want is specific and slightly boring: feedback on the student's own drafts, questions rather than sentences, nothing supplied. The fifth is operational — who teaches if this tutor becomes unavailable, and does the rate change. The sixth is the only one about money that matters early: is the quoted figure per hour or per session, and is anything added on top. Three of those six answers can be checked against a document. The other three tell you whether you are talking to someone who has sat in a Diploma classroom.
bullets: Which subject and level has this named tutor taught, and in which year most recently?
Which permit category applies, and may we see the document?
Does the tutor teach at a school my child attends?
What exactly will you not do with an internal assessment draft?
Who covers a session if the tutor is unavailable, and at what rate?
Is the figure per hour or per session, and what is added to it?

sections.heading: Who the UAE permits to give private lessons, category by category
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues it through its smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing. The published completion time is two working days. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who tells you the paperwork is expensive is describing something else.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. That breadth is why eligibility alone is a weak signal. A permitted tutor and a tutor who can teach Higher Level Chemistry are different claims, and only one of them is about the document. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any specific figure quoted at you is unsourced.

The category that matters most to a UAE family is the school-teacher one, because of the conflict rule attached to it. An Abu Dhabi school's own staff may not take paid private work with students from that school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is worth verifying against the current policy document rather than treating as settled, but the direction is clear enough: the convenient option of hiring your child's own class teacher privately is the one option a careful parent should rule out first.

sections.heading: A tutor's permit and a centre's licence are not the same object
paragraphs: Parents comparing an individual tutor against a tuition centre often assume the centre is the safer choice because it holds a licence. The licence is real, but it licenses a different thing. In Dubai, a tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit for a training institute, obtained through an initial approval and then a sequence of permit and licence steps with a maximum of six months to complete them, renewed annually with the request submitted at least thirty days before expiry. That is a business authorisation covering a venue and an activity.

An individual tutor's permit is a work authorisation covering a person. Neither document says anything about teaching quality, and neither is a quality mark that a tutoring business may attach to its tutors. This is why pairing an authority's name with a word like approved is a category error as well as a liability: the authority has not assessed the teaching, it has authorised an activity. IB Gram holds neither instrument — it is a matching platform without premises in the Emirates, and it does not describe itself as anything a regulator has assessed.

The practical difference for a family is about who is accountable and for what. A centre takes responsibility for the venue, the staffing and the timetable, and usually teaches in small groups at a lower price per student. An individual tutor takes responsibility for the teaching alone. A platform sits in between, carrying the matching, the records and the replacement when a match fails. Knowing which of those three you are buying from makes the price comparison in the next section mean something, because the same hourly figure buys different things in each model.

sections.heading: The subjects inside your child's timetable that no IB tutor will mention
paragraphs: A UAE parent planning Diploma support is often surprised to find subjects on the report card that belong to no IB subject group. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the authority's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind that is simple: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations.

The delivery rules are specific enough to matter to a tutoring plan. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and any mandatory-subject lesson is advised to run at least twenty-five minutes.

Two consequences follow for anyone choosing a tutor. The first is a credential point: schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate authority approval to teach those subjects, which is a higher bar than a general tutoring permit and a fair question to ask of anyone offering Arabic support. The second is a content restriction: for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who offers to work through their own Arabic workbook instead of the school's scheme is offering something the school cannot use.
