sections.heading: What a tutor should know about your school before the first lesson
paragraphs: A tutor who asks nothing about the school is going to teach a syllabus rather than a student. Five pieces of information change how the first month runs, and a provider worth paying asks for them unprompted. Which authority holds the school's file, because that determines what published evidence about the school exists and on which scale it is reported. Which programme and which year group, because the Middle Years and Diploma assessment models reward different habits. Which exam board, where IGCSE sits behind the Diploma. Which internal deadlines the school has set for assessed work. And what the school has already said about the student, in writing.

That last one does more work than any diagnostic test. A school report that shows strong attainment and weaker progress is describing a different problem from one where both are low, and the tutoring response differs: the first is usually technique and pace, the second usually foundation. Different emirates report on different scales, so a parent comparing a Dubai report with a Sharjah one is comparing two instruments, not two schools. Ask the tutor to read the actual report before proposing a plan.

Scale matters too. Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 students across 227 schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes accounting for seven per cent of enrolment. Seven further private schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, creating 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. Those numbers explain something a parent feels directly: an IB cohort inside a large non-IB market means a school may run one teaching group per Higher Level subject, and a student who does not fit that group's pace has nowhere inside the school to go.

sections.heading: The accuracy test: equivalency, and the number a ranking page gets wrong
paragraphs: There is a quick way to test whether a tutoring provider checks its facts. Ask what the Ministry of Education requires for equivalency on the British track. The published position is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A page currently ranking in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. It is wrong, and it is wrong in a direction that costs families money.

The American track has its own published thresholds: English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No points threshold for the IB Diploma appears in that source, which is why none appears on this page. Anyone publishing an IB equivalency figure without a ministry citation is guessing in public, and a parent planning a Diploma around a guessed number is the person who pays for it.

Equivalency is also not a service a tutoring business performs. It is a process run by the ministry and the emirate attestation channel, and the correct role for anyone else is to describe it, name the authority and point to the official route. Tutoring is not required for it, and nobody should suggest otherwise. What tutoring can legitimately do is make sure the subjects and grades a student finishes with are the ones the route needs, which is a Year 10 and Year 12 conversation rather than a Year 13 one.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and what each band is actually buying
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The bands below are market rates in AED, taken from what providers publish about themselves and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are not IB Gram's price list. What they are good for is calibration: knowing the band tells you whether a quote is normal, and knowing what sits inside each band tells you what the extra money is paying for.

The spread runs from AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Most of that gap is explained by two variables and not by teaching quality: who is in the room, and who is in the car. Monthly packages seen in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits at an address. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Context helps a family judge whether any of it is proportionate. The Dubai authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. School fees are therefore a known quantity for the coming year, which makes tutoring the variable line in the education budget — and a good reason to decide the number of hours before the first session rather than after the third invoice.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against one-to-one online, for a UAE family
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real and substantial market here, and a parent searching for it is not making a mistake. It is worth understanding what it costs and what it delivers. A visiting tutor's published band runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, and the two-hour minimum most visiting tutors insist on exists because a single hour does not pay for the drive. In practice a family is buying a teaching hour, a journey and a pool of candidates bounded by how far someone will travel on a weekday evening.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition instead, over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service offered only in India; no one from IB Gram travels to an address in the Emirates, and this page will not imply otherwise. The argument for the online version is not that it is cheaper, though the published bands suggest it usually is. The argument is about which tutors become reachable. A family in Fujairah or Al Ain choosing from people who will drive to them is choosing from a short list. A family choosing from everyone who can teach the subject at that level is choosing from a long one, and at Higher Level the length of that list is the whole question.

What the online format gives up is the physical presence that some students genuinely need, and a page that pretends otherwise is not being straight. What it adds back is specific: a shared screen where a marked script can be annotated live, a recording the student can return to the night before a paper, a diary with one set of constraints instead of two, and a replacement tutor who can start on Tuesday rather than when someone local frees up. The table below sets the two side by side on the dimensions that actually differ.

sections.heading: Three different bodies set the dates, and one of them gives your school a zone
paragraphs: Families often discover late that the calendar governing their child is not set by the school. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential that a school uses the correct version of the timetable for its zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Two schools in the same emirate can therefore sit one paper at different times, which is why comparing notes with a friend at another school is unreliable.

Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, and the choice between the two UAE series is the clearest worked example. A Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and a November entry closes a comparable distance ahead of its own papers; the exact day is fixed per series and reaches the family on the statement of entry, which is why the honest instruction here is to ask the exams officer rather than to trust a date found in a search result. Treat November as the resit route rather than the main event: a June grade that disappoints leaves a short review-of-results window and then a November entry deadline, and both of those pass quickly while a family is still arguing about whether to accept the grade. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, a January release that runs straight into the entry window for the next series. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against.

IB dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site cannot be confirmed by the automated checking behind this research, so no IB session or results date is published here. UAE schools sit the May session, and the right source for the exact windows is the school's Diploma coordinator or ibo.org directly. A tutor who starts by asking which series your child is entered for, and which zone the centre sits in, is reading the correct calendar; one who talks about exam season in general has not.

sections.heading: Academic honesty is the hardest test a tutoring provider has to pass
paragraphs: One business ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not tutoring. Submitting purchased work is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not the vendor. A parent choosing between providers should treat the honesty question as a filter applied before price, because it is the only variable in this market that can cost a child the whole Diploma.

The boundary is not vague, and a good tutor can state it in a sentence. A tutor teaches the skills the task needs, explains the criteria, asks questions about the student's own argument, points at a weak method, and gives feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor does not supply sentences, rewrite paragraphs into their own prose, or hand over a structure the student then fills in. Everything the student submits must have been composed by the student. Where a school asks whether outside support was used, the answer should be yes with the support described, and any provider nervous about that declaration is telling you where their line sits.

Two related practices are worth refusing on sight. The first is any offer to supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads: those belong to the boards, should be referenced and linked rather than reproduced, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. The second is examiner language used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Nobody has that access to sell, and a provider implying they do is making a claim about the integrity of an examination system rather than about their teaching.

sections.heading: Starting, and what honest unavailability looks like
paragraphs: The first step is a conversation about the student rather than the package: subject, level, board, school, the internal deadline nearest in the diary, and the most recent marked work. From that comes a named tutor, a trial lesson at no charge — one per student, booked without card details — and a written note afterwards describing what the trial found. A parent who has read the preceding sections already knows which questions to ask on that call, and asking them is welcome rather than awkward.

Sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free. A niche Higher Level combination on a narrow weekday window is the usual case, and there are only three truthful responses: a different time slot with the right specialist, a different specialist with a compromise on something named, or a wait with a date attached. No competitor researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere on their site, which is a strange silence in a market where scarcity at Higher Level is the main constraint. A provider who always has someone available for everything is answering a sales question, not an availability one.

What happens after the trial is a schedule, feedback a parent can read, and a point at which the arrangement is reviewed against something other than a feeling. Six sessions is a reasonable interval: enough for technique changes to show in marked work, short enough that nobody is paying for momentum. Keep the review honest in both directions. A tutor who cannot show what changed should be replaced, and a student who has not done the work between sessions is not going to be rescued by booking more of them.

process.title: Tell us the five facts that matter
process.description: Subject, level, board, school and the nearest internal deadline. With those five, a match is a real suggestion rather than a roster pull. Bring the most recent marked script or report if you have one; it changes the plan more than any description of the problem does, because it shows where marks were lost rather than where they were expected.

process.title: Read the tutor's record before the lesson
process.description: You get a named tutor with the subjects and levels they teach, the boards they have worked with, their years of experience and their permit position. If anything there is vague, say so and ask for a different match. The point of naming the tutor before the trial is that the four checkable claims can be checked before any money moves.

process.title: Use the free trial as a test, not a demonstration
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, booked without card details, delivered one-to-one over live video. Ask the tutor to work on something real from this week's class. A trial spent on a polished set-piece tells you nothing; a trial spent on the topic your child is currently failing tells you whether this person can teach it.

process.title: Agree the schedule and the honesty boundary in writing
process.description: Session length, frequency, the time slot in Gulf Standard Time, and what happens if a week is missed. For any assessed-work support, write down what the tutor will and will not do, so the answer exists before a deadline makes it urgent. If the school asks whether outside help was used, you want that note to hand.

process.title: Review against marked work after six sessions
process.description: Not against a feeling. Compare a marked piece from before with one from after and ask the tutor to point at what changed and why. If nothing moved and the work was done, change the tutor rather than adding hours. If the work was not done, more hours will not fix it and nobody should pretend they will.

whyPoints.title: Checkable claims instead of superlatives
whyPoints.description: Every tutor comes with four things a parent can test: subject and level taught, board experience, years in the classroom, and permit position. There is no star rating on this page because a rating a business issues about itself is not evidence. The trial lesson is the sample, and it costs nothing to take.

whyPoints.title: A pool bounded by subject, not by distance
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the shortlist for Higher Level Chemistry is everyone who can teach Higher Level Chemistry, rather than everyone who will drive to your emirate on a Tuesday evening. In a market where single-group Higher Level cohorts are normal, that difference is the thing that most often decides whether support is available at all.

whyPoints.title: The regulatory position stated, never implied
whyPoints.description: This page explains what the emirate authorities do, which permit covers which activity, and what the Ministry of Education requires at equivalency. It claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, because IB Gram holds none. A provider implying otherwise is making a claim a parent cannot verify and a regulator may not recognise.

whyPoints.title: A coursework boundary written down in advance
whyPoints.description: Support for internal assessment and the Diploma core is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is supplied for submission. The boundary is agreed in writing before the work starts, so the answer exists before a deadline creates pressure to move it, and the school can be told exactly what help was given.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, including when it is bad news
whyPoints.description: If no suitable specialist is free for the subject, level and slot you need, you are told that, with the alternatives and a date. Nothing researched for this project suggests any competitor publishes a coverage limit, which makes a straight answer about scarcity unusually useful in this market and considerably cheaper than discovering it in week three.

faqs.question: What does "best IB tutor" actually mean when nobody publishes a ranking?
faqs.answer: It means whatever the page saying it decides. The IB does not rate tutors, and neither does any UAE education authority, so no league table exists to be top of. The useful substitute is a short list of claims a parent can check: which subject and level this named person has taught and when, which permit category they fall into, what they will and will not do with assessed work, and how lessons are delivered. Four questions, four answers you can verify. Anything presented as a ranking in this market was issued by the business claiming it.

faqs.question: Which claims on a tutoring site can a UAE parent actually verify?
faqs.answer: The permit, the teaching record, the honesty position and the delivery method. A private tuition work permit is a document issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation with a stated validity, and asking to see it is routine. A teaching record can be interrogated by subject, level, board and year. The honesty boundary can be put in writing before work starts. Delivery can be confirmed by asking how the first lesson will physically happen. Star ratings, examiner claims and promised grades sit on the other side of that line: a parent has no mechanism to audit any of them.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the UAE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: A wider group than most parents expect. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website or e-services system, with a published completion time of two working days. Eligibility is therefore a floor rather than a recommendation: it tells you someone may legally teach, not that they can teach Higher Level Physics.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre's permit the same as an individual tutor's permit?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating them is a common error. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and then a sequence of permit and licence steps completed within six months, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry. An individual tutor holds a work permit covering a person, not a venue. Neither document assesses teaching quality. IB Gram holds neither: it is a matching platform without premises in the Emirates, and it does not describe itself as something an authority has assessed.

faqs.question: Should I believe a tutor who describes themselves as an examiner?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unverified unless the individual can evidence a current appointment. There is no public register in this region a parent can search, which means the claim rests entirely on the provider's word. More importantly, ask what the claim is being used to suggest. Examiner experience can genuinely sharpen how someone teaches mark schemes and command terms. It does not come with access to marking in progress, grade boundaries before release, or paper content, and any implication that it might is a claim about an examination system's integrity rather than about teaching.

faqs.question: How do I tell a teaching service apart from an essay-writing one?
faqs.answer: Ask one question: what exactly will you not do with my child's draft? A teaching answer is specific and slightly dull — explain the criteria, question the argument, flag a weak method, comment on writing the student produced. An essay-mill answer is fluent about outcomes and vague about process, and will often quote a fixed price for a finished piece. One business ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Submitting purchased work is malpractice under IB rules, and the penalty falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: My child's coordinator asks whether outside help was used. What do we say?
faqs.answer: Say yes, and describe it. Outside tutoring is not prohibited; undeclared assistance that crosses into producing the work is. A straightforward description — weekly subject lessons, plus feedback on drafts the student wrote — is what a coordinator needs in order to authenticate the submission. Keep the written boundary you agreed with the tutor at the start, because it answers the question for you. A provider who becomes uncomfortable at the mention of declaring their involvement has told you something more useful than any testimonial on their site.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the tutor is not sitting in the same emirate as us?
faqs.answer: For one-to-one teaching over live video, the tutor's location changes two things: the time zone they schedule in and the school systems they have seen. Both are worth asking about. What it does not change is the teaching, provided the person knows the syllabus version and the board. Location matters enormously in the visiting-tutor market, where a candidate pool is drawn by driving distance, and matters far less once the journey is removed. The honest trade is a smaller presence in the room for a much larger pool of subject specialists.

faqs.question: We live in Sharjah and the school is in Dubai. Whose rules apply to us?
faqs.answer: The school's regulator, not the family's address. A Dubai school answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which sets its inspection reporting and the mandatory-subject requirements inside its timetable, even when most of its families live in another emirate. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods there. For any question about reports, curriculum approval or mandatory subjects, follow the school. For questions about a tutor's permit, the authority is federal and the same everywhere.

faqs.question: Should a tutor know anything about Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies?
faqs.answer: They should know these subjects exist on the timetable and consume real hours. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated in forty-minute lesson units. That matters for planning: a Diploma student has less discretionary evening time than their subject load suggests. If you want support in those subjects specifically, note that schools must ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold the appropriate authority approval, which is a higher bar than a general tutoring permit.

faqs.question: Is it true that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and the figure is worth correcting because a ranking page publishes it. The requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Verify it on moe.gov.ae before making a subject decision, because this is exactly the kind of number that gets copied between sites without checking.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education publish a points figure for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not in the source used for this page, which is why no figure appears here. The published equivalency detail covers the British and American routes in specifics — subject counts, minimum grades, SAT and IELTS or TOEFL thresholds — and says nothing about an IB points requirement. Any site quoting one without a ministry citation is guessing, and a family planning a Diploma around a guessed threshold is the one who pays for the error. Check moe.gov.ae or ask the school's university-guidance office, and treat the answer you get there as the only usable one.

faqs.question: Why did another school sit the same paper at a different time?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. The practical consequence is that comparing exam times with a friend at another school is unreliable, and so is a revision plan built on someone else's dates. Get the timetable from your own school, which holds it as the registered centre.

faqs.question: How long should we give a new tutor before deciding the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: About six sessions, judged against marked work rather than atmosphere. Six is long enough for a technique change to show up in a graded piece and short enough that nobody is paying out of inertia. Compare a marked script from before with one from after and ask the tutor to point at what changed and why. If the work between sessions was done and nothing moved, change the tutor rather than adding hours. If the work was not done, more hours will not fix it, and a tutor who claims otherwise is selling time.

faqs.question: What should we have ready before the trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take ten minutes to gather. The subject and level exactly as the school lists them, including which mathematics route or which language course. The exam board where one applies. The most recent marked piece of work, with the teacher's comments left on it. And the nearest internal deadline in the school's own calendar. With those, a trial can be spent on something real from this week rather than on a demonstration, which is the only way to find out whether this person can teach your child the thing your child is currently getting wrong.

faqs.question: Who teaches my child if the first choice stops being available?
faqs.answer: You are told before the next session, given a named alternative with their subject and level record, and the rate position is stated rather than adjusted quietly. Where no suitable specialist is free, there are three honest answers: a different time slot with the right person, a different person with a named compromise, or a wait with a date. Nothing researched for this project suggests any competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit at all, so ask the question of anyone you are considering and listen to how comfortable the answer sounds.

best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the four questions, then take the trial
best-ib-tutor.closingBody: The search that brought you here does not have a ranked answer, because no authority in the UAE ranks tutors. What it has is a set of checks: which subject and level this named person has taught and when, which permit category they fall into, what they will not do with assessed work, and how the lesson physically happens. Ask those four of anyone you are considering, including us. Then take the free trial lesson — one per student, booked without card details — and spend it on the topic your child is currently losing marks on. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and the written note afterwards tells you what the hour found.

Each profile names the syllabus codes that person has taught to a terminal series, because that is the single fact a parent can check against a statement of entry before any money moves.

intro.heading: What a value question looks like once you take the word "best" out of it
paragraphs: Searching for the best IGCSE home tutor in the UAE puts you in front of about a dozen providers who all use the same adjectives. Measured against each other in October 2026, the strongest page in this market ran to roughly 2,294 words, carried two tables, and refused to answer its own FAQ about price. Three of six ranking pages published no figure at all. Two quoted US dollars, a currency no family in Dubai or Abu Dhabi actually transacts a tuition invoice in. None of that is useful to a parent comparing two quotes on a Tuesday evening.

So treat the search as a procurement problem rather than a shopping one. You are buying a scarce teaching hour inside a fixed system: the school holds the licence, Cambridge or Pearson holds the specification, the emirate regulator holds the inspection file, and the federal Ministry of Education holds the equivalency rules your child's certificate will eventually be measured against. None of those things move because you hire a tutor. What a tutor changes is narrower and far more measurable — whether the student can answer the command term the paper actually uses, inside the time the paper actually allows.

That narrows the value question to three parts. First, is this person permitted to charge for private lessons in the UAE at all? That is a yes-or-no question with a free, two-year, government-issued answer, and it is the only credential in this market that a parent can verify without taking the provider's word for anything. Second, has this person taught the exact specification your child is entered for, through to a terminal series? Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 are not the same paper, and an hour spent on the wrong one is paid for and wasted. Third, what does the market charge for that, and does the quote in front of you sit inside the published band or outside it?

IGCSE home tutor cost in the UAE spans a wider range than any other line on a family's education budget. Published hourly figures run from AED 45 at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor. The same subject, the same tier, the same hour — fourteen times the price. Nothing about a rate at either end of that spread tells you about teaching quality on its own, which is precisely why price has to be read alongside the two checks above rather than instead of them.

This page is built to be read in that order: what the claims mean, what the permit proves, what the market charges, what the format changes, and what the calendar does to the value of an hour bought in October against the same hour bought in February. Every AED figure is attributed to the provider or the rate survey that published it. None of them is an IB Gram price list, and where this page needs to talk about our own arrangement it points to the first lesson at no charge and the consultation instead of inventing a number.

best-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE is not one qualification but a family of them, sat under two main boards with different entry mechanics, and reached from a lower-secondary stage that most UAE families never think about until the tier decision arrives. These are the four stages a tutoring plan actually has to fit around.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the shared content of a Cambridge IGCSE subject and is assessed on papers written for grades C to G. It is the right entry for a student who needs a secure pass across a wide timetable rather than a high grade in a narrow one. The constraint that matters is the ceiling: a Core entry cannot produce an A or A*, whatever happens in the exam room.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this tier decision is usually taken by the department head in Year 10, often on the strength of one internal assessment, and it is recorded on the entry the school submits to Cambridge months before the papers. A parent who wants a tier reviewed has to raise it while the entry is still amendable, not in the revision term. Ask the school's exams officer for the submitted tier in writing; it is the single most consequential line on the form.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended adds the supplement content and is assessed on papers written for grades A* to E. Most UAE British-curriculum schools enter the bulk of a cohort here for the sciences and mathematics, because A-Level and IB Diploma entry requirements are written in Extended-tier grades. The supplement topics are where the tutoring hours concentrate, since they are the part the Core teaching group never sees.
programmes.countryNote: Extended is the tier a UAE family usually needs if the plan runs towards A-Levels at a Dubai or Abu Dhabi sixth form, or towards the IB Diploma at one of the emirate's International Baccalaureate schools. It also matters for the Ministry of Education equivalency file, which counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 — a Core entry can clear that floor, but it cannot carry a competitive university application behind it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs on codes beginning 4, tiered as Foundation and Higher in mathematics and untiered in several other subjects. Exams are available in May/June and in November each year, and some subjects are structured so that units can be sat across more than one series. The practical consequence is that a Pearson cohort and a Cambridge cohort in the same emirate can be working to different deadlines in the same term.
programmes.countryNote: A number of UAE schools run a mixed entry — Cambridge for the sciences, Pearson for mathematics or English, sometimes split within one student's timetable. That is normal and it is also the commonest reason a tutoring hour misses. Before the first lesson, read the board and code for each subject off the statement of entry rather than the school prospectus, because the prospectus describes the curriculum and the statement describes what will actually be marked.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE, with Checkpoint tests offered in March, May and October. It carries no grade a university will ever read, which is exactly why it is the cheapest place to buy a correction. A Year 9 student who cannot rearrange an equation reliably will meet that same gap again in an Extended-tier algebra paper two years later, at four times the hourly rate.
programmes.countryNote: UAE families move schools and systems often — between emirates, between CBSE or American provision and a British curriculum, and in and out of the country. A student arriving into Year 9 from a different system is the clearest case for support at this stage, because the gap being closed is content the IGCSE specification assumes rather than content it teaches. Closing it in Year 9 costs a fraction of closing it in the Year 11 revision term.

best-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families ask about most, with the Cambridge and Pearson codes that decide which tutor is the right one. Each note says where marks actually go, because that is what an hour has to be spent on.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in the Emirates and the one most often mismatched by board. A Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tutor and a 4MA1 tutor are working from different question styles and different tiering language. Extended-tier marks drain away in algebraic manipulation, trigonometry in non-right-angled triangles, and the two or three multi-step problems per paper that carry no scaffolding.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical-skills component are where UAE candidates lose most. Students who can recite the formula for resistance routinely fail to read a circuit diagram with an ammeter in the wrong branch. The alternative-to-practical or practical-based component rewards a specific drill — reading scales, tabulating with consistent significant figures, plotting and drawing a line of best fit — that classroom time rarely has room for.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and the qualitative-analysis tables are the two blocks that decide the grade. The arithmetic is teachable in a handful of focused hours; the ion tests are memory work that has to be scheduled, not revised once. Organic chemistry sits late in most UAE school schemes of work, so it frequently arrives underdone three weeks before a paper.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to feel confident in. Marks are lost on command terms rather than knowledge: a question asking candidates to explain is answered with a description, and the mark scheme has nothing to give it. Data-handling questions on unfamiliar experiments are the other reliable gap, because they test method rather than recall.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · Pearson 4ES1)
subjects.description: Taken by a large share of UAE candidates, and routinely confused with First Language English. The two have different papers, different mark schemes and different value to a university file. Marks go missing in the directed-writing task, where candidates write well but ignore the audience, format or purpose the question specified.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: The reading passages carry more of the grade than most students believe. Summary and directed-writing questions are scored against a rubric that rewards selection and compression, not fluency. A strong writer with no summary technique loses marks on every paper, and that is a fixable, drillable gap rather than a talent problem.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 · Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the top band. Axes mislabelled, no shift arrow, no new equilibrium marked — the analysis may be sound and the marks still will not come. Evaluation questions need a judgement with a reason attached, and UAE candidates with strong content knowledge often stop at two-sided description.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 · Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole subject. Marks go to candidates who use the given business, its sector and its numbers; generic textbook answers score the lowest band however accurate they are. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are the most commonly skipped easy marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 · Pearson 4CP0)
subjects.description: Two very different halves: theory that is examinable by recall and problem-solving that is not. Pseudocode and trace tables reward practice on paper rather than at a keyboard. Binary, hexadecimal and data-representation questions are quick wins that students lose through arithmetic slips under time pressure.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Sat by some UAE candidates alongside the Ministry-mandated Arabic provision their school must deliver regardless of curriculum. Worth knowing that this subject, and Islamic Education, sit outside the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education counts for British-track equivalency, so its value to a file is academic rather than procedural.

best-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The regulator changes at the emirate border, and so does the depth of the local teaching pool. These notes say what each place does to a tutoring quote and to the wait for a specialist.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools licensed in 2024-25, 17 curricula, and UK provision the largest single share at 37% of enrolment. The deepest IGCSE teaching pool in the country and the widest rate spread — AED 45 and AED 650 are both advertised inside this one emirate.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here. Its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, which thins the evening pool exactly where families look first. An online IGCSE tutor in Dubai or further afield is often the realistic route to an Extended Chemistry specialist.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, courses and assessment methods. A Sharjah IGCSE timetable can therefore differ from a Dubai one in ways a visiting tutor who works across both emirates will not have noticed.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Inside ADEK's remit alongside Abu Dhabi, with a smaller British-curriculum cluster. A visiting Extended-tier Physics specialist free at 5pm on a Tuesday may simply not exist within reach, and the advertised in-home rate quietly reflects the distance rather than the teaching.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here are routinely quoted a visiting rate built around a Dubai-based tutor's drive, which is paid for in both dirhams and in the hour the student is actually alert.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like SPEA, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah returned zero mentions across the competitor pages surveyed for this market, which tells you how much local attention families here get.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, a small private-school cluster on the east coast, and a two-hour drive from the Dubai tutoring market. For an IGCSE subject with one or two teachers in the emirate, live video is less a preference than the only way to reach a specialist at all.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school cluster in the country, also under Ministry of Education supervision. A Cambridge 0620 or 4CH1 specialist is unlikely to be resident, so the honest comparison here is not visiting against online — it is online against nothing.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE entries in the country, spread across British-curriculum schools that sit in both Cambridge and Pearson entry patterns. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; the entry board and tier differ school by school and sometimes subject by subject within one timetable.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: A smaller but long-established British-curriculum cluster under ADEK. Evening availability is tighter here than in Dubai because of the professional-ethics position on school staff tutoring their own pupils, so families searching for an IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi more often end up matching outside the emirate.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Subject coverage thins quickly outside Sharjah city, which is where the value argument for one-to-one over live video is strongest.

modes.description: The default and the most measurable. One hour a week against a named syllabus code, with the week's work set against the next school assessment rather than against a generic revision plan. Progress is read off past-paper question types the student could not do in week one and can do in week six, which is a check a parent can apply without taking anyone's word for it.

modes.description: Where a family wants a fixed outlay rather than an open commitment, hours are bought as a block counted backwards from a specific paper or a specific school assessment. This is the format that makes the value argument visible, because the block has an end, a target component and a review point, and you can judge whether the next one is worth buying.

sections.heading: "Best" is a word nobody audits, so here are six checks that replace it
paragraphs: Every provider in this market describes itself in the same register, and not one of them is audited on it. There is no UAE authority that scores tutoring companies, no published league table for them, and no inspection report for a business that sells hours rather than places. KHDA inspects schools in Dubai. ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah. None of the three has anything to say about the person who will teach your child at seven o'clock this evening.

That leaves the adjective doing no work, so convert it into questions that can be answered inside a fifteen-minute call. Six claims recur across this market: experienced, qualified, examiner-led, regulator-recognised, results-driven and vetted. Two are verifiable in minutes. Two need a document the provider has to produce. One of them — regulator recognition for a tutoring company — usually means nothing, because the KHDA permit that genuinely exists is an Educational Services Permit issued to a training institute with premises, initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An online tutor matching service is not that thing, and any provider implying it is has told you something about itself.

The sixth claim, results-driven, is the one to press hardest. Competitor pages in this set publish a self-asserted 4.9 rating, a figure of 480 reviews beside a figure of 850 on the same page, and in one case a satisfaction percentage with no sample size, no date and no method attached. A number with none of those three attached is not evidence. Ask what n was, when it was measured and how, and listen to whether the answer arrives or the subject changes.

The table is the part of this page worth screenshotting before a call. Run the left column down the list, ask for the middle column, and treat the right-hand column as the point at which to stop paying attention to the rest of the pitch.

Ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and when it was issued
Ask for the figure behind any published rating: sample size, date and method
Ask what happens to the money if the match is wrong after one lesson

sections.heading: The one credential in this market that is free, dated and checkable
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page lists it as "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time. It is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any figure you see circulating for it should be treated as rumour.

Two things follow from this, and both are useful to a parent weighing value. The first is that there is no cost argument for not holding one. A permit that is free for two years is not a barrier to a serious tutor; a tutor who has not obtained one has made a choice. The second is that eligibility is broad on purpose. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students can all apply. That breadth is exactly why the permit answers the legality question and not the quality question.

There is a boundary inside the permit that matters in Abu Dhabi in particular. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the holder's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and verify it against the current policy document. The practical rule for a family is simple: do not go looking for your child's own class teacher privately, and be wary of any provider that offers to arrange it.

A permit also does not confer any of the things a parent might assume from the word licensed. It does not evidence subject knowledge, it does not evidence examiner status, and it does not certify a company. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. None of this is a reason to skip the permit question. It is a reason to ask it first and then keep asking.

sections.heading: What a UAE IGCSE hour costs, and who put each number into public
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition rates in AED are published by almost nobody in this market, which is odd given it is the first question every parent asks. Three of six ranking pages surveyed in October 2026 carried no price at all, and one of them asks the question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. The figures below were read off provider pages and off a Dubai 2026 rate survey, and each is attributed to whoever published it. They describe the market. They are not an IB Gram price list, and this page does not pretend to one.

Read the bands as information about a provider model rather than about a teacher. The budget online band is populated by platforms using university students and recent graduates, and at AED 45 to 65 an hour that model is honest about what it is. The qualified-subject-tutor band is where most serious IGCSE work sits. The in-home band carries travel inside the number, which is the single most under-examined line in UAE tutoring: you are paying for a drive from Al Barsha to Khalifa City at the same rate as the teaching. The premium band buys scarcity and reputation, and sometimes buys examiner status, which is worth asking about directly rather than inferring.

Monthly packaging muddies comparison further. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The Dubai rate survey's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Before comparing two monthly numbers, divide both back to an hourly rate and check how long a session actually is. A two-hour in-home session with a fourteen-year-old in week nine of a revision term is not two productive hours.

There is a context figure worth holding alongside all of this. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. School fees were held. Tutoring rates were not, because nobody approves them. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for schools — not for the tutor you hire privately. That asymmetry is the reason a tutoring quote needs reading in a way a school invoice does not.

sections.heading: A visiting arrangement and a specialist on screen, priced side by side
paragraphs: This page targets the phrase parents type, and the honest answer to it has two halves. The first half: a visiting IGCSE tutor is a real product in the UAE, widely advertised at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and for some families — a Year 9 student who will not settle at a screen, two siblings taught in one booking, a household with unreliable connectivity — it is a reasonable purchase. Nothing on this page argues otherwise, and a provider that pretends the visiting market does not exist is not being straight with you.

The second half: IB Gram does not sell it. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video. Home visits are part of what we offer in India, not in the Emirates. That is stated the same way on every country page on this site, and it is stated here before the comparison rather than after it, because a comparison written by the party that sells one of the options is only worth reading if the position is disclosed first.

With that out of the way, the comparison is mostly about pool depth, and pool depth is where the money is. A visiting arrangement selects from whoever can reach your address and be back for a second booking, which in practice is a radius of twenty to thirty minutes in Dubai traffic and considerably less usefully defined in Al Ain or Fujairah. Live video selects from everyone who has taught Cambridge 0620 or 4CH1 to a terminal series, in any time zone that overlaps the Gulf evening. For a high-volume subject in central Dubai those two pools may both be adequate. For Extended-tier Chemistry in Umm Al Quwain at 6pm, one of them is empty.

The arithmetic underneath is worth doing once. If a visiting tutor's rate carries a thirty-minute drive each way, roughly a third of what you pay funds a car. At AED 300 an hour that is AED 100 a session, AED 400 a month, and across a two-year IGCSE course something in the region of AED 9,000 spent on travel rather than teaching. The question is not whether the visiting model is bad. It is whether that money buys more sitting in the room than it would buy as additional specialist hours.

sections.heading: The code on the statement of entry decides whether an hour is worth anything
paragraphs: Of every pound of value destroyed in this market, the largest share goes on tutoring the wrong specification. A parent books a mathematics tutor; the tutor is fluent in Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tiering; the student is entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher. Both are real qualifications, both are called IGCSE in conversation, and the papers do not look alike. The student spends six weeks practising question styles that will not appear. Nobody is lying to anybody. The purchase was simply made from the wrong document.

The document to buy from is the statement of entry, which the school's exams officer produces for each candidate. It names the board, the subject code, the tier where there is one, and the components. The school prospectus describes the curriculum; the statement of entry describes what will actually be marked. Ask for it before the first lesson, not after the first invoice, and send it to whoever is matching the tutor. One UAE family in this situation discovered a mixed entry — Cambridge for the sciences, Pearson for mathematics — which is common and entirely normal, and which also means two different sets of specimen papers.

Board choice is a school decision, not a family one, so this is not a section about choosing. It is a section about reading. Where the two boards diverge usefully is in structure: Pearson's International GCSE sits on codes beginning 4 and offers May/June and November series, with some subjects structured across units; Cambridge runs June and November series with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The entry calendars therefore differ, and so does what a tutor should be doing in a given month.

One Cambridge administrative detail deserves more attention than it gets in the Gulf. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge's exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a UAE family that is not trivia. It is the reason to take paper dates from the school's own statement and timetable rather than from any page on the internet, including this one.

sections.heading: Where an IGCSE grade is actually bought, component by component
paragraphs: If value is the question, the useful unit is not the hour but the component. An IGCSE grade is assembled from separately weighted pieces, and those pieces are not equally responsive to teaching. Some move quickly under focused work, some move slowly, and one or two barely move at all in the time most families have. Spending the same hourly rate across all of them equally is how a budget disappears without the grade changing.

Exam technique on written theory papers is the fastest-moving piece, because the gap is usually procedural rather than conceptual. A student who writes a description when the question says explain, or who answers four parts of a six-part question because the first two took too long, is losing marks that a drill recovers. Practical-skills components behave similarly: tabulation, consistent significant figures, reading a scale, drawing a line of best fit. These are closed skills with right answers, and they respond to repetition faster than almost anything else on the paper.

Content gaps from an earlier stage move more slowly, and are the reason a Year 11 crisis is expensive. A student who cannot rearrange an equation reliably is not short of IGCSE teaching; they are short of Year 8 algebra, and that takes weeks rather than sessions. Coursework and extended-response work moves slowest of all, partly because it has to be the student's own, and partly because the criteria have to be understood before anything is drafted. The exact weighting of every component sits on the current subject specification at cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, and those are the pages to read before agreeing to a block of hours — the split differs by subject and is revised.

The practical consequence for a family deciding where the money goes: buy exam technique and practical-skills drilling early and in quantity, buy content repair as soon as it is identified rather than in the term before the paper, and buy coursework support as criteria teaching rather than as drafting help, because the alternative is not available at any price.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: paying to lift a ceiling the entry form has already set
paragraphs: The tier decision is the highest-leverage and least-discussed item in IGCSE spending. Cambridge's Core tier is assessed on papers written for grades C to G; Extended is assessed on papers written for grades A* to E. Pearson tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher and leaves several subjects untiered. Once the school has submitted the entry, the grade ceiling is fixed by the papers the candidate will sit, and no quantity of tuition reaches above it.

This produces two completely different spending problems, and they are frequently confused. A student entered for Core who is capable of more needs the entry reviewed, which is a conversation with the head of department and the exams officer while the entry is still amendable. Buying hours instead of having that conversation is the most expensive mistake available in this market, because the hours are real, the teaching is real, and the ceiling is still there on results day. A student entered for Extended who is at risk of a low grade has the opposite problem: the ceiling is high and the floor is the worry, and that is what tuition is actually good at.

There is also a budget argument for Extended that nobody makes out loud. Extended-tier teaching has to cover the supplement content, which the Core group never meets, and that content is where a disproportionate share of a tutor's hours go. A family that moves a student from Core to Extended in December is buying both the ceiling and the supplement, late. A family that settles the tier question in Year 10 buys the same supplement across eighteen months at whatever rate they prefer. The qualification is identical; the cost profile is not.

For the Ministry of Education equivalency file, the floor is what matters rather than the ceiling: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, as reported in the Ministry's July 2026 clarification. A Core entry can clear that floor. What a Core entry cannot do is carry a competitive application to a selective sixth form or a selective university behind it, which is why the tier question belongs in the first conversation about value and not the fifth.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E, and what the equivalency file does to your spending order
paragraphs: There is a procedural step most UAE families meet late and should meet early. A secondary certificate earned on a British curriculum has to be measured against the federal Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements before it works inside the UAE system. As reported in July 2026, the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that reorders a budget is this: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. One page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects. That is wrong, and acting on it means paying for an entry and a year of tuition nobody asked you for. Read the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it, and treat any version of it on a commercial page — including this one — as a prompt to go and check.

For families on the American track the shape is different again. English proficiency is satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that reporting, so no page should publish one — including pages that currently do. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or expedites. It is a process run by the authority, and the honest role of a tutor is to make sure the grades on the certificate clear the floor.

What this changes about spending order is concrete. Five subjects have to clear grade E or 3, and the two Ministry-mandated subjects your school delivers do not count towards them. Before buying hours in a subject your child enjoys, check that the five that will carry the file are safe. A family that spends a term lifting a borderline grade D to a C in a subject inside the five has bought something structural. A family that spends the same term on a sixth subject outside the count has bought enrichment and should know that is what it bought.

sections.heading: The Ministry hours already inside the fee you are paying
paragraphs: Before buying any additional teaching, it is worth knowing which teaching the school fee already contains. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind that is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations.

The rules around these subjects are unusually specific, and they constrain what any outside support may legitimately do. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details matter to a tutoring plan. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That last line is a real limit, not a formality: outside support here means helping a student access the school's own prescribed material, not substituting a parallel syllabus for it.

KHDA also requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That is a requirement on the school and its staff, and it is a useful question to put to a school rather than to a tutoring company. For a family budgeting IGCSE support, the practical read is that these hours are already funded inside the fee, they sit outside the five subjects the equivalency count uses, and they are the last place to add paid hours rather than the first.

sections.heading: The series counted backwards, and the weeks when the same hour is worth more
paragraphs: An hour of IGCSE tuition does not hold a constant value through the year, and the dates that change its value are published months in advance by the boards themselves. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Those windows are fixed by the board, not by the school, and everything a family does should be counted backwards from them.

The worked example below counts a Cambridge June series backwards, because June is the series almost every UAE candidate actually sits and the gap that catches families out sits near the top of it. Start at the papers and walk towards the present. The June window is the fixed point, published separately for each of the six administrative zones. Cambridge closes June entries in the spring, about four months out from the first paper, and that is the hard one: the exact day comes from the centre and is printed on the statement of entry rather than from anything a family can find online. Before it, hours can still change the entry itself — a tier, a subject, a late addition. Once it passes, the tier is set, the subjects are set, and tuition can only work inside the entry that exists. November then sits in the year as the resit route rather than as a second first attempt.

Pearson's published dates make the same point from the other direction. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the one after next, which is why every date on this page should be re-checked against the live official timetable rather than trusted from a commercial page.

Two UAE-specific timing factors sit on top of the board calendar. Ramadan shifts the shape of a teaching week — school hours compress, energy moves to the evening, and a late-afternoon slot that worked in January stops working. Live video handles that without renegotiating a drive: a session moves to a post-Iftar slot and keeps running. And the Cambridge zone rule means paper dates have to come from your own centre's timetable. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and using the wrong zone's timetable is a risk Cambridge explicitly says it cannot accept responsibility for.

sections.heading: What the highest price in this market must never buy
paragraphs: There is one product sold in this market that no family should buy at any rate. A provider in this set sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and the consequence lands on a sixteen-year-old's certificate rather than on a company's balance sheet. The same logic applies to IGCSE coursework and to any internally assessed component: the submitted work has to be the student's own.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and more useful than it sounds. A tutor explains the assessment criteria in the board's own language before anything is drafted. A tutor reads what the student has produced and marks it against those criteria. A tutor explains what the next version needs and why the current one does not get there. A tutor teaches the skill the criterion is testing. What a tutor does not do is author any part of a submitted piece, supply finished text, or edit a draft into something the student could not have produced. We say that in the first conversation, and a provider that will not say it plainly has told you what it sells.

The same boundary covers materials. IGCSE syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. The right thing to do is to reference them and link the official page — cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com — rather than hand out copies. A provider offering a library of mark schemes as a selling point is distributing someone else's copyright and has not thought hard about what else it is relaxed about.

The last piece of honesty belongs to availability. There are IGCSE codes and tier combinations for which no specialist is free at the hour a family wants, and the UAE's smaller emirates meet that more often than Dubai does. When it happens we say so and give the realistic match time rather than filling the slot with someone who last taught the subject at a different tier on a different board. A provider that is never unavailable is not well staffed. It is matching on availability rather than on the code, and you are the one paying for the difference.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, not the school name
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the document that names the board, the subject code, the tier and the components. A school name narrows the field to a curriculum; a statement of entry narrows it to the paper that will actually be marked. If it has not been issued yet, the exams officer can confirm the intended board and tier in writing.

process.title: A first lesson at no charge, one per family
process.description: One trial lesson per family, at no cost, booked through the consultation rather than by card. It is used as a diagnostic rather than a sales call: the tutor works through a past-paper question set on the student's own specification and forms a view on where the marks are currently going.

process.title: A written diagnostic you keep
process.description: After the trial you receive a short written note naming the components that need work, the question types the student could not complete, and an honest view of how many hours that is likely to take. It is yours whether or not you book anything, and it is the baseline the six-hour review is measured against.

process.title: Agree a block with a review point attached
process.description: Hours are agreed as a block scoped to named components and counted against a real date — a school assessment or a paper. The block has an end. That is deliberate: renewal should be a decision made on evidence rather than a subscription that continues because nobody cancelled it.

process.title: Review at six hours, in writing
process.description: At six hours we compare the current position against the week-one diagnostic, in writing, naming question types rather than impressions. If the gap has not moved, that is the moment to change tutor, change the component focus, or stop. Carrying on without that comparison is how tuition budgets quietly become permanent.

whyPoints.description: We match on the board, code and tier on the statement of entry rather than on the school's name or the subject in general. It is the difference between a tutor fluent in Cambridge 0580 tiering and one fluent in Pearson 4MA1 Higher, and it is the commonest reason a paid hour produces nothing.

whyPoints.title: The permit question asked first

We ask about it, we expect you to ask about it, and we treat the eligibility breadth of the permit as a reason to keep asking about subject depth separately.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line written down

It is not authored for the student and finished text is not supplied, at any price. A provider in this market sells completed assessments; the consequence of buying one falls on the student's certificate.
