best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four routes cover almost every IGCSE-shaped request from UAE families. The tier and the board matter more than the label: two children in the same Year 11 classroom can be entered for different papers in the same subject, and a tutor briefed on the wrong one wastes the term.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the shared part of the syllabus and is examined on its own papers - in Mathematics 0580 that is Paper 1 and Paper 3. The grades available run from G to C, so a child aiming higher has to move tier, not just work harder. Core is the right entry for a student who needs the subject securely rather than at depth, and it leaves more of the week for the subjects that carry the university application.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the tier decision is usually made by the school in Year 10 and entered months before the papers. Because Ministry of Education equivalency counts five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, a Core entry still counts towards the file - a point several families only discover after results day, when the choice is no longer reversible.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended tier adds the supplementary content and is examined on harder papers - Paper 2 and Paper 4 in 0580, with the full grade range to A*. Most UAE British-curriculum schools enter the majority of a cohort at Extended in the core subjects and use Core as a safety tier. The step up is in question structure as much as content: multi-step problems with no scaffolding, where a correct method scores nothing if the setting-out is unreadable.
programmes.countryNote: Extended entries are where UAE tuition demand concentrates, and where the subject-specialist shortage shows. Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1 and Arabic as a first language 0508 are regularly unavailable from a tutor within driving distance of Ajman or Fujairah, which is the practical argument for matching online across the whole country instead of one emirate.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs to its own specifications - 4MA1 in Mathematics A, 4PH1 in Physics, 4CH1 in Chemistry, 4BI1 in Biology - with Foundation and Higher tiers in place of Core and Extended. Some specifications allow a modular route, so a paper can be sat in one series and banked. Grading uses 9 to 1 rather than A* to G in most subjects, and the assessment objectives are written differently, which changes what a mark scheme rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Plenty of UAE schools run a mixed board policy: Cambridge for the sciences, Pearson for Mathematics, or the reverse. The statement of entry is the only reliable source, and the specification code on it is what a tutor needs. Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November, and a provisional timetable ahead of each one.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level, the step after
programmes.description: The IGCSE year matters partly because of what it gates. An International AS and A Level programme sets prior-attainment conditions subject by subject, and a grade 5 in Extended Mathematics rarely survives contact with A Level Further Mathematics. The Ministry's British-track equivalency rule asks for one A Level at no less than grade E, or two AS Levels at the same grade, on top of the five IGCSE subjects.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE families the sequencing question usually arrives in the spring of Year 11, when A Level option forms go out before IGCSE results. A tutor who knows the AS entry conditions at your child's school can tell you which Year 11 grade is actually load-bearing, and which one is simply a number on a certificate.

best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Syllabus codes are the shortest way to describe a request accurately. The codes below are the ones UAE families ask for most; each entry names where the marks tend to go, which is the part a tutor brief should start from rather than end with.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers per tier, no coursework. Extended candidates lose marks in the long structured questions - transformations, bearings, compound growth and the algebra of functions - where partial credit depends on visible working. A tutor should be marking against the published mark scheme format, not just checking answers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606 · Pearson Further Pure 4PM1)
subjects.description: Calculus, trigonometric identities, vectors and logarithms, sat alongside the main Mathematics entry. It is the single hardest UAE subject to staff locally, and the one where an online match across emirates changes the answer from no to yes. Differentiation of composite functions is the usual breaking point.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism produce more lost marks than any other topic, closely followed by the practical-skills paper, where candidates describe a method without naming the controlled variable. Extended candidates also need confident rearrangement of formulae under time pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles, titration arithmetic and organic reaction pathways carry the grade. The recurring error is a correct chemical idea written in language the mark scheme cannot credit - no state symbols, no balanced equation, no reference to the observation the question asked for.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance need precise terminology, and the six-mark extended responses reward sequenced explanation. Practical-skills questions on variables and reliability are a reliable source of easy marks that go unclaimed.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening components with a separate speaking endorsement. UAE candidates frequently have strong spoken English and weak exam-register writing, so the gain comes from register, paragraph control and answering the task set rather than from vocabulary drills.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and descriptive or narrative composition, plus reading analysis. Marks are lost in the reading passage questions, where candidates summarise instead of selecting and explaining the writer's method. Timed practice with annotated scripts is the only method that moves this one.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 · Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry disproportionate weight. Candidates who can define terms and draw a labelled diagram still stall on the eight-mark evaluation, where a judgement has to be made and justified rather than a list of points offered.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 · Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole game. Generic textbook answers score the low band; answers that use the figures and context given in the case score the top band. Calculation accuracy on ratios and break-even is the other half.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language (Cambridge 0508) and Arabic foreign language (0544)
subjects.description: Dubai schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, so support has to match the stream your child is actually in. Comprehension of unseen passages and controlled written structure are where the grade is decided.

best-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Which authority covers your child's school, emirate by emirate
best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The regulator is not an administrative detail; it decides what you can look up before you hire. Dubai and Abu Dhabi publish inspection findings a parent can read. The northern emirates sit under federal supervision, where the published material is thinner and the questions move to the school itself.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and published inspection material is the richest in the country. In 2024-25 Dubai had 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools running 17 curricula; the UK curriculum accounted for 37 per cent of that enrolment.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate - the regulator named by none of the competing tutoring sites we examined. Its professional-ethics rules for school staff are the reason a tutor brief here should never be your child's own classroom teacher.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi city, so the same licensing and ethics framework applies. Local specialist supply is thinner than in the capital, particularly at Extended tier in Additional Mathematics 0606, which is where cross-emirate online matching earns its place.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the regulator is why the board on the statement of entry should be confirmed before hours are booked.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. Published school-level detail is sparser than in Dubai, so the practical route is to ask the school directly for the board, the specification code and the tier entry per subject, in writing.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: RAK's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like SPEA, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. RAK returned zero mentions across the competitor pages we studied, which tells you how much attention the northern emirates get.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The subject-specialist pool within driving distance is the smallest in the country, so for Extended-tier sciences the realistic choice is a live online specialist rather than a local generalist.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain also falls under federal Ministry supervision. Families here often commute to schools in Sharjah or Ajman, which means a 4pm session rarely works and a 6.30pm or 7pm start is the honest planning assumption for weekday lessons.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai, licensed and inspected by KHDA
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's British-curriculum schools are the largest IGCSE cohort in the country, and KHDA's published inspection material is detailed enough to point a tutor brief at a specific weak strand rather than a whole subject. The curriculum and board each school is licensed to run are published on the regulator's own school listing.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, licensed by ADEK
schoolClusters.note: Capital-region families work under ADEK's licensing framework and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff. Those rules shape who may tutor whom, which matters more here than in any other emirate when a parent is choosing between a school teacher and an external specialist.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Sharjah schools answer to SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah to the Department of Knowledge; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry. Published school-level information thins out as you go north, so the statement of entry and a direct question to the school carry more weight here.

modes.description: A fixed weekly slot with the same tutor, built around the school's scheme of work and the specification code on the statement of entry. sections.heading: What can actually be checked before you hire anyone
paragraphs: No UAE authority ranks private tutors, publishes a tutor league table, or awards a quality mark to an individual. That means the phrase a parent types into Google has no verifiable referent, and the pages competing for it are mostly asserting rather than evidencing. The useful move is to replace the ranking question with a verification question: of everything a tutor profile claims, which claims produce a document, and which are decoration?

The table below sorts the claims this market actually makes. Two of them produce paperwork - the private tuition work permit and, for an institute with premises, the KHDA Educational Services Permit. One produces partial evidence if you ask the right follow-up, which is the examiner claim. The rest produce nothing at all, including the one at the top of every advert. That is not an accusation of dishonesty; it is a statement about what is checkable in a market with no tutor register.

Treat the trial lesson as the test for everything the paperwork cannot cover. Subject competence, pace, and whether a fourteen-year-old will talk to this person for an hour are not documentable in advance. What a trial can show in sixty minutes: whether the tutor names the specification code without being prompted, whether they mark against the mark scheme's language rather than their own, and whether they can say which two topics they would start with and why. A tutor who answers those three well has demonstrated more than any badge on a profile page.

sections.heading: The permit: the one filter that produces a document, and it is free
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting you a specific figure is quoting something that cannot be sourced.

The eligible categories are wider than most parents expect. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students can all hold the permit. That breadth is exactly why the permit is a floor rather than a ceiling: a permitted tutor may be a Year 13 student or a twenty-year veteran of Extended-tier Chemistry, and the document reads the same either way. It tells you the arrangement is lawful. It does not tell you the hour is worth AED 300.

A tuition centre is a different legal animal. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. So when a provider says it holds a KHDA permit, the honest reading is that an institute holds an institute permit - which says nothing about the individual teaching your child. IB Gram holds neither instrument and does not present itself as holding one.

sections.heading: Why your child's own subject teacher is the wrong answer
paragraphs: The most tempting shortcut in UAE tutoring is also the one a parent should decline. Asking the teacher who sets your daughter's mock papers to tutor her privately feels efficient: they know the scheme of work, they know her, and no briefing is needed. The professional rules point the other way. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics framework for private and charter school staff prohibits teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document itself, so verify the current wording with the school before relying on it - but the direction is unambiguous enough that no reputable platform should arrange such a match.

The reason is not bureaucratic. A teacher who is paid privately by some families in a class they also assess is placed in a conflict they cannot resolve. Internal marks, forecast grades, tier entry recommendations and set changes all run through that teacher. Forecast grades in particular are the school's own judgement, and Cambridge sets a published deadline for them in every series a UAE centre enters, June and November alike - a date the school owns rather than the family. Nobody benefits from those decisions sitting next to a private invoice.

The practical alternative is specific rather than vague. An external tutor who has never met the school can be briefed properly in one email: the board and specification code, the tier entry, the scheme-of-work position, the last two assessment scores and the teacher's written comment. That briefing takes ten minutes and buys independence. IB Gram does not match a student with a tutor employed by that student's own school, and parents who ask us to are told why not.

sections.heading: Five authorities, one country: what each one lets you look up
paragraphs: The regulator map is the piece of UAE context the competing pages simply do not carry. Across the sites examined for this project, ADEK was named by nobody and SPEA appeared once, inside a lead-generation widget. That is a strange gap, because the regulator decides what information about your child's school is public, and public information is what a tutor brief should be built from.

Two of the five publish material you can read before you hire. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and its inspection reporting is granular enough to name a weak strand within a subject. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes school ratings alongside its staff ethics rules. In both emirates the useful move is to read the published findings for the subject you are considering tutoring, and to book against the specific weakness it names instead of against the subject as a whole.

The other three change the questions rather than the answers. SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools. Where published school-level detail is thin, the substitute is a direct written question to the school: which board, which specification code, which tier, which series. A school will answer that in a sentence, and the answer is worth more than any inspection summary.

sections.heading: The specification code decides what good even means
paragraphs: Exactly one syllabus code appeared across an entire seven-page competitor cluster we examined. That is the clearest signal available that the market is selling tutoring in the abstract. An IGCSE is not one qualification: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 cover overlapping content through different papers, different assessment objectives and different grading scales, and a tutor fluent in one is not automatically fluent in the other.

The statement of entry settles it. It carries the board, the specification code, the tier and the series, and it is the document a tutor brief should quote. Parents who cannot find it should ask the examinations officer for the entry details in writing, which is a routine request. Where a school runs a mixed board policy - Cambridge sciences with Pearson Mathematics is a common UAE pattern - the code differs by subject within the same child's timetable, and a single tutor covering two subjects needs both.

Grading differs in ways that matter to a conversation about targets. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G in most subjects; Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1 in most. Some Pearson specifications allow a modular route, so a component can be sat in an earlier series and banked, which changes the planning calendar completely. A tutor who asks for the code in the first email has told you something about how they work before they teach a single lesson, and a tutor who never asks will be planning from a textbook rather than from the paper your child will sit.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in this market, with every figure attributed
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages studied for this project publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars - a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here is the market in AED, with the source of each figure named. These are published market rates collected in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list; our own model starts with a trial lesson and a consultation, because the right number depends on the subject, the tier and how many weeks are left.

The spread is the useful information. The same hour of IGCSE Mathematics is sold at AED 33 and at AED 650 in this market, and the difference is not a twentyfold difference in teaching. At the low end you are usually buying a university student's time with no marking and no planning. In the middle you are buying a qualified subject teacher. At the top you are usually buying scarcity, a reputation, or an examiner claim - and the examiner claim is the one worth asking to see in writing, because current examiner status is a checkable fact and an old one is not.

Two line items are routinely left out of a quote. The first is marking: an hour of teaching plus annotated written work takes the tutor longer than an hour, and a rate that includes it is not comparable to one that does not. The second is travel, which only arises for a visiting tutor - Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors to AED 500, and the travel sits inside the fee rather than beside it. Ask what an hour includes before comparing two hourly rates.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live one-to-one online, under UAE conditions
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real and reasonable thing to want, and it is what most UAE parents mean when they start searching. It is worth answering honestly. A visiting tutor gives you a person in the room, paper scripts marked in front of the child, and no dependence on a connection. The published market rate for that in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, and the practical constraint is geography: your choice narrows to the specialists willing to drive to your address for that slot on that day.

That narrowing is the cost nobody prices. For Extended-tier Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language 0508 or Further Pure 4PM1, the pool of tutors within reach of Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain is very small, and in some weeks it is empty. A family then takes a generalist who is available rather than a specialist who is not - and the hour is cheaper to buy and worth less to have. Travel also compresses the usable evening: a 4pm start rarely survives a school run, and a tutor crossing Dubai at 6pm is pricing the traffic into your fee whether the invoice says so or not.

IB Gram does not arrange home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with scripts screen-shared and annotated during the hour and saved afterwards. The argument for it is not that screens are better than rooms. It is that a family in Fujairah gets the Extended-tier Chemistry specialist instead of whoever lives twenty minutes away, the lesson starts on the hour with no travel either side, and the same tutor continues through a summer spent abroad.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the week a tutor does not own
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies. So a Year 11 timetable carrying nine IGCSEs also carries these, and the hours have to come from somewhere.

The rules are specific enough to constrain how support can be described. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab pupils and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for others. Schools are required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects - a credential question that applies to the school's staff, and a reasonable thing to ask about.

Two practical points follow. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and any mandatory-subject lesson is advised to run at least 25 minutes - so these subjects are not a rounding error in the week. And the use of any different or additional content for them, without prior permission from the Ministry, is strictly prohibited. Support for these subjects therefore works from the school's own set content, in the stream the child is placed in, and never from substitute material a tutor prefers.

sections.heading: The five-subject rule a good IGCSE tutor already knows
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the quiet reason some Year 11 subject choices matter more than they look. For the British track, a student must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One page currently ranking for these queries tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, and getting that wrong in either direction changes a family's planning.

Note what the rule does not say. It sets a floor, not a target: grade E or grade 3 is a pass threshold for the equivalency file, not an entry standard for a competitive university course. A Core tier entry still clears it. Equivalency is also a Ministry process, not a tutoring product - IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee any part of it, and no tutor should imply that hiring them is a step in it. The honest service is simply knowing the rule exists and flagging the subject count before results day rather than after.

For comparison, the American track asks for English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold appears in the sources this project can cite, so none is published here. Verify every figure on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation channel before you act on it.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: One of the sites competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a malpractice route that puts the student's certificate at risk and the parent's money with it. The boundary worth stating plainly: a tutor teaches the skill, reviews the student's own draft, and gives feedback the student then acts on. A tutor does not author, part-author or finish an assessed piece, does not supply text to be pasted in, and does not sit beside a controlled assessment. If a provider offers any of that, the offer itself tells you what you are buying.

The same line applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge International and Pearson. They are to be referenced and linked from the boards' own sites, not reproduced or handed over as downloads by a tutoring provider. A tutor can absolutely work through a past paper the student has legitimately obtained from the school or the board's published material, mark it against the published mark scheme format, and explain where the credit sits. What a tutor should not do is run a private library of board-owned documents.

Where this gets practical is a deadline at 9am tomorrow. The useful answer in that hour is triage, not authorship: identify which question is worth the remaining time, what the mark scheme is actually asking for, and what the student can realistically write themselves before the deadline. That is slower comfort than a finished draft, and it is the only version that leaves the grade attributable to the student. Say it out loud to a tutor before you book, and see how they answer.

sections.heading: When the best tutor is already booked: the UAE year against the series
paragraphs: Availability is the part of this market nobody discloses. The specialist you want for Extended-tier Chemistry in March is usually booked by November, because UAE demand concentrates in the same eight weeks every year. The calendar below is built from the boards' own published key dates, and the point of it is simple: the decisions that cost nothing in September cost a great deal in April. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

The entry deadline is the date most families miss, and the two series a UAE centre actually enters make the point cleanly. Cambridge closes final entries for June in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and for November a comparable distance ahead of its own October to November window; the exact day is fixed per series, comes from the centre and is printed on the statement of entry rather than from anything written on a tutoring site. Pearson has the same shape with firmer public dates attached: its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, on entries submitted long before the autumn term got going, and its November results reach students in January. Either way the tier entry locks months before anyone opens a paper. There is a second trap on top of it - every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

Ramadan and the UAE term calendar reshape the revision block rather than the exam window. Weekday lessons move later, often to a post-Iftar slot, and the tutors who can hold a 9pm slot are fewer than those who can hold 5pm. Families who want that window should ask for it in advance rather than in week one of the month. The other fixed point is results: Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - which is the week a retake decision has to be made, not the week to start thinking about it.

sections.heading: What we do when no specialist is free for your subject
paragraphs: Not one competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit. Several route UAE parents to a +91 number without saying where the teaching happens. Disclosure is cheaper than discovery, so here is ours. Mainstream Extended-tier requests - Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1, the three sciences, English, Economics and Business - are usually matched within a few days. Narrower requests take longer: Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, Arabic as a first language 0508, Computer Science 0478 and the second-language modern foreign languages are the ones where a specific slot may not exist in a given week.

When that happens there are three honest options, and we will say which applies. The first is a later or earlier slot with the specialist you want, which usually means an evening on Gulf Standard Time. The second is a different specialist with adjacent experience - a Mathematics tutor who has taught 0606 but not 4PM1, briefed on the difference, which works for topic repair and less well for whole-course coverage. The third is a wait, with a date. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of an Extended-tier exam-year student and describe them as a specialist.

The same transparency applies to the trial. One trial lesson per family, at no charge, with no card required to book it, and no obligation afterwards. It exists so you can test the things the paperwork cannot show: whether the tutor names the specification code unprompted, whether they mark in the language of the mark scheme, and whether your child will actually talk to them. If the answer to any of those is no, say so and take a different tutor. The hour was the point.

process.description: The first message that helps us is short and specific: the school and emirate, the board and specification code, the tier entry, the series your child is entered for, and the last two assessment marks. The statement of entry carries most of it. Without the code we are guessing at papers, and guessing wastes the first fortnight.

process.title: We shortlist, and send you what you can check
process.description: You get two or three profiles naming the syllabus codes each tutor has taught, the tiers, the components they have marked, and confirmation that they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. We do not shortlist a tutor employed by your child's own school. Ask for anything on the profile to be evidenced.

process.title: One free trial lesson, conditions stated here
process.description: One trial lesson per family at no charge, no card needed to book it, no obligation afterwards. Use it to test what documents cannot show: does the tutor name the code unprompted, do they mark in the mark scheme's language, and will your child talk to them for an hour? A no on any of those is a reason to try someone else.

process.title: A written baseline inside two lessons
process.description: After the trial and the first paid lesson you get two or three lines in writing: the topics costing the most marks, the component they sit in, and the order the tutor will take them in. It is deliberately short enough to argue with. A plan you cannot challenge in a sentence is not a plan.

process.title: Review points set by the series, not the term
process.description: Review dates are counted backwards from the series on the statement of entry - entry deadline, mock window, the last full timed paper, then the exam period itself. Each review asks one question: is this working, and what should change? Stopping is always a legitimate answer, and we would rather you stopped than drifted.

whyPoints.title: Claims that come with paperwork
whyPoints.description: Every tutor brief starts from documents a parent can see: the private tuition work permit, the specification code, the tier entry. We hold no regulator accreditation and we do not imply one. Where a fact on this page comes from KHDA, MoHRE, the Ministry or a board, it is attributed so you can check it yourself.

whyPoints.title: No tutor from your child's own school
whyPoints.description: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct points the same way. We will not arrange that match even when a family asks, because the person writing forecast grades should not also be invoicing you.

whyPoints.title: The whole country, not one commute
whyPoints.description: Delivering one-to-one over live video means a family in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain draws on the same specialist pool as one in Dubai. For Additional Mathematics 0606 or Arabic as a first language 0508 that is the difference between a specialist and whoever happens to be nearby.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can trace to a source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a published market rate with the provider named and the month stated, not an invented band. We will not quote a hard price before knowing the subject, the tier and the weeks remaining, because the number would be fiction. The trial lesson and the consultation come first.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line, stated before you ask
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, reviews and gives feedback on your child's own work. Coursework is never authored or finished for a student, board documents are linked rather than handed over, and no grade is promised by anyone. If that rules out what you were hoping to buy, better to know now.

faqs.question: Nobody ranks IGCSE tutors in the UAE, so what should I compare instead?
faqs.answer: Compare documents and specifics. Three things are checkable before you pay: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is issued free for two years; the syllabus codes and tiers the tutor has actually taught, year by year; and whether they mark against the published mark scheme format. Then use the trial lesson for the things no document covers - whether they name your child's specification code without prompting, which two topics they would start with, and whether a fifteen-year-old will engage with them for an hour. A tutor who answers those well has shown you more than any badge on a profile.

faqs.question: My shortlist all sound identical on paper. What should the trial lesson actually test?
faqs.answer: Set it three tasks. Ask the tutor to open with your child's own recent script rather than a generic worksheet, mark one question aloud against the mark scheme's wording, and finish by naming the two topics they would prioritise and why. That hour tells you whether they work from evidence or from a lesson plan they brought with them. Watch for the specification code: a tutor who asks for 0580 versus 4MA1 before the lesson has told you how they operate. Afterwards ask for two written lines. If nothing in writing arrives, that is also information.

faqs.question: A tutor quotes AED 400 an hour for IGCSE Maths. What would justify that in this market?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for a specialist sit around AED 200 to 450 and above - TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table runs AED 200 to 450 and above - so AED 400 is inside the specialist band rather than outside it. What should come with it: marked written work between lessons, a plan tied to your child's specification and tier, and a verifiable teaching history on that exact code. What does not justify it: an unevidenced examiner claim, a long list of school names, or a star rating the provider gave itself. Ask what the hour includes before comparing it with a cheaper one.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE tutor be able to tell me about my daughter's syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Which board it belongs to, which papers it examines, what the tier ceiling is, and where candidates typically lose marks on it. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier that means Paper 2 and Paper 4, grades to A*, and marks lost in multi-step structured questions where working has to be visible. For Pearson 4MA1 the papers, the grading scale and the assessment objectives differ. A tutor who treats the two as interchangeable will teach the wrong paper structure for a term, and that is a term you do not get back.

faqs.question: Is a former examiner automatically the better choice for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No, and the claim needs care. Examiner experience can help a tutor explain how credit is awarded, but it is only useful if it is current, for the right board and the right subject, and evidenced in writing. Past examining tells you less than recent teaching of the exact specification. It also gives no access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, and a tutor who hints otherwise is misrepresenting what the role is. Treat an unevidenced examiner badge the way you would treat any unverifiable claim: interesting, not decisive, and no reason to pay a premium.

faqs.question: Our son's school is licensed in Sharjah. Does the emirate change who we should hire?
faqs.answer: It changes what you can look up rather than who can teach him. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the regulator, not only inspection. Practically, confirm the board and specification code with the school in writing before booking hours, because that is the detail a tutor brief depends on. Since lessons run over live video, the tutor does not need to live in Sharjah - and for a narrow subject at Extended tier, insisting on one would shrink your choice for nothing.

faqs.question: Why would you refuse to arrange a tutor who teaches at my child's own school?
faqs.answer: Because the rules and the incentives both point against it. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics framework prohibits private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond compliance, that teacher may set internal assessments, submit forecast grades and recommend tier entry. None of those judgements should sit next to a private invoice. An external tutor briefed properly in one email gets you the same subject knowledge without the conflict.

faqs.question: What paperwork can I reasonably ask to see before the first IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit and its validity dates, which is a fair request because the permit is free and lasts two years, so there is no cost reason to be without one. Also ask for the specification codes and tiers taught by year, and which components the tutor has marked. If a provider tells you it holds a KHDA permit, ask which one: the KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises and says nothing about an individual tutor. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and will tell you so rather than blur the point.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the tutor may not be based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It matters that you are told, and that the arrangement is lawful and workable. IB Gram delivers tutoring for UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are offered only in India. What should not change is the brief: the same specification code, the same tier, the same school scheme of work. Ask how scripts are shared and marked, and whether the recording and data handling are explained to you. Several competing sites conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number, which is a different thing from disclosing it.

faqs.question: Nine IGCSEs and two tutors already. How do I tell which hours are working?
faqs.answer: Measure against papers, not against feelings. Ask each tutor for a timed section marked to the published mark scheme format every three or four weeks, and compare the mark on the same component over time. A tutor who cannot produce that is teaching without a measure. Also look at where the marks move: a jump in recall questions with no change in extended responses means the hours are landing on the easier half of the paper. Two subjects honestly reviewed beat four drifting along, and dropping an hour that is not working is a legitimate outcome of a review.

faqs.question: How many hours a week make sense for a Year 11 IGCSE student here?
faqs.answer: For most families one hour a week per supported subject, plus marked work in between, with no more than two subjects running at once. Bestimate's UAE monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, so three subjects simultaneously becomes a significant monthly commitment. The constraint is usually the student's week rather than the budget: nine IGCSEs plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies already fills the timetable.

faqs.question: What is the honest answer when no specialist is free for my son's subject?
faqs.answer: You get told which of three things applies. Either a specialist is available at a different hour, usually a later Gulf Standard Time evening; or an adjacent-experience tutor can be briefed on the difference, which suits topic repair better than whole-course coverage; or there is a wait, with a date attached. Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1 and Arabic as a first language 0508 are the requests where this comes up most. What will not happen is a generalist being placed in front of an Extended-tier exam-year student and described as a specialist.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between helping with IGCSE coursework and doing it?
faqs.answer: The student writes every word that is assessed. A tutor teaches the skill the task needs, reads the student's own draft, and gives feedback the student then acts on themselves. A tutor does not author or finish a piece, supply text to be pasted in, or sit beside a controlled assessment. The same line applies to materials: board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked from Cambridge's and Pearson's own sites, not handed over as a private library. A provider offering completed work is telling you what it sells, and the risk lands on your child's certificate.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE grade profile need anything extra for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education equivalency rule for the British track asks for five accredited subjects on GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That is a floor for the equivalency file, not an admissions standard, and a competitive course will ask for much more. Verify every detail on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation channel; equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan, and does that change the price?
faqs.answer: Lessons can move, and the rate does not change for the hour of day. What changes is availability: fewer tutors hold a 9pm or 9.30pm slot than a 5pm one, so ask for the Ramadan schedule several weeks before the month rather than during its first week. The practical approach is to agree the altered slot and a shorter session length in advance, keep the marked work between lessons steady, and treat the term break that follows as recovery time rather than as a revision block that will not happen.

faqs.question: We are moving from Abu Dhabi to Dubai mid-year. Does the tutor have to change?
faqs.answer: No, and that is one practical advantage of online delivery. The tutor stays, the slot stays, and the brief updates. What does change is the regulator and possibly the board: schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed by ADEK, Dubai schools by KHDA, and the new school may enter your child for a different specification or tier in the same subject. Get the new statement of entry, send the codes and tier to the tutor, and expect a fortnight of overlap work while the two schemes of work are reconciled. Mid-year moves cost marks in sequencing, not in ability.

best-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the statement of entry, not with a shortlist
best-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to a useful IGCSE match is one message containing five things: the school and emirate, the board, the specification code, the tier entry, and the series your child is sitting. From that we can shortlist tutors who have taught that exact code at that exact tier, and show you the permit and the teaching history behind each one. Then take the free trial lesson - one per family, no card needed, no obligation - and judge the hour on what you saw. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we will tell you plainly when a specialist is not free rather than filling the slot.

intro.heading: What a family is actually paying for when it leaves A Levels for the Diploma
paragraphs: British-curriculum families in the UAE reach this decision at a predictable moment: the IGCSE results are in, the sixth form offers both routes, and somebody at a school open evening has described the Diploma as broader and harder. Both descriptions are true and neither is useful for deciding. The decision is about what the next two years will cost in time, in money and in the particular kind of attention a Diploma asks a household to supply, and about what the family gets in exchange.

Start with the structural difference, because every cost follows from it. A Level students in the UAE typically take three subjects, sometimes four, and nothing else. A Diploma student takes six subjects across six groups — language and literature, a second language, individuals and societies, a science, mathematics and an arts or elective — with three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. On top of those sit three core requirements: a 4,000-word Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge with an essay of about 1,600 words and an exhibition, and the CAS programme of creativity, activity and service. The maximum score is 45, of which three points come from the combination of Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades.

That shape produces three cost lines a family should see before committing. The first is subject support: six subjects means six possible points of failure rather than three, and the subject a student is weakest in is a Standard Level they did not choose but had to take to fill a group. The second is the core, which no school teaches in a single timetabled lesson and which almost every Diploma family ends up supporting in some way. The third is unpriced and real: the Diploma occupies evenings and weekends in a way three A Levels do not, and that falls on whoever in the house is managing deadlines.

The school-fee side is unusually favourable this year, which is worth knowing before anyone negotiates. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Supply is also rising: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A family choosing a Diploma place has more leverage than the same family had two years ago.

On tutoring, this page quotes the market rather than a price list. Published rates in Dubai run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 or above for exam-year specialists, and AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where travel is priced in. Those figures belong to the providers and rate tables that published them, named in the tables below. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on the subject's scarcity and the level, and a figure printed here would be a figure we had to defend rather than one you could rely on.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, to families in every emirate. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Diploma family that is usually the better arrangement, because the scarce thing is not proximity but a Higher Level specialist in the right subject who can also supervise an internal assessment properly.

british-curriculum-to-ib-transition.programmesIntro: Four routes a British-curriculum family is choosing between at 16, each with a different cost profile and a different set of doors at 18. The Diploma is one of them, not the default.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, assessed by external examinations and internal assessments in every subject. The core adds a 4,000-word Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge with an essay of around 1,600 words and an exhibition, and CAS. Scores run to 45 points, with three awarded from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, International Baccalaureate students made up 7 per cent of the private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula, so the Diploma is a minority route here with a strong institutional base. Three of the seven schools opening for 2026-27 are IB, which means more places and more competition for experienced Diploma teachers at the same time.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study and its own core, including a reflective project and personal and professional skills. Less common in the UAE than the full Diploma but offered by some schools, and genuinely useful for a student who wants two academic subjects in depth alongside a vocational focus.
programmes.countryNote: Worth asking about if your child's IGCSE profile is uneven — strong in two subjects, weak in a third that a full Diploma would force them to carry. Availability in the UAE is limited and varies by school, so confirm with the sixth form directly rather than assuming the IB label covers it.

programmes.name: Cambridge or Pearson A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken in depth, with AS available as a standalone qualification after one year in the Cambridge system. No compulsory breadth, no core, and no second language requirement. Assessment is almost entirely terminal written papers, with practical endorsement in the sciences depending on the board and specification.
programmes.countryNote: The route most British-curriculum UAE schools default to, and the cheaper one to support: three subjects means three possible tutoring lines rather than six plus a core. For a student with a clear single direction — medicine, engineering, architecture — the depth is an advantage and the breadth of the Diploma is a tax.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma in an IB continuum school, assessed against criteria A to D in each subject group with a Personal Project in the final year. Students arriving into DP1 from MYP are already fluent in criterion-based marking, command terms and reflective writing, which is the single largest difference between them and an IGCSE arrival.
programmes.countryNote: This is the comparison a British-curriculum family should make honestly. A DP1 cohort in a Dubai IB school usually contains both MYP continuers and IGCSE arrivals, and the IGCSE arrivals spend the first term learning criteria-based assessment that the others have used for five years. That first term is where support money is best spent.

british-curriculum-to-ib-transition.subjectsIntro: These notes are about cost and risk rather than content. For each subject, where an IGCSE background puts a student ahead, and where the Diploma version turns out to be a different animal that needs paid help.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route for students heading to engineering, physics, economics or mathematics. HL is the most demanding single subject in most Diploma timetables and the most common reason a British-curriculum arrival buys weekly support from term one. Proof, series and complex numbers are the usual breaking points; the exploration is the usual deadline crisis.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with a technology-permitted assessment design. Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches because the content is more self-contained, but the HL statistics and the exploration still absorb hours. Check the university prerequisite before choosing it to save money — some engineering courses want Analysis.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A comfortable transfer from IGCSE 0625 or 4PH1 in content and an uncomfortable one in style: the Diploma expects uncertainty treatment, graph linearisation and extended explanation as a matter of routine. The internal assessment, an individual investigation, is where unsupported students lose most, and where supervision rather than teaching is what is needed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole work and organic mechanisms arrive in reasonable shape from IGCSE. Energetics, equilibrium and the HL organic sequence are new in depth, and the data-based question rewards a habit of reading the booklet rather than recalling a value. Commonly the second subject a family adds support in, after mathematics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the cost here. Diploma Biology is wide, examined with precise command terms, and unforgiving of approximate definitions. Students strong at IGCSE 0610 often underestimate it for a term and then need a concentrated block, which is more expensive than the steady weekly hour they declined in September.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Where IGCSE English leaves a student well prepared in writing and poorly prepared in apparatus. The individual oral, the HL essay and the paper on unseen texts all want analysis of how meaning is constructed in context. A strong IGCSE grade is no predictor here, which is why families are surprised by the first DP1 report.

subjects.name: English B and other Group 2 languages
subjects.description: The group that catches British-curriculum arrivals who dropped their language after Year 9. A second language is compulsory in the Diploma, and the realistic options are to resume one at ab initio or Standard Level, or to take the student's home language where the school offers it. This is a cost line nobody plans for and it is often the cheapest to fix early.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Popular with British-curriculum arrivals and genuinely different from IGCSE 0455. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles against specific criteria, which is a research-and-writing skill rather than a content one, and it is the component that most often needs structured supervision rather than subject teaching.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven with a substantial internal assessment, and at HL a pre-released case study that the whole cohort prepares. Students arriving from IGCSE Business Studies find the content familiar and the evaluation demands unfamiliar: recommendation and justification carry the marks, and generic answers sit at the bottom of the band.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a historical investigation with a formal structure and a source-evaluation section, and the HL extension adds depth study with its own paper. IGCSE History arrivals have the source skills; what they lack is the scale of reading, which is a time cost rather than a tutoring cost.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Fieldwork-based internal assessment plus HL core extension topics. The data skills transfer from IGCSE 0460 but the Diploma's synthesis questions ask students to argue across units, which is a habit that has to be taught and is cheap to teach early and expensive to teach in DP2.

subjects.name: Visual Arts, Theatre and Music
subjects.description: Group 6 choices with heavy portfolio and process requirements, assessed against criteria over two years rather than in an exam week. Support here is almost entirely process coaching: journals, documentation, deadlines. Families who treat these as the easy subject in the timetable usually discover otherwise in DP2.

british-curriculum-to-ib-transition.regionsTitle: Where the Diploma is available, and what that does to the price
british-curriculum-to-ib-transition.regionsIntro: Diploma provision in the UAE is concentrated, which affects both school choice and tutor availability. These notes are about supply and its effect on what a family ends up paying.

regions.name: Dubai: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: The densest Diploma provision in the country sits in this corridor, and so does the deepest pool of experienced IB teachers. That has a price effect in both directions: more places to negotiate over, but also local tutors who know they are scarce. Three of the seven schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 are IB, which adds capacity here first.

regions.name: Dubai: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Newer communities where IB and British-curriculum campuses have opened close together, so families often choose between the two routes without changing school group. The practical constraint is the bus run rather than availability: a 6.30pm or 7pm online session holds better here than a 5pm one.

regions.name: Dubai: Deira, Garhoud and Mirdif
regions.note: Established schools, several running the Diploma alongside other curricula, and a long commute for anyone attending a sixth form on the other side of the creek. Evening sessions have to be scheduled after the return journey, which is the single most common reason a weekly slot gets moved.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Diploma provision is real but thinner than Dubai's, and ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which removes the cheapest-looking option and makes an independent specialist the practical one.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under ADEK, with a small number of schools and real distances between them. A family here choosing the Diploma is often choosing the only Diploma available, which removes negotiating leverage on fees and makes subject-level support a question of online matching rather than local search.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. Diploma places are limited, so a number of Sharjah families commute into Dubai for sixth form and absorb an hour of traffic each way into the daily cost of the route.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah and the Northern Emirates
regions.note: Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by the Department of Knowledge; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma provision is sparse, and Higher Level specialist cover in the local market is sparser. Online matching is the realistic route rather than the convenient one.

regions.name: Al Ain and Abu Dhabi schools offering both routes
regions.note: A growing number of UAE schools run A Level and the Diploma side by side, which is the cheapest place to make this decision because the child does not have to change school to change route. Ask the sixth form how many students sit each, and how many teachers hold IB examiner or workshop experience in the subjects you care about.

schoolClusters.note: Schools running the IB Diploma in Dubai, inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Several also offer A Level or another curriculum in the same building, which is worth knowing when a family wants to compare routes without comparing schools.

schoolClusters.note: Outside Dubai the choice between A Level and the Diploma is often a choice between two schools rather than two routes in one. sections.heading: The honest price of breadth, in one answer
paragraphs: A British-curriculum family moving to the Diploma should expect to support more subjects, for longer, than the same family would on A Levels, and the reason is arithmetic rather than difficulty. Three A Levels give three places where a student can be weak. Six Diploma subjects plus three core components give nine, and at least one of those six subjects will be one the student did not want and took to fill a group. In practice the subjects that need paid help in a Diploma are rarely the Higher Levels the student chose; they are the Standard Level the timetable chose for them, and the core.

Put rough numbers on it from published market rates rather than from ours. A qualified subject tutor online in Dubai runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above. One weekly hour in one subject across a 30-week school year is therefore an order of magnitude families can model themselves; two subjects plus a core block is roughly double it. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions put budget support at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more.

What a family gets for that is not a higher score — nobody can promise one, and this page does not — but a different kind of two years. The Diploma's value is in the components A Levels do not have: a 4,000-word independent research project with a supervisor, a reflective course that forces a student to interrogate how claims are made, and a compulsory second language. Universities that like the Diploma like it for those things. A student who treats them as box-ticking has bought the expensive route and taken none of the benefit.

The other half of the honest answer is who should not make this move. A student with a single clear direction and an uneven IGCSE profile is usually better served by three A Levels in their strengths. A student who dropped languages at 14 and dislikes writing will find the Diploma's compulsory breadth a two-year tax with no payoff. Those are real cases, and a tutoring company telling every family the Diploma is the right answer is selling rather than advising.

sections.heading: Three A Levels against six Diploma subjects, compared properly
paragraphs: Most comparisons of these two routes are written by someone selling one of them. The useful version compares what a week actually contains, what is assessed, and what each route closes. On contact hours, three A Levels and six Diploma subjects occupy roughly similar timetabled time, because the Diploma spreads the same school day across more subjects at shallower depth per subject — Standard Level sits somewhere below A Level depth, Higher Level somewhere near it.

Assessment is where the routes separate. A Levels are overwhelmingly terminal: the grade arrives from written papers in a single series, with practical endorsement in some sciences. The Diploma assesses internally in every subject — an exploration in mathematics, an individual investigation in the sciences, commentaries in economics, a historical investigation — and those internal assessments carry a fixed share of each subject grade and fall due across DP1 and DP2 rather than at the end.

That difference is the one that costs money. An A Level student in difficulty needs teaching. A Diploma student in difficulty frequently needs supervision: somebody to help them scope a question, hold them to a plan, and read a draft against criteria. Those are different services, and the second is the one UAE schools are least able to supply at scale because it needs one adult per student per component.

paragraphs: Families ask what tutoring costs and then discover the other lines later. Setting them out together makes the decision cleaner, and this year the fee line is unusually stable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family moving school to access the Diploma, that means the published fee is the fee for the year ahead.

The second line is capacity, which affects negotiating position rather than price directly. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A family being told a Diploma place is scarce should check that claim against the published expansion before accepting a waiting list or a deposit.

The third line is support, and the figures below are what named providers publish rather than what IB Gram charges. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650 for premium named tutors. The fourth line has no price and is the one families report as hardest: the household time the Diploma absorbs. Deadlines for internal assessments, Extended Essay milestones, Theory of Knowledge drafts and CAS evidence arrive in parallel, and somebody at home ends up tracking them. That is not an argument against the Diploma. It is an argument for pricing the route honestly before choosing it.

sections.heading: What actually drives the number on your quote
paragraphs: Tutoring prices in this market look arbitrary and are not. Four things move the figure, and a family that understands them can tell a fair quote from an opportunistic one. The first is scarcity of the specific combination. A Standard Level Business Management tutor is plentiful; a Higher Level Further Mathematics or Theatre specialist who can also supervise an internal assessment, in a Gulf Standard Time evening slot, is not. The second is level: Higher Level work takes longer to prepare per hour taught, and that is reflected everywhere in the market.

The third is format, and this is the one families can control. In-home visits carry travel inside the rate, which is why Bestimate's Dubai figures put them at AED 180 to 350 while online qualified tutors sit at AED 150 to 300 for comparable expertise. Group classes are cheaper per student and paced for the group, which works for revision of shared content and fails for a student with a specific gap. The fourth is what the hour contains: a session with written feedback, a marked past-paper section and a progress note costs more to deliver than an hour of conversation.

A fifth factor is worth naming because it inflates quotes without adding value: claimed examiner status. Some providers price on it. Examiner status that cannot be evidenced is a marketing claim, and even where it is real it gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Pay for subject expertise and for the ability to teach a specific student, not for a label.

sections.heading: Year 11 to DP1, and the first term nobody budgets for
paragraphs: The transition itself has a shape and it is consistent enough to plan around. An IGCSE arrival into DP1 is competent in content and unfamiliar with criteria. The Diploma marks against published criteria in every internal assessment and uses command terms with fixed meanings across all subjects, and a student arriving from a terminal-exam system reads those criteria as guidance rather than as the mark scheme they are.

That produces a specific first-term pattern. The student works hard, writes competently, and receives criterion marks in the middle bands because they have answered a question adjacent to the one the criteria asked. Parents read the first DP1 report as a verdict on ability and buy help in three subjects at once. In most cases the cheaper and more effective purchase is one block of work on criteria and command terms, shared across subjects, because the problem is common rather than subject-specific.

The second predictable cost is the Group 2 language. British-curriculum students frequently drop languages after Year 9, and the Diploma requires one for two years. A student starting at ab initio or Standard Level with no recent language experience needs steady low-intensity support from the beginning, which is cheap, rather than rescue in DP2, which is not.

The third is the Extended Essay, and specifically its scoping. Most Extended Essays that go wrong go wrong at the question, not at the writing: a question too broad to answer in 4,000 words, or too narrow to sustain one. A single session on the question before research begins is the highest-value hour in the whole two years, and almost nobody buys it.

sections.heading: Maths AA or AI: the choice that costs or saves two years
paragraphs: This single decision does more financial damage than any other in a Diploma timetable, in both directions. A student placed in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level because it sounded more impressive, who then needs weekly support for two years to survive it, has bought an expensive course. A student placed in Applications and Interpretation who then finds their intended engineering degree asks for Analysis has bought a problem that money cannot fix in DP2.

The honest framing is that the two courses serve different destinations. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-oriented route, expected by most engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics programmes. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led with technology permitted throughout, and suits business, social sciences, design, medicine in some systems, and many other routes perfectly well. Neither is the easy one; they are differently hard.

The decision has to be made against named requirements rather than general advice, and the requirements belong to the universities rather than to the IB. A UAE family applying across several systems — UK, United States, Canada, Europe, local universities — should read the mathematics prerequisite on each target programme's own admissions page before the subject form goes in, because those pages differ and they change. This page deliberately does not state what any named university requires, because any figure here would be out of date before your child applies.

What a tutor can usefully do at this point is diagnose rather than advise in general terms. A session that sets a student real Analysis and real Applications questions, marks both, and reports which one they can actually do is worth more than a conversation about ambitions. sections.heading: Where the money should not go
paragraphs: A page about cost owes families the other half of the advice: the purchases that do not work. The first is four weekly subjects bought in the first term of DP1 in response to a first report. That report is usually measuring criteria unfamiliarity, which is one shared problem rather than four separate ones, and it resolves with a single block of work on criteria and command terms plus time.

The second is a weekly hour continued out of habit. A student whose gap has closed does not need a standing session, and keeping one running teaches them that their work depends on an adult arriving every Tuesday. Any provider unwilling to tell you when to stop is being paid to not tell you.

The third is paying for revision material. Official syllabuses, specimen papers, past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards and should be referenced and linked, never bought from a third party or downloaded from a tutoring site. We do not reproduce or supply board documents here for that reason, and a site that hosts a mark scheme is a site to be careful with generally.

The fourth is buying outcome promises. Nobody can promise a score, a points total or a university place, and any provider who does is pricing a claim they cannot honour. Nor should anyone be paying for claimed examiner status without evidence, or for a self-asserted rating: two providers in this market publish contradictory review figures on the same page, which is worth knowing before a star rating moves a decision.

sections.heading: What a supervisor may do with an internal assessment, and what you are not buying
paragraphs: The Diploma puts more assessed independent work in front of a student than any other route a UAE family is choosing between, so the honesty boundary is a practical matter rather than a disclaimer. A tutor may teach the subject skill, explain the assessment criteria in the subject guide's own language, discuss a proposed question, model an approach on a different topic, and give feedback on a draft the student has produced themselves. That is supervision, and it is the most valuable service in the Diploma.

A tutor may not become the author of an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. That is not a stylistic position: submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student, and it can end a Diploma. Any provider offering to produce assessed work is offering to put your child at that risk in exchange for money.

It is worth knowing what is actually for sale in this market. One operator in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. A family comparing quotes should treat that offer as information about the seller rather than as an option, and should be sceptical of softer versions of the same thing — editing to completion, rewriting a draft, supplying a model essay on the student's own title.

The same line applies to materials and to credentials. We link official board documents rather than reproducing them. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, and we do not use examiner status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it gives none. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education.
