sections.heading: Getting started, and the honest version of what happens next
paragraphs: The useful first step is not booking a tutor. It is writing down three things: the six subjects your child would take on the Diploma route and the three they would take at A Level, the university direction as currently understood, and the IGCSE grade profile subject by subject. Those three documents turn a general anxiety into a decidable question, and most families find the decision becomes obvious once they are side by side.

The second step, if the Diploma is the choice, is to identify the forced subject. Every Diploma timetable contains one subject the student would not have chosen, and that subject is where the two-year support budget should be aimed. Families who aim the budget at the favourite Higher Level instead are protecting the subject least at risk.

The third is to buy the core scoping early. A session on the Extended Essay question before research begins, and a session on Theory of Knowledge structure before the first draft, cost less than any rescue work later and they move three points that come from the core matrix rather than from a subject. Almost nobody does this, which is why it is worth saying twice.

What happens after you contact us: a free trial lesson with the specialist who would actually teach the subject, no card details and no commitment, followed by a written view on what the two years need and what they do not. If no specialist is free for a scarce combination — Higher Level Theatre, a particular Group 2 language in an early-evening Gulf slot — we say so with an honest timeframe rather than offering an adjacent subject and hoping it reads as the same thing.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma more expensive to support than three A Levels?
faqs.answer: Usually, and for structural reasons rather than because Diploma teaching costs more per hour. Three A Levels give three places where a student can be weak; six Diploma subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS give nine. The subject that needs paid help is typically the Standard Level the timetable forced into the gaps, not the Higher Level the student chose. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above, so the arithmetic follows the subject count.

faqs.question: Which part of the Diploma do British-curriculum students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Criteria, in the first term, across every subject at once. The Diploma marks internal assessments against published criteria and uses command terms with fixed meanings, and a student arriving from a terminal-exam system reads criteria as guidance. The result is competent work in middle bands and a first report that looks like an ability problem. It is one shared problem, not six, and a single block on criteria and command terms is usually the cheaper and more effective purchase than three weekly subjects bought in panic.

faqs.question: My child dropped languages after Year 9. What happens in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: A second language is compulsory for both Diploma years, so the realistic options are resuming a language at Standard Level, starting one at ab initio where the school offers it, or taking a home language if it is available. This is the cost line British-curriculum families consistently fail to anticipate. The useful move is steady low-intensity support from the first term, which is inexpensive, rather than rescue work in DP2, which costs several times more and arrives when every other deadline is also live.

faqs.question: What does school actually cost if we move for a Diploma place in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published fee, this year, with unusual certainty. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Supply is also rising: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A family told a Diploma place is scarce should check that against the published expansion before paying a deposit.

faqs.question: How do I choose between Maths Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Against a named university requirement, not against general advice. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-oriented route expected by most engineering, physics and mathematics programmes; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led with technology permitted throughout, and suits business, social sciences, design and many health routes. Neither is a soft option. Read the prerequisite on each target programme's own admissions page before the subject form goes in, and have your child attempt marked questions from both courses rather than guessing.

faqs.question: Is a Higher Level subject worth the extra support cost?
faqs.answer: It is if the university direction requires it and the student can hold it alongside five others. Higher Level sits near A Level depth and costs more per taught hour to support, because preparation rises with level — which is why published market bands move from AED 150 to 250 for a qualified Standard Level tutor up to AED 200 to 450 or above for a Higher Level specialist. Three Higher Levels chosen by ambition rather than by requirement is the most common way a Diploma timetable becomes unaffordable in both money and evenings.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest moment to get help with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Before any research starts, at the question. Most Extended Essays that go wrong go wrong because the question is too broad to answer in 4,000 words or too narrow to sustain one, and no amount of later help recovers a well-written essay answering an unanswerable question. One scoping session is the highest-value hour in the two years and almost nobody buys it. Three of the 45 available points come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix together, so the core is where marginal gains are cheapest.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise an internal assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the most useful service in the Diploma. A supervisor may teach the subject skill, explain the criteria in the subject guide's own words, discuss a proposed question, model an approach on a different topic, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A supervisor may not author any part of assessed work. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. Editing to completion and supplying a model essay on the student's own title are the same offence in softer language.

faqs.question: Should we switch at the end of Year 11 or stay on the British route?
faqs.answer: It depends on the IGCSE profile and the direction, not on which curriculum is better. An even profile across languages, humanities, sciences and maths plus genuine interest in independent research points towards the Diploma, and the core is what universities value in it. An uneven profile with one clear direction — medicine, engineering, architecture — usually points to three A Levels in the strengths, where depth helps and breadth is a tax. A student who dislikes extended writing and dropped languages at 14 will find the Diploma expensive in every sense.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma tutor cost per hour in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published figures as of October 2026: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor online; TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or above. Those are other providers' figures. IB Gram quotes per subject after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Are monthly packages better value than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: Only if the scope is written down. Packages seen in the Dubai market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. The question to ask is session length, who the tutor is, what happens to unused sessions, and whether internal assessment supervision is inside or outside the package.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai for Diploma lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Diploma lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time evening slots. For this route that is usually the stronger option, because the scarce resource is a Higher Level specialist who can also supervise an internal assessment properly, and that person rarely lives within driving distance. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced inside them.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student realistically need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy, and aimed at different subjects than they expect. A common pattern that works is one weekly hour in the single hardest Higher Level, a finite block on the forced Standard Level, and two or three scoping sessions across the core. Four weekly subjects bought in the first term of DP1 almost always treats one shared criteria problem four times over. We review every half term and will say when a session should stop, because a standing slot nobody questions is a standing charge.

faqs.question: Does the Diploma leave room for the mandatory UAE subjects in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: The school has to make room, because the requirement sits with the regulator rather than the curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For a family budgeting support hours, those periods reduce the free study time a six-subject timetable leaves.

faqs.question: Can you promise my child will score higher on the Diploma than on A Levels?
faqs.answer: No, and neither can anyone else. Nobody can promise a score, a points total, a grade improvement or a university place, and a provider pricing such a promise is charging for something they cannot honour. What can be said is where the risk sits: in the forced subject, in the Group 2 language, and in the core components no school teaches weekly. Support aimed at those three places does more than the same money spread across six subjects, which is advice rather than a guarantee.

faqs.question: What should I ask a provider before paying for Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Five things. Which syllabus and subject guide version they teach from. Whether internal assessment supervision is inside the quote and what they will and will not do with a draft. How many sessions the quote covers, over what period, towards which deadline. Whether any examiner claim can be evidenced, and what they say it gives access to — correct answer: nothing about marking or boundaries. And whether they will tell you when to stop. A provider unwilling to answer the last one is being paid not to.

Send those over and a free trial lesson with the matched specialist follows, with no card details and no commitment, delivered live online wherever in the Emirates you are. You will get a written view of what the two years need, what they do not, and which single subject the support budget should actually be aimed at.

intro.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE hour costs a UAE family, and what sits inside the number
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE home tutor in the UAE is priced between roughly AED 150 and AED 450 an hour, and the spread is the whole story. Two families in the same Dubai community, both wanting help with maths, can pay AED 160 and AED 400 for an hour that looks identical on a calendar invite. Neither has been cheated. They are buying different things, and almost no page in this search tells them which. Three of the six strongest pages ranking for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family pays a tutor in.

The first thing inside the number is the syllabus code. Cambridge IGCSE is not one qualification; it is a catalogue of separately examined syllabuses, each with its own code, its own paper pattern and its own supply of people who have actually taught it. Mathematics 0580 is the easiest hour in this market to buy, because every agency in the UAE lists it and the teaching pool is deep. International Mathematics 0607, Computer Science 0478 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 sit at the other end, because far fewer tutors in the Emirates have marked a full set of those papers. Scarcity sets the rate long before anybody discusses your child.

The second thing inside the number is format. A visiting tutor's rate has to absorb the journey, and the journey does not teach anybody anything. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour while a qualified online tutor starts around AED 150, and independent home tutors in the Emirates advertise up to AED 500. The gap is not a quality signal. It is the Sheikh Zayed Road at five in the afternoon, converted into money.

The third thing is tier and timing, and both are decided by a school, not by a tutor. Core and Extended entry set the grade ceiling before a single hour is taught, and the entry itself locks months ahead of the paper. UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June series or the November series, and for a June sitting the final entry goes in during the spring term, roughly four months before the first paper, with the forecast grade following from the subject teacher later in the same term. The exact day is on the centre's statement of entry rather than on any tutoring website. A family that starts funding tutoring after the forecast grade has gone in is buying from a shorter runway, which in practice means more hours a week for fewer weeks, at the top of the band rather than the middle.

The fourth thing is what nobody itemises: preparation, marking turnaround, a written record of each session, and whether a replacement exists if the tutor stops answering in April. An AED 60 hour with none of those around it is often the most expensive hour on this page, because the marks it was bought to recover are still missing in June. IB Gram's position on all of this is stated once and not repeated: lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of our India service only, and we do not send a tutor to a UAE address. What that buys you instead is a specialist for the exact code on the entry form, rather than whoever was willing to drive to your community before dinner.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a continuous route from Lower Secondary through to International AS and A Level, and the money a UAE family spends on tutoring behaves very differently at each stage. The four blocks below are the ones that actually appear on UAE entry forms, with what each one costs you in attention rather than in fees.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE, assessed through Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which Cambridge offers in March, May and October. Checkpoint does not carry an IGCSE grade and does not cover Extended-tier content. What it does carry is an externally marked read on arithmetic fluency, reading comprehension and written accuracy, two full years before any entry form is signed. It is the cheapest diagnostic a family will ever be handed, and most of them file it unread.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this is the stage where tutoring is almost always over-bought. A weak Checkpoint strand does not justify a two-year weekly block; it justifies six to eight targeted hours on the named strand, then a re-test of the same question types. Families who act here pay the lower end of the market band, because there is no deadline pressure in the price.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The lower of the two entry tiers, covering the core subject content and carrying a capped grade ceiling. Core is the right entry for a candidate who needs a secure pass rather than a top grade, and for a subject that is not a prerequisite for anything the student plans next. It is also the tier that gets chosen quietly, in a school office, and then discovered by the parent much later.
programmes.countryNote: Core entry changes the tutoring arithmetic for a UAE family in one specific way: it lowers the ceiling that paid hours can reach. Before funding a block, confirm with the school which tier the entry carries. For Ministry of Education equivalency, the reported British-track rule asks for five subjects at no less than E or grade 3, which a Core pass can satisfy where the grade band allows.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: The full-content entry, with the higher grade ceiling and the harder written papers. Extended is where almost all UAE tutoring money goes, because it is the tier that feeds Cambridge International AS and A Level and the IB Diploma. It is also where the mark loss is most diagnosable: extended-response questions, multi-step calculation, and the command term the candidate answered instead of the one printed.
programmes.countryNote: Extended work is the reason the specialist band exists in this market. An Extended Physics 0625 or Chemistry 0620 candidate aiming above grade 6 needs somebody who has marked those papers, and that is a far smaller pool in the Emirates than the one advertising general science help. Expect to pay the AED 200 to 450 band, and expect the hour to be worth more than two at the bottom band.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two-year route most UAE Cambridge schools run after IGCSE, and the reason an IGCSE tutoring decision is rarely a one-year decision. AS and A Level content assumes the Extended-tier IGCSE foundation, so a gap closed cheaply in Year 11 is a gap that does not have to be closed expensively in Year 12. The Ministry's reported British-track equivalency route also asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the UAE routinely fund IGCSE tutoring, stop at results day, and then fund a bridging block in October of Year 12. Reading the two years as one budget usually costs less in total. If your child is heading for AS Mathematics, the Extended maths work in Year 11 is the cheapest insurance available against a Year 12 catch-up block.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The list below is by Cambridge syllabus code, because the code is what decides who can teach the hour and what that hour costs in this market. Confirm your child's codes from the statement of entry rather than from the school website, and confirm the current component pattern for your series on cambridgeinternational.org.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The deepest tutor pool in the UAE and the lowest reliable price. Written papers split across a non-calculator and a calculator assessment, so confirm the current pattern for your series. Marks go missing in multi-step algebra, in rounding before the final line, and in questions that ask the candidate to show a method they have only ever done mentally.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: A different syllabus, not a variant of 0580. A graphic display calculator is expected throughout, and the assessment leans on investigation, modelling and written reasoning. A 0580 tutor is not automatically a 0607 tutor, which is why this code sits at the specialist band almost everywhere in the Emirates.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a practical component, sat either as the practical test or as the alternative to practical paper. Electricity and the mechanics of moments are where UAE candidates lose most, usually because a formula was recalled correctly and the units were not. Tutors who have marked the practical-route paper are scarcer than those who have taught the theory.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Electrolysis, moles and organic reaction pathways account for a disproportionate share of lost Extended marks. The six-mark extended-response question is the single most coachable item on the paper and the one most often answered as a list of facts rather than as a linked explanation. Specialist rates apply above grade 6 work.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: A deeper teaching pool than Physics or Chemistry in the UAE, so rates sit lower, around AED 180 to 350. The gap is almost never content. It is extended-response technique: naming a process is one mark, explaining the mechanism in sequence is four, and candidates who revise by recall alone keep collecting the one.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: One entry covering biology, chemistry and physics content, awarded as a double grade. The thinnest supply on this list, because it needs a tutor comfortable across three disciplines rather than specialist in one. Families often pay three single-subject tutors instead, which is both dearer and harder to timetable.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, assessed by mark bands rather than by right answers. The deepest pool and the most price-competitive hour in the UAE, with real options at AED 150. Marks are lost to unanchored commentary, to a register that ignores the stated audience, and to a composition that never answers the task set.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: A different assessment from 0500, with a speaking component in the 0511 variant. A large share of UAE candidates sit this rather than First Language, and schools do move students between the two. Confirm which code is on the entry, because the preparation is not transferable and a mis-matched tutor wastes paid hours.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Multiple choice plus structured questions, where the diagram carries marks that prose cannot recover. Candidates in the Emirates lose most on evaluation: a question asking whether a policy should be used is answered with what the policy is. Supply is reasonable in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, thinner in the Northern Emirates.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Computer systems theory alongside algorithms, programming and logic. The narrowest supply of any code on this page in the UAE, because pseudocode marking and trace tables are specialist skills rather than general IT knowledge. Expect the AED 220 to 450 band, and expect a general IT tutor to be poor value here at any price.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study assessment where the marks sit in application to the named business rather than in the definition. Strong supply across Dubai and reasonable pricing. The common failure is a textbook answer that never mentions the company in the stem, which costs application and evaluation marks on every question it touches.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Both reward structure over volume: a case study deployed precisely beats three recalled in outline. History source questions are marked on use of provenance, which almost no candidate is taught explicitly. These are the codes families cut first when triaging a nine-subject budget, and often the right cut.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: Three Ministry-mandated subjects run alongside the Cambridge timetable in every UAE private school, whatever curriculum the school is licensed for. They are already inside the fee you pay, and they are the part of the week most tutoring plans ignore until a report card arrives.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as a first language
igcseSubjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the language of instruction and separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, with combined classes strictly prohibited. The grade does not count towards the Ministry's five-subject British-track equivalency total.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
igcseSubjects.description: The non-Arab stream, taught separately under KHDA's class-organisation rule. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, with at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson.

igcseSubjects.name: Islamic Education
igcseSubjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. KHDA requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask the school about directly.

igcseSubjects.name: Social Studies and Moral, Social and Cultural studies
igcseSubjects.description: Arabic is the primary language of instruction for Social Studies for Arab students. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which limits what any outside tutor may legitimately supply.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Cambridge IGCSE support across the seven emirates
cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Price and supply are not the same in every emirate, and the regulator holding your child's school file is not the same either. The notes below are about what each location does to the cost and the availability of a Cambridge IGCSE hour, not about scenery.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest market and the most competitive pricing, under KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai held private school fees flat for 2026-27. Nothing holds a tutoring rate flat, and the specialist codes still clear at the top band here.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, so the cheapest option a parent imagines is not available. Supply is good, pricing slightly above Dubai for scarce codes.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller Cambridge cohort and a visibly thinner local tutor pool. A visiting arrangement for 0607 or 0478 is close to unobtainable here at any rate, which is precisely where a live-video specialist stops being a compromise and becomes the only route to the code.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Several large British-curriculum cohorts sit IGCSEs here. Travel across the Dubai border at peak hour is why in-home quotes climb before any teaching is costed.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The local pool of Extended-tier science specialists is small, and families here routinely pay Dubai travel premiums for a tutor who then arrives late. Live video removes the premium and the lateness together.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah returns almost no mentions across the competitor pages in this search, which tells you how much local Cambridge-specific tutoring supply there is to compete for.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education oversight, east-coast geography, and the longest journeys in the country for anyone considering a visiting tutor. A single evening session can cost a tutor two hours of driving, and that is what the quote reflects. A 0654 Double Award candidate here has effectively one sensible delivery route.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country, under Ministry of Education supervision. Zero competitor pages in this research set mention it at all. For a Cambridge candidate here, the question is not what a specialist costs but whether one exists within driving distance, and usually the answer is no.

sections.heading: What a parent is actually asking when they search for a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase means one-to-one help with named Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses, bought privately and paid for by the hour, with the tutor arriving rather than the child travelling to a centre. That is a reasonable thing to want, and in the UAE market it costs between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour depending on the emirate, the code and how far anybody has to drive. The word home in the search is doing one job: it separates private one-to-one from a group class at a tuition centre. It is not really a statement about geography.

IB Gram answers the one-to-one part and declines the driving part. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day. Home visits are part of our India service only, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. That is stated here rather than buried, because the alternative is a family discovering it after a deposit.

The reason to prefer the online version is not cost, although it is usually cheaper. It is the pool. A Computer Science 0478 or International Mathematics 0607 specialist who has marked those papers is a small population in the Emirates, and smaller again once you require them to be within a twenty-minute drive of one community at five in the afternoon. Remove the drive and the constraint becomes the syllabus code instead of the postcode. A family in Fujairah gets the same choice as a family in Jumeirah.

The honest limit of this is worth stating too. There are things a screen cannot do. It cannot run a titration for your child, it cannot invigilate a mock, and it cannot replace a school's laboratory for the practical route in the sciences. What it can do is teach the theory and the alternative-to-practical technique, read a marked script line by line, and put a specialist in front of a candidate who would otherwise have had a generalist. Where the practical paper is the barrier, say so early and we will tell you honestly what the sessions can and cannot address.

sections.heading: The syllabus code sets the price before the subject does
paragraphs: Ask any UAE agency what maths tutoring costs and you will get a band. Ask what Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 tutoring costs and the band moves, because that is a different question with a different answer. Cambridge IGCSE is a catalogue of separately examined syllabuses, each with its own code printed on the statement of entry, and the supply of people who have actually taught and marked a given code varies enormously inside the Emirates. Price follows supply. It does not follow difficulty, and it certainly does not follow how hard your child finds the subject.

The practical consequence is that the single cheapest thing a parent can do before spending anything is find the codes. They are on the statement of entry the school issues ahead of the series, not on the school's prospectus and not in the parent portal's subject list. A family that walks into a conversation with 0620 Extended and 0607 Core written down gets quoted accurately. A family that says science and maths gets quoted the agency's average, which is always above what the common codes should cost and below what the scarce ones really require.

The table below sets out the codes UAE Year 11 cohorts most often carry, what the written assessment is actually testing, where the teaching pool is thin, and the market band each code tends to clear at. The bands are the published market figures, not IB Gram prices, and the component patterns should be confirmed for your series on cambridgeinternational.org before you rely on them. Read the fourth column as the explanation of the fifth: every premium on this page is a scarcity premium, and scarcity is the one thing a parent can plan around.

One further note on the arithmetic. A scarce code does not mean more hours; it usually means fewer, because a specialist diagnoses in one session what a generalist circles for six. Two hours at AED 400 that identify a specific pseudocode trace-table habit are better value than twelve at AED 120 spent re-teaching content the candidate already knew. That comparison is the single most useful one on this page, and it is the one no competitor page in this search makes at all.

sections.heading: 0580 or 0607: the maths code that prices the next two years
paragraphs: Two Cambridge maths codes appear on UAE entry forms, and most parents never learn which one their child is sitting until somebody asks. Mathematics 0580 is the mainstream entry across British-curriculum schools in the Emirates. International Mathematics 0607 turns up where a school is running the IB Middle Years Programme underneath, or steering a cohort towards the Diploma, and it is a genuinely different syllabus rather than a relabelled one. The graphic display calculator is expected throughout 0607, and the assessment asks for investigation and interpretation alongside manipulation.

This matters to a budget in a way no other subject decision does, because maths is the one code that reaches forward into everything. A 0607 cohort is usually a Diploma cohort, which means the tutoring question is a two-year arc ending in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, not a one-year sprint ending in August. A 0580 cohort is usually heading for Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics, where the Extended-tier algebra from Year 11 is assumed rather than revisited. Either way, the cheap hour is the one bought in Year 10.

The scarcity picture is the clearest on this page. A 0580 tutor can be found at the lower end of the qualified band in every emirate. A 0607 specialist who has taught the calculator techniques and marked the investigative questions is a much smaller group, and in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain a visiting one is close to unobtainable at any rate. That is the single clearest case for buying the specialist over live video rather than buying proximity and hoping.

The one thing to avoid is paying a 0580 tutor to teach 0607 content. It happens constantly, it is not dishonest, and it is still waste: the tutor teaches what they know, the candidate practises questions from the wrong paper style, and the gap that prompted the booking is still there in February. Send the statement of entry first. If the code on it is 0607 and no 0607 specialist is free at your hour, we will say so rather than substitute.

sections.heading: Supply, not sentiment: what sits behind a Cambridge rate in this market
paragraphs: A tutoring rate in the UAE is not a verdict on anybody's teaching. It is the output of a market with a large, growing demand side and a slow-growing specialist supply side, plus a set of rules that quietly close off the cheapest options. Reading those forces is what lets a parent tell a fair quote from an opportunistic one, and almost none of this appears anywhere in the pages currently ranking for this search.

Start with scale. Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 pupils across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of pupils, Indian 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. That makes IGCSE demand the single largest block in the emirate, which is exactly why general IGCSE hours are competitively priced and niche codes are not. Then add new supply: Dubai's 2026-27 intake brings seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

Now the rules. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Your school bill is held; nothing holds a tutoring rate. Meanwhile the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is granted free of charge for two years, which means no part of a premium is explained by licensing cost. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils at their own school, closing the one route parents try first.

Put those together and the shape of the market is clear. Volume codes cheap, scarce codes dear, no regulatory cost to pass on, a growing Year 10 population every September, and the free option legally unavailable. A rate at the top of the band is defensible when it buys a named syllabus specialist. It is not defensible when it buys a generalist, a long drive, and a promise.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and what each published figure leaves out
paragraphs: Here are the numbers. They are market figures, each attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. We publish them because the alternative is what this search currently offers: one strong competitor page whose own FAQ asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer, and two others that quote in US dollars.

The honest reading of a rate table is the fourth column rather than the second. A band tells you what an hour is advertised at; it tells you nothing about what the hour contains. Preparation time, marking turnaround on a practice paper, a written record you can read afterwards, and a replacement if the tutor stops answering in April are all real costs that somebody absorbs. When an advertised rate is unusually low, one of those four has usually been removed, and the family finds out in the week it matters most.

Monthly packages deserve particular care. Advertised UAE packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Before signing one, ask two questions: what happens to unused sessions, and does the month include school-holiday weeks. A UAE month containing Eid, a half-term and a travel week is not a month of teaching.

IB Gram's own position: we do not publish a rate card on these pages, because the right figure depends on the code, the tier and how many weeks are left, and a number invented for a landing page would be worse than no number. What we do instead is quote against the bands above, start with a trial lesson at no charge and with no card details taken, and tell you before you pay if the only specialist for your code is unavailable at the hour you want.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room against a specialist on screen, priced per taught minute
paragraphs: The comparison most families make is rate against rate, and it is the wrong comparison. The right one is cost per taught minute, because a visiting arrangement bills an hour and consumes considerably more than an hour of the household's evening. Nobody teaches in a car, and nobody teaches in the fifteen minutes of settling that follows a late arrival. Once the journey is priced honestly, the gap between the formats narrows at the top and widens at the bottom.

The arithmetic below uses AED 250 an hour as a mid-market figure, purely as arithmetic rather than as anybody's price. At that rate, two sessions lost in a term to illness or traffic is roughly AED 500, and a visiting arrangement is far likelier to charge for them because the journey was already made. Over a two-year Cambridge IGCSE run, the difference between formats is usually several thousand dirhams, which is a meaningful slice of the specialist budget for a second subject.

The non-financial argument is stronger, though, and it is the pool. The whole purpose of identifying the syllabus code is to buy the person who has taught it. If the search is then restricted to people prepared to drive to one community at five in the afternoon, the code advantage disappears and you are back to a generalist. A 0478 or 0654 candidate in Ajman or Fujairah has no realistic visiting option, and pretending otherwise is how families end up paying specialist rates for general help.

What the screen does not solve, again plainly: laboratory work, invigilated conditions, and the physical handling of apparatus for the practical-route science papers. Those stay with the school. Everything else in a Cambridge IGCSE year, including reading a marked mock script question by question and rebuilding extended-response technique, works at least as well over live video with a shared screen, and leaves a written record the household can audit afterwards.

sections.heading: The diagnostic you have already paid for
paragraphs: Most UAE families buy their first tutoring hours on a feeling, and the feeling is usually accurate about the subject and wrong about the cause. Before any money moves there are five pieces of evidence already sitting in the household or in the school office, all of them produced at no additional cost, and together they say whether paid hours are the right purchase and which code to spend them on. Reading them is the highest-return half hour in this entire process.

The Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint report is the earliest of them. Cambridge offers Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the report is externally marked, which makes it the only objective read a family gets two years before an IGCSE entry. It says nothing about Extended-tier content, so it cannot justify a two-year weekly block. It can absolutely justify six targeted hours on a named strand, which is the difference between spending AED 1,500 in Year 8 and AED 9,000 in Year 11.

The two documents that matter most, though, are the marked mock script and the statement of entry. The script tells you which question types bleed marks, which is the only diagnosis worth paying for; a tutor who starts from a marked script rather than from a topic list earns the first hour back immediately. The statement of entry tells you the code, the tier and the components, so the specialist you hire matches the paper the candidate will actually sit, and it also carries the series the candidate is entered for, June or November. Add the forecast grade, which the school submits to Cambridge during the exam term and before the first paper rather than after it, and you have a written statement of what the subject teacher expects.

The pattern to avoid is the one this market rewards: booking a weekly hour in six subjects because results felt disappointing. That is the most expensive possible response and the least likely to work, because it spreads attention across codes with completely different failure modes. Triage against the evidence, fund one or two codes properly, and revisit at six hours. If the evidence does not point anywhere, the honest answer is that tutoring is not yet the right spend, and we will say that.

sections.heading: Command terms are where Cambridge marks quietly leave the room
paragraphs: A large share of the marks a UAE Cambridge candidate loses are not lost to ignorance. They are lost to answering a different question from the one printed. State, describe, explain, calculate, suggest and evaluate each have a defined expectation in the mark scheme, and each has a characteristic failure: a described answer where an explanation was wanted collects a fraction of the available marks even when every fact in it is correct. This is the most coachable thing in the entire qualification, and it is the reason a specialist hour can move a grade band faster than a term of content revision.

The pattern repeats across codes with its own local flavour. In Chemistry 0620 the six-mark extended response is answered as a list of true statements rather than a linked chain of cause and effect. In Biology 0610 a process is named where a mechanism in sequence was required. In Physics 0625 the formula is recalled correctly and the unit is dropped, or the rounding happens two lines before the final answer. In Mathematics 0580 the method mark is thrown away because a step done mentally was never written down. In English 0500 the directed-writing task names an audience and a form, and the composition ignores both.

Diagnosing this needs a marked script, not a topic list, which is why the mock paper is worth more to a tutor than anything a parent can describe over the phone. The work itself is unglamorous: rewrite the same six-mark answer four times against the published command-term expectation until the structure is automatic. It does not feel like tutoring and it is where most of the recoverable marks in a Cambridge IGCSE year actually live.

One caution on materials. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge, and no tutor should be supplying them to you as downloads. A tutor references them, cites the official page and works from what the school has legitimately provided to the candidate. If a provider's selling point is a library of papers and mark schemes to hand over, that is a copyright problem rather than a feature, and it tells you something about the rest of the operation.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: dropping a Cambridge entry to save money
paragraphs: Families triaging a nine-subject Year 11 budget reach the same question eventually: can we drop one. Academically that is a school conversation. Financially and administratively there is a harder constraint, and it is the Ministry of Education equivalency file that a UAE-based candidate will eventually need. Getting this wrong is cheap to do and expensive to discover, because it is usually discovered at an admissions desk.

As reported from the Ministry's July 2026 clarification, the British-track route asks the candidate to pass five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The point that catches UAE families is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A page currently ranking for this query states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The Ministry's clarification, as reported, says five, and the exclusion is what makes the counting feel like six.

The practical rule that follows is simple. Secure five accepted subjects at the reported minimum first, then triage. A humanity is usually the safest thing to drop once the five are safe; a science or maths almost never is, because every later route asks for them and replacing one costs far more than the tutoring you avoided. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or expedites, and nothing on this page should be read as implying tutoring is required for it. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before acting on any figure, including the ones here.

The budget version of this is worth stating plainly. Funding tutoring across nine subjects is the most expensive plan available and the least effective. Funding it across the two codes that are both at risk and structurally necessary, while confirming that five accepted subjects are secure, is the plan that costs least and protects most. That is an arithmetic decision made against the entry form, not a judgement about anybody's ability.

sections.heading: What a missed Cambridge date costs, counted in series rather than in hours
paragraphs: Cambridge runs its IGCSE assessment in series, and a series is a door that closes. That single fact governs the cost of every scheduling decision a UAE family makes, because a slip does not usually produce a late fee. It produces a wait, and a wait means another entry, another revision block and another set of funded hours. In the UAE there are two doors a year: Cambridge's exam timetable page sets out a June series and a November series. The February/March series that turns up in search results is offered to India only, so a UAE family planning against it is planning against a sitting their child cannot enter.

Count a June series backwards and the shape becomes obvious. The papers themselves run across May and June, spread over several weeks by zone. The final entry closes in the spring term, roughly four months before the first paper, which is why a family deciding in April to fund serious support is deciding after the entry has already been locked. The forecast grade goes in from the subject teacher during that same exam term. Results reach centres on Cambridge Direct in August and certificates follow months later, by which time the only remaining lever is a November resit. Pearson's International GCSE calendar makes the same point with published dates: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while the November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Take the exact days from your own board and zone timetable rather than from a tutoring page, including this one.

There is one further trap that costs more than any of the others and is almost never mentioned. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone's timetable was used. A revision plan built on the wrong zone's dates is a plan that can lose a paper outright. Ask the school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable only.

The planning consequence for a budget is the one worth keeping. Hours bought twelve weeks out are bought at the middle of the market band and spread across a sensible week. Hours bought three weeks out are bought at the top of the band, in doubled sessions, from whoever happens to be free, and they are competing with the school's own revision timetable for the same tired evenings. The date is what makes the hour expensive, not the tutor.

sections.heading: Results, remarks and a November resit: the arithmetic after the papers
paragraphs: Results day is where the most expensive decisions of the whole process get made, usually in a hurry and often while the family is out of the country. Pearson's published pattern gives a sense of the clock: June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's UAE pattern runs on the same rhythm: June-series results reach centres on Direct in August, November-series results in January, with certificates following months later. Whichever board your child sits, two windows open on results day and both shut quickly.

The first is the enquiry about results, the review or remark route, which runs through the school rather than through the parent and carries a deadline set by the board. It is worth considering when a grade sits one mark-band below everything else the candidate has produced all year, and it is worth nothing when it is being used as a substitute for accepting a result. The school's exams officer is the only person who can submit it, which makes the first call on results day a call to the school, not to a tutor.

The second is the resit decision, and here the arithmetic is uncomfortable but clear. A resit means a fresh entry in a later series, a revision block running alongside the first term of the next course, and an opportunity cost measured in attention rather than money: the Year 12 content being taught while the Year 11 paper is being re-prepared. Priced honestly, a resit almost always costs more in total than the tutoring that would have prevented it would have cost in February. That is not an argument for panic buying; it is an argument for buying earlier and smaller.

The third thing to do on results day is administrative and nobody enjoys it. Open the equivalency file. Check that five accepted subjects at the reported minimum grade are present, remembering that Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count, and confirm the current requirement on moe.gov.ae rather than on any landing page, including this one. Certificates arrive weeks after results, and an admissions deadline that needs a certificate does not care which week it is.

sections.heading: What no fee buys: the honesty line around Cambridge coursework and practicals
paragraphs: Some things in this market are for sale and should not be. At least one provider ranking in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The same logic is applied to IGCSE coursework components, and it is the single fastest way to end a candidate's entry. A tutor teaches, explains, models an approach, asks the questions a marker would ask, and gives feedback on work the candidate produced. A tutor does not write coursework, does not redraft it to completion, and does not supply text to be submitted under somebody else's name.

That boundary holds across the Cambridge components where it matters most. In English 0500 a tutor can teach the directed-writing form and mark a practice piece against the band descriptors; the composition submitted is the candidate's. In Business 0450 and History 0470 a tutor can interrogate an argument and point out an unsupported claim; the writing stays with the student. In the sciences, practical skills assessed through the practical test or the alternative to practical paper are prepared through technique, data handling and past question practice, while the apparatus and the invigilated conditions remain the school's responsibility.

The materials boundary runs alongside it. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge's property. A tutor cites them and links to the official page; a tutor does not distribute them as a download library, and a provider advertising one is advertising a copyright problem. The same applies to anything described as leaked, advance or inside information about a paper, which no legitimate tutor has and no parent should want.

None of this is a disclaimer bolted to the end of a sales page. It is the practical reason the honest version of this service is worth paying for. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and anybody selling one is selling something else. What a specialist hour can do is make the difference between a candidate who knows the content and a candidate who can convert it into marks under a named command term, inside a timed paper, in the zone their centre actually sits in. That is the product, and it is the only one we sell.

process.title: Send the entry form and one marked paper
process.description: Two documents start this properly: the statement of entry, which carries the Cambridge code, the tier and the components, and the most recent marked script with its mark scheme. Together they replace a guess with a diagnosis. A family who sends these gets an accurate answer about availability and cost; a family who describes the problem gets an average.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge
process.description: Thirty minutes, one-to-one over live video, with no card details taken and no obligation to book a block. The purpose is diagnostic rather than promotional: the tutor works through a question the candidate got wrong and names the habit behind it. If the match is wrong, say so and we will change the tutor or tell you honestly that the specialist you need is not free.

process.title: A written target, then a counted block
process.description: Before money moves, the target gets written down: the code, the question types, and what the tier allows. The block is then counted backwards from the series rather than forwards from today, and quoted as a total so you know the figure before the first session. Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, with Ramadan and holiday weeks handled separately.

process.title: Review at six hours against what was written
process.description: Six paid hours in, there should be something to read: session notes, annotated questions, and a marked piece of the candidate's own work showing the habit changing. If there is not, the honest conclusion is that the plan or the match is wrong, and the review exists to say so rather than to renew automatically. Blocks can be paused during school exam weeks.

process.title: Hand back to the school calendar
process.description: The last stage is deliberately a stop. Once the forecast grade is in and the paper is close, the school's own revision timetable should own the candidate's evenings, and extra paid hours start competing with sleep. We will tell you when we think that point has arrived, which is the part of this that costs us money and is still the right advice.

whyPoints.title: The price is on the page
whyPoints.description: Market bands in AED, each attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and dated October 2026, sit in the open on this page rather than behind an enquiry form. Three of the strongest competitor pages in this search publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A family should be able to sanity-check a quote before they make a call.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: We match on the Cambridge syllabus code from the statement of entry, because 0580 and 0607 are different syllabuses and a general maths tutor is poor value for the second. If no specialist for your code is free at the hour you want, we say that rather than substituting somebody who will teach the paper they know instead of the paper your child sits.

whyPoints.title: Online because of the pool, not to cut corners
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of our India service only. The reason is supply: a Computer Science 0478 or Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 specialist is a small population in the Emirates, and smaller still if they must also live near one community. Removing the journey widens the pool and removes travel from the rate.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, with the gaps admitted
whyPoints.description: Every regulatory and calendar fact on this page is attributed: u.ae for the regulator map and the permit, KHDA for the fee position and the mandatory subjects, Cambridge for the series dates, Pearson for the results pattern. Where a figure could not be verified, it is absent rather than estimated, and that includes IB session dates, which we do not publish.

whyPoints.title: An independent platform, with no claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation, licence, partnership or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, we claim none, and we occupy no office in the UAE. Named schools appear here as school-system context only. Anyone claiming regulator approval for private tutoring is worth a second question.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line, stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the candidate's own work. Coursework is not written, redrafted to completion or supplied. No grade is promised, no outcome is guaranteed, and past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than distributed. That boundary is why the service is worth paying for rather than a footnote on the way out.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting one-to-one arrangement, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a named syllabus specialist. Budget options advertise lower: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table shows in-home at AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures as published by each source and read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. What moves your own number is the syllabus code, the tier and how many weeks are left.

faqs.question: Why does a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 tutor cost more than an English 0500 tutor?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. English as a First Language 0500 has the deepest teaching pool in the Emirates, so real options exist around AED 150 and providers compete on price. Physics 0625 above grade 6 needs somebody who has taught the Extended theory and, ideally, marked the practical-route paper, and that is a far smaller group across the UAE. The same logic puts Computer Science 0478 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 at the top of the band, because pseudocode marking and three-discipline teaching are specialist skills rather than general ones. Scarcity sets the rate before anybody looks at your child's work, which is also why identifying the code first saves money.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Cambridge IGCSE tutor to our address in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day. Home visits are part of our India service only, and no tutor is dispatched to a UAE address. The reason is the pool rather than the cost: a specialist for a scarce Cambridge code is unlikely to live within a short drive of any one community, so insisting on proximity means accepting a generalist. Removing the journey means the only constraint is the syllabus code. The limits are stated honestly too: laboratory work, apparatus handling and invigilated conditions stay with the school.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the month contains. Advertised UAE packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 monthly at the mid band for a weekly hour. Before signing, ask two questions. What happens to unused sessions, and does the month include school-holiday weeks. A UAE month holding Eid, a half-term and a travel week is not a month of teaching, and a package priced on calendar weeks rather than taught sessions quietly transfers that loss to you.

faqs.question: How many Cambridge IGCSE subjects should we actually fund tutoring for?
faqs.answer: One or two, almost always. Funding a weekly hour across six or nine subjects is the most expensive plan available and the least likely to work, because the codes have completely different failure modes and the candidate's attention is finite. Triage against evidence you already hold: the marked mock script, the end-of-Year-10 paper and the forecast grade. Fund the codes that are both at risk and structurally necessary, usually maths and one science, and confirm that five subjects the Ministry accepts are secure. Then review at six hours. A humanity is usually the safest thing to leave unfunded once the five are safe.

faqs.question: Should we pay for tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper for the same result, and that is arithmetic rather than sales talk. The same number of hours spread over two years is bought at the middle of the market band instead of the top, leaves room to change tutor if the first match is wrong, and attacks method habits rather than just drilling past papers. By January of Year 11 the entry is locked, the forecast grade is weeks away, and a family is buying doubled sessions from whoever is free. The date is what makes an hour expensive. The tutor is usually the same person either way.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 worth paying a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Yes, because 0607 is a different syllabus rather than a variant of 0580. A graphic display calculator is expected throughout and the assessment leans on investigation, modelling and written justification alongside manipulation. A competent 0580 tutor who has never taught 0607 will teach what they know, the candidate will practise the wrong paper style, and the original gap will still be there in February. That is not dishonesty, it is mismatch, and it is the most common waste we see in UAE maths tutoring. Send the statement of entry so the code is known before anybody is booked.

faqs.question: What does the MoHRE private tuition permit tell me about the rate I am quoted?
faqs.answer: That no part of the premium is licensing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. So the permit is a legal baseline rather than a quality mark. It certifies permission to charge, not the ability to teach Extended-tier Cambridge content.

faqs.question: How do I find out which Cambridge syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: From the statement of entry the school issues ahead of the series, not from the school prospectus and not from the subject list in a parent portal. The statement carries the code, the tier and the components, which is exactly the information that decides who should teach the hour. If it has not arrived yet, the exams officer can tell you, and the same conversation is the moment to ask which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because that decides which version of the timetable your revision plan should be built on.

faqs.question: Is a small group class cheaper than one-to-one for Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, usually a third to a half of the one-to-one rate per student. Whether it is better value depends on one thing: does the group share your child's code and tier. A group mixing Core and Extended candidates, or mixing 0580 with 0607, teaches to the middle and the marginal candidate learns least. Groups work well for content coverage and badly for the thing most UAE candidates actually need, which is line-by-line work on their own marked script. If the diagnosis is command-term technique, a group will not reach it.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor end up costing more by the time the papers arrive?
faqs.answer: Often, and the mechanism is specific rather than vague. An advertised rate well below the qualified band has usually had something removed: preparation time, marking turnaround on practice papers, a written record of each session, or a replacement if the tutor stops answering in April. Those are real costs and somebody absorbs them. Twelve hours at AED 120 re-teaching content a candidate already knew is dearer than two at AED 400 that identify the actual habit, because the marks the hours were bought to recover are still missing in June. Judge the hour by what it leaves behind.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Cambridge alternative to practical paper over video?
faqs.answer: Yes for the paper, no for the laboratory. The alternative to practical paper assesses understanding of experimental method, data handling, graph work, sources of error and improvements to a procedure, and all of that is taught well over live video with a shared screen and past questions. What a screen cannot do is run a titration, handle apparatus or provide invigilated conditions, and where a candidate is on the practical-test route the school's laboratory remains the only place that work happens. Tell us which route the entry carries and we will say plainly what the sessions can address.

faqs.question: What happens to the money we have spent if the Cambridge entry deadline is missed?
faqs.answer: The hours are not wasted, but the timetable is. A missed entry does not usually produce a late fee; it produces a wait for a later series, which means another entry and in practice another funded revision block alongside the next course's first term. For UAE candidates the later series is the real cost, because Cambridge offers only two here: June and November. A June entry closes in the spring term, months before the first paper, and a candidate who misses it waits until November. The exams officer holds that date, not the family, which is why it is worth asking about in September rather than discovering it in March. Ask for the date in writing and for the zone the centre sits in, because the timetable differs by zone.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to resit in a later series than to add tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Priced honestly, almost never. A resit means a fresh entry, a revision block running against the first term of the next course, and an opportunity cost measured in attention rather than dirhams: Year 12 content taught while a Year 11 paper is re-prepared. Compared with a counted block bought twelve weeks before the original paper at the middle of the market band, the resit route is more expensive in total and more disruptive. That is an argument for buying earlier and smaller rather than for panic buying, and no tutor can promise a particular outcome in either direction.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects the Ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No. As reported from the Ministry's July 2026 clarification, the British track asks for five subjects passed in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They remain mandatory in school under KHDA rules regardless of the licensed curriculum. One page ranking for this query states six IGCSE subjects; the exclusion is what makes five feel like six. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before acting on it.

faqs.question: What should one paid hour of Cambridge IGCSE tuition actually produce?
faqs.answer: Something you can read afterwards. Shared-screen notes, at least one annotated exam question showing the method the marker wanted, and a single written next step for the week. Six paid hours in there should also be a marked piece of the candidate's own work showing a named habit changing: units retained, method lines written down, a six-mark answer built as a chain rather than a list. If none of that exists after six hours, the plan or the match is wrong and the review conversation should say so rather than renewing the block automatically.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code on the entry form, not with a quote
cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest useful thing you can do today costs nothing: find the statement of entry, write down the Cambridge syllabus codes and the tier, and dig out the last marked script with its mark scheme. Send those two things and you will get a straight answer about which specialist fits, what the market band for that code looks like, and whether anybody is free at the hour you want. The trial lesson is thirty minutes, one-to-one over live video, with no card details taken. If the honest answer is that tutoring is not yet the right spend, we would rather say that than sell you a block.

intro.heading: Online lessons work to the series calendar, not to the school's week
paragraphs: There are two clocks running in a Cambridge IGCSE year and families usually only see one of them. The school clock is visible: homework, end-of-topic tests, a report in January. The board clock is invisible until it bites. It sets a final entry deadline months before the first paper, a coursework submission window that closes while the class is still being taught new content, a forecast-grade request that lands inside the exam period itself, and a review-of-marking window that opens and shuts inside a fortnight in August. A Cambridge IGCSE online tutor who ignores the second clock is a homework helper with a better microphone.

This page is organised around that second clock. Both boards publish their own key dates, and they are specific enough to plan against. Pearson gives the cleanest worked example because its dates are already published and dated: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read a series in that order and the shape of the year appears: the entry closes weeks or months before the first paper, the papers run in a fixed window, results land in August for a summer sitting and in January for a winter one, and everything a tutor can still influence sits before the entry closes rather than after it.

Cambridge works the same way with two doors a year rather than four. In the UAE, Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October that are diagnostic rather than certificated. The February/March sitting that appears in search results is offered to India only, so it is not a date a UAE family can plan against. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Two boards, two usable sittings each, and a family that knows which one applies to them is already ahead.

Delivery is the second half of the answer. Every lesson described on this page is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the UAE; the one-to-one visiting model is something we run in India, and pretending otherwise on a UAE page would be a promise we do not keep. What online delivery buys in exchange is specific and it is mostly about time. A session set for 17:00 Gulf Standard Time starts at 17:00, not at 17:25 after Sheikh Zayed Road. It survives a February half-term in Europe, a Ramadan timetable and a mock week that moved twice. And the tutor is chosen for the syllabus code rather than for the postcode, which is the whole argument when the code is Computer Science 0478 rather than Mathematics 0580.

The rest of the page is practical. There is a month-by-month map of the two-year course, a table of who actually presses each button in the entry process, the private-candidate route for a child taught outside a school roll, the Gulf Standard Time slots UAE families actually book, what the market charges with every figure attributed to whoever published it, the regulator map across the seven emirates, and the decisions that close in the fortnight after results. Where a date or a rule comes from a board or a government source, the source is named so you can check it rather than take our word for it.
