sections.heading: Six administrative zones, and why the timetable you downloaded may not be yours
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and its guidance for exams officers is unusually blunt about the consequence: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and the board states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong version was used. A Cambridge administrative zone is an administrative fact about the centre rather than about the country, so two UAE schools are not automatically in the same one.

In practice this is the most common planning error a tutor sees. A parent searches for the timetable, finds a PDF, pins it to the fridge and books sessions around it. Two of the subject dates turn out to be an hour out and one is a day out. Sessions end up scheduled on the morning of a paper. The fix costs nothing at all: ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in and which version of the timetable it is working to, then plan the last fortnight from that document and nothing else.

It also explains something families find suspicious. A cousin in another country sits the same paper at a different local time, and a classmate who transferred in remembers different dates entirely. Neither is evidence of a leak or an administrative error. Zoning exists so that papers are sat inside a controlled window across many time zones at once. For a UAE household the working rule is to treat the centre's own document as the only calendar and anything found through a search engine as a draft.

sections.heading: Reading a component number before you buy an hour
paragraphs: Parents are handed component numbers and given no translation. On a Cambridge science syllabus the numbering follows a pattern which, once learned, tells you most of what a session should cover. Odd and even pairs separate Core from Extended on the written theory papers, and a practical test and a written alternative to practical paper sit at the end of the list. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and its chemistry and biology equivalents are all numbered on that same shape.

This matters commercially because one subject name hides two different pieces of work. A student entered for the practical test needs laboratory technique and a teacher who can coach method at a bench. A student entered for the written alternative needs something quite different: reading a described experiment, identifying the controlled variable, completing a results table, criticising a method they never performed themselves. One of those is taught over video without compromise. The other needs the school laboratory, and an honest tutor says so in the first conversation.

Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 works on the same tier-split logic, with a calculator and a non-calculator paper in each tier on the current syllabus. Confirm the component numbers from the statement of entry rather than from a syllabus PDF found online, because syllabuses are revised and the version your child sits is the one the centre entered them for. The table gives the pattern to expect; your child's own entry gives the fact you should plan against.

sections.heading: The tier conversation to have before the autumn entry goes in
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. The core and extended tier split is not two difficulty settings of one exam; they are different papers with different grade ranges, and the entry decides which range is available to a candidate. A school places a student on the evidence it holds: end-of-Year-10 results, topic tests and how the student copes when a question is unfamiliar. That decision is usually taken in the autumn of Year 11, which is precisely why October is when the conversation is worth having.

Families get into difficulty in two opposite directions. The first is a Core entry made for a student who was quietly improving all summer, which caps a grade below the level a sixth-form course asks for. The second is an Extended entry defended by a parent against the school's evidence, where the student then loses marks steadily across the whole paper instead of securing the top of the lower tier. Neither of those is fixed by buying more hours the following April.

What tuition is genuinely good for here is producing evidence before the entry is submitted. Six to eight weeks of marked work on Extended-style questions, with the marks shown to the subject teacher, is an argument a school can act on. After the deadline the work changes shape: on a Core entry the job is to secure the top of that tier cleanly, which is a real and respectable outcome rather than a consolation prize, and it needs different hours from a reach attempt.

sections.heading: Command words: where Cambridge marks are quietly lost
paragraphs: A student who knows the content and still comes out at grade 5 is usually answering a different question from the one that was asked. Cambridge questions are built on command words, and each one has a mark scheme behind it expecting a particular shape of answer. State wants a fact and no reasoning. Explain wants a mechanism, and will not award the bare fact. Suggest expects a plausible answer applied to a context the student has not seen before and cannot have revised.

This is the single most repairable cause of lost marks, and it stays repairable late in the year because it needs no new content. A session takes four questions the student has already attempted, reads the command word, counts the marks on offer and rewrites the answer to that shape. Two or three weeks of that work moves scripts that have plateaued for a term. It is also why marked past papers matter more than worked solutions: the student has to see where their own sentence failed to earn a mark.

The table pairs common command words with what a mark scheme tends to reward and the failure a tutor sees most often. It is a diagnostic rather than a revision list. Used properly, a parent can read a marked mock script beside it and tell the difference between a child who does not know a topic and a child who knows it and is writing the wrong kind of sentence about it. Those two problems need completely different hours.

sections.heading: What Cambridge IGCSE support costs across this market
paragraphs: Published UAE rates for an hour of secondary tuition run from roughly AED 45 at the budget end to AED 650 at the top of the market, and the spread is not arbitrary. It tracks who is teaching, whether the hour includes marking, and whether anyone has to travel. Budget online hours are generally taught by university students. Specialist IGCSE and IB hours in this market are published between about AED 200 and AED 450, and a visiting tutor's rate carries the travel inside it.

Monthly packages seen in this market include online blocks around AED 799 for eight sessions and visiting-tutor blocks between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A Dubai cost survey estimates monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's price list.

Two things are worth checking before any of that is paid. First, whether the quoted hour is sixty minutes or a school period of forty, since KHDA itself calculates mandatory-subject time on a forty-minute unit and some providers quote on the same basis. Second, what the rate includes: marking a past paper properly takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes outside the lesson, and a rate that excludes it is not the cheaper rate it appears to be. Ask for both in writing.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor in this market, set against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts with what a visiting tutor genuinely offers. Someone in the room can read a hand-written page without a camera angle, can reach for a textbook, and can hold the attention of a young student who drifts on a screen. For a Year 7 or Year 8 Cambridge Lower Secondary student that is a real argument, not a weak one. Published UAE rates for a visiting hour run roughly AED 180 to 500, with the travel priced inside the number.

The cost of that model is the tutor pool. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah choosing from the people willing to drive to them is choosing from a short list, and that list rarely contains a specialist who can teach the Extended supplement and the alternative to practical paper for a tiered science syllabus. Travel also eats the evening: a four o'clock session needing a forty-minute drive each way costs the tutor two hours and the household a fixed slot it cannot move.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online Cambridge IGCSE tuition over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The trade is specific. You give up the person in the room and you gain a specialist matched to the syllabus code and tier, plus a session that can shift by thirty minutes when traffic or a school event intervenes. sections.heading: Results day, a statement of results, and the fortnight that follows
paragraphs: Cambridge releases results to centres first, on Cambridge Direct, and the centre passes them on to candidates. For a June sitting the release to centres falls in August, with certificates issued months later; for a November sitting the release lands in January. Pearson's International GCSE pattern is comparable in shape and already documented: its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The pattern worth taking from all of this is that certificates always trail results by weeks.

That gap is the thing a family should plan around. Schools and universities asking for evidence in the days after results will accept the statement of results, and nobody needs to wait for a certificate before accepting an offer or registering for a sixth-form course. Families travelling during the UAE summer should decide before they leave who in the household can log in, who will read the statement properly, and who will contact the exams officer if a grade looks out of line with the marked work.

Queries about results run through the centre rather than the family, and they run on a short clock. If a grade sits a mark or two under a boundary on a paper where the student's own marked work was consistently stronger, that is the case to put to the exams officer within days. A tutor's useful contribution at that point is evidence: marked scripts, timed papers and a record of where the student was scoring. It is also why keeping the marked work matters.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside a Cambridge option block
paragraphs: A Cambridge timetable in the UAE does not run on its own. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's published requirements had to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Year 11 student carrying nine Cambridge subjects, these are additional timetabled lessons, additional homework and, in Arabic, an additional set of assessments to prepare for.

The rules are specific enough to matter to a tutoring plan. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Mandatory-subject time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that no mandatory lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes, and teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate KHDA permission to teach them.

There is one constraint parents should know before buying outside help for these three subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Support for them is therefore about the school's own material, the school's own assessments and study technique, rather than an alternative course taught in parallel. Where the real pressure on a household is Cambridge grades, the answer is often timetable triage instead of putting more subjects under paid tuition.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the tutor's permit, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Three compliance points come up in nearly every first conversation. The first is Ministry of Education equivalency. On the British track, as reported when the ministry clarified its requirements in July 2026, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify it on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

The second is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published anywhere official.

The third is academic honesty, and it is the one that ends school careers rather than costing money. A tutor teaches, explains, questions and gives feedback on work a student has already produced. A tutor does not author an assessed piece, redraft one to completion, or supply sentences for it. Where a provider offers a finished coursework piece for a fee, the student carries the malpractice risk and the provider keeps the money. Ask any tutor what they will refuse to do; the answer tells you what you are actually buying.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Or the timetable the centre gave you. It carries the syllabus code, the tier, the component numbers and the candidate number, and it is the only document that settles which course your child is actually on. Everything after this step is built from what it says.

process.title: Say which weeks are left
process.description: The series date, the school's mock window and any travel. A plan counted back from a real date is a different thing from a general offer of help, and the number of weeks decides whether the first session rebuilds a topic or goes straight to a marked past paper.

process.title: A trial session on a question that went wrong
process.description: Thirty minutes, at no charge and with no card details taken, built around a specific question your child lost marks on. You hear whether the tutor knows the syllabus code, and your child hears whether the explanation lands. Both matter, and only one of them shows up in a profile.

process.title: Confirm the tutor, the slot and what is included
process.description: In writing: the length of the hour in minutes, whether marking between sessions is included, and the rate. Forty-minute school periods and sixty-minute hours are both quoted in this market, and that is the single most common misunderstanding about what tuition costs.

process.title: Review at the mock, then again four weeks out
process.description: Two fixed checkpoints rather than a vague promise of progress. The mock script shows whether the plan is working. The four-week review decides what gets dropped, because by then the honest question is which topics to abandon rather than which ones to add.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 0607 are different courses, and 0625 Core and 0625 Extended are different papers. The match starts from the code and tier on your child's entry, which is why the statement of entry is the first thing asked for and the last thing a general tutoring enquiry ever mentions.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the board, not from memory
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are cited from those boards' own published key dates and timetables, with the month they were read. IB session dates are deliberately absent: the IB's site blocks automated checking, so no unverified exam date is published here at all.

whyPoints.title: Marked work between the sessions
whyPoints.description: Watching a worked solution feels productive and changes little. The student attempts the question, the tutor marks it against the mark scheme, and the next session starts from where the marks were lost. That loop is slower to set up, and it is what moves a script that has plateaued.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one, so the hour goes where the marks went
whyPoints.description: A group class moves at the pace of its weakest understanding of each topic. One student means a session can abandon its own plan when a marked script shows the real problem is unit discipline rather than the topic everyone at home had assumed it was.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer when nobody is free
whyPoints.description: Uncommon subject and tier combinations sometimes have no specialist available in the week you want to begin. You are told that, with the realistic alternatives, instead of being matched to whoever happens to be free. A mismatch costs more than a fortnight's wait does.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated before you book
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. Nobody here authors an assessed piece or redrafts one to completion, and any provider willing to do that is handing the student a malpractice risk while quietly keeping the fee.

faqs.question: A February exam window came up at our school. Is that a Cambridge series?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, and this is worth getting straight. Cambridge offers a February and March sitting to India only; a UAE centre cannot enter a candidate for it. In a UAE school, a February exam window is the mock series the school runs itself, which is valuable but carries no Cambridge grade. The sittings available to your child are June and November, and the only reliable confirmation of which one the centre has entered is the statement of entry from the exams officer. If a tutoring site tells you the UAE exam window is in February, it has copied an Indian calendar, and you should treat the rest of its dates with the same suspicion.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge syllabus code is my child entered for, and where can I read it?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry the exam centre issues before each series. It lists every subject with its syllabus code, the tier and the component numbers. The code matters because a subject name hides different courses: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 ask different questions and reward different preparation. If the sheet has not arrived yet, the exams officer can confirm the codes by email. Any tutor quoting for the subject without knowing its code is quoting for a course they have not actually seen.

faqs.question: What do the component numbers on a Cambridge statement of entry mean?
faqs.answer: They name the papers your child will sit. On a tiered science syllabus the written theory papers are split between Core and Extended by number, and a practical test and a written alternative to practical paper sit at the end of the list. Knowing which of those two your child is entered for changes the teaching completely: one needs laboratory method, the other needs reading a described experiment and criticising it. Confirm the numbers from the entry rather than from a syllabus PDF found online.

faqs.question: Why do two Cambridge candidates in different countries sit one paper at different times?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. The board's guidance to exams officers is explicit that the correct version for the zone must be used, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. For a family this produces one practical rule: plan the final fortnight from the document your centre gives you, and treat any timetable found through a search as a draft.

faqs.question: Our son is on the Core tier in 0580. What grade does that cap him at?
faqs.answer: A Core entry makes only the lower part of the grade scale available, because he sits the Core components and those papers cannot award the top grades. That is a real constraint on sixth-form courses whose published entry grades sit above it. The moment to argue a change is the autumn of Year 11, with six to eight weeks of marked Extended-style work to show the subject teacher. Once the final entry has gone in, the useful target is the top of the Core range, secured cleanly.

faqs.question: Our school asked for a forecast grade in February. What is it used for?
faqs.answer: It is the subject teacher's predicted outcome, submitted to Cambridge by the centre on the board's own date, and used in administering the series rather than in setting your child's result. The grade itself comes from the scripts. It is still worth caring about, because the evidence a teacher has in front of them in February is the marked work from the autumn term and the mock. That is the window in which a student can change what the teacher sees.

faqs.question: There are eleven weeks until paper one. What can still be changed?
faqs.answer: A good deal, provided the work is targeted. Eleven weeks is enough to rebuild one or two weak topics and then spend the back half on marked past-paper sections and answer shape. What it is not enough for is re-teaching a whole syllabus, and any plan implying otherwise is selling hours rather than a result. The sequence that works is topic repair first, marked papers next, and retrieval and timing only during the final fortnight before the paper.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge command word such as 'suggest' actually ask for?
faqs.answer: It asks for a plausible answer applied to a context the student has not seen before, which is exactly why it cannot be answered from memory. Each command word has an answer shape behind it: state wants a fact with no reasoning, describe wants what happens without the cause, explain wants the mechanism, and calculate wants working and units as well as a number. Learning those shapes is the fastest repair available to a student who knows the content and still lands on a grade 5.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge science component stands in for the laboratory, and can it be taught over video?
faqs.answer: The written alternative to practical paper, which sits at the end of the component list on the tiered science syllabuses. It is a reading and reasoning paper: a described experiment, a controlled variable to identify, a results table to complete, a method to criticise. All of that is taught well over live video. The practical test itself needs the school laboratory and a teacher at the bench, and no online provider should pretend otherwise to win the booking.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge results reach a candidate, and when does the certificate follow?
faqs.answer: Results go to the centre first on Cambridge Direct, and the centre releases them to candidates. For a June sitting that release falls in August, with certificates issued months later; a November sitting releases in January. Pearson's pattern is comparable and already published: its June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. The practical point is that certificates always trail results by weeks, and schools and universities accept the statement of results in the meantime.

faqs.question: A grade sits one mark under a boundary. What can be done, and how quickly?
faqs.answer: Queries go through the exam centre rather than the family, and the window is short, so the conversation with the exams officer should happen within days of release. What helps the case is evidence: marked past papers, timed scripts and a record of where your child was consistently scoring. Keep that work rather than clearing it out after the exams. A tutor's contribution at this stage is the paper trail, and there is nothing to assemble if it was thrown away in June.

faqs.question: Which figure should we budget for one Cambridge IGCSE subject in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the top, with qualified subject tutors online between roughly AED 150 and AED 300 and IGCSE specialists between about AED 200 and AED 450. A Dubai cost survey puts monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session between AED 600 and AED 1,200 in the middle band. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's own prices.

faqs.question: The lessons are described as one-to-one. Where do they actually take place?
faqs.answer: Over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student at their own desk anywhere in the Emirates. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The gain is the match: a tiered science entry needs someone who teaches that syllabus code and tier, and the chance that such a person lives twenty minutes from a family in Al Ain or Fujairah is low. Written working is shared on screen or photographed and marked.

faqs.question: Our daughter has six Cambridge IGCSEs and one is Islamic Education. Does the ministry count all seven?
faqs.answer: On the British track, as reported when the Ministry of Education clarified its requirements in July 2026, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. The count would therefore be taken from her other subjects. Verify the rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it, and note that at least one ranking UAE site publishes a six-subject version that does not match the clarification.

faqs.question: Can we see the permit a private tutor holds, and what should it say on it?
faqs.answer: Ask for it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Its code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Someone offered to rewrite my son's Cambridge coursework for a fee. What is wrong with that?
faqs.answer: The piece has to be his own work, and a submission produced by somebody else is malpractice. The student carries that risk, not the person who was paid for it. A tutor can teach the skill, question the argument, point at a weak paragraph and explain what the criteria reward, all on a draft your son has already produced himself. Nobody here authors an assessed piece or redrafts one to completion, and a provider willing to do it is selling your son a problem.

faqs.question: Our revision block runs through Ramadan and Eid. How do sessions get rearranged?
faqs.answer: Timings move rather than stopping. Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, energy is lowest in the late afternoon, and the Eid break removes a run of days from a counted-back plan. The usual pattern is to move sessions earlier or to after iftar, to put content-heavy work before the month and retrieval work inside it, and to write the lost sessions back into the plan rather than quietly losing them. Agree the revised slots before the month begins.

faqs.question: If no specialist covers my child's subject and tier, what are we told?
faqs.answer: That nobody is available, and what the realistic alternatives are: a short wait for a named tutor, a different slot that opens one up, or a different format for the component in question. Uncommon combinations, such as an Extended entry in a smaller option subject, are where this happens. Matching a student to whoever is free costs more than a fortnight's wait, because the hours go on the wrong paper and the family concludes tuition does not work.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the search
cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you take one habit from this page, take the habit of asking for the statement of entry and the centre's own timetable version before anything else. Those two documents give you the syllabus code, the tier, the components and the real number of weeks left, and they turn a vague worry into a plan with dates attached to it. Send them with your first message, say which subject went wrong and how it went wrong, and the trial session can go straight to a question your child lost marks on. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate.

intro.heading: What a family is actually buying when it moves from CBSE to the Diploma
paragraphs: The UAE has one of the largest concentrations of Indian-curriculum schooling outside India. Dubai alone had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with Indian curricula accounting for roughly a quarter of that enrolment. Every year a portion of those students leave CBSE at the end of Class 10 and enter the Diploma Programme, usually at a different school, and almost always because a family has concluded that the Diploma opens university routes the Indian boards make harder to reach.

That conclusion is often right and it is rarely costed. The move involves a change of school with its own fee structure, two years of a programme that assesses in a way CBSE never did, and in most cases a period of paid support while the student learns a new kind of academic work. Set against that is a genuine return: a qualification read directly by admissions offices in the United Kingdom, North America, Europe and the UAE, and a transcript built from six subjects in depth rather than from a single terminal examination.

The academic picture is more balanced than either side of the argument usually admits. CBSE trains procedural mathematics and quantitative science to a standard that frequently puts a student ahead of their Diploma cohort in the first term. What it does not train is the thing the Diploma weights most heavily outside the examination hall: an independent piece of assessed work the student scopes, carries out and writes up alone, worth a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most subjects. A strong CBSE student is not behind on content. They are starting from zero on a component worth a quarter of every subject.

The cost side has one piece of genuinely good news attached to it this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools, four following UK curricula and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A family moving school in this cycle is doing so into a market with more capacity and a frozen fee position.

This page sets out the move in that order: what it buys, where Class 10 leaves each subject, what the support actually costs at published market rates, the two-year arcs compared, the route decision in mathematics and science, and a plain view on when the move pays and when it does not. Every AED figure names the provider or authority that published it. Teaching for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE.

cbse-to-ib-transition.programmesIntro: Three qualifications sit in this decision, and the structural differences between them matter more than their reputations. Reading them side by side is what makes the real gap visible.

programmes.name: Central Board of Secondary Education
programmes.description: A national Indian curriculum built on NCERT material, with board examinations at the end of Class 10 and Class 12 and a comparatively small internal component. The strengths are systematic coverage, strong procedural mathematics and quantitative science, and a clear path through a known syllabus. Assessment rewards accuracy and recall under timed conditions, and the student is rarely asked to decide what a question should be.
programmes.countryNote: CBSE schools in the UAE follow the Indian academic calendar, which runs from April rather than from September, so a student moving to a Diploma school is also moving between academic years. That calendar mismatch creates either a short gap or an overlap, and it is worth planning for deliberately rather than discovering in March.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level with 240 recommended taught hours each and three at Standard Level with 150, graded 1 to 7, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Internal assessment contributes a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most subjects. There is no public examination in the middle of the two years.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma accounts for a small share of Dubai private school enrolment, so a student moving from a large CBSE school into a Diploma cohort is usually moving from a year group of several hundred into one of a few dozen. That changes the social experience as much as the academic one, and families are better served hearing it than discovering it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1 to 8 scale, with the Personal Project in MYP 5. A student moving from CBSE Class 10 into DP1 skips the MYP entirely, which means they arrive without the inquiry-based habits their classmates spent five years building. That is the single clearest structural disadvantage in the move, and it is a habit gap rather than a knowledge gap.
programmes.countryNote: Where a family is considering the move earlier, at the end of Class 8 or Class 9 into MYP 4 or MYP 5, the transition is materially easier because the student meets criterion-based assessment and the Personal Project before the Diploma stakes apply. Families who can move a year earlier usually should.

cbse-to-ib-transition.subjectsIntro: What follows is the handover point for each subject: what CBSE Class 10 finished with, and what the Diploma course assumes early in DP1. The gap, not the subject, is what paid support should be spent on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: CBSE Class 10 algebra and trigonometry are usually a strong foundation, and CBSE students frequently find the first term of Analysis comfortable. The gap appears at formal proof and at the exploration, which asks the student to develop mathematics of their own choosing rather than solve set problems.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content goes well beyond CBSE Class 10, particularly at Higher Level where inference and hypothesis testing appear, and a graphical display calculator is assumed in every paper. CBSE students often arrive with long-hand habits that cost time on a calculator-permitted paper.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Content overlap is substantial and often favourable. What is new is uncertainty and error treatment, and the scientific investigation, which requires the student to design an experiment, justify the method and handle messy data. Neither has a CBSE Class 10 equivalent.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Quantitative chemistry and mole calculations usually transfer well. Organic mechanisms are treated as a reasoning system rather than a set of named reactions, which is a shift in approach rather than in content, and it takes about a month to settle.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The terminology load is comparable, so content is rarely the issue. The change is in what gets marked: application of a named process to unfamiliar data, under strict command-term discipline, plus an independently designed investigation. Students who memorised well find this harder than students who understood well.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: This is the subject where the gap is widest for most CBSE students. The course assesses unseen non-literary text, a spoken individual oral on a global issue, and at Higher Level a formal essay on a studied work. Sustained independent argument is a skill built over months, not a topic to be covered.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Usually a new subject, which removes the problem of unlearning. The real demand is diagram fluency and three commentaries on published articles, which requires reading the financial press rather than a textbook. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Accessible content with a demanding internal assessment, which at Higher Level is a research project on a real organisation. CBSE students often choose it as a safe Group 3 option and then meet the research project, which is the component with no prior equivalent.

subjects.name: Hindi B
subjects.description: A genuine advantage for many students arriving from CBSE, where Hindi has been studied for years. Availability varies between UAE Diploma schools, so confirm whether the school teaches it or would require a school-supported arrangement before assuming Group 2 is settled.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: CBSE Class 10 computing exposure varies widely by school. The Diploma course is conceptual as well as practical, with abstract data structures at Higher Level and a case study released ahead of the session. Provision at Higher Level is thin across UAE schools, so check availability first.

cbse-to-ib-transition.regionsTitle: Where the UAE's Indian-curriculum communities sit
cbse-to-ib-transition.regionsIntro: CBSE schooling in the UAE clusters in particular communities, and the Diploma schools families move into are frequently in different ones. The practical consequence is a longer commute or a school-bus route, which decides what time a tutoring session can start.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda, Dubai
regions.note: One of the densest Indian-curriculum catchments in the country, with several large CBSE schools and long-established year groups. Families moving to a Diploma school usually move across the city, which adds commute time to a DP1 week that is already full.

regions.name: Karama, Bur Dubai and Oud Metha
regions.note: Older established Indian-curriculum schooling with very large cohorts. A student leaving a year group of several hundred for a Diploma cohort of a few dozen notices the change socially before they notice it academically, and that is worth talking about before the move.

regions.name: International City and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Apartment communities with heavy school-bus dependence and long routes. Evening tutoring slots work better than late-afternoon ones here, and online delivery removes the second journey a home visit would require.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: A mix of Indian-curriculum and international schools within a short radius, which occasionally makes a move possible without a change of community. Where that is available it removes most of the logistical cost of the transition.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Muwaileh, Sharjah
regions.note: Large Indian-curriculum schools serving Sharjah and the Dubai border communities. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula, programmes and assessment methods, so provision changes slowly and deliberately.

regions.name: Mussafah, Khalifa City and Al Wahda, Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The capital's Indian-curriculum provision, with Diploma schools concentrated elsewhere in the emirate. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools, and a change of school here often means a materially longer journey.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Private schools in both emirates are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma provision is minimal, so families moving curriculum generally move emirate too, and online teaching is the practical way to get subject-specific support either side of that.

sections.heading: What CBSE trains strongly, and what it does not train at all
paragraphs: An honest account of this transition begins with what the student brings, because most published advice treats the move as a remedial exercise and it is not. CBSE produces strong procedural mathematics: a Class 10 student who has worked seriously is typically fast and accurate with algebra, comfortable with trigonometric manipulation, and well drilled in the quantitative parts of physics and chemistry. In a Diploma cohort assembled from several curricula, that student often leads the first term of mathematics and is visibly ahead in the calculation-heavy parts of science.

The board also trains examination discipline. CBSE's terminal structure rewards accuracy under timed conditions and systematic coverage of a known syllabus, and students who have been through two board years arrive with revision habits their Diploma classmates may lack. That is a real asset in DP2, when a broad syllabus has to be covered against multiple papers in a short window.

What CBSE does not train is independent academic work. There is no equivalent of an internal assessment in which the student decides the question, designs the method, handles data that does not behave, and writes it up against published criteria over several weeks. There is no equivalent of the Extended Essay. There is no equivalent of Theory of Knowledge, where no syllabus exists to revise. Those components carry a quarter of most subject grades and up to three further Diploma points, and a strong CBSE student starts from zero on all of them.

The second thing it trains less is extended written argument. Diploma English A assesses unseen non-literary text and a spoken individual oral, and at Higher Level a formal essay on a studied work; several Group 3 subjects assess sustained evaluative writing. A student used to structured answers of a known length finds this harder than any mathematics in the programme, and it is the gap most families under-budget for because it does not look like a content deficit.
bullets: Strong: procedural mathematics, quantitative science, examination discipline
Absent: independent assessed work the student scopes alone
Absent: extended written argument against published criteria
The gap is a task gap, which is why it is invisible on a report card

sections.heading: Class 10 to DP1, subject by subject
paragraphs: The table below is the transition map for this specific move. Each row names where CBSE Class 10 leaves a student, what the Diploma course assumes early in DP1, the gap between the two, and a realistic number of support weeks assuming one session a week alongside normal school work. The weeks column is an estimate from teaching experience and not a published figure.

The pattern across the rows is the useful thing. In mathematics and the quantitative sciences, the content column shows overlap or advantage, and the gap column names a task rather than a topic: the exploration, the investigation, the uncertainty treatment. In English and the Group 3 subjects, the gap is a skill with a long build time. A family reading this table top to bottom usually revises its assumption about where the money should go.

One row deserves separate comment. Hindi B is an asset rather than a gap for many students arriving from CBSE, and it can turn Group 2 from a problem into a strength. Availability is the constraint: not every UAE Diploma school teaches it, and where it is not taught the alternative is another language from a standing start or a school-supported arrangement the coordinator has to agree. Settle that before the option form rather than after.

The weeks column also assumes the student has nothing else academic running, which is true in a summer gap and false once DP1 has started. A gap estimated at six weeks over a holiday is realistically a full term's work alongside five other subjects, and it is being closed while new content arrives on top of it every week. That is the argument for using whatever calendar gap the April-to-September mismatch creates rather than treating it as time off.

sections.heading: The cost of the move, in AED, with sources
paragraphs: This is the section competitor pages in this market do not write. Three of the six researched for this project publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in. What follows is the market in AED, attributed row by row, so a family can do the arithmetic before committing rather than after.

Start with fees, because that is the largest number and this year it is unusually stable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Supply is also rising: seven new private schools join the emirate for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment grew by 6 per cent.

Then the support. Published market rates in October 2026 run from a budget online tier, where EdFlik listed AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, through a qualified subject tutor band where Unitors advertised IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, to a specialist examination-year band where TutorChase listed AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table reached AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sat at AED 180 to 350 in that table and up to AED 500 with independent tutors, with travel accounting for much of the difference. BartyED listed AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram's prices; ours are discussed in the consultation following a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Two very different two-year arcs
paragraphs: Class 11 and 12 under CBSE and DP1 and DP2 cover the same two years of a student's life and are organised on opposite principles. CBSE concentrates the stake in a terminal board examination at the end of Class 12, with the syllabus known and the preparation strategy clear. The Diploma distributes the stake across internal assessments submitted through both years, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and final examinations in the May session, and there is no public examination at the midpoint to tell a student where they stand.

That difference changes what good work looks like. A CBSE student optimises by covering the syllabus and drilling past papers, which is a rational strategy for a terminal examination. A Diploma student who uses the same strategy misses the internal deadlines that are already scoring, arrives at the Extended Essay late, and treats Theory of Knowledge as revisable when it is not. The effort is identical; the allocation is wrong.

The table below compares the two arcs across the dimensions that actually change behaviour. Read the internal assessment row and the independent research row together: they are where a quarter of every subject grade and up to three Diploma points live, and they are the two rows with no CBSE counterpart. Everything else in the comparison is a matter of degree.

The mid-point feedback row is the one that catches careful families. Under CBSE a parent can read a Class 11 performance against board-style papers and form a reasonable view of where a Class 12 result will land. In DP1 there is no such instrument, and the only available signals are school assessments and internal assessment marks that most parents have never seen scored before. Taking those marks seriously in the first year, rather than waiting for something that looks like a board examination, is the behavioural change that matters most.

sections.heading: Choosing the maths and science route after CBSE
paragraphs: CBSE students arrive at the Group 5 decision with an unusual profile: strong procedural algebra, less exposure to open-ended modelling, and very little practice at writing mathematics up as an extended independent piece. On aptitude that profile usually points to Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and in most cases that is the right route. The complication is the exploration, which both routes require and which is unfamiliar as a task rather than as mathematics, so the route choice does not avoid it.

Where the decision needs care is the level. Analysis at Higher Level adds formal proof, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors and further calculus, plus a third paper of extended unprompted problem solving. A CBSE student who is fast and accurate may still find unprompted extended problems difficult, because fluency and independence are different things and only one of them was tested at Class 10. The useful diagnostic is an unfamiliar problem with no method given, not a test of what they already know.

On the sciences, the same pattern holds. Content transfers well and the scientific investigation does not transfer at all. A student taking two sciences at Higher Level is committing to two independently designed investigations in the same window as the Extended Essay, which is a workload question rather than an ability question. Families whose plan is medicine or engineering should check the named requirements for three or four specific programmes before fixing the combination, and verify each one on the institution's own admissions pages rather than from any summary.

sections.heading: The practical cost of changing school mid-stream
paragraphs: Most CBSE to Diploma moves involve changing school, and the non-academic costs of that are real enough to belong in the decision. A student leaves a year group that may number several hundred for a Diploma cohort of a few dozen, in a different community, often with a longer commute. Friendships, the familiar commute, the teachers who know how the student works, and in many cases a sibling's school routine are all affected. None of that appears on a fee schedule and all of it affects the first term.

The academic calendars do not line up either. CBSE schools in the UAE run an Indian academic year beginning in April, while Diploma schools start in late August or early September. Depending on when the move happens that produces either a gap of several months or an overlap, and both need planning. A gap is an opportunity if it is used as a bridge and a liability if it is treated as a holiday. An overlap means a student finishing one year while a new school expects preparatory work.

There is also an administrative tail. Certificates from two systems accumulate, and at the end of school they have to satisfy the Ministry of Education's equivalency process if a UAE university place is in view. That process is completed by the family with the authority, not by a school or a tutoring provider, and no provider should present it as a service it delivers. The sourced requirements for the British and American tracks are published; for the Diploma, check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly, and start earlier than feels necessary, because attestation of documents from more than one system takes time.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why it matters more in this move than most
paragraphs: A student arriving from a terminal-examination system into a programme where a quarter of each grade comes from work done at home is meeting a new kind of risk. Under CBSE the examination hall supplies its own integrity controls. Under the Diploma, the student submits an internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay with a declaration that the work is their own, countersigned by the school, and a breach is handled as malpractice with the consequence falling on the student.

The boundary for paid support is therefore worth stating before any work starts. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain exactly what each assessment criterion rewards, discuss whether a proposed question is answerable within the word limit, mark practice work and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not supply text, hand over finished work, or edit a draft to the point where the writing is no longer the student's. Saying this explicitly is not legal decoration; it is a genuine difference between providers in this market.

It matters particularly here because families new to the Diploma have no basis for knowing where the line is, and because this market contains providers who cross it openly, including one selling completed internal assessments at a published price. A parent comparing options should read what is actually offered rather than how it is described: a service priced per assignment rather than per hour is selling a product that puts a Diploma at risk. IB Gram holds no board or regulator accreditation, offers no guarantee of a grade, and will say when a request falls on the wrong side of the line.

sections.heading: When the move pays, and when it does not
paragraphs: The honest answer depends on the student, and a page that says the Diploma is always the better choice is selling something. The move pays most clearly where a student is heading for undergraduate study outside India and has the appetite for independent written work, because the Diploma is read directly by admissions offices in the United Kingdom, North America, Europe and the UAE, and the breadth requirement is an advantage rather than a tax for a student with wide interests.

It pays least where a student's strength is narrow and deep, where the family's university plan is Indian, or where the student is two years from examinations and genuinely struggles with extended writing. Six subjects including a language and a humanities subject is not a kindness to a student who wants three sciences and nothing else, and the Diploma does not allow that concentration. In those cases the alternatives are worth naming: continuing with CBSE, moving to A-Levels where three subjects are permitted, or the Career-related Programme where a UAE school offers it.

The table below sets out the profiles we see most often, what the Diploma adds in each case, what the move costs, and a plain verdict. It is written to be disagreed with by a family who knows their child better than any page does, which is the point of writing it down rather than implying that one answer fits everyone. If none of the five rows describes your child, that is useful information too: it means the decision rests on something specific to them rather than on a general comparison between two systems, and it is worth an hour with a subject teacher before it is worth a deposit.

process.title: Write down the destination list first
process.description: Three or four specific programmes at specific universities. If they are Indian, the arithmetic for this move usually does not work. If they are British, American, European or UAE institutions, it often does, and the named entry requirements then shape the subject choices before any preference is expressed.

process.title: Get the Class 10 teachers' view on written work
process.description: Not the mathematics mark, which is usually reassuring. Ask the English and social science teachers how your child handles an extended answer with no set structure, because that is the ability the Diploma weights most heavily and the one CBSE reports least clearly.

process.title: A free trial on an unfamiliar task, not a familiar one
process.description: One online session with a problem or a text the student has not met, and no method given first. For a CBSE student this is the only reliable way to separate fluency, which they usually have, from independence, which the Diploma requires and Class 10 did not test.

process.title: Spend the bridge on the written components
process.description: Most families book mathematics and most CBSE students do not need it. The block that pays is English A, the Group 3 written component, and a working understanding of what an internal assessment and an Extended Essay actually require. The topic list is agreed before the first session.

process.title: Map DP1 deadlines before the first week
process.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay question and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition arrive in overlapping windows set by the school. Putting them on one page in August, counted backwards from submission, is the highest-value hour of preparation available and involves no subject content at all.

whyPoints.title: The move is priced, not just recommended
whyPoints.description: Fees, new capacity and every tutoring band appear in AED with the authority or provider that published them. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which makes the arithmetic impossible for a UAE family from their pages.

whyPoints.title: What CBSE does well is stated as plainly as what it does not
whyPoints.description: Procedural mathematics, quantitative science and examination discipline are genuine strengths, and a transition page that treats the move as remediation misdirects the support budget to the subject where the student is already ahead.

whyPoints.title: The support goes where the gap is
whyPoints.description: For most students arriving from CBSE the widest gap is English A and the independent assessed components, not mathematics. We will say that in the first consultation even when a family has arrived asking for maths, because spending on the wrong subject is the most common waste in this move.

whyPoints.title: A verdict that includes not moving
whyPoints.description: Where the destination list is Indian, or where a student's strength is narrow and deep, the honest answer may be to stay with CBSE or to look at A-Levels instead. The comparison table on this page says so, because a page that recommends one answer to every profile is not advising.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency described, never performed
whyPoints.description: Certificates from two systems need the Ministry of Education's equivalency process if a UAE university place is in view. That is a process your family completes with the authority. This page states the sourced requirements and sends you to moe.gov.ae for the Diploma figure, which has not been read on a Ministry source.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, so the specialist is reachable
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, which means a family in Ajman or Umm Al Quwain reaches a Diploma English A specialist rather than the nearest available tutor of any subject.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma harder than CBSE Class 11 and 12?
faqs.answer: Harder is the wrong comparison, because the two are organised on opposite principles. CBSE concentrates the stake in a terminal board examination with a known syllabus, which rewards coverage and drilling. The Diploma spreads it across internal assessments scored through both years, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and final examinations, with no public examination at the midpoint. Most CBSE students find the content manageable and the independent assessed work genuinely difficult, because nothing in Class 10 asked them to decide a question, design a method and write it up against published criteria.

faqs.question: Will my child be behind in maths after CBSE Class 10?
faqs.answer: Usually the opposite. CBSE trains procedural algebra and trigonometry to a standard that frequently puts a student ahead of a mixed Diploma cohort in the first term, and the quantitative parts of physics and chemistry transfer well. The gap in mathematics is not content but the exploration, an independent piece of mathematical writing worth a fifth of the grade, and formal proof at Higher Level. Families who book mathematics support on arrival often find after a month that the money would have gone further in English A.

faqs.question: What does the whole CBSE to Diploma move cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Fees plus support, and this year the fee side is unusually stable: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27. On support, published October 2026 market rates ran from AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik's budget tier, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, to AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist examination-year work in Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table, with TutorChase at AED 270. Those are market figures from the named providers, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is it better to move at the end of Class 8 or wait until Class 10?
faqs.answer: Earlier is materially easier where it is practical. Moving into MYP 4 or MYP 5 means a student meets criterion-based assessment and the Personal Project before Diploma stakes apply, so the unfamiliar kind of work is learned at low cost. A Class 10 leaver enters DP1 having skipped the Middle Years Programme entirely and arrives without five years of inquiry-based habits their classmates have. The content is not the issue in either case; the habit is, and buying two low-stakes years to build it is a good trade.

faqs.question: Which Group 2 language should a CBSE student take in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Hindi B is frequently the strongest option, because years of prior study turn Group 2 from a problem into an advantage. The constraint is availability: not every UAE Diploma school teaches Hindi, and where it is absent the alternatives are another language from a standing start or a school-supported arrangement the Diploma coordinator must agree to. Settle this before the option form, because a Group 2 choice made from a standing start affects the whole workload picture and is one of the hardest subjects to change later.

faqs.question: Does the Indian school calendar make the move awkward?
faqs.answer: It does, and it is worth planning rather than discovering. CBSE schools in the UAE run an academic year beginning in April, while Diploma schools start in late August or early September. Depending on when the move happens, that leaves either a gap of some months or an overlap in which a student is finishing one year while a new school expects preparatory work. A gap used as a bridge is valuable; a gap treated as a holiday is the most common missed opportunity in this transition.

faqs.question: Can my child take three sciences in the Diploma like a CBSE science stream?
faqs.answer: Partly. The Diploma requires one subject from each of five groups, and the sixth can be a second subject from Groups 1 to 4 instead of an arts subject, so three sciences is structurally possible. What is not possible is dropping the language or the humanities subject, which a CBSE science stream effectively allows. Three Higher Level sciences also means three independently designed investigations in the same window as the Extended Essay. For a student who genuinely wants only sciences, A-Levels permit the concentration the Diploma does not.

faqs.question: How long does it take a CBSE student to settle into Diploma assessment?
faqs.answer: About a term for the content and most of DP1 for the assessment. Content settles quickly because the overlap is substantial and often favourable. The internal assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are new kinds of task, and competence at them builds across the first year rather than in a few weeks. The practical implication is that a slow first term is normal and a slow first year is not, because internal assessment marks earned in DP1 are already counting towards the final grade.

faqs.question: Will a Diploma from a UAE school be recognised for Indian universities?
faqs.answer: Recognition arrangements for Indian admissions are set by the individual universities and by the national bodies that govern them, and they change, so the only reliable step is to check the specific institution's admissions page and any association of Indian universities guidance that applies. What this page will say is that a family whose plan is Indian undergraduate study should establish that before paying for the move, because the clearest return on a Diploma is in admissions systems that read it directly, and CBSE already serves the Indian route well.

faqs.question: My child memorises well and writes poorly. Is the Diploma a mistake?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily a mistake, but it is a known cost that should be budgeted. Diploma English A assesses unseen non-literary text and a spoken individual oral, and several Group 3 subjects assess sustained evaluative writing, so a student who writes poorly meets that demand in four or five of their six subjects. Eight to sixteen weeks of focused support in English alone is a realistic estimate. Where the family's plan allows it, A-Levels with three subjects avoiding extended writing is a legitimate alternative worth comparing properly.

faqs.question: What is the Extended Essay, and is there anything like it in CBSE?
faqs.answer: It is an independent research piece with a strict word limit, in a subject the student usually studies, chosen and managed by the student across DP1, contributing with Theory of Knowledge up to three points to the Diploma total. There is no CBSE equivalent, which is why it is the single most commonly underestimated component in this move. The research itself is rarely the difficulty. Scoping a question that can actually be answered in the words available, and holding a self-set timeline over months, are the real demands.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write parts of the internal assessment if my child is struggling?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who agrees to is putting your child's Diploma at risk rather than helping. Internal assessments are submitted with the student's declaration of authorship and countersigned by the school, and a breach is handled as malpractice with the consequence falling on the student. Legitimate support is teaching the content, explaining exactly what each criterion rewards, discussing whether a question is answerable, and giving feedback on the student's own draft. This market contains providers selling completed assessments at a published price; that is a different product.

faqs.question: How does a smaller Diploma cohort affect my child?
faqs.answer: More than families expect. A student may leave an Indian-curriculum year group of several hundred for a Diploma cohort of a few dozen, which changes the social experience, the range of subject sets available, and the likelihood that a chosen Higher Level class runs at all. Smaller cohorts also mean less room for a level or subject change in DP1, because the receiving class may not exist. Ask the new school how many students are expected in each Higher Level class before the option form is signed.

faqs.question: Are there more Diploma places available in Dubai this year?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following UK curricula and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment rising 6 per cent. Combined with KHDA's confirmation on 22 May 2026 that fees would not increase for 2026-27, a family moving curriculum in this cycle is doing so into a market with more capacity and a stable fee position than in several recent years. Availability still varies sharply by community and by subject.

faqs.question: Does the Diploma leave room for the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education periods?
faqs.answer: It has to, because they are required and they are not optional in either system. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A CBSE student is already used to these periods, which is one part of the move that involves no adjustment at all.

cbse-to-ib-transition.closingHeading: Do the arithmetic before the deposit
cbse-to-ib-transition.closingBody: This move is usually a good decision and it is never a free one. Write down three or four specific universities and read their entry requirements. Ask the Class 10 English teacher, not the mathematics teacher, how your child handles an extended answer with no set structure. Then book one trial lesson on an unfamiliar task with no method given, which is the only reliable way to separate fluency from independence. The session is online, one to one and free, and the written note afterwards will say where the support should actually go.
