sections.heading: Why a claim of regulator approval deserves a second look
paragraphs: The most dangerous sentence available to a UAE tutoring website is one that places a regulator's name immediately before the word approved. It reads as a licence and it usually is not. The permit KHDA issues in this space is an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, granted to an organisation with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first, a cap of six months to finish the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. It is a real document with real conditions, and a company with no premises in the emirate cannot hold it. Borrowing the name of it is a misrepresentation rather than marketing.

The boards work the same way. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes and trains teachers who work in them. Cambridge International and Pearson appoint exam centres and publish rules those centres must follow. None of the three issues anything to a tutoring platform. A page claiming otherwise is either confused about its own status or hoping you will not ask. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation with the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Education, and holds no permit or accreditation from any of them. We run no office, centre or branch anywhere in the Emirates.

Three related habits in this market are worth treating with the same suspicion. A star rating a provider has written about itself, with no countable reviews behind it, is a self-serving number rather than evidence. A statistic without a sample size, a date and a method behind it is decoration, which is why no satisfaction percentage or average tutor score appears on this page. And a tutor described as a current examiner should be asked, politely, for the board and the year, because examiner status cannot be inferred and does not come with access to marking, boundaries or unreleased papers. What we publish instead is narrow and checkable: the permit position, the qualification, the board and syllabus taught, and the fact that lessons happen over video.

sections.heading: The UAE subjects that run beside the IB, and who may teach them
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. This sits on top of a federal rule that private schools need not follow any specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. A Diploma student in Dubai is therefore carrying six IB subjects plus a set of national requirements, and the timetable pressure is real.

The organisation rules are specific enough to be worth quoting to any tutor who claims to cover these subjects. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is delivered in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

There is one constraint that reshapes what Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring can honestly offer. For the mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who advertises their own bespoke Arabic programme for these lessons is describing something the rules do not permit. The honest version is narrower and more useful: work from the school's own scheme and set material, build reading fluency, script control and answer structure, and leave the content selection where the Ministry has put it. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the KHDA approval those subjects require.

sections.heading: Where the honesty line sits on the IA, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: A tutor may teach the skill, discuss a plan the student has proposed, ask questions about a draft the student has produced, point at the published criteria, and mark practice work. A tutor may not supply sentences for assessed coursework, restructure the student's text, or hand back a version to submit. The student's work has to be their own, and the school's coordinator has to declare that it is. This is not a house rule we invented to be awkward; it is the line the IB's academic-honesty regulations draw, and crossing it puts the student's diploma at risk rather than the tutor's reputation.

That line has a practical shape in a session. The student opens their own file and shares the screen. The tutor reads what is there, asks what the method was meant to show, asks where the criterion is being met, and says plainly when it is not. The student makes the changes afterwards, in their own words, in their own file. Nothing is typed into the document by the tutor and nothing is sent back rewritten. A short written note of what was discussed goes to the family, which has a second use: if a coordinator asks what outside support was involved, there is an honest and specific answer rather than a shrug.

Supervision is the other boundary parents miss. The Extended Essay has an appointed supervisor at the school who signs the reflections, and a tutor is an additional reader, never a replacement for that person. The TOK essay belongs to the TOK teacher. One UAE-facing site in this market advertises finished internal assessments for sale at a four-figure price in dirhams; that is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student who buys it, and it is the clearest possible reason to ask what a provider actually does before paying. We also do not reproduce or hand out syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference the official sources and link to them.

sections.heading: The school system a tutor has to fit into
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of pupils, Indian curricula 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate about seven in a hundred. Read that last figure twice. The IB is a minority programme inside the country's largest private-school market, which is the real reason an experienced Diploma teacher is harder to find than a GCSE maths tutor, and why price is the wrong first question. Scarcity of people who have taught the course is the binding constraint.

The sector is also moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. New IB places are good news for admissions. They do nothing for teacher supply in the short run, because new schools recruit from the same pool of experienced Diploma teachers everyone else is recruiting from.

What all of this means for a tutoring plan is specific. The subject your child needs help with may not be the subject the school is strongest in, and the inspection report is where that shows up. A school that is excellent in English and only acceptable in mathematics will produce exactly one kind of parent enquiry. Because delivery is online, the match is made on syllabus fit rather than on which community the tutor lives in, so a family in Fujairah and a family in Jumeirah are choosing from the same specialists at the same rate.

sections.heading: Which board sets the dates, and why the centre's zone matters
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Those Checkpoint windows belong to Years 7 to 9 and are not an IGCSE sitting, and the February and March examination series that keeps surfacing in search results is offered to India only, so no UAE centre enters a candidate for it. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. That single rule explains a conversation UAE parents have every year: two cousins at different schools sitting the same paper at different times, and both schools being right.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including series more than a year ahead, so any plan should be built from the board's live timetable rather than from a date copied onto a tutoring page and left there.

On the IB this page deliberately stops short. UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session exists as a second route. We are not publishing an IB examination or results date here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none: a family that plans six weeks of revision around a wrong week has lost the six weeks. Ask the school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly. One thing is constant across all three boards. The IB exam entry deadline, like the Cambridge and Pearson ones, is set months before the first paper, and it is the school that submits entries, not the family.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the paperwork that follows the certificate
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can act on, and it is the step families forget until results day has passed. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises most parents.

For the American track the requirements are tests rather than subject counts. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five. Getting that number right is worth more to a family than any amount of reassuring prose, and it is the kind of error that should make you check everything else on a page.

On the IB, this page publishes no figure at all. The source that sets out both the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate requirement for the Diploma has to be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before anyone plans around it. Two further points. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, submits or influences, and no tutoring is required for it. Any page suggesting that tuition smooths a regulatory process is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: What to ask before the first paid lesson, and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Five questions settle most of this. Which permit do you hold, and may I see the record? What is your teaching or subject qualification, from which institution, in which year? Which board and syllabus have you taught, and for how many cohorts? What will you not do with my child's internal assessment? And can the first session be built around a question from the current paper rather than an introduction? A tutor who has taught the course answers the fifth question with enthusiasm, because it is the part of the job they are good at. Hesitation there is more informative than any certificate.

The honest part most providers leave out is coverage. Some subject and level combinations have very few experienced teachers anywhere in the Emirates: Higher Level Physics, Computer Science, Economics HL in an exam term, and the smaller language B courses. When no UAE-resident specialist is available for the slot you need, we say so. The alternative we offer is an India-based IB specialist teaching the same syllabus over the same video link in the same Gulf Standard Time slot, and we tell you that is what is happening rather than hiding it behind a local-sounding phone number. If neither works, we will say that too.

One last thing, because enquiry forms about children collect more than people realise. We ask for the school, the programme, the subject, the level and the year group, because the match cannot be made without them. We do not need a photograph, a full report card or a medical history to arrange a trial lesson, and a provider asking for those without explaining why is worth a question. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection sits behind this, and the privacy link on every page sets out what is kept and how to have it deleted.

process.title: Tell us the school, the board and the subject
process.description: One message with the school name, the emirate, the programme, the subject and the level is enough to start. The school matters because its regulator, its option blocks and its internal deadlines shape everything that follows. If you have the most recent inspection report or a subject report to hand, say what it flagged.

process.title: See the credential position in writing
process.description: Before any payment, you get the tutor's qualification, the board and syllabus they have taught, their programme experience and their permit position in writing. Nothing in that note describes anyone as approved by a regulator, because no regulator issues such a thing to private tutors. Ask follow-up questions; that is what the note is for.

process.title: Trial lesson on a real syllabus question
process.description: The first session is a working one, built on a question from your child's current syllabus rather than an interview. There is no charge for it, it covers one subject, and no payment details are taken beforehand. You decide afterwards whether the match holds. Most families know inside twenty minutes.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video at the same time each week, with the student's own files on screen. The slot is set around the school run, prayer times and homework load, and shifts to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. A short written note after each session records what was covered.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the school's assessment dates, mock window and coursework deadlines rather than a generic programme. If the subject is no longer where the problem is, we say so and change it. Pausing during exam weeks or travel is normal and does not cost anything.

whyPoints.title: The credential question answered honestly
whyPoints.description: We publish what can be evidenced and name what cannot. A permit, a qualification, a syllabus taught and a cohort count are checkable. A regulator's endorsement of a private tutor is not available in the UAE, from anybody, so you will not read it here. That distinction is the whole point of this page.

whyPoints.title: Regulator detail that matches your emirate
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education each govern different schools. We tell you which one holds your school's file, what it actually approves, and which document to read before deciding tuition is the answer.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on work the student has produced. No text is supplied, no file is edited, no coursework is produced on a student's behalf. A short written record of each session exists partly so that a coordinator's question about outside support can be answered with specifics.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are delivered over live video, the pool is not limited to people who can reach your community before dinner. A family in Umm Al Quwain and a family in Dubai Marina choose from the same Higher Level specialists, and the travel cost that sits inside a visiting tutor's rate is simply absent.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, or none
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page comes from a named source: the federal portal, KHDA documents, Cambridge and Pearson's own date publications, the Dubai media office. Where a number is not verifiable, including the IB session dates, we leave the space empty and say why rather than filling it with something plausible.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist covers your subject, level and slot, you are told at the enquiry stage, along with the alternative and where the tutor would be teaching from. No local-sounding phone number, no office address in the Emirates that does not exist, and no pretence that every combination is always covered.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a certified IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Not as a single credential. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes and trains teachers who work inside them; it does not license private tutors, and neither does any UAE education authority. What exists instead is a bundle of separate things: a MoHRE private tuition work permit, a teaching qualification, a subject degree and documented experience of the syllabus your child sits. A provider using the phrase should be able to say which of those four they mean. If the answer is vague, the word is doing marketing work rather than describing a document somebody issued.

faqs.question: What qualification should a certified IB tutor actually hold?
faqs.answer: For Diploma teaching, look for a degree in the subject plus either a recognised teaching qualification or several cohorts of classroom experience with that exact course. The degree proves content depth beyond Higher Level. The teaching qualification proves training in how to explain things. Neither proves knowledge of IB command terms, published criteria or the way marks are allocated in that subject, which is why the cohort question matters most. Ask which board, which course, which years, and which option topics they have taught, then judge the answer in a working first session rather than on paper.

faqs.question: Which document proves a tutor may legally charge for lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The federal portal states it is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted online with caution. The permit covers legality, nothing more. It says nothing about subject knowledge, teaching skill or whether the person has ever seen an IB mark scheme.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring company describe itself as certified by a UAE authority?
faqs.answer: Only if it holds the specific permit it is referring to and can show it. The relevant one in Dubai is a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to a training institute with premises, with initial approval first, a six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal. A platform with no premises in the emirate cannot hold that permit. IB Gram does not hold it, operates no centre in the Emirates, and has no accreditation or partnership with KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah authority, the Ministry of Education or any examination board.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a separate credential to teach the Diploma rather than IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No separate licence exists for either, which is exactly why the experience question carries the weight. The practical difference is large. IGCSE rewards coverage and clean examination technique across a two-year syllabus. The Diploma adds internal assessment with published criteria, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and papers written by the IB rather than the school. A tutor who has taught IGCSE for a decade may have never marked a Diploma investigation. Ask about the specific course and level, not the board, and ask what they would look at first in a weak draft.

faqs.question: If the specialist teaching my child is not resident in the UAE, what certification applies?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE permit regime applies to people providing private tutoring in the UAE, so a tutor resident elsewhere is working under the rules of the country they live and pay tax in. That is one reason we say plainly where a tutor is based rather than implying a local presence. For a family, the questions that then matter are qualification, syllabus experience and timing: lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time either way, and an India-based IB specialist teaching the same course is often the only way to cover a scarce Higher Level subject.

faqs.question: Is paying someone to proofread an Internal Assessment against the rules?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what proofreading means in practice, which is why the word is best avoided. A tutor may read work the student has written, ask questions about the method, point to the published criteria and say where a criterion is not being met. The student then makes changes themselves, in their own words. If somebody rewrites sentences, restructures paragraphs or returns a polished version ready to submit, that is no longer feedback and it puts the student's diploma at risk. The school's coordinator has to declare the work is the student's own.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need KHDA approval to teach Arabic or Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: The requirement sits on schools rather than on private tutors. KHDA requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval to teach those subjects, and that approval attaches to the post inside the school. A private tutor working with your child in the evening is in a different position, but a real constraint still applies to the content: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. So a tutor should be working from the school's own scheme, not a programme of their own design.

faqs.question: Why is lesson time for the mandatory UAE subjects counted in 40-minute units?
faqs.answer: Because that is the unit KHDA uses to calculate instructional time for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Schools may vary the actual lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For parents this explains a timetable oddity: two schools can meet the same requirement with very different-looking weeks, one with short daily lessons and one with longer blocks. It also explains why squeezing extra IB revision into the school day is not something a school can simply decide to do.

faqs.question: Which emirates have no education regulator of their own?
faqs.answer: Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Private schools in those three are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so there is no local inspection portal to browse the way Dubai families browse KHDA's. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. If your school sits with the Ministry, ask the school directly for its most recent report and for the board it enters candidates with.

faqs.question: Do the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 make a specialist easier to find?
faqs.answer: For admissions, yes. The 2026-27 intake adds seven schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For tutoring, not in the short term. New schools recruit experienced Diploma teachers from the same pool every existing school draws on, so the number of people who have taught Higher Level Chemistry for several cohorts does not rise because a building opened. Scarcity of experience, not capacity, is what makes a specialist hard to book.

faqs.question: Does a tutor with more certification charge more per hour?
faqs.answer: Usually, though the market pays for scarcity rather than for paperwork. Published UAE rates run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online and university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist, with named or examiner-level tutors advertised higher again. Those are figures published by other providers, not ours. A permit costs nothing to hold, so it adds nothing to a rate; a decade of marking Diploma investigations is what the upper band is actually paying for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor speak to my child's subject teacher or attend a school meeting?
faqs.answer: Only if you arrange it and the school agrees, and it is worth asking. A tutor who has read the school's own feedback works faster than one guessing from a report card. What a tutor should not do is approach the school independently, present themselves as part of your child's provision, or ask a teacher for material the school has not released. In Abu Dhabi there is a further wrinkle: ADEK's professional-ethics position bars school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so that particular arrangement is not available.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry ask American-curriculum students for that it does not ask of IB students?
faqs.answer: The published American-track requirements are test scores rather than subject counts: English proficiency through a 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The same published guidance sets out the British track as five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus an A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. It states no IB points threshold, so confirm the Diploma position on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What should we have in writing before any money changes hands?
faqs.answer: Four things. The tutor's qualification and the awarding institution, the board and syllabus they have taught and for how many cohorts, their permit position, and what they will and will not do with assessed coursework. Add the practical terms: session length, the rate, what happens to a lesson cancelled at short notice, and who to contact if the match is wrong. The trial session comes before any of this costs you anything, covers one subject, and needs no payment details. If a provider will not put the first four in a message, that is the answer.

certified-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the document, not the adjective
certified-ib-tutor.closingBody: A search for a certified IB tutor is really a search for a shortcut through a judgement nobody can make for you. There is no register to check, because no UAE authority or examination board licenses private IB tutors. What there is: a MoHRE permit that makes the lessons lawful, a qualification with a name and a year on it, a syllabus somebody has genuinely taught, and a first session that shows whether they can teach it to your child. Tell us the school, the emirate, the subject and the level, and we will send the credential position in writing before anything is booked. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What you are actually buying when you pay more for a certified IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: Nobody certifies IGCSE tutors. Cambridge International awards qualifications to candidates and accredits exam centres; Pearson does the same for its International GCSE. Neither body issues a licence to a private tutor, and no UAE authority issues a subject teaching certificate to one either. So when an advertisement in this market promises a certified IGCSE tutor in the UAE, it is pointing at something else: a teaching qualification earned abroad, a university degree in the subject, a professional development award, seasonal marking experience, or the one document UAE law genuinely requires, the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Each of those sits at a different point on the AED 45 to AED 650 an hour this market charges, and only some of them change what happens inside a lesson.

That is why this page is organised around money rather than badges. Private tutoring here runs on a permit: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, MoHRE grants it free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount belongs on this page.

The permit is the legal floor rather than a measure of teaching quality. It establishes that a person may lawfully charge for lessons in the UAE. It says nothing about whether they have taught Cambridge IGCSE 0580 at Extended tier, whether they can read a Paper 6 mark scheme aloud and explain why a correct answer scored zero, or whether they know that your daughter's school sets its coursework deadline ten weeks before the board does. Those are the things that move a grade, and none of them appears on a certificate. A family paying AED 250 an hour deserves to know which of them that money buys, which is what the tables below set out tier by tier.

Market rates read in October 2026 spread across five recognisable bands. Budget online tutoring starts low: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit higher, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150. A tutor who travels to a family costs AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the price, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. Subject specialists run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At the top of the market BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour. Each of those is that provider's own published figure rather than ours.

Teaching arranged through IB Gram is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run, prayer times and the bus. Nobody is sent to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a decision about supply, not about saving money. A family in Al Barsha choosing from everyone willing to drive to Al Barsha on a Tuesday evening is choosing from a very short list, and the list gets shorter the rarer the subject. A family choosing online one-to-one IGCSE lessons is choosing from every specialist free at that hour, which is how a Computer Science 0478 or Accounting 0452 request gets filled at all.

certified-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: The word certified means something different at each stage of a British-curriculum school in the UAE, and so does the rate. These are the four stages families ask about, with what a credential is genuinely worth at each one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined by written papers at the end of Year 11, with a June series and a November series each year and Core or Extended tier set per subject. Syllabus codes are four digits: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. The tier decides the grade range available, the papers sat and the content examined, so a tutor who has only ever taught Core will mis-pitch an Extended candidate by a whole band of difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of pupils in Dubai's 227 private schools, which is why Cambridge IGCSE support is the most heavily supplied part of this market and the most variable in price. Centres are allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, so the first thing a competent tutor asks for is the statement of entry rather than the textbook.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same qualification level under a different board, with its own codes: 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language. Exams are available in May/June and November each year. Papers, tiering and the balance between recall and application differ from Cambridge, and some subjects are structured so that units can be sat across more than one series. A tutor who teaches one board's papers with the other board's technique costs a candidate marks that have nothing to do with knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Plenty of UAE schools enter candidates for both boards across a nine-subject block, which is the single most common reason a family finds their tutor working from the wrong past paper. Ask the school which board each subject is entered for, write it down, and match the tutor to the code. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable on its own site is the only version worth planning around.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE block, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. This is where a certified tutor is worth least in badge terms and most in diagnostic terms: the gaps that surface here, particularly in algebraic manipulation and scientific writing, are the gaps that cap an Extended grade two years later. Hourly rates at this stage sit at the lower end of the market because the content is less specialised, not because the teaching matters less.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving mid-year from an Indian, American or national-curriculum school usually land in these years, and the subject gap is rarely where parents expect it. A Year 8 arrival from a CBSE school often has stronger arithmetic and weaker extended writing than their UAE classmates. Two or three diagnostic lessons at AED 150 to 200 an hour buy a written picture of that gap, which is a cheaper way to spend money than a year of general support.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The year after IGCSE, where the credential question sharpens because content depth genuinely requires a subject degree. A tutor who can carry a candidate through 0580 Extended may not be able to teach International AS Mathematics, and the honest ones say so. This is also where the gap between a teaching qualification and subject depth becomes visible: pedagogy transfers across levels, but nobody teaches further calculus they have not studied.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE families this stage also carries the Ministry of Education equivalency paperwork. The published British-track rule asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before you plan around it.

certified-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Credential value is not spread evenly across subjects. In some, a strong graduate is plenty; in others, the market is short of anyone who has taught the Extended paper at all. The notes below say which is which, with the codes to quote when you ask.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Cambridge IGCSE 0580 · Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: The most supplied subject in this market and the one where a certificate tells you least, because almost every tutor offers it. The useful question is tier experience: Extended papers reward algebraic fluency and multi-step reasoning that Core never tests. Ask how many Extended candidates they have taken through a full series.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: A different subject wearing a similar name, and a genuine scarcity point. Calculus, trigonometric identities and matrices appear at a depth most general maths tutors have not taught since university. Here a subject degree earns its premium, and a tutor who hesitates over the syllabus code is the wrong match.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Cambridge IGCSE 0625 · Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Marks leak in two places: unit and prefix handling in calculations, and the written explanation questions where a correct idea scores nothing without the required vocabulary. The alternative-to-practical paper is its own skill, testing apparatus reasoning and data handling rather than recall, and it is routinely under-prepared.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations separate the top grades from the middle, and organic reaction pathways reward memorised structure over improvisation. A tutor with a chemistry degree reads a candidate's working and sees the misconception; a tutor working from an answer key sees only a wrong number.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content is largest and the marking the most precise. Grades turn on command-term discipline: describe, explain and compare are marked against different criteria, and candidates who write everything they know about a topic score less than candidates who answer the question asked.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: A qualification in which marks are awarded against assessment criteria rather than for correct answers, which makes credential checking harder and more important. Ask to see written feedback on a real response, anonymised. A tutor who marks against the published criteria will annotate against them by name.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Heavily entered across the UAE and often confused with First Language English when a family books support. The two have different papers, different grade descriptors and different teaching. Confirm the code on the statement of entry before a single lesson is paid for, because the codes differ by one digit.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries the marks that candidates assume prose will carry. Axes labelled correctly, shifts drawn in the right direction and the explanation tied to the diagram are worth more than a page of general argument. A tutor who has marked this subject will say so and show you what the mark scheme rewards.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the case material is where grades are decided. Candidates who answer in general business language score the lower band; candidates who quote the stimulus and apply a named concept score the upper one. Scarce at Extended tier in the smaller emirates, which is where online matching earns its keep.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: One of the hardest subjects in the UAE to find a local specialist for at any price. Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the data-representation topics are taught badly by anyone who has only written production code. This is the clearest case for drawing on a national pool rather than a drive radius.

subjects.name: Accounting
subjects.description: Narrow, technical and routinely mis-taught by generalists. Double-entry discipline and the layout conventions the mark scheme expects are learnable in a term with the right tutor and never learnable from a textbook alone. Availability is thin, so expect to book a time that suits the specialist rather than the family.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language
subjects.description: Sits alongside the UAE mandatory subjects rather than replacing them, and the two are frequently confused. The IGCSE qualification is examined by the board; the mandatory school stream is set under Ministry rules and taught by staff the school must hold approval for. Be clear which one you are buying help with.

certified-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where certification is checked, emirate by emirate
certified-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The regulator changes across the seven emirates, and with it what a school must verify about a teacher and what a parent can look up. Rates follow supply, which is thickest in Dubai and thinnest in the north.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees the quality of private education in the emirate: 227 private schools, 387,441 pupils and 17 curricula in 2024-25. Deepest tutor supply in the country and the widest published rate spread, from AED 45 an hour to AED 650.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which rules out the most commonly offered arrangement.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller and more spread-out school network. Specialist supply for subjects such as Computer Science 0478 and Accounting 0452 is noticeably thinner than in the capital, and an evening slot taught over live video is usually the only way to get one at all.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the emirate regulator means a school's licensed syllabus is a matter of record rather than a marketing line.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. Families often commute towards Sharjah or Dubai for school, which compresses the evening window and makes a fixed online slot easier to hold than a visiting arrangement.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Local tutor supply at Extended tier is limited, and named subject specialists are almost always taught in remotely.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under Ministry of Education supervision, on the east coast and separated from the main school corridor by a mountain drive. Fujairah returns essentially zero mentions across the competitor pages in this market, which is a fair reflection of how little local specialist supply exists.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest school network in the country, also supervised by the Ministry of Education. A family here looking for a qualified IGCSE subject teacher in a minority subject is choosing between a long drive and a video call, and the video call is the one that gets a specialist.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai, UK-curriculum IGCSE schools
schoolClusters.note: The densest IGCSE cluster in the country, and the one where parents most often compare notes on tutor rates. Schools here enter candidates for both Cambridge and Pearson across a nine-subject block, so the board must be confirmed subject by subject rather than assumed from the school.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: A more dispersed network across the islands and the mainland, under ADEK. Because ADEK's ethics rules bar school staff from tutoring their own enrolled students, families here are choosing from outside the school from the start, which makes the credential question the first one rather than the last.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Fewer schools, longer distances and a much shorter list of local subject specialists. Students here sit the same papers on the same days as their Dubai counterparts, which is the whole argument for matching on syllabus code rather than postcode.

certified-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families buy this, priced differently because the credential required differs. Every format below is taught one-to-one or in a named pair over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Diagnostic block, then a decision
modes.description: Six lessons with one aim: a written picture of where the marks are actually going, built from the student's own marked work and a past paper sat under timed conditions. At the end you get the diagnosis in writing and decide whether to continue, change tutor or stop. It is the cheapest honest way to test a credential claim, because teaching quality shows up in a diagnosis long before it shows up in a grade.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: The standard arrangement across Years 10 and 11: one fixed hour a week with the same specialist, working a term ahead of the school's scheme of work rather than a week behind it. Homework is set and marked, and a short note after each lesson tells you what was covered and what was weak. Continuity is the point, which is why the slot is fixed rather than rebooked each week.

modes.title: Two-subject science or maths block
modes.description: Physics and Chemistry, or Mathematics and Additional Mathematics, taught by one tutor who holds both syllabus codes where that is genuinely possible. It saves a family one scheduling negotiation and lets the tutor use calculation technique from one subject in the other. Where no single specialist covers both at Extended depth we say so and propose two, because a stretched generalist is worse value than two specialists.

modes.title: Pre-series intensive
modes.description: A short, dense block before a June or November series, built backwards from the papers and the entry already made. Content coverage stops; paper technique, mark-scheme language and timed practice take over. This is the format where examiner-level experience is worth the premium that market tier charges, because the whole exercise is about how marks are awarded rather than what the syllabus contains.

sections.heading: Certified by whom? Six things that word is doing in a UAE tutoring advertisement
paragraphs: Start by asking who issued the certificate. The six credentials in the table cover almost every use of the word in this market and they are not interchangeable. A PGCE earned in the United Kingdom evidences training in pedagogy and classroom assessment. A BSc in Chemistry evidences subject depth well beyond IGCSE Extended. A Cambridge professional development award evidences a structured course in teaching and assessing a Cambridge syllabus. Marking experience evidences practice in applying a mark scheme. The MoHRE permit evidences lawful permission to charge for lessons in the UAE. Only the last of those is a UAE document, and it is the only one the law has a view about.

The right-hand column matters more than the rest, because every claim here can be checked in a five-minute conversation. Ask for the awarding institution and the year rather than the acronym. Ask which Cambridge award it was and whether it was completed. Ask which component was marked, in which series, and whether the appointment is current, because a seasonal examiner appointment lapses and nobody announces it. Ask to see the MoHRE permit itself: it costs nothing to hold, which means it has no good reason to be missing. A tutor who cannot produce any of this detail has told you something useful.

Read the last row twice. Platform-internal certification means a tutoring company tested its own people against its own standard, which can be rigorous or decorative with no way to tell from the outside. The questions that settle it are what the test was, who marked it and what the pass mark was. Our own screening is described in sentences rather than badges: the board, the tier, the syllabus codes taught and the components the tutor has prepared candidates for. A specific sentence beats a seal, and it is also the only version a parent can check.

sections.heading: The permit UAE law requires, and the things it still does not tell you
paragraphs: Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring for payment without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Abu Dhabi adds a layer that catches families by surprise. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's school. That makes the most frequently offered arrangement in this country, your child's own subject teacher privately after hours, the one to decline. It is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so check the current ADEK wording before relying on the detail, but the direction is clear and it is not a grey area worth testing.

A company is a different legal animal from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit licenses the business and its premises. It is not a statement about any individual tutor's subject knowledge, and a company permit quoted at you as though it were a teaching credential is a category error. IB Gram holds no permit of that kind and makes no claim to one.

sections.heading: What this market charges, and the credential sitting behind each number
paragraphs: IGCSE tutor rates in the UAE run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour, and the spread is not noise. Each band buys a different thing. The figures below are the published rates of the providers named, read in October 2026, together with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are presented as the market, not as our prices: IB Gram quotes per family after a trial lesson, and three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, which is why a sourced table is worth more here than another paragraph about value.

The pattern worth noticing is that the credential premium and the format premium are separate charges. Moving from a university student to a qualified IGCSE subject teacher roughly doubles the hourly rate. Moving from online delivery to a tutor who travels adds AED 180 to 500 an hour in Bestimate's figures, and that increment buys travel time rather than teaching. Extended tier IGCSE tuition is charged at the same hourly rate as Core by most providers in this market; what changes is how many hours a candidate needs, which is the number families should be comparing.

Monthly packaging muddies comparison, deliberately. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Convert every package to an hourly figure before you compare anything, and ask whether marking between lessons is inside the price or outside it.

sections.heading: Two IGCSE years, priced by credential rather than by format
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead because nobody buys one hour. The arithmetic below takes the bands published above and multiplies them out across a realistic plan, so a family can see what a credential decision costs over Years 10 and 11 rather than over sixty minutes. A UAE school year gives roughly 36 teaching weeks, so one weekly hour across both IGCSE years is about 72 hours of teaching. Every total here is arithmetic on the market bands in the previous table, not a quotation from us, and the IGCSE tutor cost per hour inside each row is the published band rather than a figure we set.

What the table shows is that the credential premium is smaller than the duration decision. Two years of weekly lessons with a qualified subject teacher costs more than three times a focused exam-year block with a specialist, and more than five times a diagnostic block followed by targeted work. Families who start in Year 10 because they are worried, rather than because a diagnosis said to, routinely spend the most and gain the least. The money works hardest when a weakness has been named first and the hours are aimed at it.

The sensible order is therefore diagnosis, then dose. Buy six lessons from the best-credentialled tutor you can find, insist on a written diagnosis, and only then decide the length and the tier of what follows. If the diagnosis says the problem is reading speed in Biology extended-response questions, that is twelve focused hours, not two years of general support. If it says Mathematics 0580 algebra never consolidated in Year 9, that is a longer plan and worth paying a qualified teacher for. Both answers are cheaper than guessing.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor hired locally against live one-to-one online, for a UAE family
paragraphs: The honest comparison is not quality against quality. A good tutor sitting in your living room and the same good tutor on a screen teach almost identically, and anyone claiming a large general advantage either way is selling something. The real difference is who you get to choose from, and what happens when the arrangement is tested by traffic, travel, illness or a minority subject. That is what the table compares, and it is also why IB Gram teaches UAE families online rather than sending anyone to an address here.

Choice is the decisive column. A family hiring locally is choosing from tutors who will travel to that community at that hour, which in Dubai is a reasonable list, in Al Ain a short one and in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain close to empty. For Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606 or Accounting 0452 the local list is often empty everywhere. Online one-to-one IGCSE lessons widen the pool to every specialist free in that slot, which is the difference between the right tutor and the available one.

The practical columns matter more than families expect. A visiting arrangement collapses in the two weeks of the year it is needed most, because exam-season traffic, a tutor's own marking commitments and a single illness all land at once. A fixed online slot survives a trip to Al Ain, a family holiday in a different time zone, and a week when your child has a cast on their leg. Recordings of worked solutions, shared annotated papers and a written note after each lesson are also simply easier to produce on a screen than on a dining table.

sections.heading: Seven questions that test a certification claim before any money moves
paragraphs: Everything on this page reduces to a short conversation you can have before paying for a lesson. The questions below are ordered so that the cheapest ones to answer come first; a tutor or agency that stalls on the first three is unlikely to improve on the last four. None of them is hostile, and a well-credentialled tutor enjoys answering them, because they are the questions that distinguish them from the budget end of the market they are competing with on the same search page.

Notice what is not on the list. Do not ask whether the tutor is good, whether students improve, or whether they can get a grade 8. The answers carry no information and the last one should not be answered at all: no tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you about their sales process rather than their teaching. Ask instead for facts that can be wrong, because only a checkable claim is worth anything. A tutor who says they have taught 4PH1 Paper 1 for six series has said something you can test in ten minutes of conversation about that paper.

Get the answers in writing before the first paid hour. A short email or message thread naming the tutor, the board, the code, the tier, the rate per hour, what happens to a cancelled lesson and when you will next review the arrangement is enough. It is not a contract so much as a shared memory, and it prevents the most common dispute in this market, which is a family and a tutor holding different beliefs about what was agreed in a friendly first conversation.
bullets: Which board and which syllabus code is my child entered for, and have you taught that exact code?
Which qualification are you describing as certification, who issued it and in which year?
Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it?
How many candidates have you taken through a full series at Extended tier?
What will you have produced in writing by lesson six?
Is marking between lessons inside the hourly rate or charged separately?
What is your position on coursework, and what will you refuse to do with it?

sections.heading: Lesson twelve: the evidence that a credential is reaching your child
paragraphs: A certificate is a prediction. Twelve lessons in, you can replace it with evidence. The checkpoints below are deliberately observable from outside the lesson, because a parent cannot assess subject teaching directly and should not try. What a parent can see is whether the work is being diagnosed, whether marking is happening between lessons, and whether the language the tutor uses matches the language the mark scheme uses. Those three things correlate far better with grades than any badge in the first table.

The most informative checkpoint is the earliest. A qualified tutor spends the first lesson finding out where the marks are going, usually by having the student attempt something under timed conditions and then reading the working rather than the answers. A tutor who opens with a lecture on the first topic of the syllabus has skipped the diagnosis, which is the part that needed the qualification. That is a correctable fault in lesson two and a reason to change tutor by lesson four.

Act on the right-hand column promptly. Families tend to wait for a report or a mock result before changing a tutoring arrangement, which can waste a full term at AED 200 an hour. Twelve lessons is enough evidence, and the money already spent is not an argument for spending more. Where a change is needed we will say so, including when the honest answer is that the problem is not a teaching problem at all and more paid hours will not fix it.

sections.heading: What no certificate authorises: coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: No qualification, award or permit entitles a tutor to produce work that must be the student's own. This matters commercially in the UAE because the same search results that show tutoring services also show operators selling finished assessed work, in one researched case at AED 3,750 for a completed internal assessment. Buying that is not a shortcut; it is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller. A tutor's job is to teach, to review the student's own work and to give feedback on it.

The distinction is easier to hold than it sounds, and the table states it component by component. Teaching the technique a coursework task requires is legitimate. Explaining why a paragraph does not meet a published criterion is legitimate. Rewriting that paragraph is not. Drafting a plan the student then writes to is legitimate; supplying the sentences is not. A tutor who cannot articulate that line without hedging is a risk to your child's entry, and a tutor who volunteers it before you ask has told you something reassuring about how they work.

Practical science needs its own paragraph, because the alternative-to-practical paper is routinely confused with a lab skill. It tests reasoning about apparatus, method, variables and data rather than manual technique, and it is examinable without a laboratory. Where a school-assessed practical component exists, that assessment belongs to the school and the student and a tutor stays outside it entirely. We also do not reproduce or supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes: those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, are available from them, and we link rather than copy.
