sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: where a UAE authority does check the teacher
paragraphs: There is one part of a UAE school timetable where teacher approval genuinely is a regulated matter. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For these subjects, schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. That is a real, checkable credential rule, and it applies to school staff rather than to private tutors.

The organisational rules are specific enough to be worth knowing before you buy help. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two practical consequences follow. First, instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes, so the timetable pressure on an IGCSE option block is real and arithmetic rather than a matter of opinion. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which means support here stays squarely inside the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course.

sections.heading: The deadlines a certificate cannot move
paragraphs: Credentials do not change dates, and families who hire late often discover that the expensive part of the calendar has already closed. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Entries are made by the centre, not the family, and they close months before the papers. Pearson's November 2026 series is the clearest published example of the gap: the final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that fixed which papers each candidate sat was submitted long before the autumn term started. Cambridge works the same way — a June entry closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and a November entry a comparable distance ahead of its own window — and the exact day reaches a family through the centre on the statement of entry rather than from a date printed on a tutoring page.

The zone rule is the other thing a parent should know before paying anyone for a revision plan. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That makes the statement of entry, not a published generic timetable, the document any plan is built from. A tutor who has not asked to see it is planning in the abstract, whatever their qualification.

Results timing shapes what a retake decision costs. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge publishes a release day on Direct for each series it runs, August for the June sitting and January for November, with certificates following some weeks later. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and dates can be revised, always work from the live official timetable on the board's own site, and get the school's internal coursework deadlines in the same calendar.

process.title: Send the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Start with the statement of entry or the school's subject list rather than a description of the problem. Cambridge IGCSE 0620 Extended and Pearson 4CH1 are different jobs, and the code decides which specialists are even candidates. If you cannot find it, the school office can confirm it in a sentence and it is worth the email.

process.title: See the credential before the trial lesson
process.description: We name the tutor, the qualification held and its issuer, the boards taught and the components they have prepared candidates for. Where a tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit we say so; where they teach in from outside the UAE we say that instead, with who is accountable for the slot. No badge is used in place of those sentences.

process.title: Take the trial lesson, then decide
process.description: A trial lesson with the proposed specialist, free and with no card details taken to book it. Its job is not to impress anyone but to produce a diagnosis: the topic the marks are leaking from and what would be done about it. If that does not arrive, tell us and we will propose a different tutor rather than a different sales pitch.

process.title: Agree the rate, the cadence and the review point in writing
process.description: One short message naming the hourly rate, whether marking between lessons is inside it, the weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, the cancellation position and the date of the lesson-six review. Any figure quoted to you states whether VAT is included. This is the step that prevents almost every dispute in this market.

process.title: Review at lesson six, in writing
process.description: A written progress note against the original diagnosis: topics closed, topics still open and the hours each needs. Continue, change the tutor, or stop. We say plainly when more paid hours are unlikely to help, including when the issue is attendance, sleep or a subject choice rather than teaching, because that is the honest answer more often than this industry admits.

whyPoints.title: The credential is named, never implied
whyPoints.description: Each tutor profile states the qualification, who awarded it and when, the boards taught and the syllabus codes worked on. No seals, no unexplained badges, no borrowed regulator logos. If a claim cannot survive the question who issued it and in which year, it does not go on a profile in the first place.

whyPoints.title: No regulator badge we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. We explain what each of those bodies does because UAE families need to know, and we keep our own position separate from theirs. The most dangerous phrase available to pages like this one is the one we leave out.

whyPoints.title: AED figures are sourced or they are absent
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. Where arithmetic is used, the inputs are the published bands and the sum is shown. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no average score and no star rating, because none of those could be backed with a sample, a date and a method.

whyPoints.title: Your child's work stays your child's work
whyPoints.description: Coursework support is teaching, criterion-level feedback and review of the student's own draft. Nothing is written, rewritten or edited to completion, and nothing assessed is supplied. The operators in this market selling finished assessed work put the candidate at risk, not themselves, and declining that business is a position rather than a disclaimer.

whyPoints.title: Online because the specialist pool is larger than a drive radius
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to a UAE address and home visits are a service we run only in India. For Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606 or Accounting 0452 in the northern emirates, that is the difference between the right specialist and whoever happens to be nearby.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: Some subject and tier combinations have thin cover at a given hour, especially minority IGCSE options and early-evening slots during exam season. We say so before taking a booking, and we offer the slot that genuinely exists rather than the one you asked for. A waiting list stated plainly is worth more than a match made in a hurry.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge or Pearson issue a certificate to IGCSE tutors?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International awards qualifications to candidates and accredits exam centres, and Pearson does the same for its International GCSE. Neither issues a licence or certificate to a private tutor. Cambridge does offer professional development qualifications that individual teachers can complete, which is a genuine credential, but it is awarded to the teacher for completing a course rather than appointing them as an approved tutor. So a tutor may honestly say they hold a Cambridge professional award; nobody can honestly describe themselves as licensed by the board. Ask which award, which year, and whether it was completed.

faqs.question: What does certification actually add to an IGCSE tutor's hourly rate here?
faqs.answer: On published figures read in October 2026, moving from a student tutor to a qualified subject tutor roughly doubles the rate: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Unitors publishes IGCSE rates from AED 150. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and the premium tier reaches AED 650 at BartyED. The jump is real, but it tracks subject depth and board experience more closely than it tracks any particular certificate. A teaching qualification with no experience of your child's syllabus code earns the higher rate without earning the result.

faqs.question: Is the MoHRE private tuition permit a qualification or just permission?
faqs.answer: Permission. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and establishes that someone may lawfully charge for private lessons in the UAE. It tests nothing about subject knowledge, teaching skill or board experience. Its eligible categories include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, which tells you how wide it is. Treat it as the legal floor: a tutor without one is a problem, and a tutor with one has cleared the first step rather than the last. The qualification questions come after it, not instead of it.

faqs.question: How long does the private tutor permit take to get, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: MoHRE's service page for the permit, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, states a completion time of two working days and lists no fees, with applications through the MoHRE smart app, the website or the e-services system. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. That matters for a parent for one practical reason: because it costs nothing and takes two days, there is no good explanation for a tutor charging UAE families not having one. Anyone offering private lessons without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can I ask to see a tutor's certificate before paying for a lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should. Ask for the awarding institution and the year rather than the acronym, because a certificate number and an institution name can be checked while an acronym cannot. For a degree, check the named subject rather than the level. For a marking appointment, ask which component, which series, and whether it is current, since examiner appointments are seasonal. For the MoHRE permit, ask to see the permit. A tutor who treats these questions as an insult has answered them. One who answers in specifics has told you how they work.

faqs.question: Our school enters Pearson papers. Does a Cambridge-trained tutor still fit?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but it has to be checked rather than assumed. The two boards examine the same level of qualification with different papers, different tiering arrangements and a different balance between recall and application. A tutor who knows Cambridge 0580 inside out will know the mathematics for Pearson 4MA1 and may still teach the wrong paper technique. Ask directly how many series they have prepared candidates for on your board's code. The cost of getting this wrong is not knowledge; it is a candidate answering a question in the style the other board rewards.

faqs.question: Nobody near us teaches IGCSE Computer Science 0478. What happens then?
faqs.answer: That is the most common scarcity in this market, along with Additional Mathematics 0606 and Accounting 0452. Locally, in Al Ain or the northern emirates, the honest answer is often that no specialist is available at any price. Because teaching here is one-to-one over live video, the pool is every specialist free in that slot rather than everyone willing to drive to your community on a Tuesday. If nobody covers the subject and tier at the hour you want, we say so and offer the hours that genuinely exist instead of filling the slot with a generalist.

faqs.question: Is a university student with a grade 9 in the subject worth AED 60 an hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a specific job. A recent strong candidate is genuinely useful for supervised practice, working through exercises and keeping a Year 10 student honest about homework. What they usually cannot do is diagnose why marks are leaking, teach to a mark scheme they have never marked against, or sequence two years of syllabus. At AED 45 to 150 an hour that may still be the right purchase for the right task. It is the wrong purchase twelve weeks before a series, when technique rather than content is deciding the grade.

faqs.question: Does a tutor with marking experience justify the top of the market?
faqs.answer: For a narrow job, in a narrow window. Published premium rates in this market reach AED 650 an hour, and what that buys is familiarity with how a specific component's mark scheme is applied: why a technically correct answer scored nothing, which phrasing earns the mark, how examiners read a long response. That is worth real money in the final weeks before papers. It is poor value in Year 10, when the student needs content sequencing. Marking experience never includes access to live papers or grade boundaries, and any suggestion that it does should be treated with real scepticism.

faqs.question: My son's own subject teacher offered to tutor him privately. Is that allowed?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy text, so check the current ADEK wording, but it is not an arrangement worth testing. Beyond the rules, the conflict is obvious: the person teaching, setting and marking your son's work should not also be paid privately by your family.

faqs.question: Do we need a certified tutor for Arabic as an additional language?
faqs.answer: Be clear which Arabic you mean, because two different things share the name. Arabic as a Foreign Language at IGCSE, Cambridge 0544, is a board-examined qualification like any other option subject. The mandatory Arabic stream every Dubai private school must run is set under Ministry rules, and schools are required to ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval. For the mandatory stream, the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so support stays inside the school's own material.

faqs.question: After how many lessons should we expect to see something for the money?
faqs.answer: A named weakness after lesson one, marked homework by lesson two, a full timed paper marked by lesson eight and a written progress note against the first diagnosis by lesson twelve. Those are observable from outside the lesson, which is the point: a parent cannot assess subject teaching directly but can see whether diagnosis and marking are happening. If lesson twelve arrives with no written picture of what has closed and what is still open, change tutor rather than extend. Money already spent is not a reason to spend more.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my daughter's coursework before she submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skill the task requires, explain the published criteria, and give feedback on her own draft against them. What they may not do is write, rewrite or edit passages to completion, or supply sentences for her to use. The distinction is whose words reach the examiner. Any operator offering finished assessed work for a fee, and some in this market do, is putting your daughter's entry at risk rather than their own. If a tutor hedges when you ask where their line sits, that is the answer.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre with a KHDA permit a safer choice than an individual?
faqs.answer: It is a different thing, not automatically a safer one. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and completed within a maximum of six months, with renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That licenses the business and its premises. It says nothing about the subject knowledge of whoever is actually in the room with your child. Ask the same credential questions you would ask an individual, and ask who specifically will teach the lessons.

faqs.question: Is the rate quoted per hour or per lesson, and does it include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask both, in writing, before the first paid session, because this market mixes them. Published packaging in the UAE includes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits, which are not comparable until you convert them to an hourly figure. Ask separately whether marking between lessons is inside the price. Any figure quoted to your family states whether VAT is included; the VAT treatment of tuition fees generally is a Federal Tax Authority matter and not something this page states a view on.

faqs.question: Does anyone from IB Gram come to our address in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Teaching for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run and prayer times. Home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a supply decision rather than a cost-cutting one: a fixed online slot draws on every specialist free at that hour instead of the shorter list willing to travel to your community, and it survives traffic, travel and a week of illness. On published figures, a visiting arrangement in this market also costs AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the commute inside the rate.

certified-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Send us the board and the syllabus code from your child's statement of entry, the tier, and the hour that actually works in Gulf Standard Time. We will name the tutor, the qualification they hold and who awarded it, the components they have prepared candidates for, and the rate, before anything is paid. The trial lesson that follows is free, needs no card details, and exists to produce a diagnosis rather than a sales pitch. If nobody suitable is free at the hour you need, we will say so. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider that published it, read in October 2026, and none of them is a quotation from us.

dubai.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma and both IGCSE boards at the levels Dubai schools actually enter students for. Each one is listed with the subjects and levels they examine at, so you can check the match against your child's syllabus before you book a trial rather than after.

intro.heading: Start with the inspection report, not the tutor search
paragraphs: Dubai has the densest private-school market in the UAE, and it is also the most heavily documented one. KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, inspects every private school in the emirate and publishes the findings for anyone to read. Before you compare tutors, read the KHDA inspection report for your child's school. It names, phase by phase and subject by subject, where attainment sits against curriculum standards and where progress stalls against a cohort's own starting points. That single document usually tells you whether your child needs a subject specialist, an exam-technique coach, or nothing more than a quieter room and a timetable that someone enforces.

What the report cannot tell you is anything about your child. It judges a school. A school rated Very Good across six performance standards can still run a Diploma Chemistry class with no HL specialist in the room, because one department is not six standards. The report is also historical: by the time you read it, a year has passed, two teachers have moved on in June, and the Year 11 cohort it described has sat its exams. Read it for the pattern, not the verdict, and then test the pattern against your own child's last three pieces of marked work.

The families who contact us from Dubai arrive with specific problems, not general worry. A Year 11 mock grade that fell two steps between November and February. A DP1 report carrying a 4 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL when the university offer needs a 6. An Internal Assessment due in three weeks with no data collected. A June IGCSE grade that missed an A-level entry requirement by one mark, and a November retake that nobody has planned. Each of those is a different job, and each needs a different tutor.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. Tuition for families in Dubai is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor and student sharing a screen and working through the same past paper. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are something we run only in India. The trade is deliberate and it favours you: instead of choosing from the people who can reach Dubai Marina by 5pm, you choose from whoever teaches your child's exact syllabus and is free in the slot that fits the school run.

The rest of this page is the detail nobody publishes. What the six KHDA bands mean in plain words. What IB Diploma tuition in Dubai actually costs across the market, in AED, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. The exam year counted backwards from the May session. Assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations, so you know what an IA mark is made of. The line a tutor may not cross on coursework. MoE equivalency and attestation. Arabic, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural Studies running alongside the IB. And what Ramadan does to a revision plan.
bullets: KHDA publishes an annual inspection report for every private school in Dubai, free to read
Attainment and progress are judged separately, and a strong school can be weak in one subject
The Internal Assessment is worth 20% of most IB subject grades, and it is marked at school
Dubai candidates can sit the IB in May or November, and IGCSE in January, June or November

dubai.programmesIntro: Dubai runs more curriculum combinations than any other emirate, and the switches between them are where most tuition requests begin. These are the four programme families we are asked for, with what each one assesses and how Dubai schools actually sequence them.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, scored 1 to 7 for a maximum of 42, plus up to three core points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. The diploma is awarded at 24 points with conditions attached: no grade 1, a minimum of 12 points across HL subjects, CAS completed, and no academic misconduct finding. An E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition on its own, whatever the point total says.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB schools run the Diploma mostly on the northern-hemisphere calendar, so the May session is the live one and November is for retakes and a small number of candidates. The hardest month in a Dubai DP1 year is usually February, when the exploration deadline, the Extended Essay first draft and the TOK exhibition commentary land inside a few weeks of each other. Most families who ask for IB Diploma tuition in Dubai are asking for that window, not for the whole two years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and reported on a 1 to 7 scale after a conversion the school controls. There are no external papers until the optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. Marks come from criterion-referenced tasks, so a student can hold a steady 6 and still have no experience of a timed two-hour paper under exam conditions.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the single most common reason Dubai parents look for a tutor. A student who has been assessed on criteria for five years meets Paper 1 in DP1 and discovers that command terms, timing and a non-calculator section are skills nobody taught separately. Schools running the full continuum in Dubai, including GEMS Modern Academy and Uptown International School, handle this internally; students arriving from a British-curriculum school mid-MYP usually do not get that bridge.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined externally and graded 9 to 1, with tiering in several subjects: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Mathematics splits into Core and Extended, and the sciences split the same way. From the 2025 syllabus, Extended Mathematics is assessed by a non-calculator Paper 2 and a calculator Paper 4, each worth half the grade. Edexcel International GCSE uses 4MA1 for Mathematics and offers a January series Cambridge does not.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai by enrolment, which means most Dubai students meet IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma. The decision is made in Year 11, usually on a mock grade, and it is the point at which an IGCSE tutor in Dubai is worth most: a 7 in Extended Mathematics opens Maths AA HL, while a 5 effectively closes it. Ask the school's exams officer which board each subject is entered for, because one school commonly uses both.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, finishing in the Year 6 exhibition. Reporting is narrative and against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages, so a parent reading a PYP report often cannot tell where a child sits in maths against an age expectation. Benchmark testing fills that gap, which is why schools run standardised assessments alongside the programme.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA asks Dubai schools to run international benchmark assessments as part of the National Agenda Parameter, so a PYP child in Dubai typically has CAT4 or similar data sitting behind the narrative report. Ask for it. It is the only place a Dubai primary parent can see a percentile rather than a paragraph, and it is far more useful than a tutor's opinion about whether your eight-year-old is behind.

dubai.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects Dubai families request most, with what each one is actually assessed on. The weightings matter more than the syllabus titles, because a student losing marks on a data-based paper needs a different six weeks from one losing them on the exploration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: HL is assessed by Paper 1 without technology at 30%, Paper 2 with technology at 30%, Paper 3 at 20% and the exploration at 20%. SL drops Paper 3 and weights the two papers at 40% each. HL marks go missing in the Paper 3 extended response, where a long unfamiliar problem has to be carried through several linked parts under time pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is required throughout, which misleads students into thinking the course is lighter. HL carries the same paper structure as AA, including Paper 3 at 20%. The losses here are in statistics and modelling: choosing the wrong test, reading a regression output without commenting on its limits, or writing a conclusion the data does not support.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Assessed by a multiple-choice and data-based Paper 1, an extended-response Paper 2, and the Scientific Investigation worth 20%. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Dubai students most often stall, and the investigation loses marks on criterion A long before it loses any on chemistry, because the research question was never narrow enough to answer.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Most lost marks are not physics at all: they are unstated assumptions, missing units, and uncertainty treatment in the practical work. HL adds depth in fields and quantum effects, and the step from MYP science to HL Physics is the steepest in the Diploma for students who have never derived a result algebraically before DP1.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on command terms. The difference between outline, explain and evaluate is worth several grade boundaries across a paper, and students who revise content without practising command terms plateau at a 5. The Scientific Investigation rewards a clean research design more than an ambitious topic, which is the opposite of what most students assume.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks that content knowledge cannot rescue. HL adds quantitative questions and the policy paper. The three commentaries in the portfolio are where students lose ground, usually by summarising a news article instead of applying one key concept to it with a labelled diagram and an evaluation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study for Paper 1 rewards preparation more than any other IB paper, and most students underprepare it. Tools have to be applied to the case rather than described. HL students also submit a research project on a real organisation, where the common failure is a question that cannot be answered with the data a student can actually obtain.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, and the Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts. Dubai cohorts are often strong on content and weak on the guiding-question framing of the oral, which is where a recorded practice run with feedback does more than another read of the novel.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a working solution with documentation, and the documentation is what is marked. Students who can code lose marks on success criteria agreed with a client and on the record of testing. HL adds abstract data structures and a case study released annually, which needs reading long before the final term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: TOK is a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title, worth two-thirds of the grade, plus an exhibition of three objects with a 950-word commentary. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words assessed on five criteria. Together they contribute up to three diploma points, and an E in either is a failing condition regardless of subject scores.

dubai.igcseSubjectsIntro: Most Dubai IB students sat IGCSE first, and most Dubai students who never take the Diploma are entered for one of these. Syllabus codes matter here: Cambridge and Edexcel examine the same subject with different papers, different tiering and different series.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580 · Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge Extended now runs a non-calculator Paper 2 and a calculator Paper 4, each worth half. Students who learned the course on a calculator lose a full paper's worth of fluency. Edexcel 4MA1 Higher tier is a single tier with two equally weighted calculator papers, which changes how you revise.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge Extended is Paper 2 multiple choice at 30%, Paper 4 theory at 50%, and either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper at 20%. Electricity and circuits generate more lost marks than any other topic, usually from reading a circuit diagram rather than from the physics itself.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Same 30-50-20 split as Physics on the Cambridge route. Qualitative analysis and the mole concept are the reliable failure points, and the alternative-to-practical paper is a distinct skill: students are marked on reading someone else's method and spotting what is wrong with it.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Large content load, small command-term vocabulary. Marks are lost on describing a graph when the question asked for an explanation, and on vague answers about transport in plants. The extended-response questions reward structure far more than extra detail.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 · Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the reading passages carry most of the risk. Students raised on MYP criteria write at length without selecting evidence, which costs reading marks on a question that wanted four precise references. Timing practice on the full paper is worth more than another vocabulary list.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 · 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both papers reward applying a diagram or a tool to the scenario in front of the student. The four-mark and six-mark bands have distinct expectations, and most students answer every question as though it were worth two. Case-study discipline is learnable in a handful of sessions.

dubai.regionsTitle: What tuition looks like in each part of Dubai
dubai.regionsIntro: Dubai is a long city with a school run at both ends of it. The practical difference between areas is not which tutors live nearby, since lessons are online, but when a session can realistically start and which school cluster the family sits inside.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Tower families, almost all of them on a school bus to Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. A 4pm start rarely survives the bus; 5:30pm onwards is the slot that holds. Apartment study space is tight, so a headset and a shared screen beat a kitchen table with a sibling at it.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: An IGCSE-heavy cluster feeding Jumeirah College, Kings' School Dubai and Dubai College, where the Year 11 decision is A Level against IB Diploma rather than which university. Requests here peak in January, straight after mock results, and concentrate on Extended Mathematics and the sciences.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the emirate, with several continuum schools inside a few kilometres. Demand concentrates on HL Chemistry, HL Economics and Maths AA HL, which are exactly the subjects where a locally available tutor is least likely to be a specialist in the right level.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Villa communities with single-carriageway exits, which is why home tuition in Dubai costs more out here than the hourly rate suggests. JESS Arabian Ranches runs the Diploma, so DP1 and DP2 coursework support is the standing request, often for two siblings in the same evening.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Continuum territory, with students who have been inside one IB school since PYP. The gap that shows up is external-exam technique rather than content, because a cohort assessed on criteria for a decade meets its first timed public paper in DP2.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: The eastern side of the city, where a tutor based on the Marina side would lose an hour each way. Deira International School and Uptown International School anchor the cluster, and the Diploma and IGCSE requests arrive in roughly equal numbers.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer Diploma provision, including Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, with families who often moved mid-programme. Transfer cases dominate: a student who did two terms of a different syllabus and needs the delta mapped rather than the course retaught.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Younger families and a mostly primary and MYP intake, with Arcadia School and several newer schools. Local specialist supply is genuinely thin at HL level, which is the clearest case on this page for online one-to-one tuition in Dubai rather than a local search.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Dubai Media City
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's main concentration of IB World Schools, several running the full continuum from PYP to the Diploma. Students arriving from this cluster usually need HL depth and coursework structure rather than remedial content work, and their deadlines are set by school calendars that are published a year ahead.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Dubai Marina
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum weight, with IGCSE at 16 and a split into A Level or the Diploma afterwards. Requests from here are seasonal and sharp: Extended Mathematics and science papers between January and May, then A Level and DP1 bridging work over the summer.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan, Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
schoolClusters.note: A mix of continuum IB schools and large British-curriculum schools on the eastern and central side of the city. This is where the November IB session and the November IGCSE series come up most often, because retake planning here starts in July rather than September.

Most Dubai families start with one subject at one hour a week and add a second only if the first is working. Sessions are usually booked from 5pm once the school bus has arrived, with Friday and weekend mornings available for longer coursework work.

sections.heading: What KHDA's six bands actually say about your child's school
paragraphs: KHDA inspects Dubai's private schools annually and reports against six performance standards: students' achievement, their personal and social development, teaching and assessment, the curriculum, the care and support the school provides, and leadership and management. Each is graded on a six-point scale running Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak. Good is the standard Dubai expects a private school to reach, which means Acceptable is not a middling result; it is the floor.

The part parents skim is the part that matters for tuition. Inside students' achievement, the report grades attainment and progress separately, by phase and by subject. Attainment is measured against curriculum standards. Progress is measured against where that group of students started. A subject can be Good for attainment and Acceptable for progress, which describes a bright cohort being carried rather than taught, and that is a very different problem from a weak cohort improving quickly.

Use the report as a map of the building, not a verdict on your child. If Mathematics in Phase 4 is graded lower than English in the same phase, the class your child sits in is more likely to be the constraint than your child is, and a weekly specialist hour will show a return quickly. If every subject in the phase is Very Good, the honest answer is often that nothing is wrong at school and the gap is homework discipline, sleep, or a single topic from two years ago that never got fixed.

One more practical note: inspection grades drive what a school may charge. KHDA links permitted fee increases to inspection outcomes, so a report is a commercial document as well as an educational one. That is worth knowing when a school presents an improved rating to parents, and it is another reason to read the subject-level judgements rather than the headline band.

sections.heading: Attainment, progress and the gap a school report card hides
paragraphs: A Dubai school report usually carries a working-at grade, a target grade and an effort score. None of those three is an exam grade. The working-at grade is assembled from classwork, criterion-referenced tasks and internal assessments, and in the MYP it comes from a conversion scale the school itself sets. The target is generated from benchmark data. Neither is a prediction of what will happen to a student in a two-hour paper with a strict mark scheme and a clock.

This is the gap that produces most of our Dubai enquiries, and it has a recognisable shape. A student holds a 6 in MYP 5 Mathematics, moves into Analysis and Approaches HL, and scores a 4 in the first DP1 assessment. Nothing has gone wrong with the student. The assessment changed from criterion-referenced tasks over several days to a timed non-calculator paper where method marks depend on written working. Those are different skills, and only one of them had been taught.

KHDA requires Dubai schools to run international benchmark assessments as part of the National Agenda Parameter, so the data to close this gap usually exists already. Ask the school for your child's benchmark results alongside the report, and ask the subject teacher one question: what did my child lose marks on in the last timed assessment, by topic. A teacher who can answer that in specifics has diagnosed the problem for you, and a tutor's first session should start from that answer rather than from the beginning of the syllabus.

If the school cannot produce the detail, the marked script will. Send us the last paper your child sat with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it. An hour spent sorting those lost marks into content gaps, command-term misreadings and timing losses is worth more than a term of general revision, because the three categories need three different interventions and most students only have one of the three problems.
bullets: A working-at grade is not a predicted exam grade, and in the MYP the conversion is school-set

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tuition costs in Dubai, and who charges what
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. So here is the market in AED, with every figure attributed to whoever published it. These are market rates collected from competitor pages and from published Dubai rate tables. They are not our price list; IB Gram matches tutors and the rate depends on the subject, the level and the tutor, which is what the free trial and the consultation are for.

Read the table as a map of what you are buying rather than a ranking. The bottom band is usually a university student working from a textbook, which is adequate for Year 9 homework support and inadequate for Paper 3. The middle band buys a qualified subject teacher. The top bands buy someone who has marked the paper your child will sit, and for a DP2 student with a conditional university offer in May, that difference is the entire point of hiring anyone.

Monthly packages are common in Dubai and they make comparison harder, deliberately. Figures published across the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits to the home. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Divide any package by the number of contact hours before you compare it with an hourly rate.

Two costs sit outside the hourly figure and catch families out. The first is travel: a rate quoted for a visit to a villa community has the drive priced into it, and it is charged whether the traffic cooperates or not. The second is VAT. A tutor or agency only has to register for VAT once taxable turnover passes AED 375,000 a year, so some quotes include it and some are from people who are not registered at all. Ask which, in writing, before the first invoice.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the room: the Dubai arithmetic
paragraphs: Parents searching for home tuition in Dubai are asking a fair question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. A tutor who sits in the room with a nervous twelve-year-old has something real that a screen does not. For a young child, for a student with significant additional needs, or for a family where supervision is the actual problem, a person in the house can be the right answer and we will say so.

Above about Year 9, the arithmetic changes, and it changes because of geography rather than pedagogy. Dubai is roughly fifty kilometres end to end on one spine road. A tutor who can reach Arabian Ranches by 5pm and be home by 8pm can take two students a night, so the rate carries the dead time. More importantly, the pool you are choosing from shrinks to the people who can make that drive, which is why a family in Dubai Sports City looking for a Chemistry HL specialist is often offered a general science tutor instead.

Online one-to-one tuition in Dubai inverts that. The pool is everyone teaching your child's syllabus who is free in your slot, so an IB Maths AA tutor in Dubai can be matched on HL Paper 3 experience rather than on postcode. The session starts at the minute booked. A past paper sits on a shared screen with annotations both people can see, and the file is still there next week. If a school fixture moves, the lesson moves the same evening, because a slot is a calendar entry rather than a journey.

To be plain about what we sell: IB Gram delivers tuition to Dubai families as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not place tutors in UAE homes, and the home-visit service we run in India is not available here. If a visiting tutor is genuinely what your child needs, the market rates in the previous table tell you what to budget, and a tuition centre holding a current KHDA licence is the other place to look.

sections.heading: The exam year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: No competitor page for this market names a single exam session, registration deadline or results date. That is a strange omission, because the whole shape of a tuition plan comes from counting backwards from one fixed date. Dubai IB candidates sit the May session on the northern-hemisphere calendar, with the IB's candidate registration deadline for May falling in mid-November of the preceding year and results released in early July. The November session exists for retakes and for the small number of candidates on the other calendar.

IGCSE gives Dubai schools more routes. Cambridge runs a June series with entries closing with the centre in late February and results in mid-August, and a November series with results in mid-January. Edexcel International GCSE adds a January series, which is the reason a Year 11 student who missed a grade in June can hold a better certificate before A Level or Diploma applications close. Your school's internal entry deadline is always weeks earlier than the board's, and the exams officer is the only person who can tell you what it is.

The dates below are the published pattern and they move by a few days each year, so treat them as the shape of the year rather than a calendar to diary. What matters is the backwards count. A May candidate's exploration should be finished before mock season, because February in a Dubai DP1 or DP2 year carries mocks, the Extended Essay draft and the TOK commentary at once, and in the years immediately ahead Ramadan lands in the middle of that same stretch. Work that slips past February does not get done; it gets handed in unfinished.

The same logic applies to a retake. A June IGCSE grade released in mid-August leaves roughly ten weeks to the November series, which is enough for a one-subject repair and not enough to relearn two sciences. Decide in the week results arrive, not in October.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go: criteria, limits and weightings
paragraphs: Not one competitor page in this market names a single assessment criterion or its mark allocation. That is where the most useful conversation with a student starts, because a mark out of 20 that a student cannot break down is a mark they cannot improve. The IB publishes the criteria, the letters and the marks attached to each. A student who knows that personal engagement is worth three marks and use of mathematics is worth six will spend their last week on the right half of the document.

Take the Mathematics exploration, which is 20% of the grade in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at HL and SL alike. It carries five criteria: presentation worth four, mathematical communication worth four, personal engagement worth three, reflection worth three, and use of mathematics worth six, for twenty marks in total. Most Dubai students we see lose the bulk of their marks on reflection and personal engagement, not on the mathematics, because nobody told them those words have defined meanings in a rubric.

The sciences changed shape with the current guide: a single Scientific Investigation, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each for twenty-four, inside a three-thousand-word limit. The failure mode is almost always criterion A. A research question that cannot be answered with equipment a school in Dubai actually has produces thin data, and thin data caps the other three criteria no matter how well the student writes.

The core components have hard limits that are worth taping to a desk: four thousand words for the Extended Essay, one thousand six hundred for the TOK essay, nine hundred and fifty for the exhibition commentary across three objects. Examiners stop reading at the limit. A student who writes five thousand words has not written more essay; they have written four thousand words of essay and a thousand words nobody will ever read.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that needs saying out loud. One site competing for these searches openly sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum in AED. That is not tutoring. It is academic misconduct under IB regulations, it puts a diploma at risk rather than a grade, and the student carries the consequence while the seller keeps the money. We will not do it, and no reputable tutor in Dubai will either.

The rules themselves are not vague. A student's coursework must be their own work, the supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and the student declares the same. Help is permitted and expected: that is what a supervisor is for. What is not permitted is another person producing text, data, code or structure that then appears in the submitted work. The test a tutor should apply before every intervention is simple. Could the student have arrived at this themselves after the explanation, or did I hand it to them finished?

In practice this makes coursework sessions more useful rather than less. Reading a student's own draft against criterion C and explaining what critical thinking means in the rubric teaches something transferable. Supplying a paragraph teaches nothing and risks everything. The table below is the boundary we work to, and it is worth reading before you brief any tutor in Dubai, ours or anyone else's, because a tutor who offers to write it for you has told you what they are.

One practical consequence for families: keep the drafts. A student who can show the progression of their own work has an answer if authenticity is ever questioned, and version history in a document is the cheapest insurance available in a Diploma year.

table.caption: THE COURSEWORK BOUNDARY, TASK BY TASK

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and attestation for Dubai's IB and IGCSE leavers
paragraphs: A qualification earned in Dubai is not automatically usable in Dubai. For a UAE university place, a government job or a professional licence, a student generally needs a certificate equivalency from the Ministry of Education, and the documents behind it have to be attested. Not one competitor page in this market mentions equivalency at all, which is a remarkable omission given that it is the administrative step most likely to delay a Dubai school leaver by a month at exactly the wrong time.

The requirements are published by the Ministry and they differ by curriculum, so check the current list on the Ministry's own smart services rather than relying on a tutoring site, including this one. The pattern is stable even when the detail moves. The British route is assessed on a minimum number of IGCSE or GCSE passes at specified grades together with AS and A Level results, with subject requirements attached. The IB route is assessed on the full Diploma rather than individual subject certificates, which is one more reason an E in TOK or the Extended Essay matters beyond the point total.

The work that takes time is not the application; it is collecting the paperwork in the right order while the school's registrar is still at their desk. Transcripts, transfer certificates and school stamps are far easier to obtain in May than in late July, and a name spelled differently on a passport and a certificate is a correction that takes weeks. Families who moved to Dubai mid-school should also chase the leaving certificate from the previous school at the point of leaving, not years later from another country.

The table below is the document trail in the order it is usually needed. Treat the timing column as the whole point: everything in it is about doing paperwork in the term before you need it rather than in the week you do.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Ministry-mandated subjects next to its international curriculum, and almost no tutoring site mentions them. Arabic is compulsory, taught as a first language to Arabic-speaking students and as an additional language to everyone else, with the requirement continuing further up the school for Arabic speakers. Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students. Moral, Social and Cultural Studies, the framework that brought moral education and social studies together, runs for all students.

These subjects produce two distinct problems for IB and IGCSE families, and they need different answers. The first is a Diploma student with six subjects, the core, and two Ministry subjects timetabled on top, where the real constraint is hours in a week rather than ability in any one course. The second is a student who arrived in Dubai in Year 8 with no Arabic, placed in a class where most peers have had five years of it, and asked to be assessed alongside them.

Neither is solved by adding another tutored subject on top of a full timetable. The first is a scheduling problem: look at where the Ministry subjects sit in the week and protect the two evenings that are left for coursework rather than filling them. The second responds to short, frequent sessions on script, high-frequency vocabulary and reading fluency, which is a different teaching model from an hour a week on a Diploma subject.

Worth knowing for planning: these subjects appear on a Dubai school report and in inspection judgements, and Arabic attainment is reported separately for first-language and additional-language students in the KHDA inspection report. If a report shows Arabic as the weakest subject in a phase, that is a known pattern across the emirate rather than a verdict on your child, and it is usually a question of teaching time rather than aptitude.
bullets: Arabic is compulsory in Dubai private schools, as a first or additional language
Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students; Moral, Social and Cultural Studies is for all

sections.heading: Ramadan, the school calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: A revision plan written without the UAE calendar in it will not survive contact with the year. Dubai private schools follow a unified academic calendar: a start in late August, a winter break around a fortnight in December, a spring break of similar length, and an end to the year in the first days of July. Those breaks are where intensive work actually fits, and they are also when families travel, so the useful conversation is which half of the break is being kept at home.

Ramadan matters more than any of it for an exam-year student. School days shorten during the holy month, timings move, energy patterns change completely, and the month shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar. Ramadan is currently expected to begin in mid-February, subject each year to the moon sighting, which drops it directly onto the mock-examination and coursework-deadline window for anyone sitting the May IB exam session.

The practical answer is to move work rather than lose it. Coursework drafts should be finished before the month starts, because a student fasting through a school day will not produce their best four thousand words in it. Sessions during Ramadan work better after Iftar or early in the morning than at the usual 5pm slot, and because our lessons are online, moving a Dubai student's weekly hour to a post-Iftar time costs nothing more than finding a tutor whose own evening suits it. We schedule around it as a matter of course and ask families in January, not in week one of the month.

After Eid comes the compressed run to the papers. For a May candidate that is roughly six weeks, which is enough to fix technique and sharpen two or three topics and is not enough to learn a syllabus. Plan on that basis in October, and the February crunch is a busy month rather than a crisis.

process.title: Send the report, and the KHDA grade for the school
process.description: Start by sending your child's last school report, the marked script if you have one, and the subject-level judgements from the KHDA inspection report for the school. Those three documents tell us whether the problem is the class, the technique or a specific topic, which decides what kind of tutor you actually need.

process.title: A short diagnostic on the real paper
process.description: Before any plan, a tutor spends part of a first session on a question from the actual paper your child will sit, at the actual level. What they get wrong, and more usefully how they get it wrong, sorts the losses into content, command terms and timing. That sorting is the plan.

process.title: Matched by syllabus code and exam board
process.description: We match on the specifics: Analysis and Approaches HL rather than maths, Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended rather than IGCSE, Scientific Investigation rather than coursework. Because lessons are online, the match is made on who teaches that syllabus and is free in your slot, not on who can drive to your area by five.

process.title: A free trial, then a fixed weekly slot
process.description: The first session is a free trial so your child can decide whether this particular tutor is someone they will talk to. If the answer is no, say so and we match again; a student who will not ask a question has not got a tutor. After that, a fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Reviewed against the school's own calendar
process.description: Progress is checked against the next thing the school will actually assess, not against a generic timeline. When no specialist is free for a niche HL subject, we say so and give you an honest wait rather than offering a general tutor in the right-sounding subject.

whyPoints.title: The inspection report comes first
whyPoints.description: Most tuition decisions in Dubai are made from a worry rather than a document. We start from the KHDA inspection report and your child's marked work, because that is how you find out whether you are buying a specialist, an exam-technique coach, or nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are published by other people and attributed to them, so you can verify every line. Nobody else competing for these searches publishes a rate table in dirhams at all, and three of the main pages publish no price in any currency.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, levels and boards, named
whyPoints.description: A match on 0580 Extended with a non-calculator Paper 2 is a different job from a match on 4MA1 Higher, and Analysis and Approaches HL is not Applications and Interpretation SL. Every match is made on the code and level your child is entered for, and we tell you which tutor examines what.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line in writing
whyPoints.description: Our tutors mark a student's own draft against the published criteria and explain what the next band needs. They do not write, edit or supply work for submission. The boundary is on this page so you can hold us to it, and so you can ask the same question of anyone else you consider.

whyPoints.title: One timezone, no commute
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so a session begins at the minute it was booked and moves the same evening when a school fixture gets in the way. No part of your fee pays for Sheikh Zayed Road at six o'clock.

faqs.question: What is KHDA and how does it rate private schools in Dubai?
faqs.answer: KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the regulator for private education in Dubai. It inspects every private school in the emirate each year and publishes the report. Schools are judged against six performance standards, including students' achievement, teaching and assessment, and leadership, each graded on a six-point scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Good is the standard Dubai expects, so Acceptable is the floor rather than a middling result. Inside students' achievement, the report grades attainment and progress separately for each phase and subject, which is the level of detail worth reading before you hire anyone.

faqs.question: My child's school is rated Very Good, so does tuition make any sense?
faqs.answer: Often yes, for a reason the headline band hides. A school rated Very Good overall can be graded lower in one subject in one phase, because a band summarises six standards across the whole school and your child sits in one class. Read the subject-level judgements for your child's phase rather than the headline, and compare them. If Mathematics is graded below English in the same phase, the class is more likely to be the constraint than your child is. If every subject is strong, the honest answer is usually that the gap is homework discipline or one unfixed topic, not teaching.

faqs.question: What is the difference between attainment and progress in a Dubai inspection report?
faqs.answer: Attainment measures how students perform against the standards of the curriculum they follow. Progress measures how far they have moved from their own starting points. The combination is what tells you something. Good attainment with weaker progress describes a capable cohort being carried rather than stretched, which is the pattern that quietly costs a bright student a 7. Weaker attainment with strong progress describes a group climbing fast, where patience often beats intervention. Read both grades for your child's subject and phase, then test the pattern against the last piece of marked work that came home.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, as published by other providers, run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online or university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a tutor travelling to a home with the drive priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist. Named or examiner-level tutors are published as high as AED 650. Those are market figures attributed to the providers who published them, not our price list; our own rate depends on subject, level and tutor, and starts with a free trial.

faqs.question: Is online tuition actually cheaper than hiring a home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the saving is structural rather than a discount. A rate for a tutor travelling to a Dubai address has the drive built into it, which is why published home-visit rates sit around AED 180 to 500 while online specialist rates sit around AED 150 to 300. You also stop paying for time nobody teaches in. The bigger difference is not price: a visiting tutor has to come from whoever can reach your area, while an online match comes from whoever teaches your child's exact syllabus. For HL subjects in Dubai, that is the difference that moves a grade.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every regulatory source we checked states that the permit itself carries no fee. Residents who are employed elsewhere generally need their employer's consent as part of the application, and tutoring at a scale that becomes a business needs a proper licence instead. Ask any tutor you are considering whether they hold a current permit. A tutor who cannot answer that question clearly has told you something about how they operate, whatever their subject knowledge looks like.

faqs.question: Should a quoted hourly rate in Dubai include VAT, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, before the first invoice. UAE VAT registration becomes mandatory once taxable turnover passes AED 375,000 a year, so some tutors and agencies are registered and charge it, and others are below the threshold and do not. That means two quotes of the same number can mean two different final costs. Request a written statement of whether the rate is inclusive or exclusive, and ask for a tax invoice if the provider is registered. The same question applies to monthly packages, where the number of contact hours is often the detail that is quietly left out.

faqs.question: When are the IB and IGCSE exam sessions that Dubai students actually sit?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB candidates sit the May session, with the IB's candidate registration deadline falling in mid-November beforehand and results released in early July. A November session exists and is used mainly for retakes. Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series, with centre entries closing in late February and results in mid-August, and a November series with results in mid-January. Edexcel International GCSE adds a January series, with results in early March. Your school sets its own internal entry deadline weeks before the board's, so the exams officer is the person to ask for the dates that actually bind you.

faqs.question: Where is the line for a Dubai tutor helping with my child's Internal Assessment under IB academic-honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, pressure-test whether a research question can be answered with reachable data, mark a student's own draft against the published criteria, and say what the next band needs. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit text that appears in the submitted work, supply a dataset or a bibliography, or hand over a topic as a finished package. Coursework carries an authenticity declaration signed by both student and supervisor. Keep the drafts: version history is the simplest evidence that the work progressed from your child's own hands.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB Mathematics exploration worth, and where are they lost?
faqs.answer: The exploration is 20% of the grade in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at HL and SL, and it is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. Students who lose marks rarely lose them on mathematics. They lose them on reflection and personal engagement, because those phrases have defined meanings in the rubric that nobody explained, and on communication, where notation drifts between sections. Reading the criteria with a tutor before writing is worth more than editing afterwards.

faqs.question: What is MoE equivalency and when should a Dubai family start it?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education's recognition of a foreign qualification for use in the UAE, needed for most local university places, government roles and professional licences. The requirements differ by curriculum and are published on the Ministry's smart services, so check them there rather than on any tutoring site. The British route is assessed on IGCSE or GCSE passes together with AS and A Level results; the IB route is assessed on the full Diploma rather than individual certificates. Start collecting transcripts and stamps in the term before you need them, while the school registrar is still available.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies still apply if my child does the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in Dubai teach Ministry-mandated subjects alongside their international curriculum, whatever the programme. Arabic is compulsory, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for everyone else, and Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students. Moral, Social and Cultural Studies runs for all students. For a Diploma candidate this is usually a timetable problem rather than an academic one: six subjects plus the core plus Ministry subjects leaves fewer free evenings than families assume, so protect the ones that remain for coursework rather than booking them.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we plan for it rather than reacting to it. School days shorten during Ramadan and the usual late-afternoon slot stops working, so we move sessions to after Iftar or to early morning. Because lessons are delivered online, moving a Dubai student's weekly hour needs only a tutor whose own evening suits the new time, with no travel to rearrange. The more important piece is sequencing: Ramadan now opens in mid-February, give or take the moon sighting, which drops it onto mock season, so coursework drafts should be finished before the month starts.

faqs.question: Which maths route should my child take, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree, and the decision is made in Year 11 rather than in DP1. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-heavy route and is what engineering, mathematics, physics and most economics programmes expect at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with technology throughout, and suits business, design, social sciences and life sciences. Check the entry requirements of specific universities your child is likely to apply to, including UAE institutions, before choosing. A strong IGCSE Extended grade keeps the Analysis and Approaches HL option open; a mid grade effectively closes it.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's subject and level?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give you a realistic wait. Niche combinations genuinely run short at peak times, with HL Chemistry, HL Economics and Paper 3 work the usual pressure points in Dubai between January and April. The dishonest move would be to offer a general science tutor for HL Chemistry and hope you do not notice until the third session. Instead you get the actual position, an estimate of when a specialist frees up, and, when it helps, a shorter diagnostic session with someone who can at least sort the lost marks into categories while you wait.

faqs.question: How do online lessons work if the tutor is not in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Lessons run over live video, one to one, with a shared screen and a digital whiteboard. Timing is set in Gulf Standard Time, so a 6pm Dubai slot is a 6pm Dubai slot regardless of where the tutor sits, and most sessions are booked from 5pm once the school bus has arrived. Work happens on the real paper: a past paper opens on screen, both people annotate it, and the file is still there the following week. Written notes follow each session saying what was covered and what comes next, which is also what makes a handover possible if a tutor ever changes.

dubai.closingHeading: Read the report, then decide what you are buying
dubai.closingBody: The useful order for a Dubai family is almost always the same. Read the KHDA inspection report for your child's school and find the subject-level judgements for their phase. Ask the subject teacher which topics lost marks in the last timed assessment. Then decide whether you need a specialist for an HL paper, a technique coach for exam conditions, or a plan rather than a tutor. If one of the first two is the answer, send us the marked script and the report and we will match on the syllabus code and level your child is actually entered for, with a free trial lesson first, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/1-to-1-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below take one student at a time, with the subject, level and papers they teach to named on each profile. You approve the proposed match and the session length before anything is scheduled, and the first session with that tutor is the free one.

intro.heading: What a ratio of one is actually worth
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in Dubai describes its sessions as personalised and most of them mean something different by it. A class of eight is personalised in the sense that the teacher knows the students' names. A pair session is personalised in the sense that the pace is closer to each student. A ratio of one is personalised in the only sense that changes what can be diagnosed: the entire hour is spent on one student's own work, in their own order, at the pace their understanding sets. The difference is measurable in minutes and it is worth measuring before paying for it.

The arithmetic is unglamorous and it decides most of the value. A sixty-minute session with eight students contains, at best, around seven minutes of direct attention per student once explanation to the room is counted as shared rather than individual. With four students it is closer to fifteen. With two it is roughly twenty-five, because some explanation genuinely serves both. With one it is sixty, every minute of which can be spent on the specific question this student got wrong for a reason nobody has yet identified.

That is why the per-hour comparison misleads. A group seat in Al Quoz at a fraction of an individual rate looks dramatically cheaper and sometimes genuinely is. Measured per minute of direct attention, the gap narrows sharply and in some cases reverses. The honest version of the comparison needs both numbers: the cost of the hour, and the share of the hour the student receives. This page publishes both, using market rates with their sources named.

There is a second thing a ratio of one buys that no amount of group teaching provides, and it is not attention at all. It is sequence. A student who has misunderstood something in September will carry that misunderstanding through everything built on it, and only an individual session can stop, go back three topics and rebuild. A class cannot do that for one student without failing the other seven, and a good teacher in a group knows it. That single capability is the reason individual sessions exist, and it is the one thing a cheaper format cannot substitute for at any frequency. A student carrying a broken foundation through a Diploma year is not short of teaching hours; they are short of one hour spent in the right place.

Where IB Gram sits is specific. Every match is one student with one tutor, delivered over live video with the student writing on a shared whiteboard the tutor annotates. There are no premises in Dubai and no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. Dirham figures on this page are market rates with the publisher named, never an IB Gram quote, and the one commitment made is a free first lesson, one per student and one student per family, with no card details collected.
