dubai/1-to-1-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Ratio matters differently in each IB programme. A primary child needs frequent short contact. A Middle Years student needs criterion wording unpicked on their own writing. A Diploma student needs papers marked and a sequence repaired. These are the three programmes Dubai schools run, described by what the ratio of one specifically adds in each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: At primary level the value of a ratio of one is attention span rather than content. A seven-year-old reading aloud to one adult who stops at every error gets something a reading group structurally cannot provide. Sessions should be short, which also makes the individual rate affordable: thirty minutes of genuine one-to-one twice a week usually outperforms an hour-long group session once a week, at a comparable monthly figure.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary cohorts turn over constantly, and the commonest individual request here is a short diagnostic to tell a real difficulty apart from a curriculum sequencing difference. That question cannot be answered in a group at all. KHDA's mandatory Arabic streams also begin in these years, taught separately for Arab and non-Arab students, and any individual support has to follow the school's own stream and material.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years subjects are marked against four criteria out of 8 each, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. The criterion a student is losing is specific to that student's writing, which is exactly the thing a group cannot address: criterion C in one student's history essay and criterion D in another's are different problems. Individual sessions here are usually short runs around a reporting point rather than continuous.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai continuum schools often run Middle Years to Grade 10 before offering a Diploma or British route, so a Grade 9 individual session frequently has two jobs: repair the criterion that is costing marks, and produce evidence about whether Higher Level will be viable. Both need one student's own work in front of the tutor, which is why a pair arrangement rarely suits this stage even between friends.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where a ratio of one earns the premium most clearly. Six subjects on a 45-point total, internally assessed work in each, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and every one of those components fails for student-specific reasons. Marking a student's paper, sorting their lost marks and rebuilding the topic underneath cannot be done to a room, and the second year leaves no time to discover that the hours were spent at the wrong ratio.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma teaching in Dubai concentrates in fewer schools than the surrounding British sector, which means a student taking a minority Higher Level subject may be one of very few in their community doing so. There is often literally no group to join. For those students the choice is not between ratios but between an individual online specialist and no specialist at all.

dubai/1-to-1-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are subjects where Dubai families most often conclude that a ratio of one is necessary rather than preferable, with the specific thing an individual session does that a group cannot. The test in each case is whether the fix depends on this student's own written work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency fails in individual ways: one student drops signs, another cannot factorise under time pressure, a third sets up calculus correctly and loses marks on presentation order. A group drills the average of those three. An individual session finds which one is yours in twenty minutes of watching the student work and then drills only that.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Long-answer questions need a sequence: define, state the relationship, substitute, evaluate. Watching a student write one in real time shows where the sequence breaks, which a marked script alone only hints at. The internal investigation needs a research question narrowed against that student's available equipment, which is inherently an individual conversation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanisms expose whether a student understands electron behaviour or has memorised arrows. The diagnosis takes one unfamiliar mechanism and a tutor watching the pen move. If the understanding is missing, bonding and periodicity have to be rebuilt, which means going back three topics for one student while the rest of a class moves on.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive skills carry the grade and they are impossible to build in a group at any useful rate, because each student needs their own errors corrected as they speak. Fifteen minutes of corrected speaking per week moves a grade. In a group of eight, fifteen minutes of speaking practice is less than two minutes each.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Dubai students arrive at Arabic B with wildly different starting points, from household fluency with written weakness to no prior exposure. Grouping them produces a session that fits nobody. Individual work can match script practice, vocabulary range and speaking correction to the actual starting point, which is the only way the course is manageable for a late starter.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the missing evaluation sentence are both habits, and habits are corrected by interruption at the moment they occur. The internally assessed commentaries depend on the student's own chosen articles, which cannot be supervised collectively because every student has different articles and different diagram requirements.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Students describe studies accurately and never link them to the question, which is a writing habit specific to how that student plans an answer. Individual sessions can rebuild the planning step directly on their own paragraphs. The experimental study needs a simple replicable design, and talking a student out of an over-ambitious one is a one-to-one conversation.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle produces work nobody else in the room is doing, so there is no shared content to teach. Individual supervision is the only realistic format: a project at a particular stage, with particular constraints, needing particular criteria explained. This is one of the subjects where Dubai families most often find no local group exists at all.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A subject chosen as a manageable option and then marked on precise physiology and data handling. The gap is almost always between confident practical knowledge and imprecise written answers, and closing it means marking that student's own extended responses. Group revision of content rarely touches the actual problem.

subjects.name: Music
subjects.description: Assessment combines analysis, creating and performing, and no two students present the same portfolio. Support has to be built around the pieces and the written commentary that student has actually produced, which makes a ratio of one the default rather than an upgrade. Dubai cohorts in this subject are small, so an online individual match is usually the only option.

dubai/1-to-1-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and what the ratio of one changes locally
dubai/1-to-1-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: An individual online session reaches every Dubai community identically, so geography does not change the tutor. It changes whether a group alternative exists at all, and it changes which evening slots a household can realistically protect for one child at a time. These are the communities where individual enquiries cluster.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and Dubai Marina
regions.note: Apartment households where the practical constraint is one quiet room shared between siblings. Individual sessions get staggered rather than stacked here, and 45 minutes with headphones works better than a 90-minute block that competes with a younger child's bedtime.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Established villa communities with large Diploma cohorts, which means group options genuinely exist for mainstream subjects. Families here are usually choosing between a local group and an individual session, and the honest answer depends entirely on whether the problem has been diagnosed yet.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer family communities with younger cohorts and long bus routes. Children arrive home late and tired, so shorter individual sessions on a protected weekday slot hold far better than longer ones, and weekend mornings are frequently the most reliable option.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Growing communities near Creek-side continuum schools, with a high proportion of mid-year arrivals part way through a programme. The first individual session here is usually diagnostic rather than remedial: establishing what has actually been covered before any teaching sequence is planned.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mizhar
regions.note: Lower density and longer drives, which historically limited families to whichever visiting tutor could reach them. For a minority Higher Level subject that radius often contained nobody suitable, and an individual online match is the whole difference rather than a saving.

regions.name: Remraam, Mudon and Serena
regions.note: Communities where several families often share a school bus route and sometimes ask about pairing two students. That works for consolidation of the same content at the same level and fails for diagnosis, so we agree which of the two the session is for before arranging anything.

regions.name: Garhoud, Deira and Oud Metha
regions.note: Older established areas with a dense mix of curricula and strong demand for individual Arabic and mathematics support. Parents commuting locally can usually protect an earlier slot here than in the southern communities, which suits Middle Years students who fade after seven.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Spread-out communities where the nearest Diploma provision is a drive and the local tutoring supply skews towards generalists. Individual matching by subject rather than by proximity is the practical argument for online delivery in this part of the emirate.

schoolClusters.city: Large Diploma cohorts where groups do exist
schoolClusters.note: In these schools a mainstream Higher Level subject has enough students that a group or a school revision class is a genuine alternative. Families here benefit from sequencing: an individual diagnostic block first, then cheaper group consolidation once the error class is identified and being worked on.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Schools with small cohorts in minority subjects
schoolClusters.note: Where only a few students in a year take a given Higher Level option, there is no group to join at any price and individual support is the only format available. This is also where internal assessment supervision load falls heaviest on a small teaching team, and a second reader is most often wanted.

modes.description: The format most Middle Years students and many Standard Level students work best in. Forty-five minutes of genuine individual attention is more than most students receive in a fortnight of group teaching, and it finishes before concentration goes. It also keeps the weekly figure lower, which matters for families running two children or two subjects at once.

sections.heading: Minutes of attention per ratio, and what each ratio can diagnose
paragraphs: The useful comparison between tutoring formats is not the hourly rate. It is the cost of a minute of attention directed at your child, combined with what each ratio is structurally capable of doing. A group can teach content well. Only a ratio of one can find out why a specific student is losing marks, because that requires reading their work and changing the explanation until it lands.

The attention figures in the table are estimates from how sessions actually run rather than a published study, and they are deliberately generous to the groups. Explanation delivered to the whole room genuinely serves everybody, so it is not counted as lost. What is counted is the time available for one student's own questions, their own written work and the correction of their own errors, which is where diagnosis happens.

The dirham column converts published Dubai market bands into cost per student per hour at each ratio. Those bands come from providers' own pages read in October 2026 and are market figures rather than an IB Gram quote. The pattern they show is consistent: group seats are far cheaper per hour and the gap per minute of attention is much smaller than it looks, while the capability difference is absolute rather than gradual.

The last column is the one to decide on. If the job is revising content a student already broadly knows, buy the cheapest ratio they can keep up with. If nobody yet knows why the marks are being lost, or if the work is internally assessed and specific to that student, a ratio of one is not an upgrade but a requirement.

sections.heading: The attention arithmetic, worked through on a real week
paragraphs: Take a Grade 11 student in Dubai with a 5 in Higher Level Chemistry and no clear idea why. Option one is a group class of eight for ninety minutes a week at the lowest published band. Option two is a single individual hour at the mid specialist band. On paper the group is a fraction of the cost and half again as long, and most families choose it.

Now count what the student receives. In the group, roughly eleven minutes of attention directed at them across the ninety, almost none of it spent reading their own written answers, and a pace set by whichever topic the majority needs. In the individual hour, sixty minutes on their own work, including fifteen spent on an unfamiliar mechanism that reveals they have memorised arrows rather than understood electron behaviour. One of those two sessions has found the problem.

Over a term the divergence compounds. The group student knows more content and is still losing the same marks, because the lost marks were never about content. The individual student has had bonding rebuilt, which is three sessions of apparently backwards work that nothing in a group could have delivered. The grade moves for the second student and does not for the first, and the first family concludes that tutoring does not work.

This is not an argument that groups are bad value. It is an argument that the two products answer different questions, and that buying the cheaper one for the harder question is the expensive mistake. The efficient sequence for most Dubai families is individual diagnosis first, then group or independent consolidation once the target is known and being hit.

sections.heading: Why individual rates in Dubai sit where they do
paragraphs: An individual hour is priced from costs a group hour spreads across several families, and knowing which they are makes a quote legible. Preparation for a specific student, marking that student's work outside the session, writing the record, and the simple fact that the tutor cannot sell that hour to anyone else are the four that matter. In-home arrangements add a fifth, which is the slot lost to travel.

Preparation and marking are the ones families underestimate. A specialist marking a Higher Level paper section against the published criteria and writing a useful note is doing perhaps thirty minutes of unpaid work around a sixty-minute session. That work is the reason the specialist band exists, and it is also exactly what a cheaper arrangement quietly omits. Asking whether marking is inside the hour is the single most informative price question available.

The travel component is the one Dubai distorts most. Published in-home one-to-one rates in this emirate run from around AED 180 to 500 across sources, with Bestimate's 2026 table at 180 to 350 and some home tutors quoted up to 500. A late-afternoon crossing can consume the time of most of another session in each direction, and that sits inside the figure whether a provider itemises it or not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. Every UAE match runs over live video, which removes the travel component from the cost structure entirely and, more importantly, removes the geographic limit on which tutor a family can choose. The table separates the components so a quote from anyone can be read against them.

sections.heading: What 45, 60 and 90 minutes can each actually finish
paragraphs: Session length is treated as a budget decision and it is really a cognitive one. A student can absorb a limited amount of new correction before returns fall away, and that limit is lower than most families expect, particularly in the second Diploma year when school has already consumed the day. Buying ninety minutes for a tired Grade 12 student frequently purchases twenty-five minutes of value and fifteen of resentment.

Forty-five minutes is enough to finish one thing. One error class, one topic repaired, one section of a paper marked and taught from. The discipline of finishing rather than starting is what makes short sessions effective, and it is why they often beat longer ones for Middle Years students and for anybody working after seven in the evening.

Sixty minutes is the natural length for Diploma subject work because the cycle has three parts: read what the student produced, teach into the gap, set and explain the next task. An hour accommodates all three without rushing. It is also the length most published dirham bands in this market are quoted against, which makes it the easiest to compare across providers.

Ninety minutes has one strong use and several weak ones. Sitting a whole paper to time and marking it in the same sitting cannot be split, and neither can a serious read-and-review of an internally assessed draft. Outside those jobs, the extra thirty minutes is usually better spent as a separate session later in the week. The table sets each length against what it can finish and roughly what it costs at mid-band market rates.

sections.heading: Testing an individual match in the first hour
paragraphs: Everybody is impressive in a trial lesson, which is why judging a one-to-one tutor on manner is close to useless. The free first session should be used as a test with a known answer: send a piece of marked work in advance and watch what the tutor does with it. A specialist reads the lost marks, sorts them into categories, names the most expensive one and teaches into it within the hour.

Three failure signals show up reliably in a first session. The first is a tutor who begins with their own placement test rather than the work you sent, which usually means they intend to teach a programme rather than respond to a student. The second is a tutor who explains a topic confidently and never watches the student write, because errors appear in the writing and nowhere else. The third is a session that produces no written record, which makes the next four weeks unauditable.

The positive signals are equally concrete. The tutor asks which school, because internal assessment calendars differ across Dubai and the answer changes the plan. They ask what the student thinks went wrong, and listen to the answer. They go backwards when the student's explanation reveals a missing foundation, rather than pressing on with the planned topic. And the note afterwards names a category of error rather than describing the lesson.

If the match is wrong, a free hour is a good way to find that out. Changing the proposed tutor after a trial is normal and costs nothing, and a provider that treats a rejected match as a problem rather than as information is managing its roster rather than your child's grade.

sections.heading: Siblings and pairs: where sharing an individual session works
paragraphs: Dubai households frequently have two children in the same programme and ask whether one session can cover both. Sometimes it can, and the honest answer depends on three things: whether they are at the same level, whether the thing being worked on is shared content rather than individual error correction, and whether they can tolerate each other's pace without one of them disengaging.

Pairing works best for a specific case: two students at the same level, in the same subject, consolidating content both have been taught and neither has mastered. There, the second student genuinely benefits from hearing the first one's questions, and the per-student cost drops materially. Pairing also works for timed practice, where both sit the same paper and the marking is discussed together with individual points made privately afterwards.

Pairing fails for diagnosis, for internally assessed work and across levels. Two students losing marks for different reasons cannot both be diagnosed in one hour; the tutor will find one problem and guess at the other. Internally assessed components are specific to each student's own draft and must be discussed individually. And a Standard Level student paired with a Higher Level sibling is usually paying to watch someone else's lesson.

Where a family does want a pair arrangement, we agree which student the session is primarily for and say so, rather than pretending the hour serves both equally. Siblings in different programmes are almost always better served by two shorter individual sessions, staggered, which is also easier in an apartment with one quiet room.

sections.heading: Fitting one tutor into a Dubai evening
paragraphs: An individual slot has to survive a school year, and in Dubai the thing that kills it is almost never the teaching. It is the calendar. School buses that arrive late, a sibling's activity, a parent's commute back across the city, Ramadan timings, and the simple fact that a tired child at eight in the evening learns very little. Agreeing the slot properly at the start is worth more than a better tutor on the wrong slot.

Earlier is better for younger students and often impossible for working households. The compromise most Dubai families land on is a protected weekday slot that is slightly inconvenient for everybody and therefore actually holds, plus an agreed fallback on a weekend morning for weeks when the weekday fails. Writing the fallback down at the start removes the weekly renegotiation that quietly ends arrangements by week six.

Ramadan deserves explicit planning rather than improvisation. School days shorten, late-afternoon energy drops noticeably, and the usable window for many families moves to after Iftar. A session fixed at five o'clock in September will be missed through Ramadan, so agreeing the alternative timing when the slot is first set preserves continuity across the month instead of losing four sessions.

sections.heading: Continuity, and what happens when an individual match fails
paragraphs: A ratio of one depends on continuity in a way a group does not. The value accumulates in what the tutor knows about this particular student: which error class they repeat, which explanation finally worked, which topic was rebuilt in October. A rotating roster destroys that, which is why the same tutor stays with a student here unless a change is requested, and why we would rather decline work than cover a slot with whoever is free.

Matches still fail, and they fail for reasons that are nobody's fault. A tutor whose explanation style does not reach a particular student, a personality mismatch, a scheduling change neither side can accommodate. The honest handling is to change the match quickly rather than to persist, and to carry the record across so the new tutor begins from the diagnosis rather than repeating it.

The practical mechanism is the record. Marked scripts, the error-class tally and the session notes belong to the family, so a replacement tutor can read a term of work before the first session. That is the difference between changing tutors costing one session and costing a month. It is also the reason to insist on a written record from week one even when the match is going well.

Availability limits apply and are stated rather than concealed. Coverage is deep in Diploma mathematics, the sciences, economics, business and English, and thinner in several group two languages, some arts subjects and minority options. Where no suitable specialist is free, we give a realistic wait instead of offering someone who teaches an adjacent subject, because at a ratio of one the substitution is obvious within a fortnight.

sections.heading: Individual sessions on internally assessed work
paragraphs: Internally assessed components are the clearest case for a ratio of one and the clearest place where the boundary has to be stated. Every student's exploration, investigation, commentary, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is their own, which makes group supervision close to meaningless and individual supervision genuinely valuable. It also makes the temptation to over-help immediate.

What an individual session may do is specific. Explain what a criterion asks for in the criterion's own language. Read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is not yet met and why. Ask the questions the criteria ask until the student finds the gap. Teach the content, the statistics or the method the work requires. Hold the student to the school's schedule, which is usually the single most useful thing in the whole arrangement.

What it may not do is equally specific. No sentences supplied for insertion. No restructuring performed on the student's behalf. No research question handed over for the student to adopt. No editing that lifts a draft from one band to another without the student doing the thinking. Operations in this market sell completed work; a student submitting it faces an academic honesty investigation reaching well beyond one subject grade.

Because the boundary matters, feedback is logged with a date so a school supervisor can see the shape of the support if they ask. Schools also set their own rules on how many formal drafts may be commented on, and those rules take precedence over anything a tutor would otherwise prefer. Ask the school first; the answer is in their academic honesty policy.

sections.heading: When a ratio of one is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: Individual sessions are the most capable format and the most expensive, which makes them the wrong purchase in several common situations. A student who simply has not covered the content because they missed a term needs volume, and volume is cheaper in a group or through structured independent work with marking attached. Paying specialist individual rates to deliver a syllabus is paying a diagnostician to read a textbook aloud.

A second case is breadth. A family needing some support across four subjects on a fixed budget will get more from a mixture than from one individual subject done beautifully while three others drift. The honest advice there is to pick the subject where the most marks are at stake for individual work and handle the others more cheaply, rather than to spread an individual budget thinly across all four.

A third case is where the problem is not academic at all. A Grade 12 student sleeping five hours and carrying three overdue components does not have a subject problem, and nor does a Grade 7 student who cannot yet read fluently. Both present as grades. Neither responds to a weekly subject session, and the first conversation on every match asks what else is happening precisely so this gets identified before money is spent.

What happens next, if a ratio of one is the right purchase, is short. Send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work. We come back with a named tutor, a proposed session length and a slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually within two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family with no card details taken, and it is spent on the work you sent rather than on introductions.

process.title: Work out whether you need diagnosis or volume
process.description: If nobody knows why marks are being lost, buy a ratio of one. If the content is simply missing and the reason is known, volume is cheaper elsewhere. This single question decides more about value for money than any comparison of hourly rates between providers in this city.

process.title: Choose the session length for the student, not the budget
process.description: Forty-five minutes finished beats ninety minutes endured, particularly after seven in the evening in the second Diploma year. Tell us what time the student will actually be sitting down and how they are by then, and we will propose a length rather than default to an hour.

process.title: Send marked work before the free session
process.description: The trial is a test with a known answer. A specialist reads your child's lost marks, sorts them by category, names the most expensive one and teaches into it inside the hour. Watch for whether they open your work or their own placement test; the difference tells you what you are buying.

process.title: Protect one slot and agree the fallback
process.description: Pick a weekday slot that is slightly inconvenient and therefore holds, agree a weekend morning fallback for the weeks it fails, and settle Ramadan timing in writing at the start. Arrangements in Dubai end from calendar drift far more often than from bad teaching.

process.title: Review at four sessions and keep the record
process.description: You get a written continue, change or stop recommendation with the evidence behind it. The marked scripts, error-class tally and session notes belong to you, so changing tutor costs one session rather than a month. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will recommend it when it is the right one.

whyPoints.title: The ratio is measured, not claimed
whyPoints.description: Minutes of direct attention set out at ratios of one, two, four and eight, with published dirham rates converted to cost per student at each. Every provider in this city calls its sessions personalised; this page states what the word is worth in minutes and lets a family compare.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, named, kept
whyPoints.description: The same specialist stays with a student unless a change is asked for, because at a ratio of one the value sits in what the tutor knows about that student. A rotating roster cannot tell you whether February's mistakes are September's mistakes, which is the only question that matters.

whyPoints.title: Session length chosen for the student
whyPoints.description: Thirty, forty-five, sixty or ninety minutes, matched to what the student can absorb in a sitting rather than to a standard package. Ninety minutes is used for whole timed papers and draft reviews, not sold as a better version of an hour.

whyPoints.title: Sharing recommended where it genuinely works
whyPoints.description: Pairs work for same-level consolidation and timed practice and fail for diagnosis, internally assessed drafts and mixed levels. We will say which applies to your two children rather than take the booking and pretend one hour serves both equally.

whyPoints.title: Costs broken into their components
whyPoints.description: Teaching time, preparation, marking, record-keeping, the irreducible opportunity cost of an undivided hour, and travel where it applies. A quote read against those six components is legible; a quote compared only against another quote is not.

faqs.question: How much attention does my child actually get in a group IB class in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly seven minutes of directly individual attention in a sixty-minute session with eight students, once explanation delivered to the whole room is counted as genuinely shared rather than lost. With four students it is closer to fifteen minutes, with two around twenty-five, and at a ratio of one it is the full hour. Those are working estimates from how sessions run rather than a published study, and they are deliberately generous to the groups. The number matters less than what each ratio can do: only a ratio of one can diagnose.

faqs.question: Is one individual hour better than three hours in a group?
faqs.answer: For diagnosis, yes, clearly. For covering content a student has simply missed, no, and the group is far better value. The distinction is whether anyone yet knows why marks are being lost. If they do not, three group hours will teach more content and leave the same marks being dropped, because the lost marks were never a content problem. If the gap is identified and the work is practice, buy the cheaper ratio. The efficient sequence is individual diagnosis first, then cheaper consolidation.

faqs.question: Why does marking cost extra with some Dubai tutors and not others?
faqs.answer: Because marking a student's work against the published criteria and writing a useful note is roughly thirty minutes of work around a sixty-minute session, and somebody has to be paid for it. Specialist bands in this market include it; cheaper arrangements usually omit it without saying so. Asking whether marking of your child's own written work sits inside the hour or is billed separately is the single most informative price question available, and a vague answer usually means the marking is not happening at all.

faqs.question: Can my two children share one IB session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on three things: whether they are at the same level, whether the work is shared content rather than individual error correction, and whether they tolerate each other's pace. Pairing works well for consolidating content both have been taught, and for sitting the same paper to time. It fails for diagnosis, for internally assessed drafts and across levels, where one child usually ends up watching the other's lesson. For different programmes, two shorter staggered sessions work far better than one shared hour.

faqs.question: What session length should a Grade 12 student in Dubai book?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for routine subject work, and ninety only for a whole paper sat to time or a serious read-through of an internally assessed draft. The constraint is not budget but absorption: a Grade 12 student sitting down at half past seven after a full school day has limited capacity for new correction, and ninety minutes frequently buys twenty-five minutes of value. Two shorter sessions in a week usually beat one long one, which is a scheduling question rather than a pricing one.

faqs.question: What should I watch for during the free first individual lesson?
faqs.answer: Whether the tutor opens the marked work you sent or their own placement test. A specialist reads your child's lost marks, sorts them by category, names the most expensive one and teaches into it inside the hour. Three warning signs: starting with their own assessment instead of your evidence, explaining confidently without ever watching the student write, and producing no written record afterwards. Positive signs: asking which school, asking what the student thinks went wrong, and going backwards when a foundation turns out to be missing.

faqs.question: Does one-to-one work as well over video as in the same room?
faqs.answer: For the work that matters at this ratio, yes, because the marking happens on the student's own writing either way. The student writes on a shared whiteboard, the tutor annotates it, and both see the pen move. What changes is who is available: online, a Dubai family picks from specialists rather than from whoever can reach their community by five o'clock, which decides the match entirely for minority Higher Level subjects. Presence in the room is a real preference, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: How do I stop a weekly individual slot from collapsing by week six?
faqs.answer: Agree the fallback at the start. Pick a weekday slot that is slightly inconvenient for everybody and therefore holds, add a standing weekend morning option for the weeks the weekday fails, and settle Ramadan timing in writing in advance rather than when the month arrives. Dubai arrangements end from calendar drift far more often than from bad teaching: a late school bus, a sibling's fixture, a parent's commute. Writing the exceptions down removes the weekly renegotiation that quietly kills the arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens if we do not get on with the individual tutor we are matched with?
faqs.answer: The match changes, quickly, and it costs one session rather than a month because the record travels. The marked scripts, error-class tally and session notes belong to your family, so a replacement tutor reads a term of work before their first lesson and starts from the diagnosis rather than repeating it. Matches fail for reasons that are nobody's fault, including explanation style and plain personality mismatch. A provider that treats a rejected match as a problem is managing its roster rather than your child's grade.

faqs.question: Is individual tutoring worth it for a subject my child is already passing?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the target is and where the marks sit. Moving a 5 to a 6 in a subject that matters for an offer is often the most efficient individual work available, because the gap is usually technique rather than content and technique responds fast to marking. Moving a 6 to a 7 is harder and takes longer. Moving a 3 to a 4 is usually a content and sequence problem that needs more hours than families expect. Ask which of the three you are buying before you commit.

faqs.question: Can an individual tutor help with my child's Extended Essay without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific rather than a matter of judgement. A tutor may explain what a criterion asks for in its own language, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is unmet and why, ask the questions the criteria ask, teach the method or statistics the work needs, and hold the schedule. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure on the student's behalf, hand over a research question, or edit a draft into a higher band. Your school's own rules on drafts take precedence.

faqs.question: When is a ratio of one the wrong thing to buy in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three cases. When the content is simply missing because a term was lost and the reason is already known, in which case volume is cheaper in a group or through marked independent work. When a family needs some support across four subjects on a fixed budget, where a mixture beats one subject done beautifully while three drift. And when the problem is not academic at all, which is why the first conversation asks what else is happening rather than what the grade is.

faqs.question: Do individual Dubai tutors need a government permit to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation grants the private tuition work permit free of charge for two years through its own smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount sceptically.

faqs.question: How quickly can a 1-to-1 match be arranged in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually a named tutor, a proposed session length and a slot in Gulf Standard Time within two working days of receiving the subject, level, school and a sample of marked work, with the free first lesson shortly after. The honest exception is coverage. Diploma mathematics, the sciences, economics, business and English are deep. Several group two languages, some arts subjects and minority options are thinner, and when nothing suitable is free we give a realistic wait rather than filling the slot with an adjacent-subject teacher.

faqs.question: Is there any discount for booking a term of individual sessions up front?
faqs.answer: We would rather you did not, and that is deliberate. Buying a term in advance removes the one decision point that protects a family's money, which is the four-session review where you receive a written continue, change or stop recommendation with the evidence behind it. Four sessions is enough to produce a diagnosis, marked work and a named recurring error class, and short enough that stopping costs little. If any provider will only sell a term, ask yourself what the review would have told you.

dubai/1-to-1-ib-tutor.closingBody: Decide first whether you need diagnosis or volume, because that answer settles the ratio and most of the cost. Then send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work. We come back with a named tutor, a proposed session length and a protected slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually within two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family with no card details collected, and it is spent on the work you sent. Every match is one student with one tutor over live video, and if nothing suitable is free when you need it, you will be told so rather than offered a substitute.

dubai/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE one-to-one: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications, Core and Extended tiers, Foundation and Higher papers. intro.heading: The hour you are actually buying
paragraphs: One-to-one tuition is priced per hour, but an hour is not what you are buying. You are buying the share of that hour in which a teacher is looking at your child's working, deciding what is wrong with it, and saying so. In a Dubai school class of twenty-two, that share is measured in seconds. In a tuition centre group of eight it is a few minutes. In a one-to-one session it is the whole hour, which is why the hourly figure looks high and why the cost per corrected mistake is usually the lowest of the three.

That is the trade this page prices. Market rates for one-to-one IGCSE tuition in Dubai sit roughly between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and roughly AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit once travel is inside the fee. Specialist and examiner-tier rates run above both. Those bands come from what providers in this market publish; they are not IB Gram's price list, and every figure on this page is attributed where it came from.

IB Gram is an independent IB and IGCSE tutor-matching platform. It is not affiliated with Cambridge International, with Pearson, or with any Dubai school named on this page. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate design choice rather than a limitation, and the comparison table further down sets out what a Dubai family gains and gives up because of it.

The practical effect is subject depth. A family in Mirdif looking for a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 specialist who can teach Paper 4 and Paper 6 properly is choosing from everyone available at that hour across time zones, not from whoever will drive to Mirdif at 16:00 on a Tuesday. For Core-tier Maths that distinction barely matters. For Additional Mathematics 0606, for Economics 0455 data-response work, or for a child sitting the November series alone as a private candidate, it decides whether the right tutor exists at all.

What follows is arranged as a cost argument. First what the hour costs and who charges it; then where the sixty minutes go; then the attention arithmetic that explains the premium; then how many hours a grade move takes; then the Dubai-specific things that move the number, from the KHDA fee position to the school-run corridors that decide whether a 16:30 start is realistic. Read it in order and you should be able to put a budget and a session count on paper before you speak to anyone.

dubai/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits in the middle of a British-curriculum school career in Dubai, between Key Stage 3 and a post-16 route that splits towards A Level or the IB Diploma. One-to-one hours are worth different things at each of those stages, and the tier your child is entered for changes the ceiling on what those hours can reach.

programmes.name: IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the Core subject content and is capped: on Cambridge syllabuses the highest grade available from Core papers is C. Students sit the Core paper set, usually Paper 1 and Paper 3 in the sciences, and are assessed on a narrower band of content than Extended candidates. One-to-one work at Core tier is mostly about securing the grades already in reach and about deciding, honestly and early, whether a move to Extended is realistic before the entry deadline closes it off.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools make the Core-or-Extended decision at different points in Year 10, and because entries are submitted months before the papers are sat, a late change is often an administrative impossibility rather than a teaching judgement. If your child is being entered Core in a subject they need at A Level, that conversation belongs in the autumn term with the head of department, and a diagnostic hour with a tutor who knows the syllabus can tell you whether the case is arguable.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended tier carries the full syllabus content and the full grade range to A* or 9, depending on whether the school reports letters or numbers. The paper set is harder and longer, and the additional content is where most of the marks are lost: non-linear algebra and transformations in Maths, moles and electrolysis in Chemistry, momentum and electromagnetism in Physics. This is where the great majority of one-to-one IGCSE hours in Dubai are spent, and where a specialist is worth more than a generalist.
programmes.countryNote: Extended entries dominate in the Dubai schools that feed sixth forms running A Level or the IB Diploma, because both post-16 routes expect the Extended content as a starting point. A child who scrapes a grade 5 at Extended Maths and then takes Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches in the Diploma will spend the first Diploma term closing the same gaps. Fixing them in Year 11 is cheaper in hours than fixing them in Year 12.

programmes.name: Years 8-9 bridge into IGCSE
programmes.description: The two years before the IGCSE course are where the arithmetic, algebraic fluency and scientific vocabulary that IGCSE assumes are either built or not. Children arrive in Year 10 able to rearrange a formula or they do not, and the course does not stop to teach it again. One-to-one work at this stage is cheap relative to its effect: shorter sessions, fewer of them, and no exam pressure forcing the pace.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's British-curriculum schools take in new arrivals across the year as families relocate, so Year 9 classes often hold children who have come from CBSE, from an American curriculum, or from a different British school with a different Key Stage 3 scheme. The gaps are rarely general weakness; they are specific topics nobody taught in that sequence. A diagnostic session names them in an hour, and a short block of one-to-one closes them before Year 10 starts.

programmes.name: Post-IGCSE: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide which post-16 route and which subjects a Dubai sixth form will accept, and those thresholds are published by each school rather than set nationally. A grade 6 or B at Extended is a common floor for taking a subject further; the sciences and Maths often ask for more. One-to-one hours in Year 11 are therefore buying optionality at 16, not just a line on a certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai schools run both post-16 systems, often on the same campus, the same IGCSE grade can open an A Level place and fall short of a Higher Level Diploma place, or the reverse. Ask your child's school for its own published entry requirements per subject before you set a target grade, then work the one-to-one hours backwards from that number rather than from a general wish to improve.

dubai/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Dubai families most often book one-to-one, with what each is actually assessed on and where the marks go missing. Syllabus codes are Cambridge unless stated; your child's school will have entered them for one specific code, and the first thing a tutor should ask is which.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580) and Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Extended 0580 loses marks in algebraic manipulation, transformations, and the multi-step problems that carry method marks for working that students do not write down. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a different animal again, assuming fluency the main syllabus only introduces, and is usually taken alongside rather than instead of 0580.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Marks go in two places: the quantitative topics, where momentum, circuits and electromagnetic induction demand exact use of formulae, and Paper 6, the practical component, where candidates lose marks on graph axes, significant figures, and describing a control rather than naming one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The mole dominates the Extended mark distribution, and students who cannot move between mass, moles and concentration without prompting lose marks across several papers at once. Electrolysis, rates of reaction, and the organic chemistry at the end of the syllabus are the other reliable losses.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Biology looks learnable and is marked strictly. Candidates lose marks for naming a process where the command term asks them to explain it, for describing a graph instead of interpreting it, and for using everyday words where the syllabus has a precise term. Much of the one-to-one work here is command-term discipline.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Double and single award science compress three subjects into one grade, so a weakness in one of the three pulls the whole result down invisibly. A diagnostic that splits performance by discipline is worth the first hour, because the fix is almost always narrower than the grade suggests.

subjects.name: English Language (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.levels: First language and second language routes
subjects.description: 0500 rewards controlled, purposeful writing and precise reading responses; 0510 rewards accuracy and task completion. Dubai cohorts frequently contain children entered for the wrong one of the two, which is a conversation with the school rather than a tutoring problem, and worth having early.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Both are lost on the longer questions. Candidates define terms competently, then fail to apply them to the data or the case study in front of them, and the evaluation marks go unclaimed. One-to-one time here is spent on answer structure and on the discipline of using the stimulus material.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: 0478 Paper 2 asks for algorithms and pseudocode under time pressure, and students who can program fluently in Python still lose marks on the published pseudocode conventions. Paper 1 theory on data representation and networks rewards exact vocabulary, which is a memorising problem one-to-one work can structure.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in Dubai private schools as a mandatory subject under KHDA requirements, and the first-language and additional-language routes are genuinely different courses with different assessment demands. Children are sometimes placed by nationality rather than by competence, and that placement is worth checking.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Both are source-and-skills subjects dressed as content subjects. History candidates lose marks by narrating instead of arguing from the source; Geography candidates lose them on case-study specificity and on the data-response and fieldwork components, where general answers earn nothing.

dubai/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Dubai's geography matters to one-to-one tuition mainly through time: when a child gets home, how long a school run takes on the corridor they live on, and therefore whether a session can start before homework and fatigue have taken the evening. These are the areas families most often ask about.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Dense apartment living, high relocation turnover, and a school run that usually means Al Sufouh or Barsha rather than a walk. Sessions here typically start from 17:00 once the bus has arrived, and siblings often need staggered slots rather than one shared one.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Villa communities with large British and Indian-curriculum cohorts and schools close enough that children are home early. Earlier starts from 16:00 are realistic, which matters in exam term when a 90-minute session will not fit after 18:00.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Long internal distances inside the community itself, and a school run that feeds several British-curriculum schools on the Al Qudra and Umm Suqeim corridors. Families here often book two subjects in one evening, which works online and is awkward with a visiting tutor.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Older villa districts feeding long-established British-curriculum schools, with the shortest school runs in the city and the earliest realistic session starts. Parents here are frequently balancing IGCSE tuition against swimming and music commitments that already own the early evening.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment towers with little quiet study space, which is a practical constraint on any tuition format. A one-to-one session online needs a door that shuts; where there is not one, families often book the slot before parents are home rather than after.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing mid-market communities with school runs crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, where a 20-minute journey becomes 45 in the afternoon peak. This is the clearest case for online delivery: the travel surcharge on an in-home visit here buys nothing a parent wants.

regions.name: Mudon, Town Square and Dubailand
regions.note: Newer outlying communities where the pool of tutors willing to drive out is thin and the fee for doing so is highest. Subject scarcity bites hardest here, and it is the main reason Additional Mathematics or Computer Science requests from these areas go unmatched locally.

regions.name: Deira, Bur Dubai and Al Qusais
regions.note: Older districts with a large Indian and Pakistani-curriculum presence alongside British-curriculum schools, and strong demand for IGCSE Maths and the sciences. Session timing here is usually built around Maghrib and family dinner rather than around the school run.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools on the Al Sufouh and Barsha corridor
schoolClusters.note: This cluster serves Marina, JBR, Al Barsha and Tecom families and runs IGCSE at 16 before splitting towards A Level or the Diploma. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; naming them is ecosystem context, not a relationship.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa and the Qusais side of the city
schoolClusters.note: A mix of British and Indian-curriculum provision with large IGCSE cohorts and earlier home times, which is why one-to-one sessions from these areas tend to start before 17:00 and why Maths and the sciences dominate the requests.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving the Ranches, Dubai Hills and Al Qudra communities
schoolClusters.note: Villa-community schools with long internal catchments, several running both A Level and the IB Diploma post-16, so the IGCSE grade thresholds parents are working towards differ by route even inside one campus.

dubai/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: One-to-one is a format, not a single product. These are the three shapes it takes for IGCSE families in Dubai, and the hourly cost and the number of hours needed differ between them more than the headline rate suggests.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the year
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same slot each week from September. The session tracks the school's scheme of work rather than running ahead of it, so the tutor is fixing this week's lesson while it is still fresh and the homework is still open. This is the cheapest route per grade moved because nothing has to be re-taught from scratch, and it is the only shape that makes the Core-or-Extended decision in good time.

modes.title: A fixed diagnostic block
modes.description: Four to six sessions bought as a block to answer one question: what is actually wrong, and how many hours would it take to fix. The first session is diagnostic, using a past paper under timed conditions rather than a conversation, and the block ends with a written plan and an hour count. Families who are unsure whether tuition is the right spend at all usually start here rather than committing to a year.

sections.heading: What a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor in Dubai costs per hour
paragraphs: A qualified subject tutor working one-to-one and online with a Dubai family charges roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour at October 2026 market rates. An in-home visit is higher, roughly AED 180 to AED 500 once the travel is inside the fee. Named specialist and examiner-tier tutors sit above both bands. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's rate card.

The bands come from what providers in this market actually publish. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65, and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, both at the university-student end of the market. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 for its premium named tier. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Monthly packages circulating in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Three things are worth noticing about that list. First, half the pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in. Second, the spread between the cheapest and dearest published figure is roughly twentyfold, which means the word tutor is doing very different work at each end. Third, IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly price on this page, because the rate depends on the subject, the tier and the series: the honest route is a free trial lesson and a quote for your child's actual subject and target.

sections.heading: Where the sixty minutes go
paragraphs: A one-to-one hour that works is not an hour of explaining. It is roughly ten minutes of finding out what went wrong, twenty of the child attempting something under supervision, fifteen of marking that attempt against the actual mark scheme, and the rest spent setting what happens before next week. If a session is forty-five minutes of a tutor talking and ten of a child nodding, the format's advantage has been thrown away and a recorded video would have done the same job for nothing.

The marking matters more than the explaining, and it is the part families most often do not get. A grade on a piece of work tells a child nothing. A mark scheme annotation that says this answer described the graph where the command term asked you to interpret it, so the two application marks were never available, tells them exactly one thing they can change. IGCSE papers are marked to published criteria, and those criteria are consistent enough that a tutor who knows them can predict where a particular child will leak marks before they sit the paper.

This is also why the between-session work is part of what the hour buys. A tutor who sets a timed question set, marks it before the next session and arrives knowing the two topics that need the time is using the hour differently from one who opens a textbook at the start of the lesson and asks what the child would like to look at. When you compare quotes in Dubai, the useful question is not the hourly rate but what happens to written work in the six days between sessions.

sections.heading: The attention arithmetic a group class cannot beat
paragraphs: The premium on one-to-one is not mystical. It is arithmetic. In a sixty-minute session, the total quantity of individual feedback available is sixty minutes divided by the number of students, minus whatever time goes on managing the group. One child gets fifty-plus usable minutes. Four children get rather less than fifteen each, because transitions and shared explanation eat the difference. A class of twenty-two gets under two minutes each, which is why a child can attend school diligently for a term and still carry the same misconception they started with.

That arithmetic explains something counter-intuitive about price. A group class at AED 80 per student per hour delivers perhaps twelve minutes of individual attention, which is an effective rate of roughly AED 400 per hour of attention. A one-to-one session at AED 250 delivers close to the full hour, an effective rate of around AED 280. The group looks cheaper per hour and is often dearer per unit of the thing you are actually buying. Whether that matters depends entirely on what is wrong: a child who needs more practice does fine in a group, while a child with a specific misconception needs someone to find it.

Group teaching is not therefore a worse product. It is a different one, and for revision of material already understood it is good value. The distinction to hold onto is diagnostic versus practice. If nobody has yet established why your child's Chemistry marks are stuck at grade 5, a group class will not establish it, and three terms of group revision can pass without the cause ever being named. Once it has been named, group practice is a perfectly sensible place to consolidate.

sections.heading: How many one-to-one hours a grade move usually takes
paragraphs: The question behind the hourly rate is always how many hours, and the honest answer is that it depends on the distance and the cause. A child who understands the content and loses marks on exam technique can move a band in a handful of hours, because nothing has to be learned, only re-expressed. A child missing the algebraic fluency that half the Extended Maths syllabus assumes is looking at a term, because the gap sits underneath the content being taught rather than inside it.

The figures in the table below are planning estimates drawn from how blocks are usually scoped, not a promise about any individual child, and no tutor can promise a particular outcome. They are useful for one purpose: turning a vague wish into a budget. Twelve hours at AED 220 is AED 2,640, which is a decision a family can actually make. Improve my daughter's Chemistry is not a decision, and it tends to turn into an open-ended monthly payment nobody reviews.

Two scheduling facts change those numbers more than anything about the tutor. Starting in September rather than February roughly halves the hours needed for the same movement, because the work happens alongside first teaching rather than on top of it. And a child doing the set work between sessions needs materially fewer hours than one who does not, which is the single largest variable in the whole calculation and the one entirely within your household's control.

sections.heading: What moves the number in Dubai specifically
paragraphs: Several of the things that change a tutoring quote in Dubai have nothing to do with the tutor. The first is time of year. Demand for IGCSE specialists peaks twice, before the January mocks and from February into the May/June series, and a named specialist booked in February costs more and is harder to get than the same person booked in September. Cambridge runs only June and November for a Dubai candidate, so the second peak is the autumn one: families chasing a November resit place start competing for the same specialists in September, while the June cohort is still thinking about mocks.

The second is geography, but only if someone has to travel. The school-run corridors decide when a child is home: a family in Jumeirah 2 whose school is ten minutes away can start a session at 16:00, while a family in Jumeirah Village Circle crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road in the afternoon peak is realistically starting at 17:30. For an in-home visit, that journey is inside the fee and the dead time is paid for. Online, the geography changes the start time and nothing else, which is why the quoted rate does not move with the community you live in.

The third is subject scarcity. Dubai has a deep pool of IGCSE Maths and English tutors and a thin one for Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode work, Arabic as a first language 0508, and anything taught to a child sitting as a private candidate. Scarcity, not quality, is what drives the top of the market. The fourth is context: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so for most families the tuition line is the part of the education budget that is actually moving, which makes reviewing it properly worth an hour of your time.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against in-home visiting in Dubai
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition for families in Dubai is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative is a page that implies one thing and delivers another, and because the comparison is one a Dubai family deserves to make on the facts rather than on a sales preference.

The honest version of the comparison is that in-home tuition wins on two things. A tutor physically present can hold the attention of a younger or very distractible child in a way a screen struggles to, and for a family that simply prefers a person in the room, that preference is legitimate and not something a table can argue away. What in-home loses on is everything downstream of the travel: the fee carries dead driving time, the pool of available tutors shrinks to whoever is within a tolerable radius of your community, and a cancelled session is harder to move because a journey has to be rescheduled too.

For IGCSE specifically, the pool question is decisive more often than parents expect. The difference between a Physics graduate who can teach 0625 and a Physics teacher who has marked Paper 6 practical questions for several series is large, and it is not a difference you can find twice inside a twenty-minute drive of Mudon. Online, the constraint becomes the clock rather than the map, and Gulf Standard Time overlaps comfortably with both Europe and South Asia for an after-school slot.

sections.heading: The first paid hour: what a diagnostic has to produce
paragraphs: A first session should not be a conversation. If an hour is spent asking a fifteen-year-old how they feel about Chemistry and which topics they find hard, you have bought their self-assessment, which is the least reliable instrument available. A diagnostic hour should put a past paper or a section of one in front of the student under something close to timed conditions, and then read the working rather than the answers. The errors are in the working.

What should come out of it is specific enough to be checked. Not needs to work on algebra, but cannot rearrange an equation when the unknown appears twice, loses method marks by doing arithmetic mentally and writing only the result, and treats every Explain command term as if it said Describe. Three sentences like that are worth more than a page of general comment, because each one implies a different piece of teaching and each can be tested again in a fortnight.

The diagnostic should also produce an hour count and a stop condition. A tutor willing to say this looks like fourteen hours, and if the marks have not moved by session eight something in my analysis is wrong is a tutor taking responsibility for their own estimate. Open-ended arrangements with no review point are how families in Dubai end up two years into a monthly payment with no evidence either way. Ask for the review date at the start, and put it in the calendar.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects Dubai families book one-to-one most often
paragraphs: Extended Mathematics is the single most requested one-to-one subject in this market, and the reason is structural rather than cultural: Maths is a prerequisite for most of what follows it, the Extended content moves fast, and a gap in Year 9 algebra is still a gap in Year 11 trigonometry. The sciences follow, with Physics and Chemistry ahead of Biology, largely because both carry quantitative content that cannot be learned by reading and a practical paper that rewards a skill nobody teaches explicitly.

English is requested less often than it should be. Families treat 0500 as a subject their child either can or cannot do, when in practice the reading-response marks are among the most teachable on any IGCSE paper, because they reward a specific technique rather than a general flair for language. The second-language syllabus 0510 is a different case: here the most useful intervention is often checking the entry itself, because a child entered for the wrong route is capped or stretched for administrative reasons rather than educational ones.

The scarce subjects are where one-to-one earns its premium. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 with its pseudocode conventions, Arabic as a first language 0508, Economics 0455 evaluation technique, and the whole category of private-candidate entries where no school is sequencing the work. In those cases the question is not what an hour costs but whether anyone in a reasonable radius teaches it at all, and that is the specific problem an online match solves.

sections.heading: Cost in context: fees, entry and a year of weekly sessions
paragraphs: Tuition is easier to judge next to the other numbers in a Dubai education budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of Dubai's economic incentives packages. Each school's own fee is published on its KHDA profile, so the comparison is available to any parent without asking anyone. Against a frozen fee, a weekly one-to-one subject at market rates is a meaningful but not enormous addition, and it is the line in the budget you control.

Exam entry is the other number families forget. School candidates have entry fees folded into the school's charges; private candidates pay the centre directly, and that amount is set by the centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so it must be checked with the centre you intend to enter through. Final entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers themselves. A Cambridge June entry closes with the centre in the late winter, roughly four months before the first paper, and a November entry closes a comparable distance ahead of its own October to November window; the exact day is on the statement of entry, which is the document to ask the centre for rather than trusting a date found online. Pearson is the same shape with a published window attached: its November 2026 papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Missing whichever date applies costs more than any tuition decision.

The table below is a planning frame rather than a price list. Fill in your own school's published fee and your own centre's entry charge, then put the tuition rows next to them. The point of doing it on paper is that tuition is usually the only line you can change mid-year, and seeing it in proportion tends to produce better decisions than either guilt or panic does.
